531768|2026-06.headline: Poly Medicure Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 30.3% to INR525 crore (12.4% organic), with consolidated EBITDA margin at 24.1% and standalone at 28%.
531768|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 30.3% to INR525 crore, of which INR72.3 crore came from acquisitions, leaving organic growth at 12.4% to INR453.1 crore. Standalone revenue rose 12.3% to INR431 crore and standalone EBITDA was INR120.8 crore (28% margin), above the 25-27% FY27 guidance, helped by price hikes and inventory gains. Middle East sales fell 32% due to West Asia logistics disruption, while renal degrew 3.8% amid Chinese pricing pressure. Management maintained FY27 guidance and launched a "PolyMed 3.0" target to double revenue by FY30.

531859|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.7% YoY to INR137.6 crore, with EBITDA up 43.7% to INR20.9 crore and margin at 15.2%.
531859|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR137.6 crore against INR117.9 crore a year earlier, up 16.7% YoY. EBITDA rose 43.7% to INR20.9 crore, with margin expanding 286 bps to 15.2%, and PAT rose 83% to INR10.7 crore (7.8% margin). Management attributed the sequential revenue moderation to the US-Iran war and a fuel and gas supply crisis in March-April, which it says is now largely resolved. The consolidated order book stood at about INR1,692 crore as of August 11, 2026, with INR1,526 crore at OFPL wagons and INR166 crore in coach interiors. Management also laid out smart wagon, next-gen wagon, wagon leasing and JV initiatives.

segments.commentary: About 75% of consolidated revenue and about INR106 crore in Q1; management guides wagon volumes up more than 45-50% YoY on better capacity utilisation. Installed capacity is 2,400 wagons per annum, with FY26 utilisation around 50%.

segments.name: Seats and berths (rolling stock interiors, ORIL)
segments.commentary: About 16% of revenue; the business holds over 30% market share with installed capacity of about 3,600 coaches per annum. Management expects other businesses to grow 8-10%.

segments.name: Rexine upholstery (ORVIN)
segments.commentary: About 5% of revenue; in-house capacity is 36 lakh meters per annum serving railway and non-railway users.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for sequential revenue moderation and Q2 run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q1 to the US-Iran war and the fuel and gas supply crisis in March-April, now largely resolved. Q2 is running faster, with about 500 wagons expected versus roughly 300 plus in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How many wagons does the INR1,526 crore OFPL order book represent and what is the execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3,800 wagons, executed at about 200 wagons per month from Q3 FY27 (October-December).

qa_highlights.question: Capacity expansion plans and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is to go from 2,400 to 3,600 (capex INR60-70 crore), then 4,800 over 12-18 months from FY28; the capacity application is planned for Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did freight revenue not grow in FY25-FY26 (INR458 crore to INR409 crore), and what changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed a railway wheel shortage that restricted supply and underutilised capacity. Backward integration into springs, draft gears and couplers has since stabilised supply.

qa_highlights.question: Debt, cash flow and leverage outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash flow should improve with utilisation and debt will reduce, but declined to give FY27/FY28 debt or debt-to-equity figures.

qa_highlights.answer: No FY27 order additions targeted; management expects about INR600 crore of inflow in Q1 FY28. Government wagon tenders are typically clubbed for about two years.

531859|2026-09.headline: Oriental Rail Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 29% YoY to INR172.5 crores, PAT up 44% to INR15.3 crores, with H1 order book at INR1,571 crores.
531859|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was INR172.5 crores (+29% YoY), EBITDA INR27.9 crores (+29%, 16.2% margin) and PAT INR15.3 crores (+44%). H1 revenue was INR310.1 crores (+23%), EBITDA INR48.8 crores (+35%) and PAT INR26.1 crores (+58%). Wagon output (subsidiary OFPL) rose 30% QoQ to 390 units, but was short of the 500 target because plant changes ran about 15 days late. Management guided to 600 wagons per quarter from Q3 and H2 revenue at least 25-30% above H1, while new initiatives (smart wagons, 25-ton bogie, leasing, coach refurbishment) are mostly pegged to FY28.

segments.name: Railway interiors and seats (parent)
segments.commentary: Current interior furnishing revenue about INR45-50 crores of the INR310 crores H1 base; management expects at least 100% growth over the next 4-5 quarters. Parent claims about 30% share of the organised seat and berth market, with 3,600 coach-set capacity.

segments.name: Freight wagons (OFPL, wholly owned)
segments.commentary: Produced 390 wagons in Q2 vs 300 in Q1 (+30% QoQ) against a 500 target; installed capacity 2,400 wagons a year; order book above 2,000 wagons, covering roughly three to four quarters.

H2 FY27 revenue at least 25-30% above H1 (H1 INR310.1 crores), per management's reply to a question.
Production growth of at least 30-35% in Q3 over Q2.

Interior refurbishment: order book of at least INR100 crores plus by March 2027; target order inflow of about INR130 crores from INR400 crores of tenders quoted by December 2026, at a 30% strike rate.
Smart wagon order (RDSO tender, about 300-400 wagons, with HUM International): expected by mid-November 2026, with a conservative minimum of 200 units.
EBITDA margin expected to improve by about 6 percentage points relative to prior levels (for example 12-15% to 16-16.5%), per management's framing.
Capacity augmentation to 3,600 coach sets planned to start from April 2027; leasing entry from April 2027 onwards.
25-ton axle load bogie and gondola: RDSO design submission by December 2026; prototype and field trials in 6-9 months; regular supply orders from FY28.
capex_capacity: Wagon production: 390 units in Q2 vs 500 target; the shortfall was due to capital and technical changes on the plant completed about 15 days behind schedule.
Wagon capacity: installed capacity 2,400 wagons a year at OFPL; about 3,600 coach sets a year for seats and berths; four manufacturing units across about 100 acres.

Capacity augmentation planned to be finalised by February-March 2027 and implemented from April 2027. Land and permissions are already available, and the modern wagon design will be built in a new facility.
Backward integration: spring manufacturing in operation for about one year. Two or three more components are in discussion, with production expected from the middle of FY28.
Vande Bharat chair car seat order to be delivered by quarter ending June 2027; turnkey Vande Bharat furnishing readiness by January 2028.
demand_pricing: Management estimates Indian Railways needs about 35,000-40,000 wagons a year (about 20,000 replacement and 12,000-15,000 growth), against industry capacity of about 30,000-35,000. Management described this as its own estimate rather than a railway forecast.

Last large railway wagon tender was in 2023, covering about 80,000-90,000 wagons over three years. Management said timing of the next tender cannot be predicted, though visibility is 'definitely' there.
Interior furnishing market is about INR700-800 crores with three to four participants; management hopes to win about INR150 crores in the first one to two years, rising to about INR200 crores.

Steel prices rose sharply in the last quarter (Q2), including HR, stainless and spring steel; the company says price variation formulas in railway tenders largely cover the increase. Supply tie-ups and advance orders were placed.

Management said that Vande Bharat is a target and that private freight operators (Tata, Jindal) are a target for the modern wagon once RDSO-vetted; export discussions with a public sector network are at an early stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why were only 390 wagons produced against the 500 target, and what is the Q3 run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed technical and capital changes on the plant that finished about 15 days late. It expects to clear the 390 backlog and deliver about 500 plus 110 in Q3, and later said 600 per quarter from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt as of 30 September and the inventory build-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management first said around INR300 crores; the footnote corrects this to INR193.5 crores. Inventory rose because of advance steel buying amid volatile supply, and inventory should be under control by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue run rate for H2 and EBITDA margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 revenue should be at least 25-30% above H1. Management said price variation mechanisms limit raw-material downside, and margins should improve on higher utilisation and backward integration.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the smart wagon tender and the 25-ton bogie development?
qa_highlights.answer: The smart wagon financial bids are expected to open shortly, with orders by mid-November and a minimum of 200 units. The RDSO design submission is due by December 2026, with regular supply orders from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for wagon leasing and the impact of a railway tender delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Leasing entry is planned from April 2027. Average lease tenure is about 10 years (9-12). Management named railway leasing companies and private operators (GATX, Tata) as alternative buyers.

qa_highlights.question: Is any refurbishment order flow in place, and what margins apply?
qa_highlights.answer: Tenders of about INR150 crores are quoted against about two to three competitors, with a further INR200 crores pipeline. Management declined to disclose refurbishment EBITDA margins on the call, citing the investor presentation.

risks_watch: Execution: Q2 wagon output missed the 500 target. Q3 must reach 600 wagons as guided, and H2 revenue must be 25-30% above H1.
Working capital: short-term borrowings rose in H1 to fund inventory built up ahead of steel price moves; watch inventory days and whether they fall by March 2027.

Dependence on railway tenders: the order book covers about 3-4 quarters, and the next large railway wagon tender has no timeline. Leasing, HUM smart wagons and private operators are not yet revenue-generating.
Interior refurbishment: the INR150 crores of bids have not yet converted to orders; management target of about INR130 crores assumes a 30% strike rate.
Investor queries left open: net debt was misquoted on the call, and the INR50 crores loan and advance asset query was taken offline. Management also declined to comment on share price performance.
Steel price volatility: management says price variation clauses cover most of it, but the company will need to show margins holding in Q3 and Q4.

532054|2026-03.headline: KDDL standalone Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 87.6% YoY to INR36.4 crore at a 25.1% margin; FY26 standalone revenue INR506 crore, up 31.9%.
532054|2026-03.overview: Management reported standalone Q4 FY26 total income of INR145.3 crore (up ~42% YoY) and PAT of INR19.8 crore (13.6% margin). Consolidated Q4 total income was ~INR585 crore (up ~35.6%) with PAT of INR34.5 crore, and consolidated FY26 revenue reached INR2,207.8 crore (up ~30.3%). Watch components (ex-Ethos, ex-bracelets) grew ~20% to ~INR240 crore, Precision Engineering (Eigen) grew 35%+ to ~INR200 crore, and Ornapac grew ~37% to INR23 crore. Management guided to a 25% medium-term CAGR for bracelets and precision engineering, slightly lower for watch components, and no major margin change this year.

segments.name: Watch components (dials, hands)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR240 crore vs INR200 crore last year, ~20% growth. Recovered in H2 FY26 after a quiet H1; management expects H1 FY27 export roughly stable and growth more visible in H2.

segments.name: Bracelets
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR40 crore, export-led, reported separately from the INR240 crore watch component figure. Capacity utilisation ~75-80% on existing capacity; expects 20-25% growth.

segments.name: Precision Engineering (Eigen)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ~INR200 crore vs INR147 crore, up 35%+. Expansion underway with backward integration into plating and some capacity additions; Bangalore-related capex expected to commission in 3-4 months.

segments.name: Ornapac (packaging)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR23 crore vs ~INR17 crore, up ~37%. Still loss-making during ramp-up; management expects profitability in H2 FY27.

segments.name: Ethos (retail, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Crossed 100 boutiques in FY26; management targets doubling the network in ~3 years and revenue growth of 20-25% p.a. Results were declared a week before the call; no Ethos financials were detailed on the call.

segments.name: Favre-Leuba (Silvercity Brands, Switzerland)
segments.commentary: Present in 20+ countries with 80+ points of sale; sales well above plan and stores short of stock. Management expects sales to more than double in FY27. Not disclosed in financial terms.

guidance_outlook: Precision Engineering and bracelets: ~25% medium-to-long-term value CAGR; watch components slightly lower.
Bracelets: good revenue growth in FY27 and FY28, with margins moderating near term as newer, lower-price customers ramp.
Favre-Leuba: sales expected to more than double in FY27.
Ornapac: expected to turn profitable in H2 FY27.
Capex of ~INR50 crore planned for FY27 across standalone businesses (bracelets, watch components, precision engineering, packaging); excludes subsidiaries such as Favre-Leuba.
No major change in margin picture expected this year; currency tailwind from CHF expected to persist at similar levels.

Ethos: aims to double store network in ~3 years (Pranav Saboo said it may take 4); a new format at INR25,000-2 lakh price point is planned this year; Swiss franc pricing gap of ~7-8% expected to be passed on over time.
risks_watch: Weak Swiss luxury watch demand in China and Europe could keep H1 FY27 export growth flat.
Margin pressure from lower price points of new bracelet customers and from Ethos Swiss franc pricing lag.
Ornapac must reach profitability in H2 FY27 as guided.
Eigen expansion timing (commissioning in 3-4 months) and customer concentration in the busbar OEM.
Bracelet customer concentration, flagged by an analyst; management says new customers are being added.
Ethos store expansion and working capital (inventory days ~221) need monitoring.
532054|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth and results, but evasive on granular disclosures: volume, currency-adjusted numbers, Favre-Leuba financials, bracelet peak capacity and capex asset turns were not shared. Management was cautious on near-term export demand and on margin direction for this year.
key_quotes: It is in our nature in our DNA to be cautious in our promises, but aggressive enough performance.
We expect to more than double the sales in FY27 and greatly expand our global footprint with exciting new product launches.

Eigen as such is not a product selling company. For Eigen, it does not matter whether it's a busbar or some other component for some other applications, we continue to remain a capability selling company.

qa_highlights.question: Is bracelet revenue part of the INR240 crore watch component figure, and what is its size?
qa_highlights.answer: Bracelets are separate from the INR240 crore watch component figure; bracelet revenue is around INR40 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the standalone volume growth versus value growth, and is the INR50 crore capex for standalone only or including Favre-Leuba?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify volume growth, saying volumes across products are too disparate to sum. The INR50 crore capex covers standalone businesses (bracelets, watch components, precision engineering, packaging) and excludes subsidiaries such as Favre-Leuba.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bracelet utilisation level and how will it ramp, and are new customers being won?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing bracelet capacity was about 75-80% utilised this year; capacity is being added incrementally, and new customers are being added, so utilisation is expected to rise this year.

qa_highlights.question: Will Eigen's Bangalore capex commission soon, and is the new capex backed by orders or OEM visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: The Eigen capex started last year is still in progress; backward integration of processes is expected to be commissioned in the next 3-4 months. Management described Eigen as a capability-selling company, not dependent on the busbar product.

qa_highlights.question: Will the standalone margin improve as store expansion costs in Ethos mature, and what drove the Q4 margin jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Ethos store costs are already in the P&L and the expansion continues; margin direction depends on currency and price pass-through. For standalone, the CFO said margins are expected to stay in the same band with no dramatic change, and the currency benefit has run through the full year.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Swiss franc move has Ethos passed on, and how much remains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing is roughly 7-8% below required levels, with the gap to be passed on over time, typically every six months, since about 50 brands decide prices comparatively.

capex_capacity: Planned capex of ~INR50 crore for FY27 across standalone businesses (bracelets, watch components, precision engineering, packaging), including maintenance and growth capex; excludes subsidiary investments such as Favre-Leuba. Management said major part goes to Precision Engineering and bracelets.
Capex of ~INR34 crore invested in FY26 across divisions (standalone).
Eigen (precision engineering) capex started last year is still in progress; backward integration into plating (previously outsourced) expected to be commissioned in the next 3-4 months.

Bracelet capacity: ~75,000 units approximate original capacity; utilisation ~75-80% on existing capacity in FY26; management plans to expand to ~110,000-120,000 units over the next 12 months; capacity added incrementally and measured in value rather than units.

Management declined to give peak-utilisation revenue for bracelet and packaging capacities, Eigen capacity before/after expansion, Favre-Leuba size, or asset turns on capex, citing confidentiality and mix-driven capacity.
demand_pricing: Watch components (dials, hands) recovered in H2 FY26 after a quiet H1; management expects H1 FY27 export business roughly stable with growth more visible in H2 FY27; domestic business expected robust. Management said growth could exceed 11-12% if global luxury watch demand improves.

Weak luxury demand in China and parts of Europe; global brands cautious on inventory and procurement; Swiss watches face headwinds in several markets. Customer diversification beyond Switzerland to brands at different price points underway; Switzerland still largest by value.

Bracelets: export-led, ~INR40 crore revenue FY26 (separate from INR240 crore watch components); good revenue growth expected FY27 and FY28 with near-term margin moderation from lower price-point new customers. Management guides 20-25% growth; steel remains ~80% of metal bracelets globally; other metals not ruled out.

Precision Engineering (Eigen): FY26 revenue ~INR200 crore vs INR147 crore (35%+); growth from deeper existing customer relationships, new customers and new products; export focus; EV, energy storage and electronics named as priority sectors. Management says Eigen's precision-stamping market share is very small.
Ornapac packaging: FY26 revenue INR23 crore vs ~INR17 crore (~37%); supplies to international brands for the domestic market began; loss-making in ramp-up, expected profitable in H2 FY27.

Pricing and margins: management guides no major change in margin picture this year; CHF strength is a tailwind expected to persist at similar levels; Ethos Swiss franc pricing gap of ~7-8% expected to be passed on over time (roughly every six months, across ~50 brands). Standalone margin rise partly attributed to CHF strength per CFO.

rows.why: Management guides no great change in the margin picture this year, with standalone EBITDA margin at 23.1% in FY26 and 25.1% in Q4; bracelet margins to moderate near term and Ethos store costs are already in the P&L, while the CHF tailwind is expected only at similar levels.

rows.why: Bracelet utilisation at 75-80% on ~75,000 units, with a plan to add ~50% capacity (to 110-120k units) over 12 months, and Eigen plating backward integration due to commission in 3-4 months, with new capacity being added incrementally.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides about 25% value CAGR for bracelets and precision engineering, 20-25% bracelet growth, and watch components slightly lower; volume was not quantified, and the Eigen revenue rose 35%+ to ~INR200 crore in FY26.

rows.why: Ethos plans a new format at a INR25,000-2 lakh price point this year, and Eigen is adding new products and customers; no specific standalone product launch dates were given.

rows.why: Ethos pricing is about 7-8% below required levels after the CHF move, with the gap to be passed on across ~50 brands roughly every six months.

rows.label: Ornapac profitability
rows.why: Ornapac revenue rose ~37% to INR23 crore in FY26 but is still loss-making in ramp-up, and management expects profitability in H2 FY27.

rows.why: The brand is present in 20+ countries with 80+ points of sale, sales are well above plan, and stores are short of stock; management expects sales to more than double in FY27 (no financials disclosed).

532067|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue about INR142 crore and PAT nearly INR60 crore; management guides 15-20% growth for FY27 across the group.
532067|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated revenue of about INR142 crore and PAT of nearly INR60 crore, with Coris BioConcept (acquired August 2025) contributing INR35.91 crore for seven months. 3B India molecular diagnostics grew about 10% to INR86.47 crore, below internal projections, which management attributed to a high base from FY25 flu and dengue/chikungunya demand and Middle East disruption to export markets. Standalone non-export revenue grew about 7.1% and exports about 25%, and the company guided to 15-20% growth in FY27 with margins broadly maintained. Coris carries a loss-making first half and is guided to be only slightly EBITDA positive in FY27, while management said M&A is still under way with no deal closed.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR78.34 crore in FY25, about 10% growth
vs INR17.03 crore in FY25, about 25% growth
PAT boosted by one-time HAT order

financial_highlights.metric: Coris revenue, 15-month accounting period (Jan 2025 to Mar 2026)
Consolidated EBITDA margin FY26 (as cited by analyst)
financial_highlights.change: management cited 61.84% EBITDA figure in response; terms not reconciled on call

financial_highlights.value: 55% (INR53 crore operating profit on INR97 crore)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1.08 crore in FY25; about INR4 crore from Coris

financial_highlights.value: about INR230 crore (cash about INR90 crore plus investments about INR150 crore, per analyst)

segments.name: 3B India molecular diagnostics
segments.commentary: Sales INR86.47 crore in FY26, up about 10% from INR78.34 crore, with non-export domestic growth about 7.1% and exports about INR21.4 crore (includes exports to TRUPCR). Management said domestic growth would be about 15% in a normal year, with the FY25 flu/dengue/chikungunya spike worth about INR4.2 crore.

segments.name: TRUPCR Europe
segments.commentary: FY26 sales GBP1.75 million (INR20.67 crore), up from GBP1.28 million; management cited about 40% CAGR over four years. Its EBITDA margin was described as about 15-20%.

segments.name: Coris BioConcept (Belgium)
segments.commentary: Consolidated from 29 August 2025 with FY26 sales INR35.91 crore and PAT INR8.76 crore, lifted by a one-time HAT order. Management guided to about INR50-52 crore revenue on a full-year basis in FY27 and slightly EBITDA positive, with EBITDA margin of about 10% targeted in FY27-28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% on a consolidated basis; management said EBITDA should grow at a similar 15-20% pace and margin profile should be maintained.

Coris expected to be slightly EBITDA positive in FY27, with the first two quarters loss-making; about 5-7% EBITDA targeted in FY28 and about 10% in FY27-28 per management, with revenue of about INR5 million (about INR50 crore) in FY27.

Management said US FDA clearance for selected AMR products is a process with timing uncertain (1 to 1.5 years or later); the US could contribute about 20% of AMR revenue, about INR11-16 crore (USD1-1.5 million).
Depreciation for FY27 guided at about INR4.5-5 crore for the full year.
Sample-to-answer system (via OEM) expected to start installations at two to three labs from Q3 FY27, with the validation said to be positive; this is included in the 15-20% guidance.
Management intends to keep a reserve of about INR50 crore and deploy the rest into M&A over the next one to two years; a deal was targeted by year-end but no timing was committed.
Company will move to two earnings calls per year (next in the half-year).
capex_capacity: Current capacity utilisation about 50%; management said any capacity increase would cost about INR4-5 crore, so expansion capex is small.
Coris capitalised about INR8 crore of R&D under Belgian law; INR1.6 crore amortised in FY26 at 20% per year, with the R&D capitalisation expected to continue at a somewhat lower scale.
IVDR: BSI appointed as notified body; IVDR-aligned QMS audits completed; technical documentation review progressing for key product families.
demand_pricing: Management said price competition is contained: fierce only in low-priced single tests (TB, HBV, HCV), while multi-panel respiratory and meningitis and oncology are less contested; Chinese players are underpricing respiratory and enteric products.
Management views the Indian molecular diagnostics market at about INR500-600 crore, with the company holding about 15% share; the market is expected to grow 8-10%.
Average selling price to distributors about INR700-800 per kit (range INR300 to INR2,000); distributor markup 15-20%, with hospitals and labs marking up further.
Coris's Resist-5 (AMR product) is about 30-35% of Coris revenue; US rapid AMR diagnostic market estimated around INR100 crore, mainly served by imports.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR21.4 crore export figure include TRUPCR, and what is domestic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the INR21.4 crore includes exports to TRUPCR. Non-export standalone revenue grew about 7.1%; adding back about INR4.2 crore of FY25 flu and chikungunya/dengue sales, domestic growth would be about 12.5-13%.

qa_highlights.question: What is Coris's full-year FY26 revenue on a 12-month basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Coris did about INR50 crore for the full year; with Coris's accounting aligned to 31 March, the 15-month period to March 2026 gave INR57.65 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How does the margin look for FY27 and how is Q1/Q2 Coris loss treated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide quarterly; it said full-year revenue and EBITDA should both grow 15-20%, with Coris losing money in Q1 and Q2 and benefiting from HAT order timing in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the M&A pipeline and cash deployment?
qa_highlights.answer: Two or three opportunities are in advanced discussion with consultants in France, UK and US; European valuations are high, and the company will hold a reserve of INR50 crore with the balance for M&A over one to two years. Treasury is about 90% in FDs, government bonds and AAA corporate bonds, and about 5-7% in equity mutual funds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Coris contract status and the EBITDA trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Of a EUR6 million four-year contract (Congo, affected by Ebola), about EUR3.45 million has been executed and about EUR2.4 million remains; Coris is guided to slightly EBITDA positive in FY27, about 10% in FY27-28.

risks_watch: Coris earnings depend on the HAT order timing; the Congo contract is at risk from the Ebola outbreak.
FY26 domestic growth (~10%) lagged the chains' reported test volume growth of 10-11%; the company said it is high-base affected.
FY27 consolidated margin depends on Coris losses in H1 and the M&A outcome; the cash pile of about INR230 crore is not yet deployed.
Chinese competition in respiratory and enteric products, including export markets, and IVDR compliance timing for EU exports.
US FDA clearance timing for AMR products remains uncertain.

Several answers were also unclear on the numbers, with the chairman asking the analyst to check the slide during the Coris Q4 depreciation discussion.
key_quotes: So, growth of 15% to 20% is what is we are trying to achieve and let's look forward to it.
So, we will do only two earning calls every year.
Coris will become slightly EBITDA positive.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Consolidated revenue guided to 15-20% growth in FY27, backed by Coris (about INR50-52 crore revenue vs about INR35.91 crore for seven months in FY26) and standalone growth of about 7.1% non-export, though domestic growth lagged at about 10% due to the FY25 high base.

rows.why: Utilisation is about 50% with capacity increases costing only INR4-5 crore, so no large capex is needed; the cash pile of about INR230 crore is more likely to go to M&A than to plants.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Coris HAT order timing in Q3-Q4 FY27 and the sample-to-answer OEM rollout could lift results above the 15-20% guide, but management declined to guide quarterly and the Coris Congo contract (about EUR2.4 million left) is at Ebola risk.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Coris is loss-making in Q1 and Q2 FY27, domestic growth (about 10% in FY26) lagged chains' test volume growth of 10-11%, and Chinese players are underpricing respiratory and enteric products.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Sample-to-answer system is expected to start installations at two to three labs from Q3 FY27 after positive validation, and IVDR technical documentation review is progressing for key product families, but no specific launch dates or revenue sizes were given.

rows.label: US FDA clearance for selected AMR products
rows.why: The US could contribute about 20% of AMR revenue, about INR11-16 crore (USD1-1.5 million), but timing is uncertain and management gave no firm date.

rows.label: M&A deployment of about INR180-200 crore of cash
rows.why: Two or three targets are in advanced talks with consultants in France, UK and US, and about INR230 crore of treasury cash is held with a INR50 crore reserve; management targeted a deal by year-end but committed to no timing.

rows.label: Coris Congo EUR6 million contract execution
rows.why: About EUR3.45 million of the four-year contract is executed and about EUR2.4 million remains, but the Ebola outbreak in Congo puts the balance at risk.

532134|2026-03.headline: Bank of Baroda Q4 FY26 net profit rose 11.2% YoY to a record Rs 5,616 crore; FY26 net profit Rs 20,021 crore, with FY27 loan growth guidance raised to 12-14%.
532134|2026-03.overview: Global business crossed Rs 30 lakh crore at Rs 30.78 lakh crore (+13.9% YoY), with global advances up 16.2% and total deposits up 12%. Q4 operating profit was Rs 9,069 crore (+11.5% YoY) and NII grew 8.7%, with NIM at 2.89% (+10 bps QoQ) helped partly by interest on income-tax refunds. Asset quality improved (GNPA 1.89%, net NPA 0.45%), but Q4 credit cost rose to 0.76% after a Rs 1,500 crore floating provision funded from IT refunds. Management raised FY27 loan and deposit growth guidance and set a Rs 6,000 crore AT-1/Tier 2 raise plan, while cautioning that cost of deposits will stay sticky in Q1 given tight liquidity and West Asia tensions.

financial_highlights.value: 0.76% (0.32% excluding Rs 1,500 crore floating provision); FY26 0.46% (0.34% excluding floating provision)

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Organic retail book grew 17.9% YoY and crossed Rs 3 lakh crore; auto loans +20.6%, mortgages +19.3%, home loans +14.6%, education +10.9%, personal loans +8.7%. RAM share of advances is 61%.

segments.name: Agriculture and MSME
segments.commentary: Agriculture advances grew 20.7% and organic MSME 15.6%. MSME book is about Rs 1.6 lakh crore, of which 55-60% is working capital; ECLGS disbursement estimated at Rs 12,000 crore plus.

segments.name: Corporate and international
segments.commentary: Corporate loans grew 11.2% YoY. International advances grew 24.4%; US operations are about 37-38% of the international book. Management says Middle East exposure is about Rs 50,000-60,000 crore across multiple countries, with no asset-quality impact yet.

guidance_outlook: FY27 loan growth guidance raised to 12-14% from 11-13%.
FY27 deposit growth guidance raised to 10-12% from 9-11%.
FY27 NIM guidance 2.75-2.95%, which management says includes volatility from IT refund interest; management said it would not breach 2.75% over the four quarters.
ROA guidance kept at more than 1%; slippage ratio kept at 1-1.25%; full-year credit cost guided below 0.60%.
Normalised recoveries from written-off accounts guided at Rs 750-800 crore; management said Q4 recovery was higher than guidance.
Cost of deposits expected to stay sticky in Q1 FY27 given tight liquidity. Management sees scope to reprice MCLR-linked assets; MCLR is 36% and repo-linked 35% of the book.
Hiring of 4,000-5,000 headcount in FY27, against a plan of 6,000-7,000.
capex_capacity: Capital plan: Rs 6,000 crore of AT-1/Tier 2 in FY27, with no fixed timeline and execution depending on pricing. An enabling Rs 8,500 crore equity raise runs through FY28.
Tech spend (opex plus capex) was about Rs 4,500 crore; management says it is adequately covered, with extra spend possible if needed. Tech spend is about 10% of operating profit as a norm.

New subsidiaries: BOB Securities and Gilt Edge Ltd (primary dealer, operational from 1 April 2026, Rs 2,000 crore capital committed, Rs 500 crore availed); pension fund sponsorship approval received, with 6-9 months expected to launch.
Green infrastructure bond of Rs 10,000 crore raised, 3x subscribed; green deposits of Rs 1,899 crore.
demand_pricing: Deposit growth of 12% outpaced by the 16.2% advances growth, a gap management views as sustainable given excess SLR and bulk deposit usage.
Bulk deposits rose to 19% of total deposits in March from 17% a couple of quarters earlier; management says it will stay below 20%.
Domestic SLR is about 22.5-23%, roughly 4.5-5% above the statutory level; management targets 3-3.5% excess SLR.
Collection efficiency excluding agriculture is 98.9%, up from December. CRILC SMA-1 and 2 fell to 0.18% from 0.33% a year earlier.
Management said MSME stress (SMA-0 to SMA-2) was better in March than December, and auto loan stress remains very small.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 NIM improvement came from IT refund interest, and how much is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a number and said it is a recurring but volatile line item (about Rs 100 crore to interest income in Q4 per a later reply). It treats the 2.89% as core and the 2.75-2.95% range as covering refund volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 1,500 crore floating provision linked to ECL or West Asia?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a balance-sheet buffer funded by IT refunds, aimed at lifting PCR and keeping net NPA low. It cannot be used without regulatory approval and is separate from ECL. ECL impact is not yet quantified; management said it should be broadly in line with earlier estimates.

qa_highlights.question: Why was loan guidance raised after a 16.2% growth year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth has been strong since 31 March on a daily YoY basis, the deposit base is recovering, and it expects the geopolitical disruption may not last long. It raised guidance by 1 percentage point.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of deposits outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of deposits (4.78% total, 4.99% domestic) is expected to stay sticky for at least the next three months as liquidity remains tight; management does not expect further reductions and sees repricing mainly on the asset side.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exposure to the Middle East and overseas book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put Middle East exposure at about Rs 50,000-60,000 crore across multiple countries, some A-rated, with US about 37-38% of the international book. Trade is below 20% of overseas exposure, and no asset-quality impact has been seen yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for agriculture and the weak monsoon?
qa_highlights.answer: Agriculture GNPA fell year on year. Fresh slippages are normal and were offset by recoveries. Management does not expect a weak monsoon to materially affect the portfolio.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: a prolonged war or high oil prices could affect the overseas book, Middle East operations and MSME borrowers; management is watching this closely over the next couple of quarters.
Cost of deposits is sticky and asset repricing is still to be shown; NIM guidance of 2.75-2.95% relies partly on volatile IT refund interest.
ECL implementation: quantification is pending, with management indicating it will show up in the books from the first quarter of implementation.
Credit cost run rate is guided below 0.60%, but the Q4 level of 0.76% included the one-time floating provision.
Bulk deposit share, LCR (about 127%), and the timing and pricing of the Rs 6,000 crore AT-1/Tier 2 issuance.
532134|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, profitability and asset quality, with several guidance upgrades. Cautious and hedged on margin, deposit costs and West Asia exposure, repeatedly saying impacts are unquantified and depend on liquidity and the conflict's duration. Evasive on ECL quantum and bilateral accounts such as Vodafone Idea.
key_quotes: So, in terms of customer income, we have improved, the NIM has improved vis-a-vis the last quarter from 2.79% to 2.89% with the domestic NIM at 3.04%.
The credit cost for the full year is going to be less than 0.60%.
I'm not predicting any increase in deposit rate.
Our floating provision cannot be used without the regulatory approval and that can only be used on extraordinary scenarios.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM rose 10 bps QoQ to 2.89% in Q4 (partly IT refund interest), with management seeing repricing scope on MCLR-linked assets (36% of book), but cost of deposits stays sticky at 4.78% in Q1 and it guides only to a 2.75-2.95% range.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Global advances grew 16.2% and deposits 12% in FY26, with FY27 loan guidance 12-14% and deposit guidance 10-12%; retail organic book up 17.9% past Rs 3 lakh crore and agriculture advances up 20.7%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No physical capex discussed, but the Rs 6,000 crore AT-1/Tier 2 raise in FY27 (no fixed timeline, pricing dependent) and the enabling Rs 8,500 crore equity raise through FY28 signal capital actions; tech spend about Rs 4,500 crore is covered, with extra spend possible.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 loan growth guidance was already raised to 12-14% (from 11-13%) after 16.2% advances growth in FY26, and deposit guidance raised to 10-12%; management says growth has been strong since 31 March on a daily YoY basis.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: NIM guidance of 2.75-2.95% relies partly on volatile IT refund interest (about Rs 100 crore in Q4), cost of deposits is sticky at 4.78% through at least the next three months, and West Asia exposure of Rs 50,000-60,000 crore is unquantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Pension fund sponsorship approval received with 6-9 months expected to launch, and BOB Securities and Gilt Edge Ltd (primary dealer) operational from 1 April 2026 with Rs 500 crore of Rs 2,000 crore capital availed.

rows.label: Hiring 4,000-5,000 in FY27 vs plan of 6,000-7,000
rows.why: Management guided 4,000-5,000 headcount additions in FY27, below the 6,000-7,000 plan, reflecting a slower hiring pace.

rows.label: ECL implementation impact on provisions
rows.why: ECL impact is not yet quantified and management says it will show up in the books from the first quarter of implementation, with the floating provision of Rs 1,500 crore sitting alongside it.

rows.label: Excess SLR and bulk deposit funding
rows.why: Domestic SLR is about 22.5-23% (4.5-5% above statutory), with management targeting 3-3.5% excess SLR; bulk deposits are 19% of total, which management says will stay below 20%.

tone.note: Management was confident on loan growth, record profit, asset quality and raised guidance, but cautious and hedged on margins, sticky deposit costs, West Asia exposure and ECL quantum; analysts pressed on IT refund contribution, the floating provision and the Middle East book.

532134|2026-06.headline: Bank of Baroda Q1 FY27 net profit fell to INR 1,278 crore after a USD 600 million NMC settlement; ex-item profit was INR 5,528 crore.
532134|2026-06.overview: Global business reached INR 30.5 lakh crore, up 15.4% YoY, with global advances up 17.4% and domestic deposits up 14.7%. Operating profit was INR 8,127 crore, roughly flat YoY, as NII grew 9.5% but treasury income fell to about INR 800-900 crore from over INR 2,000 crore a year earlier. The USD 600 million NMC out-of-court settlement, paid on 1 July 2026 and expensed in Q1, cut reported ROA to 0.25% (1.10% excluding the item). Asset quality improved YoY, with GNPA at 1.99%, credit cost at 0.29% and slippage at 0.91%, though sequentially GNPA and NNPA ticked up due to a lower write-off of INR 625 crore versus INR 2,200 crore a year earlier.

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -29 bps YoY; Net NPA -10 bps YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Domestic CASA ratio / domestic CD ratio

segments.name: Advances
segments.commentary: Global advances +17.4% YoY (domestic +16.1%, international +23.3%). Organic retail +18.4%, agriculture +18.7%, organic MSME +20.3%, corporate +15.3%; auto +25.3%, mortgage +27.4%, home loan +14.7%, education +10.8%.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Total deposits +13.8% YoY (domestic +14.7%, international +8.9%). Domestic CASA +10% and term deposits +17.8%; management says current account growth was 14.5%.

segments.name: Treasury and other income
segments.commentary: Treasury income about INR 800-900 crore versus over INR 2,000 crore in Q1 FY26, mainly on revaluation as G-sec yields rose to about 6.78% from about 6.10%. Recoveries from technical write-offs exceeded INR 1,000 crore, and PSLC sales of about INR 270 crore were added. Commission and fee income fell about 47% YoY.

segments.name: International book
segments.commentary: Overseas book is about 16-17% of global book and grew 15-20% over recent quarters; international NIM is about 1.4-1.5%.

guidance_outlook: Credit growth 12-14% (unchanged despite outperformance; management cites geopolitical caution).
Deposit growth 10-12%; CD ratio 84-86%.
NIM 2.75-2.95%; slippage ratio 1-1.25%; credit cost below 0.6%; ROE 15-16%.
Full-year ROA guidance deferred to Q2; management expects Q2-Q4 ROA above 1%, and said full-year ROA may not exceed 1%.

ECL transition impact about INR 12,000 crore (about 110 bps on CRAR), with INR 2,500 crore floating provision offsetting part; run-rate credit cost impact about 15-20 bps (earlier cited 20-22 bps on CRAR).
FCNR(B)/OFCB/ECB inflow target USD 4-5 billion; about USD 600-700 million raised so far; USD 1 billion expected via bonds; swap window open until 31 December.
capex_capacity: Capital plan: INR 8,500 crore equity over the medium term to March 2028; about INR 6,000 crore Tier 2 intended in FY27, subject to pricing and timing.
Branches: about 8,400 total; about 260 added last year. Headcount hiring plan of about 7,000 in FY27 after about 6,000 planned last year.
IT budget (OPEX plus capex) above INR 4,000 crore.
Average LCR about 127%; management targets around 120%.
Investment duration increased QoQ and YoY; yields on the book moved from a peak of about 7.13-7.14% to about 6.75-6.80%.
demand_pricing: Corporate book shows a YTD decline. Management says it let go of some low-priced non-MCLR assets and is moving them to MCLR or near-MCLR, helping asset yields.

Bulk deposits and CD together were about INR 2.31 lakh crore, of which bulk deposits were INR 2.11 lakh crore. Bulk deposit rates eased after the FCNR(B) scheme, so incremental bulk deposit cost is now below March levels, per management.
FCNR(B) Rupee deposit rate of about 6.4-6.5% is the landed cost of funds. Loans against FCNR(B) are offered to NRIs, and overseas branches price these loans at their own cost of funds.
Domestic NIM at 2.93% described as top quartile. Global NIM is also described as top quartile.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the bank settle the NMC case, and what changed from the annual report stance of defending it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the defence position is unchanged, but the decision reflected the stage of trial and negotiation, legal advice, and time and cost. The settlement was USD 600 million, the terms are confidential, and it was described as far below the oral claim quantum. Recovery against principal individuals continues in India and abroad.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no specific provision earlier, and what is the ECL transition impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a specific provision is not allowed on litigation under legal advice. The ECL transition impact is about INR 12,000 crore (110 bps CRAR), offset by the INR 2,500 crore floating provision, with the remainder to be amortised. Credit cost impact is about 15-20 bps; CRAR impact per year is about 20-22 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Why not raise the credit growth guidance given strong performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited geopolitical headwinds and uncertainty over deposit growth. It said guidance could be upsized if deposit growth becomes more certain.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the decline in treasury and other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury income fell to about INR 800-900 crore from over INR 2,000 crore, mainly due to revaluation as yields moved. This was offset partly by about INR 1,000 crore of TWO recoveries and PSLC sales of about INR 270 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the NIM and the FCNR(B) inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed the 2.75-2.95% NIM guidance, citing asset repricing and lower incremental bulk deposit costs. FCNR(B) inflows are targeted at USD 4-5 billion, with about USD 1 billion expected via bonds, subject to pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Is there stress in the book from global headwinds, and what do the asset quality indicators show?
qa_highlights.answer: No; CRILC SMA-1 and 2 fell to 0.07% from 0.40% a year earlier, and collection efficiency excluding agriculture was 99.2%. Management said ECLGS supports MSMEs and that slippage and recoveries were better YoY.

risks_watch: NMC settlement: the terms are confidential and the case is sub-judice against other defendants; management says no further claims on the bank in the two courts.
ROA: full-year guidance deferred to Q2; management expects Q2-Q4 ROA above 1%, but the Q1 reported figure was 0.25%.
ECL transition: about INR 12,000 crore impact and a 15-20 bps run-rate credit cost increase. Management said pricing pass-through is subject to RBI spread-change rules.
Margin pressure: asset growth of 16-17% is running ahead of NII, with the NIM at 2.77% against 2.8%+ last quarter.
Sequential rise in GNPA and NNPA due to a lower write-off (INR 625 crore) and a lower denominator. Management said write-offs were kept conservative to protect PCR.
Funding and capital: the INR 8,500 crore equity raise (by March 2028) and about INR 6,000 crore Tier 2 are pending; the FCNR(B) and dollar bond timing depend on pricing.
Non-interest income: commission and fee income fell about 47% YoY; management says pricing is under review.

532143|2026-03.headline: SKM Egg Products FY26 sales rose 58% to ₹767 crore and PAT crossed ₹100 crore for the first time (₹102 crore).
532143|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 results: sales up 58% YoY to ₹767 crore, operating profit about ₹163 crore, PBT ₹136 crore and PAT ₹102 crore, the first year above ₹100 crore PAT. Q4 FY26 sales were ₹197 crore, with PBT ₹41 crore and PAT ₹32 crore against ₹9.7 crore and ₹6.22 crore a year earlier. Management said powder capacity is now running at full utilisation, so FY27 volume growth will be modest. The company is funding a ₹400 crore layer-shed expansion (about 20 lakh birds, completion targeted 2028-29) and is bringing the associate SKM Universal into the listed entity.

financial_highlights.change: up from ₹33 crore; first year above ₹100 crore
vs ₹180 crore in the prior-year quarter as stated on the call

segments.name: Egg powder (export)
segments.commentary: About 7,000 tonnes of powder today with a stated target of 10,000 tonnes over roughly five years; powder capacity was 7,320 tonnes as of 2023. Management said FY27 powder volume growth will be small because capacity is fully used.

segments.name: Shellac (export and domestic)
segments.commentary: Export business is about ₹100 crore and domestic about ₹40 crore; management expects this to keep growing and to be a source of FY27 growth.

segments.name: Branded / value-added egg products
segments.commentary: Products include egg in tetra-pack, egg liquid, egg white cube and Egg Pro protein drink. Management reformulated Egg Pro for launch in June, and an R&D division is planned within six months. Revenue from these products has been small so far.

guidance_outlook: Management said the ₹1,000 crore revenue target is for 2030, not FY27.
FY27 powder top-line growth will be modest because the company is at full capacity; shellac and domestic growth expected to add to it.
Q1 FY27 realisation expected to continue near the Q4 level (~₹722/kg powder terms), with some international market changes but no major impact expected.
The ₹400 crore layer-shed capex is a cost-saving, bottom-line investment (not a top-line one) and is expected to be completed by FY28-29, taking the flock from about 20 lakh to 40 lakh birds.
Management said it expects about ₹0.20 per egg of production-cost savings from the new system, and a gross margin of about ₹0.50 per egg.

qa_highlights.question: What were FY26 sales volumes and realisation per kg, and what is the outlook for FY27–28, including the ₹1,000 crore target and the SKM Universal consideration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no exact volume or consideration figures on the call. It said capacity is full, realisation rose through FY26 with a Q4 dip on mix (~₹722/kg powder), and the ₹1,000 crore goal is for 2030. For SKM Universal, the valuation is about ₹37 crore for the whole company; the group already holds 26%, so the 74% stake costs about ₹27.75 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the country-wise revenue split and competitive position, and what is driving elevated egg prices in Japan?
qa_highlights.answer: The country split was declined as it is not public. Competitors are European producers in Japan and Russia. Management said it earns about 5% more than competitors. Price strength was attributed to bird flu culls, which take about two years to repopulate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current capacity, the 400 crore capex timeline, and the value-added product plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Flock is moving toward 40 lakh birds by 2028-29. The capex is a cost-saving investment, not a revenue driver. Management is developing value-added products (Egg Pro relaunch, egg white cube) and an R&D unit. Shellac export and domestic are also growing.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Indian producers not consistently profitable outside bird flu cycles, and how are contracts priced and hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bird-flu disruptions are sporadic and under control, with vaccination under discussion with the government. Contracts are mostly 3–6 months, priced on cost and competition, and the forex hedge is currently only about 30%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected ROC on the new EC-shed project and what drives FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exact ROC figures would follow later. It said the project cuts production cost by about ₹0.20 per egg. FY27 growth is expected to be small in powder and larger in shellac and domestic sales.

qa_highlights.question: How does the USD–EUR rate affect other expenses, and will the investor presentation be shared?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe is a small share of business and most pricing is in USD. Russia is invoiced in rupees and rubles, and Japan from H2. The presentation will be uploaded to the website.

risks_watch: Bird flu outbreaks drive the price cycle in both directions; India's current situation is described as sporadic, but a major outbreak would affect supply and realisation.

Power outages were noted during the call, and the new capex is roughly 2.5 times the company's FY26 PAT. Funding relies on a ₹302 crore bank loan, and the ₹403 crore cost may change with foreign-currency payments.
Only about 30% of forex exposure is hedged at present, against a normal 60–70%.

Management said it cannot share country-wise revenue, so the market concentration risk (Japan, Russia, Europe) cannot be assessed.

532143|2026-06.headline: SKM Egg Products' Q1 FY27 realisation rose to about Rs 770/kg from Rs 722 last quarter, while management flagged feed-cost pressure lasting at least two more quarters.
532143|2026-06.overview: Management said the company is running near full capacity, so volume growth is capped and results depend on international egg product prices, exchange rates and feed costs. Realisation was stated at about Rs 770 per unit against Rs 722 last quarter, mainly helped by the rupee, while margins were hit by a substantial rise in soya-based feed costs. Management said the company is moving into domestic branded eggs, with a business plan due by end-March, and is adding easy-shed capacity with completion targeted for November-December 2028. Capex approval for further expansion is expected at the next board meeting, with a target of October. The call was largely Q&A; no formal presentation was given, and several answers were vague on numbers.

segments.name: Egg powder (export)
segments.commentary: Realisation about Rs 770 per unit this quarter; management guided that the quarterly average will likely stay above Rs 700, with a range of Rs 720-750 cited. Russia shipments run about 150 tons per month.

segments.name: Branded eggs (domestic, new)
segments.commentary: Structure set up after the company took over a brand company; business plan due by end-March. Management said margins are lower than egg products and gave no brand EBITDA or revenue figure beyond the Rs 40-50 crore turnover expected this year.

segments.name: Easy sheds / egg production
segments.commentary: About 20 lakh birds planned; first four sheds completed earlier, all to be complete by November-December 2028. Management said the cost advantage is at least 5% of overall production cost, from higher productivity and feed efficiency.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth limited by capacity for the rest of FY27; the company is running at full capacity.
Feed-cost pressure expected to persist for at least two more quarters, per management.
International egg white prices seen as stable, with possible improvement of 2-3/4 for egg white; inventory positions still high.
Japan office approval delayed one to two months for resubmission; new business expected in the second half of the year.
Next board meeting in October expected to approve a further expansion plan (capex timing, capacity numbers not given).

Backward integration and plant expansion referenced; management has not disclosed capacity numbers.

Phased capex to come in FY28 and FY29; capacity by end FY27 or FY28 not disclosed on the call.

Russia war reported as not affecting exports; Iran-related shipping disruption led to about 6-7 containers being returned from Dubai and re-airlifted.

qa_highlights.question: What is the contribution and margin of branded products?

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost savings from easy sheds?

532143|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 turnover ~363 crore vs 380 crore, PAT ~40 crore flat; Q2 PAT fell to ~16 crore as feed raw material costs rose.
532143|2026-09.overview: Management described H1 FY27 as broadly flat year on year: turnover about 363 crore versus 380 crore, EBITDA about 67-44 crore (transcript reads "6744 crores", unclear) and PAT about 40 crore in both periods. Q2 turnover rose to about 184 crore from 179 crore in Q1, but EBITDA fell to about 28 crore from 38 crore as feed raw material costs increased. Q2 PBT was about 22 crore (32 crore in Q1) and PAT about 16 crore (24 crore in Q1). Management guided to a 100 crore-plus profit for the full year but declined to give quarterly guidance, and the company is in a heavy capex phase funded largely by term debt.

segments.name: Egg powder / egg products
segments.commentary: Powder sales were 1,625 MT in Q2 versus 1,831 MT in Q1, and 3,457 MT in H1 versus 4,289 MT in the prior-year half. Average realisation was cited at about 700 rupees per unit, with management expecting 700-plus in H2 and volumes slightly better.

segments.name: Domestic shell eggs / branded eggs
segments.commentary: Management said it currently sells about 1.5 lakh eggs a day in the branded egg segment and targets 5 lakh eggs a day in two to three years. Business model, segment (premium vs mass) and pricing are still under internal discussion, with a decision expected in about three months.

segments.name: SKM Universal (wholly owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Board approved merger of SKM Universal into the listed company; it will cease to exist by April next year. Management said scale-up plans begin in FY28, and a 17.5 crore goodwill-like item in Q2 was described as a share purchase cost from a sister company.

guidance_outlook: Full-year PAT of 100 crore-plus reiterated, described as a ballpark figure; no quarterly guidance given, citing SEBI limits and export volatility.
Next six months expected to continue the past six months with a small margin improvement; more aggressive growth expected from next financial year.
Average realisations not expected to correct significantly over the next six months; Japan pricing reduced due to US oversupply, with pressure elsewhere limited.
Real sales increment from the expanded capacity expected from FY28-FY29; no top-line or bottom-line numbers given.
Dividend payout to be maintained at about 25% even during the high-investment and debt phase.
capex_capacity: EC (layer) farm phase two: 2.4 million birds target by September 28; first rearing house expected complete in about two weeks, chicks to be placed from November 15; project running about one week behind schedule.
Board approved term loan of nearly 300 crore (200 crore State Bank, 100 crore Access Bank); documents to be signed the following week.
Powder capacity expansion from 7,000 to 10,000+ tons at about 180 crore (30 crore margin, about 150 crore term loan at 8.25%), with capacity commissioning around H2 FY28 and 3-5 years to fill.
Management described total debt for the investment phase as about 450 crore.
Cash of about 167 crore held; management said about 100 crore is kept as a minimum for seasonality.
demand_pricing: US oversupply of eggs is reducing prices in Japan; management said pressure elsewhere has been limited and international prices are set by global competitors (Europe, Ukraine, South America, Mexico), not by Indian costs.

Feed raw material (soya and other ingredients) costs rose sharply in Q2; the company cannot fix prices in contracts and has no pass-through mechanism. Management could not confirm pass-through to customers.
Management plans to import soya for about six months of requirement, expected to be about 10% cheaper than local prices; implementation expected in a week or two.
South Korea: two customers have approved samples; bigger trial shipment is under way, with a first order targeted for October-December quarter.
Freight costs rose due to the US-Iran conflict and the Ukraine-Russia war; management said the rupee depreciation offsets part of this and demand has not been affected.

qa_highlights.question: What are realisations outlook for the next six months, and will domestic sales drive growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said US oversupply has hit Japan pricing only; average realisation is about 700 rupees and not expected to correct much. Grading equipment arrives by April, and a relaunch strategy will follow, with the business model still under discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Will profit stay around 100 crore for the year, and can raw material inflation be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is very confident of repeating 100-plus crore this year. It said international prices are set by global competition, not Indian cost, so pass-through is uncertain; soya imports and backward integration are the offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Will quarterly profits exceed 16 crore in the next two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give quarterly projections, saying it did not think SEBI permits it, and reiterated only the 100 crore-plus ballpark for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the expansion receive interest subvention, and what capex is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: The 3% interest subvention applies only to farm investment, not egg processing. Powder expansion is about 180 crore with 150 crore term loan at 8.25%; benefits from the farms come gradually and fully by September 28.

qa_highlights.question: Why hold about 167 crore cash while borrowing 300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company keeps about 100 crore for seasonality and that its cost of funds is about 5.25% after 3% interest subvention; it targets returns above 10% on surplus cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will branded domestic eggs become a substantial part of turnover within two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects it to become an important revenue stream within two to five years, but segment choice (premium, mid, or mass) is still being decided and should be firmed up in about three months.

Japanese price pressure from US oversupply and softening international egg-powder prices.
EC farm commissioning slippage (already about one week behind) and the 2.4 million bird target by September 28.

Freight cost increases from geopolitical events; South Korea first order targeted October-December.

532149|2026-06.headline: Bank of India Q1 FY27 net profit rose 36.23% YoY to Rs 3,068 crore; Global NIM eased to 2.52% and FY27 guidance was kept unchanged.
532149|2026-06.overview: Bank of India reported Q1 FY27 net profit of Rs 3,068 crore, up 36.23% YoY, with operating profit up 25.99% to Rs 5,051 crore and NII up 12.61% to Rs 6,833 crore. Asset quality improved on a YoY basis, with Gross NPA at 1.81% and Net NPA at 0.51%, and slippage ratio at 0.24%. Global business grew 16.57% YoY to Rs 17.55 lakh crore, with advances up 18.64%. Management reiterated FY27 guidance for advances growth of 15-16% and deposit growth of 13-14%, and raised a dollar-funding target of $4.2 billion through FCNR(B), OFCB/MTN and ECB routes by December 2026.

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -111 bps YoY; NNPA -24 bps YoY

segments.commentary: Global business Rs 17.55 lakh crore (+16.57% YoY). Global deposits Rs 9.58 lakh crore (+14.90%); domestic deposits Rs 8.25 lakh crore (+16.15%). CASA Rs 3.02 lakh crore, CASA ratio 36.68%.

segments.name: Advances
segments.commentary: Global gross advances Rs 7.98 lakh crore (+18.64% YoY); domestic advances Rs 6.74 lakh crore (+19.20%). RAM advances Rs 3.93 lakh crore (+19.75%), 58.30% of advances.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book about Rs 57,000 crore at yield of about 9.10%, growing about 52% YoY; NPA below Rs 100 crore.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: International business touched about Rs 2.56 lakh crore; around 32% of international loan book is trade finance, which management plans to reduce.

segments.commentary: Bank of India mutual fund AUM about Rs 16,000-17,000 crore; no near-term plan for public issue.

Cost-to-income ratio at about 46% in Q1, but guided to 48%-49% on a consistent basis during FY27.
ROA guidance of 1% and above on a consistent quarter-on-quarter basis in FY27 (Q4 FY26 1.01%, Q1 FY27 about 1%).
FCNR(B) target of $1.2 billion by 30 September 2026; OFCB/MTN target about $2 billion by 31 December 2026; ECB target about $1 billion; total dollar raising about $4.2 billion by December 2026.

FCNR(B) deposits: about $200 million garnered so far; three-year FCNR at 6.25%, 3-4 year at 6.30%, five-year at 6.50%; leverage product up to nine times; management cited a spread of about 50 bps on five-year deposits, with CRR/SLR not applicable.
Management declined to give current leverage spread, citing a moving target in borrowing and dollar rates; leveraged share of FCNR not quantified.
Personal loans grew only about 3% YoY after guardrails were put on low-ticket and non-salaried personal loans.
ECLGS: about Rs 6,000 crore sanctioned, Rs 4,600 crore disbursed; expected total sanctions and disbursal of about Rs 8,000 crore by scheme end.
SMA-0 for accounts of Rs 5 crore and above fell to about Rs 4,090 crore (0.52% of standard book), from about Rs 4,700 crore at March 2026 and above Rs 7,000 crore at June 2025.
Q1 fresh slippages including incremental NPA debits about Rs 1,800 crore vs Rs 2,100 crore in Q1 FY26; sectors under watch include chemicals, ceramics and oil/gas importers/exporters.
PSL income about Rs 277 crore in Q1; management said further PSL income possible in Q2 and Q3 but gave no number.

qa_highlights.question: Is stress visible in MSME and small loan accounts from the West Asia crisis, and what is the ECLGS position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SMA and slippages show no major stress; ECLGS sanctions of about Rs 6,000 crore with Rs 4,600 crore disbursed, expected to reach about Rs 8,000 crore. Certain sectors are being monitored closely.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FCNR, OFCB/MTN and ECB plan and how does the leverage product work?
qa_highlights.answer: FCNR(B) target is $1.2 billion by 30 September; OFCB/MTN about $2 billion by 31 December; ECB about $1 billion (about $500 million already approved in principle). Leverage product is up to nine times, with three-year FCNR at 6.25%.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan strategy and growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loan book about Rs 57,000 crore at about 9.10% yield, growing about 52% YoY; NPA below Rs 100 crore; three-notice, 90-day auction SOP applied.

qa_highlights.question: Why did personal loans grow only 3%, and what is the credit card plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Guardrails were put on low-ticket and non-salaried personal loans, shifting to salaried and service-sector borrowers with NACH. Credit card base target is 3 lakh by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CASA and retail term deposit ratios fall while cost of deposits dropped 15 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a roughly 3% fall in CASA and retail term deposit share, as bulk deposits above Rs 3 crore were used to fund credit growth; cost of deposits was reduced via Rs 3-25 crore FD campaign and mix changes.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIM and CIR hold, and how will yields on advances move?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is NIM 2.55%-2.60% and CIR 48%-49% for FY27. Yields on advances expected to pause falling, supported by MCLR-linked loans, mid-corporate growth and reduced low-margin trade finance.

Treasury gains in Q1 may not repeat as yields move adversely.

532149|2026-09.headline: Bank of India Q2 FY27: H1 net profit about Rs 6,000 crore, Global NIM 2.47%, Gross NPA 1.60%; ECL front-loading planned from Q3, about 0.5% CRAR impact per year.
532149|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong YoY growth: global business up 21.13% to Rs 18.92 lakh crore, and global advances up 20.58%. Operating profit rose 33.18% to Rs 5,089 crore and net profit rose 25.32% to Rs 3,202 crore for Sept'26 (the Q2 figure as stated on the call). Asset quality improved, with Gross NPA at 1.60% and Net NPA at 0.42%, and credit cost fell to 0.12% from 0.15% in June'26. Global NIM eased 5 bps YoY to 2.47%, which management attributed mainly to FCNR-linked leverage. financial_highlights.change: +Rs 20,539 crore YoY; ratio down from prior quarters
down 5 bps from 2.52% (management cited Sept'25 at 2.41%)

segments.name: Corporate and pipeline
segments.commentary: Corporate pipeline about Rs 65,000 crore as of 30 Sept; total pipeline across corporate, RAM, digital, pool/co-lending and supply chain about Rs 86,000-87,000 crore. segments.name: RAM
segments.commentary: RAM advances up 18.68% YoY to Rs 4.13 lakh crore, 58.63% of gross advances, with RAM pipeline about Rs 20,000 crore.

segments.name: Supply chain / trade
segments.commentary: Supply chain book just over Rs 1,000 crore, with a Rs 1,500 crore first-year target; trade and MSME-linked assets grew about 10% in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 global advances growth guided at 15-16% and global deposit growth at 16-17%.

Recovery in written-off accounts expected to sustain the run rate of about Rs 900-1,000 crore a quarter; non-interest income expected to hold above Rs 2,500 crore a quarter.
