532285|2026-06.headline: Geojit Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR160.4 crore and PAT to INR19.8 crore, but management guided to continued cost pressure and no hiring for several quarters.
532285|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR160.40 crore, up 11% YoY, with PBT of INR25.99 crore (up 4% QoQ) and PAT of INR19.83 crore (up 14% QoQ). Employee cost rose INR18 crore on sales force expansion, DIFC hiring, tech team additions and higher incentives, though management said employee cost would normalise after a lower insurance-incentive quarter. Customer assets reached INR1.11 lakh crore (up 15% QoQ), mostly from market appreciation, with recurring assets at INR26,000 crore. Management said margin benefits from FY26 investments would take a couple more quarters, and that hiring has been paused except for replacements due to Middle East conflict and market conditions. Leadership succession was also confirmed, with Jones George becoming MD from 1 October.

qa_highlights.question: Why do investors choose Geojit given weak PAT over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Geojit focuses on delivery and MF trail income rather than F&O. It expects margins to improve in coming quarters, not immediately.

532286|2026-03.headline: Jindal Steel Q4 FY26 consolidated adjusted EBITDA was INR 2,647 crores (INR 10,093/t) on ASP up INR 4,743/t QoQ, with FY27 sales guided at 10.5–11 Mt.
532286|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sharp sequential recovery: consolidated gross revenue rose 28% QoQ to INR 19,399 crores and adjusted EBITDA reached INR 2,647 crores, helped by a rise in HRC and TMT rebar prices and Angul volume ramp-up. Sales volume grew 15% QoQ to 2.62 Mt as the Angul expansion took steelmaking capacity to 15.6 Mtpa from 9.6 Mtpa. A one-time impairment of INR 1,433 crores (standalone) and INR 834 crores (consolidated) was booked on the Australian WCL asset after the shaft was closed. Management said the major capex programme is essentially complete and the focus shifts to asset sweating and deleveraging.

segments.name: Steel (India, Angul/Raigarh/Patratu)
segments.commentary: FY26 production 9.25 Mt (+14% YoY) and sales 8.68 Mt (+9% YoY). Q4 production 2.65 Mt (+6% QoQ, +26% YoY) and sales 2.62 Mt (+15% QoQ, +23% YoY). Flat/long mix was 52:48 in Q4 and 49:51 for FY26.

segments.name: Raw materials / overseas mines
segments.commentary: Iron ore sourcing about 60% outside purchases and 40% captive, with pricing described as stable. Mozambique is EBITDA positive, South Africa operating but not EBITDA positive, and Australia is closed with minimal cash burn.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: 1,050 MW Shree Bhoomi power plant commissioned (two 525 MW modules); ramp-up to complete within H1 FY27. Surplus power to be sold but described as not material to financials.

Q1 FY27 coking coal prices expected to rise by USD 20–25/t sequentially; iron ore movement of plus/minus INR 100–150/t per month.
Slurry pipeline (Barbil–Angul) to be commissioned in Q1 FY27; savings of about INR 700/t of iron ore, or INR 750–1,000/t of steel as it ramps up.
Port facility to be commissioned; DRI-2 (2 Mtpa) expected towards end of FY27; PP2 also remaining.
Capex guidance of INR 7,500–10,000 crores for expansion and sustenance capex; remaining programme capex INR 11,545 crores.
Leverage expected to normalise by Q2 FY27; value-added flat mix expected to move from about 50% toward 70%.

532300|2026-03.overview: Management hosted an investor meet on 4 June 2026 (disclosed 11 June) after the US FDA approval of Zaynich (cefepime-zidebactam), described as the first Indian-discovered research product approved by the FDA. FY26 revenue was INR3,373 crore, EBITDA about INR630 crore (margin about 18.6%, up from about 5.4% three years earlier) and profit before tax INR238 crore. Management framed the next phase as scaling growth: US launch of Zaynich via an operationally light model, India and emerging-market launches, and biosimilar diabetes expansion. Most numbers were given verbally; no quarterly figures or formal guidance were disclosed in the presentation.

segments.name: Pharma core (India, UK, Ireland)
segments.commentary: About 75% of business; UK is top-five with 18% covered-market share and focuses on specialty injectables. India driven by diabetes, orthopedics, pain and regenerative medicine (Emrok, Miqnaf).

segments.name: Biosimilars / biotech (diabetes)
segments.commentary: Grew 27% in FY26; human insulin output scaled 2x and glargine 1.5x. Two products commercialised, five in pipeline (aspart, RN 30/70, degludec, degludec aspart, semaglutide); registered in 30 emerging markets.

segments.name: Novel antibiotics (Zaynich, Emrok, Miqnaf, Odrate)
segments.commentary: Specialty (biosimilars plus novel antibiotics) is 23% of business. Zaynich has US FDA and CDSCO India approvals; US launch planned with leadership hired and a commercial operating partner; European approval expected by end of calendar 2026.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: 28% of turnover, growing 35%, supported by partnerships in Brazil, Thailand, Algeria and Malaysia. Plans to launch Zaynich in seven to eight high-carbapenem-resistance markets within 18 to 24 months.

guidance_outlook: Zaynich global peak sales of $1.5-2 billion per year, with US roughly 40% of global revenue; country-wise split not given.
Revenue ramp expected to be slow initially (hockey-stick pattern), with breakeven in 12 to 18 months in the Zaynich business; first 12-18 months may see a slight loss, per the Chairman.
Zaynich US price expected at roughly $1,200-1,500 per day, with India pricing about 75-80% below US; Europe and US pricing described as price-neutral versus existing antibiotics.
Long-term target of about 20-25% share of resistant cases globally; India possibly higher.
Biosimilar business expected to double in 24-36 months; capacity to double in 12-15 months; five pipeline products to launch about two years out.
Capex of INR200-300 crore over next three years, primarily for biologicals capacity; R&D spend to stay at similar percentage of sales.
Foviscu DCGI filing expected in two to three months; approval timing not predictable. Odrate is about four years away and Phase 2 waiver not expected.
capex_capacity: Planned capex of INR200-300 crore over the next three years, mainly for biologicals capacity.
Biosimilar capacity to double within 12-15 months.

Zaynich manufacturing: US supply from an FDA-approved European site; India supply from Indian facility; emerging markets to be supplied from either India or Europe depending on timelines (Europe could save six to nine months).
Company has 11 manufacturing facilities and two R&D centres in-house.
Management said US, Europe and emerging markets filings are submitted or in progress, with European approval expected by end of 2026.
demand_pricing: US cUTI is the largest of about 1.2 million US gram-negative hospital infections (about 600,000 cUTI cases); management cited about 20-25% readmission rate for cUTI.
India: about 600,000-700,000 gram-negative infection patients, with 35-45% estimated carbapenem resistance (ICMR surveillance caveated by regional variation).
Phase 3 vs meropenem: composite cure rate 96.8%, about 20% higher than meropenem per management.
Management said new anti-infectives in the US market total about $1 billion; the company does not plan to create new demand but to take share, with price neutrality.
Competition: cefiderocol (Fetroja) cited as the closest competitor; management claimed Zaynich has a better efficacy and safety profile, without numerical head-to-head data.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue from Zaynich over the next 6 to 24 months, and capex and commercial costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman expects slow initial revenue growth, a hockey-stick curve after 12-18 months, INR200-300 crore capex over three years, and no capex for sales build-out, only revenue cost. Breakeven expected in 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Does Zaynich qualify for the 10% PLI and what is the China strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Government funding recognised but immaterial versus R&D spend. China: Chinese patients in trial were insufficient; a small China study is ongoing and a partner may be sought.

qa_highlights.question: Will Zaynich be made in Europe for the US and in India for emerging markets?
qa_highlights.answer: US supply from an FDA-inspected European site as a de-risking step; India supply from India; emerging markets from India or Europe depending on timelines.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Wockhardt exit US generics and will it re-enter?
qa_highlights.answer: US generics were about 5% of the portfolio and loss-making, amid the 2012-13 FDA import alert. Management said it is re-entering with innovative products sourced from European manufacturers, with India production for India.

qa_highlights.question: Patent life and exclusivity for Zaynich, Emrok and Miqnaf?
qa_highlights.answer: Zaynich patent runs to 2038 in India with further filings planned; Miqnaf patent to early 2033 in India. QIDP status gives five extra years in US; minimum 10-year market exclusivity in US and Western markets.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing and patient targets for FY28-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: US price about $1,200-1,500 per day, typically $10,000-15,000 per course; India priced about 75-80% below US. Long-term share of 20-25% of resistant cases, with no FY28-29 patient numbers given.

qa_highlights.question: Peak sales of Zaynich?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said $1.5-2 billion per year globally at peak, not cumulative, with US around 40% of global revenue.

risks_watch: Commercial execution: a new US sales model for antibiotics with a commercial operating partner, 6,000 US hospitals to segment, and a first-time anti-infective launch for the company.
Losses or breakeven in the first 12-18 months from US launch costs; Chairman's comments on profitability were clarified as Zaynich-only.
Regulatory timing: European approval expected by end-2026, emerging market filings to follow; DCGI approval for Foviscu not predictable.
Label scope: US approval is for cUTI; HAP/VAP and other indications need a further trial, so off-label use is a question.
Zaynich Phase 2 waiver for the aztreonam combination (Odrate) not expected; Odrate timing about four years.
Hospital segment profitability and ROCE targets were not answered (hospitals deemed out of scope; ROCE question deflected).
532300|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and promotional on Zaynich and the R&D pipeline, with forward-looking claims (peak sales, market share) given without detailed assumptions. Evasive or deflective on ROCE, hospitals, Foviscu timing and China specifics, and on country-wise revenue split.
key_quotes: Wockhardt, as you know, in the last few days, is now the first Indian company to have an Indian research product approved with the US FDA, Zaynich.
So, it is in your financial terms you say investment, I mean, asset-light and capital-heavy.
We will stick to only antibiotic research for next 10 years.
Peak sales per year.

financial_highlights.change: about 35% in last year per Q&A

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides a Zaynich launch that is a slight loss for the first 12-18 months, with bottom-line breakeven in 12-18 months, so launch costs weigh on margins even though FY26 EBITDA margin was about 18.6% (up from about 5.4% three years ago).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management guided biosimilar capacity to double within 12-15 months, with human insulin output already scaled 2x and glargine 1.5x, backed by INR200-300 crore capex over three years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Biosimilar and biotech grew 27% in FY26 and emerging markets (28% of turnover) are growing 35%, with Zaynich US launch planned, though Zaynich revenue ramp is expected to be slow initially (hockey-stick after 12-18 months).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of INR200-300 crore over three years, mainly biologicals, is already firmly planned; utilisation was not disclosed, so further capex beyond this is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric revenue or margin guidance for FY27 was given, and the Zaynich peak sales of $1.5-2 billion are long-dated, so an upgrade depends on early US launch traction that has not yet been reported.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Execution risk is high: first-time anti-infective launch in the US via a commercial partner, a 6,000-hospital segmentation task, Foviscu DCGI timing not predictable, and an expected Zaynich loss in the first 12-18 months.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Zaynich US launch now; European approval by end-2026; five b
rows.why: Zaynich has US FDA and CDSCO approvals with leadership hired and a commercial partner in place; European approval is expected by end of calendar 2026, and emerging-market launches in seven to eight markets are planned within 18-24 months.

rows.label: Zaynich emerging-market launches in 7-8 high-CRE markets
rows.why: Management plans launches in seven to eight high carbapenem-resistance markets, with emerging markets already 28% of turnover growing 35% and partnerships in Brazil, Thailand, Algeria and Malaysia.

rows.label: Biosimilar business doubling
rows.why: Management expects the biosimilar business to double in 24-36 months after growing 27% in FY26, with 2 products commercialised and 5 in the pipeline registered in 30 emerging markets.

rows.label: Foviscu DCGI approval
rows.when: filing in 2-3 months; approval timing unpredictable
rows.why: Filing is expected in two to three months, but management would not predict approval timing, so this is a binary timing risk.

tone.note: Management was confident on Zaynich peak sales of $1.5-2 billion, the biosimilar doubling and the 20-25% resistant-case share, but was evasive on ROCE, hospitals, Foviscu timing, China and the country-wise revenue split, while analysts pressed on Zaynich revenue, losses and capex.

532305|2026-06.headline: Ind-Swift Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 2.85x YoY to ₹33.32 crore, a 17.91% margin, with management guiding to 20%+ from Q3.
532305|2026-06.overview: Operating income grew 21.16% YoY to ₹186.08 crore and operating EBITDA reached ₹33.32 crore (17.91% margin, up 1258 bps). PAT excluding exceptional items was ₹24.68 crore (13.26% margin vs 4.99%). Management attributed the step-up to exit of litigation and other costs borne by the formulation business after the merger, and to a higher own-brand export mix. CDMO contracts with Viatris, Manx and Arrotex were commercialised in the quarter but contributed only about ₹5-6 crore so far, with ramp-up expected from Q2 and Q3. Management reiterated FY27 export sales of about ₹750 crore and ₹1200 crore revenue by FY29, and declined to revise targets at this stage.

segments.name: Export own-brands
segments.commentary: 57.20% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 48% in Q1 FY26; management cites this mix shift as a key margin driver. Export gross margin was stated at about 55%.

segments.name: Export contract manufacturing (CDMO)
segments.commentary: 26.64% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 29% a year earlier. Viatris, Manx and Arrotex partnerships commercialised in the quarter, with about ₹5-6 crore booked from Viatris products (Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules) so far.

segments.name: Domestic segments
segments.commentary: Branded generics 6.41%, ethical 6.14% and domestic contract manufacturing 3.61% of Q1 FY27 sales, all lower than a year ago. Management describes these as a stable cash-generation base; domestic sales are seasonal.

segments.name: Product portfolio
segments.commentary: Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin was about ₹25 crore in Q1 FY27 per management, partnered with Tiffen-Becker. FY26 revenue: Atorvastatin ₹85.50 crore, Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin ₹80.78 crore, Fexofenadine ₹74.32 crore, Quetiapine ₹19.75 crore, Famciclovir ₹18.64 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 export sales target of about ₹750 crore, with roughly 45% from CDMO (per management).

FY29 revenue target of ₹1200 crore; management said it is not revising this yet and will revisit by year-end. Mentioned FY27 expectation of about ₹900 crore and a longer-term aspiration of ₹1500 crore revenue and ~₹200 crore net profit by FY30.
EBITDA margin of 18% described as sustainable; management expects to move above 20% from Q3 FY27 (Q2 internally targeted), potentially 21-22% with sequential sales growth.
Viatris CDMO volumes expected to double in Q2 versus Q1; Arrotex Macrogol push expected in Q2, and Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules to contribute in Q3-Q4.
Medium-term growth of 20-25% CAGR referenced, with EBITDA margins above 18% (management answered 'yes').
Dossiers to reach 400+ additions, taking the total from 2,100 to about 2,500 by Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: About ₹250 crore of cash to be deployed in capex over roughly 2 to 2.5 years across a new warehouse, capacity enhancement at the existing facility, and the Jammu facility (EU-GMP/PIC/S audit under way).
Samba facility upgrade to EU-GMP and PIC/S standards in progress as planned.
Capacity utilisation for Ibuprofen and granules about 70% in Q1 per management; management expects 90% utilisation of planned FY29 capacity over time.
Capex for a potential new CDMO customer deal estimated at ₹50-75 crore, with revenue of ₹150+ crore expected.
R&D working on 5-6 molecules for FY27-29; capex to follow only after filings are completed. New R&D land bought in Panchkula area.
demand_pricing: CDMO economics: Viatris paid about USD 2 million for development work, to be reimbursed through orders.
Selection criteria for new products include a minimum 50-55% gross margin and customer confidence in R&D delivery. Candidate molecules include Rosuvastatin, Mirabegron, Sitagliptin and Empagliflozin.
Tiffen-Becker arrangement: transfer-priced supply with about 43% of the customer's margin shared with Ind-Swift.
Management expects no dearth of capacity for the planned growth; new partnerships under discussion with 3-4 existing overseas customers, not expected to contribute this year.

qa_highlights.question: What was the CDMO contribution in Q1 and what growth to expect from the Viatris partnership over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Gagan Aggarwal said Viatris products (Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules) booked only about ₹5-6 crore in Q1, with growth reflecting in Q2 and Q3. He said about ₹100-130 crore is expected from these two products, not the full ₹200 crore in year one, and that it would build over about two years.

qa_highlights.question: What are export margins for CDMO and own-brands, and how will the ₹250 crore cash and Synthimed stake be used?
qa_highlights.answer: Export gross margin is about 55%. The ₹250 crore cash will be deployed as capex over about 2.5 years (warehouse, existing capacity, Jammu). No plans to divest the Synthimed stake this year; Synthimed budgeted EBITDA is about ₹750 crore and Q1 results are on track.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 18% EBITDA margin sustainable, and could it rise further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 18% is fully sustainable and could reach 21-22% if sales grow quarter on quarter. It denied calling Q1 a turnaround, citing litigation and other costs borne by the formulation business for about 1.5 years that are now over.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY29 revenue guidance of ₹1200 crore not being raised, and when does growth come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will not revise at this stage and will revisit by year-end. Growth is H2-weighted via Arrotex Macrogol in Q2 and Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules in Q3-Q4. FY27 expectation is about ₹900 crore, with export sales of about ₹750 crore, roughly 45% from CDMO.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the API business sold and what R&D capability was retained?
qa_highlights.answer: The API business was sold to Synthimed in FY24 for net about ₹2000-2100 crore, used to repay group debt of about ₹1250-1300 crore. Retained R&D in Panchkula handles regulatory compliance, tech transfer and global filings, with new land bought for a further R&D facility.

qa_highlights.question: What is capacity utilisation and will there be a capacity shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Ibuprofen and granules ran at about 70% in Q1 on pilot batches. Management expects 90% utilisation of the FY29 plan over time and sees no capacity dearth. Capex for new molecules will follow only after filings are complete.

risks_watch: CDMO ramp-up timing: Viatris volumes are guided to double in Q2 from a ₹5-6 crore base, and Arrotex Macrogol and Ibuprofen and granules contributions depend on Q2-Q4 execution.
Margin trajectory: management targets above 20% EBITDA margin from Q3 FY27 (Q2 internally), against 17.91% in Q1; a shortfall would challenge the 21-22% view.
Capacity and capex: ₹250 crore capex over about 2-2.5 years, Jammu and Samba EU-GMP/PIC/S audits in progress, and the new CDMO deal needs ₹50-75 crore capex; delays could cap FY28-29 revenue.
Revenue guidance: FY27 about ₹900 crore and FY29 ₹1200 crore; management says it will revisit by year-end, so the next quarter's run-rate matters.
Synthimed stake: ~7.8% holding, no divestment planned this year, tag-along right on any PE exit; monetisation timing is open.
Customer concentration and unnamed partners: two new overseas CDMO deals and 3-4 existing customers are under discussion but not named; 'the war' is cited as slowing signings.
Several questions were deferred (market size, Q1 capacity utilisation, new registrations, packaging differentiation), so follow-ups via IR are pending.
key_quotes: Yes, yes, 18% is fully sustainable and we plan if the sales we are able to increase quarter-on-quarter they might go up to 21 to 22%.
Sir, not at this stage. Maybe after if we are able to achieve our, overachieve our results this financial year, we may revise this.
So that ₹250 crores will be deployed in capex over a period of 2.5 years approx.
We don't want to spend a single penny in R&D before we sign off any agreement with our customers.
532305|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on margins and the export mix, stating 18% EBITDA margin is fully sustainable and describing the quarter as an excellent start. Cautious on guidance, declining to revise the ₹1200 crore FY29 target and avoiding firm commitments on the 20% margin timing, the new partnerships and the CDMO revenue split. Evasive on several detailed questions, including market size, Q1 capacity utilisation, partner names and new registrations, which were deferred to follow-up.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin 17.91% (up from 5.33%) with own-brand exports at 57.20% of sales vs 48%, export gross margin ~55%, and management guiding above 20% from Q3 FY27 and 21-22% if sales grow sequentially; not yet proven and Q1 margin was helped by exit of litigation and other costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About ₹250 cr capex over 2-2.5 years for new warehouse, existing-facility capacity enhancement and Jammu, plus a ₹50-75 cr capex for a potential new CDMO deal, but the capacity additions are not dated to a specific quarter and utilisation is only ~70%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to ~₹900 cr and export sales ~₹750 cr (~45% CDMO), with Viatris volumes guided to double in Q2 from a ₹5-6 cr base and Arrotex Macrogol in Q2, but Q1 CDMO contribution was small and FY27 implies a step-up from ₹186 cr in Q1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex already raised to ~₹250 cr and a ₹50-75 cr CDMO-specific capex is pending a new customer deal, but Ibuprofen/granules utilisation is ~70% and management said no capacity dearth, so a fresh board-level capex is conditional on signing new deals.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to revise FY29 ₹1200 cr target and will revisit only by year-end; the CDMO revenue split and partner signings are still unconfirmed, with only ₹5-6 cr CDMO booked in Q1.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: CDMO ramp is back-end loaded (Ibuprofen/Clarithromycin in Q3-Q4, ~₹100-130 cr from Viatris over two years vs ₹200 cr year-one expectation) and 'the war' is cited as slowing new signings, so FY27 ₹900 cr could slip if Q2-Q3 run-rate lags.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Arrotex Macrogol push in Q2, Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules in Q3-Q4, and 5-6 R&D molecules for FY27-29 (Rosuvastatin, Mirabegron, Sitagliptin, Empagliflozin candidates) with dossiers rising from 2,100 to ~2,500 by Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Viatris CDMO volume doubling in Q2
rows.why: Viatris volumes guided to double in Q2 from ₹5-6 cr booked in Q1, with Viatris CDMO expected to contribute ~₹100-130 cr over about two years.

rows.label: New overseas CDMO partnerships
rows.when: not expected to contribute this year
rows.why: Two new overseas CDMO deals and partnerships with 3-4 existing customers are under discussion, unnamed, and management said they are not expected to contribute this year.

rows.label: Synthimed stake monetisation
rows.why: Stake ~7.8%; management said no divestment planned this year, though tag-along right exists on any PE exit and Synthimed budgeted EBITDA ~₹750 cr.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 18% margin being sustainable and on the export mix, but cautious on guidance: it declined to revise the ₹1200 cr FY29 target, gave no firm date on the 20% margin, and deferred questions on market size, Q1 utilisation, partner names and registrations; analysts pushed o

532309|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 PBT from continuing operations hit INR 119 crore, but one-offs (incl. ~INR 44 crore BHEL ECL reversal) drove much of it; underlying FY26 EBITDA margin 11%.
532309|2026-03.overview: GE Power India reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 316 crore (up from INR 266 crore YoY) and FY26 revenue of INR 1,269 crore (up 21%), led by Core Services (+14%) and Upgrades (+24%). Profit before tax and exceptional items from continuing operations was INR 119 crore in Q4 versus a loss of INR 15 crore a year earlier, and INR 340 crore for FY26 versus INR 22 crore, with management flagging sizeable one-offs in both periods. Order intake fell sharply to INR 877 crore for FY26 from INR 2,183 crore, and order backlog declined to INR 1,628 crore from INR 2,662 crore, mainly due to termination of FGD-EP contracts. Management is pushing a service-led, short-cycle strategy, has settled with BHEL and Jaypee, and has signed a Durgapur demerger to JSW Energy, with a recommended dividend of INR 7 per share (70% of face value).

segments.name: Core Services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 14% YoY and core orders rose 32% YoY; Core Services order backlog up about 40% YoY. Management says about 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book executes in FY27 (12-month cycles).

segments.name: Upgrades
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 24% YoY, driven by upgrade volumes in Q4; Vindhyachal and Wanakbori complex upgrade orders of INR 591 crore were booked in FY25.

segments.name: New Build / FGD EPC (AQCS)
segments.commentary: In close-out mode; FGD-EP contracts of Jaypee Bina and Nigrie (INR 775 crore) were terminated, driving backlog decline. Seven operational acceptances and four unit completions achieved in FY26.

segments.name: Durgapur manufacturing (discontinued)
segments.commentary: Being demerged to JSW Energy; asset of about 660 acres, reported losses in recent quarters. Five-year JSW supply and capacity agreement signed to protect core services manufacturing needs.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give numeric FY27 guidance; CFO said the FY26 underlying EBITDA base (11%) is set and FY27 margins should be at par or better, without a range.
About 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book (INR 1,628 crore) expected to execute in FY27, implying roughly INR 1,380-1,470 crore; this is a management estimate from the call, not formal guidance.
Durgapur demerger to JSW Energy: filed with NCLT; target completion in calendar 2026, and within 12 months of 31 Mar 2026 at the latest.
Core Services target addressable fleet of about INR 3,500-4,000 crore; company holds about 18% share and aims to grow it before considering other areas.
Management says the ECL impact from the BHEL settlement is fully recognised as of 31 Mar 2026, so no similar reversal is expected in FY27.
capex_capacity: Durgapur manufacturing facility to be demerged to JSW Energy; a five-year agreement with JSW covers reserved manufacturing capacity and supply for core services boiler components.
Management aims to build an alternate supply chain for boiler components within about 18 months to become independent of JSW after the five-year agreement.
Three PG tests completed for key new-build units and multiple synchronisations and facility closures achieved in FY26.
Eighteen new first-of-its-kind service products ordered during FY26; first-time generator repairs, turbine upgrades and control system solutions delivered.
demand_pricing: Management says thermal plant PLF and availability are rising, increasing services demand; target addressable market quoted at INR 3,500-4,000 crore.
Q4 order intake of INR 254 crore was below the prior-year INR 285 crore (which included INR 52 crore O&M); FY26 orders fell 60% YoY on the FY25 FGD-EP and complex upgrade wins.

FGD mandate: per the July 2025 notification, Category C plants (over 200 GW) were removed and Category A (about 8 GW, mainly Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra) must install FGD; Category B is optional with no tariff pass-through if they opt in. Management says the mandate has limited near-term order impact.
Management is pursuing 13 countries for boilers, including Vietnam, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Indonesia, while stating its perimeter remains India-only for GEPIL and non-GEPIL assets.

qa_highlights.question: Does GEPIL participate in gas turbine, HRSG or combined-cycle business?
qa_highlights.answer: Puneet Bhatla said no; HRSG and gas-plant business belong to GE Vernova's gas business and fall outside GEPIL's objects, which are steam and thermal only.

qa_highlights.question: Of the order book, how much is executable in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Aashish Ghai said short-cycle orders typically complete within 12 months, so about 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book is expected in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will backlog grow after the current book runs off, and is the business widening beyond core?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is new-build close-out. Core backlog is up about 40% YoY; the company plans to grow its 18% share of the INR 3,500-4,000 crore fleet before expanding to other areas.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 450 crore loan and what yield does it earn?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said it is surplus cash lent to a promoter-group cash pool benchmarked to HSBC, with rates of 5.5-6.35% in FY26, about 0.25% above commercial bank deposit rates. Lending is board-approved, shareholder-approved and audited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope of the FGD opportunity and the margin range?
qa_highlights.answer: Roshan Singh outlined the notification: Category A (about 8 GW) must install FGD, Category B is optional, and Category C was removed. He said the mandate has limited weight for GEPIL unless utilities act proactively. No margin range was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR 880 crore net cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Puneet Bhatla said the cash is under evaluation for deployment into growth in services, with no specific plan disclosed yet and shareholder value as the stated priority.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Durgapur demerger timeline and benefit to minority shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said the NCLT petition is filed, creditor and shareholder approvals and tax/bank NOCs are required, and completion is targeted for this calendar year and within 12 months of 31 Mar 2026. Shareholders receive entitlement shares in the resulting company.

qa_highlights.question: Will the demerger affect manufacturing needed for core services?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said no, because a five-year JSW Energy agreement reserves manufacturing capacity at pre-set schedule and price. An alternate supply chain is targeted within about 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the underlying EBITDA margin excluding one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said FY26 normalised entity-level EBITDA was 11%, with Q4 at about 18%. He declined to give a numeric margin range for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will ECL-related reversals continue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said no; the BHEL settlement is fully executed, with the final tranche received in March 2026, and the ECL impact is complete as of 31 Mar 2026.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR 266 crore in Q4 FY25 (about 19% YoY as stated in the call)

financial_highlights.metric: PBT before exceptional items, continuing ops (Q4 FY26)
financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR 15 crore in Q4 FY25; includes ~INR 44 crore BHEL ECL reversal (CFO later said ~INR 41 crore with other benefits)

financial_highlights.metric: PBT before exceptional items, continuing ops (FY26)

532341|2026-03.headline: IZMO Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record INR109.16 crore (+82.5% YoY), with FY26 revenue up 26.8% to INR284.88 crore.

532343|2026-03.headline: TVS Motor FY26 revenue rose 30% to INR 47,270 crores with record Q4 revenue of INR 12,808 crores and 13.1% EBITDA margin.

Q4 revenue of INR 12,808 crores grew 36% YoY with EBITDA margin of 13.1%, against 6.5% when the margin recovery began. Management flagged near-term supply disruptions (gas, labour at Tier 2 suppliers, raw material timing, container lead times) and 3-5% commodity cost inflation, and guided to a strong single-digit industry growth in FY27 with capex of about INR 3,500 crores.

rows.why: Middle East orders are slowing, APAC and Africa are slower, and contracts are slipping by a month or two from legal and liability negotiations, though management said nothing has been lost and a Tier 1 Middle East renewal was secured.

rows.label: ESOP share purchase from market (up to 2% in FY27)
rows.why: 5% ESOP pool approved and postal ballot planned within about two weeks, with purchases expected around Q3 for up to 2% of equity.

rows.label: Q2 FY27 fair value markup on unlisted stake from ID Central sale
rows.why: Management planned a fair value markup on the stake received on the sale of ID Central in Q2 FY27, which would lift reported income, though the amount was not given.

tone.note: Management was confident on profitability (EBITDA about 4x year-ago, 21.2% margin) and the PEM rebuild, but cautious on Middle East and APAC deal timing and declined to give order value, pipeline numbers, growth targets or margin thresholds, which analysts pressed on.

532349|2026-06.headline: TCI Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew ~9% (24th straight quarter of growth) while standalone profit turned slightly negative on lower JV dividends and bunker costs.
532349|2026-06.overview: Management reported 9% consolidated top-line growth and 7% standalone growth for Q1 FY27, with the freight business up 10-11%. Standalone EBITDA margin was about 1.6% and PAT slightly negative, largely because JV dividend income was lower; consolidated EBITDA was about 5%. Seaways margins were flat as bunker prices rose to around Rs 86,000/ton, partly offset by rate increases; the Concor JV grew about 88% and Cold Chain about 48%. Management guided supply chain to 12-15% growth and freight to 10-12%, with capex of Rs 550-600 crore for FY27 (Rs 167 crore spent in Q1).

segments.name: Supply chain (standalone)
segments.commentary: Growth moderate against a high base; EBITDA margin slightly improved but EBIT flat. Management expects 12-15% top-line growth for FY27, pick-up in H2 from new contracts and diesel pass-through bills.

segments.name: Freight
segments.commentary: Top line up ~10-11% with slight margin improvement; 10 of planned 30 new branches opened in Q1. FY27 guidance 10-12% growth with higher profitability.

segments.name: Seaways
segments.commentary: Revenue up on pricing with similar voyages (one ship dry-docked); margins flat. Bunker prices at ~Rs 86,000/ton; Q2 EBITDA guided at 25-30%, and new ships expected Sept-Oct and Oct-Nov.

segments.name: Concor JV
segments.commentary: Grew ~88% per management; revenue moderated vs last quarter per Q&A. Rail shift from road limited due to lean season and rail congestion.

segments.name: Cold Chain JV
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~48% from contracts won in Q3-Q4 FY26; still small in quantum.

segments.name: Trans System JV (Toyota-linked, Mitsui partner)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~11.5%, but margin fell to ~9% from 14-15% on pricing pressure and production cuts; profit run-rate down to ~Rs 30 crore from Rs 40-42 crore. Management sees ~10% margin as reasonable.

Freight revenue growth 10-12% for FY27 with higher profitability year on year.

Rail congestion and monsoon/lean season limited shift from road to rail; containers backlog ~10,000-12,000 at JNPT.
Trans System pricing pressure and production cuts at Japanese OEM clients; some low-priced business not renewed.

qa_highlights.question: Can supply chain reach 12-15% growth in H2 and how much diesel-linked price growth came in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites pipeline and new contracts from H2, plus supplementary diesel bills from mid-May; Q1 diesel-linked benefit was minimal, mostly volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Seaways profitability with bunker volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Bunker prices are volatile; Q2 EBITDA expected at 25-30%. New ships take 4-6 months to reach full utilisation; breakeven timing not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Why is freight profit not improving despite the auto recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Some customers were served from Q4 pipeline inventory; longer-haul replenishment expected in subsequent quarters; mix shift and 30 new branches to drive margin, a slow process.

qa_highlights.question: Receivable days and capex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital days ~55-56; some pressure expected from rate hikes but credit policies in place. FY27 capex mainly ships, trucks/rakes, warehouses.

qa_highlights.question: Margin impact of LTL mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: LTL gross margin ~20% vs FTL ~10%; mix shift from ~35-37% to ~40% is gradual, adding a few basis points per 1% shift.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Trans System margins fall and what is the JV earnings outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment in expansion, pricing pressure and lost low-priced business; ~10% margin seen as reasonable. JV profitability guided similar to last year; Toyota plant at Aurangabad to need investment next fiscal.

Supply chain growth must accelerate to 12-15% in H2 from a moderate Q1; auto customer demand timing uncertain.

532356|2026-03.headline: Triveni FY26 revenue rose 10.6% to ₹6,291 crore and PBT reached ₹378 crore, while Q4 revenue dipped on PTB order slippage.
532356|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue net of excise was ₹6,291 crore (up 10.6%), with the net profit at ₹268.7 crore (up 12.8%) and EBITDA of about ₹624 crore (16.9% margin). Q4 revenue was just over ₹1,500 crore, slightly down YoY, due to scaled-down ethanol dispatches to OMCs and short delivery deferment in Power Transmission. The distillery segment staged a sharp turnaround on record volumes and lower maize costs, while sugar crush fell 8.8% to 8.25 million tonnes. The composite scheme became effective on 19 May 2026, with the TPTL demerger and listing targeted by end-August 2026.

segments.name: Sugar
segments.commentary: Revenue grew almost 13% and PBIT was about ₹272 crore (marginal growth). Crush fell 8.8% to 8.25 million tonnes, with West UP down 17%; gross recovery rose 26 bps to 11.06%, and net sugar output was about 913,000 tonnes. Domestic sales volume was 9.79 lakh tonnes at ₹40,680/tonne.

segments.name: Distillery
segments.commentary: Record production and sales volumes with FY26 revenue net of excise of ₹1,550 crore. Realisation averaged ₹61/litre (lower due to FCI rice mix), and grain made up 56% of ethanol sales (maize about 33%). Management said conversion and raw-material costs fell significantly.

segments.name: Power Transmission (PTB/gearboxes)
segments.commentary: Q4 was weak on steam-turbine order finalisation delays and West Asia-related deferrals, with finished gearboxes awaiting export. Order book closed at just under ₹500 crore (up 25% YoY). Aftermarket was about 40% of gears sales in FY26 versus over 30% historically; PBIT margin is about 35%.

segments.name: Water
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 15% to over ₹270 crore on EPC execution. Closing order book was just over ₹1,500 crore, of which about ₹1,077 crore is long-duration O&M. FY26 order inflow was ₹165 crore, and receivables are about ₹125–150 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the gearbox CapEx of ₹340 crore (approved in three tranches) to finish by September 2026. About ₹231 crore was spent by 31 March 2026, with ~₹109 crore to be spent in Q1 and Q2 FY27; this is expected to support about ₹700 crore of gearbox output.
Management expects exports to exceed 50% of PTB original-equipment sales in the very near future.

National sugar production is estimated at 27.8 million tonnes; Triveni's closing sugar stock is projected at 4.6–4.8 million tonnes. The sugar season is expected to start in the second half of October 2026.
Ethanol: 17.18 crore litres allocated under cycle one; further OMC and private tender allocations are expected shortly. Management also said the ethanol tender this year was a disappointment.
Short-term borrowings are expected to fall sharply from April and reach almost zero by September or October 2026.
TPTL demerger: record date for Triveni shareholders expected to be set within about four weeks, with listing targeted by end-August 2026.
capex_capacity: Gearbox CapEx of ₹340 crore approved in three tranches; ₹231 crore incurred by 31 March 2026, of which ₹78 crore was for the defence facility, with completion targeted by September 2026.
New multi-modal test facility in Mysore is now fully operable; defence facility machinery commissioned in Q4 and test facility to be installed over the next couple of quarters.
Shamli distillery, which has not operated since acquisition, is expected to add capacity without new CapEx; some distillery capacities are being debottlenecked.
Sugar CapEx currently under way is aimed only at lowering production costs; varietal replacement is ongoing.
Khatauli unit was the only one in West UP to cross 200 lakh quintals crushing capacity this season.
demand_pricing: Ex-mill refined sugar prices were about ₹42.20/kg, and sulphitation sugar about ₹41.50/kg; refined sugar averaged ₹41.32/kg in FY26. Inventory of ~60 lakh quintals was valued at ₹38.1/kg.
Cane price rose ₹300/tonne in UP; management said recoveries and cost measures absorbed it.
Maize cost is about ₹0.75–0.80/kg lower than last year, per the distillery head, though rupee depreciation raises export exposure.
PTB enquiry book is strong and skewed to exports; management said Q1 FY27 saw a surge of domestic enquiries after capex slowdown in Q3–Q4.
Water segment demand is supported by stricter ZLD and liquid discharge rules; management expects more orders soon.
Defence orders are in the double-digit to triple-digit crore range with 1–4 year delivery; RENK is increasing tender presence but management said it is not winning more high-speed orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of PTB sales between original-equipment and aftermarket, and how is the distribution network built?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not split OE and replacement revenue; aftermarket was about 40% of gears sales in FY26, versus above 30% historically. It is building agency partners abroad and treats AVL approvals as a multi-year process.

qa_highlights.question: Are the aftermarket and gas-segment opportunities growing, and is RENK a competitive threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gas qualification work is underway for data-centre-linked gas turbines and engines and is expected to yield AVL wins within a few quarters. RENK is more visible in tenders but management does not think it is winning more high-speed orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA/PBIT outlook for PTB after the demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Suresh Taneja said PTB has consistently maintained about 35% PBIT and expects the same trend to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ethanol feedstock mix and FY27 grain-based EBITDA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Maize was about 33% of ethanol mix (down from 44%) because the ESY tender required 40% of grain allocation to come from FCI rice; grain was 56% of total. Management said FY27 depends on the next tender and government policy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital and water receivables picture?
qa_highlights.answer: Total receivables are about ₹500 crore, including ₹125–150 crore from water. Higher short-term borrowings reflect higher cane price working capital, which should fall from April.

qa_highlights.question: What is the defence business order size and the CapEx split?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence orders are double-digit to triple-digit crore; about 40% of the pending ₹109 crore CapEx goes to defence.

risks_watch: Q4 PTB slippage: export-bound gearboxes sitting in finished goods and steam-turbine order finalisation delays linked to West Asia.
Sugar: El Niño and a possible Super El Niño could affect monsoon and crop yields; cane diversion to gur and khandsari hit crush this season.
Ethanol: delays in OMC and private tender allocations, a legal dispute in South India, and government preference for FCI rice over maize could compress distillery margins.
TPTL demerger and listing timing (end-August 2026), plus approvals needed for record date and share dispersal.
Q1 FY27 board results for TEIL and TPTL, and whether PTB's order conversion picks up.

rows.why: No new product, brand or model launch was discussed; gas-turbine and engine AVL wins are expected within a few quarters but are not a launch.

532356|2026-06.headline: Triveni Q1 FY27 revenue rose 2% YoY to ₹1,581 crore and PBT turned positive at ₹5 crore (vs ₹9 crore loss), led by sugar and distillery margins.
532356|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 is the first quarter after the power transmission business was demerged into Triveni Power Transmission Ltd (effective 1 April 2026; scheme effective 19 May 2026), so figures are for continuing operations with prior periods restated. Revenue grew 2% YoY to ₹1,581 crore and EBITDA rose 6%, with sugar margins and distillery PBIT (up 32%) doing most of the work. Water revenue fell 21% on slower Prayagraj and Vadodara EPC execution. Management said the quarter was better than its own expectations and flagged improving sugar prices and a stock-limit order from the government for Aug–Nov 2026.

segments.name: Sugar
segments.commentary: Domestic dispatches up 7% and realisation up 3% YoY; segment revenue ₹1,235 crore and PBIT ₹14 crore (+82%). Sugar inventory at 30 June 2026 was 3.59 lakh MT at ₹38.41/kg versus 4.45 lakh MT a year earlier.

segments.name: Alcohol / Distillery
segments.commentary: Production 57,488 KL (-12% YoY) and sales 50,483 KL (-19% YoY) on lower sales orders; grain-based share of alcohol sales rose to 61% from 58%. PBIT ₹31 crore (+32%) on lower maize costs, better DDGS realisation and efficiencies.

segments.name: Water
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹43 crore (-21%); orders received ₹9 crore in the quarter; closing order book ₹1,472 crore, including ₹1,065 crore of long-duration O&M. Bids in the quarter exceeded ₹300 crore.

segments.name: Country liquor / branded alcohol
segments.commentary: Country liquor volumes about 15.5 lakh cases, marginally down on a UP excise quota revision. Branded spirits are launched in UP and Delhi and are not yet profitable per management.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a significantly better operating season in FY27 (sugar season 2026-27) for Triveni's cost economics, led by a rebound at Shamli and CapEx benefits at the other seven sugar units.
Management expects a good Q2 on the back of sugar price strength.

Sugar: management sees 'excellent' sugar pricing ahead, with pricing expected to hold at current levels; domestic sugar consumption estimated at 28.3 MT by Triveni versus government estimate of 28.1 MT.

Ethanol: management estimates next-year (ESY 2026-27) ethanol procurement of about 1,300 crore litres and expects a roughly 3:1 grain-to-sugary feedstock ratio; expects Triveni to match that mix via multi-feed distilleries.
Water: management expects to achieve the year's operating plan, though execution is lumpy; recent tenders are under pursuit.
Management said there is sufficient country-liquor capacity for at least the next three quarters.
capex_capacity: Sugar crush for 2025-26 was 8.25 million MT, down about 9% YoY on poorer yields and higher diversion; gross recovery improved 26 bps to 11.1%.
Sir Shadi Lal (Shamli) crushed 82 lakh quintals at 10.4% recovery in FY26; management expects a higher number of operating days, lower diversion and better recovery in 2026-27.
Some CapEx has gone into sugar plant cost efficiency (steam economics, bagasse savings) for the upcoming season.
Management will maximise crystallisation capacity for sugar next year rather than divert juice to ethanol in UP.
Capital allocation review is under active examination by the board; management said water needs better ROCE before more capital, and country liquor needs little capital but is capped by UP geography.
demand_pricing: Sugar prices: refined sugar about ₹4,600/quintal and sulphitation sugar about ₹4,525/quintal as of the call date, versus the previous-quarter average.
Government order effective 1 Aug–30 Nov 2026 caps dealer stock holdings at 4,000 quintals and 30 days.
Industry closing stock for 2025-26 estimated at about 4 MT, the lowest since Sept 2017 (3.88 MT).
Sugar cane price (SAP) hike last season was ₹30/quintal, the highest ever; management is uncertain about SAP for the next season given UP elections in early 2027.

Maize prices rose in the single-digit percentage range over four to five months; DDGS realisation offsets the maize rise. MP maize procurement expected from November; current maize is covered until Oct–Nov.
Country liquor is a competitive market; Triveni claims top-five position in UP. Branded spirits (about 5-6% of volume) are growing but unprofitable.

Ethanol: Supreme Court has ordered status quo on existing allocation framework; AG has proposed allocation of 100 crore litres to be divided among about 200 bidders, with a hearing expected early the following week.

qa_highlights.question: Expected sugarcane yields going forward after the lower 2025-26 crush?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 2025-26 output fell about 9% on poorer yields and higher diversion, partly offset by higher recoveries. For 2026-27 it reported pest and disease incidence well below monitoring lines and adequate rainfall at five of eight factories, while stressing the next six weeks of grand growth are critical.

qa_highlights.question: What are the bottlenecks in the water business execution (Prayagraj etc.) and how will they be resolved?
qa_highlights.answer: Suresh Taneja called the slippage part of the business's lumpy execution and said the company should still achieve the full-year operating plan.

qa_highlights.question: How will Maharashtra and Karnataka cane output and national sugar balance look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a flattish performance in Maharashtra and Karnataka, with limited upside. It estimates FY27 domestic consumption at 28.3 MT against the government's 28.1 MT, and says sugar supply is sufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Will mills divert more cane juice or B-heavy to ethanol and cut sugar output, and what diversion is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Triveni will maximise crystallisation capacity in UP next year. Diversion is expected to be between zero and 3 MT, with B-heavy likely to be diverted and juice diversion uncertain until October 2026 cane estimates.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ethanol offtake fall, and will capacity utilisation stay below 70%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ethanol procurement was above 1,100 crore litres this year and expects about 1,300 crore litres next year. It expects standalone distilleries running at 20-50% utilisation to face viability pressure once interest moratoriums end, so utilisation will vary by group and multi-feed capacity matters.

qa_highlights.question: Maize price outlook and cost cover?
qa_highlights.answer: Maize prices rose in the single-digit percentage range over four to five months, offset by higher DDGS realisation. Procurement covers until October-November, and MP maize is expected from November.

qa_highlights.question: Sir Shadi Lal standalone numbers and recovery outlook; debt and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Sir Shadi Lal is amalgamated, so separate EBITDA and PAT are not disclosed. FY26 crush was 82 lakh quintals at 10.4% recovery, with a rebound expected in 2026-27. Working capital borrowings are expected lower; the board is examining capital allocation, with water needing better ROCE and country liquor capped by UP geography.

532375|2026-03.headline: Tips Music Q4 FY26 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR103.9 crore and PAT 93% to INR59 crore; management targets 20% top-line and 20% bottom-line growth in FY27.
532375|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR103.9 crore (+32% YoY), operating EBITDA INR76.9 crore (+106% YoY) and PAT INR59 crore (+93% YoY), with management saying there were no one-offs. For FY26, revenue was INR375.5 crore (+21%) and PAT INR216.6 crore (+30%), and the company distributed INR166 crore in dividends. Digital was about 70% of FY26 revenue and non-digital about 30%, with brand publishing and public performance cited as growth contributors. Content cost fell to about 15.8% of revenue as a film's music release slipped from Q4 to June 2026. Management guided to 20% top-line and 20% bottom-line growth for FY27 and declined to raise that target further.

segments.commentary: About 30% of FY26 revenue; brand publishing and public performance were cited as the main contributors, and the Q4 non-digital share rose versus earlier quarters.

Two films, Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai and Main Vaapas Aaunga, are slated for theatrical release on 22 May and 12 June 2026; their music costs will be expensed in Q1 FY27 on release.
YouTube Shorts deal renewal is due around June 2026; negotiations were expected to start at end-April or early May 2026. Management said the view decline does not affect the renewal.

demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 release of 66 new songs (47 film, 19 non-film), with a focus on quality over quantity.
YouTube subscribers at 153 million; a catalogue song on Instagram reached 3 billion views and another 1.5 billion.
Management attributed the growth to the repertoire, with several catalogue songs trending across Instagram, YouTube and Spotify.
Public performance industry is about INR500 crore; management expects it to reach at least INR3,000 crore in about three years (over 50% CAGR).
Management said bundling with telecom packs gives lower payouts and prefers pure-play music platforms.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is normal, with viral spikes causing peaks, and sees no material impact on renewal. Negotiations start at the end of April or early May 2026, and no replacement has been named for Hari Nair.

qa_highlights.question: Why did content cost fall to 15.8% of revenue versus 23% last year, against an 18% target?

qa_highlights.question: Will employee costs stay at the Q4 level?
qa_highlights.answer: No; the Q4 increase reflects the annual increment provision, and cost should return to Q2 and Q3 run rates.

qa_highlights.question: What is paid subscription's share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Paid subscription is 10% to 15% of digital revenue, up from about 10% to 12% last year, and it is growing at 30% to 40% CAGR.

532395|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue grew 12.4% to 1,159 crores and EBITDA rose 24.6% to 178 crores, but reported PAT fell 4.3% to 72 crores after a 142 crore Q4 revenue deferment.

Management signed a definitive agreement on May 26, 2026 to sell the heavy engineering, energy and automotive practice to Akkodis for USD 30.63 million, with closure expected in Q2 FY27. FY27 consolidated revenue is guided at about 1,377 crores (52% growth on the retained base), and the company reiterated its 9,000 crore FY30 revenue target.

532395|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first quarter of the divestment-led transition: Engineering Services is shown as discontinued operations (₹163 crore revenue), leaving continuing operations at ₹183 crore, up 94% YoY. qa_highlights.question: Why divest the profitable aerospace services business when the company wants to build aerospace manufacturing, and could both have been done together?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aim is to shift from services to product and solutions, citing OEM consolidation in services and a sale price that let proceeds fund Power 930 without equity dilution. KP Mohanakrishnan conceded doing both together was hypothetically possible but said the strategy chose product-based growth.

qa_highlights.question: Where are the Rs 10 crore receivable provision, Rs 3.5 crore hedge provision and Rs 22 crore deal cost booked?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Shashidhar SK said the ~Rs 21 crore transaction cost sits in discontinued operations as an exceptional item, visible in the notes. The hedge unwinding of Rs 3.5 crore sits in continuing other expenses. Provisions of about Rs 6.5 crore (Ministry of Defence order) and Rs 3.14 crore (a defence PSU) were also cited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalized PAT outlook for FY27 on Rs 1,377 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mukund Santhanam reiterated FY27 EBITDA of Rs 270 crore and PAT broadly around 50% of that, about Rs 135 crore, possibly higher as divestment proceeds pay down debt and cut interest. He confirmed the analyst's view that Q2-Q4 would ramp up.

qa_highlights.question: Status and timing of acquisitions, and what happens in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Two acquisitions (aerospace AS9100 manufacturer, XiDA business transfer) are targeted to close this quarter, with a third aerospace deal targeted by Q4. Management said most acquisitions will be in place by FY27-end and later ones will be smaller in scale than this year's.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the Rs 4,557 crore defence assured visibility take to execute, and what is the wider pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Sharadhi Babu said the visibility is to be covered before FY30, about 3 years, with possible spillover into a fourth year. The total pipeline is about Rs 24,000 crore across unmanned systems, missiles, radar and DEW. Management also reiterated 75%+ defence growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Power 930 target (FY30 PAT Rs 960 crore) still intact, and is the acquisition-led plan at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Mukund Santhanam said the Power 930 targets remain firm, with FY30 PAT of Rs 960 crore. He acknowledged acquisitions are binary, saying aerospace and XiDA are at advanced stages while other deals are still at non-binding offer stage.

qa_highlights.question: What are the year-wise CapEx plans and how will they be funded before divestment proceeds arrive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give year-wise CapEx, saying spend will be timed to inflows (Q2 and Q3 FY27, then FY28 and FY29) and to partner readiness. A short-term bridge facility will fund the gap, with actual drawdown not more than Rs 100-150 crore. Shashidhar SK also said Rs 200+ crore of gain is expected in Q2 and the bulk in early Q3.

risks_watch: Closing timelines: Akkodis Phase 1 (~Rs 190 crore post-tax cash) targeted by Aug 31; Phase 2 (~Rs 525 crore) targeted by Nov 30, with management trying to pull it to about September. Slippage delays the Rs 1,255 crore extraordinary gain and debt paydown.

532424|2026-03.headline: GCPL Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11% in INR on 6% underlying volume growth; EBITDA up 10% at 21.7% margin, with a revenue-presentation change.
532424|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11% in INR on 6% underlying volume growth, EBITDA grew 10% with a 21.7% margin, and reported PAT grew 10%. India standalone was the standout: 8% volume growth, 10% sales growth, 18% EBITDA growth and a 24.7% margin, led by Home Care (+12%). Africa/US/Middle East grew 20% in sales but EBITDA rose only 2% after doubling media spend, and Indonesia grew 3% in sales with 4% volume growth. From this quarter, customer-related trade spends are netted off revenue following an ICAI Expert Advisory Committee opinion, with no impact on absolute EBITDA or PAT. Management guided to margin pressure in Q1 and likely Q2 FY27 from crude-linked and palm oil input inflation of roughly 7-9%, offset by price hikes and share gains.

532424|2026-06.headline: GCPL Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 19% YoY on 9% underlying volume growth, EBITDA up 14% with 19% margin; India gross margin hit by war-linked input costs.
532424|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 19% YoY with underlying volume growth of 9%, EBITDA rose 14% at a 19% margin, and net profit grew 11%. India gross margin fell sharply as LPG, kerosene and LABSA roughly trebled during the war-driven spike, with India cost impact near 6% over plan. Africa (GAUM) delivered an exceptional quarter with constant-currency growth around 25% and EBITDA margins moving to mid-teens, while Indonesia returned to stable growth at about 10%. Management says it is on track for full-year guidance and expects to exceed it on revenue, and possibly on EBITDA and volume.

segments.name: Africa / GAUM
segments.commentary: Constant-currency growth about 25%, driven by FMCG (air care at double-digit market share in South Africa within six months of launch) and hair extensions cost improvements. FY26 growth split was about 50:50 FMCG and hair.

segments.name: Indonesia
segments.commentary: Growth about 10% on a slower base, step-up in air media, and early El Nino benefit; Stellar business growing faster.

segments.name: Soaps (India)
segments.commentary: Volumes grew positively in Q1; management expects early single-digit growth in Q2 and Q3, soap margins at normative levels.

segments.commentary: Growth of about 70-80% from acquisition run rate; EPS accretive from day one, profitable digital-first brand.

segments.commentary: Committed INR500 crore capital; additional INR200 crore rights commitment referenced by analyst. Product-market fit achieved in Tamil Nadu; expansion to rest of South India under way.

532443|2026-06.headline: Cera Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.5% (volume-led) to INR 486 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.1% on one-time factors management says reverse from Q3.
532443|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 19.5% YoY to INR 486 crore, with Sanitaryware up 14%, Faucetware up 25% and growth mainly volume-driven. EBITDA excluding other income fell to INR 49.2 crore (10.1% margin vs 13.1% a year ago), which management attributed to a wage settlement, under-absorption from single-kiln operation in April-May, project-order foreclosures and delayed price pass-through. PAT was INR 45 crore vs INR 47 crore. Turnover discounts were reclassified from expenses into revenue deductions, lowering reported revenue by about 2.5-3% with no absolute profit impact. FY27 guidance of 18-20% revenue growth and 13.5-14% EBITDA margin was maintained.

segments.name: Sanitaryware
segments.commentary: 47% of revenue; grew 14% YoY (volume ~10%, price ~2%, mix ~2%). Capacity utilisation 61% in Q1, roughly 80% across both plants from June.

segments.name: Faucetware
segments.commentary: 40% of revenue; grew 25% YoY (volume 18%, price 4%, mix 3%). Utilisation 96%; gross margin severely hit by brass cost inflation.

segments.name: Tiles
segments.commentary: 11% of revenue; grew 22% YoY.

segments.name: Wellness
segments.commentary: 2% of revenue; declined 7% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 18-20% reiterated.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 13.5-14% maintained; management says it will be met on a full-year basis, implying a recovery after Q2.
Q2 expected to carry some residual impact as project orders still at old prices; project price revisions to flow from Q3.
Gross margin expected to return to ~51% from Q3 if brass and gas prices hold; Q1 gross margin was ~46%.
FY27 wage cost add-on of INR 18.3 crore (INR 6.3 crore one-time arrears plus INR 12 crore for the year); FY27 staff cost guided at ~INR 300 crore.
FY27 capex outlay ~INR 43 crore, mainly Faucetware brownfield expansion (capacity expected from Q4 FY27), efficiency, digital and infrastructure.
FY27 brand-building and marketing budget ~INR 85 crore, which management says can be increased.
Management declined to guide FY28 margins; said it would revisit at year end. Long-term margin of 16% not committed to a timeline.
capex_capacity: Sanitaryware utilisation 61% in Q1 FY27 (one kiln run in April-May; second kiln started June); both plants running from June at ~80% of total capacity.
Faucetware utilisation 96% in Q1; management says it can go beyond 100% via in-house and outsourced supply until brownfield expansion comes in from Q4 FY27.
Greenfield sanitaryware project (earlier INR 130-150 crore, deferred) to be reviewed by year-end; would take ~18 months to build once decided.
Internalising higher-selling SKUs from Morbi outsourcing partners; incremental casting-line investment of INR 2-3 crore.
Long-term in-house/outsourced split about 50:50; Sanitaryware skewed more towards outsourcing recently due to bought-out parts.
demand_pricing: Cumulative price increases (March and May 2026): ~12% in Sanitaryware, ~16% in Faucetware; management says absorbed well by the market.
Price hikes reflected mainly in retail; project contracts (43% of Q1 revenue vs 39% in Q4) to move to revised pricing from Q3.
Brass prices rose from INR 665 (Dec) to ~INR 880 (June) and ~INR 900 (July) per management; further hike possible if prices go to INR 950-1,000.
Product mix: premium 44%, mid 37%, entry 19%. Tier 1 and Tier 3 at 38% each, Tier 2 at 24%.
Management described growth as volume-driven and broad-based across retail and project, with Sanitaryware demand up from ~10% growth in prior quarters to 14%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 19.5% growth was volume vs price, and what was the Senator/Polipluz contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanitaryware: volume ~10%, price ~2%, mix ~2%. Faucetware: volume 18%, price 4%, mix 3%. Management would not split out Senator and Polipluz numbers, saying they are in build-up phase and FY27 targets are unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What was the one-time wage settlement and what is the staff cost run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 6.3 crore arrears for Sept 2025-Mar 2026 booked in Q1, plus INR 3 crore for the current quarter. Full-year wage impact INR 18.3 crore. Staff cost expected ~INR 300 crore for FY27 excluding the one-off.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the margin drop, and how much is one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a 4.35 percentage point one-time impact: wage arrears 1.3%, under-absorption from single kiln 0.75% (INR 3.7 crore), accelerated project order closures 0.8% (INR 4 crore), and delayed retail price pass-through 1.5%. Ex-these items EBITDA would be ~14.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Morbi and SKU internalisation need capex, and how many flagship stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Internalisation needs only INR 2-3 crore of casting-line changes. Senator stores to rise from 35 to ~50 by year end, on track.

qa_highlights.question: Who leads Senator and Polipluz after Mr. Baliga's resignation?
qa_highlights.answer: The existing national head under the succession plan will lead them. Baliga stays until 30 September. Management says targets are unchanged and no execution impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Should the greenfield sanitaryware plant be revived?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand improving (Sanitaryware growth 14% vs ~10% earlier). Review by year end; if approved the plant takes ~18 months. Some capacity remains available.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further price hikes and where does gross margin go?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin ~46% in Q1 (Faucetware hit hardest); expected ~51% from Q3 if brass and gas hold. Further hike to be evaluated if brass goes beyond INR 900-950.

532454|2026-03.headline: Airtel FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record ~Rs 2,11,000 Cr; Q4 India ARPU rose only Rs 3 to Rs 257 on EDB basis.
532454|2026-03.overview: Management reported a record FY26 with consolidated revenue of about Rs 2,11,000 Cr and EBITDAaL of about Rs 1,08,000 Cr (51.2% margin). Q4 consolidated revenue was about Rs 55,400 Cr, up 2.6% QoQ, with Q4 constant currency growth of 1.1% hit by seasonality and fewer days. India mobile ARPU rose only Rs 3 QoQ on an EDB basis, which management said it was not happy with, citing West Asia-linked international roaming and handset price pressures. The Board recommended a dividend of Rs 24 per share (vs Rs 16) and approved a no-cash share swap with ICIL to acquire an additional 16.3% of Airtel Africa. Management flagged geopolitical cost pressures on capex, energy, roaming and servers/memory, and pivoted home broadband back to fiber from FWA.

segments.commentary: Q4 added 4.7 mn customers (5.8 mn smartphone adds in the quarter per the call); ARPU Rs 257, up Rs 3 on EDB basis. Mobile is about 52% of revenue.

segments.commentary: Q4 net adds 1.1 mn; added 4.2 mn customers in FY26 and crossed 45 mn home passes after ~8 mn passes rolled out in FY26. Digital TV added nearly 0.5 mn customers in Q4 on IPTV.

segments.name: Airtel Business (B2B)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about Rs 5,500 Cr, +2.6% QoQ; order book grew 17% in FY26; digital businesses revenue +27% in FY26. Non-mobile India is 13% of revenue.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Africa is 29% of group revenue; Q4 constant currency growth 1.1%, affected by seasonality and fewer days.

segments.commentary: Airtel Money received RBI approval to operate as an NBFC; monthly loan disbursement run rate over Rs 550 Cr; Payments Bank has ~120 mn monthly transacting users and deposits over Rs 4,600 Cr (+27% YoY).

qa_highlights.question: How will capital be allocated given strong India FCF and the dividend payout level, and are non-India acquisitions planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Priorities are core business first, then deleveraging, then adjacencies (data centers, financial services, cloud). Management said nothing further outside India is planned for now beyond bolt-ons in towers, cloud, cybersecurity and B2B.

qa_highlights.question: Does ARPU growth need tariff hikes, and what will change the trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued pricing architecture must be fixed rather than just raising entry prices, which it said must be done with caution. Levers cited: postpaid, best-fit plan upgrades, roaming and data-consumption upgrades.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 ARPU expansion slow given roaming and handset headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Shashwat said organic levers (postpaid, plan upgrades within tiers) provide headroom for many quarters, but handset price rises need watching.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans for the coming year and capital allocation shift toward growth bets?
qa_highlights.answer: Radio capex moderating in India; transport, edge data centers, homes, data centers and cloud to get focus. FY27 capex expected roughly in line with FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROCE targets and Nxtra's business model, including Google partnership?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not give ROCE targets; consolidated ROCE ~19%, expected to improve with operating leverage. Nxtra is colocation-led, with Google's Visakhapatnam AI data center being built as colocation.

qa_highlights.question: Is wireless capex near the bottom, and what is the homes ARPU trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Wireless capex is derived at ~16% of sales and is moderating; 5G densification would be done if needed. Homes ARPU dilution is from mix; acquisition ARPU stable, and quarterly ARPU is bottoming.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 ARPU lag and what is the regulatory charge at Hexacom?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower roaming, handset price rises and 5G pack adoption were the drivers. The regulatory charge was a prudential provision from a changed interpretation of an existing matter, not new demand.

532454|2026-06.headline: Airtel group Q1 FY27 revenue Rs58,500 Cr (+5.7% QoQ), EBITDAaL Rs29,800 Cr at 51% margin; India homes net adds slowed to 473,000 on tighter FWA acquisition quality.
532454|2026-06.overview: Group consolidated revenue rose about 5.7% sequentially to Rs58,500 Crores, with EBITDAaL of Rs29,800 Crores (+4.2%, 51% margin) and capex of about Rs13,390 Crores. India ex-passive infra grew 3.6% sequentially, while Africa posted 5.7% constant-currency revenue growth. Management flagged a deliberate pullback in FWA acquisition after aggressive low-price adds led to higher churn and weaker cohorts, and a pivot toward fiber. Airtel Money is preparing a London listing in 2H 2026 and Nxtra raised $1bn of funding.

segments.name: India mobile
segments.commentary: Added 3.3 million revenue-earning customers and 5 million smartphone data customers; ARPU Rs264 with one extra day in the quarter. Postpaid push supported by Fast Lane 5G network slicing.

segments.name: India homes
segments.commentary: Net adds of 473,000, a moderation after FWA acquisition quality was tightened; digital TV added 6,000 customers, led by IPTV adoption. Management is pivoting to fiber, with FWA limited to where fiber is not available.

segments.name: India B2B (Airtel Business)
segments.commentary: Revenue about Rs5,670 Crores, +3.2% QoQ and nearly +12% YoY, driven by large global connectivity deal wins; digital businesses (cloud, cybersecurity, IoT, CPaaS) grew nearly 6% QoQ.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Constant-currency revenue growth 5.7% QoQ; annualised EBITDA above Rs35,000 Crores. Airtel stake raised to over 79% via an EPS-accretive share swap; Indus expanding into three African markets.

segments.name: Airtel Money / Payments bank / NBFC
segments.commentary: Airtel Money Q1 revenue over $400 million (+26% YoY constant currency), London listing planned 2H 2026. Payments bank 120 million monthly transacting users; NBFC lending live, with loan disbursements over Rs750 Crores per month via Airtel Finance.

segments.name: Data centers (Nxtra) and Airtel Cloud
segments.commentary: Data center market share about 12%, targeting 1 GW from 120-130 MW over next few years; Google contract included. Airtel Cloud has 33 customers after 11 added in the quarter. Nxtra raised $1bn to fund expansion.

guidance_outlook: Management sees mid-term mobile ARPU headroom from upgrades, unlimited-plan migration and postpaid; long-term ARPU growth needs data-charging pricing architecture repair, which management says will not be achieved single-handedly.
Management estimates 4-5% sustained ARPU growth over five to seven years from better price architecture, with no need to change entry-level pricing.
Homes: expects momentum to return as acquisition quality repairs; Hexacom expects both circles to return to old growth rates in the next one to two quarters.
B2B margins expected to trend slightly downward over time as digital mix rises, with faster revenue growth as the key metric.
Airtel does not set ROCE targets and says it will fund growth capex without holding back; Nxtra will need debt and equity, funding route to be decided over time.
capex_capacity: Radio capex has moderated over the last couple of years; majority of capex is going to transport (fiber), which includes homes.
5G standalone capex is modest, being largely a software switch; data center build-out is lumpy and will create a period of rapid capex.

Data centers: ambition of 1 GW from 120-130 MW in the next few years; a couple of hundred MW under construction over the next couple of years, with Mumbai land parcels being finalised for the balance.
Over the last three years, about 139,000 km of fiber deployed; Cloud first-round investment completed across three regions.
Hexacom capex directed to 5G densification, network modernisation, fiberisation and homes/IPTV.
demand_pricing: Africa: tele-density about 45%, smartphone penetration 52%, home broadband penetration only 2%, population about 680 million across 14 countries; market structure typically two to three players with cheap spectrum.
FWA: aggressive low-entry pricing led to round-tripping and poor cohort quality; memory and chipset price inflation challenged FWA economics; management says memory cost impact on fiber is modest.
Hexacom mobile customer base 29 million, net adds about 210,000, smartphone adds 344,000; mobile ARPU Rs259.
B2B wholesale runs at low margins and faces price pressure and messaging shift to WhatsApp; connectivity market grows at low single digits.
