Dahej MPP debottlenecking capex targeted for commissioning in Q3 FY27.
Chemours project (initial capacity to accelerate market adoption) expected to complete by end June or early July 2026; future capex to be decided after about 18 months of market understanding.
cGMP4 (dedicated Fermion block) commissioned in Q4 FY26 (December per management); management said Phase 2 (cGMP5) is possible with space for 5-7 molecules.
AHF plant commissioned in February 2026; revenue expected to flow mainly from FY28.
demand_pricing: Management reports robust customer demand with no demand destruction seen so far; order visibility is solid, and restocking may follow once conditions improve.
Raw material inflation (sulfur, methanol) has been largely passed on to customers; management said there were no shutdowns due to raw material shortages.
Contracts differ: service-play contracts have pass-through mechanisms; product contracts are being renegotiated.
R32 pricing: management said China prices are near USD9/kg and that the USD600-875 range was a downside case used for investment approval.
Management said agrochemical pricing is subdued and expected to rise more slowly than volumes in FY27.
Middle East: export exposure is small; roughly INR15-16 crore of Middle East shipments were missed in Q4 and are excluded from Q1 numbers.
Management said the Chinese market could absorb Nectar product at reasonable margins.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain comes from currency versus operations, and how will raw material inflation be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said currency and inflation largely offset each other. Of the roughly 990 bps EBITDA margin gain, about 70% came from capacity and volume and about 30% from pricing. Pass-through clauses cover service contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Is the R32 pricing downside case of USD600-875 realistic given new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the USD600-875 range was a downside case that is always prepared for investment approval, and its belief is driven by demand-supply and GWP dynamics.

qa_highlights.question: Will HPP and Specialty Chemicals grow at high double digits in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a number but said it would be surprised if growth were not double-digit, citing utilisation going from 50-60% to 70-75%, the HF plant, Nectar, Chemours and cGMP4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Nectar plant's balance of volumes and how will the second 50% be placed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said qualifications are under way with 2-3 customers beyond the marquee customer. Utilisation is targeted at 75% in FY27 and the balance later, with some shipments already made outside contracted volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did contract liabilities rise to about INR211 crore from INR239 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contract liabilities reflect customer capital contributions for the Chemours project and the marquee Nectar molecule project.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 HPP revenue decline sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a planned shutdown and a catalyst recharge at one plant ahead of the heat season, plus about INR15-16 crore of Middle East shipments that did not go out.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict: raw material (sulfur, methanol) availability, energy prices and logistics; management said there has been no disruption so far.
Government R32/HFC quota allocation and new capacity coming in CY26-27 could pressure R32 pricing; management disputed the downside case.
Pricing lag on calendar-year contracts for HFO and CDMO if raw material inflation persists.
Nectar merchant volumes depend on qualifications of 2-3 customers beyond the marquee customer; utilisation is slower than originally planned.
Chemours and Dahej commissioning timelines (end June / early July 2026 and Q3 FY27) and the R32 timeline in Q3 FY27.
Margin sustainability: management guides about 30% for FY27 with a plus or minus 1-2% range, against a 34.2% Q4 margin.
532504|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on operations and FY27 visibility, but guarded on Middle East risk, R32 pricing and currency-driven margin benefits, which management largely declined to quantify.
key_quotes: So far, we have not seen any disruption. We have seen inflation go through.

I think it's about 990 basis points from FY to FY, you will see 70% of that for Navin is coming from our capacities coming on the ground, our volumes going up and 30% is coming from affirmative actions on pricing that we've taken.
So therefore, we are talking of the 75% this year and then the balance next year.
I would be surprised if it's not double-digit, but I'm happy to clarify if it is not separately.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin about 30% (plus or minus 1-2%) versus 32.6% for FY26 and 34.2% in Q4, and says agrochemical pricing will rise more slowly than volumes; about 30% of the 990 bps gain came from pricing and currency offset inflation.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3 FY27 (HFC/R32 15,000 MTPA and Dahej MPP debottlenecking);
rows.why: HFC/R32 15,000 MTPA expansion is on track for Q3 FY27 commissioning, Dahej debottlenecking targeted Q3 FY27, and Chemours project expected to complete end June or early July 2026; AHF plant already commissioned in Feb 2026 with revenue mainly from FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Utilisation expected to rise to 70-75% in FY27 from 50-60% in FY26, HFC/R32 15,000 MTPA due Q3 FY27, and agrochemicals about 80% capacity visibility; HPP has moved to about INR400 crore per quarter from INR250-300 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 80% today per management, but R32 quota uncertainty and the Chemours follow-on capex is to be decided after about 18 months of market understanding; cGMP5 Phase 2 is possible with space for 5-7 molecules.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Utilisation rising to 70-75% in FY27 from 50-60% in FY26, plus CDMO $100m FY27 target still held, could push growth above the double-digit guide, but management gave no number.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 30% (plus or minus 1-2%) versus a 34.2% Q4 margin, with Middle East raw material and logistics risk and R32 pricing pressure from new capacity; Middle East shipments of INR15-16 crore were missed in Q4.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: About 13 new molecules were added in FY26 (three in Q4), 50-55 CDMO molecules are in the pipeline with about half late-stage commercial, and Nectar qualifications are under way with 2-3 customers.

rows.label: Net working capital at 75-80 days vs 90 days earlier guidance
rows.why: Net working capital days fell to 74 from 90 and management now guides 75-80 days of sales, against prior indicative 90 days.

rows.label: Robust demand with no demand destruction; Middle East exposure small
rows.why: Management reports robust customer demand and solid order visibility, with Middle East export exposure small and only INR15-16 crore of Q4 shipments missed and excluded from Q1.

rows.label: R32 pricing pressure from new capacity and quota
rows.why: China R32 prices are near USD9/kg, management says USD600-875 range was a downside case, and a competitor R32 capacity above 120,000 MT by FY27 raises supply risk; quota allocation is the key question.

tone.note: Management was confident on utilisation, the Q3 FY27 capacity start-ups and the CDMO $100m target, but cautious on Middle East raw-material risk, R32 pricing and the currency-driven margin benefit it declined to quantify; analysts pressed on R32 quota and competitor capacity above 120,000 MT.

532504|2026-06.headline: Navin Fluorine Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 44% YoY to INR1,044-1,045 crore, with EBITDA up 73% and PAT up 108% to INR243 crore.
532504|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 44% YoY to about INR1,045 crore, with operating EBITDA of INR357 crore (34.2% margin, up 566 bps YoY) and PAT of INR243 crore. All three verticals (HPP, specialty chemicals, CDMO) grew strongly, and the company became net debt free during the quarter. Management announced a new INR90 crore advanced materials adoption capex and a Phase 2 CDMO cGMP capex of INR125 crore. Management guided to a 32-33% EBITDA margin range going forward (plus/minus 1%), while flagging gross margin pressure from higher raw material costs.

segments.name: HPP (HFCs/fluorochemicals)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR540 crore, up 33% YoY on healthy volume growth and improved realisations; management describes HFC pricing as constructive given demand-supply dynamics.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals (agchem)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR325 crore, up 48% YoY. Management plans campaign orders for 4-5 agchem molecules this year; LatAm agchem pricing pressure persists, and EBITDA is not expected to return to the old ~30% level.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue INR180 crore, up 82% YoY. Pipeline of 30-40 molecules, about 10 late stage; 3-4 molecules expected to get FDA readouts in the next 8-12 months. Management targets about $100 million for FY27.

segments.name: Advanced materials (incubating within HPP)
segments.commentary: Not separately reported. Chemours liquid cooling project targeted for completion by end Q2 FY27; Chemours reportedly sold about $1 million of two-phase cooling liquid in the quarter (per analyst). DRDO TDF partnership announced.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected in the 32-33% range (plus/minus 1%) on a normalised basis over the next one to two years, supported by HFC, debottlenecking and Chemours capacity.
CDMO FY27 target of about $100 million reiterated; FY29 asset turn of 3x on INR288 crore cGMP4 capex stated as the near-term view.
Gross margin dipped about 100 bps QoQ from Q4 FY26 on raw material costs; management said price pass-through will lag.
Advanced materials adoption capex (INR90 crore) to be done in two phases, first phase around mid-Q4 FY27 for commercial-scale qualification; not included in any return projections.
Growth visibility beyond FY28 depends on the current capex cycle (cGMP Phase 1, adoption capacity, Chemours).
capex_capacity: New advanced materials adoption capex of INR90 crore, internally funded, to be set up at Surat; creates two core platforms and augments analytical equipment.
CDMO cGMP4 Phase 2 capex of INR125 crore (part of INR288 crore approved Feb 2024), operationalisation expected Q4 FY27; Phase 1 operational in Q3 FY26. Dedicated to European CDMO partner.

HFC capacity addition of up to 15,000 MT of R32 on track for Q3 FY27; company currently has about 9,000-10,000 MT and total would be about 25,000 MT. Revenue band of INR600-825 crore cited from original capex approval.
MPP debottlenecking at Dahej on track for completion by Q3 FY27; management cited 2x asset turn.
AHF capacity of 60,000 MT between Surat and Dahej seen as adequate for the next 4-5 years; AHF commissioned in the subsidiary NFASL.
Renewable project of INR15.73 crore (14.9 MW hybrid) expected to supply more than 60% of energy needs once operational.
demand_pricing: R32: management expects a 35-45% contracted share of capacity over five years; a couple of contracts signed and more at a late stage.
R32 long-term demand said to double over a decade while quota-driven supply shrinks by half; Indian oversupply expected for about five years with exports to global market.
Specialty chemicals: volume recovering, but pricing pressure persists in LatAm; 13-14 new molecules launched last year and 5 new molecules being participated in, of which 3 are patented.
HFO supply to Honeywell: asset commercialised July 2022; original seven-year term with a three-year extension at Honeywell's option, so runway beyond FY29.
Management stated that raw material cost inflation is rising amid global war tensions and supply chain risk.

qa_highlights.question: Advanced materials: end-use applications, and growth beyond FY28 given current capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is to make advanced materials a material business unit by end of decade, modelled on today's CDMO. Focus on data centers, electronics, semiconductors, defence; the adoption capex is phased, with first phase complete around mid-Q4 FY27 to start commercial-scale qualification.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR90 crore adoption capex a pilot or commercial scale, and what is the payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said five products are already lab-approved and this capex takes them to commercial-scale qualification; not a pilot. No asset turn is assumed in numbers for the INR90 crore.

qa_highlights.question: R32 pricing and India capacity additions versus quota start in Jan 2028?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give pricing; said it will stay the lowest-cost R32 producer through its integrated HF chain and renewable power. Expects India oversupply for about five years and exports.

qa_highlights.question: Why did subsidiary (NFASL) margin fall about 12 pp QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Campaign mix differs quarter to quarter, and AHF transfers from Dahej to Surat are at arm's-length, so value shows up at Navin Fluorine (NFIL) level; group margin remains solid.

qa_highlights.question: CDMO: is the new capacity dedicated, and is the MSA for an extra molecule with the same customer?
qa_highlights.answer: New capacity dedicated to European CDMO partner; an MSA for an extra molecule in the same supply chain takes Navin to API minus 1. Also working on an early-phase molecule with the same customer.

qa_highlights.question: Is the $100 million CDMO target for FY27 still on track, and is INR900 crore cGMP capex math right?
qa_highlights.answer: $100 million target reiterated as on track. Management confirmed the 3x asset turn on INR288 crore by FY29, and that Phase 1 and Phase 2 combined are about INR900 crore is not exactly right; the INR288 crore figure is the approved base (3x = about INR900 crore revenue).

qa_highlights.question: HFC contracts, AHF utilisation, and the reason for the margin mix change YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: A couple of R32 contracts signed, with more near conclusion; balanced approach kept. Margin mix explained by HF price highs in Q1 FY26 and rising RM costs now; gross margin down about 100 bps QoQ, offset by fixed-cost productivity.

risks_watch: R32 pricing and contracted share: management targets 35-45% of capacity under five-year contracts, with a couple signed and more near conclusion; watch for contract signings and any price disclosure, since pricing was not given.

Gross margin pressure: gross margin fell about 100 bps QoQ on raw material inflation, with price pass-through expected to lag; watch whether the 32-33% EBITDA range (plus/minus 1%) holds as the HFC, debottlenecking and Chemours capacity come on line.

Advanced materials execution: INR90 crore adoption capex is phased, with first phase around mid-Q4 FY27 and commercialisation of about five lab-approved products; no asset turn assumed, so timing and qualification outcomes are key.

CDMO readouts: 3-4 molecules expected to get FDA readouts in the next 8-12 months after one readout did not go well; $100 million FY27 target and 3x asset turn on INR288 crore by FY29 depend on these.
Subsidiary NFASL margin swing: standalone-to-consolidated EBITDA margin gap was about 12 pp QoQ, attributed to campaign mix and arm's-length AHF transfers; watch for downstream capacity at NFASL.
Specialty chemicals (agchem) LatAm pricing pressure persists; management said EBITDA will not return to the old ~30% level, and campaign orders for 4-5 molecules are expected this year.
key_quotes: The revenue of the quarter grew 44% Y -o-Y to INR1,044 crores and EBITDA stood at INR357 crores, up 73% year-on-year and PAT at INR243 crores, registering a growth of 108% year-on-year.
I don't think this is a case of being equal.
Yes, the $100 million is very much on track.
So as we get into more HF you would see that overall, the margin will remain at a group level quite solid.
So, for Navin, the operating leverage on 32 is going to be fantastic.
532504|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, capex pipeline and the 32-33% margin range, but cautious and evasive on R32 pricing, the DRDO order economics, AHF split and CDMO molecule-level details, which management repeatedly declined to quantify. Management leaned on "wait and see" framing for Chemours scale-up and on the 15-month window.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides 32-33% EBITDA margin (plus/minus 1%) normalised, but Q1 FY27 was 34.2% and gross margin fell about 100 bps QoQ on raw material inflation with pass-through lagging, so the guide implies flat-to-lower margins from here.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Up to 15,000 MT R32 HFC capacity (taking total from about 9,000-10,000 MT to about 25,000 MT) is on track for Q3 FY27 commissioning, Chemours liquid cooling completes end Q2 FY27, and Dahej MPP debottlenecking completes by Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 FY27 revenue up 44% YoY to about INR1,045 crore with HPP up 33%, specialty chemicals up 48% and CDMO up 82%; CDMO FY27 target of about $100 million is reiterated as on track and 4-5 agchem campaign orders are planned this year.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: already announced; phase 1 around mid-Q4 FY27
rows.why: Board approved INR90 crore internally funded advanced materials adoption capex at Surat, and CDMO cGMP4 Phase 2 of INR125 crore is operational around Q4 FY27 with the INR288 crore approved base; utilisation was not disclosed, so no further capex is signalled yet.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the $100 million CDMO FY27 target and 32-33% margin range, but gave no revenue or margin raise, and flagged raw material cost inflation and LatAm agchem pricing pressure.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gross margin fell about 100 bps QoQ on raw material costs with pass-through lagging, and 3-4 CDMO molecules face FDA readouts in the next 8-12 months after one readout did not go well, both of which bear on the $100 million CDMO target and the margin range.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Five products are lab-approved and to be taken to commercial-scale qualification via the INR90 crore adoption capex (first phase around mid-Q4 FY27), and 13-14 new agchem molecules were launched last year with 5 more in participation, 3 patented.

rows.label: R32 long-term contracts (35-45% of capacity over five years)
rows.why: A couple of R32 contracts are signed and more are at a late stage, targeting 35-45% contracted share of the expanded capacity over five years, though no pricing was disclosed.

rows.label: Advanced materials as a material business by end of decade
rows.why: Target is to build advanced materials into a material unit modelled on CDMO, targeting data centres, electronics, semiconductors and defence, with Chemours liquid cooling completion at end Q2 FY27 and about $1 million of two-phase coolant sold in the quarter per analyst; no revenue number was given.

rows.label: CDMO FDA readouts for 3-4 molecules
rows.why: Pipeline of 30-40 molecules with about 10 late stage; 3-4 expected FDA readouts after one readout did not go well, and these underpin the $100 million FY27 CDMO target and 3x asset turn on INR288 crore by FY29.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the capex pipeline (R32 Q3 FY27, CDMO Phase 2 Q4 FY27) and the 32-33% margin range, but cautious and evasive on R32 pricing, DRDO economics, AHF split and CDMO molecule details, which analysts pressed on and management declined to quantify.

532505|2026-03.headline: UCO Bank FY26 net profit rose 13.21% to Rs 2,768 crore; gross NPA fell to 2.17%, and FY27 guidance was held at 12-14% credit growth.
532505|2026-03.overview: UCO Bank reported strong FY26 results, with gross advances up 19.44% YoY against 12-15% guidance and deposits up 11.59%. Asset quality improved, with gross NPA at 2.17% (down 52 bps), net NPA at 0.27%, and PCR at 97.79%. Management held FY27 guidance broadly unchanged despite analyst concern over the West Asia conflict, and said it holds about Rs 1,900 crore of provisioning buffers. Treasury was negative in Q4 due to MTM losses on AFS and HFT books.

segments.name: RAM (retail, agri, MSME)
segments.commentary: RAM advances grew 24%+ YoY, with retail up 26%+, agriculture up 26% and MSME up 19%. RAM share of book was 65%, against a 61-63% target.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Housing loans grew about 19% and car loans about 71%. Retail gold loans stood at about Rs 5,400 crore, and the 'others' bucket grew about 40% YoY, mainly on gold loans.

segments.name: Agriculture gold loans
segments.commentary: Agri gold loan book is about Rs 12,200 crore, so total gold loans are about Rs 18,000 crore at an estimated 8.5-9% yield.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: Q4 treasury income was negative Rs 16 crore versus about Rs 130 crore in Q3, after a Rs 135 crore MTM hit on the AFS book. Management cited a Rs 848 crore treasury segment profit against Rs 557 crore, which it said it would clarify offline.

guidance_outlook: FY27 deposit growth 10-12%, credit growth 12-14% (unchanged on deposits, credit range held at 12-14%).
FY27 CASA 37-38%; RAM share raised to 62-65%; CD ratio 80-82%.
FY27 credit cost below 0.75%; global NIM 2.8-2.9%.
FY27 gross NPA below 2%, net NPA below 0.2%, slippage ratio below 1%.
FY27 recovery and upgradation target Rs 2,000-2,500 crore.
ROA of 0.87% in FY26; management expects 0.95-1% by end of FY27.
FY27 IT budget above Rs 1,000 crore, following Rs 899 crore spend in FY26.
capex_capacity: Network: 3,412 domestic branches plus 2 overseas branches (Hong Kong, Singapore) and 1 representative office in Iran; 110 branches added in FY26; 61% of domestic branches in rural and semi-urban areas.
IT spend rose from Rs 576 crore (FY24) to Rs 642 crore (FY25) and Rs 899 crore (FY26).
Completed: CBDC app on iOS and Android, Murex treasury, Kolkata data centre consolidation, API gateway, ALM TPM automation, MuleHunter integration.

Planned for FY27: omnichannel mobile banking, cash management, supply chain finance, RPA, forex and prepaid cards, document management, e-notes, identity access management, Kolkata DR, centralised forex processing, and a CASA back office.
QIP approved by the Board, but management will seek shareholder approval at the AGM first and will not launch it this quarter.
demand_pricing: Corporate pipeline of about Rs 14,000 crore, but disbursement is held back by pricing; management said it will not grow corporate credit at the cost of margins.
Demand is coming from renewables, data centres, smart metering and road projects.
AAA-rated exposure is about 33% of the book (unchanged YoY); AA exposure fell to 26% from 29%.
About 65% of the loan book is linked to the repo rate; retail and MSME make up over Rs 1.1 lakh crore of the book.
CD ratio rose to 80.21% from the 75-77% target, which led the bank to push deposit mobilisation, with a focus on retail term deposits, savings and current accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 guidance (credit growth of 12-14%) a sign that the West Asia conflict is weighing on the bank, and is SMA 1 rising stress for MSMEs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guidance is conservative and has been 12-14% for three years while actual credit growth was 16% in FY24, 17.72% in FY25 and 19.44% in FY26. It attributed the rise in SMA 1 (to Rs 651 crore from Rs 260 crore) to the February 28-day effect rather than stress, and said total SMA 0-2 is 0.45% of standard advances.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs fall to Rs 182 crore from Rs 278 crore QoQ, and what buffers exist against ECL and the Labour Code?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the drop reflects a Rs 260 crore PLI provision in FY25, of which only about Rs 100 crore was paid in FY26, leaving about Rs 160 crore provided. It said it holds an ECL provision of Rs 1,038 crore, a Rs 341 crore contingency provision, and a Rs 530 crore COVID provision, for about Rs 1,900 crore of total buffers.

qa_highlights.question: Given the share price and the Rs 1,900 crore buffer, will the bank raise capital this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no plans to raise capital this quarter. It will seek AGM approval first and then launch the QIP at an opportune time when markets support it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-to-income drop driven by, and what is the outlook for ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited fee income growth of 32% QoQ and 25% YoY, and tighter control of controllable costs, with recoveries from written-off accounts at about Rs 1,300 crore in FY26 against Rs 2,400-2,500 crore a year earlier. It expects ROA to reach 0.95-1% by end of FY27, from 0.87% now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the West Asia war on MSMEs, and what share is covered by CGTMSE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not seen a major impact, with MSME slippages flat QoQ and no sharp rise in SMA. About 40% of advances are covered under CGTMSE.

qa_highlights.question: Why was treasury negative and what is the AFS reserve position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 treasury income was negative Rs 16 crore versus about Rs 130 crore in Q3, after a Rs 135 crore AFS MTM hit as yields rose above 7%. Yields have since eased to 6.95-6.98%, and AFS reserves stood at negative Rs 140 crore at March 2026.

risks_watch: Corporate loan growth could stay subdued while pricing discipline holds back disbursements from the Rs 14,000 crore pipeline.
The West Asia conflict may weigh on MSMEs; watch SMA 1 and SMA 2 buckets and MSME slippages in Q1 FY27.
Bond yields and treasury MTM could swing again; FY26 AFS reserves were negative Rs 140 crore.
Employee costs could rise when the Rs 160 crore residual PLI provision is paid, and the Labour Code effect is not yet quantified.
Deposit growth may lag credit growth (11.59% vs 19.44%), which keeps CD ratio pressure on margins; watch whether bulk deposits rise.
Management did not clarify the Rs 848 crore treasury segment profit figure on the call and said it would respond offline.
532505|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on headline delivery, with management repeatedly stressing that FY26 results beat guidance. Defensive on the FY27 guidance and SMA questions, where it attributed changes to the February day-count effect and to the bank's conservative pricing, not to stress.
key_quotes: So, there is no such thing that because of this temporary crisis, we have shifted our guidance downwards.
We do not want credit growth in the Corporate segment at the cost of margins.
February impacts every financial year. SMA 2 is 60 days, but February has 28 days, while January and March have 31 days.
So, all three put together today, we are holding around Rs.1,900 crore of additional provision as a buffer towards our ECL framework.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Fee income rose 32% to Rs 516 crore and cost-to-income fell 581 bps to 52.66%, and ROA is targeted at 0.95-1% from 0.87%; against that, global NIM guidance is 2.8-2.9% and CD ratio is rising to 80.21%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Network stands at 3,412 domestic branches after 110 added in FY26, with no further branch additions guided; the FY27 spend is on IT and back-office, not new physical capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Credit growth guidance of 12-14% and deposit growth of 10-12% imply continued expansion from a 19.44% advance growth base in FY26, backed by RAM growth of 24%+ and a Rs 14,000 crore corporate pipeline.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex discussion is limited to IT (FY27 budget above Rs 1,000 crore vs Rs 899 crore in FY26) and no utilisation figure or new plant was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Credit grew 19.44% in FY26 against 12-14% FY27 guidance, and management called the guide conservative, but corporate disbursements are held back by pricing on a Rs 14,000 crore pipeline.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Credit growth guidance of 12-14% sits well below the 19.44% delivered in FY26, and the Rs 160 crore residual PLI payment and unquantified Labour Code effect could pressure employee costs; the risk is more that guidance is conservative than that it is cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management has a dated FY27 plan for omnichannel mobile banking, cash management, supply chain finance, forex and prepaid cards, and e-notes, following completed CBDC app and Murex treasury projects.

rows.label: Corporate loan pricing discipline
rows.why: Management will not grow corporate credit at the cost of margins, so the Rs 14,000 crore pipeline converts only if pricing clears, which caps credit growth near the 12-14% guide.

rows.label: Asset quality and recovery target
rows.why: Gross NPA is at 2.17% against a sub-2% FY27 target, and the recovery and upgradation target is Rs 2,000-2,500 crore against about Rs 1,300 crore recovered from written-off accounts in FY26.

rows.label: QIP after AGM approval
rows.why: The Board has approved a QIP, but the launch needs AGM approval and waits for market conditions; there is no plan to raise this quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 delivery, ROA path and recoveries, but defensive on the FY27 guidance and the SMA 1 rise to Rs 651 crore from Rs 260 crore, and it left the Rs 848 crore treasury segment profit figure to be clarified offline.

532505|2026-06.headline: UCO Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 8% YoY to Rs 656 crore despite a Rs 1,237 crore one-time DTA charge; operating profit up 79.8% to Rs 2,810 crore.
532505|2026-06.overview: UCO Bank reported Q1 FY27 with advances up 21.18% YoY to Rs 2,72,768 crore and deposits up 11.28% to Rs 3,32,315 crore. Operating profit rose 79.8% to Rs 2,810 crore, helped by Rs 1,018 crore of technical write-off recoveries, of which about Rs 800 crore is from a few accounts management does not expect to recur. Net profit was held to Rs 656 crore by total tax of Rs 1,919 crore, including a one-time Rs 1,237 crore DTA remeasurement on the shift to the new tax regime. Management said most asset-quality and margin metrics were within guidance, and that it would review credit growth guidance only after Q2.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,919 crore (regular ~Rs 625 crore plus one-time DTA Rs 1,237 crore)

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -55 bps YoY; NNPA -20 bps YoY
Was 54.06% last year and 52.66% in March; management expects normalised ~50%

segments.name: Retail

qa_highlights.question: Can management give full-year guidance on cost of funds, cost of deposits, cost-to-income, RAM and corporate advances, ROE and ROA?

qa_highlights.question: What upside does UCO get from West Bengal's investment climate, given its Kolkata head office?

qa_highlights.question: What would ROA have been under the old tax regime, and what are NIM, ROA and EBITDA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No figure given; the shift to the new regime is statutory. Management said ROA could have been above 1% excluding the Rs 1,237 crore charge, a rough estimate. ROA of 0.68% now, seen near 1% by year-end; NIM guidance 2.8-2.9%.

qa_highlights.question: Where is competition coming from (PSU, private, NBFC)?

qa_highlights.question: Should the 12-14% credit growth guidance be raised given 21% actual growth?

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECLGS sanction and disbursement, and is any MSME stress visible?

qa_highlights.question: How much ECL provision is already held versus the requirement?

qa_highlights.question: Retail loan pricing trends and corporate pricing; was there JP Associates interest recovery in TWO income?

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of deposits rise QoQ, why did fee income from loan processing fall, and what drove other commission?

532505|2026-09.headline: UCO Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 26.77% YoY to Rs 786 crore; advances grew 24.70%, well above the 12-14% guidance.
532505|2026-09.overview: UCO Bank reported Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs 786 crore, up 26.77% YoY from Rs 620 crore, with operating profit of Rs 1,872 crore (up 16.04%). Global advances grew 24.70% to Rs 2,87,690 crore, while deposits grew 14.36% to Rs 3,49,590 crore and CASA ratio slipped to 36.77%. Gross NPA fell 60 bps YoY to 1.96% and net NPA to 0.18%, both within guidance. Management said the quarter's slippage rise was mainly agriculture crop-loan marking done half-yearly in September, and that the June quarter had a one-off Rs 785 crore recovery that did not recur.

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -60 bps YoY; NNPA -25 bps YoY

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 30.23% YoY; housing loan growth above 20% YoY with average home-loan ticket up from about Rs 35 lakh to about Rs 45 lakh.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri advances grew 29.59% YoY; agri slippages rose to Rs 205 crore in Q2 from Rs 73 crore in Q1, but were below Rs 238 crore a year ago.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 20.32% YoY; management sees scope for more growth here.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew 24.15% YoY; sanctioned but undisbursed corporate pipeline is about Rs 10,000 crore.

segments.name: RAM portfolio
segments.commentary: RAM portfolio is Rs 1,68,736 crore, up 26.92% YoY, and its share of advances has crossed 65% against the 62-65% guidance.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Hong Kong and Singapore branches are operating; GIFT City IBU opened in Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Advances growth guidance of 12-14% for FY27 was kept; management said it aims to grow above guidance but will not revise it mid-year.
Deposit growth guidance of 10-12% was exceeded (actual 14%+).
GNPA guidance is below 2% by 31 March 2027; already at 1.96%.
Net NPA guidance is below 0.25% for the year; already at 0.18%.
Global NIM guidance of 2.80-2.90% was exceeded (3.00%); management expects to sustain NIM above guidance with repo pass-through.
Credit cost guidance is below 0.75% for FY27; Q2 is 0.65%.
Cost-to-income expected to be around 50% for the full year and possibly below 50% next year.
ECL transition on 1 April 2027 estimated at about Rs 3,200 crore+ requirement; bank has provided about Rs 2,500 crore over and above existing provisions.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 3,439 after adding 27 branches in the quarter; business per branch Rs 185 crore vs Rs 161 crore a year ago.
Business per employee Rs 30 crore vs Rs 25 crore a year ago.

Digital business balance sheet under Project Parivartan above Rs 48,000 crore as of 30 September 2026.
Seven processes automated via RPA; digital marketing solution onboarded; customer 360-degree portal rolled out in branches.
Recruitment of specialist officers (data analysts, CAs, trade finance officers) in FY27; further recruitment of professional officers and customer service associates planned.

Deposit rates unchanged for now; management said no immediate need to raise term deposit rates, with any hike applying only to new deposits and renewals.
Gold loan yield is about 9% (slightly below) and unchanged QoQ.
Housing loan growth above 20% YoY from both volume and ticket size; second-hand car loans are not tracked separately and are small.
Domestic yield on advances 8.11%; global yield 7.79%; cost of funds 4.44%, up slightly.

qa_highlights.question: Recoveries from written-off accounts fell to Rs 301 crore from Rs 1,018 crore; is this a normalised rate, and what is the treasury outlook given rising yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the June quarter included a one-off Rs 785 crore recovery from one large account; excluding it, June recovery was about Rs 233 crore, so Rs 301 crore is the normalised run-rate. On treasury, management said yield hardening pressures profitability, but ~66% of advances are repo/EBLR-linked, so NII gains should offset treasury losses; FVTPL book is small.

qa_highlights.question: Slippages rose from Rs 428 crore to Rs 538 crore and SMA-1 rose from Rs 228 crore to Rs 437 crore; what is driving this?
qa_highlights.answer: Slippages were Rs 549 crore in the quarter per management; the rise is mainly half-yearly crop-loan agriculture marking in September. SMA-1 and SMA-2 (Rs 1 crore and above) stood at 0.42% vs 0.77% a year ago, with a QoQ uptick described as manageable.

qa_highlights.question: Will deposit rates be raised, and with what lag?
qa_highlights.answer: No immediate need to raise deposit rates; current term deposit rates maintained. Any hike would apply only to new deposits and renewals, decided later based on deposit requirement.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a change in corporate stance, and will the bank raise its credit growth target?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate advances grew 24.15% YoY; RAM share crossed 65% (guidance 62-65%) and is expected to hold around 65%. Corporate sanctioned but undisbursed pipeline is about Rs 10,000 crore, dependent on lending rates and capex. Guidance of 12-14% kept; management aims to exceed it but will not revise mid-year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL transition estimate for 1 April 2027 and has it changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Transition requirement estimated at about Rs 2,500 crore in one answer and Rs 3,200 crore-plus in another; bank has provided about Rs 2,500 crore over and above existing provisions, including COVID provisions of Rs 530 crore, extra provisions of Rs 341 crore and about Rs 1,600 crore ECL-specific. Estimate not materially changed from three months earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gold loan yield and how is it trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loan yield is around 9%, slightly below; no change QoQ as no rate changes were made. Any EBLR-linked gold loans will reprice with the repo hike.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other operating expenses rise by about Rs 160 crore, and is it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is normal, reflecting IT investment, physical infrastructure and network expansion, plus a lag in opex growth in earlier quarters; expected to stay in a similar range, depending on transaction volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost and cost-to-income outlook for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost was 0.65% vs guidance below 0.75%, with ECL provisioning of Rs 570 crore in the quarter and accelerated NPA provisioning to bring NNPA to 0.18%. Cost-to-income was 50.39% (about 45% excluding the June one-off effect); expected around 50% for FY27 and possibly below 50% next year.

qa_highlights.question: Second-hand car loan growth and yield, and housing ticket size?
qa_highlights.answer: Second-hand car loans are not tracked separately and are a small share of car loans; management will work out numbers. Average home-loan ticket rose from about Rs 35 lakh to about Rs 45 lakh, with growth from both volume and ticket size.

qa_highlights.question: Is NII growth enough to offset treasury stress, and what NIM is expected in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said repo-linked NII growth (about 66% of advances) would more than offset treasury stress, and that FVTPL exposure is small. Global NIM was 3.00% and domestic 3.19%, against guidance of 2.80-2.90%; management expects to sustain NIM above guidance.

ECL transition on 1 April 2027: requirement of about Rs 2,500-3,200 crore plus, with Rs 2,500 crore already provided; any further top-up depends on profitability.

So, overall, the asset quality has been maintained.
We are ready to take up the growth, whatever the credit growth we can take up in all the sectors.

532508|2026-03.headline: Jindal Stainless Q4FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 37% YoY to INR1,455 crore; FY27 volume guided at 7-9% with EBITDA/ton of INR18,000-20,000 for H1 only.
532508|2026-03.overview: Q4FY26 deliveries were 0.64 million tons, flat YoY, while consolidated EBITDA rose about 37% YoY and 3% QoQ to INR1,455 crore and PAT rose about 41% YoY to INR834 crore. For FY26, volumes grew 8% to 2.57 million tons, EBITDA rose 19% to INR5,560 crore and PAT rose 27% to INR3,185 crore. Net debt fell to INR3,040 crore (0.55x net debt/EBITDA). Management flagged a sharp, sudden rise in gas and utility costs from the Middle East conflict (up around 2.5x-3x), a temporary QCO suspension, and CBAM uncertainty, and gave FY27 volume guidance but EBITDA/ton guidance only until H1.

financial_highlights.change: reduced further; net debt/EBITDA 0.55x, net debt/equity 0.15

segments.name: Stainless steel (India and Indonesia)
segments.commentary: Consolidated, with EBITDA/ton guidance covering the whole stainless business including Indonesia and Rathi. Domestic share about 92%, export share 8% of FY26 sales.

segments.name: RKEF nickel (Indonesia)
segments.commentary: Management said recent EBITDA has been around $3,000/ton of nickel versus a prior guided range of $500-1,500/ton, but flagged it is volatile and tied to Indonesian ore pricing formulas.

segments.name: Rathi (rebar subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Operated at about 80-85% utilisation in FY26; stainless rebar was about 25% of Q4 volume. Company stated Rathi is EBITDA positive, with no separate figures given.

segments.name: Jindal Stainless Steelway (fabrication subsidiary)
segments.commentary: First fabrication facility in Patalganga started operations, initial investment about INR125 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at 7-9% (management also said 'at least 8-10%' early in the call, later clarified as 7-9%).
FY27 EBITDA/ton guidance of INR18,000-20,000 for H1 FY27 only; to be reviewed after six months depending on the situation.
FY27 capex guidance around INR2,600 crore; FY28 capex to be given later.
Sales volume target of 3.5 million tons per annum by FY29, described as double-digit CAGR over three years.
CRAP capacity to reach 2.67 million tons per annum by FY28, including the 0.17 mtpa CRAP line at Jajpur and additional INR900 crore for cold rolling at Hisar and Kharagpur.
Indonesia melt shop (1.2 mtpa) ramp-up expected to reach 70-80% of capacity during FY27.
capex_capacity: Indonesia 1.2 mtpa stainless melt shop commissioned ahead of schedule; total melting capacity now 4.2 mtpa, of which 3 mtpa in India.
Jajpur 1.1 mtpa HRAP line upcoming commissioning; 0.17 mtpa CRAP line also at Jajpur.
Additional INR900 crore to augment cold rolling at Hisar and Kharagpur.
Maharashtra greenfield: land acquisition under way, most of this year expected to go into land acquisition; downstream to be built first, then upstream. Clear plan needs a few more months.
Partial commissioning of a 315 MW solar/wind hybrid project with Oyster Renewable Energy in Q4.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand cited as resilient across automotive, ornamental and industrial pipe and tube, railway, metro, lift and elevator, and white goods; metro and passenger coach demand strong, with stainless demand expected to rise 2-3x over 3-4 years.
Export volumes rose QoQ in Q4 despite subdued global trade; focus on Japan, Korea, Taiwan and Germany; Americas remain key.

Management said cost increases were only partly passed on to customers, depending on the product and competitor pricing; imports from competitors without the same cost increases were cited as a constraint.
Gas and utility costs (propane, LPG, natural gas, ammonia, acid) rose about 2.5-3x. Management declined to quantify gas consumption.
QCO suspended for six months; management said this encourages substandard imports and dampens MSME capacity plans. Antidumping verifiers to be appointed in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can volume and EBITDA/ton guidance be given for FY27 given Middle East headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 volume growth of 7-9% and EBITDA/ton of INR18,000-20,000 for H1, with a review after six months; availability of gas is no longer the constraint in May, but cost is much higher.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the export share falling, and what is the FY27 export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 exports were 8% of sales versus 9% in FY25. Management expects to hold 8-10% of exports in the FY27 volume growth, with disruption from the war and CBAM.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Maharashtra capex and the FY27/FY28 capex number?
qa_highlights.answer: Land acquisition is under way; FY27 capex guidance is about INR2,600 crore; FY28 figure deferred.

qa_highlights.answer: RKEF EBITDA recently around $3,000/ton of nickel versus the earlier $500-1,500 range. qa_highlights.question: What are the mitigation plans for gas shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: Jajpur has started using natural gas for part of its needs and plans to scale up; coal gasification/syngas and green hydrogen (600 mm cube plant at Jajpur, running June-July) are being pursued; Hisar and Ghaziabad are also being worked on.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 400 series share falling, and does it affect EBITDA/ton?
qa_highlights.answer: 400 series was 18% in FY26 versus 17% in FY25, with Q4 at 19-20%. Management said it is pursuing 400 series growth and only adds volumes that improve EBITDA/ton.

532508|2026-06.headline: Jindal Stainless Q1 FY27: revenue up 10.5% YoY and PAT up 7.7%, but finished-goods volume fell 7.3% on gas shortages; FY27 volume guidance held.

Revenue, EBITDA and PAT grew 10.5%, 1.4% and 7.7% YoY, with management prioritising value-added mix and thinner grades. Consolidated net debt fell to INR 2,950 crore (net debt/EBITDA 0.53x). Management kept FY27 volume guidance (8-10% growth) and the INR 18,000-20,000/t H1 EBITDA guidance, deferring any revision to the next quarter. Indonesia melt shop (1.2 MTPA) has started ramping up; the Jindal Stainless Indonesia structure changed from subsidiary to associate effective 1 July 2026.

532509|2026-03.overview: Management reported that Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,000 crore on a quarterly run rate, with consolidated PBT of about INR 97 crore, almost double last year. Full-year revenue grew about 17% and EBITDA about 19-20%, helped by the SCS (ex-SES) turnaround, which turned EBITDA positive in Q4 at about +2% after roughly -20% in Q1. Standalone and ex-SCS growth was more modest (standalone revenue +7.1%, ex-SCS consolidated revenue +8.7%). Management guided to double-digit FY27 revenue growth and a 12-13.5% consolidated EBITDA margin, with GCM (including SCS) margins rising from about 6% to 10-12%.

532522|2026-06.headline: Petronet Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 33% to INR 1,133 crore despite company LNG volumes falling to 207 TBTU, aided by trading and inventory gains.

Volumes fell: company LNG processed was 207 TBTU versus 220 TBTU a year earlier, and company utilisation was 58% versus 76%. Management attributed the profit resilience to trading gains of INR 301 crore and inventory gains of INR 193 crore, as Qatar supplies remained under force majeure and tolling cargoes from other sources replaced most of the gap. Dahej's nameplate capacity was raised from 17.5 to 22.5 MMTPA on 31 March 2026, which lowers reported utilisation.

532523|2026-03.headline: Biocon Q4 FY26 operating revenue up 10% YoY ex-lenalidomide to biosimilars-led growth; EBITDA Rs1,073 crore at 23% margin.

Management said the biosimilars and generics integration was completed in under 100 days and the major capex phase is substantially complete, shifting focus to utilisation, margins and deleveraging. Net debt has fallen to about $1.1 billion from more than $1.5 billion in March 2025, and interest cost savings of about Rs70-75 crore per quarter are now in the P&L.

rows.why: Biosimilars revenue grew 16% YoY to INR2,855 crore with management guiding to meaningful acceleration in H2, backed by Aflibercept US launch in August 2026 with contracts being tied up and insulin glargine US share gains, though price erosion is real.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said there will be no increase in US manufacturing capex and will use partnerships and existing US facilities; no utilisation figure was disclosed and no new capex plan was announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held biosimilar mid-20s margin guidance without going beyond it, and Syngene guides to single-digit rupee revenue decline in FY27 with H1 revenue down, so no raise is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Syngene revenue fell 16% YoY to INR736 crore on a key biologics client's lower offtake, with H1 FY27 revenue expected to decline; biosimilar price erosion and H2 acceleration delivery are also watch items.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Aflibercept (Yesafili) launched in the US in August 2026 and denosumab is launching in Europe, with management aiming for at least one new US or European launch every year through 2030.

rows.label: Aflibercept US launch ramp into H2 FY27
rows.why: Yesafili launched in the US in August 2026 with contracts being tied up; management expects a strong start building into H2 on biosimilar revenue of INR2,855 crore.

rows.label: Debt reduction from free cash flow
rows.why: Finance cost fell 23% YoY to INR213 crore, but net debt rose sequentially on inventory build (biosimilar DIO normalised to 280-290 days from over 400); FCF is to go first to debt reduction once inventory converts to sales.

rows.label: Inventory conversion to sales
rows.why: Working capital build is mostly inventory for H2 scale-up; conversion depends on the Aflibercept, denosumab and insulin ramp.

tone.note: Management was confident on biosimilar H2 acceleration, Aflibercept launch and the Malaysia insulin line, but cautious and deflecting on generics base growth, R&D cost drag and margin guidance beyond mid-20s; analysts pushed on generics competitive intensity, biosimilar margin normalisation from 27%

532524|2026-03.headline: PTC India Q4 FY26 standalone volume rose 24% YoY to 23.6 BU, but PAT fell 85% to ₹75.7 crore on the prior-year PEL sale gain.
532524|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone trading volume rose 24% YoY to 23.6 billion units, and FY26 volume grew 12% to 92.8 BU. Reported profit fell sharply because Q4 FY25 included the PEL (PTC Energy) sale gain of about ₹521 crore; excluding it, standalone PAT rose 18% to ₹75.74 crore for the quarter and was flat at ₹397 crore for the year. Management said the DISCOM liquidity surplus cut rebate and surcharge income (rebate fell from ₹121 crore to ₹97 crore), so operating income held near ₹450 crore for the year. The board has lifted its pause on the PFS divestment, with the route and advisers still to be decided by a board committee.

financial_highlights.change: Q4 down from ₹17.6; FY26 down from ₹28.88
Around ₹2,400 crore as of call date (approx.)

segments.name: Short-term / exchange trading
segments.commentary: Now about 56% of business by management's account, up from the 50:50 target mix, driving most of the Q4 volume growth. Competes with more than 70 licensed traders.

segments.name: Cross-border and long-term trading
segments.commentary: Management describes a niche edge here with only about 4-6 credible competitors. Cross-border is one of three cited moats alongside balance sheet and relationships.

segments.name: Renewable energy certificates (REC)
segments.commentary: 68 lakh certificates delivered in FY26 to cover balance renewable obligations. The company also trades power for Himachal Pradesh from 14 hydro projects.

segments.name: Consultancy and new initiatives
segments.commentary: Includes PM KUSUM smart meter and rooftop solar work, an ADB project for Laos, Thailand and Cambodia, and BESS power trading. Green power supply to GAIL Vijaipur green hydrogen (10 MW) is also in place.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth expected to track or slightly exceed national power demand growth of about 5% a year.
Trading margins guided flat, with movement of only plus or minus a few basis points; growth to come from volume rather than margin.
Medium- and short-term contracts expected to take a larger share; long-term contracts may shrink to 10-12 years from 25.
PFS divestment process restarted after the board lifted its pause; a board committee will decide the structure over the next few months, with material developments to be disclosed.
NLC India JV: about 2,000 MW initial hydro/renewable portfolio, subject to DIPAM-level government approval.
Teesta Urja: cofferdam phase to supply about 40-50% of capacity by September or October 2026; full dam completion targeted for 2029.
capex_capacity: Net cash about ₹2,800 crore at 31 March 2026, around ₹2,400 crore on the call date, per management.
Cash is held for working capital needs (the business is cyclical), a strategic 'war chest' for small, value-adding investments, and returns to shareholders.
NLC India JV: MoU for about 2,000 MW initially; may go higher or lower depending on government permissions.
Teesta Urja hydro: cofferdam phase first, full dam later.
PFS divestment proceeds would be reinvested in trading-adjacent opportunities; management said no fixed return benchmark will be applied.
demand_pricing: Management reported record peak demand of about 260 GW the previous day; electricity demand is growing about 5% a year.
Renewables reached about 26% of energy consumed, against a 29% government target for the year.
Competition is intense on exchange and short-term trades, with over 70 licensed traders. Margins are under pressure; management says trading margin growth is difficult.
Customer base is more than 800 consumers. Data centres and green hydrogen are emerging demand segments.
Rebate and surcharge income fell as DISCOM payments became timely, reducing income.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT contribution from the PEL sale and how will it affect future earnings?
qa_highlights.answer: The PEL sale produced a PBT gain of about ₹521 crore in the prior year, and PAT from PEL was about ₹33 crore in FY25. FY26 numbers have no PEL profit and are a good base for trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: What volume growth do you expect over the next 2-3 years, and is PFS divestment still on?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth is expected at about 5%, slightly above national growth. The board's pause on PFS divestment has been lifted, and a board committee will decide the structure over the next few months.

qa_highlights.question: How intense is competition, and does it pressure margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition is strong on exchange trades (over 70 traders) and limited in long-term and cross-border trades (about 4-6 players). Growth will come from volume, not margin expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How will the large cash balance be deployed, and what is the return hurdle?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash is kept for cyclical working capital, strategic investments that add value to the core business, and returns to shareholders. Management said it would not hold the company to a fixed ROCE or IRR benchmark that delays value realisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pipeline across long-, medium- and short-term contracts, and how are spreads moving?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term contracts are harder to win, with more focus on medium- and short-term deals. Spreads are not expected to rise much or fall much, with margin changes of plus or minus a few basis points.

qa_highlights.question: What are the NLC JV plans, capex and timing, and what is net cash and asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: NLC JV targets about 2,000 MW initially, awaiting DIPAM approval, with no timeline. Net cash is about ₹2,800 crore at March-end and about ₹2,400 crore now. Management said distressed assets were largely resolved and remaining ones are expected to be resolved in the near term.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from competition, with management saying margins will stay roughly flat in the next 2-3 years.
Reliance on short-term exchange trades, which raises volume volatility and reduces contract visibility.
Lower rebate and surcharge income as DISCOM payments improve; this has already cut income.
PFS divestment timing, route and value, with no investment banker yet announced.
Capital allocation of a large cash balance (about ₹2,400-2,800 crore) without a stated return target.
Asset quality of the remaining financing book, which management would not detail.
NLC JV and Teesta Urja timelines depend on government approvals and construction schedules.

key_quotes: Margins we don't expect to grow substantially. Marginal, you know, decimal percentage is plus and minus.
So if many people enter into this space and I think many people have entered but then their volumes speak for themselves.
Now we have to report now that that particular decision to pause is not there.

rows.why: Teesta cofferdam supplies about 40-50% of capacity by Sep/Oct 2026 and full dam is targeted for 2029, but NLC JV's ~2,000 MW MoU is subject to DIPAM approval with no timeline, so no firm capacity date is in place.

rows.why: Net cash of about ₹2,800 crore (March 2026) is held for working capital, small value-adding investments and shareholder returns, with no fixed return benchmark stated.

rows.why: Gross debtor days fell to 44 from 51 and net working capital days to 8 from 19, with gross debtors down to about ₹4,380 crore from ₹4,762 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume growth, cash position and franchise moats, but cautious on margins and evasive on PFS divestment details, asset quality and capital deployment, deferring specifics to future disclosures.

532524|2026-06.headline: PTC India Q1 FY27 standalone PBT fell 32% to Rs 96 crore on 12% higher trading volume of 25.78 BU, as lower surcharge and rebate income offset gains.
532524|2026-06.overview: Trading volume rose 12% to 25.78 billion units at a stated margin of 3.35 paise per unit, and total operating income rose 2% to Rs 113 crore. Standalone PBT fell 32% to Rs 96 crore and PAT fell 33% to Rs 71 crore, which management attributed to lower net surcharge and rebate income as Discoms' liquidity improved. Consolidated PBT fell 48% to Rs 151 crore, also reflecting a Rs 82 crore impairment reversal in the year-ago quarter. Management declared an interim dividend of Rs 23 per share, which it described as one-time, linked to the PTC Energy (PEL) asset sale to ONGC.

segments.name: Power trading
segments.commentary: Volume up 12% to 25.78 BU, with 60% from exchange-traded products and the rest bilateral short, medium and long-term. Management said the volume growth came mainly from exchange trade.

segments.name: Consultancy / C&I services
segments.commentary: Management said the business is steadily growing and is a stable piece, but declined to give projections. No figures were disclosed.

segments.name: Power exchange associates
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 total income Rs 13.98 crore and PAT about Rs 5.16 crore, as disclosed in response to a question.

segments.name: PTC Financial Services (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Management described performance as less than spectacular. Its PBT decline also drove part of the consolidated fall, and the company is now looking to divest it, with SBI Capital engaged as transaction advisor.

guidance_outlook: Management expects power demand to grow 4%-6% annually, with short-term volatility from weather.

Long-term capacity additions: management said no new long-term contracts are expected in FY27 or FY28 because of regulatory constraints. Growth will come from battery storage and time-of-day/seasonal trades.
NTPC Green 1,200 MW long-term solar PPA is expected to come online around FY29.
Teesta Urja (1.2 GW) is under construction; a cofferdam-stage power start is expected around December 2026, with about 40%-50% generation initially.
Interim dividend of Rs 23 per share is a one-time measure and should not be expected annually.
PFS disinvestment: management expects to say more to the market closer to the end of FY27; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Long-term PPA of 1,200 MW signed with NTPC Green for solar power procurement, expected online around FY29.
Teesta Urja 1.2 GW hydro project under construction after the cloudburst-related washout, with staged commissioning.
NLC India JV: DPE approval received; Board has approved investment of up to Rs 500 crore, to be deployed over time.
Battery storage: management said it is in discussions and evaluating whether to own storage assets or contract for storage services, with no tie-up announced.
demand_pricing: Standalone PBT decline was driven by lower net surcharge and rebate income, which management attributed to improved Discom liquidity and Discoms paying on time to capture rebates.
Long-term volume decline YoY was attributed to lower hydro generation under long-term agreements.
Management said pricing is competitive and that some contracts are taken as marketing calls. Trading margins are expected to depend on portfolio mix, with exchange markets providing lower margins.

Management said trading on spot and exchange markets is only about 8,000-9,000 MW against peak demand of about 260,000 MW, and that policy changes such as merchant capacity mandates could deepen the market.
Contracts for difference (SECI pilot) and the futures market were cited as policy developments.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the long-term PPA book expires in the next one to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nothing is likely to expire in the next three years. It did not give the average remaining tenor and promised data by email.

qa_highlights.question: Why did long-term capacity decline YoY, and will it grow?
qa_highlights.answer: The decline was due to lower hydro generation under long-term agreements. Management said no new long-term contracts are expected in FY27 or FY28 due to regulatory constraints.

qa_highlights.question: Why did rebate income decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Discoms are now paying early and capturing rebates themselves, while PTC pays generators early and then recovers from Discoms later, so PTC's net rebate income fell.

qa_highlights.question: Why was a Rs 17.4 crore provision booked (Note 8)?
qa_highlights.answer: It relates to a generator's claim from a legal dispute over a contract. The adjudicating authority ruled that PTC pay first and recover later. The provision was made on auditor consultation, with no clear visibility on recovery from the counterparty.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash position and who are the top debtors?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone net cash was Rs 2,451 crore at 30 June, before the interim dividend. Top debtors: Punjab (about Rs 860 crore), UP (about Rs 600 crore), Haryana (about Rs 500 crore), Rajasthan (about Rs 400 crore), and Tamil Nadu (about Rs 300 crore). Management said PTC's own exposure is not more than 60 days, as back-to-back pass-through items inflate gross debtors.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for PFS and how much stake will PTC keep?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a transaction advisor (SBI Capital) is appointed and the process is under way. No stake or timeline was committed, and the structure depends on advisor input.

qa_highlights.question: Will CERC's HPX rule affect PTC?
qa_highlights.answer: The CERC rule caps shareholding at 5% for trading members. PTC holds more than 22% of HPX, so it cannot be a trading member unless it reduces its stake below 5%, which management said depends on several factors.

risks_watch: Lower net surcharge and rebate income: management attributes it to improved Discom liquidity and early Discom payments, and called the cyclicality uncertain; no split of surcharge between long-term and short-term sources was given, with data promised by email.

Receivables: gross debtors of Rs 4,469 crore at 30 June, with Punjab (about Rs 860 crore), UP (about Rs 600 crore) and Haryana (about Rs 500 crore) as the largest; management says PTC's own exposure is not more than 60 days, but back-to-back items inflate the figure.
Rs 17.4 crore provision (Note 8) for a generator's legal claim; recovery from the counterparty is not assured and may lead to further litigation.
Long-term book and volumes: long-term volume fell YoY on lower hydro generation; no new long-term contracts expected in FY27 or FY28; average remaining PPA tenor not disclosed.
Timing risk on new capacity: Teesta Urja (1.2 GW) first power around December 2026 at 40%-50% initially; NTPC Green 1,200 MW PPA around FY29; battery storage still in discussion with no tie-up.

PFS disinvestment: transaction advisor (SBI Capital) appointed; no stake, structure or timeline committed beyond 'closer to end of FY27'. HPX: PTC holds more than 22% and cannot be a trading member unless it cuts below 5%.
key_quotes: Obviously, this kind of dividend, 23 rupees per share, cannot be sustained or should not be expected every year.
Nothing is likely to expire in next three years.
But as far as the PTC exposure is concerned, so that is not more than, I will say not more than 60 days wherein PTC has taken an exposure and that is pending.
So, we are not expecting to add any long-term contracts in that duration.

532525|2026-03.headline: Bank of Maharashtra FY26: net profit INR7,019 crore (+27% YoY), full-year NIM 3.91%, ROA 1.86%, all guidance met; FY27 ROA guidance 1.80%.
532525|2026-03.overview: Management reported that all FY26 guidance metrics were met, several with headroom, with total business up 17% and advances up 22% YoY. Gross NPA fell 29 bps to 1.45% and net NPA to 0.13%, while operating profit rose 16% to INR10,826 crore. Management created an INR200 crore "global geopolitical uncertainties" provision in Q4 as a buffer against the West Asia crisis, and said stress is not yet visible in MSME. Non-interest income was weak (2.51% growth) due to a one-time INR290 crore MTM hit from the RRB amalgamation. FY27 guidance was issued across 18-19 parameters, with ROA lifted to 1.80%.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail grew 32% YoY; home loans +29%, vehicle loans +56%, gold loans +53% to INR24,000 crore, of which about INR5,000 crore is co-lent with NBFCs. Retail slippages in Q4 were about INR100 crore.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate book grew 22% YoY, with RAM split 63:37 (retail/agri/MSME vs corporate). Corporate reported no slippages in Q4; INR72,000 crore sanctioned in FY26 with INR34,500 crore undisbursed.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME grew 11% YoY (about INR6,000 crore added per management); MSME NPA fell to 1.54%. Q4 MSME slippages were about INR400 crore.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri grew 13% YoY; agri NPA was 7.72% (about INR3,100 crore). Q4 agri slippages were about INR300 crore.

segments.name: GIFT City IBU
segments.commentary: Overseas advances rose to INR6,142 crore from INR3,517 crore (2% of book). Management said the IBU turned profitable in March after covering all overheads; 650 million USD booked against a 1 billion USD 12-month aspiration.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: AFS reserve swung from +INR175 crore in Q3 to -INR362 crore at 31 March; FVTPL MTM gain of about INR40-45 crore booked.

guidance_outlook: FY27 total business growth 16-17%; advances 18%; deposits 14-15%; CASA around 50%.
RAM growth 18% with RAM corporate mix at 60:40 (+/-2%); non-interest income growth 10%; NII growth 15%.
FY27 NIM guidance 3.75%; cost to income below 40%; ROA 1.80%; ROE 20% or more.
GNPA within 2%, NNPA within 0.25%, slippage below 1%, credit cost around 1%, PCR around 98%, CRAR maintained at 18%.
Management expects FY27 tax at about 10% of PBT (OP tax rate 13-14%), with PBT-basis tax about 18-20%, after unabsorbed losses of about INR1,200-1,300 crore were used up in Q1.
Debt waiver: about INR2,000 crore expected (INR917 crore overdue + INR1,067 crore NPA eligible KCC accounts), with approval expected Q2 to Q3 FY27; agri NPA could fall to about 5.33%.
capex_capacity: Project 321: 321 new branches in the first 3-year phase, 183 functional to date; Board has approved 1,000 branches over 5 years.
GIFT City IBU: first business booked September 2025; retail products planned for H2 FY27.
PLI for Scale 4 and above not yet released; 100% provision made, release pending discussions.
demand_pricing: Management expects West Asia crisis impact to show from Q2 FY27 rather than Q1, with Brent above USD115 cited as a risk; no MSME stress seen as of March.
Q4 SMA-1 was INR241 crore and SMA-2 INR56 crore as of 31 March (per analyst).
Management said it would price risk more carefully where risk rises, but gave no specific pricing action.
Pool/assignment book of about INR14,000 crore is largely lent to AA/AAA NBFCs; security cover is low as it is pool-based.
Gold co-lending slowed after RBI's CLM1 guidelines from 1 January 2026; fresh underwriting resumed in early March, with 9 NBFC co-lending partners signed.

qa_highlights.question: How will the West Asia war affect corporate and MSME accounts from April onward, and what stress is visible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no stress was visible in March and MSME NPA fell to 1.54%, but impact is expected from Q2 FY27 and depends on how long the crisis lasts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the special provision fall to INR1,010 crore from INR1,200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the COVID buffer was released, and a new INR200 crore global geopolitical uncertainties provision was built in Q4, with no regulatory prescription behind it.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the one-time non-interest income drag?
qa_highlights.answer: A one-time INR290 crore MTM provision was taken on investments in the RRB (Vidharbha Konkan Gramin Bank) that was amalgamated into a single Maharashtra RRB, with the bank as sponsor.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net worth fall QoQ and gold loans drop about 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Net worth fell due to AFS reserve movement and dividends (interim 10% plus final 12%, about INR1,692 crore total). Gold loans dropped because fresh underwriting paused during the shift from CLM2 to CLM1 co-lending; underwriting resumed in early March.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank is on the normal tax rate from Q2 FY26, with OP tax at 13-14%. FY27 PBT-basis tax is expected around 18-20%, and the call gave a 10% figure for the tax on PBT in the same answer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the segment split of Q4 slippages?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail about INR100 crore, agri about INR300 crore, MSME about INR400 crore, and corporate nil.

risks_watch: West Asia / crude-driven stress in MSME and corporate books from Q2 FY27; a 1.2% to 2% geopolitical provision top-up is open.
Timing and size of the state KCC debt waiver (about INR2,000 crore); the scheme is not yet approved.
Tax-rate normalisation to about 25% creates an earnings headwind; management guided FY27 PBT-basis tax at 18-20%, but the figures given on the call are inconsistent.
Non-interest income growth (2.51% in FY26) versus 10% target; a fee-income push is planned for FY27.
Gold co-lending volume recovery after CLM1 transition; the book fell about 17% QoQ.
Pending PLI payout for Scale 4 and above, and the NCLT recovery pipeline (about INR7,500 crore in NCLT).

key_quotes: we have been able to meet all the guidance and at some of the places with a decent margin above the guidance that was shared in the beginning of the year.
These are sacrosanct numbers for us. We will be achieving itself.
So we can only hope that the crisis resolves and what damage must have happened, the impact, how fast it can be replaced is also needs to be seen.

rows.why: The waiver covers INR917 crore overdue plus INR1,067 crore NPA eligible KCC accounts, with approval expected Q2-Q3 FY27, and agri NPA could fall to about 5.33% from 7.72%.

rows.label: PLI payout for Scale 4 and above
rows.why: 100% provision is already made, but release is pending discussions, so any release would be an upside to other income with no date given.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 delivery and FY27 guidance (targets called sacrosanct) but cautious and somewhat evasive on West Asia impact, which it said cannot yet be gauged; analysts pressed on tax-rate inconsistency, the 10% vs 18-20% PBT tax figures, and the gold book's 17% QoQ drop.

532525|2026-06.headline: Bank of Maharashtra Q1 FY27: net profit up 27% YoY to INR2,020 crore, advances up 27%, NIM 3.85%, all guidance parameters beaten.
532525|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 (quarter ended June 2026) with total business up 19% YoY, advances up 27% and deposits up 13%, against guidance of 16-17%, 18% and 14% respectively. Operating profit rose 21% YoY to INR3,117 crore and net profit rose 27% to INR2,020 crore. Asset quality held: gross NPA flat QoQ at 1.45%, net NPA 0.13%, credit cost 0.99%. Management kept its FY27 guidance unchanged despite the faster growth, and flagged the NIM (3.85%, down 10 bps YoY) and the rising cost of deposits QoQ as the points to watch.

financial_highlights.value: INR1,04,000 crore added in past year

financial_highlights.change: Guidance 14%; no CDs raised in Q1
vs INR33 crore in March quarter; includes one-time SR of INR104 crore

segments.name: Agri
segments.commentary: Agri advances grew 30% YoY; agri gross NPA 7.58%, down from about 9% a couple of quarters back.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 23% YoY; MSME gross NPA 1.60%, and MSME gross NPA rose QoQ.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew about 30% YoY, up from 17-18% in the prior four quarters; RAM:corporate mix at 63:37.

capex_capacity: Opening about 200 new branches a year under a 5-year expansion plan; new branches are staffed from day one.
Staff strength about INR17,500 crore (figure as stated) vs about INR13,000 crore two years ago; recruitment to continue.

5-year FCNR deposit offered at 6.60%, positioned against the best PSB offers.

Retail term deposit growth 16% vs total deposits 13%; management attributes the QoQ rise in deposit cost to special retail TD schemes.
Gold loans about INR13,000 crore, up 75% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NII (14.5%) lag advances growth (27%), and would management revisit the 18% loan growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept NII guidance of 15% and NIM of 3.75%, citing a branch-level profitability dashboard and tighter pricing. It said it would keep the 18% advances guidance, with IBU contributing 3 points of the 27% growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did current account balances fall sharply QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it not a major concern: the decline is about 2,500-3,000 bps of the current account book, and CASA still grew 9% YoY, adding INR14,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Agri provisions and debt waiver impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Eligible portfolio INR3,500 crore; government receivable INR2,750 crore; maximum haircut INR450-500 crore, already covered by INR1,700 crore of provisions. Settlement expected within FY27, plus INR50,000 per farmer incentive into SB accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the tax rate lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Tax rate is about 12-13% on an operating-profit basis and 16-17% on a PBT basis, aided by rural advances (about 40% of branches rural), bad-debt write-off benefits and DTA.

qa_highlights.question: Opex growth of 8-9% vs balance sheet growth above 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost growth is driven by staffing new branches from day one; cost-to-income is 36-38% and guided below 40%. Branches opened three or more years ago have all turned profitable, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did treasury profit jump to INR266 crore and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury included a one-time SR of INR104 crore, with part of the payment possibly coming in later quarters; no treasury profit targets are set.

qa_highlights.question: SMA-2 jump from INR56 crore to INR208 crore; is MSME stress rising?
qa_highlights.answer: A single government entity account of INR87 crore moved into SMA-2 and is expected to regularise. SMA-1+2 stands at 1.34%, down 5 bps YoY.

Agri gross NPA at 7.58% and the debt-waiver haircut timing; the Rs 87 crore government account in SMA-2 needs to regularise.
Agri and MSME gross NPA rose QoQ (MSME 1.60%); watch for stress from geopolitical conditions (West Asia).
NIM pressure from MCLR resets, with the yield on advances down 71 bps YoY to 8.57% globally; the rate-hike benefit depends on repo-linked share at 53%.
Equity raise of INR5,000 crore pending government approval; treasury gains include a one-time item of INR104 crore.
ECL provisioning of about INR125 crore per quarter through March 2031 against net worth.
