532525|2026-09.headline: Bank of Maharashtra Q2 FY27: business up 25% YoY, advances up 30%, ROE 26.98%, GNPA down 47 bps to 1.25%.
532525|2026-09.overview: Management said all FY27 guidance metrics were met in Q2, with business crossing INR7 lakh crore and advances growing 30% YoY (23% ex-IBU). Operating profit rose 31% and net profit 41% YoY, lifting ROE 440 bps to 26.98% and NIM 12 bps to 3.97%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 1.25% and NNPA at 0.12%, helped by write-off recoveries and lower NPA provisions, while INR500 crore of ECL provisions was booked in the standard asset line. Cost of deposits fell 4 bps YoY to 4.38%, though management acknowledged a QoQ rise tied to FCNR(B) and OFCB raises of about $1.65 billion.

financial_highlights.metric: Cost of deposits / cost of funds

segments.name: Advances / large credit
segments.commentary: Large credit up 38% YoY to INR36,000 crore, of which INR18,000 crore from GIFT City IBU and INR18,000 crore domestic (19% growth). Domestic credit ex-IBU grew 23%, with RAM, retail, agri and MSME each above 20%.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Deposits up 22% YoY, or 19% ex-FCNR(B); CASA up 12% YoY with INR19,000 crore CASA added over the last FY.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri book INR44,000 crore, up 34% YoY (about INR11,000 crore). Agri gold loans INR18,600 crore vs INR6,500 crore in Sep-25; agri stress down 35 bps to 3.51%.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Total gold loan outstanding INR33,000 crore; MSME gold loan about INR2,000 crore. Retail gold declined QoQ as loans were reclassified to agri/MSME under RBI norms.

guidance_outlook: Management said all FY27 guidance metrics across growth, profitability, asset quality and capital were met in H1.
Domestic credit guidance is 18%; management sees no challenge sustaining above 18% with INR23,000 crore pipeline and INR10,000 crore expected to be disbursed by March 2027.
Recovery target from written-off accounts of INR1,300-1,500 crore annually for the next 4-5 years; FY27 recovery so far INR1,023 crore.
ECL: total assessed requirement INR2,500 crore over 4 years; INR750 crore already provided (INR250 crore earlier plus INR500 crore in Q2), which management says covers more than 1 year.
Maharashtra debt-waiver government receivable (about INR2,700 crore of eligible INR3,500 crore): about INR1,200 crore received to 30 Sep; SLBC timeline for balance is 31 March 2027.
capex_capacity: Branch expansion: about 200 branches planned annually; 77 branches made functional in H1 FY27.
Employee strength raised to 17,500 from about 13,000 two years earlier, driven by branch expansion and specialist hiring (treasury, IBU, IT).
IT budget: INR900 crore in FY25 and INR985 crore in FY26, with a large share on cyber security.
Pipeline sector mix: infra power about 18%, roads/HAM about 12%, renewables about 10%, metals and others about 10%; data centres cited as a niche growth area.
demand_pricing: Credit growth ex-IBU of 23% YoY; IBU book INR18,500 crore funded partly by about $560 million of FCNR(B) leverage. The FCNR(B) special window has closed.
Repricing: management raised rates on several MCLR-linked state PSU facilities (several thousand crore, about 25 bps on some) in Q1, contributing to NIM gains.
Global yield on advances 8.86%, domestic 9.02%; IBU yield not disclosed on the call.
Gold loan pricing tiers: agri lowest, MSME about 50 bps higher, non-priority retail highest.
EBLR-linked loans are 47% of the loan book.

qa_highlights.question: Provisioning: standard/restructured provisions rose to INR603 crore from INR76 crore; what is the ECL preparedness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NPA provisions fell from INR580 crore a year ago to INR120 crore this quarter, helped by recoveries. Standard-asset provisions rose to INR603 crore including INR500 crore of ECL; total ECL assessed at INR2,500 crore over 4 years, with INR750 crore already provided.

qa_highlights.question: Will credit growth sustain after the FCNR window closes, and will write-off recoveries continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IBU leverage was about $560 million from FCNR(B) and the window is closed; domestic growth is 23% and the INR23,000 crore pipeline supports growth above the 18% guidance. Write-off recovery target is INR1,300-1,500 crore a year for 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of deposits rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FCNR(B) is fixed at 6.51%, OFCB at 6.11%, and 1-year CDs at about 7.75-7.9%. About $1.65 billion was raised via FCNR(B) and OFCB against a $1.5 billion plan, with 5-year fixed-cost borrowings and a 3x oversubscribed MTN issue; YoY cost of deposits fell 4 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the 30 bps QoQ rise in yield on advances despite IBU mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to repricing of MCLR-linked state PSU accounts (about 25 bps on several thousand crore), a one-off write-off recovery impact of about 2-3 bps on NIM, and a 3-4 bps ITR refund. Only INR30 crore of the INR125 crore recovery has gone to interest income so far.

qa_highlights.question: Drought exposure and restructuring under SLBC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no visible agri stress; special SLBC restructuring applies at 33-50% crop loss (1-year moratorium, up to 3-year tenor) and above 50% loss (5-year tenor including 1-year moratorium). Farmer applications open till February 2027; past experience suggests 10-15% take-up, with about 5% provisioning on the restructured amount.

qa_highlights.question: Agri gold and retail gold trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Agri gold loans rose to INR18,600 crore from INR6,500 crore YoY. Retail gold declined QoQ because loans were reclassified to MSME/agri under RBI norms; total gold outstanding INR33,000 crore and MSME gold about INR2,000 crore.

risks_watch: Drought and El Nino: Maharashtra drought could trigger SLBC restructuring; management estimates 10-15% take-up and says no visible stress yet.
ECL transition: INR2,500 crore total assessed; management said the number may fall; surplus provisions of INR1,600-1,800 crore (COVID, global uncertainties INR200 crore) can be used.
Cost of deposits: QoQ increase from high-cost FCNR(B)/OFCB/CD raises; FY28 impact on margin depends on deployment.
Maharashtra debt-waiver balance of about INR1,500 crore receivable; management does not count on it and timing depends on state process (deadline 31 March 2027).
Pace of IBU growth after the FCNR(B) window closed; IBU yield not disclosed.
Cyber and DPDP compliance; management deferred detailed answer.

rows.why: Total ECL assessed at INR2,500 crore over 4 years with INR750 crore already provided, leaving INR1,750 crore to be provided, though surplus provisions of INR1,600-1,800 crore can be used.

rows.why: About INR1,200 crore of eligible INR3,500 crore (about INR2,700 crore eligible) received to 30 Sep, with about INR1,500 crore balance; SLBC timeline is 31 March 2027 and management does not count on it.

rows.label: Data centre lending niche
rows.why: Data centres cited as a niche growth area alongside infra power (about 18% of pipeline) and roads/HAM (about 12%), but no quantified target was given.

532527|2026-03.headline: Ramkrishna Forgings Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 28% YoY to Rs 1,216.78 crore, with EBITDA margin at 17.1%, and management guides to further improvement in FY27.
532527|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was Rs 1,216.78 crore, up 28% YoY and 11% QoQ, with EBITDA excluding other income of Rs 208.19 crore (up 111% YoY, 27% QoQ) and margin of 17.1%. Profit before tax was Rs 64.33 crore, held back by about Rs 10.4 crore of consolidation effects (Rs 5.9 crore subsidiary profit elimination and Rs 4.5 crore Mexico subsidiary loss). FY26 consolidated revenue was Rs 4,238 crore (up 5%) and EBITDA Rs 642.70 crore (up 15%), while PBT fell 24% to Rs 112.58 crore versus Rs 148.79 crore (excluding exceptional items) in FY25. Q4 orders won totalled Rs 594 crore over four years, split 56% automotive and 44% non-automotive.

financial_highlights.change: +28% YoY vs Rs 947.21 crore; +11% QoQ vs Rs 1,098.52 crore
+111% YoY vs Rs 98.5 crore; +27% QoQ vs Rs 163.37 crore
Up about 220 bps QoQ (stated as 'almost 2 20 basis points', read as ~220 bps)
+117% QoQ vs Rs 29.69 crore in Q3 FY26
+5% YoY vs Rs 4,034 crore in FY25
+15% YoY vs Rs 559.56 crore in FY25
-24% YoY vs Rs 148.79 crore excl. exceptional item in FY25
Management targets about Rs 250 crore in FY27; market share 4-5% now, targeting ~10%

segments.name: Forgings
segments.commentary: Forging utilisation about 70% in Q4 FY26 versus 83% in Q4 FY25, per the analyst's reading of the presentation; management attributes the gap partly to the 8,000-ton press line added. Cold forging utilisation is about 40%, held back by slow global PV approvals; management hopes for 75-80% by FY26 year-end (FY27 per the call's context).

segments.name: Castings
segments.commentary: Capacity is 62,000 tons (cited as 78,000 tons by one analyst, with about 70,000 tons referenced by management); production was 26,000 tons in FY26 and sales are lower due to machining mix. Management expects 85-90% utilisation over the year and margins of about 15-16%, with Rs 400-500 crore of incremental revenue from the new March-end capacity.

segments.name: Aluminium forgings
segments.commentary: Post commissioning, bulk supplies have started to EV equipment makers globally; management cites margins of about 14-15%, with commodity realisation near Rs 400/kg.

segments.name: Railway wheelsets (JV)
segments.commentary: Rail wheel JV expected to start production by Q1 FY27, with 230,000-wheel capacity and a railway offtake guarantee of about 40,000 wheels in FY27 for revenue of roughly Rs 400-450 crore.

segments.name: Trailer axles
segments.commentary: Revenue of about Rs 120 crore in FY26; management targets about Rs 250 crore in FY27 and a 10% market share.

guidance_outlook: Revenue: no FY27 number given; management expects 'healthy growth' on current order book and capacity. Analyst cited a prior 10-15% CAGR upper limit for FY27-28, and management declined to confirm it.
EBITDA margin: management expects continued improvement, with 100-150 bps better margin at around 80% utilisation if energy price increases are passed on.
Utilisation: overall capacity utilisation targeted at about 80% in FY27, roughly 350,000 tons of forging and casting; press plant around 85% by FY27 year-end.
Debt: reduction of at least Rs 400-500 crore in FY27, supported by promoter funding and operating performance.
Capex: FY27 capex limited to about Rs 400 crore at most, mainly JV contribution (about Rs 50 crore still to be paid) and value-add; no FY28 capex frozen yet.
Export mix: management expects exports to rise above 40% of volumes within about two years (from a historical 40:60 export:domestic split), with exports more remunerative.
Titanium/stainless aerospace alloys: order book reflection expected by FY26 year-end, but revenue not expected before FY29.
capex_capacity: Rail wheel JV: commercial production to start immediately after commissioning, around end-May/June 2026; 300 trial wheels to be submitted in June/July 2026.
Forging press line: 8,000-ton press added; press plant utilisation targeted at about 85% by FY27 year-end.
Casting: about 62,000-ton capacity, 26,000 tons produced in FY26; new capacity added by end-March 2026 is expected to generate Rs 400-500 crore of revenue in coming years.
Standalone casting business began commercial production on 31 March 2026, so nil standalone revenue in FY26.
Ring rolling running at 121% utilisation; no plans to add ring rolling capacity in FY27.
demand_pricing: North America Class 8 demand is strong; destocking in North American warehouses over the last three months, with fresh revenue expected from Q1 FY27; management expects this to last to about Q3 CY27.

Q4 orders of Rs 594 crore (four-year program): Rs 334 crore auto (Rs 323 crore CV, of which more than 50% export; Rs 11 crore EV) and Rs 258 crore energy (energy storage, North America) plus Rs 2 crore off-highway.

Pricing is pass-through: steel is passed on quarterly with a one-quarter lag; gas and other consumables are negotiated yearly. Management is seeking compensation for geopolitical energy cost increases via force majeure, with talks at an advanced stage.

Realisation: management attributed the lower realisation versus Q4 FY25 to lower raw material prices and cited a better product mix in H2 FY26; the analyst cited export realisation rising from Rs 1.77 lakh to Rs 1.85 lakh per ton.
Shipping costs up 15-20% and transit times up 15-20 days; floating inventory said to be in line. No West Asia revenue or exposure.
Domestic auto demand was strong after the September GST rate cut, with M&HCV, tractors and PVs reporting double-digit wholesale growth in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Rs 1,550 crore FY27 order book include castings, and what casting volumes and revenue are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: The figure covers forgings and castings together. Management expects 85-90% casting utilisation over the year, with margins of about 15-16% and Rs 400-500 crore of additional revenue. Management declined to put a figure on the incremental revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 debt and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is to be reduced by at least Rs 400-500 crore in FY27. Capex is capped at about Rs 400 crore, mostly JV equity and value-add, with about Rs 50 crore of JV equity still to be paid.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins and revenue growth in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No revenue number was given, but management expects healthy growth. The EBITDA margin should keep improving, and at about 80% utilisation it could be 100-150 bps above the Q4 level if energy cost increases are passed on.

qa_highlights.question: How much did trailer axles contribute, and what are the targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue was about Rs 120 crore in FY26 at a 4-5% market share. The FY27 target is about Rs 250 crore at about 10% share.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wheelset JV's contribution and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Production starts by Q1 FY27 and about 40,000 wheels are expected in FY27 under the railway offtake guarantee, for revenue of roughly Rs 400-450 crore. Pricing is still being reset for two years of inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing for aerospace/titanium revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders should start reflecting in the order book by FY26 year-end, but revenue is not expected before FY29 given 12-24 month lead times and approvals.

risks_watch: Energy and gas cost pass-through: consumables are not automatically passed on, and the compensation claim from customers is still under negotiation.
Cold forging utilisation at about 40% depends on slow PV approvals in global markets.
Rs 400-500 crore debt reduction target depends on promoter funding and operating performance.
Geopolitical and Middle East conflict risks, plus freight costs up 15-20% and transit times up 15-20 days.

Mexico subsidiary loss (Rs 4.5 crore in Q4) and consolidation eliminations (Rs 5.9 crore) weighed on PBT.
Rs 42 crore ECL provision on receivables booked in Q4, linked to electricity duty income recognised as exceptional income.

532528|2026-06.headline: Datamatics Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9.9% YoY to INR 513.9 crore, with EBITDA margin up 343 bps to 19.7%.
532528|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 9.9% YoY to INR 513.9 crore and EBITDA rose to INR 101.1 crore at a 19.7% margin, with the margin gain attributed to cost discipline and operational excellence. Digital Operations drove growth (revenue up 16.1%, EBIT margin 19.3%), while Digital Technologies grew 6.1% at an 8.9% EBIT margin and Digital Experiences declined 5.3%. Management reiterated high single-digit FY27 revenue growth guidance, citing softness from geopolitical uncertainty, and said about 60% of FY27 deals won were AI-led or AI-driven. The TNQTech integration into Lumina Datamatics was completed in the quarter, and a INR 200 crore TNQTech payout was made in Q1.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not compete much with large listed IT players. Competition comes from funded local AI start-ups, GCCs and in-house tech teams.

qa_highlights.question: What are the risks to the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Key risks are customers automating in-house instead of outsourcing, captive/GCC setups, and geopolitical softness.

qa_highlights.answer: Target of about INR 3,000 crore over roughly three years from about INR 2,000 crore now, with organic growth from AI platforms and bolt-on acquisitions.

532531|2026-03.headline: Strides FY26 revenue rose 6.4% to INR48,587 mn and EBITDA 15% to INR925 crore at 19% margin; Q4 US revenue weak at $70 mn as flu season failed to materialise.
532531|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 6.4% YoY to INR48,587 mn, held back by a weak second-half US flu season and donor-funding pressure in access markets; management says underlying growth was about 10% excluding access markets. Ex-US revenue grew 21% and reached about 50% of Q4 revenue, while EBITDA margin expanded 140 bps to 19% for the year. Q4 EBITDA rose 10% YoY to INR240 crore (18.1% margin), with about INR20 crore of logistics and air-freight cost pressure. Operational PAT crossed INR500 crore for the first time at INR518 crore, and the Board recommended a dividend of INR5 per share.

Controlled substances from the Chestnut Ridge ANDA acquisition are in their first full year, with 4 products launched and quota allocations below expectations.

segments.name: Other regulated markets (ORM)
segments.commentary: Quarterly revenue rose from about $31 mn in Q1 FY24 to a $52 mn exit run rate in Q4 FY26, with traction in Europe, UK, Australia and the Nordics.

segments.name: Africa / growth markets
segments.commentary: Focus is shifting toward branded business, with Francophone Africa growing faster than the underlying market. The Sandoz product acquisition (announced Feb 2026) is expected to contribute from H2 FY27 and to lift the branded portfolio more than 1.5x.

US growth expected to pick up from H2 FY27; FY26 seasonality was roughly 50:50 H1:H2 versus the usual 45:55.

Sandoz portfolio expected to contribute from H2 FY27; R&D spend to be $20-25 mn a year over the next 2 years; tangible and intangible investment run rate about INR300 crore; nasal sprays, patches and films expected to contribute mainly from FY28-FY29.

Patches and thin films: filing expected in 12-18 months.
demand_pricing: US flu-season demand did not recover in H2 as it had in prior years, and wholesaler discipline also contributed.

Intense competition in a few molecules led to market-share rationalisation; management prioritises profitability over volume.
Q4 logistics and air-freight costs of about INR20 crore hurt margins; price increases are being negotiated with customers.
Access markets are facing donor-funding challenges, which management describes as tactical.

qa_highlights.question: What is happening in the US, including discontinuations and delayed launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the missing flu season, controlled-substance quota timing, and a policy of not launching until market conditions are attractive. It said 150 products are in the portfolio and launches will continue through FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Are controlled substances and nasal sprays structurally higher-margin, and how big is the controlled substances opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said controlled substances are an in-US-for-US strategy and margins will be similar to the current profile, not dramatically different. It declined to give revenue potential, saying the company needs more DEA quota first, and the company has gone back to the DEA for additional quota.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q4 SG&A and freight spike persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SG&A will stay around the current range, with Q4 freight costs elevated. It said a discount factor should be applied to Q4 when modelling.

qa_highlights.question: What are the nasal spray and new modality timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: One or two nasal products could launch earlier, but bulk revenue is expected in FY28-FY29. Patches and thin films filings are expected in 12-18 months, with about 5-6 additional third-party nasal programmes added.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sandoz deal's impact and the R&D outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The Sandoz deal is expected to close in H2 FY27 (October-March). R&D spend is expected to be $20-25 mn over the next 2 years.

532538|2026-03.headline: UltraTech Q4 FY26: consolidated EBITDA/ton of INR1,253 (ex-West Asia ~INR1,240), 200 MTPA capacity crossed, dividend INR240/share proposed.
532538|2026-03.overview: UltraTech crossed 200 million tonnes of Indian cement capacity a year ahead of target and completed 100% brand migration for India Cements and Kesoram at end-March 2026. Q4 consolidated volumes were above 44 million tonnes (brand volume up 19% YoY), grey cement prices rose about 2.5% across most geographies, and consolidated EBITDA per tonne was INR1,253 versus INR1,225 in Q4 FY25 (ex-acquired assets INR1,296). West Asia conflict is a headwind on fuel, packing bags (about INR90 crore extra bag cost in March), freight and forex mark-to-market (about INR120-130 crore). Management guided 7-8% sustainable volume growth, double-digit volume growth for FY27, and a Board-proposed dividend of INR240 per share for FY26.

532538|2026-09.headline: UltraTech Q2 FY27: volumes up 13.8% with 71% utilisation; trade prices exited September ~3% above Q1 average and are about 5% above Q2 average.
532538|2026-09.overview: Management described a quarter where a weak monsoon kept construction active, while a West Asia conflict pushed fuel costs higher. Q2 trade prices averaged roughly 1-1.5% below Q1 on a soft August, but rose sharply in late September and October. Volume growth of 13.8% ran ahead of an industry estimate of about 10%, and net profit rose 21% YoY. Fuel cost per bag rose to INR 51.5 from INR 45, and the company expects the price increases to flow mainly into Q3 earnings.

financial_highlights.change: absolute fixed costs up 4% vs volume +13.8%

segments.name: Cement - regions
segments.commentary: North grew over 20% and South 15-20%; East ~5%, West ~10%, Central ~10%. Utilisation was above 70% in North and South, about 70% in West, and about 60% in Central and East.

segments.name: Wires and Cables (Ultravolt)
segments.commentary: Launched 3 September 2026 with INR 1,800 crores planned capex, of which INR 1,100 crores is spent or committed. Production of house wire, panel wire and multicore cable has started; power and control cable lines are due in H2. Management says it is too early to judge revenue or margins; it is a division, not a subsidiary.

guidance_outlook: Trade prices exited September at least ~3% above Q1 average; October prices are about 5% above Q2 average, with management expecting more increases in the next couple of months.
Full benefit of price increases expected in Q3 earnings rather than immediately, given festive-season slowdown.
FY27 capex guidance held at about INR 10,000 crores (plus or minus), with a fuller view after Q3.
Net debt/EBITDA expected below 1x by end-March 2027.
Fuel cost guidance: INR 2.1/kcal may rise to about INR 2.2/kcal, assumed to hold for H2 if pet coke stays near $180/tonne; management expects only a marginal Q4 impact from current inventory.
Business-as-usual delivery of the INR 1,400/tonne EBITDA exit-March-2028 target, with cost pressures expected to be covered by price increases.
Expects industry volume growth of about 8% in H1 FY27 and very strong momentum to March 2029.
Ultravolt: a mature business expected in FY28; April-June 2027 quarter is flagged as one worth discussing.
capex_capacity: Commissioned 4.6 Mtpa in September, taking domestic cement capacity to 204.7 Mtpa, including the 3.6 Mt greenfield plant at Petnikota (Andhra Pradesh) and 1 Mt of debottlenecking at 3 units.
On track for 240 Mtpa as planned; next phase of organic growth to be announced, with North capacity expansion plans to come before end-FY27.
Added 116 MW renewable power and 10 MW waste heat recovery; 47% of power from non-fossil sources; 2 GW green power for captive use.
Thermal substitution rate about 7.2% after AFR systems commissioned at 2 plants.
Ultravolt plant at Jhagadia (Gujarat); 1 main warehouse, 5 regional distribution centres and about 16 branch warehouses.
India Cement kiln shutdowns planned for upgrades (WHRS, preheater height) with benefits expected from Jan-Mar 2028 quarter.
demand_pricing: Q2 average trade prices were 1-1.5% below Q1 owing to a soft August; prices rose 7-10 per bag month-on-month in the second half of September, with non-trade prices higher.
Mumbai prices rose 3-4% per bag; South showed the strongest momentum in prices, volumes and utilisation.
Trade ratio stable at 65-67%; industry sales were 463 Mt in FY26 against UltraTech's 145 Mt.
Management says the industry is now sold out, so pricing is leading volume.
Domestic coal is constrained because Coal India prioritises the power sector; pet coke was about $180/tonne, and pet coke share was cut to about 25%.
Rural demand may soften in some areas; the company cites weak monsoon, drought in pockets and farm-income risk.
UBS network above 25% of trade sales, with about 6,500 stores targeting 10,000 by FY28-29.
Ultravolt pricing is at market parity; the company says differentiation comes from premium Class 5 HR/FR products.

qa_highlights.question: What cost inflation is expected in H2 from current spot levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not forecast peaking. The fuel kcal cost may go from INR 2.1 to INR 2.2, which is assumed to hold if nothing else changes; marginal Q4 impact expected from inventory.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the price increase versus the Q2 average?
qa_highlights.answer: Spot realisation is about 5% above the Q2 average, with September and October combined.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt rose QoQ; why?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by capex and the dividend payment. Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26x from 0.94x at March 2026, and management expects it below 1x by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest costs rise about 22% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 5,000 crores of NCDs at 7.25% were raised and held for about 2 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will Ultravolt's capex go beyond INR 1,800 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: No sanction beyond INR 1,800 crores. Management says the ramp-up is the focus and that the revenue target could reach INR 16,000-18,000 crores on copper prices, against the earlier INR 10,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Will the industry return to pricing power?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says pricing is leading, the industry is sold out, and the price increases will cover cost pressures.

qa_highlights.question: Will the EBITDA per tonne target of INR 1,400 hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Business as usual, with cost pressures covered by price increases; management confirmed delivery of the INR 1,400 commitment.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: pet coke, imported coal and industrial diesel costs are elevated, and any escalation adds to H2 cost pressure.
Whether October price increases hold through the festive slowdown and are absorbed in Q3.
Rural demand softening after a weak monsoon and drought pockets; household inflation.
Ultravolt: early-stage, with ramp-up, dealer stabilisation and margins unproven; revenue and utilisation not yet disclosed.
Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26x; the company targets below 1x by March 2027.
Eastern markets (Bihar, West Bengal) still underperforming with utilisation near 60%.

rows.why: Volumes grew 13.8% YoY against an industry of about 10%, the 4.6 Mtpa commissioned in September lifts capacity to 204.7 Mtpa, and the industry is sold out with management expecting about 8% industry growth in H1 FY27 and strong momentum to March 2029.

rows.why: Utilisation at 71% is below the 80% threshold, but the industry is sold out and management has said North expansion plans will come before end-FY27 on the way to 240 Mtpa; FY27 capex is held at about INR 10,000 crore, with a fuller view after Q3.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: H2 FY27 (power and control cable lines)
rows.why: Ultravolt launched on 3 September 2026 with house wire, panel wire and multicore cable production started, and power and control cable lines are due in H2 FY27 on INR 1,800 crore planned capex (INR 1,100 crore spent or committed).

rows.label: Ultravolt ramp-up and revenue target
rows.why: Ultravolt is a mature business expected in FY28, with revenue target possibly INR 16,000-18,000 crore against the earlier INR 10,000 crore, but revenue and margins are not yet disclosed and pricing is at market parity.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA below 1x by March 2027
rows.why: Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26x from 0.94x at March 2026 after capex and dividend, and management has committed to below 1x by March 2027.

rows.label: Price increases of 7-10 per bag in late September
rows.why: Prices rose 7-10 per bag month-on-month in the second half of September, and spot realisation is about 5% above the Q2 average, with management expecting more increases over the next couple of months.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, pricing and the South region and reaffirmed the INR 1,400/tonne and sub-1x leverage targets, but was evasive on forward cost curves, fuel contract terms and Ultravolt numbers, which were deferred; analysts pushed on H2 cost inflation and fuel costs.

532539|2026-03.headline: Uno Minda Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 18% YoY to INR 5,336 crore with EBITDA margin of 11.3%, but commodity and labour cost pressure is expected to weigh on coming quarters.
532539|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was INR 5,336 crore (+18% YoY) and EBITDA was INR 603 crore (+14%) at an 11.3% margin, both company records. PAT attributable to shareholders rose 22% to INR 326 crore. For FY26, revenue was INR 19,589 crore (+17%), normalised EBITDA INR 2,182 crore (+16%) at 11.1%, and normalised PAT INR 1,166 crore (+24%). Management flagged that aluminium and labour cost spikes (Haryana labour rates up about 35%) are expected to hit coming quarters sizably, and is negotiating faster price pass-through with customers.

financial_highlights.change: Planned increase on capex and working capital borrowings

financial_highlights.metric: Share of profit from associates and JV (Q4 FY26)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR 55 crore in prior year

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue from operations (FY26, excl. Q1 prior period income)
Normalised PAT (FY26, excl. prior period income and exceptional items)

financial_highlights.change: ROCE includes land bank and CWIP
Includes INR 861 crore expansion and INR 149 crore CSN land

financial_highlights.value: INR 2.65 per share (about INR 153 crore), incl. final INR 1.75

segments.name: Switch systems
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 1,343 crore (+17%, 25% of consol), a record quarter; 2-wheeler switches grew over 26% and 2-wheeler switch exports were INR 86 crore. FY26 revenue INR 4,871 crore (+16%).

segments.name: Lighting systems
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 1,154 crore (+13%, about 22% of consol); FY26 INR 4,402 crore (+14%). Management says 4-wheeler lighting is now in consolidation after a threefold expansion over five years.

segments.name: Casting (alloy wheels and die casting)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 982 crore (+14%, about 18% of consol): 4-wheeler alloy wheels INR 535 crore, 2-wheeler alloy wheels INR 259 crore, die casting INR 188 crore. FY26 INR 3,694 crore (+15%). Aluminium pass-through contributed about 4-5% of growth.

segments.name: Seating systems
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 381 crore (about 7% of consol); FY26 INR 1,416 crore (+23%). Q4 exports INR 54 crore.

segments.name: Green mobility (new reporting segment)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 423 crore (+25%, 8% of consol): alternate fuels INR 186 crore, 2W/3W EV systems INR 147 crore, 4W EV INR 46 crore, EV controllers INR 44 crore. FY26 INR 1,405 crore (+7% on restated INR 1,313 crore).

segments.name: Others (incl. acoustics, sensors/ADAS, blow moulding, aftermarket)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 1,053 crore (+25%, about 20% of consol): sensors and ADAS INR 205 crore, acoustics INR 225 crore, blow moulding INR 118 crore, non-EV controllers INR 86 crore. FY26 INR 3,801 crore (+26%). Acoustics was moved into this category.

segments.name: Aftermarket and international
segments.commentary: Q4 aftermarket revenue INR 340 crore (about 7% of consol) plus INR 232 crore to OEM spare parts division. International business was about 10% of Q4 revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated capex planned at about INR 1,750 crore: about INR 650 crore sustaining and about INR 1,100 crore growth, plus land; more land may be needed at CSN, Hosur and Gujarat.
Annual EBITDA margin guided at about 11% plus or minus 50 bps, including known start-up costs of new plants.
Automotive industry expected to sustain growth momentum in FY27; 7 of 11 ongoing projects to commence production or ramp up in FY27.
Sunroof manufacturing commissioning expected by end FY27; EV powertrain Khed Phase 1 expected in H2 FY27.
Physical exports from India (ex overseas plants) of about INR 600 crore in FY26 expected to cross INR 1,500 crore in the next few years.
Labour cost impact of about a couple of hundred crore for Haryana and Gujarat alone, with other states yet to announce floor wages; mitigation via customer pass-through being negotiated.
Expected sizeable commodity-driven margin impact in coming quarters; management seeks shorter pass-through cycles (monthly or quarterly instead of half-yearly).
capex_capacity: Khed City (Pune) EV powertrain facility to begin operations in H2 FY27; Phase 1 of the Kharkhoda/Farrukhnagar-linked programmes also in progress.

New greenfield EV powertrain plant at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar under UMAIPL: total investment about INR 550 crore, EDU with Inovance Automotive technology partner, DHT through a customer partnership, commissioning by Q2 FY28.
CSN casting plant of about INR 300 crore to serve EDU and DST; combined EV powertrain capex about INR 1,200 crore, revenue potential more than 2x (INR 2,500 crore+, peak up to about INR 3,000 crore).
4-wheeler switch shifting from Manesar to Farrukhnagar expected to complete over the next 6 months; 2-wheeler lighting's three plants being merged into one at Kharkhoda.
Capacity post expansion: about 9.5 million 2-wheeler alloy wheels per year and about 7 million 4-wheeler alloy wheels, based on announced projects.
Commissioned in Q4: 4-wheeler lighting plants at Khed City and Indonesia, 2-wheeler alloy wheel expansion at Supa, 4-wheeler alloy wheel Phase 1 at Kharkhoda, and Bawal expansion.
Sunroof order book potential exceeds INR 350 crore after a new INR 85 crore annual peak order; facility commissioning by end FY27.
demand_pricing: Industry: FY26 PV production a record 5.5 million units (+9%); 2W production a record 26.6 million (+12%); CV production 1.17 million (+13%); 3W Q4 production +32%. Management cited EV penetration of 4.2% in PV and 6.5% in e-2W.

Q4 alloy wheel penetration moderated: 4-wheeler customers shifted mix to entry-level models with lower alloy adoption; in 2W, some programmes switched to steel wheels. Current penetration is about 70% in 2W and about 40% in 4W (as stated).

Pass-through: 3- or 6-month cycles set by customer policy, not by commodity; 1-2 customers operate annually. Management says commodity spikes of 30-40% are not normal and is seeking monthly or quarterly adjustments.

Gross margin compressed by about 1% YoY in Q4, attributed to newer lower-margin businesses and commodity impacts; the trading business (EV-related, about INR 40-45 crore) is too small to be significant.

New wins: 2W lighting order with annual peak value about INR 450 crore (SOP H2 FY28, about 25% of current 2W lighting revenue); 2W silver-box display order about INR 200 crore (production from Q4 FY27); CV seating export orders about INR 390 crore from 3 customers in Europe and North America (supplies from FY28); IVI order about INR 600 crore (SOP Q3 FY29, via Denso JV, outside consolidated revenue).

qa_highlights.question: Why set up a second 4W EV powertrain plant (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) while Khed is still under construction, and how will the multiple plants (about 9 starting FY27, ~INR 1,800 crore capex) be executed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited firm customer partnerships for DST and EDU and a customer push to be closer to them; Khed capacity was earmarked for existing businesses. It said one plant commissions this year and the second after about a year. Execution is handled by separate business teams, so no team overlaps across plants. Revenue guidance for the new plant was not given.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Q4 debit/credit note quantum affecting margin, and how much aluminium pass-through and commodity impact was there?
qa_highlights.answer: Quantum of the Q4 debit/credit note adjustments was not shared because it differs by business. Some customer price settlement income was booked in Q4. Aluminium pass-through contributed about 4-5% of casting growth. Commodity impact is expected to be sizable in coming quarters; Haryana labour rates are up about 35%.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the new 4W EV plant revenue potential and how much of the 1.85 lakh capacity is booked?
qa_highlights.answer: Booked share was not disclosed; the 1.85 lakh figure is eventual capacity and will be built as business is won. Khed (INR 400 crore+) and the new plant (INR 550 crore) plus about INR 300 crore CSN casting total about INR 1,200 crore capex, with revenue above 2x, at least INR 2,500 crore and up to about INR 3,000 crore at peak.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin impact from the labour and commodity pressures, and how does pass-through work?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour impact is about a couple of hundred crore for Haryana and Gujarat alone, with other states yet to announce floor wages. Pass-through cycles are set by each customer (3 or 6 months, with 1-2 customers annual), not by commodity. Management is seeking monthly or quarterly adjustments. The 11% plus/minus 50 bps guidance includes known start-up costs.

qa_highlights.question: What are the alloy wheel penetration levels and the 2W alloy wheel and 4W alloy wheel capacity post expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Current alloy wheel penetration is about 70% in 2W and about 40% in 4W. Capacity post expansion is about 9.5 million 2W alloy wheels per year and about 7 million 4W alloy wheels, based on announced projects.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross margin down about 1%, and how large is the trading drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin fell about 1% YoY. Management attributed this to newer lower-margin businesses and commodity impact. The EV-related trading business is about INR 40-45 crore and too small to matter. Exports from India were about INR 600 crore in FY26 and are expected to cross INR 1,500 crore in the next few years.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the Denso JV infotainment (IVI) order and how does it reflect in consolidated numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: The IVI order has annual peak value of about INR 600 crore, with SOP in Q3 FY29 and about 70% of current JV revenue of INR 846 crore. It sits in the Denso JV and is excluded from consolidated revenue, appearing only as share of JV profit. No further new business timing was committed.

risks_watch: Commodity (aluminium) and labour cost spikes (Haryana up about 35%; labour impact about INR 200 crore for Haryana and Gujarat) hit coming quarters, and pass-through cycles of 3-6 months (1-2 customers annual) lag the cost increase.

Start-up costs and execution load as about 7 of 11 projects commence or ramp in FY27, including Khed EV powertrain (H2 FY27), sunroof (end FY27) and CSN/Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar plants; the 11% plus/minus 50 bps EBITDA guidance must absorb these.

Capex of about INR 1,750 crore in FY27 and possible additional land at CSN, Hosur and Gujarat; net debt rose to INR 2,179 crore, partly from the INR 200-odd crore FRIWO-linked acquisition.
Q4 debit/credit note adjustments were not quantified, so the underlying Q4 margin base is harder to assess; monitor Q1 FY27 margin and the pass-through reset to monthly or quarterly.

key_quotes: So some of the customers have been positive with some of the customer discussions have been happening, and we still have like 1, 1.5 month for this quarter.
Normally, you expect labor price to be 5%, 7%, 8%, 10% kind of a thing. But 35%, obviously, is not something which can be absorbed easily.
And we expect to complete the transition of Manesar plant to Farrukhnagar over the next 6 months.
But we do expect to absorb all this in our current profitability.

532539|2026-06.headline: Uno Minda Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% YoY to INR 5,557 crores; EBITDA margin 10.3%, with FY27 guidance of 11% ±50 bps held.

532540|2026-03.headline: TCS Q4 FY26 revenue rose 1.2% QoQ in constant currency, third straight sequential gain, with $12B TCV and 25.3% operating margin.
532540|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was ₹70,698 crore (up 5.4% QoQ in INR, $7.621B up 1.5% QoQ, 1.2% QoQ in constant currency), the third consecutive quarter of sequential growth. Q4 TCV was $12B including three mega deals, and client additions were seen across all revenue bands after about two years. Full-year FY26 revenue declined 2.4% in constant currency to $30.017B, while operating margin reached 25%, a four-year high. Management said the restructuring programme is complete, and the company announced annual increments effective April 1 with top performers getting double-digit increases.

532548|2026-03.headline: Century Plyboards posted record Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 1,492 crores (+24.5% YoY) with consolidated EBITDA margin ex-forex at 13.6%.
532548|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered record quarterly revenue of INR 1,492 crores, up 10.5% QoQ and 24.5% YoY, with consolidated EBITDA margin excluding forex losses at 13.6% versus 12.6% in Q3 and 12.1% a year ago. For FY26, revenue grew 19.2% and EBITDA ex-forex rose to INR 702 crores (13.0% margin) from INR 502 crores (11.1%), with PAT up 44% to INR 268 crores. Management has taken a 7% plywood price increase in April and an industry-wide 15% increase in MDF/particle board amid chemical and resin cost inflation, but gave no FY27 segment guidance, citing fluid geopolitical conditions. Capex is focused on plywood (Hoshiarpur, UP, Orissa land), with no frozen capex for MDF or particle board.

Utilisation ~80-85%; Badvel shut down in Q4 to add 20% capacity; South plant brownfield adds 60,000-70,000 CBM in Q1 FY27 (total to ~6 lakh CBM).

segments.name: Particle Board
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +3.9% QoQ and +108.3% YoY, EBITDA margin 7.2%; FY26 revenue +38.2% but FY26 EBITDA margin only 1.2%. Old multi-daylight plant shut and to be scrapped; new continuous line capacity 2,40,000 CBM, Chennai plant cost cited at ~INR 550 crores.

segments.name: Century Ports
segments.commentary: Wholly owned subsidiary commenced commercial operations at KPD-1 West, Kolkata, in Q4 FY26; management expects it to be cash positive from Q1 FY27. Management said no cost saving accrues to Century Ply; it remains a separate profit centre.

Plywood: UP plant capex expected to start late FY27 (Feb-March 2027 or Q1 FY28), commissioning in about 15-16 months after land is ready, targeted around Q1 FY29; Orissa land procurement underway (MoU covers plywood or MDF/particle board, nothing finalised).

Vishu Goel said MDF and plywood price increases of 10-12% were largely in Q1 and predominantly cover chemical cost increases.
Timber prices reported as broadly stable; management described a marginal correction, not 10%.
Plywood secondary demand stable post price increase, per management; MDF demand described as stable with normal April-May correction from Q4 exuberance.
March 2026 channel stocking was cited as a partial driver of MDF Q4 volume growth; management said April was not slow.
Plywood Sainik MR (around 8% of revenue last quarter) is being moved in-house after Hoshiarpur comes online, to reach 100% in-house production.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of MDF's ~39% YoY growth, utilisation and price increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Sumant Wattas cited year-end stocking, network expansion in the South and secondary-channel demand; utilisation 80-85% of rated capacity, with a practical max of 85-90%. Industry price increase of 15% barely covers chemical cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company give FY27 segment guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal said the situation is too fluid to guide now; management expects to be in a better position at the next call.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity plans for plywood FY27-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Nikita Bansal said utilisation is near 99% in Q4 and capacity rises ~30% in FY27 (about 20% brownfield plus Hoshiarpur in October); a new plant is needed in FY28-29, with UP and Orissa land being procured.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the new particle board plant cost lower than earlier?
qa_highlights.answer: Sumant Wattas said the old multi-daylight plant (~INR 70 crores) was archaic and is being scrapped. The new continuous line cost about INR 550 crores, not INR 700 crores as the analyst cited.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook for MDF after Q4 erosion?
qa_highlights.answer: Sumant Wattas said Q4 margin fell ~1 pt QoQ from chemical disruptions and one-off ATL spend; steady state is a high-teens EBITDA margin, with no firm timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Debt levels, forex exposure and capex funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Arun Julasaria said long-term debt will not exceed 1:1 debt-to-EBITDA, working capital debt will rise with growth, and forex exposure is within INR 600 crores, mostly mark-to-market on long-term debt for imported machinery. Management is not increasing forex exposure.

532548|2026-06.headline: Century Plyboards Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue hit record INR1,561 crore (+33.5% YoY) and PAT rose 57% to INR83.3 crore, helped by a 7% plywood price hike.
532548|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly consolidated revenue of INR1,561 crore, up 33.5% YoY, with EBITDA margin excluding forest losses at 13.0% and PAT up 57% YoY to INR83.3 crore. Plywood led, with revenue up 32.4% YoY and EBITDA margin of 16.9%, aided by a ~7% price increase taken in April on chemical input cost pressure. MDF was hit by a planned shutdown for the Andhra Pradesh capacity expansion (700 to 950 CBM/day), causing a sequential revenue decline, though revenue still grew ~29% YoY. Management has stopped giving formal guidance citing volatility, and said capex will be restrained with focus on utilisation and debt reduction.

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Revenue +32.4% YoY and +8.9% QoQ with 16.9% EBITDA margin after ~7% April price hike. Management attributes growth to price-led dealer stocking plus strong June and July sales.

segments.name: Laminates
segments.commentary: Revenue +14.7% YoY, EBITDA margin 10.2% on mix and utilisation. New home press commissioned, export-grade manufacturing planned from end-July 2026. Volume de-grew QoQ on size adjustment, per analyst question.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~29% YoY but down sequentially due to Andhra Pradesh expansion shutdown (700 to 950 CBM/day). Management targets 15%+ EBITDA margin without a date.

segments.name: Particle board
segments.commentary: Revenue +155.7% YoY and +29% QoQ on higher utilisation; margins still early-stage. Management expects ~15% margins next year.

segments.name: Logistics (Khidderpore Docks / CFS)
segments.commentary: Operations stabilised and EBITDA-positive; 9,000+ containers handled in July. Management is evaluating a possible strategic partner at valuation accretive to the company.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance on revenue, volume or margins; management cites volatility from geopolitical developments.
MDF: aim for 15%+ EBITDA margin as soon as possible; growth trajectory to be maintained for FY27.
Particle board: margins to rise quarter-on-quarter with utilisation; ~15% margin targeted next year.
Long-term: ROCE target of 20% for MDF and particle board; long-term debt to be within 1x EBITDA.
Revenue aspiration: INR12,000 crore, implying ~INR4,000 crore incremental revenue; indicative incremental capex ~INR2,500 crore at 1.5-2x asset turnover.
capex_capacity: Hoshiarpur greenfield plywood plant (60,000 CBM per annum) expected to commence in Q3 FY27.
Chennai brownfield plywood capacity: 8,000 CBM/month in Q1, 10,000 in Q2, 12,500 from Q3 FY27.
Andhra Pradesh MDF expanded from 700 to 950 CBM/day during Q1.

Uttar Pradesh plywood plant (~INR200 crore capex) targeted for April 2028 if land is secured by year-end; UP MDF to follow with a lag, timing not finalised. Odisha project still at land-selection stage.

No large capex planned in the near term; third laminate press capex ~INR25 crore; no large MDF or particle board capex planned. Particle board capacity expansion beyond ~240,000 CBM via efficiencies only, not 20%+.
demand_pricing: Industry growing ~5-7%; company estimates its share at 9.5-10% of the industry at end-FY26, targeting 15% in five years (implies 12-15% annual growth).

Price hike: ~7% in plywood (April), ~15% in MDF (part since rolled back as raw material prices moved), ~10% in domestic laminate and slightly lower in exports. Price increases remain above pre-war levels across most segments.
Channel inventory at June-end described as okay; July was a high sales month to date.
Brand spend ~4-4.5% of revenue including schemes. Total Cover assurance programme (10-year, covers furniture-related costs) launched; management states claim ratio of 0.06%.
Management declined to give volume guidance or premium/standard split.

qa_highlights.question: Is plywood growth from industry growth or share gain, and where is market share heading?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says share was 9.5-10% last year and the goal is 15% in five years. Growth was driven by the 7% price hike, dealer stocking and a strong June. Quarterly share is not tracked.

qa_highlights.question: When will balance sheet and gearing improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt rose on working capital for ~33% growth in a 60-day debt industry. Cash flows go to debt repayment, with no large capex planned. Target is long-term debt within 1x EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is it possible to give MDF FY27 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance has been stopped due to volatility. The objective is 15%+ MDF margins and a good growth trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: Will particle board capacity increase by minor capex to ~3 lakh?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The line was pre-designed in two parts. Efficiency gains are possible but a 20%+ increase is unlikely.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for UP and Odisha greenfield projects?
qa_highlights.answer: UP land is not yet secured; target is to acquire by year-end, with the plywood plant by April 2028. Odisha is still in government talks with no land selected. UP MDF timing is not finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable ROCE for MDF and particle board, given particle board capex and realisation differences?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the analyst's numbers do not match its capacity basis. The target for both segments is 20% ROCE, which it believes is achievable over time.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for the logistics business and its structure?
qa_highlights.answer: The business is EBITDA- and cash-flow-positive and not core. A strategic partner may come in at an accretive valuation. Only half of phase 1 of the new port is operating, and CFS is expected to grow double digits.

risks_watch: Plywood growth of ~30% YoY was helped by a ~7% April price hike and dealer stocking; watch whether volume growth holds once the price-led stocking unwinds, given management says July is a high sales month to date and quarterly share is not tracked.
Working capital and debt: management attributes the debt rise to 33% growth in a 60-day debt industry; track whether long-term debt moves within 1x EBITDA as targeted, with no timeline given.

MDF margins: target of 15%+ EBITDA margin has no date; Andhra Pradesh expansion (700 to 950 CBM/day) and roll-back of part of the ~15% MDF price hike make the margin path uncertain; management expects improvement in H2 FY27.
Particle board: margins are early-stage and management aims for ~15% next year; ROCE of 20% for MDF and particle board is a long-term target that an analyst challenged as unsupported by the numbers.

Execution on capacity: Hoshiarpur plant (Q3 FY27), Chennai ramp to 12,500 CBM/month from Q3 FY27, and UP land not yet secured (target by year-end, plant April 2028); Odisha still at land-selection stage.
Geopolitical volatility: management has withdrawn formal guidance and volume guidance, so quarterly results are the only checkpoint for the company's stated trajectory.
key_quotes: Currently, we have stopped giving guidance. The reason we have stopped giving guidance is because the situation is very volatile.
So, I think the maximum amount of cash flow that we're going to be generating will go towards the repayment of debt.
The objective is to reach towards that as soon as possible, and we are going to be heading towards the same.
I don't think a 20% plus quantum will be likely.

532553|2026-03.headline: Welspun Enterprises Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14% YoY to INR1,199 crore and EBITDA 31% to INR272 crore; FY26 order book about INR20,000 crore after Pune-Shirur win.

532555|2026-03.headline: NTPC group added a record 9,618 MW in FY26 and standalone Q4 PAT rose 51.4% to INR8,747 crores.
532555|2026-03.overview: NTPC's Q4 FY26 and FY26 call (hosted by JM Financial, 23 May 2026) showed standalone Q4 PAT up 51.4% YoY to INR8,747 crores, while FY26 standalone total income fell 2.69% to INR1,69,725 crores on lower daytime demand and backing down of thermal plants. Group PAT rose 15% to INR27,546 crores and NGEL revenue grew 29% in FY26. Management guided to about 9,557 MW of FY27 capacity additions, mostly renewables via JVs and subsidiaries, and flagged a higher FY27 renewable grid-connectivity risk. Management said West Asia tensions have no material operational impact, with about 18 days of coal stock and about 18% of coal needs met from captive mines.

532555|2026-06.headline: NTPC reported Q1 FY27 PAT of INR 5,343 crore, up 12% YoY, and targets 150 GW by FY32 and 250 GW by FY37.
532555|2026-06.overview: NTPC's 22nd Analysts and Institutional Investors Meet (held 27 July 2026, post Q1 results) centred on demand growth, the 250 GW FY37 capacity plan and INR 17 lakh crore capex envelope. Management reported Q1 FY27 PAT of INR 5,343 crore (up 12% YoY) and said FY26 standalone PAT was a record INR 23,162 crore. Renewable additions lagged target: 4.2 GW in FY26 and 1.9 GW added in FY27 to date, against a FY27 RE target of 7-8 GW. Technical-minimum and curtailment issues for thermal units, and a shift in the tender vs cost-plus debate, were the main analyst focus.

qa_highlights.answer: CMD said RE should not be measured in MW alone; storage is needed, and 7 GW with storage is equivalent to about 8 GW. Transmission delays are a key constraint.

532612|2026-03.headline: Indoco Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 25.8% YoY to INR 4,291 mn and EBITDA margin hit 14.7%, with international formulations up 94.6%.
532612|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the first positive quarter in about six quarters, driven by international formulations in regulated and emerging markets, while India was muted by a weak season in anti-infectives and respiratory. Standalone EBITDA rose to INR 630 mn (14.7%) from INR 35 mn a year earlier. Trade receivables rose sharply, mainly on long-credit emerging-market collections, and supplier/MSME payables were stretched. Consolidated debt is about INR 960 crore, with management guiding to roughly INR 140 crore of annual repayments and a tight capex freeze. Management also announced the hive-off of its India and Africa ophthalmic business to Sunway.

qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the swing to low-margin trading sales, a COGS spike, and expired-product write-offs of about INR 4 crore. Management noted that the net worth figure includes Warren Remedies, which is also loss-making.

532626|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 56% YoY to INR931 crore and PAT 32% to INR36 crore, while lead volumes fell on supply-chain disruption.
532626|2026-06.overview: Revenue, EBITDA and PAT grew 56%, 30% and 32% YoY to INR931 crore, INR56 crore and INR36 crore, with EBITDA margin about 6%. Copper volumes more than tripled YoY to record levels and copper EBITDA per ton rose 66% to INR48,488. Lead volumes moderated as shipping delays via the Strait of Hormuz constrained scrap imports, and management chose to prioritise value-added products (85% of lead revenue), giving a record lead EBITDA of INR21,595 per ton. Management says demand is intact and the constraint is supply, not demand.

segments.name: Lead
segments.commentary: Volumes moderated due to supply constraints; value-added products were 85% of segment revenue. Export mix 55% of lead sales. Management guides sustainable lead EBITDA of INR18,000-20,000 per ton.

segments.name: Copper
segments.commentary: Production and sales volumes each rose more than 3x YoY to record levels (about 4,000 tonnes in the quarter per analyst); export mix 25%. Copper expected to be about 45% of FY27 revenue. Existing capacity about 75% utilised.

segments.name: Plastics
segments.commentary: Turned profitable in Q1 with net profit of about INR15 lakh on about 800 tonnes of volume.

segments.name: Aluminium
segments.commentary: Small production of about 200 metric tonnes in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Lead value-added mix for FY27 targeted at 65-70% (FY26 about 63%).
Lead EBITDA sustainable at INR18,000-20,000 per ton as volumes rise; Q1 INR21,595 was driven by 85% value-added mix.
Copper EBITDA per ton before value-addition guided above INR40,000 (earlier guidance INR35,000-40,000); cathode blended EBITDA guided INR60,000-65,000 per ton.
Management reiterated earlier FY27 lead volume guidance of about 1.25-1.3 lakh tonnes, saying it expects to close near that level, though it did not give a revised number.
2030 roadmap: over 15% volume growth, 20%+ CAGR in revenue and profitability, EBITDA margin above 8%, ROCE above 20%, over 60% revenue from value-added products.
FY27 capex about INR175 crore: maintenance INR20-25 crore, balance INR140-150 crore for copper plant. Management did not give volume guidance for FY27/FY28 by product yet.
capex_capacity: 36,000 tpa copper cathode plant at Thervoy Kandigai, Tamil Nadu, total investment about INR200 crore, funded from internal accruals; about INR25 crore spent so far.
Phase 1 (18,000 tpa) on track for commissioning in December 2026, trial runs in Q4 FY27; machine installation from end-September, Phase 2 (18,000 tpa) targeted for Q3 FY28.
Incremental 6,000 tpa copper recycling capacity commissioned in Q4 FY26 (copper recycling total about 12,000 tpa, in Andhra Pradesh); about 75% utilised. Target utilisation about 75% through FY27.
New 72,000 tpa lead (TKD) capacity utilisation below 50% because of the focus on value-added pure lead.
CRISIL upgraded outlook to A positive from A stable, rating reaffirmed.
demand_pricing: Management says there is no demand softness; the constraint is delayed shipments and supply-chain disruption.
Lead exports go mainly to Southeast Asia, not Europe; Middle East procurement below 5% of sourcing, with the main issue being shipping routes via the Strait of Hormuz.
Lead sourcing about 97% international in Q1; domestic prices were too high for profitable domestic buying, though management has started looking at domestic procurement.
Copper pricing was supported by tight availability, enabling a premium on copper sales.
Copper sourcing: mostly imports, with plans for 25-30% domestic sourcing going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Can lead volumes reach the 1.25-1.3 lakh tonne FY27 guidance given the current run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of closing up to the committed numbers but will see how supply chains evolve over the next 1-2 months; no revision given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there demand softness in lead, given exposure to Western and Middle East markets?
qa_highlights.answer: No demand softness; exports are mainly Southeast Asia. Only supply delays are affecting volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 16% YoY and 44% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Logistics is a small part; the major driver is fuel prices and some additive prices that rose over the last three months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the record lead EBITDA per ton one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a sustainable level is INR18,000-20,000 per ton; Q1 was high because of the 85% value-added mix.

qa_highlights.question: Capex split for FY27 of about INR175 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance INR20-25 crore; the balance of INR140-150 crore is for the new copper plant.

qa_highlights.question: Copper EBITDA per ton outlook before value addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects above INR40,000 per ton going forward, aided by capacity efficiencies and a premium in the current tight market.

qa_highlights.question: EPR credits and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: EPR benefit minimal this quarter as most purchases were imports; unmonetised EPR credits remain on the books. Working capital not stretched because payments are made about a week before arrival at port.

risks_watch: Lead volume shortfall from shipping disruption (Strait of Hormuz) could put the 1.25-1.3 lakh tonne FY27 guidance at risk; monthly production fell in May and early June.
Cost inflation from fuel and additive prices, with other expenses up 44% QoQ.
Copper cathode commissioning slipping beyond December 2026 would delay margin uplift; the cathode blended EBITDA of INR60,000-65,000 per ton is not yet proven.
Copper scrap security as global supply tightens and more countries retain scrap; reliance on imports for most copper sourcing.
Lead EBITDA per ton could normalise toward INR18,000-20,000 as the value-added mix falls from 85%.
Lead volumes fell sharply YoY, with analysts noting a much steeper decline than a competitor; management declined to comment.

532630|2026-03.headline: Gokaldas Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin rose to about 12% (16% ex-tariff impact per management), with FY27 guided to a couple of points of margin improvement.
532630|2026-03.overview: FY26 was disrupted by US reciprocal tariffs that stayed near 50% for much of the year, with AGOA lapse hitting Africa, yet total income rose 4% to INR4,065 crores and the EBITDA margin was held at the prior-year level. Q4 standalone margins improved on volume-driven operating leverage and the post-February normalisation of the penal tariff, with no tariff refunds booked. Management guides to a Y-o-Y margin improvement of a couple of percentage points in FY27 and Africa revenue of about $115-120 million, while BTPL is being merged in and is expected to turn EBITDA positive in H2 FY27. Net debt rose by INR395 crores on capex, BTPL investment and working capital, and management targets a INR75-100 crore working capital reduction in Gokaldas and Atraco.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone operating EBITDA margin Q4 FY26
financial_highlights.value: about 12% (about 16% adding back tariff impact; about 15.5% excluding provision reversals)
financial_highlights.change: Improved Q-o-Q and Y-o-Y, per analyst read of 200-400 bps

financial_highlights.metric: Net discount to customers FY26 (tariff offset)

segments.name: India operations (Gokaldas standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 operations grew 2% Y-o-Y while Indian apparel exports fell 10%; FY26 India operations grew 10% Y-o-Y. Standalone volume was 10.19 million pieces in Q4 (8.6 million ex-Matrix at INR773 realisation) and 33.627 million pieces for FY26 at INR765.

segments.name: Africa (Atraco)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about $80 million; FY27 target $115-120 million, with H1 run-rate about $24-25 million per quarter. Q4 volume 5.63 million pieces at INR405; FY26 16.27 million pieces at INR420. Management expects H2 FY27 EBITDA margin of 8-10%.

segments.name: BTPL (Bombay Rayon, fabric)
segments.commentary: Merger initiated subject to NCLT approval, expected in Q3 FY27. Utilisation near 50 lakh meters/month against 70 lakh capacity, expandable to 100 lakh for INR50-60 crores capex. FY27 revenue guided above INR1,000 crores; EBITDA breakeven in H1 and about 6-7% in H2 FY27.

segments.name: Matrix and other Indian subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Had minor setbacks in Q4 as customers shifted business to other regions during the 50% tariff period; management expects reversal in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone Y-o-Y EBITDA margin improvement of a couple of percentage points, conditional on no new tariff disruption; H1 FY27 margins still absorb about 3% sharper pricing given on H1 orders.
Africa FY27 revenue target $115-120 million (worst case $115 million), with H2 FY27 Africa EBITDA margin of 8-10%.
Working capital to be reduced by INR75-100 crores in FY27 across Gokaldas and Atraco, excluding BTPL merger impact.
Medium-term (FY28 steady state, excluding new capacity drag): India EBITDA margin 13-13.5%, Africa 10-10.5%, India:Africa revenue split about 75:25 to 80:20; BTPL about 12% in FY28 and 14% in FY29.
Management said FY27 revenue growth would be much more than 10-12% excluding U.K./EU FTA benefits, which are not factored in; it targets at least 15% growth.
Two new premium customers in India (one US, one European) and two in Africa (one US, one European) to contribute revenue from FY27, about 5% of revenue in year one.
capex_capacity: Africa capacity expansion completed in FY26; one factory running 2 shifts on 20-25% of its capacity, with a second-shift opportunity without major capex.

Karnataka (Kolar Gold Fields) half-factory ramp-up expected through Q1-Q2 FY27 to full utilisation; Madhya Pradesh (Bhopal) 1,000-machine unit expected at full utilisation by Q3 FY27 (Sept-Oct), adding about INR175 crores revenue at full capacity; Karnataka adds about INR125 crores at steady state.
Two further planned factories (about INR300 crores steady-state revenue) with capex of INR80-100 crores over two years; decision expected in the next quarter or so, with revenue mainly FY28.
Total capacity to reach 104 million pieces including 12 million added (India about 7.5 million, Africa about 4.5 million); India 52 million and Africa 40 million pieces currently, per management.
BTPL: 70 lakh meters/month capacity, expandable to 100 lakh with INR50-60 crores capex; captive fabric consumption by Gokaldas about 30-35%.
demand_pricing: Reciprocal tariff of about 50% (including penal 25%) on India until mid-February 2026; penal tariff withdrawn, then a 10% tariff applied until July 24, 2026. Section 301 tariffs may reset to about 20% for rest of world from late July; Africa not under Section 301 probe (Kenya stays at 10%).
Tariff rebates given during the penal regime were up to about 15% of order value, partly clawed back from the supply chain; sharper pricing of about 3% continues in H1 FY27 and is removed in H2.
AGOA extended to December 2026; US administration reportedly moving to country-by-country deals; Kenya FTA not expected by end-2026.
US retail sales grew 8% and UK 6% in CY25; US retailers pared imports from H2 CY25. Spring 27 orders being booked; customers ordering conservatively.

Input cost inflation from Middle East war (polyester, packaging, fuel, trims, cotton); pass-through being attempted in H2 orders, with partial recovery expected given customer resistance and competitor under-utilisation in SE Asia and China.
Hedging: about 80% of revenue hedged for the next two quarters at INR87-91/USD; 50% for the following two. Rupee depreciation benefit not yet in numbers, expected in H2.
Labour cost inflation in India: Haryana announced 35% wage increase from April 1 and UP 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 12% standalone margin be sustained, and what is the Africa margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Africa H2 FY27 EBITDA margin of 8-10% and operating leverage in India; Matrix and other subsidiaries were hit by pivoted orders in Q4 and should recover in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital reduce in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a reduction of INR75-100 crores in Gokaldas and Atraco, with BTPL's working capital to be added on merger; the INR200 crore increase reflected inventory build for Q1 orders (Chinese holidays) and year-end receivables.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to volumes if AGOA lapses again?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it refused to share AGOA-related discounts last time and let volume fall; now it has a broader Africa customer base and can offer some AGOA-related support if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Were tariff refunds booked in Q4 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No tariff reversals were factored in; the Q4 gain came from volume-driven operating leverage and no tariff discounts after mid-February.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 margin outlook with BTPL included?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady-state FY28 India EBITDA margin 13-13.5%, Africa 10-10.5%, BTPL about 12% in FY28 and 14% in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Are the acquired entities meeting internal targets?
qa_highlights.answer: No, not in FY26 due to tariff disruption; management expects them to perform to plan in FY27.

risks_watch: Section 301 tariff reset from July 24, 2026 and whether India returns to about 20%.
AGOA expiry in December 2026 and timing of renewal; Kenya FTA uncertainty.
Cotton, polyester and fuel cost pass-through versus customer resistance in H2 FY27.
BTPL NCLT merger timing (Q3 FY27) and its loss-making run-rate (-4 to -5% EBITDA in Q4 FY26); integration working capital.
Labour cost inflation in North India (Haryana 35%, UP 25% wage increases).
Rupee hedges at INR87-91/USD could limit currency gains; debt rising with capex and net debt up INR395 crores.
Tax expense elevated at consolidated level because losses at overseas and new Indian subsidiaries get no tax credit.
