532630|2026-06.headline: Gokaldas Q1 FY27: consolidated income up 21% YoY and EBITDA up 17%, with Africa up 45% and India up 16% amid a sector-wide 12% decline.
532630|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong, broad-based quarter, with consolidated income up 21% YoY and consolidated EBITDA up 17% (India EBITDA up 14%). India revenue grew 16% YoY against a 12% fall in Indian apparel exports, partly helped by the lower US tariff regime. Africa grew 45% YoY on AGOA renewal and a weak prior-year base, but Africa EBITDA margin was about 8%, below normal. Cost pressures from wages (Haryana minimum wage up 35% from April 2026), fuel, chemicals, logistics and freight were significant, partly offset by overhead control and a weaker rupee. BTPL (fabric unit) remains loss-making at the operating level, with merger expected in Q3 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Target: double-digit by Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28

financial_highlights.metric: India wage cost increase in Q1
Other expenses cost hit (utilities and logistics)

financial_highlights.change: Mix-driven; management disputed the volume metric

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue up 16% YoY and EBITDA up 14%, versus a 12% decline in Indian apparel exports. Matrix plus stand-alone India ASP cited at INR 613 with about 1.53 million pieces for the old Gurgaon units. Central India plants running at about 85% utilisation; South India plants full.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Revenue up 45% YoY on AGOA renewal and a weak Q1 FY26 base. EBITDA margin about 8%, with management targeting double-digit by Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28. Utilisation at 80-85%; FY27 visibility of USD 112-115 million against a USD 120 million target.

segments.name: BTPL (fabric unit)
segments.commentary: Running at 50-53 lakh meters per month, with Q1 turnover around INR 170 crore and operational EBITDA of about -7.5% to -8%. Targets EBITDA break-even in H1, EBITDA positive in Q3 and PBT positive in Q4 FY27; merger expected in Q3 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Growth: management said 15%-plus growth is 'straightforward' and it should do better; mid-to-high-teens was floated by the analyst, with management not confirming a number. Q2 FY27 revenue expected to resemble Q1; Q3 and Q4 orders are being booked.
Africa FY27 revenue visibility of USD 112-115 million against the USD 120 million target, with a quarterly run-rate of about USD 30 million.
Africa EBITDA margin expected back to double-digit in Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28.
ETR guided at 20-22% for FY27 as international operations contribute.
Wage, fuel and logistics cost pressure expected to partly ease in H2 if conditions improve; uncertainty remains. Pass-through pricing being applied to new orders.

Capex: about INR 80 crore mentioned in presentation; Jharkhand and Karnataka greenfield units total about INR 100 crore (INR 70-75 crore in FY27), with steady-state revenue of about INR 350 crore from FY29. Bhopal second unit yields revenue from H2 FY27.
Potential 2,000-3,000 extra machines (about INR 200 crore revenue per 1,000 machines) to be decided within 3 months; larger spend in FY28.
capex_capacity: Bhopal second unit ramping up, expected to reach near full utilisation by Q4 FY27; adds about 3.5 million pieces and about INR 175-200 crore steady-state revenue.

Karnataka and Ranchi existing-factory machine additions (about 500-700 machines) are being commissioned in FY27; total of commissioned Bhopal Phase 2, Karnataka and Ranchi adds about INR 275 crore revenue potential.

New Jharkhand and Karnataka facilities: total investment about INR 100 crore, about 3.5 million pieces each, steady-state revenue about INR 350 crore combined; expected on stream H2 FY28, full potential FY29.
Africa: capacity already in place to deliver about USD 120 million annual revenue; second shift used for swing capacity; no significant Africa capex planned until existing options are exhausted.
BTPL capacity about 50 lakh meters per month, expected to grow about 30%; new customer onboarding with operations starting in Q2.
demand_pricing: US and UK end-consumer demand grew strongly through the first six months of CY26, though US growth slowed in June; EU and UK apparel imports declined through the first five months of FY27 per management.
US Section 301 tariff places India on par with competing sourcing countries, while China and Vietnam face 12.5%. India-UK FTA brings parity with Bangladesh and Vietnam in the UK.
Management says European buyers and US buyers are increasing inquiries and business towards India, extending beyond fashion and outerwear into shirts and bottoms; denim inquiries also rising.
Pricing: fabric cost pass-through is standard; some items (poly bags, cartons, fuel) were not priced into Q1 orders set in January and will be priced going forward.
Product mix: ASPs range from about USD 40-50 for high-value products to lower-value items; average realisation in India about INR 613 per piece for Gurgaon units.
UK is about 4-4.5% of total revenue; focus on larger UK players such as Marks & Spencer. Fibre mix about 65% cotton and up to 30% man-made (annual).

qa_highlights.question: India volume growth was only 3.4%, so where does India volume go from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume is a misleading metric because Q1 and Q2 are high-value outerwear with 150-250 minutes of content per garment, versus about 22-25 minutes for a shirt; it added there is no YoY volume drop and growth is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Does the strong order book mean the mid-teens growth guide holds, or can growth be mid-to-high teens?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Spring '27 orders execute in Q3 FY27 and revenue traction for that period and beyond looks similar to Q1; 15%-plus growth was called 'straightforward' and it should do better.

qa_highlights.question: When will Africa EBITDA margin recover to double digits from about 8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects double-digit in Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28, with H2 the differentiator; it cited AGOA expiring December with a 2-year extension passed by the Senate and awaiting the House and presidential assent.

qa_highlights.question: What is the visibility on shipping delays, and could they delay orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is the worst shipping environment; outbound FOB shipments can wait about 2 weeks for a vessel, and it expects easing over the next two quarters as the war and typhoon issues ease.

qa_highlights.question: How do India incentive cuts (RoSCTL) and the BTPL merger affect margins, and is the Africa margin base higher?
qa_highlights.answer: RoSCTL is about 3.5% and management's worst case is a halving to about 1.75%, which it expects to offset; BTPL should reach mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA after merger in Q3. Management said the EBITDA margin would be a bit higher than the analyst's base, and it sees the rupee weakness as a cushion (about 70% of dollars hedged at about INR 89).

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 and H2 visibility, particularly for India?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 and Q2 are booked; Q2 revenue should look like Q1. Q3 and Q4 orders are being booked now and the projection looks good despite US inflation concerns.

qa_highlights.question: Is India gaining share from China and Vietnam after the tariff change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 2.5% advantage is not remarkable by itself, but European and US buyers are increasing inquiries for India across shirts, bottoms and denim, not just fashion and outerwear.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 35% minimum wage hike a larger hit, and how is it being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Haryana minimum wage rose 35% from April 2026 but overall wages for the Gurgaon/Manesar units rose only 14-15%; India wage cost increase in Q1 was about INR 20 crore, absorbed in the system. Karnataka increase was about 5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the other expenses increase and the ETR outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses rose by about INR 5-6 crore on utilities, gas, fuel and chemicals plus inbound and outbound logistics, partly expected to ease in H2; FY27 ETR is guided at 20-22%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BTPL Q1 performance and the break-even timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: BTPL had about INR 170 crore fabric turnover in Q1 with operational EBITDA of about -7.5% to -8%; management targets EBITDA break-even in H1 (Q2), EBITDA positive in Q3 and PBT positive in Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and capacity plan, including Jharkhand, Karnataka and Bhopal?
qa_highlights.answer: Jharkhand and Karnataka together need about INR 100 crore (INR 70-75 crore in FY27) for about INR 350 crore steady-state revenue, coming on stream H2 FY28; Bhopal Phase 2 adds about 3.5 million pieces and INR 175-200 crore revenue. Management also said it may add 2,000-3,000 machines with a decision within 3 months and larger spend in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Africa plan require more capex, and what is the Africa capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant Africa capex is planned until second-shift options are exhausted; capacity in place can deliver about USD 120 million annual revenue. FY27 visibility is USD 112-115 million against the USD 120 million target, a quarterly run-rate of about USD 30 million.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Indian business share, utilisation and product-wise breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Central India plants run about 85% utilisation and South India plants are full; Africa is at 80-85%. Management gave the old Gurgaon units at 1.53 million pieces at INR 613 ASP, while Matrix alone was about 1.5 million pieces at INR 613.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fabric mix and UK exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Cotton is about 65% or a little higher and man-made fibres up to 30%, on an annual basis per management. UK is about 4-4.5% of revenue, with focus on larger players such as Marks & Spencer.

532633|2026-03.headline: Alldigi Tech FY26 revenue rose 9.6% to INR598.7 crore and EBITDA 25% to INR162 crore, with management guiding to mid-teens revenue growth in FY27.
532633|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR154.7 crore (+5.9% YoY, +1.3% QoQ) and EBITDA was INR43.7 crore (+24.2% YoY), with EBITDA margin for FY26 at 27.1% versus 23.7% in FY25. Tech & Digital (T&D) was the growth engine at +22.3% YoY in Q4, while BPM was flat YoY at INR110.4 crore as management deliberately exited low-margin domestic FTE business. Management said about 10% of the portfolio is still low-margin BPM business, and guided to mid-teens revenue growth and a 1-2% margin improvement for FY27. Q4 PAT rose 49.7% YoY to INR28.9 crore, and FY26 PAT was flat at INR82.2 crore. This was the first call with new CEO Natarajan Laxsmanan, who joined about a month earlier.

segments.name: Tech & Digital (T&D)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR44.3 crore (+22.3% YoY, +14.5% QoQ); FY26 revenue INR156.2 crore (+16.5%). Q4 segment margin INR19.5 crore (44%); FY26 segment margin INR66.6 crore (+28.9%). Processed 49.9 lakh employee records in Q4 and 191.5 lakh in FY26; added INR40.1 crore new ACV.

segments.name: BPM (CXM)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR110.4 crore (+0.4% YoY, flat); FY26 revenue INR442.4 crore (+7.3%). Q4 segment margin INR15 crore (about 13.6%); FY26 segment margin INR62.3 crore (+16.8%). International share of BPM revenue 78% in FY26 (73% prior year). Added INR54.1 crore new ACV; international BPM revenue grew 8.7% YoY in Q4.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at mid-teens, per the CEO, similar to the aspiration stated for FY26.
EBITDA margin expected to improve about 1-2% in FY27 (management said 1-1.5% annual margin growth is typical), but no absolute margin number was given.
BPM segment margin expected to hold around 13-14%; the Q4 QoQ dip was a one-off linked to a leave policy alignment with the holding company.
T&D growth expected to be slightly higher than BPM growth; international mix expected to keep rising.
Depreciation for FY27 expected to rise only modestly (management said a couple of crore from the new Chennai office), with a sub-10% increase implied on the FY26 base of about INR58.6 crore.
Management expects no significant negative currency impact on revenue; a weaker rupee is expected to add to margin.
FY27 existing-customer headcount expected to be flat, with no major positive growth in employee records anticipated.
capex_capacity: Office upgrade underway in Chennai (new office being built) and Noida, with about INR20 crore of investment for the Chennai facility.
Admin and facility capex typically runs INR20-25 crore a year.

HRMS Version 2 (integrated HRMS and payroll, AI-enabled) to be released in FY27; PulseHR.ai to automate inbound query handling and cut turnaround time.
demand_pricing: HRO international order book was about 48% of total order book as of March 31, 2026 (no comparable domestic figure given).
T&D ACV wins have consistently been more than 60% from international clients.
Pipeline of large BPM brands is in place, but timing is uncertain: client decisions were on hold due to macro conditions and the war, impacting healthcare clients.

FY27 BPM focus verticals: healthcare and RCM, international insurance, and international collections.
Existing T&D customers have plateaued; about 90% of FY26 record growth came from new customers.
Deal closure: about 30% of deals closed at CHRO/CFO level; smaller deals (under 1,000 employees) close at HR level; CEO involvement is rare.

qa_highlights.question: Why did HRO revenue grow faster than payroll-process volumes, and will that continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue is not directly proportional to employee numbers because of one-time change requests, year-end tax work, new wage code implementation, and currency benefits from international business. Higher revenue than headcount growth is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What share of FY26 growth was constant currency?
qa_highlights.answer: Avinash Jain said 3.3% of FY26 growth came from currency depreciation and 6.3% from company efforts.

qa_highlights.question: Will the BPM headcount decline continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the exit from low-margin business will continue through FY27; about 10% of the portfolio is still low-margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue CAGR below the mid-teens target, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the strategic exit from low-margin business and industry factors. It still sees mid-teens growth for FY27, which it said is slightly above industry growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to a new large BPM client and how will margins change after the exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no timeline, citing a large pipeline and deals delayed by macro conditions. It said the low-margin exit will have minimal impact because it is only about 10% of the portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: Why do segment margins (about INR129 crore) differ from reported EBITDA (INR162 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Avinash Jain said segment margins are reported at PBT level after depreciation and finance costs, net of unallocable items, other income and expenses. He offered to reconcile offline.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company win deals and what is the sales structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited price, scale, platform flexibility, operational accuracy and turnaround time. International sales are now run by geography-specific teams with rainmaker and technology partners.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex and depreciation outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Avinash Jain guided to admin/facility capex of INR20-25 crore a year plus about INR20 crore for the Chennai office, with only a small rise in depreciation from the FY26 base of about INR58.6 crore.

532636|2026-03.headline: IIFL Finance Q4 FY26: consolidated PAT of INR623 crore (up 24% QoQ) and loan AUM of INR1,08,180 crore (up 38% YoY), with gold AUM up 150% YoY to INR52,581 crore.
532636|2026-03.overview: Management reported consolidated PAT before minority interest of INR623 crore, up 24% QoQ, and pre-provision operating profit of INR1,173 crore, up 80% YoY and 9% QoQ. Loan AUM crossed INR1 lakh crore, growing 10% QoQ, with gold the primary growth engine at 62 tonnes of tonnage. Asset quality improved, with GNPA about 1.5% and NNPA 0.7%, while the housing finance arm stayed flat and weak on profitability. Management guided to FY27 AUM growth of 20-25% for gold, 18-20% for housing, a credit cost fall to 1.5-1.7%, and a 100-120 bp cost-of-funds reduction on a rating upgrade. The income tax special audit outcome remained pending, with management expecting orders within days and saying it would appeal any demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the income tax special audit and the likely impact (rumoured INR300-400 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on speculative reports. The special audit (mainly gold loans) is complete and the assessment order is expected within days or about a week; the company will appeal any demand and does not expect a material adverse outcome.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a demerger of IIFL Home Finance and Samasta?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an option to demerge into three entities (for ADIA's exit from home finance), but this is a Board decision with no timeline and no active process.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 credit cost and ROA expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost is guided to 1.5-1.7% (against 2.7-3% in FY26) and ROA to rise from 2.4% toward 3-3.5%. Credit cost applies only to the on-balance-sheet book (about 10-20% of AUM), not to assigned loans.

qa_highlights.question: How will IIFL adapt to new gold-loan rules (cash-flow assessment for loans above INR2.5 lakh) and branch expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Detailed credit assessment is in place for all loans above INR2.5 lakh and the branch model already does cash-flow assessment. Gold AUM growth is guided at 20-25%, with more branches in underserved areas.

qa_highlights.question: What are the leverage and capital plans, and is equity needed for 20%+ growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can grow without equity if co-lending and DA reach 40-45%; it is comfortable with leverage up to 4.5x and will raise debt periodically and equity when the time is right.

qa_highlights.question: Why was housing AUM muted in FY26, and why are home finance ROE and ROA weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the exit of micro-LAP (overlapping with MFI borrowers) and reduced leverage after an equity raise 2-3 years ago. Growth is expected to lift ROE back toward double digits, and LAP is being focused on at about 18% of the mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rating upgrade roadmap and its impact on cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM crossed INR1 lakh crore, GNPA is 1.5%, and profitability is improving; the remaining gap is capital adequacy, which needs more off-book growth or equity. A move to AA+ could cut funding cost by 100-120 bp, but management would not quantify the rating-upgrade impact.

532644|2026-09.headline: JK Cement Q2 FY27 net sales rose 21% YoY to INR3,561 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR500 crore on fuel-cost pressure; H1 volume up 19% to 11.3 MT.

Quarterly EBITDA was INR500 crore versus INR440 crore a year ago and INR639 crore in Q1, with the company attributing the QoQ fall to rising fuel costs and only partial pass-through. Net debt rose to INR4,571 crore, with net debt/EBITDA of 1.95x, and management expects a peak near INR6,000 crore on the 50 MT plan.

532648|2026-03.headline: YES Bank Q4 FY26 net profit rose 44.7% YoY to INR 1,068 crore, with ROA of 1.0% and GNPA at a record-low 1.3%.
532648|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered 44.7% YoY net profit growth to INR 1,068 crore and a 1.0% ROA, in line with guidance. NIM rose 10 bps QoQ and 20 bps YoY to 2.7%, helped by RIDF and mandated-deposit rundown and CASA outperformance. Asset quality improved sharply, with GNPA at 1.3% and NNPA at 0.2%, while INR 341 crore of one-time standard-asset provisioning was taken in Q4. Advances grew 11.1% YoY to INR 2.73 lakh crore, with management signalling faster momentum and FY27 growth targeted at 13-15%.

segments.commentary: Retail disbursements grew ~41% YoY in Q4 FY26 and are above 20% YoY; Retail slippage in Q4 was INR 888 crore, lowest in 9 quarters. Retail book growth guided at 10-11% for FY27.

segments.name: Corporate and Commercial Banking
segments.commentary: Corporate book growing ~20% and Commercial Banking ~18%, per management. Commercial Banking is described as a preferred growth area.

Target ROA of 1% exit rate maintained; internal aim to add 25-50 bps of core ROA improvement over 2-3 years, excluding JC Flowers ARC write-backs.
Structural NIM target of 3.25-3.5% over 2-3 years; no near-term NIM guidance given.

qa_highlights.answer: Q4 CA and SA each grew ~4% QoQ on average balances; CASA ~11% YoY on average. FY27 growth is guided at 13-15%, with sequential momentum accelerating from December to March.

qa_highlights.question: Will the mix shift between Retail, Wholesale and Commercial after the SMBC induction?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail disbursements are above 20% YoY and normalising at 20-25%; Retail book growth expected at 10-11% in FY27. Corporate is growing ~20%, and mix is expected to stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: How did the bond yield spike affect treasury and AFS reserves?
qa_highlights.answer: The trading book is small. AFS reserve is about negative INR 100 crore at March 31, with a swing of ~INR 200 crore. Most of the SLR book sits in HTM, and CET-1 absorbed ~10 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 340 crore one-time standard-asset provision?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 341 crore of provisioning was taken in Q4 under evolving and prudent policies, not linked to any credit issue. It was funded by SR recoveries of ~INR 450 crore and a INR 288 crore write-back from one corporate account.

qa_highlights.question: What is the next ROA milestone, and how sustainable is 1%?
qa_highlights.answer: The bank exited FY26 at 1% ROA. Internal aim is 25-50 bps core ROA improvement, with some JC Flowers ARC write-backs still to come in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What were credit card and personal loan slippages in INR crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit card slippage was about INR 133-140 crore and personal loan slippage about INR 160-180 crore; the figures were corrected during the call.

qa_highlights.question: Will branch expansion and branch share of disbursals change?
qa_highlights.answer: The plan is about 80 branches a year, aligned to deposit growth, credit growth and credit quality in each pin code. Branches supply ~60% of the ~50% of disbursals sourced internally.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RIDF runoff profile beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY28 and FY29 will see equal reductions, similar to FY27, with thinner runoff in FY29-FY30 as maturities taper.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AT1 case status?
qa_highlights.answer: The matter is sub judice, with Supreme Court hearings complete and judgment reserved. Management declined to comment on the likely outcome.

segments.commentary: Advertising revenue grew 12% YoY to INR 156 crore; circulation revenue grew 14% to INR 13 crore (about INR 1.5 crore absolute change, mostly pricing and mix).

segments.name: Hindi Print
segments.commentary: Advertising revenue rose YoY to INR 139 crore; circulation revenue flat.

segments.name: Radio
segments.commentary: Topline flat YoY; operating EBITDA negative INR 3 crore. Licences surrendered for certain non-viable stations.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Operating revenue down about 28% YoY; operating EBITDA negative INR 3 crore (margin -12%) after deliberate portfolio reset; OTTplay decision taken around 31 March 2026 per management.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal revenue or earnings guidance; said it is 'very hopeful' of sustaining good numbers.

Newsprint (25-40% of print bill of materials) at about USD 650-700 per tonne is the highest since COVID; management believes prices have peaked and will plateau before easing, but acknowledged no forward market exists.
Q2 newsprint expected slightly higher than Q1; Q1 Print margin of about 13% offered as a modelling baseline, with downside if dollar and newsprint rise further.
Preferential issue proceeds to retire 30-50% of the debt at HT Media and Digicontent; management says it is EPS-accretive and will improve interest coverage and credit rating.
Government ad and circulation rates were raised in November 2025 after seven years, so the price benefit continues for the next two quarters.
capex_capacity: Preferential issue at HT Media and Digicontent Ltd (DCL), priced on the SEBI formula (higher of 10-day or 90-day VWAP); promoters subscribing on the same terms, up to their regulatory maximum; ongoing vote, with a shareholder voting against.
Radio footprint reduced by surrendering licences for non-viable stations.
Cost right-sizing: consolidated employee cost fell to INR 99 crore from INR 111 crore YoY.
HMVL cash (where most of the INR 922 crore net cash sits) to be deployed at HMVL board's discretion; no preferential issue at HMVL.
demand_pricing: Commercial print revenue held on volume with yield improvement as the main driver; government revenue grew on both volume and the November 2025 rate increase.
Management stated that a substantial part of the 15% revenue growth came from pricing, not volume.
Cover price hikes seen as difficult: Hindi papers are already well priced and prior commodity-driven hikes were taken.
Circulation held steady market by market to protect copy share in English markets.
Other operating income at HMVL roughly doubled to about INR 20 crore (from about INR 10 crore), mainly job work and scrap sales.
Competitive environment described as likely to remain as is for circulation.

qa_highlights.question: Why use a preferential issue at about INR 24 per share, below book value of about INR 70, rather than a rights issue, given INR 922 crore net cash and a 15% dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all the net cash sits in HMVL, while HT Media and DCL are net debt companies. Preferential issue is faster (2-3 months), gives more certainty of raising the amount and avoids underwriter risk; pricing follows the SEBI formula with no premium. Proceeds will retire 30-50% of debt.

qa_highlights.question: Given the 15% dilution, the valuation and the moral/reputational issue, will the company withdraw the preferential issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not agree to withdraw. It said price-to-book is below 0.5x, the promoters are subscribing on the same terms, and it is raising capital to retire debt and improve EPS. A shareholder said he voted against the resolution.

qa_highlights.question: Is the debt position consistent with earlier statements that the company was debt-free?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt has built up at HT Media over the last 3-4 years post-COVID (Print English and Radio); the combined net cash figure hides this, and the number is not new.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of HMVL's other income jump, and is it MTM?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury gains from mutual funds (NAV-based) plus realised profit on sale of assets; no MTM on investments. Treasury gains depend on yield curve movements and are not predictable.

qa_highlights.question: How will newsprint costs affect Print margins, and can prices be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Newsprint is 25-40% of the bill of materials. Management expects a plateau at current levels, so Q1 Print margin of about 13% can be used as a baseline if prices don't rise further; cover price increases are difficult.

qa_highlights.question: What drove ad revenue growth at Print, and what share is government revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly commercial yield improvement with volumes holding; government revenue grew on volume and pricing. Management did not disclose the government share and called it 'substantial' but smaller than commercial.

risks_watch: Newsprint at about USD 650-700 per tonne, the highest since COVID, with no forward market; Q2 newsprint guided slightly higher than Q1, and a weaker dollar adds to cost pressure on the 13% Print margin.

Preferential issue at HT Media and Digicontent: ~15% dilution at roughly INR 24-25 per share versus book value of about INR 70; shareholder voting is ongoing and at least one minority holder has voted against, so approval and final pricing remain open.
Debt at HT Media and DCL: management said 30-50% of debt will be retired from the issue proceeds; the net cash of INR 922 crore sits in HMVL, and the consolidated figure masks standalone net debt.
Other income at HMVL (treasury gains and profit on asset sales) is not predictable and depends on yield curve movements, so the Q1 profit level may not repeat.

Digital operating revenue down about 28% with EBITDA of negative INR 3 crore after the portfolio reset; Radio EBITDA negative INR 3 crore. Track whether these turn profitable next quarter and whether the Q1 earnings step-up holds once government rate benefits cycle out after two quarters.
key_quotes: So, a substantial part of that revenue growth of 15% is driven by our pricing .
We believe that the prices have peaked and should plateau at this level before they start coming down.
Debt has been building in HT Media for the last 4-5 years post-COVID because of the Print English operations and Radio operations, etc.
Treasury gains is basically mutual funds and the NA V based process and not a MTM valuation-based process.

532663|2026-06.headline: Sasken Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to ₹339 Cr, with software services margin up 240 bps to 30.6% while Product Solutions margin fell to 5.9%.
532663|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 24% YoY and 1.6% QoQ to ₹339 Cr, led by Software Services at ₹219 Cr (+24.3% YoY). Product Solutions revenue was ₹120 Cr (+23.6% YoY, -3.9% QoQ) after a strong Q4, with memory availability and component pricing pressure. Gross margin was 21.9% (₹74 Cr), and EBIT margin was 6.3%, while PAT was ₹23 Cr (6.9% margin) and was hit by normalisation of Q4 other-income one-offs. Order booking was US$47 million TCV, including US$34 million of new deal wins, with five new logos added.

financial_highlights.change: -310 bps QoQ (Keshav Sureka cited 12.8% prior period)
Sequential decline from Q4 one-off other income and lower FX gains

segments.name: Software Services
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹219 Cr, up 24.3% YoY and 4.8% QoQ; gross margin expanded 240 bps to 30.6% on utilisation, cost discipline and scale. Management says the segment grew more than 20% YoY.

segments.name: Product Solutions (incl. Borqs)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹120 Cr, up 23.6% YoY but down 3.9% QoQ; gross margin fell to 5.9% from 9.0% in Q4 (per the 310 bps decline) due to memory cost pass-through, lower incremental margin and silicon productization mix. Management expects margins to stabilise over the full year.

guidance_outlook: No formal margin guidance; management said it will maintain margins while growing, using efficiency and value pricing.
Management targets US$4 million run-rate revenue for 93 active customers under its 60x4x3 strategy; timeline may stretch by one or two years beyond three.
Breakeven for Borqs at about US$12 million quarterly revenue, per CFO.
Expect large cash consumption in FY27 from working capital and fixed assets; management is working toward cash-flow positive, using internal accruals and external funds.
capex_capacity: Inaugurated Sasken Silicon Incubation Center in Hubballi to build semiconductor talent.
Opened a new centre of excellence in Hyderabad.
Global headcount 2,658 (about 2,400 engineers), attrition 9.8%, utilisation 85%.
Inventory build in Q1 to manage memory shortage contributed to negative cash flow; some silicon products ship through the year.
Silicon business is shifting toward productization; capacity expansion requires working capital.
demand_pricing: Order booking US$47 million TCV (US$34 million new), ACV about US$40 million (US$24 million new); the TCV is not total backlog, and management targets a 9–10 month revenue carry.
Five new logos; 93 active customers vs 79 a year ago; top-five customer share ~56% (vs ~52% previously).
Two hyperscaler engagements (different hyperscalers): a multi-year capability engagement and an OS sustenance engagement, plus an AI and automation deal covering agentic AI and LLM validation.
CSAT 4.5 out of 5 vs industry benchmark 3.75.
Revenue mix: North America 30%, EMEA ~25%, India 26%, APAC ~20%.
Automotive: Borqs instrument cluster module ready but Chinese-sourced modules remain price-competitive; no commercial order yet.
Memory pricing and component costs are being passed through to customers, but incremental margin is not recovered.
532663|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth, customer wins and Software Services margins, but cautious and non-committal on Product Solutions margins and cash flow. Management declined to give margin guidance, disclosed no project-level detail, and deferred on specific partnership and order-level questions.
key_quotes: We will make sure that we will maintain our margins while we maintain our growth momentum.
So, we do not want to give any guidance on the margins at this point in time, but as Rajiv mentioned, right, so we are constantly making sure that we are driving efficiencies in how we are doing.
So, it is a function of how the customer does the offtake of some of these products.

qa_highlights.question: What pipeline of accounts could cross the US$4 million run-rate threshold in FY27, given customer count rose from 79 to 93 and top-five concentration rose to about 56%?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Mody said the 60x4x3 target (US$4 million run-rate for 93 active customers within three years) is still the goal; the three-year timeline is metaphoric and may stretch one or two more years. Specific FY27 target accounts were not named, and sales bandwidth is being added.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Product Solutions gross margin drop from 12.8% to 5.9%: memory pricing or something else?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan said memory cost pass-through removes incremental margin even though costs are passed on, and the silicon business shifting toward productization changed mix. Some products ship through the year, so margins should be read on a full-year basis and are expected to stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Are the two hyperscaler engagements with the same hyperscaler or different ones?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Mody confirmed they are different hyperscalers.

qa_highlights.question: Headcount rose about 9% QoQ while cost rose only about 3%; how will sales and senior analog/RF leadership headcount evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Mody said at least five to six more sales heads will be added in the rest of the year, with some growth delivery-led. Priyaranjan said cost mix includes lateral and fresher hires and Q4 had non-recurring bonus catch-up; utilisation improved. Anup Savla said the teams are independent and senior niche analog/RF/mmWave skills are grown in-house.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 60x4x3 target of US$4 million run-rate be reached if extended by a couple of years, and at what growth drivers, with growth at the expense of margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Mody said the company may take one more year, not a commitment to a number, and cited silicon, specialised silicon, devices (China-plus-one and Make in India) and full-stack software services as the three vectors. On margins, he said Software Services margins went from about 2-3% to 11.5-12% EBIT over six quarters and the company will maintain margins while growing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue stay flat for years and then grow suddenly in software services?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan cited four changes: working closer to customers, empowering teams to own growth, investing in capability, and filling white spaces such as the Borqs and silicon acquisitions for end-to-end engagement.

qa_highlights.question: Why has operating cash flow been negative for two years despite profit growth, and will FY27 be cash-flow positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan said cash outflow reflects investment in working capital and fixed assets, not collection problems; a large cash consumption is expected this year, Q1 included inventory build for memory shortage. Funding will come from internal accruals and external funds, and the cash-flow positive timeline is work in progress.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Borqs break-even point still hold at the earlier US$60-70 million top line?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan said break-even is now about US$12 million of quarterly revenue, after which the business adds to the bottom line.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of GlobalFoundries and Intel IP certifications and the formal TSMC relationship?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Savla said all three are in progress with substantial progress, leading to more design activity, but no announcements can be made yet due to the non-public nature of the work.

qa_highlights.question: What are the RF and mmWave projects and when will revenue from these niche technologies show up?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Savla said projects span connectivity, automotive interfaces and power, and revenue mix already reflects such implementation, though project details were not disclosed. Hareesh Ramanna said the Borqs instrument-cluster module is ready but Chinese-sourced modules remain price-competitive, so no commercial order is yet in hand.

risks_watch: Product Solutions gross margin at 5.9% (down 310 bps QoQ) with memory cost pass-through leaving no incremental margin; watch whether margins stabilise over FY27 as management expects.
Negative operating cash flow for two years; management expects large cash consumption in FY27 and has not given a timeline to cash-flow positive. Watch working capital and any external funding.
The US$4 million run-rate per-customer target has slipped in timing by one to two years beyond the three-year goal; the 60x4x3 timeline and the 93-customer base remain unproven.
Top-five customer concentration rose to about 56% from about 52%, and the sales team is being expanded by only five to six heads.
Borqs automotive instrument-cluster module has no commercial order yet, facing price competition from Chinese-sourced modules; the TCV-to-revenue conversion (9-10 month carry) also needs tracking.

rows.why: Software Services gross margin rose 240 bps YoY to 30.6%, but Product Solutions gross margin fell to 5.9% from 12.8% and management gave no numeric margin guidance, only that it will maintain margins while growing.

rows.why: Utilisation at 85% is above the 80% threshold with no new capex guided, but management says capacity expansion in silicon needs working capital and cash is already negative, so a formal capex announcement is conditional.

rows.why: Product Solutions gross margin at 5.9% with no incremental margin recovery from memory pass-through, and top-five customer share rose to about 56% from about 52%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Borqs instrument-cluster module is ready but has no commercial order, and Chinese-sourced modules remain price-competitive; silicon productization is ongoing with products shipping through the year.

rows.label: TCV conversion into revenue (9-10 month carry)
rows.why: US$47M TCV booked (US$34M new) and US$40M ACV (US$24M new), with management targeting a 9-10 month revenue carry, which supports Software Services growth from this booking.

rows.label: Cash consumption in FY27 and cash-flow positive timeline
rows.why: Management expects large cash consumption in FY27 from working capital and fixed assets, with negative operating cash flow for two years and cash and investments at ₹356 Cr; the cash-flow positive timeline is work in progress with no date given.

rows.label: Borqs break-even at US$12M quarterly revenue
rows.why: CFO says the break-even point is now about US$12M quarterly revenue, after which Borqs adds to the bottom line; the current run-rate and timing are not disclosed.

532667|2026-03.headline: Suzlon delivered a record 830 MW in Q4 FY26 and 2,456 MW for the year, with FY26 revenue up 54% to INR16,679 crore.
532667|2026-03.overview: Suzlon reported record Q4 FY26 India deliveries of 830 MW and FY26 deliveries of 2,456 MW (up 58%). Consolidated Q4 revenue was INR5,468 crore with EBITDA of INR964 crore (up 39% YoY) and reported PAT of INR1,114 crore, while FY26 PAT of INR3,153 crore includes a INR742 crore deferred tax asset recognition. Management highlighted a shift toward EPC and development (DevCo) contracts, with EPC share of the order book rising to 28% from about 20% in Q2, and a 2.1 GW Andhra Pradesh development right extended by 24 months. Order book closed at 5.9 GW versus 5.0 GW at the start of the year, while commissioning reached 332 MW in Q4 and 744 MW for the year, with 971 MW erected but not yet commissioned.

financial_highlights.change: Record for any quarter in India; Q4 FY25 was 573 MW (about +45%)

financial_highlights.value: INR833 crore PBT; INR1,114 crore PAT
INR2,422 crore PBT; INR3,153 crore PAT
financial_highlights.change: PBT +67% YoY; PAT includes INR742 crore deferred tax asset recognition

segments.name: WTG (wind turbine generators)
segments.commentary: FY26 WTG revenue INR14,040 crore (+65% YoY) at 24.5% contribution margin. Management said WTG margins should not materially decline in FY27.

segments.name: Forging & Foundry (SE Forge)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR597 crore (+22% YoY) and EBITDA INR119 crore (+61% YoY), driven by domestic demand and exports.

segments.name: O&M services (OMS)
segments.commentary: Under management is 15.7+ GW in India with machine availability consistently above 95%. Management said the Q2 OMS EBITDA dip was a one-off that has been recouped by year-end.

guidance_outlook: Indian wind installations (industry view): about 8 GW in FY27 and about 10 GW in FY28, with 15 GW around FY30-31. Management said FY27 could be 8-9 GW.
EPC share of order book targeted to rise to 50% by FY28, from 28% now; management expects it to keep growing in FY27.
Management expects EPC order closures to be announced from June 2026 onward; no downward trend in order inflow for a couple of quarters.
Capex run rate of about INR600 crore (plus or minus INR50 crore) going forward, versus about INR550 crore in FY26.
Management did not give absolute FY27 delivery guidance; it pointed to the FY24-FY26 trend (700 MW, 1,550 MW, 2,456 MW) as the indicator.
Unrecognised deferred tax assets estimated at INR3,000-3,500 crore; only deferred tax charge (non-cash) expected in P&L for the next two years.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity of 4.5 GW is fully operational, with 3 AI-enabled smart blade factories being added.
Commissioned 744 MW in FY26 and 332 MW in Q4; 971 MW erected but not commissioned, of which about 350 MW is ready and waiting on customer-side scope.

Andhra Pradesh: PIA extended by 24 months (April 2026), giving 2.1 GW development rights; 775 MW has a PPA being converted to FDRE pending APERC tariff approval, and the remaining 1,325 MW is to be converted into EPC contracts from June over the next 6 months.
DevCo pipeline: 22-23 GW of identified sites, about 8 GW under active development; about 25 GW of land/sites overall, of which 8-10 GW is well advanced.
DevCo capital deployed is about INR300-350 crore against an earlier INR300 crore internal threshold; more working capital may be needed for connectivity and RE parks.
demand_pricing: Order book of 5.9 GW, of which 66% is C&I and PSU; opening FY26 book was 5.0 GW. Management said a Sunsure order was received after the quarter.
S144 order intake is close to 9 GW. New Blue Sky platform (S175 and S163 turbines) launched in Spain to re-enter European and export markets.
PSU demand: NTPC Green is moving from split BOP and WTG contracts to turnkey EPC, with mentions of a 215 MW AP contract and further 540 MW and 2,000 MW AP tranches.

Working capital build is mainly receivables from PSU contracts; management said this was priced into tenders and most is funded through non-fund-based limits. Cash position improved by INR400 crore-plus.
Foreign currency: some contracts carry pass-through clauses; steel is largely pass-through except some PSU contracts. Newer contracts will be priced at prevailing exchange rates.

qa_highlights.question: Will order inflow decline for a few quarters in FY27, given muted Q4 orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order book closed at 5.9 GW versus 5.0 GW opening. The shift to EPC contracts takes longer to close, but EPC closures are expected to be announced from June.

qa_highlights.question: Can Suzlon help clients manage risk if the wind DSM (deviation settlement) rules tighten?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CERC moved wind DSM bands from plus or minus 15% to plus or minus 10%. Suzlon is testing a scheduling and forecasting model at plus or minus 10% and plans to offer it as a paid service, including to existing clients.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any non-moving orders in the 5,892 MW backlog?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are currently no non-moving or slow-moving orders in the backlog.

qa_highlights.question: What drives FY27 deliveries, and is about 2,500 MW the most likely outcome?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, pointing to leading indicators and the FY24-26 trend (700 MW, 1,550 MW, 2,456 MW) instead.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a need for price hikes to protect margins given rupee depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said WTG margins should not materially decline, citing pass-through clauses and cost management. Management said pricing on new contracts would reflect current exchange rates.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope of the Andhra Pradesh FDRE project and the DevCo model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 775 MW will be converted to FDRE under a PPA, with clients possibly taking over the PPA and Suzlon supplying full FDRE. The remaining 1,325 MW will be converted into turnkey EPC contracts from June.

risks_watch: Execution: 971 MW erected but not commissioned, with about 350 MW waiting on customer-side readiness; commissioning pace and receivables recovery need tracking.
Working capital and receivables from PSU contracts; operating cash flow of about INR12 billion versus EBITDA of INR30 billion in FY26.
Possible DSM tightening (plus or minus 10%) and stay status, which may affect wind project economics.
EPC conversion timing: the 1,325 MW AP conversion and EPC contract announcements are expected from June; the 775 MW FDRE PPA depends on APERC tariff approval and client takeover.
Commodity and currency exposure on non-pass-through contracts; management gave no quantified margin guidance beyond WTG margins not materially declining.
532667|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on deliveries, commissioning and the EPC/DevCo transition, with management pointing to the FY26 commitments delivered. Evasive on specific FY27 delivery and order numbers, which they declined to give, and on monthly installation disclosure, which they said they would evaluate internally.
key_quotes: Suzlon delivered a record 830 megawatts in Q4 and 2,456 megawatts in FY '26, which are our ever-highest deliveries in India.
Our net cash balance at INR2,384 crores further enhances our financial flexibility and resilience.
WTG margins, I don't think materially can go down.
We will provide the right from land to the entire project commissioning on EPC on a turnkey basis.

rows.why: New Blue Sky platform (S175 and S163 turbines) launched in Spain to re-enter European and export markets, and a scheduling and forecasting paid service is being tested at plus or minus 10% DSM bands.

rows.why: EPC share is 28% now versus about 20% in Q2, management expects it to keep growing in FY27 and reach 50% in FY28, with EPC closures announced from June 2026.

rows.why: NTPC Green is moving to turnkey EPC with a 215 MW AP contract and further 540 MW and 2,000 MW AP tranches mentioned, and the 1,325 MW AP conversion to EPC starts from June.

532668|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue grew 20.2% to INR 1,411 crore, but Q4 missed plan on Middle East deal slippage and hyperscaler revenue timing; no FY27 growth number given.
532668|2026-03.overview: Management said FY26 was below its own standards: revenue rose 20.2% to INR 1,411 crore, with EBITDA margin at 20.02% and PAT margin at 15.02%, toward the lower end of guided ranges. The original plan was close to 30% growth, and Q4 fell short on Middle East license deal closures and project completions, a delayed hyperscaler data center project, and a one-time labour code charge. Management is stepping up expensed and capitalised investment in AI-native banking software, transit back-office software, payments and data centers, and expects higher working capital and balance-sheet pressure in FY27. It declined to give a numerical FY27 growth guide, saying only that it expects to grow ahead of industry rates.

532683|2026-03.headline: AIA Q4 FY26 revenue INR1,251 crore and PAT INR393 crore, a record quarter helped by INR65 crore FX gain; management guides realisation INR165/kg as sustainable.

Full-year FY26 volume was 258,000 tonnes (flat vs 255,000) with revenue INR4,355 crore, EBITDA INR1,744 crore and PAT INR1,270 crore. Management attributed part of the quarter to one-offs: INR65 crore FX gain, a product-mix tilt to castings, and a lower tax rate. The main narrative was a South American large-mine trial win for a lining plus new-generation discharge system solution, with a second mine conversion ordered, but no volume guidance was given.

qa_highlights.answer: Current 436,000 tonnes capacity can take utilisation to 70-75%; the paused GIDC Kerala brownfield can add 50,000-75,000 tonnes in 6-12 months, and Ghana land is finalised for 50,000 tonnes.

qa_highlights.answer: Stock is built against orders: a South American order from Oct-Nov 2025 and a billing-cycle change for another customer (billing moved to consumption) converted revenue into stock; not housekeeping.

532698|2026-03.headline: Nitin Spinners Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR859.8 crore (+7.4% QoQ) and EBITDA margin rose to 15.17%, with management guiding to a 16-20% normalised margin in FY27.
532698|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR859.8 crore, up 7.4% QoQ and 2.2% YoY, driven by better demand and yarn prices. EBITDA rose 16.9% QoQ to INR130.4 crore, with margin up 124 bps QoQ to 15.17%, and PAT reached INR57.4 crore. For full FY26, revenue fell 2.8% to INR3,213.9 crore and EBITDA fell 4% to INR452.8 crore, while PAT rose 1.2% to INR177.6 crore. Management said the capex programme (fabric and spinning expansion, renewable power) is on track for H2 FY27 commissioning.

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Yarn was 74% of FY26 revenue; spinning capacity ran at over 98% utilisation in Q4 FY26, with management guiding 97-98% going forward. Average yarn spread (realisation over cotton cost, around 33-34 count) is about INR120-125/kg, up from about INR110/kg last quarter.

segments.name: Fabric (woven and knitted)
segments.commentary: Fabric was 21% of FY26 revenue (woven about 18%, knitted about 4%, per the Q&A corrections). Woven capacity ran at over 90% utilisation in Q4; woven realisation rose about 2-2.5% QoQ and knitted about 5% QoQ. Knitted utilisation is below normal, with a 65-70% normal level expected to return in 1-1.5 years.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: Others contributed 5% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Exports were about 63% of Q4 FY26 revenue (61.9% for FY26); domestic was 37% in Q4 (31.8% for FY26).

guidance_outlook: Normalised EBITDA margin range of 16-20%, which management expects to reach in FY27.

Fabric capex adds 35 million metres, taking capacity to 75 million metres (errata to 70 million metres as stated), and spinning adds 22,000 tonnes to about 130,000 tonnes. Commissioning in H2 FY27: fabric from October-December 2026 and spinning from January-February 2027.

Capex of about INR1,000-1,100 crore is expected to add more than INR1,000 crore to top line. Normalisation of yarn prices may add 5-7% to existing turnover. Management expects 30-35% revenue growth on the existing base over time.

Renewable power: about 75 MW added including PPAs, reaching close to 100 MW installed. A 10 MW hybrid PPA is due by Q3 FY27. Expected savings of INR50 crore per year at full run-rate, with INR30-35 crore in the current year.
Total debt expected at INR1,900-2,000 crore after commissioning, including working capital. Average borrowing cost about 5.6%, working capital under 7%, blended about 6.5%.
Asset turn of about 1.2-1.3x at company level; new capex expected at about 1:1 excluding renewable capex.
capex_capacity: Fabric capacity expansion adds 35 million metres (to about 75 million metres, errata). Spinning adds 22,000 tonnes (to about 130,000 tonnes). Commissioning in H2 FY27.

Over INR300 crore spent so far, including about INR140 crore in capital advances, about INR55-60 crore capitalised from modernisation and balancing, and capital WIP of about INR100 crore. The balance is to be funded by internal accruals and debt.
Additional energy capex of about INR230-240 crore, not planned before last year. Renewable power capex is on schedule for H2 FY27.

Rajasthan Investment Promotion Scheme incentives include capital subsidy (about 20-27% of eligible investment, paid over 10 years), interest subsidy (5% of term loan or 2.5% of eligible fixed investment, whichever is lower, for 5 years), plus electricity duty and mandi tax rebates. Management did not quantify the total.
demand_pricing: Demand improved in Q4 FY26 in both domestic and export markets, driven by US tariff removal, downstream restocking and longer transit times. Management said exports of about 100 million kg of yarn a year are steady, with a possible 5-10% increase.

Yarn spread (realisation over cotton) rose to about INR120-125/kg from about INR110/kg last quarter. Management called INR120-125 the median and said it should be sustainable, with a minimum of INR100/kg against an earlier floor of INR90/kg.
Polyester prices rose more than 20% after the West Asia conflict, but synthetic yarn spreads stayed flat. Blended yarn margins improved marginally.

Cotton: domestic prices were INR52,000-55,000 per candy in the lowest period, around 4 years low, and have been rising since recent weeks. Duty on imported cotton was removed Aug-Dec 2025; the industry is asking for a repeat removal.
Fabric prices lag yarn: the company has already raised fabric prices, and management expects further improvement. The India-UK and India-EU FTAs are expected to add European and UK orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised yarn spread and margin, excluding inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the spread was about INR90/kg at the low end historically and about INR140-150/kg at the high end; a minimum of INR100/kg is now the floor, and INR120-125/kg is sustainable. Last year's margin at INR110 was about 11.5-12%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the freight and gas cost impacts from the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe sea freight is up 75-80% and other regions 15-20% versus February, but freight is normally passed on under FOB terms and has normalised since March. Gas-based yarn is a very small share, with under a day of disruption and gas costs up about 1.7x since February.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the duty removal on cotton and the top-line outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the duty removal is up to the government, with a possible permanent fix in 5-6 months. Top-line growth is expected from the INR1,000 crore+ capex, yarn normalisation (5-7%) and recovery, for 30-35% growth on the existing base.

qa_highlights.question: What are the fabric and knitted utilisation trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Knitted utilisation is expected to recover to the normal 65-70% within 1-1.5 years, as US tariffs were reduced from 50%. Some customers were lost to competing countries and are being regained.

risks_watch: Cotton import duty status and cotton availability. The industry wants duty removed; government has not committed to a timeline.
West Asia conflict: transit times up about 2 weeks, sea freight volatile, and polyester and gas costs rising. Management says these are passed on, but synthetic spreads have not widened.
Capex execution: commissioning slips from H2 FY27, and ramp-up of new fabric and yarn capacity. Management said it can increase the reach of fabric to European and UK buyers under the FTAs.
Knitted fabric utilisation is well below normal, at the 65-70% benchmark, and customers were lost in the US tariff period.
Future capex plans are not yet quantified. Management declined to give future capex or fabric margin targets.

532698|2026-06.headline: Nitin Spinners Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR875 crore (+10.3% YoY) and EBITDA margin rose to 17.78%, with PAT up 83.6% to INR75.3 crore.

Management attributed the margin gain mostly to yarn price realisation outpacing cotton cost, with smaller contributions from power cost savings and efficiency. segments.name: Spinning (yarn)
segments.commentary: Running at 98% utilisation. Yarn spread (yarn price less cotton) reported at about INR130/kg currently versus about INR110 in the prior quarter. segments.name: Woven fabric

532700|2026-03.headline: ENIL FY26 consolidated revenue rose 3.9% to INR565 crore; digital grew 84% to INR112.4 crore while Q4 non-FCT weakened on war-related event disruptions.

EBITDA excluding digital was INR76 crore (18% margin) and PAT excluding digital was INR22 crore, which includes a INR17.2 crore one-time gain from reversing deferred tax liability under the Finance Act 2026. Radio faced subdued demand and the Middle East conflict hurt international operations, while non-FCT grew strongly in the first nine months but was hit in Q4 by cancelled international artist concerts. Management reiterated that Gaana should reach breakeven in FY27 and recommended a dividend of INR2 per share.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 15% subscriber CAGR to continue for 2-3 years, prioritises profitable growth over subscriber count, and sees FY27 as the year to reach breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: Gaana Q4 and FY26 revenue split, and FCT/non-FCT split?
qa_highlights.answer: Digital revenue in Q4 was about INR21 crore (+42%) and INR81 crore for FY26 (+71%). Q4 FCT revenue was about INR74 crore and non-FCT about INR38 crore. Volume growth was described as flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Gaana revenue look flat over the last two quarters?

qa_highlights.question: Will the company disclose CAC-to-LTV?

qa_highlights.question: Why did top-line fall about INR15 crore in Q4 and how is radio doing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said radio volume share is about 25.6% and possibly up slightly; the Q4 drop came mainly from non-FCT events after international concerts were cancelled. First nine months of non-FCT grew double digits.

qa_highlights.question: How many paid music subscribers are there and how long to reach the 100 million pool?
qa_highlights.answer: Music paid subscribers are about 15 million per the EY-FICCI report; management said timing depends on behaviour change and could not give a date.

qa_highlights.question: Is cash deployment or inorganic growth planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will pursue profitable growth rather than burn cash, is evaluating inorganic opportunities, and has kept dividends rising.

532700|2026-06.headline: Domestic revenue fell 1.9% YoY to INR111 crore in Q1 FY27, while EBITDA rose 42% to INR8.8 crore on cost cuts and Digital grew 43.3%.
532700|2026-06.overview: Management attributed the soft quarter to the West Asia conflict, which caused event cancellations, curtailed artist travel and lower advertiser demand across media. Digital (Gaana) revenue rose 43.3% YoY to INR31.1 crore and its losses narrowed, with management targeting breakeven as soon as possible. Cost rationalisation drove the EBITDA and PAT improvement, with non-digital EBITDA up 7.4% and PAT up 85%. Management gave no numerical guidance and said the Events business is H2-weighted.

qa_highlights.question: Is the radio advertising weakness only due to West Asia, and will the company diversify beyond media?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the weakness is an industry-wide shift away from traditional advertising plus geopolitical impact. It said the three verticals are Radio, Digital and Events, and that the company will stay in media while experimenting with AI.

qa_highlights.question: What are Gaana's subscriber profitability and path to breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% of subscribers are at profitable margins. Management aims for breakeven as soon as possible, with the lower-value subscriber base being churned out.

qa_highlights.question: Would a buyback be considered with INR390 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a Board discussion and that the feedback would be taken.

qa_highlights.question: Has industry subscriber growth moderated, and how is pricing positioned?

532726|2026-09.headline: Gallantt Q2 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR111 crores (9.64% margin) from INR185 crores in Q1 on Gorakhpur shutdowns and power outage, with revenue flat at INR1,146 crores.

EBITDA margin compressed to 9.64% from 16.19% in Q1, and PAT fell to INR61 crores. Management attributes the hit to one-time factors and expects recovery from the Gorakhpur capacity ramp-up, power plant restart and higher steel prices in Q3. qa_highlights.question: What is the revised CRM capex, and what incentives and margins are expected?

532735|2026-03.headline: R Systems Q1 CY26 (Jan–Mar 2026) revenue rose 29.9% YoY to INR 574.8 crore; adjusted EBITDA margin 20.1%, helped by rupee depreciation.

Trailing-12-month ACV wins rose to $82.5 million from $76.5 million last quarter.

532755|2026-03.headline: Tech Mahindra Q4 FY26 revenue rose 2.4% cc YoY to USD 1,625M, with EBIT margin at 13.8% and FY27 targets of 15% EBIT reiterated.

532755|2026-06.headline: Tech Mahindra Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6.1% YoY to US$1.66bn with operating margin at 14.4%, and deal wins hit US$1.078bn.

EBIT margin rose 60 bps QoQ and 330 bps YoY to 14.4%, led by volume growth and Project Fortius savings, partly offset by Comviva seasonality and business mix. Management said Q1 was stronger than expected, helped by early delivery on a European automotive programme that it expects to reverse in Q2. qa_highlights.question: Is the DSO and free cash flow improvement sustainable?

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.20 crore 99acres revenue write-back sustainable, and how did it affect billings?

qa_highlights.question: Why did jobseeker services revenue grow so fast, and is there guidance for it?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for JobHai and its monetisation model?

qa_highlights.question: How should margins and 99acres growth be framed for FY27?

532777|2026-06.headline: Info Edge Q1 FY27: standalone billings up over 14% and recruitment billings up 17%, with underlying recruitment billings growth at about 15%.
532777|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue rose 12% YoY to Rs.824 crores and operating profit rose 33% to Rs.334 crores, with cash from operations up 25% to Rs.225 crores. Naukri recruitment billings grew 17%, which management says is about 15% after adjusting for renewal timing, with revenue up 13% and a 58% operating PBT margin. 99acres billings grew 17% and its operating PBT loss narrowed to about Rs.2 crores, near break-even. Shiksha billings fell 23% on AI-driven search traffic loss, and matchmaking grew billings 20% and was near break-even.

financial_highlights.metric: Cash balance at end of Q1

segments.name: Naukri recruitment
segments.commentary: Billings up over 17% (about 15% normalised), revenue up 13%, operating PBT margin 58%. Tech/IT/BPM billings +15%, GCCs +31%, other sectors +12%, recruitment consultants +1%.

segments.name: Naukri Jobseeker (Naukri 360)
segments.commentary: Billings up over 35%, PBT margin 63%. Paid subscribers rose from 1.3% to 2.6% of MAU over six quarters.

segments.name: NaukriGulf
segments.commentary: Grew 12%, below the roughly 20% pre-geopolitical trajectory; operating margin above 35%.

segments.name: 99acres
segments.commentary: Billings and revenue both up about 17%; operating PBT loss of about Rs.2 crores versus Rs.17 crores underlying loss in Q4 FY26. Web timeshare 49%, app 55%, iOS 69%.

segments.name: Shiksha
segments.commentary: Billings down 23% and revenue down 12% as reduced Google referral traffic hit client delivery; US and Canada study-abroad softer.

segments.name: Matchmaking (Jeevansathi, Aisle)
segments.commentary: Portfolio billings up 20%; Aisle +44%, Jeevansathi +14%; near break-even operating PBT; more than 45% profile share in Hindi-speaking markets.

segments.name: Job Hai
segments.commentary: Revenue roughly doubled on a small base; about Rs.15 crores revenue last year, burn near Rs.50 crores a year.

99acres aims to become cash-generative during FY27 and to grow revenue 18-20% a year with cost control; ultimate goal of 30% margin.

99acres: primary about 45-47% of revenue, secondary about equal, owners 7-10%; NCR is the largest market and has been affected by sales-team restructuring.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 13% revenue growth is from realisation versus customer count, and how much from AI products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about one-third of revenue growth came from renewals and volume, and about one-third from newer offerings such as AI-Rex and Talent Pulse. Premium CV views are growing over 25% from a small base.

qa_highlights.question: Is the normalised 15% recruitment billings growth adjusted for the favourable Q1 FY26 base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said normalisation nets out early and deferred renewals each quarter, which captures the prior-year base effect. GCC billings grew 31% reported, with about 2.5% of one-off timing shift from Q4 FY26 deferrals.

qa_highlights.question: Are clients paying separately for AI-Rex, and is there cannibalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: AI-Rex is charged per mandate and sold separately in many cases, by the same sales team plus specialists. Of 4,000 free trials, 400 converted; management says cannibalisation is possible, mainly among consultants who downgraded.

qa_highlights.question: Will 99acres reach 30% margin faster after the Housing acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes so: competitive intensity should fall as Aurum may cut marketing spend. Sales restructuring is mostly behind, and NCR may take one to two more months to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI-Rex renewal cycle and how is value measured?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it needs one renewal cycle to confirm success. Customers buy mandate bundles (10, 20 or 30 mandates), and internal dashboards track shortlisting, screening and delivery time.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 99acres billing reconciled against JobSpeak index trends?

NaukriGulf growth slowed to 12% due to Middle East disruption.

532777|2026-09.headline: Info Edge Q2 FY27: standalone billings up 13% YoY, revenue up 13% to Rs.842 crore, operating profit up 30% to Rs.347 crore; CEO Hitesh Oberoi steps down Dec 2.
532777|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone billings grew 13% and revenue 13% to Rs.842 crore, with operating profit up 30% to Rs.347 crore and operating PBT margin of 41% (up 541 bps). Management said renewal timing shifted billings between Q1 and Q2, so H1 (billings +14%, revenue +12%) is the better read, with underlying growth guided at about 14-15%. Co-promoter Hitesh Oberoi announced he will step down as MD and CEO at close of business on December 2, with Sanjeev Bikhchandani becoming Executive Vice Chairman, MD and Group CEO from December 3; Oberoi stays on the board subject to shareholder approval. Management said AI-first products now run at a Rs.240 crore annualised rate, and 99acres reached near-breakeven operating losses with positive cash generation.

segments.name: Recruitment (Naukri)

segments.name: Real Estate (99acres)
segments.commentary: Billings +21% YoY in Q2 (up from 17% in Q1), revenue +17%. Operating loss cut 93% from Rs.23 crore to under Rs.2 crore; operating cash flow Rs.22 crore vs Rs.2 crore a year ago. Marketing spend down about 13% YoY while enquiries grew 33%.

segments.name: Matchmaking (Jeevansathi, Aisle)
segments.commentary: Billings +23% in Q2 (Jeevansathi +18%, Aisle +40%). Segment near breakeven at operating PBT; Jeevansathi operating profit Rs.2 crore, Aisle operating loss Rs.3 crore. Segment cash generation Rs.3 crore vs cash loss Rs.2 crore a year ago.

segments.name: Education (Shiksha)

AI-driven search changes cut referral traffic; company is pivoting to domestic counselling with AI voice bots and widening Study Abroad destinations (UK, UAE, continental Europe).

segments.name: Investments
segments.commentary: Portfolio of about 135 companies across AI, deeptech and consumer tech, with about Rs.5,000 crore invested via balance sheet and AIFs.

guidance_outlook: Management views underlying business growth at about 14-15% and is setting sales team targets on that basis.

99acres expected to generate positive operating cash for FY27 and to see operating leverage progressively through the rest of FY27; aims for further traffic and revenue share gains in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q2 billings growth of 13% the new normal after Q1's 17.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said timing shifts are behind the swing; Q1 was about 14-15% underlying and business is growing about 14-15%. Revenue is recognised over 12 months, so renewal timing defers into later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI-Rex lift margins, and what is the steady-state margin?
qa_highlights.answer: AI products are high gross margin, but the GTM is penetration-first over about 24 months; management declined to give a steady-state margin and said margins should not fall.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI revenue run rate additive, and is pricing bundled?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs.240 crore is Q2 revenue x4; AI-first products contributed about Rs.60 crore in Q2 and are largely additive, with prior-year AI revenue mainly Talent Pulse and jobseeker services. Products are priced separately on rate cards but often sold as a negotiated bundle.

qa_highlights.question: Why did unique customers stay flat at 46,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said small low-ticket e-commerce buyers were pruned and offers repriced higher; e-commerce revenue is up even though buying customers fell.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Job Hai margin drag and breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Job Hai burn about Rs.45 crore a year, 2-3% of Naukri margin; breakeven at Rs.100-125 crore topline, possibly over a couple of years.

532783|2026-03.headline: LT Foods FY26 revenue rose 26% to INR11,023 crore, but reported EBITDA margin was 11.8% after U.S. tariff pass-through and brand spend.

rows.label: Working capital days down to 176 from 196
rows.why: Working capital days fell 20 days YoY to 176, but inventory of about 190-200 days (250 cited at March 31) and roughly 100 payable days leave cash flow exposed.

532783|2026-06.headline: LT Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 26% YoY to INR3,161 crore, with EBITDA up 20% to INR363 crore but margin down to 11.5% from 12.1%.
532783|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR3,161 crore (19% normalised), with gross profit up 19% to INR1,029 crore and PAT up 9% to INR183 crore. Core basmati and specialty rice revenue rose 34% to INR2,845 crore on 11% volume growth at a stable 13% EBITDA margin. Organic foods revenue fell to INR254 crore at a 4% EBITDA margin during restructuring to a direct-to-retailer CPG model. Management said results are in line with annual estimates and reiterated full-year guidance, with the organic recovery expected over 1.5 years.

financial_highlights.change: vs 12.1% in the prior-year period (stated as 11%)

segments.name: Core basmati and specialty rice
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,845 crore, up 34% YoY on 11% volume growth, with EBITDA margin stable at 13%. India revenue grew 23% YoY; market share 23.1% and household penetration 64.4 lakh households.

segments.name: International (incl. North America)
segments.commentary: Contributed 71% of consolidated revenue. North America grew 49% (29% normalised); Middle East and rest of world grew 44%. Europe/UK are in an investment phase with margin pressure from logistics costs.

segments.name: Organic foods and ingredients
segments.commentary: Revenue INR254 crore after a temporary decline during the shift from wholesale to direct retailer (CPG) sales. EBITDA margin 4%; management guides to 7-8% by year-end and double digits later.

segments.name: Ready-to-heat and ready-to-cook (RTH/RTC)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 13% YoY, with biryani kits up 42%. The US RTH facility is expected to become operational this quarter; breakeven is targeted at INR400 crore revenue within 2-3 years.

guidance_outlook: Management says Q1 results are in line with annual estimates and the company is on track across all financial parameters for the full year.
Organic EBITDA is expected to reach INR70-80 crore by year-end, with margin rising to 7-8% and returning to double digits; full recovery in growth and margin targeted for FY27-FY28.
Medium-term segment growth guidance: basmati 10-12%, RTH 15-20% (small base), organic 10-12%.
FY30 ambition is more than doubling India revenue with expanding margins; RTH revenue to double in about 3 years.
Basmati EBITDA margin historically 13-14%, with a plus or minus 1% variance possible if crop inflation occurs.
Middle East growth expected around 15% from a small base.
capex_capacity: Capacity doubled for ready-to-heat products; US RTH facility expected to become operational in Q1 FY27.
Organic capacity expanded in Europe, with a plant set up and a full sales organisation built there.
No capex planned yet for the newly opened Australia entity, which has received a very small equity infusion.
Rice inventory 346,000 tonnes at an average of INR56/kg and paddy inventory 164,000 tonnes at INR38/kg as of 26 June, described as sufficient for the next year's branded demand.
Quarterly volumes: India 109,000 tonnes; international 117,000 tonnes.
demand_pricing: US tariff on rice fell from about 50% to 10%, which management says reduced the margin distortion from tariffs; pricing volatility from tariffs is now normalising.
Rice revenue growth (32-34%) was above volume growth (11%), driven by commodity inflation pass-through and US duty.
Management said it is charging a premium in basmati and Sona Masoori in organic versus competitors.
Freight rates to the Middle East rose from $200 to $4,000 per container; the competitive landscape limited pass-through there.
Logistics cost was 4.7% of revenue in Q1 FY27 after one-offs (damage retention) in Q4 FY26 phased out.
Nielsen methodology change cited for the India market share decline from 23.7% in FY26 to 23.1%; management claims share gains in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of El Nino on the crop, and whether margins are at risk from inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 80-85% of basmati area relies on canal or groundwater irrigation and 14-15% on rain. About 20% of area faces issues; a clearer crop picture is expected by mid-to-end August. Costs would be passed on to consumers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did subsidiary gross and EBITDA margins fall YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed it to the shift from CIF to C&I shipment terms with a related US subsidiary and a drop in organic gross margin from 35% to 33%. Management said consolidated gross margin improved.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise from INR419 crore to INR486 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the increase reflects Golden Star, now 100% owned, being consolidated from this quarter. Previously it was not consolidated, so both revenue and expenses rose.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US growth net of discounts, with discounts still to come?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales are recorded net of promotions and discounts under accounting rules, so the reported growth is already net.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: The prior quarter included a one-off gain from revaluation of investments, which has not recurred; other income is now normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did organic margin fall and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the model moved from wholesalers to direct retail, with a new Europe plant and sales organisation. Margin is 4% now, targeted at 7-8% by year-end, and expected back in double digits in FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much more working capital can be released from supplier financing?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company is near optimum supplier financing, with perhaps 4-5 days of further room but not much more.

qa_highlights.question: Why is India's market share falling and will the top two players lose share to the third?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to a Nielsen methodology change. It claims share gains this quarter, with about 40%+ share on e-commerce platforms and a 20 lakh household increase last year.

risks_watch: El Nino and irrigation: crop size clarity expected by mid-to-end August; management says about 20% of basmati area faces issues and a lower crop would bring inflation, which it expects to pass on to consumers.

Organic recovery execution: margin is 4% now, targeted at INR70-80 crore EBITDA and 7-8% margin by year-end, with a return to double digits over about 1.5 years (FY27-FY28); organic gross margin fell from 35% to 33%.
US RTH facility start-up this quarter; RTH breakeven at INR400 crore revenue targeted in 2-3 years, and management acknowledged the US RTH ramp has weighed on segment margin.
Logistics and geopolitical costs: Middle East freight rose from $200 to $4,000 per container, and Europe/UK margins are under pressure; pass-through is uncertain in the Middle East.
Market share: India share fell from 23.7% in FY26 to 23.1%, which management attributes to a Nielsen methodology change; it claims share gains this quarter, which is not yet independently verified.
Working capital headroom: management sees only about 4-5 days of further supplier-financing room; US tariff refund eligibility is partly received but not yet booked.
key_quotes: So the previous rate, 10%, has continued for after that expiry as well.
So in terms of changing our route to market earlier, we were selling to the wholesaler. Now we are directly selling to the retailer, which we call CPG.
So it is the breakeven that will be coming at a revenue size of INR400 crores.
So there is no impact of demand and on the margin side also.

Cautious and less specific on organic margins, Europe/UK profitability, Middle East inroads and the El Nino crop outlook, where answers were qualified with "too early to project" and "by mid-August".
