vs 54 days at start of year

segments.name: Channel: E-commerce / D2C
segments.commentary: E-commerce is about 15% of top line, up roughly 2 percentage points vs last year; Jockey is stated to be number one in men's and women's innerwear across major platforms. Management reads consumer sentiment from EBO jockey.in, where Q4 showed a decent uplift versus the first three quarters.

segments.name: Category: Outerwear and athleisure
segments.commentary: Athleisure is reviving after distributor inventory correction; outerwear and value-added premium products are supporting premiumisation. Management did not give category-level growth numbers.

segments.name: Network
segments.commentary: About 116,600+ multi-brand outlets, 1,615 exclusive brand stores and 893 large-format stores. One large-format store was exited over commercial negotiations, reducing LFS count.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided to 19-21%, versus 22% in FY26; management said it is not expected to be as elevated as last year.
Marketing spend to rise from a little over 4% of sales in FY26 to close to 5% in FY27.
Management targets double-digit volume growth into FY27 and a better volume-value performance than FY26 (value-volume gap of about 4 points in Q4).
A further price increase is expected in Q1 FY27 to cover input cost inflation; management has not decided how much will be passed on to consumers.
Odisha subsidies expected at about INR40-50 crore in FY27; none realised in FY26. Management cautioned that the amount will vary, particularly wage subsidy tied to hiring.
New distribution management system rollout planned over the next year.
capex_capacity: Odisha and K.R. Pet plants are still on the learning curve at suboptimal efficiency; management sees margin upside once they mature.
New technology investments described as unprecedented for Page; these add to costs in FY27.
Inventory built up deliberately in Q4 as a hedge against raw material inflation and for the seasonally heavy Q1.
demand_pricing: Q4 demand improved across categories and channels; March was strong, with January and February also ahead of the first three quarters. Management attributed this to better tertiary sell-out and tighter primary-secondary alignment after distributor inventory correction.

Price increase: 2% weighted average taken from mid-January production, flowing into revenue only from mid-March under FIFO; management said the Q4 price contribution was minimal. Management said the January increase was for product enhancements, not inflation.
Premiumisation (mix shift toward higher-priced products) is the main driver of the roughly 4-point gap between volume and value growth, not price.
Competitive intensity is lower than 1-1.5 years ago in men's and women's, as several D2C brands exited or shrank offline distribution and cut discounting and marketing spend.
Input costs: fresh purchases are seeing elevated inflation, particularly cotton; management declined to quantify the current rate, calling the situation dynamic.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp volume acceleration to double digits, and what initiatives contributed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited better consumer demand in Q4 and recovery in athleisure after distributor inventory correction. Primary and secondary sales are now closely aligned, and March was strong. Management said upstocking was not encouraged and festive timing played little role.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 19-21% EBITDA margin range still hold after input cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management reiterated 19-21% for FY27, citing marketing at 5%, gross margin levels and salary costs as the basis. FY26 margin was higher because marketing was below 5% and gross margin held up.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 margin 22% and why should it moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 benefited from marketing below 5% of sales and sustained gross margin. Normal marketing at 5% plus input inflation will pressure EBITDA, though not to the 22% level.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 2% price increase cover raw material inflation, and will there be more price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: The January 2% increase was for product enhancements, not inflation. A Q1 FY27 price increase is planned to cover input costs, with the pass-through share still undecided. Management said it would absorb costs if volumes were at risk.

qa_highlights.question: Will price hikes hurt volume elasticity in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to price only to the extent volumes are unaffected and would rather absorb cost temporarily in margin than cut volume.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of market share in economic segment and the new product pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said product upgrades launched in Q3 and Q4 were well received. Groove 3 is being extended to about 500 EBOs, select MBOs and e-commerce, and the men's Bonded collection outdoor campaign launched around 20 May.

qa_highlights.question: Are digital-first brands taking share, and is distribution friction behind us?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said e-commerce has grown for 3-4 years and Jockey ranks number one on major platforms in core categories. Auto replenishment has settled in for about 2.5 years, and a new distribution management system is being rolled out over the next year.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation, particularly cotton and fresh purchases; management has not quantified current inflation.
Margin trajectory: FY27 guided at 19-21% vs 22% in FY26, with marketing rising to about 5% and technology costs.
Price elasticity of the planned Q1 FY27 price increase on double-digit volume growth.
Quarterly sales normalisation (Q1 at 25%, Q4 at 24% of annual sales versus older 28% and 20% patterns) makes Q4 growth harder to read as run-rate.
Odisha subsidy amounts are variable and depend on hiring; the INR40-50 crore estimate is not a recurring figure.
Higher inventory days (73 vs 64 at start of year) and a new distribution system rollout.

Management said most of the delayed billing and the May price increase (about 2.2% weighted average) should show up in Q2, and it reaffirmed double-digit annual volume growth and the 19–21% EBITDA margin range.

532832|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 presales hit record INR2,632 crores (+89% QoQ), but FY26 reported PAT was a loss of INR872 crores on revenue-recognition timing and merger accounting.
532832|2026-03.overview: Embassy Developments posted record Q4 FY26 presales of INR2,632 crores and FY26 presales of INR4,631 crores (+128% YoY), with 93% of the INR5,000 crore guidance achieved. FY26 collections were INR1,673 crores, slightly below FY25's INR1,852 crores, which management attributed to the lag from H2-weighted presales. Reported FY26 revenue fell to INR1,732 crores and PAT swung to a loss of INR872 crores, which management framed as structural (completion-based revenue recognition and reverse-merger fair value step-up). FY27 guidance is INR6,000 crores own presales (plus INR2,000 crores from DM projects), INR3,000 crores collections and about INR19,400 crores of new launch GDV. Two legal overhangs (CIRP petition and KIADB resumption order) were resolved, and the ASM framework exit took effect 6 May 2026.

532843|2026-03.headline: Fortis FY26 consolidated revenue rose 17.3% to INR9,128 crores and EBITDA margin expanded to 22.8%; FY27 guidance is 15%+ hospital revenue growth.
532843|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue reached INR9,128 crores (+17.3%), with hospital revenue up 19.1% to INR7,773 crores and consolidated operating EBITDA up 31.3% to INR2,085 crores (22.8% margin vs 20.4%). Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR2,365 crores (+17.8%) and PAT rose 44.2% to INR271 crores. Management flagged softer Q4 occupancy at several large hospitals, attributed to a drop in international patients and a government price cap on oncology drugs affecting CGHS/ECHS business in Punjab. Net debt rose to INR2,334 crores (1.09x net debt/EBITDA) on acquisitions and investments.

segments.name: Hospitals

segments.name: Diagnostics (Agilus)

Q4 gross revenue INR387 crores (+11.1%), EBITDA INR85 crores, margin 22%; Q4 tests ~10 million (+5%). Preventive health 13% of mix vs 11%; B2C:B2B 52:48 for FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 hospital revenue growth guided at 15%+ on an ongoing (organic) basis; acquisitions excluded and additive.
FY27 hospital EBITDA margin expected to improve by about 150 bps; long-term target of 25% by FY28 reaffirmed, with management seeing 1.5%-2% annual improvement.
Diagnostics FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 23%-24%; revenue growth targeted at double digits (currently ~8.5%), with ~70% volume and ~30% value mix.
Jaipur expected to grow ~15% in FY27 with 13%-14% EBITDA margin.
Brownfield bed additions of 500+ in FY27 and ~1,800 beds over the next 4 years; capex about INR900 crores annually (about 60% maintenance).
Dividend of INR1 per share (10% of face value), fourth consecutive year, subject to shareholder approval.
IHH reportedly plans to raise stake to 50% and infuse ~INR10,000 crores fresh equity; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR700 crores; ~250 beds added via brownfield (Manesar, Noida, Faridabad) and ~800 beds added in total including acquisitions.

Acquired People Tree Hospital (125 beds, Bengaluru, Jan 2026) with land for 300+ beds; Shrimann Super Specialty Jalandhar (228 beds, Jul 2025) with land for 450+ beds; 200-bed Greater Noida lease (Sep 2025); Adayu 36-bed mental health facility in Gurugram (Nov 2025).
FMRI new tower to be operationalised within about a week, opening ~100 beds in FY27 on a phased basis; FY27 brownfield additions of 400+ beds per earlier statement, with 500+ per later remark.
Shalimar Bagh expansion delayed pending approvals; ~300 beds moved from FY28 to FY29; Mohali, Shalimar Bagh and Amritsar large towers ~2.5-3 years away.
BG Road has ~100 beds of brownfield capacity uncommissioned until occupancy improves; Mulund considering another tower.

International patient revenue +18.5% to INR639 crores (7.8% of hospital revenue); Q4 international growth ~11%. Management is diversifying to Africa and other markets.
Oncology drug price capping (~30% of MRP) under CGHS/ECHS led Fortis to stop some high-cost drug cases, mainly in Punjab; no timeline for resolution. Management said margin impact is limited.
Focus specialties grew 18.9% and make up 62% of hospital revenue; radiation therapy volumes +19%, robotic surgeries +66%.
Diagnostics: 40.8 million tests in FY26 vs 39.2 million; 50+ new tests added; Illumina NovaSeq X operational at Mumbai reference lab.

qa_highlights.question: Why are occupancies falling at large hospitals such as FMRI and BG Road, and how will this improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal attributed the drop mainly to lower international business (Q4 growth ~11% vs 18-20% for the year) and oncology drug capping in Punjab. He said BG Road is low due to TPA/cash mix, intense competition and a 55% level versus a 63-64% area norm, with a target above 60%.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins expand given new capacity and doctor cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashutosh Raghuvanshi said doctor costs rose slightly but further increases are not expected; the 25% FY28 margin target is intact, with 1.5-2% annual improvement now seen as more confident.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue did the 800 new beds contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said Q4 hospital revenue of INR2,000 crores would be INR1,928 crores excluding People Tree, Adayu and Jalandhar, so new-unit contribution is small.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and EBITDA of Gleneagles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not consolidate Gleneagles and does not track full-year numbers; it is trending around INR70 per month.

qa_highlights.question: Is Diagnostics demerger being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said the focus is on profitability, this is not the time to lock value, and alternatives may be considered once the business matures.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Gleneagles transaction moving forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is under deliberation and evaluation; no timeline, and it would need majority-of-minority approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Manesar run-rate and FMRI ARPOB driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Manesar FY26 revenue was INR140 crores at ~48% occupancy (new beds being added) and reached EBITDA breakeven. FMRI ARPOB rise was attributed to gross-basis international business, MR Linac, Gamma Knife and day-care oncology.

532843|2026-06.headline: Fortis Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17.5% to INR 2,545 crore, but hospital EBITDA margin slipped to 21.5% from 22.1% on ESOP, ramp-up and legal costs.

Management said the margin dip reflects new ramp-up units, higher legal costs, higher doubtful-debt provisions and the new ESOP charge, and it maintained the FY28 target of about 25% margin, now framed as post-ESOP. Net debt rose to INR 2,233 crore (1.01x EBITDA) from INR 1,869 crore a year earlier.

532851|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell 12% YoY to INR612 crore as volume dropped about 13% on a delayed monsoon; gross margin rose to 31.6%.

Gross profit fell 4% to INR193.16 crore, but gross margin widened from 29% to 31.6%, which management linked to premium mix and inventory effects amid volatile raw material prices. EBITDA margin fell from 12.2% to 11.1% and PAT margin from 8.4% to 7.2%. Management said the season was deferred rather than lost and expects stronger execution over the remaining three quarters, but declined to give revised FY27 targets until after H1.

532853|2026-03.headline: Asahi Songwon Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 30.2% YoY to Rs 23 crore, with margin at 15.6% on price pass-through in Blue pigments.
532853|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs 144 crore, up 19.4% QoQ, with EBITDA of Rs 23 crore (15.6% margin vs 8.58% in Q3 and 11.53% in Q4 FY25) and PAT of Rs 10.82 crore. For FY26, revenue fell 4.78% to Rs 535.48 crore while PAT rose 5.48% to Rs 17.78 crore. Management attributed the margin recovery mainly to raw-material price pass-through and operational efficiencies in Blue pigments, with a small inventory gain, and said the API price decline of the prior three years has reversed. Gokul Jaykrishna handed day-to-day CEO duties to his son Arjun Jaykrishna, while remaining Managing Director.

segments.name: Blue pigment (standalone, ATC Dahej)
segments.commentary: Revenue and profitability improved QoQ on stronger realisation with modest volume growth. Gross margin rose to about 34% from about 29% QoQ; management cited price pass-through, operating efficiencies and a marginal inventory gain. Management said utilisation is about 80-85% and no capex is planned for capacity.

segments.name: AZO pigments (subsidiary ATC)
segments.commentary: Full-year EBITDA positive and cash break-even reached. FY26 revenue Rs 78 crore with PBT loss of Rs 2.42 crore; management expects PBT break-even in FY27. Capacity is 2,400 tpa, utilisation about 65% per management, with a planned Rs 10-15 crore brownfield expansion to about 1.5x once utilisation reaches 75-85%.

segments.name: API (subsidiary Atlas, Chattral plant)
segments.commentary: Full-year EBITDA positive. Volumes grew about 18% CAGR over three years, but realisations fell 40-45% since acquisition; Pregabalin prices are about 15% above the bottom. Pregabalin is 60-70% of API business. Chattral intermediates run at about 60-70% and finished APIs at about 30%. Q4 API revenue was reported as about Rs 30 crore with EBIT of about 10%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q1 FY27 EBITDA across all three segments to at least maintain Q4 FY26 margins, with an aim to improve.

Blue standalone: management said peak EBITDA of about Rs 50-55 crore is the goal for FY27 if prices hold, on about Rs 400 crore revenue at 13-14% margin (analyst's framing, accepted as a goal, not a formal guide).

Long-term margin targets: about 13% EBITDA for AZO and 15-16% for API; Mitesh Patel said Chattral and Atlas could reach Rs 250-280 crore turnover at peak with no capex, at 15-16% EBITDA margin within 2-3 years.
CEP certification for Pregabalin expected by end of FY27 (current financial year), seen as a driver of volume and export access.
Management aims for Rs 1,000 crore group revenue within the next few years, with priority on sustaining revenue first.
capex_capacity: AZO capacity 2,400 tpa; brownfield expansion of about Rs 10-15 crore (plant and machinery only) to lift capacity to about 1.5x, triggered at 75-85% utilisation, expected within 3-4 quarters and funded by internal accruals.
Blue: no capex planned for capacity; incremental gains expected from debottlenecking and efficiency projects.
Chattral: intermediates about 60-70% utilised; finished API utilisation about 30%, which management sees as the key lever for fixed-asset turnover.
Peak debt was Rs 220 crore after the completed four-year capex cycle; debt is falling faster than internal estimates.
demand_pricing: Blue pricing is set quarterly with MNC customers; Q4 benefit was partly locked in, so further benefit expected in Q1 and Q2. Mitesh Patel put the price increase at about 20%, and management said prices across pigments and crude rose meaningfully on raw-material tightness.
Management said China raised prices about 30-40% due to lower export incentives and VAT rebates, roughly doubled ocean freight and higher crude-linked raw material costs.

US tariffs hit AZO and Blue exports, including via India-made value-added products; US business has revived since tariffs eased but has not returned to normal. AZO export customers have restarted testing.
Management said Europe remains in a structural slowdown; India remains the main AZO growth market.
Management says the cyclical slowdown appears to be bottoming, and no new pigment capacity is expected in the industry.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA gain came from raw-material price pass-through, and does it reverse if raw material prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Jaykrishna said the strategy was to pass through as much raw-material inflation as possible via long-term supplier and customer relationships. He did not quantify the split and said revenue was under pressure while the bottom line held.

qa_highlights.question: Blue gross margin rose from about 29% to 34% QoQ. Is there inventory gain, and how do margins return to 35-38%?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun said margins reflect internal strategy, some inventory addition, and operating efficiencies. Gokul Jaykrishna later put the inventory gain as marginal, since the company held finished goods bought before the war.

qa_highlights.question: Did the Blue power and fuel cost fall to under 5% of sales in Q4 because of a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun said a one-time receipt of renewable-energy billing rebate, pending for two years, drove the drop. Management expects power and fuel as a percentage of sales to be lower than before but not at Q4 levels every quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is AZO FY26 revenue and PBT, and will it break even in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Nupur (company) said FY26 AZO revenue was Rs 78 crore and PBT was Rs (-2.42) crore. Management said it expects PBT break-even in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone Blue utilisation and possible FY27 EBITDA of Rs 50-55 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Gokul Jaykrishna corrected the analyst's 60% figure, saying Blue runs at about 80-85%. He called Rs 50-55 crore peak potential and the goal for FY27. Mitesh Patel put Blue price increases at about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Subsidiaries: peak revenue and EBITDA potential at Atlas and Chattral?
qa_highlights.answer: Mitesh Patel said the two facilities can reach Rs 250-280 crore turnover at peak with no capex and 15-16% EBITDA margin within 2-3 years. Arjun said API EBITDA depends on pricing, and management said the subsidiaries could reach about Rs 50 crore EBITDA at peak.

risks_watch: Q4 margin gains were partly one-off: a renewable-energy rebate lowered Blue power and fuel costs, and an inventory gain contributed. Q1 FY27 is the test.
Pricing is volatile: management says there is no stability in prices or the business environment; a reversal of raw-material inflation could compress margins.
API utilisation at Chattral finished products is about 30%, and the company has not yet hired senior business development or marketing leadership; a senior hire is expected in the next quarter.
FY26 consolidated revenue fell 4.78% and EBITDA 6.12%; FY26 net margin about 3.3%. AZO and API are still loss-making or marginal, so consolidation depends on Blue.

532867|2026-06.headline: V2 Retail Q1 FY27 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR997 crore, with PAT up 70% to INR41.9 crore and store count at 381.
532867|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR997 crore (+58% YoY), with reported EBITDA of INR139.5 crore (+60%, 14.0% margin) and PAT of INR41.9 crore (+70%). Pre-Ind AS EBITDA was about INR79 crore (~8% margin, +51%) and PAT INR50 crore (+64%). Gross margin eased to 28.6% from 29.5%, which management attributed to Adhik Maas reducing full-price sell-through to 90% from 92%. Store count reached 381 at June 30, 2026 (56 net adds), and management says it has since crossed 400 stores. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of at least 50% revenue growth, 8-10% SSSG, 170-200 new stores and 29-30% gross margin.

financial_highlights.change: vs 92% in prior-year Q1 per Q&A

segments.name: Store network
segments.commentary: 381 stores at June 30, 2026 covering ~40.7 lakh sq ft; 57 opened and 1 closed in Q1, net +56. Crossed 400 stores after quarter-end. Stores are mostly standalone, 10,000-12,000 sq ft, in 26 states.

segments.name: New vs mature stores
segments.commentary: New stores run ~34% lower sales per sq ft than mature stores (>2 years old at ~INR1,070-1,100/sq ft); new stores at ~INR730-740/sq ft. New-store SSSG is ~2.3 pts above old stores in Q1. Cohort SPSF cited at 886 vs 925 earlier.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance at least 50% for FY27, unchanged.
SSSG guidance 8-10% for the full year, retained despite Q1 at ~7.5%.
Gross margin guided at 29-30% (earlier 28-30% range), dependent on sell-through.
170-200 store openings planned for FY27; no change in plan despite capex inflation.
Targeting ~50% CAGR growth for the next 2-3 years, per CEO.
Price increase of 4-5% in garment MRPs from Q3 FY27 to offset raw material inflation.
EBITDA margin to be maintained despite the new-store expansion; new stores pay back in 2.5-3 years and break even from their first month.
Funding via internal accruals, release of ~INR150-200 crore from normalising creditor days, and bank limit increases; no QIP planned.
capex_capacity: New store capex has risen ~10% to INR1.22 crore from INR1.1 crore, due to input inflation.
Inventory held ~100 days (earlier 90-100 days target) and creditors ~45-50 days; safety stock raised due to geopolitical tension and to be reduced later.
Inventory for new stores is staged ~2 months ahead, with ~INR100-150 crore tied up per quarter of 50-55 openings.
MOU signed for the next 100 stores; ~15-20 store locations finalised each month based on regional data.
Store-level replenishment cut to 2-3 days of sales cover from 10-12 days, with store back-room space converted into selling area.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is inelastic; kids' wear is ~25% of sales. July-August trends described as in line with plan, but too early to judge given festive shift into Q3.
Adhik Maas (30 days in Q1) and fewer wedding dates weakened Tier 2/3 demand and cut full-price sales to 90%.
Price increase of 4-5% on garment cost from Q3; management says past increases reduced volume slightly but were offset by ASP.
Repeat customers within first year rose from ~40% to ~55% over three years, per management.
80% of stores face 3-4 other value fashion retailers in the same catchment.

qa_highlights.question: Will price increases be passed on, and what is the volume impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material inflation to hit from Q3 as H1 orders were placed earlier; a 4-5% rise in garment cost will be passed to consumers. Past price hikes reduced volume slightly but were offset by ASP.

qa_highlights.question: Will the store addition pace slow or need new equity?
qa_highlights.answer: 170-200 openings remain on track with no capex slowdown. Internal accruals, INR150-200 crore from normalising creditor days, and bank limit increases will fund it; no QIP planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin contract, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Adhik Maas cut full-price sales to 90% from 92%. Guidance remains 29-30% gross margin, dependent on season sell-through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new-store productivity gap closing?
qa_highlights.answer: New stores run ~34% below mature stores on SPSF; 10-12 stores are below INR600/sq ft, which management says is too early to judge. Management expects maturity in 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why are stores appearing in Tier 1 cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said V2 has long operated in Tier 1 (about 11 stores in Delhi NCR) and that Tier 1 is part of the target market.

qa_highlights.question: Customer experience: are NPS or other KPIs tracked?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not focus on Google reviews; an NPS link is sent after billing to ~40% of customers as a pilot, with store incentives linked to NPS. AI on CCTV flags long checkout queues.

risks_watch: Gross margin at 28.6% is below the 29-30% guided range; the recovery depends on full-price sell-through in the festive season (Q2-Q3).
New-store productivity is ~34% below mature stores, with 10-12 stores below INR600/sq ft; RK Retail acquisition will consolidate from Q2.
Working capital is inflated by vendor prepayments; cash release depends on creditor days normalising to 45-50 days.
Capex inflation (~10%) and rising rent escalation (12-15% every 3 years) could pressure store economics.
Geopolitical risk is driving higher safety stock and raw-material inflation; the timing of 4-5% price pass-through is a watch item.
Customer experience issues (store-level reviews and checkout queues) could weigh on repeat rates and SSSG.
532867|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth and store expansion; cautious and deflective on near-term demand, saying it is too early to call July-August trends ahead of the festive quarters. Management gave few numbers on the post-quarter trend and deferred several questions to the next call.
key_quotes: We delivered an amazing 58% year -on-year revenue growth in the first quarter while maintaining healthy returns.
So we need to have that inventory at least 2 months prior to the opening of the store.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin guided to 29-30% from 28.6% in Q1, helped by the 4-5% garment price increase from Q3, but dependent on sell-through and offset by new stores running ~34% below mature sales per sq ft and rising capex (~10%) and rent escalations.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 57 stores opened and 1 closed in Q1 (381 at June 30, 2026), crossed 400 after quarter-end, with 170-200 openings guided for FY27 and 15-20 sites finalised monthly; MOU signed for next 100 stores.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue guided to grow at least 50% in FY27 with 170-200 openings on top of 381 stores; Q1 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR997 crore and SSSG was ~7.5%, though management said past price hikes reduced volume slightly.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation metric was disclosed and no new plant or capex programme is discussed; growth is store-led and funded from internal accruals, creditor-day release of INR150-200 crore and bank limits, with no QIP planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held all FY27 guidance (at least 50% revenue growth, 8-10% SSSG, 29-30% gross margin) despite Q1 SSSG at ~7.5% and gross margin below range, and July-August trends were called too early to judge.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 SSSG was ~7.5% against an 8-10% full-year target, gross margin of 28.6% sits below the 29-30% guided range, and full-price sales fell to ~90% from 92%, with the recovery depending on festive sell-through.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or category launch was discussed; kids' wear is ~25% of sales but no new line was flagged.

rows.label: 4-5% garment MRP increase from Q3 FY27
rows.why: Raw material inflation hits from Q3 as H1 orders were placed earlier, and management plans to pass a 4-5% rise in garment cost to consumers, saying past hikes cut volume slightly but were offset by ASP.

rows.label: Creditor-day normalisation releases INR150-200 crore
rows.why: Creditor days are ~45-50 against a 45-50 target after vendor prepayments inflated working capital, and inventory of ~100 days is to be cut later; cash release depends on this normalising.

rows.label: RK Retail acquisition consolidates from Q2 FY27
rows.why: The brief says RK Retail acquisition will consolidate from Q2, which adds to revenue, but no size or contribution figure was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on store expansion, the 50% growth guide and funding without a QIP, but cautious and deflective on July-August demand, gross margin recovery and new-store productivity; analysts pushed on gross margin and the new-store productivity gap.

532868|2026-03.headline: DLF posted a record FY26 collection of over INR 13,500 crore (+15% YoY) and zero gross debt in development, with FY26 sales bookings of INR 20,143 crore in line with guidance.
532868|2026-03.overview: Management reported a strong close to FY26, citing record collections of over INR 13,500 crore (+15%) and cash surplus of over INR 7,700 crore (+25%). FY26 sales bookings were INR 20,143 crore, in line with guidance despite deferral of a couple of launches, with Q4 sales of about INR 3,967 crore led by Dahlias. Q4 consolidated revenue was about INR 2,452 crore with reported net profit of INR 1,256 crore; FY26 net profit was INR 4,256 crore (+16%). The rental business shows a 95% occupancy portfolio of 50 million sq ft and a 4-5 year NOI growth guidance of mid-teens, with 20-25% CAGR on a longer basis. Management steered the Q&A away from presales volume toward margins and cash flows.

financial_highlights.value: INR 14,155 crore, of which ~INR 11,200 crore in RERA escrow accounts

financial_highlights.metric: DCCDL FY26 revenue / EBITDA / PBT before exceptional
financial_highlights.value: ~INR 7,400 crore / over INR 5,700 crore / INR 2,726 crore

segments.name: Rental (annuity) business
segments.commentary: Rental portfolio of 50 million sq ft at 95% occupancy; FY26 NOI growth of about 34-35% driven by assets completed late FY25 reaching full lease. Non-SEZ office occupancy 98-99%, SEZ 88-89%, and income loss from vacancy down to ~3.5%.

segments.name: Development (DevCo)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales of INR 20,143 crore; Dahlias sales about INR 5,000 crore in FY26, guided to INR 5,000-6,000 crore in FY27. Management targets ~INR 9,000-10,000 crore of margin creation and INR 7,000-8,000 crore of DevCo FCF annually.

segments.name: Retail malls
segments.commentary: Existing mall income expected to grow 10-11% in FY27, plus three new malls. Midtown Plaza 95% leased and operational; Summit Plaza 95-97% leased, opening likely second half of July; Promenade Goa 50% leasing line of sight, completion around August.

segments.name: Office (Atrium Place, Downtown)
segments.commentary: Atrium Place (JV with Hines, 3.2 million sq ft) fully leased; three towers have OC and fourth tower OC expected Q2 FY27, generating ~INR 700 crore rent. Downtown Taramani 3.5 million sq ft ~500,000 sq ft leased, completion expected Q2 FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales guidance of ~INR 20,000 crore maintained; management said upside possible if demand stays strong.
Annual margin creation of ~INR 9,000 crore guided to continue.
Rental NOI guidance: mid-teens growth in NOI and 20-25% CAGR over the next 4-5 years, though management cautioned FY26's 34-35% growth should not be extrapolated.
FY27 exit rental of ~INR 8,200 crore across DCCDL and the rest of DLF assets combined.
Launch pipeline of almost INR 20,000 crore for FY27, including a large DLF City launch (INR 8,000-9,000 crore or higher), Arbour Senior Living, Westpark next phase, Dahlias, and possibly Goa.
Dividend: no formal guidance given; ~two-thirds of dividend is funded by Cyber City's dividend to DLF.
Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 (Towers 5-8) completion late FY28/early FY29; Taramani completion Q2 FY28.
capex_capacity: Atrium Place fourth tower OC expected Q2 FY27; Summit Plaza opening likely second half of July; Promenade Goa mall completion around August with opening 2-3 months later.
Downtown Taramani 3.5 million sq ft: completion expected Q2 FY28; central atrium design change made.

Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2: 7.5 million sq ft integrated development (2 million sq ft mall, 5.5 million sq ft offices); Tower 7 (2.2 million sq ft) nearly fully leased; Towers 5 and 6 being leased; finishing late FY28/early FY29; iconic tower construction to start in ~2.5 years.
Westpark Mumbai pipeline above 5 million sq ft; ~900,000 sq ft launched so far, next phase of ~800,000 sq ft in FY27, then 500,000-600,000 sq ft.
SEZ portfolio of 16-17 million sq ft; ~4 million sq ft converted to non-processing areas. Chennai operating portfolio above 10 million sq ft, rising to 14-15 million sq ft.
demand_pricing: Dahlias (super luxury, Gurugram): 32 apartments sold in Q4 plus 2 Camellias; per-unit prices now ~INR 90-110 crore for the first phase units vs ~INR 60-75 crore at launch. Dahlias per sq ft pricing is about INR 1 lakh on super area vs Camellias ~INR 1.2 lakh (INR 80-150 crore per unit).
Office SEZ rentals: gap to Cyber City rentals narrowed to 10-12% for new take-up; Cyber City vacancy lowest in SEZ portfolio; Hyderabad SEZ vacancy 17-20%.
Chennai Taramani top-floor leases at INR 145-150 per sq ft; average realisation expected INR 125-130 per sq ft.

Management flagged that large tenants are reviewing internal processes, which could defer leasing decisions, though no portfolio impact so far; cited AI and Iran-US war as factors but said there was no impact yet.
Management declined to chase presales volume, saying margins and cash flows are the priority; said presales of INR 50,000 crore a year are possible given land bank.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the medium-term launch pipeline shown as ~INR 60,000 crore versus INR 67,000 crore earlier, and is the company less confident about the market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the figure is a status update on a INR 1,14,000 crore 5-year launch pipeline announced ~2 years ago; launches are paced to market absorption and execution capacity, with further phases identified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 launch and presales plan given the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Aakash Ohri said the pipeline is ~INR 20,000 crore, including a DLF City launch of INR 8,000-9,000 crore or more, Arbour Senior Living, Westpark next phase, Dahlias, and possibly Goa (approvals in place but a PIL pending).

qa_highlights.question: Why is presales growth limited to ~INR 20,000 crore versus peers at INR 30,000-35,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Tyagi said presales is not the right metric and the company is chasing margins and cash flows; it could do INR 50,000 crore a year if chosen, with delivery capability the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the FY27 presales is expected from Dahlias and how much from the launch pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Dahlias sales were about INR 5,000 crore in FY26 and are expected at INR 5,000-6,000 crore in FY27; management expects INR 13,000-14,000 crore to come from the ~INR 20,000 crore launch pipeline, as not all launches will sell out at launch.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR 11,200 crore in RERA escrow accounts and the cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Badal Bagri said the RERA cash unlocks from FY27-28; uses are shareholder returns, DLF rental capex (committed), and opportunistic margin-accretive land deals. Revenue recognition is on completed-contract method, with large projects like Arbour delivering from FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the dividend sustainable and how is it funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Tyagi said about two-thirds of the dividend comes from Cyber City's dividend to DLF, and no dividend guidance is being offered, though the trajectory has been of continuing growth.

risks_watch: Rental NOI growth of 34-35% in FY26 was driven by one-time lease-up of assets completed late FY25; management cautioned against extrapolation.

Dahlias sell-out and per-sq ft price trajectory is a key driver of FY27 presales; management admitted Dahlias pricing has moved fast.
Rising brokerage and overhead costs in Q4 linked to collections and year-end provisioning; management said full-year overheads should stay around current levels.
Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 and Taramani completion timelines, plus Atrium Place fourth tower OC expected Q2 FY27.

532868|2026-06.headline: DLF Q1 FY27 net profit rose to INR 794 crore (from INR 766 crore) while pre-sales were muted at INR 657 crore amid Aureva launch deferment.
532868|2026-06.overview: DLF reported a resilient Q1 FY27 with collections of INR 2,406 crore, operating cash flow above INR 1,300 crore and net cash of INR 15,200 crore, of which close to INR 11,000 crore sits in RERA escrow accounts. Pre-sales were INR 657 crore, held back by the deferred Aureva senior living launch awaiting approvals and a deliberate pacing of Dahlias sales. Rental revenue was INR 1,605 crore with EBITDA of INR 476 crore, and occupancy stayed above 95% by space and 97% by value. DCCDL posted revenue up 10% YoY to INR 1,917 crore and PAT of INR 717 crore, up over 20%, though this included one-time tax entries. Management said FY28 would be the reporting inflection as large projects begin contributing under completed-contract accounting.

segments.name: Office rentals
segments.commentary: Vacancy is very low; newer assets Cyber Park, Atrium Place, Downtown Gurgaon and Downtown Chennai are nearly 100% leased. Rentals in the portfolio grew about 8.5%-9% from Q1 FY26.

segments.name: Retail malls
segments.commentary: Midtown Plaza is fully operational, about 85% open and 96%-97% leased; Summit Plaza had a soft launch and is about 90% leased; Goa mall has OC, is 64% leased as of 31 July, and is targeted to open late 2026 or early 2027. Retail spend grew about 13.5%-14%.

segments.name: Residential (Dahlias, Golf Links)
segments.commentary: Dahlias is about 65% sold with 34 units sold in the quarter; price realisation is above INR 1 lakh per sq ft, reaching INR 1.20-1.25 lakh on higher floors, with entry ticket above INR 100 crore.

segments.name: Data centres
segments.commentary: DLF will act only as real estate developer and builder for data centres, not own technology or operate them; Data Center 3 in Noida expected to add rental around March-April 2027.

guidance_outlook: FY28 expected to be the reporting inflection point as large projects starting with Arbour contribute to P&L under completed-contract accounting.
Management hopes to stick to broad FY27 sales guidance; Goa residential shortfall would be about 10% of the INR 20,000 crore guidance and is expected to be covered.
Group exit rentals for FY27 guided at INR 7,300-7,500 crore.
Midtown Plaza and Summit Plaza expected to reach steady-state rentals by Q4 FY27; Goa to stabilise around May-June 2027; Atrium Place Tower 1 OC expected in September 2026.
Q2 and Q3 expected to be good quarters for office leasing as global companies and GCCs return to decision-making.
capex_capacity: Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 and Downtown Chennai Phase 2 construction at full speed; Gurgaon leasing about 40%, Taramani pre-leasing about 17%-18%.
Downtown Chennai Towers 4 and 5 (3.5 million sq ft) to complete by beginning of 2028; Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 by end 2029.
Atrium Place Tower 1 OC expected September 2026; all three new malls (Midtown, Summit, Goa) now operational in FY27 per management.
Cyber City 2 (70-80 acres consolidated) still on drawing board; sizing and launch decision expected within next year.
Land spend of about INR 545 crore over the last two quarters, including an INR 80 crore EMD for an NCR auction not yet concluded.
Mumbai project with potential above 5 million sq ft; launch targeted within FY27 or calendar 2026.
demand_pricing: Office demand slowed by AI-related hiring uncertainty and the Iran-US conflict since February; management sees GCC and large multinational enquiries returning in the last 4-5 weeks.

Gurgaon rentals: Atrium Place about INR 175 per sq ft weighted average, Downtown 4 about INR 150-155, Phase 2 leasing averaging INR 200; Cyber City existing rentals INR 140-150 versus INR 210-220 for newer buildings.
Dahlias: 25%-30% of demand now from rest of India and NRIs; secondary sales in Privana at INR 2,500-4,000 per sq ft.
CAM costs rose about 2%-2.5% due to minimum wage revisions; no tenant pushback reported because CAM is audited annually and passed through.
Pre-sales pacing for Dahlias to be held until Experience Centre opens after Diwali; next Privana phase expected early 2027 as a high-rise scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Is the slowdown in Dahlias sustenance sales (34 units vs typical 12-15 units per quarter) deliberate?
qa_highlights.answer: Aakash Ohri said the pace was consciously managed around the Experience Centre opening after Diwali; Dahlias is about 65% sold and entry ticket is now above INR 100 crore, with some additional sales held back pending paperwork.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Goa residential launch slip without hurting the INR 20,000 crore sales guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Tyagi said Goa accounted for only a couple of thousand crore, about 10% of guidance, and that the gap should be covered comfortably; all Goa approvals are in hand but the PIL is being addressed before taking customer payments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the stabilised run-rate of group rental income and what ramp-up remains?
qa_highlights.answer: Sriram Khattar said Midtown and Summit Plaza reach steady state by Q4 FY27, Goa by May-June 2027, and Atrium Place Tower 1 adds a full tower after its September OC; exit FY27 group rentals guided at INR 7,300-7,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: When will Cyber City 2 and the next commercial pipeline start?
qa_highlights.answer: Sriram Khattar said Cyber City 2 (70-80 acres) sizing and launch remain undecided with a decision expected within the next year; construction in Hyderabad or Cyber City is planned for sometime next year.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about Dahlias sales velocity versus price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Aakash Ohri said about 3.5 years of sales were achieved in 15-16 months, with roughly 3 years remaining; Ashok Tyagi said there is no direct binary between velocity and price, and the next phase depends on physical and commercial progress, implying a 3-year cycle.

Management said the quarter's advances growth was driven partly by a low base in corporate loans, and quarter-on-quarter advances growth was only about 2.85%. Liquidity coverage ratio fell sharply from 235% to 156%, as the bank deployed liquidity into loans.

financial_highlights.value: ₹276 crore (per Q&A); ₹621 crore vs ₹353 crore in segment comments

segments.name: Retail (RAM)
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 23.92% to ₹1,05,523 crore. Segment profit was reported at ₹1,377 crore vs ₹633 crore a year earlier in an analyst's reading of segment data.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agriculture advances grew 21.14% to ₹64,274 crore. Gold loan book is ₹36,000 crore; gold loans under agriculture are MCLR-linked, retail gold loans are not.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 18.03% to ₹71,308 crore.

segments.name: Corporate credit
segments.commentary: Corporate credit rose 46.52% to ₹1,12,770 crore from ₹76,966 crore, on a low base. Growth is concentrated in renewable energy, data centres, HAM projects and CRE. RAM-to-corporate mix is 68:32 against a 65:35 guidance (±5%).

segments.name: Wholesale and unallocated
segments.commentary: An analyst cited wholesale segment at minus ₹139 crore (vs ₹284 crore) and unallocated at minus ₹75 crore (vs ₹322 crore). Management said provisioning had not risen and did not clearly explain the change.

segments.name: Insurance associates
segments.commentary: Bank holds about 26% in Generali Central Life and Generali Central Non-Life, with ₹627 crore invested in total. Management expects higher income from both this year after the establishment phase.

guidance_outlook: Deposit growth guidance of 11% to 12% and advances growth guidance of 14% to 16% for FY27, which management said it will align with in the current quarter.
Quarter-on-quarter advances growth of about 3% expected to continue.

Cost-to-income ratio to fall by 1.5% to 1.6% in the coming year, against a target below 56%.

Growth engines named as gold loans and SHG, with dedicated divisions reporting to an Executive Director; South India cited as a gold-loan opportunity.

Undisbursed advances about ₹5,000 crore.
ECLGS 5.0: 34,824 applications sanctioned for ₹4,646 crore; guarantees issued in 30,561 accounts for ₹4,353 crore; disbursed in 27,567 accounts for ₹3,693 crore.
Business per branch ₹185 crore; business per employee ₹24 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is capital raising planned, given the Board's approval of up to about ₹7,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CRAR of 18.28% and CET1 of 16.24% are sufficient for guidance, so no capital raise is planned currently.

qa_highlights.question: Why did LCR fall from 235% to 156% and NSFR from 147% to 128%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said excess liquidity carries a cost and has been deployed; CD ratio rose from 64% to 74%. It said LCR remains above the regulatory threshold.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments drive the 28.6% advances growth, and what protects underwriting?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate grew 46.52% from a low base. Management cited a 0.29% slippage ratio, or 0.19% excluding agriculture KCC slippage of ₹200 crore, and better post-disbursement monitoring.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for deposit repricing and FCNR mobilisation?

qa_highlights.question: Plans for credit cards and GIFT City?

532885|2026-09.headline: Central Bank of India Q2 FY27 net profit rose 21% YoY to Rs1,469 Crore, with NIM at 3.01% and gross NPA at 2.39%.
532885|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs1,469 Crore (up 21% YoY, 11% QoQ), with operating profit of Rs2,268 Crore and NII of Rs4,146 Crore (up 26.28% YoY). Global advances grew 29.83% to Rs3,81,032 Crore and domestic deposits grew 14.41%, with CASA at 44.65%, below the 48% plus or minus 1% guidance. Asset quality improved on net NPA (0.31%) and slippage (0.24%), but credit cost rose to 0.53% as provisions were built for standard assets and ahead of ECL. Cost-to-income at 58.95% missed the sub-56% guidance.

financial_highlights.change: +21% YoY; +11% QoQ (from Rs1,213 Crore YoY base)
vs 62.42% in Q2 FY26; guidance was below 56%
guidance was above 3%; down about 5bps QoQ per analyst
+9.23% YoY; below 48% plus or minus 1% guidance

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate book Rs1,18,666 Crore, up about 42-44% YoY from Rs83,000 Crore; focus on roads, infrastructure, data centres, renewables. Pipeline: Rs7,000 Crore undisbursed sanctions, Rs5,200 Crore under process, Rs11,000 Crore under consideration.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book Rs41,000 Crore at average yield above 8.5%; plan to open or customise 116 gold loan branches with TAT up to 30 minutes.

segments.commentary: GIFT City branch opened June 29, 2026, contributing overseas advances of Rs8,093 Crore. FCNR(B) raised USD 926.74 million across 731 accounts; overseas loans against it USD 794.60 million.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: Yield rose to 7.19% at September 30, 2026 and was reported higher at 7.25-7.40% since; AFS book Rs1,023 Crore (from Rs843 Crore). Treasury earned Rs56 Crore from IPO participation; management sees treasury outlook as challenged.

guidance_outlook: Management says ECL requires Rs5,000-5,500 Crore in total, with Rs1,525 Crore already provided; ECL applies from April 1, 2027. Whether to take a one-time hit or stagger it is undecided.
Credit cost guided at up to 0.75% for next year as well (0.53% this quarter).
ROA expected to stay above 1%, supported by rising repo rates on 61% external-benchmark-linked book; management declined to guide beyond next year.
NIM expected to rise in a rising-rate scenario; management says margin increase is likely.
Recoveries from written-off pool (Rs31,301 Crore) targeted at Rs2,500 Crore-plus this year; aviation account expected to yield Rs700 Crore via SARFAESI in the current or next quarter.
Cost-to-income: management says efficiency numbers will improve in coming quarters, but Q2 missed the sub-56% guidance.
Business growth guidance of 14-15%, deposit growth 10-12% and advances growth 14-16% were all exceeded in Q2.
capex_capacity: GIFT City branch opened June 29, 2026.
116 gold loan branches to be opened or customised with TAT up to 30 minutes.
300 marketing officers recruited; 32 places identified for MSME credit teams; CPAC revamped for higher ticket loans.
Credit card franchise to launch around June; cash management services with two modules live and more in coming months.
New banking emerging department (NBET) set up to lead digital user experience; 45 digital journeys launched and under revision.
demand_pricing: Management said yield on advances was 7.87% and cost of deposits 4.60%; the 125bp reference rate cut in the prior year hit the book.
Gold loans, SHG linkages (26 states NRLM tie-ups) and housing (over 50% of retail advances) named as growth engines; car loans via dealer and builder tie-ups.
Average ticket size is rising for housing and car loans, per management; a Rs22 Crore green home loan was cited.
Corporate growth focus on renewable energy, roads, data centres, real estate, hospitality, NBFC and agri-food processing.

qa_highlights.question: How much ECL provisioning is needed and is the bank prepared?
qa_highlights.answer: Total requirement Rs5,000-5,500 Crore, with Rs1,525 Crore already provided; management is confident profits can cover the gap before April 1, 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Will the one-time ECL hit go to net worth on April 1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the difference over Rs1,525 Crore is the remaining need; it has not decided between a one-time hit and staggering it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did provisions rise even as NPA and slippage improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited building a higher provision coverage ratio in good times and standard-asset provisions rising to Rs399 Crore from Rs37 Crore (prior year); credit cost 0.53%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ROA of about 1% sustainable into FY28 and FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROA should stay above 1% but declined to guide beyond next year given fast-changing conditions, citing El Nino and global factors.

qa_highlights.question: Why is yield on advances low versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the 125bp reference rate cut on the 61% external-benchmark book; repo pass-through lags and yields should rise as rates increase; gold loans yield above 8.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Any stress in rural collections from El Nino or drought?
qa_highlights.answer: Management saw no distress signals this quarter, except some agri slippage in Pune; it will assess the drought impact with future data.

El Nino and possible drought effects on rural and agri asset quality.

532891|2026-03.headline: Puravankara Q4 FY26 presales rose 190% YoY to INR3,547 crore; FY27 presales guidance set at INR11,200 crore and debt reduction target of INR750 crore.
532891|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was a strong quarter on sales and handovers, with presales of INR3,547 crore (up 190% YoY and 151% QoQ) and total income of INR1,541 crore (up 173% YoY) driven by 1,301 handovers. FY26 presales hit a record INR7,407 crore (up 55%) and collections a record INR4,258 crore (up 15%). Net debt was INR2,321 crore at March 31, 2026, down INR160 crore in the quarter, and cost of debt fell to 11.05%. Management guided FY27 presales of INR11,200 crore and a gross debt reduction of about INR750 crore, excluding new borrowing for business development. Collections, interest cost and FY27 delivery guidance drew the most pointed questions and several were deferred to offline follow-up.

segments.name: Residential sales
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales volume was 3.01 million sq ft (vs 1.42 million sq ft in Q4 FY25) at average realisation of INR11,787 per sq ft (up 37% YoY). FY26 volume was 7.25 million sq ft at INR10,213 per sq ft (up 21%).

segments.name: Handovers
segments.commentary: Handed over 1,301 homes (1.67 million sq ft) in Q4 FY26 and 3,747 homes (4.25 million sq ft) in FY26.

segments.name: Launches
segments.commentary: Launched three new projects (Purva SilverSky, Purva Northern Lights, Purva Estrella) and seven new phases in FY26, totalling 6.39 million sq ft. Northern Lights realisation is about INR10,700 per sq ft and it contributed INR1,100-1,200 crore to Q4 presales. Lokhandwala contributed slightly over INR800 crore in Q4.

segments.name: Commercial assets
segments.commentary: Aerocity has received OC and leasing has started; Zentech OC is expected within the month and is about 40-45% leased or sold. FY26 commercial sales and leasing was about 2.6 lakh sq ft.

segments.name: Starworth
segments.commentary: Not a reporting segment; order book is above INR2,000 crore and FY25 financials are on the website, with FY26 to follow.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales target of about INR11,200 crore, of which about 48% from sustained sales and 52% from new launches; about INR7,000 crore expected from the South and the rest from West and Commercial.
Gross debt reduction target of about INR750 crore for FY27, excluding incremental borrowing for business development; scheduled repayment is INR836 crore this year.

Collections expected to grow in double digits in FY27; management suggested 45-50% of the INR7,400 crore sales from the big launches could be collected in the first year (exact figure to be shared offline).
Estimated surplus cash flow of INR19,290 crore: INR8,816 crore from ongoing projects, INR2,131 crore from exiting commercial assets, and INR8,343 crore from the launch pipeline.
Launch pipeline of 14.85 million sq ft with GDV of INR22,547 crore; Bandra launch expected between Dussehra and Diwali after members vacate by end-June.
capex_capacity: Land bank of about 56.48 million sq ft, of which about 21 million sq ft is earmarked for the launch guidance, leaving about 35 million sq ft.

FY26 business development added over 12 million sq ft and about INR15,200 crore GDV across six projects, including Chembur (INR2,100 crore GDV), Malabar Hills (INR2,700 crore), Hennur Road JD (INR1,300 crore), Baglagere JD (INR1,000 crore), Attibele 53.5 acres (INR4,800 crore) and Northern Bengaluru JD (INR3,300 crore).
Malabar Hills: development agreement complete, registration in about 45 days, approvals expected in 9-12 months, pricing INR115,000-120,000 per sq ft on carpet area.
Two under-construction assets delivered, totalling about 2 million sq ft; FY27 residential delivery guidance to be shared offline.
Commercial: planning new verticals including data centres, warehousing and retail (about 3 lakh sq ft retail in Thane), with NCR (Delhi, Noida, Gurugram) as the expansion focus; no timelines given.
demand_pricing: Management says the Bengaluru market is steady rather than frenzied, with about 30% of the last launch sold; AI and GCC demand is seen as supportive.
NRI demand held up after the strong launch quarter; management says rupee depreciation may attract outside money but is watching global uncertainty.
Construction costs are rising about 6-7% due to diesel prices; management says margins and contingencies absorb this for now.
Project margins: new launches target above 20% gross margin (Northern Lights about 20-21%, Purva Estrella slightly above 20%); plotted development 30-40% gross margin.
Housing sales in top 8 cities were about 84,800 units, with homes above INR10 million at about 53% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Launch timing and confidence in the launch pipeline, including Bandra?
qa_highlights.answer: Bandra launch targeted between Dussehra and Diwali, with a GDV of about INR2,700 crore for the saleable portion. Management says most of the pipeline (INR22,547 crore) should launch despite past delays from Bengaluru approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Collection outlook for FY27 given weak YoY growth and flat Western collections?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said collections will grow in double digits, with about 45-50% of the FY26 sales expected to be collected in the first year; the exact figure will be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest expense rise to about INR600-650 crore, and how does the NCD accounting work?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the increase reflects debt raised for business development, and that fair-value accounting for some instruments adds to P&L cost. Cost on that instrument is above 11.05%. Detailed working to follow offline.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR750 crore debt reduction apply to gross or net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it refers to gross debt, with scheduled repayment of INR836 crore this year; excess collections and project-level sweeps may add to that.

qa_highlights.question: Commercial leasing traction at Zentech and Aerocity?
qa_highlights.answer: Zentech is about 40-45% leased or sold before OC; Aerocity has many GCC RFPs of over 2 million sq ft and large deals are expected in the next couple of quarters.

risks_watch: Collections: FY26 collections grew only 15% against 55% presales growth, and the company has not given a collection number for FY27.
Interest cost of about INR600-650 crore on roughly INR3,900-4,000 crore gross debt; management is to provide reconciliation offline.
Launch execution risk in Bengaluru amid approval changes (e-Khata, Greater Bengaluru Authority) and the Bandra vacation timeline.
Cost inflation of 6-7% from diesel prices and geopolitical impact on the RBI's FY27 growth outlook (6.9%).
Delivery guidance for FY27 residential and the timing of Zentech OC and Aerocity leasing remain unquantified.

key_quotes: FY26 has been a landmark year for the company.
We are targeting a presales value of approximately INR 11,200 crores for FY26-27

On the balance sheet front, we are targeting a debt reduction of approximately INR 750 crores for FY26-27, excluding any incremental borrowing undertaken for strategic business development opportunities.

532891|2026-06.headline: Puravankara Q1 FY27 presales rose 28% YoY to INR1,439 crores and PAT turned positive at INR25 crores; FY27 presales guidance of INR11,200 crores reiterated.

Collections rose 40% to INR1,199 crores and 745 homes (0.94 million sq ft) were handed over. Total income rose 63% YoY to INR877 crores, EBITDA margin expanded to 25% from 15%, and PAT was INR25 crores versus a loss of INR69 crores a year earlier. Management kept FY27 presales guidance and the INR700 crores debt-reduction target, while adding four Bengaluru land opportunities (GDV ~INR5,200 crores) and signing a sale of Purva Zentech to ICICI Prudential AMC at ~INR625 crores EV.

qa_highlights.answer: About INR250 crores of debt on that asset will be repaid from proceeds; the rest will be evaluated for debt reduction, business development or working capital, with closing expected this month.

qa_highlights.answer: Westend has RERA and is launched with good EOIs; Hennur Road delayed by Karnataka government change, clarity expected this week; Cityspire and Winworth only await RERA, expected this quarter.

qa_highlights.answer: Both held; launches slipping from Q1 moved to Q2 for one or two projects, and management said opportunity spend versus debt reduction will be reviewed from time to time.

qa_highlights.question: What margin is targeted over the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA margin guidance of 25-30% at portfolio level held, with product mix (plotted, JDA, outright, redevelopment) causing project-level variation.

qa_highlights.question: How much did Purva Estrella contribute to Q1 sales and how does it compare with the top projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Estrella contributed about INR200 crores in Q1 and about INR800 crores since launch; management could not confirm a separate top-three ranking, citing South's Northern Light and Provident Equinox and West's Estrella.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no zero-debt target; free cash flow will be split between new opportunities and debt, and debt is an important part of the business as the portfolio (about INR58,500 crores) grows.

532892|2026-03.headline: MOFSL FY26 operating PAT rose 16% YoY to ₹2,360 crores; Q4 operating PAT up 25% with a ₹661 crore exit run rate.
532892|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 operating PAT of ₹2,360 crores (+16% YoY), with Q4 operating PAT up 25% and the strongest of the four quarters. Asset and Private Wealth businesses grew profit 33% and now contribute about 50% of operating PAT, with Asset Management at 33% of group operating PAT versus 26% in FY25. Reported PAT including OCI was hit by notional MTM losses of about ₹1,000 crores on a ~₹9,000 crore investment book, which management said were largely recouped in April 2026. Long-term credit rating was upgraded to AA+ (stable). Q&A focused on SIP and MF flow share, yield compression from product mix, MTF and broking trajectory, digital broker competition, and treasury MTM.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SIP market share dip in the quarter and what is being done to regain it?
qa_highlights.answer: SIP run rate is ₹1,400+ crores per month; passive decline due to international funds closed to new money and a locked microcap fund, with a small active drop. SIP books are at last-year levels and should climb as performance recovers.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving revenue yield compression and the lending growth in Private Wealth?
qa_highlights.answer: TER changes had no fee impact. Compression is mix-driven, as passives (lower retention) grew fastest. Private Wealth lending is a strategy to offer solutions to UHNIs and family offices, combining loans against securities and investment assets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MTF book guidance for FY27 and the QoQ decline?
qa_highlights.answer: The decline (₹6,500 crores at 9M to ₹5,700 crores at Mar'26) is market-driven and industry-wide. Management is confident of strong growth, citing ~7% cash and MTF share and a strong balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹1,000 crore treasury loss unrealised and has it been recouped?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, it is a notional MTM loss under Ind AS, with most recouped in April 2026. The investment book's 10-year-plus IRR is ~18%, and including buybacks and dividends it has compounded at ~40% p.a.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company positioned against digital brokers and fintech SIP platforms?
qa_highlights.answer: Wealth model is research and advisory led across franchisee, direct and branch channels; cash market revenue share held. Wealth distribution AUM grew 40% to ~₹44,000 crores. Working on high-value trader positioning.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Private Wealth client quality and AUM per RM trend?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM per RM rose from ~₹300 crores a couple of years ago to ₹450 crores at Mar'26 despite a larger RM base. Among ~9,000 families, almost 50% have UHNI potential. Segments are HNI (₹50-100 crores), UHNI (₹100 crores+) and family offices.

qa_highlights.question: Why did HFC credit cost rise from 10 bps to about 1% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 typically sees higher 1+, 30+ and 90+ DPD numbers. FY26 credit cost was 0.5%, and management expects correction over the full year; GNPA is 1.1% vs 1.4% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Will the treasury book be affected by July volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said long-term compounded growth of about 40% since March 2014 is intact, though monthly or weekly figures can be volatile.

qa_highlights.question: Will alternates net flows recover and will carry income be booked?
qa_highlights.answer: Alternates saw negative net flows in Q1 due to market allocation shifts despite high gross inflows; July is tracking net positive. Listed equity carry was negligible; unlisted carry was ₹66 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will AMC and PWM PAT growth of 45% combined split out?
qa_highlights.answer: PWM PAT was up 2% due to lower TBR, so growth came from AMC, helped by the higher AUM base and accrued unlisted carry that started from Q3FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee expenses rise 16% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly annual appraisal and increments effective 1 April 2026; AMC had a one-time ESOP reversal in Q4FY26, so Q1 is a normalised base for the group going forward.

risks_watch: TBR revenue volatility in Private Wealth and Wealth Management, given high Q1FY26 base and unlisted-linked mix.
Capital markets revenue lumpiness dependent on market windows amid West Asia volatility.
Alternates net flows turned negative in Q1 as allocation shifted to competing credit and real-asset products; watch July-September net flow trend.
Impact of the 1 July 2026 prop trading regulatory change on broking and intraday funding, which management called minor but early to assess.
HFC credit cost trajectory during FY27 versus the FY26 level of 0.5%.
Mutual fund SIP market share has been range-bound; watch the 3-year vintage transition of key schemes from December 2026.
532892|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on structural growth in AMC, alternates and annuity revenues, but cautious on capital markets and treasury timing, which management repeatedly called volatile and dependent on market windows. Management was candid that TBR and alternates flows were soft in the quarter and attributed them to the high base and market conditions.
key_quotes: We have transitioned from a transaction-led to an annuity-led business model, further strengthening the quality and sustainability of our earnings
Hence, FY27 as a whole, we'll witness growth. However, on a QoQ basis, it really depends on market.
The Asset Management business contributes to 40% of the group's operating PAT in Q1FY27 versus 26% in Q1FY26 and is expected to increase based on all the pointers highlighted above.
The entire Net Interest Income is ARR. There is no transactional in it.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides group PBT margin sustained at 50-52%, with ~70% of Wealth Management costs variable and cost of borrowing expected to fall 15-20 bps over 12-18 months after the CRISIL AA+ upgrade, while ~₹66 crore per quarter of unlisted carry accrues for the next three quarters.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity is discussed; housing finance can grow without fresh capital for 2-3 years, and the only launches are a commercial real estate alternates fund in H2 FY27 and fund vintage maturity, which are not capacity additions.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Current AUM of nearly ₹1.9 lakh crore is over 15% above the FY26 average of ₹1.57 lakh crore, SIP run-rate is about ₹16,000 crore annualised, and net flows were ₹10,325 crore in Q1, though alternates flows were negative in the quarter.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed and utilisation was not disclosed; the asset-light model and adequate housing finance capital mean no announcement is implied.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects FY27 capital markets revenue to grow overall with reasonable YoY growth, and the July alternates flow is tracking net positive, but there is no quantified revenue target and QoQ outcomes depend on market windows.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Capital markets execution is lumpy across 2-3 windows and TBR is volatile against a high Q1FY26 base, with HFC credit cost at about 1% in Q1 versus 0.5% for FY26.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans 4-5 new active fund offers over the next 12 months, a commercial real estate alternates fund launch in H2 FY27, and a private credit fund final close of ₹3,000 crore targeted in Q2 (about ₹2,500 crore raised so far).

rows.label: Lower cost of borrowing after AA+ upgrade
rows.why: Management expects cost of borrowing to fall 15-20 bps after the CRISIL AA+ upgrade, with capital market spreads narrowing from 75 bps to 30-35 bps vs AAA peers.

rows.label: Unlisted alternates carry accrual
rows.why: About ₹66 crore per quarter of variable additional return accrued in Q1 and is expected to recur at a similar level for the next three quarters, with only about 70% of fair value recognised.

rows.label: Three MF schemes crossing 3-year vintage
rows.why: Three schemes (small cap, large cap, multi-cap) cross 3-year vintage in that window, 2 more by March 2027 and 8 more by March 2028, a tailwind for performance-linked flows.

tone.note: Management was confident on AMC, alternates and annuity growth and on the 50-52% margin, but cautious that capital markets and treasury timing are volatile, and admitted TBR and alternates flows were soft; the brief's Q&A focused on TBR decline, HFC credit cost and treasury volatility.

532893|2026-03.headline: VTM Ltd FY26 PAT fell about 75% to Rs 11 crore on US tariff discounts (~Rs 20 crore), with FY27 turnover guided up 12-14% and EBITDA margin targeted at 10-11%.
532893|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue growth of about 8% (base ~Rs 372 crore) but PAT of about Rs 11 crore, down roughly 75% YoY. The drop was attributed to an ~18% US tariff-related discount (~Rs 20 crore), chargeback discounts (~Rs 8 crore), a Rs 2.3 crore forex MTM loss on PCFC borrowings, a gratuity provision under the new Labour Code, and ~15% higher raw material costs. FY26 EBITDA margin was 7.43%, and management said the 18% discount to the US customer Quince is still in place, with negotiations ongoing and the current price point at about 10%. Management guided to 12-14% FY27 top-line growth, a 10-11% EBITDA margin, and a 6.5 million-unit order backlog as of 31 May.

financial_highlights.value: ~Rs 372 crore (Rs 420 crore implied at 12-14% growth for FY27)

financial_highlights.metric: PBT normalised for tariff, chargebacks, MTM

~Rs 150 crore (vs Rs 92 crore previously); inventory turnover 122 days

segments.commentary: Roughly 52% of FY26 revenue (~Rs 190-192 crore); about 50% of that is commodity items, with the rest value-added and top-of-bed. Exports are FOB, and the tariff discount is concentrated here. Export sales to non-US countries were about Rs 16-17 crore (~10% of export volume).

segments.name: Greige fabrics
segments.commentary: The remaining ~48% of revenue (~Rs 180 crore) in FY26. Exports are CIF. Management says greige fabric earns a traditional 7-9% margin, and utilisation runs at 80-83%.

FY27 EBITDA margin target of 10-11%; management called a return to ~19% a likely 'audacious goal' in the post-tariff era.

Management targets a run-rate revenue of Rs 500-600 crore with the right product mix, full outsourcing capacity utilisation and higher realisations. Timing is 'maybe this year, or next financial year'.
No further capex planned in FY27; the capex cycle is over, with new looms commissioning in Q1-Q2 FY27.
Inventory expected to return to prior-year levels within two quarters, via lean practices and an industrial engineering consultant.
New customers in the UK, Europe, Middle East, Japan and Australia; onboarding takes about one year, with results expected in 2-3 quarters.

Additional looms installed in FY26 to come into production in Q1-Q2 FY27.
Home textiles outsourcing is increasing; commodity items may be outsourced to cut costs and expand volume.
demand_pricing: Order backlog of about 6.5 million units as of 31 May (the CFO also cited ~6 million); volume growth in FY26 about 15%, with 15-20% guided for FY27 on the current order book. Management said volume growth will not fully translate into sales because of price realisation drops.

US tariff rose to ~50-60% at one point and then settled at 18%; the company shared ~10% of the tariff burden with the customer through a discount of 18% that is still in place, against a current tariff of 10%.
Customer Quince (US) is a major account; management said the discount is under negotiation and a slight price increase has been agreed on one or two products from this quarter.
Customer price sensitivity is elevated post-tariff; management cited the tariff, the war and oil price shocks as exogenous hits.
Input costs: raw material up ~15% due to the war and cotton futures moving to 78 cents from ~69-70 cents; bleaching, job work and freight costs also rose.
Working capital: payables held to 45-60 days; the company says it pays vendors within 45 days to comply with MSME rules.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 operating margin return to FY25 levels of ~19% EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: uncertain. FY26 was 7.43%; target is 10-11%. CMD said 19% is pre-tariff and may be a stretch in the post-tariff era.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak revenue at full utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said greige runs at 80-83% utilisation so ~80% is the practical ceiling. Management said the top line would reach ~Rs 420 crore at peak, with a Rs 500-600 crore run-rate possible with the right mix and outsourcing.

qa_highlights.question: How is the margin split between greige and home textiles?
qa_highlights.answer: Greige fabric earns a traditional 7-9% margin. The EBITDA drop is mainly from home textiles, where the ~Rs 20 crore tariff-linked price cut was the main hit, plus gratuity (Rs 41 lakh) and PF settlement (Rs 32 lakh) costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 18% discount still in place when US tariffs have fallen to 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the discount is still in place, the customer is more price sensitive post-tariff, and negotiations are ongoing; pipeline sales carry the earlier tariff.

qa_highlights.question: Why are payables so low compared with group companies?
qa_highlights.answer: The CMD said both companies are cash-rich and pay vendors within 30-45 days, so terms are not favourable to group entities. Pacific Cotton is a separate US entity selling basic lower-value Amazon-brand items.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 discounting fall from Rs 13.7 crore to Rs 2.3 crore, yet gross margin is flat?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: gross margin is unchanged; Q4 PBT Rs 4.1 crore vs Rs 4.87 crore in Q3, with the gap from strategy consultant costs, the PF settlement and a Rs 62 lakh Canadian liability.

key_quotes: We are being a little conservative on that front. But we're definitely not understating here.
