rows.label: CFO transition to Rakesh Mishra
rows.why: Sweta Agarwal is replaced by Rakesh Mishra as CFO effective September 1, 2026, so a leadership change falls inside the window.

tone.note: Management was confident on aftermarket records, domestic volumes and the ESC pipeline but cautious on margins and exports, citing aluminium and gas costs, the West Asia conflict and geopolitical uncertainty, and declined numeric export guidance; analysts pressed on ESC market share, AEBS/ADAS wins,

533033|2026-03.headline: ISGEC FY26 standalone revenue rose 4.2% to INR5,229 crore, below 7-8% guidance; FY27 revenue guided up 10-12%.
533033|2026-03.overview: Q4 standalone revenue grew 16% and PBT 48% YoY, with a sharp Q4 recovery after a weak full year. FY26 standalone PBT was INR455 crore (up 17%), of which about INR80 crore came from Philippines items that management classed as non-operational, leaving underlying operational PBT near INR375 crore. Consolidated PAT fell 25% to INR154 crore, driven by a catch-up depreciation charge after the Philippines business was reclassified from held-for-sale to continuing operations. Net borrowings fell to INR476 crore from INR836 crore.

financial_highlights.change: within 12-13% range for third consecutive year
up from INR532 crore; more than doubled
includes catch-up charge on Philippines assets; YoY increase INR104 crore

segments.name: Manufacturing (Products)
segments.commentary: FY26 EBIT margin 12.46%; management expects 12-13% to be maintained in FY27 and sees the bulk of FY27 growth (about INR500 crore) coming from this segment.

segments.name: Projects (EPC)
segments.commentary: FY26 EBIT margin 4.58%; management targets about 5.5% in FY27 on older projects closing, newer shorter-duration orders at better margins, and contingencies. Projects growth guided at 3-4%.

segments.name: Isgec Hitachi Zosen JV
segments.commentary: FY26 total income INR672 crore and PBT INR103 crore; orders in hand INR763 crore at 31 Mar 2026. FY27 guided to revenue near INR700 crore and PBT above INR100 crore.

segments.name: Cavite Biofuels (Philippines ethanol)
segments.commentary: Commercial production from 17 Dec 2025 to 20 Apr 2026 on sugarcane, then molasses. FY26 reported loss INR295 crore, including INR170 crore depreciation, INR95 crore forex and ~INR70 crore interest; operating loss ~INR26 crore. Plant at 70-75% utilisation now, targeted 85-90%; FY27 depreciation seen near INR150 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue guided up 10-12%, with about INR500 crore of the increase from manufacturing and 3-4% growth in projects.
Manufacturing EBIT margin of 12-13% expected to be maintained in FY27 despite input cost inflation.
Projects EBIT margin expected to improve to about 5.5% in FY27 from 4.58%.
Export revenue expected to exceed INR1,100-1,200 crore in FY27; export order book about INR1,450 crore at 31 Mar 2026 and expected to grow in percentage terms.
Opening FY27 order book about INR7,000 crore after excluding INR550 crore of cancelled orders; INR1,400 crore of new orders booked in April-May 2026.

Philippines ethanol plant expected to run at 85-90% capacity for the rest of the year, barring 1-1.5 months of heavy rain; FY27 interest cost on Cavite Biofuels expected to be borne at group level (loans now from ISGEC).
capex_capacity: Capex FY26 INR153 crore, funded from internal accruals; capacity additions underway across most manufacturing product lines and described as on schedule with minor adjustments.
Board approved an additional INR25 crore to expand capacity at the Muzaffarnagar steel castings plant (approved 1 June 2026).
Some new capacity expected to come online in FY27 and contribute to revenue; it will add depreciation.
Cavite Biofuels (Philippines ethanol) commercial production began 17 Dec 2025; operating at 70-75% capacity currently, targeted 85-90%.
Philippines business no longer held for sale; management says a buyer is being sought but no specific party is in advanced talks, and no letter of intent is in place.
demand_pricing: Demand: inquiry pipeline and order booking outlook described as strong in both domestic and export markets; no impact from geopolitical developments on existing orders.

Input costs rising for steel forgings, castings, chemicals and imported materials, plus higher logistics costs and longer transit times; gas shortages raised fuel costs but manufacturing has not been disrupted.
Cost increases expected to be absorbed mainly through contingencies and back-to-back supplier orders placed after customer orders are booked.
Export markets: manufacturing presses sold in Southeast Asia (Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia); projects work in Africa and Latin America. Southeast Asia and Africa are the main export geographies.
Sector demand: sugar, power, oil and gas, automobiles and fertilizers cited as doing well; paper weak; few new ethanol plants being built in India.
Export billing is under confirmed letters of credit in USD or EUR, with forward cover taken; projects generally run a cash surplus.

qa_highlights.question: How is FY27 10-12% growth split between manufacturing and projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manufacturing should add about INR500 crore, with projects growing about 3-4%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 12-13% manufacturing and 4.5% projects margin at risk from raw material volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing 12-13% is considered maintained via back-to-back supplier orders and contingencies; projects margin is expected to rise to about 5.5% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did manufacturing margin soften in Q4 versus Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it reflects which orders were dispatched in each quarter, since revenue is recognised on dispatch; annual margin of 12-13% is the right lens.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Cavite Biofuels post high losses in a peak season?
qa_highlights.answer: Ethanol was stored awaiting government allocations for April-June and July-September; dispatches were minimal in Q4. FY26 operating loss was about INR26 crore after depreciation, forex and interest.

qa_highlights.question: Status of INR300 crore FGD retention money expected in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: More than INR200 crore realised; INR165 crore remains, with about one-third expected in June and the rest by August.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of other income and forex in consolidated results?
qa_highlights.answer: Forex fluctuation of INR103 crore in other income, of which about INR50 crore relates to Isgec Investments Pte Ltd (Singapore) and is classified in other expenses per accounting standards.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (steel forgings, castings, chemicals, imports) and geopolitical disruption affecting logistics and margins; management says it is absorbing costs for now.

Philippines business: unsold, classified as continuing operations; sale timing uncertain and a prior deal fell through when the buyer could not pay. Ongoing depreciation of about INR150 crore for Cavite Biofuels in FY27.
Cancelled orders of INR550 crore in FY26 and FY26 revenue shortfall versus 7-8% guidance.
Negative net worth at Isgec Investments Pte Ltd and capital deficiency at Bioeq Energy Holding; funded via group shareholder loans.
Export receivables and currency risk in Africa and Southeast Asia; company says no significant money has been stuck with African customers.
Watch Q1 FY27: FGD retention collection (INR165 crore), Cavite utilisation ramp, order inflow after INR1,400 crore in April-May, and projects margin progress toward 5.5%.
533033|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the manufacturing margin range and FY27 growth, but candid that FY26 missed guidance and that the Philippines accounting and sale are uncertain. Management was evasive on Cavite Biofuels EBITDA and on sale price and timing, citing accounting constraints and geopolitical fluidity.
key_quotes: I want to be transparent about its composition. About INR80 crores of the PBT is from items related to the Philippines business.
So we are reasonably confident that 12% to 13% is going to be maintained.
We should be closer to 5.5% for FY27.
So we normally work with confirmed letters of credit. And these are denominated in dollars or euros, and we take forward covers against them.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Projects EBIT margin guided to about 5.5% in FY27 from 4.58% in FY26 on older projects closing and better-margin shorter orders; manufacturing held at 12-13% (12.46% FY26) despite input cost inflation.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capacity additions are under construction across most manufacturing product lines and described as on schedule, with some new capacity expected to come online in FY27 and add depreciation; quantum not disclosed, and capacity was not quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 standalone revenue guided up 10-12% with about INR500 crore from manufacturing and 3-4% from projects, backed by ~INR7,000 crore opening order book and INR1,400 crore of orders booked in April-May 2026.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 70% per the call, well below the 80%+ threshold, so no broad new-plant case; only a small INR25 crore Muzaffarnagar expansion was approved on 1 June 2026, and FY26 capex was INR153 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Export order book about INR1,450 crore and INR1,400 crore of orders in April-May 2026 support the FY27 10-12% guide, but FY26 revenue of INR5,229 crore missed the 7-8% guidance, so an upgrade is conditional on order conversion.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY26 missed the 7-8% revenue guide (actual 4.2%), INR550 crore of orders were cancelled, and input cost inflation in steel forgings and castings is being absorbed through contingencies and back-to-back orders.

rows.label: Cavite Biofuels ramp to 85-90% utilisation
rows.why: Plant at 70-75% utilisation now, targeted 85-90% for the rest of the year barring 1-1.5 months of heavy rain; FY26 operating loss ~INR26 crore, and FY27 depreciation seen near INR150 crore.

rows.label: Philippines business sale
rows.why: Buyer being sought but no specific party in advanced talks and no letter of intent; a prior deal fell through when the buyer could not pay.

rows.label: FGD retention money collection
rows.why: INR165 crore of the INR300 crore FGD retention remains outstanding, with about one-third expected in June and the rest by August.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 12-13% manufacturing margin and 10-12% FY27 growth, but candid that FY26 missed guidance, and evasive on Cavite Biofuels EBITDA, sale price and timing; analysts probed the margin split and Philippines losses.

533033|2026-06.headline: ISGEC Q1 FY27 standalone total income up 51% to INR 1,585 crore, but PBT up only 10% to INR 123 crore; FY27 standalone revenue guided up 10-12%.
533033|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income rose 51% YoY to INR 1,585 crore and EBIT grew 15% to INR 157 crore, with PBT up 10% to INR 123 crore as Q1 FY26 had high forex-driven other income. Manufacturing EBIT margin was 12% and projects EBIT margin 5.25%. Consolidated PBT was INR 53 crore, held back by an INR 83 crore loss at the Philippines ethanol plant, which ran at about 65-70% utilisation. Management kept FY27 standalone revenue growth guidance at 10-12% and said it is conservative, citing carry-forward of order execution into FY28.

financial_highlights.change: about 45% higher vs INR 1,374 crore in Q1 FY26
includes INR 37 crore depreciation, INR 20 crore interest, INR 10 crore forex
vs INR 381 crore at 31 Mar 2026 and INR 408 crore at 30 Jun 2025
down INR 170 crore QoQ from INR 476 crore; INR 832 crore a year earlier

segments.name: Industrial Projects (standalone)
segments.commentary: Income up on improved execution per schedule; management expects roughly INR 1,000 crore per quarter in Q2 FY27 and projects EBIT margin of 5-6% for FY27. Export orders booked in Africa and Latin America.

segments.name: Manufacturing (standalone)
segments.commentary: Income lifted by dispatch of a roughly INR 130 crore US order that had been on hold; EBIT margin 12%, guided 12-13%. Steady-state consolidated manufacturing revenue guided at INR 750 crore plus per quarter.

segments.name: Isgec Hitachi Zosen
segments.commentary: Orders in hand INR 889 crore. FY26 revenue about INR 670 crore; management expects about 10% growth in revenue and profit in FY27.

segments.name: Saraswati Sugar Mills
segments.commentary: Revenue down due to lower cane availability last season (untimely rain); cane availability improvement steps under way for next season.

segments.name: Philippines ethanol (CBPI)
segments.commentary: Q1 loss INR 83 crore at about 65-70% utilisation; crushed about 84,000 tonnes of cane, sold over 8 million litres of ethanol. Management targets about 90% utilisation by December and a much lower loss in Q2.

segments.name: Eagle Press and Isgec Titan Metal
segments.commentary: Eagle Press about INR 150 crore a year; Isgec Titan Metal expected at about INR 150 crore in FY27 vs INR 102 crore in FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue growth guided at 10-12%; management says the figure is conservative with a bias to realism.
Manufacturing EBIT margin guided at 12-13% for FY27; projects EBIT margin guided to improve slightly within 5-6%.
Isgec Hitachi Zosen revenue and profit guided about 10% higher than FY26.
Manufacturing capacity expansion (approved INR 502 crore) to add up to about INR 1,200 crore annual revenue when fully complete; main benefit from FY28-29.

Bhartauli machine-building phase 1 (INR 73 crore) to complete in early September 2026, with about INR 225 crore annual revenue potential; billing expected only from Q1 FY28 as work-in-progress builds first.
Dahej skids and modules facility expected to complete around 31 May 2027.
Philippines ethanol depreciation expected about INR 95 crore in FY27 (WDV method); interest about INR 19-20 crore per quarter.
capex_capacity: Bhartauli (Haryana) presses plant: phase 1 INR 70-73 crore completing first week of September 2026; phase 2 (INR 218 crore) completion expected around end-CY2027 or Q1 CY2028.
Dahej (Gujarat) SEZ skids and modules facility expected to complete around 31 May 2027.
Casting factory expansions, tubing and piping shops at Rattangarh and standard mechanical press factory at Bawal are running largely on schedule, with some facilities completing in FY27.
Board-approved manufacturing capex INR 502 crore; separate corporate office building under construction in projects business.
Q1 capex about INR 47 crore, funded from internal accruals.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand strong across almost all product lines; export inquiry base described as healthy.
Export orders booked in Africa, Latin America and Southeast Asia; more than INR 750 crore of export orders booked in Q1.
Standalone orders of about INR 1,200 crore booked in July to date (Q2 FY27).
Management says INR 95/USD rupee improves competitiveness versus other bidders; export logistics costs, freight rates and transit times have risen due to the geopolitical situation.

Commodity prices (steel, copper, aluminium, nickel) stabilised but slightly above pre-war levels; war-related material cost increases have a small adverse effect on profitability, absorbed through contingencies.
Project mix shifting to shorter-duration (max 33-36 months, target 2-2.5 years) technology-intensive orders; avoiding long contract/site-erection-heavy orders.
Sugar machinery export orders up, particularly sugar refineries; management declined to detail the large export orders.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 top-line guidance only 10-12% despite strong execution and a larger order book, and what is the quarterly run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a good part of order execution carries forward into FY28, which is why guidance is 10-12%. Projects are expected at about INR 1,000 crore a quarter and standalone manufacturing at a similar level in Q2 FY27, with Isgec Hitachi Zosen about 10% higher than FY26's roughly INR 670 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is steady-state manufacturing revenue on a consolidated basis, and how big was the Q1 US order?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated manufacturing was about INR 800 crore in Q1 and is guided at INR 750 crore plus per quarter for the next quarter, rising a bit later. The delayed US order was about INR 130 crore; the customer had paid 95% two or three quarters earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why is guidance conservative when Q1 alone adds about INR 570 crore of incremental revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers a conservative guidance it can meet over an aggressive one. It agreed the numbers could be higher and said there is hope for better outcomes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and revenue potential of the expansions, and when will they be complete?
qa_highlights.answer: Board-approved manufacturing capex is INR 502 crore; the corporate office in projects is separate. Full completion could add about INR 1,200 crore annual revenue, mostly from FY28-29. Bhartauli phase 1 (INR 73 crore) completes in early September 2026 with about INR 225 crore annual revenue potential, but billing starts only in Q1 FY28 as work-in-progress builds; phase 2 (INR 218 crore) completes around end-CY2027 or Q1 CY2028. Dahej completes around 31 May 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Philippines ethanol plant post an INR 83 crore loss, and when does it reach breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: The loss comprised about INR 37 crore depreciation, INR 20 crore interest, INR 10 crore forex and unrecovered fixed costs. Utilisation is 65-70%; management targets about 90% in December and a substantially lower loss in Q2, with the plant running on molasses until the next cane season starts in November.

qa_highlights.question: How much depreciation and interest does the Philippines business carry, and is shutting or selling it an option?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 depreciation is expected at about INR 95 crore on a WDV basis, so roughly INR 57-60 crore over the remaining three quarters. Interest is about INR 19-20 crore per quarter, paid to the parent. Management said it considers all options, but a shut asset would find no buyer, and it is hopeful the plant will begin to cover interest and costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone PBT grow only 10% when EBITDA grew about 64%, and what drove other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY26 other income was high due to dividends from subsidiaries (about INR 20-22 crore a year, now split across quarters), interest income and forex gains on Philippines loans. Forex will keep swinging other income up and down; management said operating income was the better measure this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the export order intake, and what are the execution timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: More than INR 750 crore of export orders were booked in Q1, from Africa, Latin America and Southeast Asia, with sugar refinery machinery up. Management cited INR 95/USD as a competitive help, offset by higher freight and transit times. Execution timelines are about 4-12 months for manufactured items, 14 months to 2.5 years for projects, 15-18 months at Isgec Hitachi Zosen and 6-9 months at Eagle Press.

risks_watch: Philippines ethanol plant: utilisation has been 65-70% and it must reach about 90% by December to cover roughly INR 40 crore a quarter of depreciation and interest for PBT breakeven; the Q2 loss reduction is the key check.
Execution timing of INR 130 crore order-on-hold type dispatches and Bhartauli phase 1 billing, which starts only in Q1 FY28, so revenue visibility from new capacity in FY27 is limited.

Export logistics and war-related costs: freight rates, container availability and transit times have worsened; commodity prices remain slightly above pre-war levels and absorption relies on contingencies.
Decline in other income (forex and dividend timing) can keep PBT growth well below EBITDA growth; there is no firm guidance on capitalisation or depreciation step-up for FY27.
Saraswati Sugar Mills revenue is expected to fall on low cane availability; cane availability steps are under way for the next season.
Management declined to quantify several items (large export orders, FY27 Philippines EBITDA at 90% utilisation, capitalisation), so these should be tracked in next quarter's disclosures.
key_quotes: So the order book, I agree, has improved substantially. But a good part of the order executions is going to carry forward to the next financial year.
It's better to give a conservative guidance and meet it rather than give an aggressive guidance and be uncertain about it.
We are being realistic with a conservative bias.
Now what we are taking maximum is something like 2.5 years at the most 33-36 months.
533033|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on domestic demand, execution and margins, but deliberately conservative on FY27 top-line guidance and cautious on the Philippines ethanol business. Management repeatedly declined to give numbers on the ethanol EBITDA outlook, export order sizes and capitalisation.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Manufacturing EBIT margin 12% guided 12-13% for FY27 and projects EBIT margin 5.25% in Q1 versus guided 5-6% with slight improvement; Philippines loss of INR 83 crore should narrow as utilisation climbs from 65-70% toward 90% by December.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Bhartauli phase 1 completes early Sep 2026; Dahej around 31
rows.why: Bhartauli phase 1 (INR 73 crore) adds about INR 225 crore annual revenue potential, but billing starts only Q1 FY28; the approved INR 502 crore manufacturing expansion adds up to about INR 1,200 crore annual revenue, mostly from FY28-29.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 standalone revenue guided up 10-12%, backed by standalone orders in hand of INR 7,727 crore and about INR 1,000 crore per quarter projects run-rate in Q2 FY27; export orders over INR 750 crore booked in Q1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Manufacturing utilisation is not a disclosed figure, but the company is already investing across most manufacturing lines with INR 502 crore board-approved and Bhartauli phase 2 INR 218 crore under construction, so further capex announcements are plausible as order flow runs strong.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management calls FY27 revenue guidance of 10-12% conservative; Q1 standalone total income rose 51% to INR 1,585 crore and standalone orders in hand reached INR 7,727 crore, but top-line upside is contingent on execution and the one-off INR 130 crore US order.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Philippines ethanol loss of INR 83 crore must narrow sharply to hit PBT breakeven, freight and war-related material costs are rising, and Saraswati Sugar revenue is expected to fall on low cane availability.

rows.label: Philippines ethanol utilisation to 90% by December 2026
rows.why: Utilisation at 65-70% with INR 83 crore Q1 loss; reaching 90% would bring the loss down to cover roughly INR 40 crore a quarter of depreciation and interest, but cane season restarts only in November.

rows.label: Export order ramp from Africa, Latin America and Southeast Asia
rows.why: More than INR 750 crore of export orders booked in Q1 with execution of 4-12 months for manufactured items and 14 months to 2.5 years for projects; export share rose to about 25% of revenue from 15%.

rows.label: Standalone order flow into Q2 FY27
rows.why: About INR 1,200 crore of standalone orders booked in July to date against standalone orders in hand of INR 7,727 crore at 30 June 2026.

533047|2026-03.headline: IMFA Q4 FY26 production about 68,500 t and PAT rose to INR103 crore on realisations of about INR109,000/t, though forex MTM weighed on other expenses.
533047|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as operationally strong, with production of about 68,500 tonnes including roughly 2,200 tonnes from the KNR 2 acquisition (closed 27 February 2026, furnaces switched on in March). Realisations rose to about INR109,000/t from about INR87,000/t a year earlier, lifting PAT to about INR103 crore from INR47 crore. Reported other expenses were hit by a notional forex mark-to-market loss of about INR28 crore on hedges (actual loss about INR3 crore), with the company stating the underlying forex gain sits in revenue. Management guided Q1 FY27 margins and prices above Q4 and expects around 80,000 t of sales in Q1 versus a normal 65,000–67,000 t.

segments.name: Ferro alloys (ferrochrome)
segments.commentary: Export sales are about 90% of volume, all in dollars. Management targets a 60:40 export:domestic mix by around late FY27, with at least about 200,000 t allocated domestically over time. Domestic prices are cited at INR118,000–120,000/t and export realisations above INR120,000/t.

segments.name: Mining
segments.commentary: Chrome ore output was about 8 lakh t in FY26 (above 7 lakh t in FY25), with FY27 target of 10 lakh t. Mahagari underground output was 536,000 t, and the long-term plan is 12 lakh t, entirely underground, under an investment of close to INR1,000 crore.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Existing power base is 200 MW thermal at Choudwar, 4.5 MW solar at Therubali and about 5 MW off-gas. Hybrid renewable of 135 MW is contracted: 70 MW from JSW Energy (around July 2026) and 65 MW from Enfinity Global (June 2027); the 40 MW earlier deal was cancelled. The company expects 35–40% of energy from renewables in FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ferrochrome output indicated at about 400,000 t, rising to about 475,000–500,000 t in FY28 (KNR 1 and KNR 2 combined).

KNR 1 (100,000 t greenfield) furnaces to be switched on around 10–15 July 2026, with the second furnace around end-August/early September; annualised 500,000 t run-rate targeted by November–December 2026.
Ethanol project: commissioning in Q2 FY27 with output expected around end-August 2026.
Partially built 33 MVA furnace at KNR 2 (adds about 50,000 t) targeted for June 2027, subject to environmental clearance; firm timeline to be given with Q1 results.
EBITDA cost per ton to fall INR3,000–4,000/t on a weighted basis once KNR 1 and KNR 2 are fully running; steady state expected from Q4 FY27.

FY27 capex about INR450 crore (balance Kalinganagar, ethanol and Sukinda underground mines), funded by about INR170 crore unutilised term loan plus internal accruals; FY28 mines capex about INR700 crore, with the bulk likely in FY28.
Coal linkage pricing expected to be INR400–500/t cheaper, benefiting from H2 FY27.
Q1 FY27: sales about 80,000 t; prices and margins guided above Q4 FY26; Q2 prices expected to be similar to Q1.
capex_capacity: KNR 1 greenfield (100,000 t): cold trials and pre-commissioning from 30 May 2026; start delayed 10–15 days due to partial manpower demobilisation and heat.
KNR 2 acquired from Tata Steel, closed 27 February 2026; operating at about 70% utilisation per analyst. Furnace tally: 100,000 t acquired plus 50,000 t from the partially built 33 MVA furnace.
Ethanol plant: pre-commissioning July 2026, commissioning Q2 FY27.
Chrome mining: 10 lakh t in FY27, moving to 12 lakh t; Sukinda open-cast ore (3–4 lakh t) to taper into underground output of about 6 lakh t.
Possible third furnace at KNR 1 on land already held; decision deferred. The earlier 220,000 t phase 2 expansion is no longer being pursued.
demand_pricing: Global ferrochrome output fell about 9.4% to just under 16 million t in 2025, supporting firmer prices along with elevated cost structures.
South African power tariff: special rate of $0.62/kWh approved versus $1.36 standard (earlier $0.877). Management views the net effect on IMFA as neutral; the outcome is uncertain.
West Asia crisis: direct impact limited to higher freight and domestic logistics costs; container and shipping availability described as under control.

Hedging policy: about 25–30% of net forex exposure hedged, mostly forwards for 12–18 months. Rupee moved from about INR89.9 (31 Dec) to INR93.65–94.65 (31 Mar) and about INR95–96 at the time of the call.
Marketing: about 70–75% of volume under long-term contracts (monthly pricing for China, quarterly for POSCO and Japanese customers); the balance is repeat spot sales.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of South African power tariff relief and the global supply response on Asian ferrochrome competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said that if South African output rises, Chinese ore supply may fall, so net supply is roughly neutral; it flagged possible upside-sharing conditions and that the tariff may not be viable if prices drop.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total power requirement met by hybrid renewables and the cost saving?
qa_highlights.answer: Power need for KNR 1 and KNR 2 is about 100 MW; 135 MW is contracted (70 MW from July 2026 and 65 MW from June 2027). Renewable tariffs are at about grid parity, fixed for 25–29 years, and coal linkage savings of INR400–500/t are expected from H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and debt plans for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR450 crore, funded by about INR170 crore unutilised term loan and internal accruals. FY28 includes about INR700 crore for mines, with the exact amount not yet calculated.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging policy and the sharp rise in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: About 25–30% of exposure is hedged for 12–18 months. The notional MTM loss is about INR28 crore against an actual loss of about INR3 crore, while the forex gain in revenue is about INR80 crore above budget for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR3,000–4,000/t EBITDA cost saving from KNR appear in current numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: The saving applies only once both KNR 1 and KNR 2 are running. Start-up costs and CTU fixed charges (about INR2–2.5 crore for the GNA RE corridor from 1 June) will ease over a few quarters, with full benefits from about November–December 2026 and steady state from Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for the export:domestic mix and H1 realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: The company aims for 60:40 export:domestic by about late FY27 (currently 90:10). Q1 FY27 sales are about 80,000 t, with prices above Q4; Q2 is expected to be similar to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Plans beyond ferrochrome, including critical minerals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pursuing critical minerals and rare earths adjacent to its mining skill set. It has bought tender documents for some blocks in Odisha and elsewhere but has not yet bid. No quantified timeline was given.

risks_watch: KNR 1 furnace commissioning slippage (currently 10–15 July) due to manpower and temperatures of 44–45°C.

rows.label: HCRO (Europe) strategic review and loss
rows.why: HCRO loss nearly doubled to about INR67 crores (up about INR20 crores YoY) on revenue up 5.7%; management expects clarity in FY27 with options including tie-up or exit-type actions.

rows.label: Keystone upgrades and realisation
rows.why: Keystone sales value up 22% YoY to INR154 crores with average unit realisation up 73% to INR14.4 lakhs, and upgrade value up 58% to INR89 crores; upgrades running at about 2,000-2,500 per quarter against about 3 lakh members.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term direction, resort occupancy (86.7%) and Keystone pricing, but cautious on near-term profit, citing renovation keys, new resorts and regulatory costs; analysts pushed on the 3% revenue growth versus the 17-18% CAGR vision, HCRO strategy and Keystone buyback terms

533088|2026-09.headline: Mahindra Holidays Q2 FY27: standalone PAT fell 16% to INR43 crores on growth costs, even as resort revenue grew 15% and upgrades rose 26%.
533088|2026-09.overview: Standalone total income rose 4% YoY to INR395 crores, with double-digit resort revenue growth offset by flat membership income, so EBITDA fell 12% to INR124 crores and PAT fell 16% to INR43 crores. Consolidated PAT grew 17% to INR19.7 crores and consolidated total income rose 9% to INR819 crores. Management cited growth-linked costs, renovation downtime, new unprofitable resorts, GST and solar subsidy effects as margin drags. Network shrank to 5,762 keys across 106 resorts after 6 exits, with about 1,000 gross keys targeted over the next six months.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR166 crores a year ago

segments.name: Vacation ownership (VO) / Keystone
segments.commentary: Upgrades grew 25-27% YoY per management; net member additions reported but expected to rise over next 1-2 quarters. Member base about 303,000; organic and digital contributed 66% of additions, with referrals at 40-50% of new sales. 12-month retention rose from about 11%.

segments.name: Resorts (standalone)
segments.commentary: Resort revenue grew 15%, the highest in 8 quarters, with occupancy at 75.6%. Resort margins were pressured by new resorts, renovation downtime, GST and solar subsidy effects.

segments.name: Holiday Club Resorts Oy (HCRO, Finland)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 8% to EUR 36.5 million; EBITDA EUR 1.7 million (vs EUR 1.3 million); net loss EUR 0.3 million. Loss in Indian books including interest and forex was INR18 crores vs INR27 crores a year ago. Strategic review in progress.

Target of 10,000 keys by FY30 is on track; 85% visibility on the target per management, with about 1,500 keys still to be identified (net figure).
Around 650 keys to be exited in FY27 in total, versus about 400 exited last year; management says the exit journey is largely done.
Capex in the next six months to be roughly equal to H1 spend, per management.
H2 expected to be more profitable than H1, with Q3 and Q4 seasonally strongest, especially for non-member business.
Capital allocation about 70% to new resorts and 30% to existing resort improvements.
Occupancy expected to climb in Q3 and Q4; management sees no major West Asia impact on occupancy, though some project costs and delays have emerged.
Upcoming openings: Ganpatipule (Q3 end or Q4 start), Kumbhalgarh (Q3), Jaisalmer (Q3), Gir (Q4 end or Q1 early).

demand_pricing: Occupancy 75.6%, up 220 bps YoY; management expects full-year occupancy of 80-81% and rising occupancy into Q3 and Q4 through algorithmic inventory allocation.
Premiumisation: 10-year Ivory is the most preferred Keystone product; 10-year and 5-year together about 80% of the portfolio.
West Asia crisis raised airfares and limited some overseas-linked occupancy, offset by driving holidays; the model is not heavily dependent on overseas travellers.
Cost of acquisition as a percentage of sales declined YoY; management targets sustained reduction.
Non-member, corporate and MICE business growing from a small base.

qa_highlights.question: How is Keystone performing across Ebony, Ivory and Jade, and what are the FY27 expectations for sales and realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 10-year Ivory product has the most members and the 10-year plus 5-year products make up about 80% of the portfolio. Upgrades grew 25-27% YoY, and net member additions are expected to rise over the next 1-2 quarters, though no formal guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much inventory is out of service for renovation, and when will it return?
qa_highlights.answer: 442 keys are under renovation, with most expected back in Q3 and Q4. No revenue offset was quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a West Asia or inflation-driven slowdown risk for Q3 demand and expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Some limited occupancy impact from higher airfares, offset by driving holidays. Project costs have risen and some openings are delayed, but no plans are being pulled back.

qa_highlights.question: How is capital allocated between new capacity and existing resorts?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% toward new resorts and about 30% toward improving existing resorts over the longer term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H1/H2 revenue split?
qa_highlights.answer: VO membership and ASF income (about two-thirds of revenue) are broadly even across quarters; the remaining third splits about 35-40% in H1 and 60-65% in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone EBITDA and PAT fall while resort revenue grew?

qa_highlights.question: Is the company raising debt to fund capex?

West Asia geopolitical and inflation pressure on travel demand into the December season.

533096|2026-03.headline: Adani Power Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA rose 27% YoY to INR6,498 crore and PAT 64% to INR4,271 crore, though continuing EBITDA grew only 9%.
533096|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA of INR6,498 crore (up 27% YoY) and PAT of INR4,271 crore (up 64% YoY), but continuing EBITDA was INR5,573 crore (up 9%), with the gap tied to recently acquired assets and PPA-related items. Full-year FY26 continuing revenue was INR55,583 crore and continuing EBITDA INR21,285 crore, both broadly flat, as weak merchant prices and lower imported-coal tariffs offset volume growth. Management reported 95% of 18.15 GW operating capacity under long- or medium-term PPAs, with merchant exposure cut from 16% to about 5%. Expansion remains on plan with a 1.32 GW Korba Phase-II and a 1.6 GW Mahan Phase-II timeline, though Mahan has been pushed toward FY28 on geopolitical labour and LPG constraints. Net debt rose to INR45,022 crore on bridge financing for capex.

segments.name: Operations (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Q4 PLF 74%, FY26 PLF 66.5%; Q4 power sales 27.2 BU and FY26 sales 99.1 BU (+3.4%). Plant availability above 91% in Q1 FY27 vs ~88% a year earlier.

segments.name: Merchant exposure
segments.commentary: Open merchant capacity is about 5% (roughly 1 GW), down from 16% at the start of FY26; remaining open capacity sits mainly at Mundra Unit 9, Mahan Stage 1 and a small part of Raipur.

guidance_outlook: Korba Phase-II (1.32 GW): Unit 1 in Q2 FY27, Unit 2 before year-end FY27; estimated FY27 EBITDA contribution about INR1,000 crore, rising in FY28 on a full-year basis.
Mahan Phase-II (1.6 GW): first unit targeted by end-FY27, at the latest Q1 FY28, second unit about six months later; slippage attributed to labour and LPG availability.
Capex about INR25,000 crore in FY27 and about INR33,000 crore in FY28, within an INR2 lakh crore expansion plan; annualised FFO about INR20,000 crore.
Management targets about INR50,000 crore EBITDA by FY31 conservatively, possibly 2030; capacity of 42 GW targeted by FY31-32, with debt repayment largely complete by FY31-32.
Commissioning deferrals average about 6 months, with 4 GW or more per year planned from FY29 to FY32; management says the 34 GW-by-2030 plan remains on track.

Maharashtra 1,600 MW PPA (INR5.30/unit: INR4.11 capacity, INR1.19 energy): PPA signing expected within about 3 months; commissioning 4-5 years out, with project location (Raigarh, Raipur or Korba) not yet assigned.
capex_capacity: Expansion: 23.7 GW thermal targeted by 2032; 13.3 GW of long-term PPAs tied up for expansion after the 1,600 MW Maharashtra LoA.
Under-construction progress: Mahan Phase-II 86%, Raipur Phase-II 54%, Raigarh Phase-II 47%; Korba Phase-II close to completion.
Korba total capex about INR8,000-8,500 crore including about INR4,100 crore acquisition cost, with a further about INR4,000 crore to spend.
Operating capacity 18.15 GW; operating capacity rose only about 600 MW YoY as Vidarbha acquired assets and expansion CWIP were added to fixed assets.
Nuclear: several SPVs incorporated, all new sites, awaiting government rules before deciding size and technology; Bhutan 570 MW hydro SPV incorporated.
demand_pricing: Power demand grew 0.8% in FY26 and 1.6% in Q4 FY26; demand revived from March, with peak demand recently reaching 256 GW.
Merchant prices were subdued through most of FY26 with a weak merchant realisation; management cited prices ranging from INR3 to INR7-8 per unit depending on weather.
PPA tariffs for imported-coal plants fell with lower import coal prices; fuel cost is a pass-through under PPAs.
About 13 GW of PPAs in the market across Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and Gujarat, plus about 4 GW new Gujarat tender.
Domestic coal supply not affected by the geopolitical situation; imported-coal shipping costs up, but pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Maharashtra 1,600 MW PPA: which project and what tariff?
qa_highlights.answer: Location not yet assigned (Raigarh, Raipur or Korba); tariff INR5.30/unit, of which INR4.11 capacity and INR1.19 energy.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and funding for FY27-28, and Korba/Mahan timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR25,000 crore in FY27 and INR33,000 crore in FY28; Korba Unit 1 in Q2 FY27, Mahan Unit 1 by end-FY27 at the latest Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Mahan (1.6 GW) pushed out from this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Conservative stance due to labour and LPG availability under the geopolitical situation; one unit still targeted by end-FY27, with Q1 FY28 as the fallback.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of borrowing after the debt increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Recent market borrowing cost about 8%, via domestic capital market (DCM) or domestic banks.

qa_highlights.question: Non-controlling interest jumped from INR8.5 crore in Q3 to INR254 crore in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by Moxie Power Unit 2 medium-term PPA with Tamil Nadu (558 MW) starting in Q4; full 12-month consolidation of Coastal Energen also added to the year-on-year rise.

qa_highlights.question: Has the group signed a long-term PPA for merchant capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: No group PPA signed during FY26; the 1,600 MW Maharashtra PPA is being served via a trading platform for residual capacity, including renewables and storage.

risks_watch: Merchant price volatility: prices range widely with weather and rising renewables, and management expects merchant prices to fall over time.
Execution risk on Mahan and Korba timelines given labour and LPG constraints linked to the geopolitical situation.
Leverage: net debt INR45,022 crore at 31 Mar 2026 and borrowing cost near 8%, with the expansion funded by interim debt before internal accruals.
Q1 FY27 PLF is lower YoY (74%) due to weak merchant prices; management expects better PLF through FY27.
Bangladesh PBDB receivable: outstanding has fallen and payments are regular, but the disputed amount remains with an expert, with possible SIAC arbitration.
533096|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and PPA visibility, but cautious and conservative on near-term commissioning dates, attributing deferrals to geopolitical labour and LPG constraints. Several answers on merchant pricing and on the reasons for the Q-o-Q non-controlling interest jump were non-committal or required follow-up.

95% of our operating capacity of 18.15 gigawatts is now tied up under long-term and medium-term PPAs.
So, we are confident that by FY31-32 our capacity will be 42 gigawatt from a planned capacity.
Our Q4 power sales reached 27.2 billion unit, while full year sales increased 3.4% to 99.1 billion unit.

rows.why: Continuing EBITDA rose only 9% YoY in Q4 (INR5,573 crore) against 27% reported growth, and FY26 continuing EBITDA was flat at INR21,285 crore as weak merchant prices and lower imported-coal tariffs offset volume growth; fuel cost is a pass-through under PPAs.

rows.why: FY26 continuing revenue (INR55,583 crore) and EBITDA (INR21,285 crore) were broadly flat YoY, and merchant exposure is only about 5% (roughly 1 GW) so there is little merchant upside, with management expecting merchant prices to fall over time.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Mahan slipped toward Q1 FY28 on labour and LPG constraints, commissioning deferrals average about 6 months, and Q1 FY27 PLF is lower YoY at 74% on weak merchant prices.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Not discussed for power generation; nuclear SPVs remain pre-decision awaiting government rules, with no launch timing.

rows.label: Maharashtra 1,600 MW PPA (INR5.30/unit) signing
rows.why: PPA signing expected within about 3 months, adding to 13.3 GW of long-term PPAs tied up for expansion; commissioning is 4-5 years out with location not yet assigned.

rows.label: Net debt rise on capex funding
rows.why: Net debt rose to INR45,022 crore with capex of about INR25,000 crore in FY27 and INR33,000 crore in FY28 funded by interim debt at about 8% before internal accruals (annualised FFO about INR20,000 crore).

rows.label: Merchant exposure cut to about 5%
rows.why: Open merchant capacity fell from 16% to about 5% (roughly 1 GW), with 95% of 18.15 GW under long- or medium-term PPAs, which limits price exposure.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term growth (INR50,000 crore EBITDA by FY31, 42 GW by FY31-32) and PPA visibility but cautious on near-term Mahan timing; analysts pushed on merchant pricing and the reason for the non-controlling interest jump, and several answers were non-committal.

533096|2026-06.headline: Adani Power Q1 FY27 continuing EBITDA rose 22% to INR6,983 crore and PAT 47% to INR4,867 crore on 78% PLF.
533096|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's strongest quarter on a continuing basis, driven by heatwave-led demand, higher PLF (78% vs 67%) and new PPAs for previously merchant capacity at Butibori and Tuticorin. Continuing revenue rose 28% to INR17,550 crore, while fuel cost rose 30% to INR9,513 crore on higher volumes and imported coal indices. Reported figures include a one-time net prior-period revenue recognition of INR1,386 crore linked to revised historic energy charges under certain PPAs. Management reiterated the 45 GW target (revised from 42 GW), an expansion capex of about INR25,000 crore this year, and a net debt-to-EBITDA band of 2-3x, while seeking an enabling resolution for a QIP.

financial_highlights.metric: Reported total revenue (incl. one-time prior period item)
Net debt / total debt as on June 30, 2026
financial_highlights.value: Net debt INR47,643 crore; total debt INR58,381 crore

segments.name: Consolidated power generation and sales
segments.commentary: Record generation of 31 billion units; dispatch 28.8 billion units (+17%); consolidated power sales about 29 billion units vs 25 billion units. PLF 78% vs 67%.

segments.name: PPA sales
segments.commentary: Power sales under PPAs grew 30% to 25 billion units. PPA tariff realisation rose 8% to INR5.93/unit, including fixed capacity charges on newly contracted Butibori and Tuticorin capacity.

segments.name: Merchant and short-term sales
segments.commentary: Merchant volumes fell to 4 billion units from 6 billion units as Butibori (600 MW) and Tuticorin (600 MW) moved to PPAs. Realisation rose 13% to INR7.04/unit.

segments.name: Godda (Bangladesh export plant)
segments.commentary: Generation 2.519 billion units vs 2.362 billion units last year; total revenue INR2,473 crore vs INR2,135 crore.

guidance_outlook: Capacity target raised to 45 GW from 42 GW, same timeline (around 2031); 23.7 GW programme unchanged in capex terms.
Expansion capex about INR25,000 crore in FY27, about INR33,000 crore in FY28, and more than INR35,000 crore thereafter; total programme about INR2 lakh crore.
Net debt-to-EBITDA currently slightly above 2x; management expects it to stay between 2x and 3x and not cross 3x.
Korba Phase-II (1,320 MW) expected before December 2026; Mahan Phase-II (1,600 MW) first unit targeted Q1 FY28, second unit about 6 months later, with an attempt to bring it into Q2.
Management expects more stability in revenue and EBITDA as most capacity moves to long-term contracts; 95% of capacity is tied up, 56% of upcoming capacity is under long-term PPAs.
533096|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on operations and financials, with firm targets on capex and capacity. Management was guarded or evasive on nuclear timing, which depends on pending government rules, and on the PTSL supply contract, where it declined to give tariff or volume detail.
key_quotes: We achieved our highest ever quarterly power generation of 31 billion units and dispatched 28.8 billion units, a growth of 17%, which was a result of improved PLF as well as greater operating capacity.
Net debt-to-EBITDA as on date, is slightly higher than 2 timex. We are expecting that net debt-to-EBITDA will not cross 3 times at any point.
So rather than distributing, we are reinvesting in the capex program.
It is not operational. It's like something like what we acquired in Butibori, more or less in the same condition.

qa_highlights.question: Will Jaiprakash be consolidated, and what expansion is possible at Bina and Nigri?
qa_highlights.answer: JPVL (24% stake) is an associate; only the share of profit is consolidated, not P&L or balance sheet line by line. Bina and Nigri have large land banks, with Bina also being assessed for nuclear suitability; no expansion planned yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nuclear plan, technology and timing for the 10 GW target by 2035?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is evaluating domestic and foreign technology on per-MW cost, but cannot finalise ordering or investment until government rules under the Act are notified. Sites are being readied and studies are underway; execution would take at least 5 years by its standard.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivable position from Bangladesh?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables were about USD400 million at end-June 2026, down quarter-on-quarter; about USD100 million is being received monthly, with collections expected slightly above monthly billing.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 3 GW additional capacity being planned and is it under PPA?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a planning-stage buffer for future state bids, since the 24 GW pipeline is tied to specific locations; capex and equipment orders are not firmed up. The 24% JPVL stake (2,220 MW) could be increased.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the strong EBITDA growth when capacity rose only about 4-5%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to higher capacity charges from converted Tuticorin, Raipur and Vidarbha capacity, higher volumes, and higher energy-charge contribution where imported coal indices rose.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex, funding and QIP plans, and has the capex changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR25,000 crore in FY27, INR33,000 crore in FY28 and over INR35,000 crore after; the programme is unchanged. Funding is mainly internal accruals (FFO about INR20,000 crore a year), with interim gaps of about INR60,000 crore from debt. The QIP is an enabling EGM resolution with no timeline or dilution detail yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt-to-EBITDA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt-to-EBITDA is slightly above 2x, and management expects it to stay between 2x and 3x and never cross 3x.

qa_highlights.question: Will dividends or bonuses be paid given large reserves?
qa_highlights.answer: No; surplus is being reinvested in the capex programme over the next 6-7 years, as management believes return on capital exceeds the dividend payout benefit.

capex_capacity: Expansion capex guided at about INR25,000 crore in FY27, about INR33,000 crore in FY28 and more than INR35,000 crore thereafter; total programme of more than INR2 lakh crore, with no change to the capex programme per CFO.

Target raised to 45 GW from 42 GW, same timeline (around 2031); management said the 23.7 GW programme is unchanged. Additional ~3 GW being planned for future state bids, at planning stage with no firm capex or equipment order.

Korba Phase-II (1,320 MW) expected before December 2026; Mahan Phase-II (1,600 MW) first unit in Q1 FY28, second unit about 6 months later, with an attempt to bring it into Q2. Raipur Phase-II and Raigarh Phase-II are over 62% and 54% complete; Mirzapur 1,600 MW greenfield execution has started. All 24 GW of BTG has been ordered.

Jaiprakash 180 MW Churk plant acquired under insolvency; not operational, expected to take about 6 months to revive, not tied to any PPA, and little contribution expected in the current year. 24% stake in JPVL is accounted as an associate (share of profit only).

Nuclear: about 10 GW target by 2035 (raised from 5 GW); ordering and capital allocation await government rules under the Act. Management said execution should take at least 5 years by its standards. Bina and Nigri have land banks for thermal or nuclear.
Hydro: 570 MW Bhutan project; PPA and tariff structure not yet finalised. Plant-level FFO of about INR20,000 crore per year cited for funding the capex plan.
demand_pricing: Peak demand hit a record of about 271 GW in May 2026; national energy consumption rose 8.4% YoY to 485 billion units in Q1 FY27 on heatwaves.

PPA tariff realisation rose 8% YoY to INR5.93/unit, including fixed capacity charges on newly contracted Butibori (600 MW) and Tuticorin (600 MW) capacity; merchant and short-term realisation rose 13% to INR7.04/unit.
PPA sales grew 30% to 25 billion units; merchant volumes fell to 4 billion units from 6 billion units as capacity moved to PPAs. Some Raipur capacity is also now under a PPA with Karnataka.

Fuel cost rose 30% to INR9,513 crore on higher dispatch and higher imported coal indices; management attributed about INR2,200 crore EBITDA gain to fuel cost change, reflecting volume, indexed variable tariffs and merchant prices.

Tied-up capacity is about 95%, with most on long-term contracts; 56% of upcoming capacity is under long-term PPAs. Bids pending: UP 4,000 MW, Gujarat 4,000 MW, Uttarakhand 1,320 MW and West Bengal about 3,800 MW (about 13 GW). 533098|2026-03.headline: NHPC FY26 PAT rose 25% to Rs 3,766 Crore, but Q4 PAT was flattered by a Rs 1,823 Crore tax credit; Rs 900 Crore one-off DTL reversal.
533098|2026-03.overview: FY26 generation rose 16% to 29,619 MU, driven by Parbati-II, Karnisar Solar and part-commissioning of Subansiri Lower (SLP), while PAF fell about 4 points to 74.75%. FY26 revenue from operations rose 12% to Rs 11,615 Crore and PAT rose 25% to Rs 3,766 Crore. Q4 PAT of Rs 1,460 Crore (up 71%) included a one-off tax credit (Q4 tax was negative Rs 1,823 Crore), and management said adjusted PAT should be about Rs 900 Crore lower than reported due to the DTL reversal. Management also disclosed about Rs 450 Crore of revenue not booked on Parbati-II and SLP because revenue is recognised at 80% of filed AFC pending CERC tariff orders.

segments.name: Hydro generation (Subansiri Lower, Parbati-II)
segments.commentary: Parbati-II booked Rs 1,320 Crore revenue for FY26 and a Rs 150 Crore loss, but Rs 104 Crore profit in Q4 after a Rs 200 Crore energy shortfall booking. SLP earned Rs 495 Crore for FY26 and Rs 487 Crore in Q4 on 506 MU generation and Rs 613 Crore revenue.

segments.name: Teesta-V
segments.commentary: No revenue in FY26; only expenditure booked. Restoration expected to start generating in June 2026. Annual AFC about Rs 500 Crore (about Rs 400 Crore ex-tax); insurance cover no longer available.

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: Karnisar commissioned in FY26. 300 MW Bikaner commissioned. Further 100 MW AP due June 2026 and 600 MW Gujarat due December 2026 under CPSU Tranche-II; 1,190 MW of solar expected in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Subansiri Lower: four of eight 250 MW units commissioned; remaining four to be commissioned one by one till March 2027. Cost Rs 30,072 Crore, Rs 26,092 Crore incurred to March 2026.
Parbati-II: CERC tariff order expected by 30 June 2026; management said revenue will be recognised in the same quarter, including interest, if the order comes in-quarter.
Subansiri Lower: interim CERC tariff awaited before billing; final order expected within about six months. Revenue booked at 80% of filed AFC.

FY27 hydro capacity addition of 2,994 MW (Subansiri balance 1,000 MW, Rangit-IV 120 MW, Pakal Dul 1,000 MW, Kiru 624 MW), plus 1,190 MW solar. Hydro regulated equity projected at Rs 30,672 Crore by end-FY27 (from Rs 18,309 Crore currently).

Five hydro projects targeted for construction start in FY27: Etalin, Sawalkot and Kamala (plus Uri-I Stage-II and Dulhasti Stage-II already awarded). Indira Sagar-Omkareshwar PSP (640 MW) construction targeted this year. Subansiri Upper likely next year.
Teesta-VI completion September 2029; Dibang completion February 2032; Ratle November 2028; Kwar March 2028; Uri-I Stage-II and Dulhasti Stage-II November 2029.
capex_capacity: Dibang (2,880 MW): estimated cost Rs 31,876 Crore including Rs 6,716 Crore grant; Rs 4,504 Crore incurred to March 2026; dam package Rs 14,446 Crore awarded April 2026; completion February 2032.
Kamala (1,720 MW, Arunachal): CCEA approved Rs 26,070 Crore on 8 April 2026 via JV with Arunachal government; subsidiary formation in progress; environment and forest clearances pending.

Pakal Dul (1,000 MW): 80% complete, Rs 9,141 Crore of Rs 12,728 Crore spent, commissioning Q4 FY27. Kiru (624 MW): 82% complete, Rs 3,637 Crore of Rs 5,409 Crore spent, Q4 FY27. Kwar (540 MW): 33% complete, Rs 1,708 Crore of Rs 4,526 Crore spent, March 2028.
Teesta-VI (500 MW): 72% complete, Rs 5,231 Crore of Rs 9,167 Crore spent, September 2029. Ratle (850 MW): 29% complete, Rs 1,538 Crore of Rs 5,282 Crore spent, November 2028.
Rangit-IV (120 MW, via JPCL, merger with NHPC in process): 96% complete, Rs 1,792 Crore of Rs 1,889 Crore spent, commissioning November 2026.
Uri-I Stage-II (240 MW, Rs 2,709 Crore) and Dulhasti Stage-II (260 MW, Rs 2,994 Crore) approved 20 February 2026; civil contracts awarded March 2026.
Solar: 40 MW Ganjam (October 2026), 50 MW floating Kerala (March 2027), 200 MW Khavda Stage-I (June 2026) and Stage-III (December 2026).
demand_pricing: Parbati-II and SLP billing: Parbati-II billing at 75% of filed tariff under CERC interim order; SLP billing awaits interim order. Both booked at 80% of filed AFC. Gross-up implies about Rs 450 Crore unrecognised revenue (Parbati-II about Rs 300 Crore, SLP about Rs 150 Crore).
Renewables: management said no recent tendering; about 23 GW awarded, of which 13 GW expected to sign PPA/PSA and 7 GW already signed.
Normative PAF: 82% consolidated, 80% standalone. FY26 PAF 75% including Teesta-V, about 80% excluding it.

Management said cost escalation is inherent in hydro (price variation), but CERC cost-plus regime allows pass-through of cost overruns beyond management control. Management said no material cost changes in current pipeline.

533104|2026-03.headline: Globus Spirits FY26 P&A revenue rose 27% to INR164 crores, while Q4 manufacturing EBITDA was INR8.3/litre and the company dropped its equity raise.
533104|2026-03.overview: Globus Spirits closed FY26 with installed capacity of 334 million litres after the UP distillery commissioning, at 80% utilisation (adjusted for UP start-up). Manufacturing EBITDA was INR6.2/litre for FY26 and INR8.3/litre in Q4, while Q4 volumes dipped on an ENA shift and a one-time inventory build-up that management expects to clear in Q1. Consumer P&A grew 27% for the year (58% excluding Delhi), but Q4 P&A EBITDA loss widened to INR5 crores, partly due to INR3-3.5 crores of label registration costs. Management said internal accruals and debt refinancing (annual debt outflow cut from INR67 crores to INR14 crores for FY27) mean there is no immediate need for the equity raise.

Global ENA supply constraints from high energy costs are creating export opportunities.

segments.commentary: Revenue grew 10% YoY to INR2,564 million, volumes up 13% YoY to 4.48 million cases and EBITDA up 13% YoY to INR440 million. UP R&O volumes grew 2.4x YoY and crossed 0.2 million cases per month.

guidance_outlook: Manufacturing EBITDA guided at INR5-7 per litre; management expects to stay in this range for all quarters of FY27.
R&O EBITDA margin guidance of 15-17%, with mix from lower-margin UP expected to pull margins toward 15-16% from the 17-18% of recent years.
Maintenance capex of about INR50-60 crore a year; no new ENA/ethanol capacity planned, with at most about 1% gain from technology. No capacity expansion planned through FY29.
P&A expected to reach profitability sooner rather than later, having moved from about negative 60% margin a couple of years ago to near breakeven.
Management expects the UK FTA to benefit the industry on Scotch costs, but said the timing and size of the benefit are uncertain and not yet visible in numbers.
West Bengal R&O re-entry expected within about 60 days of regulatory approvals, which management hopes come this quarter.
capex_capacity: Installed manufacturing capacity is about 334 million litres; Q1 utilisation was 89% against a guidance of about 85%.
UP plant utilisation was above 90% in Q1 per the CFO. About 25% of UP output is consumed captively and the rest sold in bulk, with optimisation still under way.
Capex has been limited to maintenance after UP commissioning; cash generation is being fed into P&A growth and debt paydown.
Management expects a 15-17% R&O margin band to hold while UP grows fast.
demand_pricing: Management expects ethanol demand for E20 blending to grow about 7-7.5% a year, in line with petrol growth; E85/E50 depends on car compatibility, which is limited for now.
Industry ethanol is in oversupply, but Globus ran at 89% by shifting ENA and ethanol mix and selling ENA in India and overseas, with overseas prices firming.
Glass and PET cost-push is 10-17% depending on brand and pack and is expected to persist; management says the company holds only slim packaging inventory.
Agri inflation is seasonal: Q2 and part of Q3 are inflationary, then prices ease as harvests arrive. Maize is partly hedged and FCI supplies a fixed-price portion; broken rice is unhedged.
UP is a large market of about 95 lakh cases a month. West Bengal IMIL is about 26-27 lakh cases a month, per management, slightly smaller than Rajasthan or Haryana.
Management says the company has 11 states total presence, with 4 core states plus Delhi and UP (5 core states overall), and a 6th state nearing core status.

qa_highlights.question: How will ethanol demand drivers develop given the E20 controversy, and could ethanol for cooking matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said E20 is government policy, the controversy has not hurt offtake, and demand is growing about 7.5% YoY with sticky month-on-month volumes. Cooking-fuel ethanol adoption will be slow in India without distribution and canisters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company expecting Bihar prohibition to be lifted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes prohibition in Bihar will eventually be reversed, but gave no firm timeline, estimating a change over about 1-2 years under the new Chief Minister.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of glass cost inflation on R&O and P&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Glass and PET cost-push is 10-17% by brand and pack and is expected to persist for some time, with energy costs also rising.

qa_highlights.question: Will UK FTA lower Scotch costs and expand gross profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a tailwind as inventory transitions, but benefits depend on suppliers revising base prices. Rupee depreciation of about 20% against the pound limits the net impact, and the company is not a market maker on Scotch prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of R&O in West Bengal and how is the market structured?
qa_highlights.answer: Regulatory approvals are the last step and are expected this quarter; the company would return to the market about 60 days later. Management does not see the market turning unfavourable.

qa_highlights.question: How much growth can be achieved without capex, and at what utilisation is new capex needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has no plans for new ENA/ethanol capex beyond maintenance of INR50-60 crore a year; utilisation guidance is about 85%. Capacity is seen flat through FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What are the net debt and manufacturing margin trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt was INR650 crore against INR660 crore in March 2026. Manufacturing margin is within INR5-7 per litre and management is not concerned about changes in that range.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the IMFL brand mix shift across states, with some brands rising and others falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said brand growth varies by state because category mix differs (vodka, semi-premium and deluxe whisky markets). It said no brand is structurally declining and this will continue as the company enters new geographies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UP ramp-up path and what is the margin outlook for R&O?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify quarterly UP additions but said UP is the next big bankable R&O opportunity, with a FY29 guideline already set.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company balance volume growth, input inflation and shareholder returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manufacturing margin is protected by FCI fixed-price supply, maize hedging, and monthly pass-through in the flexi-price E&A business. P&A is self-funded from cash flow, with no further capacity expansion planned.

Q2 agri inflation for broken rice (unhedged) and maize, plus the eastern India rainfall deficit.
West Bengal R&O re-entry depends on pending regulatory approvals; timing has slipped before.
P&A still loss-making at EBITDA level (negative INR13 million) and needs to reach profitability.
UP R&O mix is lowering margins toward 15-16%, and UP internal versus external sales mix is still being optimised.
Branded IMFL brand-level volatility across states; repeat behaviour for Mountain Oak and Brothers & Co. was questioned by analysts.
Ethanol overcapacity in the industry and policy ambiguity around E20 and higher blends.

533106|2026-03.headline: Oil India FY26: consolidated income Rs 38,981 cr (+3% YoY), PAT Rs 7,551 cr (+7%), with Rs 11.5/share dividend repeated.
533106|2026-03.overview: Oil India's annual investors' meet (25 May 2026, transcript filed 29 May) covered FY26 results, a record 74-well drilling year and a 1.6x GRM uplift at subsidiary NRL. Consolidated EBITDA was Rs 13,498 cr (+5%) and PAT Rs 7,551 cr (+7%) despite crude realisation falling to $69/bbl from $78. Production was 6.64 MMtoe, with about 0.1 MMt lost to a 10-15 day economic blockade. Management reiterated the 9 MMTPA NRL expansion by March 2027, a roughly 100-well-a-year drilling plan, and offshore exploration reliant on the Samudra Manthan Mission for deep-water wells.

financial_highlights.change: ~60% drilling, ~25% capital projects, ~13% investments in subsidiaries/JVs
Down from $78; lowest in last 5 years

segments.name: Upstream (Oil India)
segments.commentary: Production 6.64 MMtoe (3.45 MMt oil, 3.15 BCM gas); daily crude peaked at ~81,354 bpd, with management citing 82,200+ bpd as of late May. Record 74 wells drilled (22 exploration, 52 development) and 307 workovers. 2P reserve replacement ratio 1.20 (vs 0.94) on 231 MMt reserves, 31-year reserve life.

segments.name: Midstream (pipelines)
segments.commentary: Numaligarh-Siliguri product pipeline expanded from 1.72 to 5.5 MMTPA, completed at Rs 750 crore vs Rs 860 crore approved outlay; PM inaugurated 13 March 2026. Duliajan-Numaligarh gas pipeline expanded from 1.2 to 2.5 MMSCMD, mechanically complete, awaiting a ~7-day NRL shutdown to commission.

segments.name: Downstream (NRL, 100% subsidiary of Oil India Ltd, 3 MMTPA)
segments.commentary: Record 103% crude throughput, 99.1% availability, 87.25% distillate yield and 727 TMT MS output; GRM 1.6x prior year. Navratna status conferred Dec 2025. Expansion to 9 MMTPA targeted for March 2027, with polypropylene unit on track; expansion capex ~Rs 46,000 crore including ~Rs 7,200 crore for PPU.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Mozambique force majeure lifted Nov 2025; two LNG trains of 13 MMTPA targeted for end-2028 or early 2029, with ~$1.8 billion committed and ~$300 million cost escalation pending CCEA approval. Russian assets (Taas, Vankor) have returned ~$1 billion in dividends. Libya 95/96 major commercial discovery.

segments.name: New energy and others
segments.commentary: Oil India Green Energy Ltd (wholly-owned) has ~2 GW renewable capacity in JVs pipeline and 2 CBG plants under construction, with 2 more awarded or in tender, against a target of 25 by 2030. 49 KTPA bamboo 2G ethanol plant inaugurated Sept 2025; NRL green hydrogen plant of 2.4 KTPA (Rs 138 crore) due by end-2026.

guidance_outlook: Production: 4 MMtoe achievable with ~100 wells drilled per year; long-term target 12 MMtoe by 2030 (from 10).
Gas: 3.35 BCM guided for FY27; ~5 BCM targeted by FY28 once Duliajan feeder line and DNPL expansion are commissioned.
NRL: CDU/VDU ~mid-July 2026 (~400 TMT output after that, mostly diesel), DHDT about a month later, PFCC/RPTU by Dec-Jan, full 9 MMTPA by March 2027 (stabilised by March 2028).
Capex: rollover of ~Rs 10,000 crore a year for ~100 onshore wells per year, plus shallow-water offshore drilling.

Offshore: deep-water well targeted for spud around June 2027; four-plus-four deep-water wells at ~Rs 1,200 crore each (Rs 4,800-5,000 crore), contingent on Samudra Manthan Mission sponsorship. Shallow-water wells ~Rs 800 crore each.
NRL excise duty: ~Rs 3,000 crore accrued in FY26, with 50% NE excise benefit and no sunset clause at 9 MMTPA; management expects calibration if FOB HSD prices fall.
capex_capacity: Drilling: 74 wells in FY26 (record); released drillable location inventory ~218 vs ~45 earlier; average Assam shelf depth ~4,300 m.

Offshore: deepest well (6,000 m, Kerala-Konkan) at ~3,400 m; Andaman well 3 drilling complete and testing; KG DSF appraisal well underway; gas occurrence in Andaman well 2 under appraisal with 600 sq km 3D seismic.
Feeder/evacuation: Duliajan feeder line (3.5 MMSCMD) authorised; PNGRB approval Feb 2026, mechanical completion FY28, offtake up 40%.
Gas capacity: production ~8 MMSCMD, ramp-up path to 13-15 MMSCMD with 15-18 pure gas wells identified.
Crude import pipeline Paradip-Numaligarh (9 MMTPA) 92% physically complete as of 30 April 2026; 99% ROU acquired.
demand_pricing: Realisation: crude at $69/bbl in FY26, lowest in 5 years; government moves on royalty and post-wellhead cost realisation cited as cash-flow support.

New well gas: 1.5 MMSCMD allocated to NRL, priced at 20% premium over APM, but only accrues once NRL is commissioned and allocation is confirmed; allocation priority runs CGD, fertiliser, refinery/petchem, then power.
Gas to NE CGD: ~50,000 SCMD allocated to NE Gas Distribution and Purbabharati Gas Distribution as NRL reseller.
Product demand: management cites 7-8% growth in refined product consumption; NRL export via Indo-Bangladesh pipeline optional, not the basis for 9 MMTPA.
Competition/partners: TotalEnergies signed technology service agreement (Nov 2025) for offshore seismic and exploration support, with a say in investment decisions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the offshore exploration capex and how will the capability gap be addressed?
qa_highlights.answer: Shallow-water well ~Rs 800 crore; deep-water wells ~Rs 1,200 crore each, four plus four wells (~Rs 4,800-5,000 crore), contingent on Samudra Manthan sponsorship. Government also identified Rs 3,200 crore for four stratigraphic wells jointly with ONGC.

qa_highlights.question: NRL excise duty benefit in FY26 and impact of recent duty cut?
qa_highlights.answer: ~Rs 3,000 crore accrued in FY26; no sunset clause on 50% NE excise benefit at 9 MMTPA. Management expects excise to be recalibrated against HSD FOB prices if they fall.

qa_highlights.question: NRL 9 MMTPA viability, and terms of the TotalEnergies arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: Viability rests on domestic demand (7-8% growth) and NE/mainland logistics, with Panchgram, Singimari and Jogighopa depots and Siliguri tankage. TotalEnergies is a service agreement, with Total able to weigh in on investment decisions.

qa_highlights.question: NRL timelines, first product output, and capex spent/remaining?
qa_highlights.answer: Mother units by end-July; ~400 TMT output after that, mostly diesel. Full 9 MMT by March 2027, stabilised March 2028. Expansion capex ~Rs 46,000 crore including PPU (Rs 7,200 crore).

qa_highlights.question: FY27 production, gas and capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: 4 MMT with 100 wells; gas 3.35 BCM in FY27 and ~5 BCM 18 months out. Rollover capex ~Rs 10,000 crore per year.

qa_highlights.question: Current production exit rate and gas ramp path?
qa_highlights.answer: Current crude ~82,200 bpd, a record. Gas ~8 MMSCMD now; management says 13-15 MMSCMD possible with new pipelines, with first accrual only on allocation and commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: Mozambique incremental equity outflow?
qa_highlights.answer: ~$1.8 billion already committed; ~$300 million escalation pending CCEA. Further phases to be assessed after FID.

risks_watch: Samudra Manthan Mission notification and sponsorship mechanism still pending; deep-water capex is uncertain until notified.
NRL expansion timeline: DNPL commissioning depends on a 7-day NRL shutdown deferred by Middle East crisis; CDU/VDU mechanical completion due mid-July 2026.
New well gas premium (20%) depends on government allocation; accrual timing tied to CGD saturation in NE.
Excise benefit (~Rs 3,000 crore in FY26) may be recalibrated if product prices fall.
Production risk from economic blockades (lost ~0.1 MMt in FY26) and natural decline of 10-12% a year.
Mozambique cost escalation (~$300 million) awaiting CCEA approval.
key_quotes: Dr. Ranjit Rath, Chairman and Managing Director, Oil India Limited and Chairman of Numaligarh Refinery Limited.

The idea is that through a mechanism while the data collection in terms of 2D and 3D seismic data will be sponsored by the Government, the Government would also sponsor the deep water and ultra deep water wells which we intend to drill in our exploration acreage.

So, we would really come to know once it is notified, how many numbers of wells government is going to sponsor 100%, how many wells government is going to sponsor 50% or precisely how the mechanism would be.
So, excise to my opinion is going to get calibrated based on the overall FOB of HSD which is the driving force for the refinery transfer price which happens between NRL and the OMCs.
Now the question is this New well gas needs to be allocated by government.
533106|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on production records, NRL commissioning and offshore ambition, repeatedly stressing government support and "on track" delivery. Cautious or evasive on Samudra Manthan Mission mechanics, deep-water well sponsorship terms, and NRL excise recalibration, which management repeatedly deferred until notification or government approval.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: GRM was 1.6x prior year and NRL excise benefit (~Rs 3,000 cr) supports refining margin, but crude at $69/bbl is a 5-year low and consolidated EBITDA margin was ~36% with EBITDA up only 5% against a 3% rise in income.

rows.when: CDU/VDU mid-July 2026; full 9 MMTPA NRL by March 2027

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 4 MMtoe production in FY27 (vs 6.64 MMtoe reported in FY26 total incl. gas, so the guide is on an oil-equivalent basis still to be reconciled) on 100 wells, with gas at 3.35 BCM and 82,200+ bpd crude exit rate, but 10-12% natural decline and blockade risk are headwinds.

rows.label: New product launch
