rows.label: Samudra Manthan Mission sponsorship for deep-water wells
rows.why: Four-plus-four deep-water wells at ~Rs 1,200 cr each (Rs 4,800-5,000 cr) are contingent on the mission notification and sponsorship mechanism, which is still pending.

rows.label: Mozambique LNG two trains 13 MMTPA
rows.why: Force majeure lifted Nov 2025, ~$1.8 billion already committed, with ~$300 million cost escalation pending CCEA approval.

rows.label: Gas to NE CGD and NRL new-well gas allocation
rows.why: ~50,000 SCMD allocated to NE Gas Distribution and Purbabharati, and 1.5 MMSCMD new-well gas to NRL at 20% premium over APM, accruing only on commissioning.

tone.note: Management was confident on production records, NRL commissioning and the 9 MMTPA by March 2027 target, but cautious and deferring on Samudra Manthan sponsorship mechanics and NRL excise recalibration; analysts pressed on NRL 9 MMTPA viability and Mozambique incremental equity.

533106|2026-06.headline: Oil India Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose to INR2,870 crore from INR813 crore, on record EBITDA of INR4,605 crore and crude realisation of USD98.73/bbl.
533106|2026-06.overview: Standalone operating revenue hit a record INR7,958 crore and EBITDA a record INR4,605 crore, with margin above 54%. Crude output was 0.95 MMT, up 11%+ YoY, and daily output peaked at 10,921 MT on 27 June, later 11,017 MT on 3 August. Subsidiary NRL ran at 105% capacity utilisation with a GRM of USD35.95/bbl (about USD33 ex-inventory gain), and consolidated PAT was INR4,026 crore. Management guided to roughly 1 MMT crude per quarter and about 3.9–4 MMT for FY27, and gas evacuation hinges on DNPL/IGGL connectivity.

segments.name: Upstream (standalone crude and gas)
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 production was 1.707 MMBoE, with crude at 0.95 MMT (+11%+ YoY) and gas up 0.4% QoQ. Gas off-take has been constrained at about 2.93 BCM by evacuation limits, and management targets 3.8 BCM next year and about 5 BCM by FY29.

segments.name: NRL (refining, material subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation was 105%, distillate yield 87%, and GRM USD35.95/bbl vs USD5.02 a year earlier. Management said about USD2 of the GRM was inventory gain, and OMC discounts under SAED were netted off.

guidance_outlook: Crude production: about 1 MMT per quarter from now on, roughly 3.9 MMT for FY27 with a possible touch of 4 MMT; FY29 target of about 4.2 MMT from main producing areas, with upside from near-field exploration.
Capex: FY27 budget is INR8,600 crore (to be revised at the next review); Q1 spend was about INR3,050 crore, including INR1,230 crore on exploratory drilling.
Wells: FY27 target of 100 wells (42 exploratory, 57 development), up from 74 in FY26; a further 10% rise is intended for FY28.

NRL: CDU/VDU, DHDT and SRU to be commissioned by Oct–Nov 2026, remaining units by 31 March 2027, reaching about 75% of 9 MMT rated capacity by Q4 FY28; Paradip–Numaligarh pipeline mechanical completion targeted October and commissioning by December 2026.
Gas: 200 m connection within the NRL campus (2–3 months) to link DNPL with IGGL; DFL feeder line about 20% complete; big jump in evacuation expected from Q1 FY28 and about 5 BCM by FY29.
GST on royalty: about INR2,500 crore (excluding interest) is already provided; payment to be made, with no prospective interest. The Assam land tax is a contingent liability with no P&L impact.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR3,050 crore: survey INR450 crore, exploratory drilling INR1,230 crore, development drilling INR700 crore, capital equipment and projects INR350 crore, subsidiaries/JVs/overseas INR350 crore. FY26 actual capex was INR13,026 crore.
Wells drilled in Q1: 17 (7 exploratory, 10 development). Drilling history: FY25 22 exploratory and 35 development; FY26 22 exploratory and 52 development.

Andaman: Vijayapuram-1 spend about INR1,000–1,050 crore; hydro-frac testing in August; fourth Andaman well by a jack-up rig targeted for December 2026; 600 sq km of new 3D seismic to be processed by October.

Deep water (Mahanadi and KG): 4,200 line km and 5,300 sq km of 3D acquired; first deep-water rig expected June–July 2027, second by March 2028. Government reimbursement of up to INR675 crore per well is proposed under the Samudra Manthan scheme.

NRL expansion: about INR30,000 crore spent to date, with INR34,000–35,000 crore expected for the refinery project and another INR7,200–7,300 crore for the PPU project. NRL debt is about INR19,000 crore.
demand_pricing: Crude realisation was USD98.73/bbl and gas USD7.19/MMBtu; new-well gas is priced outside APM, and incremental volumes will all be new-well gas.

NRL's GRM is about USD33 excluding the roughly USD2 inventory gain. Diesel and petrol discounts to OMCs under SAED ran at INR13/l to INR3/l for petrol and INR10/l to nil for diesel during the quarter, and have reappeared as a monthly recalibration.

Gas off-take from BCPL is stable at about 1.25–1.35 MMSCMD (about 4.25 MMSCMD returned to the grid by Oil India). NEEPCO is cutting gas use in favour of hydro, and excise benefit fell as government calibrated excise to hold retail prices.
NRL operating cost is about USD4.5–5/bbl, targeted to fall to about USD3.5/bbl as expansion units stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current crude run-rate, and can production sustain the 10,921 MT/day level?
qa_highlights.answer: Director Operations said the company expects about 1 MMT per quarter from here, citing workover, well intervention and optimisation; output reached 11,017 MT/day on 3 August.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for gas ramp-up from 2.93 BCM to about 5 BCM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 and H1 FY28 would be flat to slow; the big jump is expected from Q1 FY28 once the 200 m NRL link and DFL/IGGL are complete, with about 1.5 MMSCMD of extra headroom from DNPL capacity expansion and 3.5–4 MMSCMD of evacuation planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised NRL GRM, and what is the exploration capex outlook given the government support?
qa_highlights.answer: NRL GRM was about USD35 including about USD2 inventory gain (about USD33 ex-gain). Exploration: 100 wells targeted in FY27 and a 10%+ rise intended thereafter, with deep-water programme funded in part by government schemes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NRL expansion status and the Paradip–Numaligarh pipeline timing?
qa_highlights.answer: CDU/VDU mechanically complete, with three units to be commissioned by Oct–Nov 2026 and the rest by 31 March 2027; pipeline ROU is secured except about 8 km, with commissioning by December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position across the group?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone: USD1.4 bn loan for Mozambique. Singapore subsidiary: USD500 mn bond due May 2027. NRL: about INR19,000 crore. Total group debt about INR37,233 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did contract costs rise, and what is the GST-on-royalty payment outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract cost rose by about INR146 crore QoQ to INR615 crore, mainly offshore G&G costs. About INR2,500 crore GST on royalty (excl. interest) is already provided, to be paid with no prospective interest; the Assam land tax is a contingent liability.

risks_watch: Gas evacuation remains the binding constraint: BCPL and NEEPCO off-take is seasonal and the DFL/IGGL and 200 m NRL link are still pending.
NRL's GRM is inflated by SAED-linked discounts and an inventory gain of about USD2/bbl; the normalised GRM is about USD33 and the discount level is calibrated monthly.
Andaman Vijayapuram-1 and -3 testing is still pending; a write-down or capitalised-cost review is possible after the September decision.
Assam land tax case is being withdrawn via the state legislature; the contingent liability is removed only once withdrawal is effective.
Q2 gas volumes could dip with monsoon and tea-garden seasonality from October; exploration cost (G&G) inflated opex in Q1.
533106|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on production records and NRL operations, with repeated emphasis on execution and integrated planning. qa_highlights.question: Why is the dividend being introduced, and what does it signal about cash generation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said surplus cash will rise as BD investment normalises relative to cash generation, so dividends will be made consistent and growing. The FY27 dividend is modest.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 collections and revenue recognition step up?

533150|2026-09.headline: Godrej Properties Q2 FY27 bookings fell 6% YoY to INR8,008 crore, but sustenance sales rose 83% to INR5,054 crore and collections hit INR5,318 crore.
533150|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 bookings were INR8,008 crore from 3,658 units (6.2 mn sq ft), down 6% YoY and 7% QoQ, while H1 bookings grew 7% to INR16,669 crore. Sustenance sales were the standout at INR5,054 crore. Collections rose 31% YoY to a record Q2 of INR5,318 crore and operating cash flow was INR1,584 crore. Reported P&L fell sharply: EBITDA down 72% to INR171 crore and net profit down 62% to INR154 crore, which management attributed to back-ended deliveries and JV exit accounting (Mahalunge, Orris). Management guided H2 bookings of INR22,500-25,000 crore and a strong Q3 launch pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA and net profit fall sharply despite higher sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajendra Khetawat said the Mahalunge JV became a 100% owned project after the partner exit, so the bulk of profit had been recognised earlier through DM fees and overheads, which led to near-equal sales and cost of sales. The Orris settlement also picked up losses on consolidation in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How long will sustenance sales stay high and what is the launch vs sustenance mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Pandey said H2 launches will likely outperform sustenance, and the 60-40 launch-sustenance mix is a guide that can flip if launches slip. Sustenance strength reflects a deliberate push after Gurgaon and Mumbai launches slipped.

qa_highlights.answer: Pirojsha Godrej said competition is ongoing but opportunities meeting return thresholds are available, and BD will remain opportunistic. Gaurav Pandey said one or two deals could close in the quarter if terms fit.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company near FCF-positive status in H2?

Management reiterated the 200 bps margin improvement target over the long term but declined to say how long near-term inflation pressure would last. Energy (LPG/PNG) was quantified at 100-120 bps, which the company said it has passed on through pricing, while wage and labour-code costs were discussed as further headwinds.

533155|2026-06.headline: Jubilant FoodWorks Q1 FY27: Domino's LFL 2.5% on high base; Popeyes LFL cited at ~45%, EBITDA margin target of 200 bps reiterated.

rows.why: Domino's LFL guided to 5-7% for rest of FY27 from 2.5% in Q1 on an 11.6% base, with Q2 FY27 expected better than Q1; Popeyes LFL ~40-45%, though delivery volume softness after price hikes and the INR 99 MOV cut are risks.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management held INR 750-900 crore guidance in line with the previous two years and said supply chain capex is past peak, so no new capex programme was flagged; utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said ~100 bps of the 200 bps margin target is ahead of track and LFL could exceed 7% on the two-quarter average math, but management held guidance rather than raising it.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 and Q4 face tougher base comparisons for Domino's LFL needing 5-7%, and input costs (LPG, cheese, oil, labour code, minimum wages in 14-15 states) could widen the headwind.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Popeyes product innovation (six chicken wing flavours, bun focus) and Wednesday dine-in offers are ongoing, but no specific new product or launch date was given.

rows.label: Calibrated price increases if input inflation persists
rows.why: Management will take calibrated price increases if LPG, cheese, oil, chicken and labour inflation persists, after ~140 bps taken in Q1 at 1.5-2% per hike with no visible volume impact.

rows.label: Dine-in and takeaway LFL recovery to flat
rows.why: Dedicated dine-in team and 2,500 neighbourhood stores; early reversal seen only on Wednesdays via Best Deals Ever Wednesday offer, and the goal is flat LFL in this channel.

rows.label: Supply chain and commissary efficiencies
rows.why: Supply chain build-out is past peak and new commissaries (Mumbai factory commissioned March) are lowering supply chain costs, offsetting part of LPG, cheese and labour inflation.

tone.note: Management was confident on Popeyes momentum, the 5-7% Domino's LFL path and the 200 bps margin target, but cautious on input costs and calibrated pricing; analysts pushed on Popeyes LFL normalisation, per-store labour costs after minimum wage hikes, and margin headwinds.

533156|2026-06.headline: Vascon Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to INR152 crores (from INR221 crores) and PAT to INR2 crores (from INR22 crores), on EPC execution delays.
533156|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations fell about 31% YoY to INR152 crores, driven by lower EPC execution from cash-flow-stalled government projects. Consolidated EBITDA was INR10 crores versus INR34 crores in Q1 FY26, which included an INR18 crores one-time investment gain; adjusted for that, EBITDA was about INR15 crores at roughly 6% margin. Management said the EPC segment stayed profitable at about 9% EBITDA margin, while real estate booked INR4 crores revenue and a INR4 crores EBITDA loss. Management guided to a recovery from Q3 and reiterated the FY27 revenue target of INR1,200 crores, while net debt rose to about INR152 crores.

FY27 EPC new order intake target INR1,500-2,000 crores.
Real estate: target annual booking value INR1,200-1,500 crores by FY31; management expects to double real estate revenue over 3-4 years from a ~INR100 crores base.
Real estate OC targets this year for Coimbatore, Tower of Ascend (Kharadi) in Q3/Q4 and Orchid Santacruz in Q4 (stretch), which would drive revenue recognition.
Working capital cycle expected to normalise from ~65-70 days back toward ~45 days; EPC short-term debt expected to roll over in 6-8 months.
capex_capacity: Sanctioned banking limits ~INR760 crores as of June 30, 2026, of which ~INR355 crores unutilised.
INR80 crores preferential warrant issue over up to 18 months; first tranche (minimum 25%) received; proceeds ~60-70% for real estate, rest for EPC working capital and corporate purposes.

Real estate pipeline: Tranquil Heights (Powai) launched in second week of June; Prakash (Santacruz West) has RERA approval, launch shortly; Tower of Future (Baner, Pune) and Ajanta (Kharadi) in near-term pipeline; together ~1.74 million sq ft, ~INR2,000 crores sales value (~INR1,000 crores attributable to Vascon).

Management stated gross profit on EPC remains 13-15%, and real estate gross margin is 25-30%.
Real estate sales: 30,690 sq ft new bookings and ~INR20 crores collections in Q1.
Competition in Mumbai redevelopment described as intense; management targets projects with GDV of INR250-300 crores and focuses on 1-2 acre sites in Western and Central suburbs.
Adani Infra engagement on 3-4 projects at an early design stage; management does not expect construction start in the next 6 months, and revenue may slip to Q4 or next year.

Royal Rides (Goa, ~INR225 crores ropeway-related order): only ~INR15 crores recognised; management assumes no revenue for the next 3 quarters. Reliance order was cancelled by mutual agreement after design and construction method changes.

qa_highlights.question: How much real estate construction spend is pending, and what free cash flow can come from sold and unsold projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said real estate gross margins remain 25-30%, with ~INR300 crores of pending construction cost against ~INR400 crores unsold inventory value plus ~INR116 crores pending collections, implying ~INR220 crores free cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Why has debt risen sharply since March 2025 and where did the cash go?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed the rise mainly to EPC: CC limit utilisation increased on milestone-based projects, and net working capital cycle stretched from ~45 to ~65-70 days over the last six months. Real estate also needed equity infusion.

qa_highlights.question: Which government projects face cash-flow issues and when will they ramp up?
qa_highlights.answer: Bihar Supaul and Sindhudurg (Maharashtra) projects; client cash flows now available and ramp-up expected within 1-2 months.

qa_highlights.question: Which real estate projects will recognise revenue and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Coimbatore and Tower of Ascend (Kharadi) OC targeted in Q3/Q4; Orchid Santacruz targeted for Q4 only if achieved.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Vedanta project, Royal Rides and Vashi Hospital?
qa_highlights.answer: Vedanta has restarted with scale-up and is expected to finish this FY; Vashi Hospital expected to start in the coming quarter; Royal Rides stalled with no client go-ahead, assumed zero revenue for next 3 quarters, but still a live order.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 INR1,200 crore revenue target still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated INR1,200 crores, with EPC at ~INR1,000 crores and real estate INR200 crores-plus, with Q3/Q4 carrying ~70% of EPC revenue.

risks_watch: Ramp-up of EPC execution: Bihar Supaul and Sindhudurg projects were said to restart within 1-2 months of client cash flows; watch Q2 EPC revenue against the 30% H1 phasing assumption.

Real estate revenue depends on OC timing: Coimbatore and Tower of Ascend (Kharadi) in Q3/Q4 and Orchid Santacruz in Q4 only if achieved; any slip pushes the INR200 crores-plus real estate contribution further out.

Net debt rise to ~INR152 crores and working capital cycle stretched from ~45 to ~65-70 days; watch whether the cycle normalises toward 45 days and whether short-term EPC debt rolls over in 6-8 months.

Royal Rides (~INR225 crores order, ~INR15 crores recognised) assumed at zero revenue for three quarters; Vashi Hospital expected to start next quarter; Adani Infra projects unlikely to start construction within 6 months.

Real estate growth target of INR1,200-1,500 crores annual booking value by FY31 requires new project acquisitions; no new transaction assigned yet, and management expects to convert opportunities over 2-3 quarters.
key_quotes: We consider this primarily a timing -related execution issue rather than a structural concern with our order book.
So this financial year, we still target to achieve INR1,200 crores because we do expect INR200 crores plus revenue coming from real estate as well, which did not come in last year.
It has been one of the worst quarters we've had over the last 3 to 4 years, but I think there's nothing structurally wrong that has led to that.
I wish I knew the answer to that question.

533169|2026-03.headline: Man Infra FY26 consolidated PAT after minority interest of INR201 crores; FY27 launches targeted at INR5,500 crores GDV and sales ambition of over INR5,000 crores across FY27-FY28.
533169|2026-03.overview: FY26 was described as a consolidation year: sales of about INR1,800 crores, collections of about INR990 crores and over 5 lakh sq ft sold, with consolidated revenue from operations of about INR630 crores. Q4 FY26 sales were about INR438 crores and collections about INR279 crores, with consolidated PAT after minority interest of INR43 crores on total income of INR187 crores. Management guided to a 35-40% rise in revenue recognition in FY27, driven by about 1 million sq ft of launches and near-complete projects, and reiterated a Vision 2030 goal of doubling GDV to over INR35,000 crores. Balance sheet was reported as net debt-free with net worth of about INR2,266 crores and liquidity of about INR686 crores against debt of about INR58 crores.

segments.name: Real estate (Mumbai)
segments.commentary: GDV portfolio above INR17,500 crores with balance sales pipeline of INR13,300 crores; management says about INR4,000 crores of the GDV is already sold and the rest is unsold. New Tardeo project adds about INR2,000 crores GDV and about 3 lakh sq ft saleable carpet; South Mumbai GDV above INR8,000 crores.

segments.name: Real estate (US, MICL Global)
segments.commentary: Estimated aggregate GDV of about US$1.4 billion across ongoing and one completed development in Florida. Minority stake acquired in West Avenue, Miami Beach project with estimated GDV above US$1 billion and over 100 units.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Current EPC order book about INR392 crores to be executed over 3-4 years. Upcoming developments have about 1 crore sq ft construction area, of which about 50% expected to add to the EPC order book once FY27 launches occur. Port segment de-emphasised; management says it will bid selectively.

segments.name: Interest income on project investments
segments.commentary: Cumulative MICL Group investment across project entities about INR1,461 crores; management presents the interest income earned as a business income contributing to 'other income'.

guidance_outlook: FY27 launch pipeline of about INR5,500 crores GDV (about 1 million sq ft), including Marine Lines, Tardeo, BKC and Pali Hill; launches to be timed around Diwali for Marine Lines and Nov-Dec for Tardeo 2.0.
Combined sales ambition of over INR5,000 crores across FY27 and FY28; management targets not less than INR2,500 crores in FY27 with a roughly 50-50 split.
Revenue recognition expected to grow about 35-40% in FY27 versus FY26, with Ghatkopar, Dahisar and Atmosphere projects nearing completion.
Over 1 million sq ft carpet area to be delivered over the next 6-18 months; Aaradhya One Park targeted for completion by March 2027; Atmosphere Tower G expected within 18 months.
Vision 2030 goal to double development portfolio to over INR35,000 crores GDV, with management aiming to achieve it before 2031.
Management expects FY25 revenue and profit levels to be surpassed over time; no price appreciation assumed in project feasibility.
capex_capacity: Aaradhya Parkwood (Dahisar): first two towers of 35 storeys to be delivered within the next 6-18 months; project of over 1,000 units across four towers is about 90% sold.
Aaradhya Avaan (South Mumbai): 38-storey members tower delivered in under 2.5 years; final top floors launched and an in-building experience centre opened.
Aaradhya One Park (Ghatkopar East): 11 towers on about 3.2 acres, targeted completion by March 2027.
Atmosphere O2 Mulund Tower G: 47 storeys, about 70% sold, expected completion over the next 18 months.
Marine Lines: land fully vacated, rehab and sale tower construction started with IOD and CC received.
Tardeo 2.0 stand-alone project acquired; permissions applied for and launch targeted for Nov-Dec.
demand_pricing: Management says it has not assumed price appreciation in feasibility and does not expect a meaningful price rise in Mumbai; it expects volume absorption to hold.
Sales momentum cited: Ghatkopar more than 50% sold, Jade Park (Vile Parle) 50%+ sold, Tardeo above 65% sold, Artek Park (BKC) more than 20% sold within about 3 months of launch.
Aaradhya Avaan experience centre recorded over 200 visitors, with a strong weekly run-rate.
Management says it is pushing ticket sizes into the INR100-200 crore range is avoided, and that larger 3-BHK units (up to about 1,500 sq ft) are selling first.
Management sees consumers 'rethinking' purchases amid the geopolitical situation and is delaying the Marine Lines launch for better sentiment.
New MS Collection Residences brand launched for ultra-luxury boutique sea-view projects, separate from the Aaradhya community-building brand.

qa_highlights.question: Project-wise reconciliation of bookings, collections, completion % and revenue recognised against INR630 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined on the call and said details would be shared post-call with the investor relations team.

qa_highlights.question: Risk of inventory overhang from ultra-luxury launches in South Mumbai over 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said MICL is not building INR100-200 crore tickets and its ticket sizes are comfortable for the micro-markets, so sales velocity risk is low.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 presales target versus the INR5,000 crore FY27-28 ambition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited INR5,500 crore of launch pipeline for FY27 and a target of at least INR2,500 crore, with a 50-50 split across the two years and no new projects assumed.

qa_highlights.question: Unsold versus already-sold inventory in the INR17,000 crore GDV, and revenue trajectory for FY27-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR4,000 crore of GDV is sold and the rest unsold; FY27 revenue recognition is expected to grow 35-40%, with no separate FY28-29 numbers given.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins be higher in ultra-luxury projects with lower asset turns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said better margins are the intention in ultra-luxury projects and will show in coming years.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company double GDV, and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is in talks with more than 10 housing societies, with a mix of JDA, JV and redevelopment and a planned commercial portfolio; funding comes from ongoing project cash flows and surplus from future launches, with no annual spend figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company moving away from EPC and ports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ports remain an option when good opportunities arise, but real estate is the main focus; EPC work from its own 1 crore sq ft pipeline or partner projects will continue.

risks_watch: Revenue recognition is back-ended and depends on OC timing and launch execution; the company did not provide a project-wise reconciliation of bookings, collections and revenue.
Launch timing risk: Marine Lines and Tardeo 2.0 are pushed to Diwali and Nov-Dec, and management cited geopolitical and macro sentiment as a reason for waiting.
Revenue depends on the INR5,500 crore launch pipeline and the INR2,500 crore FY27 sales target, which are not yet approved in all cases.
Concentration in ultra-luxury, larger-ticket South Mumbai projects with longer timelines could increase revenue and earnings volatility.
Other income includes interest on about INR1,461 crore of project-entity investments and is presented as business income; the split between operating and non-operating income was not disclosed.
Business development targets (doubling GDV to INR35,000 crore) depend on winning 10+ society redevelopments currently in negotiation.
US exposure through MICL Global (about US$1.4 billion GDV) was not detailed on earnings or capital deployed.

533169|2026-06.headline: Man Infra Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 29% YoY to ₹72 crore on revenue up 8% to ₹218 crore; management reiterates 25%+ FY27 PAT growth guidance.

Cash and cash equivalents rose to ₹768 crore at June 2026 from ₹686 crore at FY26-end, with borrowings of ₹78 crore, which management said are mostly partner contributions in joint ventures. Pre-sales in the quarter were about 85,000 sq ft, or roughly ₹290 crore, which management acknowledged is low, attributing the gap to launches that have not yet happened (Marine Lines, Berkeley House). Management kept its FY27 PAT growth guidance of over 25% and its target of ₹5,000 crore cumulative pre-sales over two years, and reiterated a ₹35,000 crore group GDV goal by 2031.

533179|2026-06.headline: Persistent to acquire Nagarro at EV €1.27bn (€81/share cash) and signed a ~$650M, 6.5-year net-new deal adding ~$125M annual value.
533179|2026-06.overview: Management held a Sunday call (28 June 2026) announcing two items: a net-new strategic deal with an existing large US-headquartered customer worth roughly $125M annually and about $650M over 6.5 years, and a voluntary public takeover offer for Nagarro at €81 per share in cash. The Nagarro offer implies an equity value of about €1bn and EV of €1.27bn, funded by a committed €1.4bn Barclays bridge facility, with a 50% plus one share minimum acceptance. Persistent has already secured 21% via a share purchase agreement, and management board members intend to tender about 13-14%. Closing is expected around Q4 CY2026 or early Q1 CY2027, subject to regulatory approvals. No Q1 FY27 financial results were discussed on this call.

financial_highlights.metric: Nagarro EBIT margin CY25 / Q1 CY26

financial_highlights.value: 140% to undisturbed close (25-26 June); 94% to 3-month VWAP

segments.name: Persistent (standalone)
segments.commentary: Five-year revenue CAGR of about 23.9%, with North America about 81%+ of revenue and Europe about 8-8.5%. Team of 27,500 across 21 countries.

segments.name: Nagarro (target)
segments.commentary: 5-year revenue CAGR of 18.4%, with about 35% of revenue from North America and about 18,500 staff (13,500 in India). Strengths cited in SAP, Siemens, OpenAI reseller and industrial/consumer verticals; management says constant-currency growth was over 5% recently.

segments.name: Combined group
segments.commentary: Pro forma about $2.9bn revenue, 46,000+ staff across 40+ countries; mix of North America 62%, Europe 22%, Rest of World 16%. Management targets European revenue of 15%+ and $5bn aspiration by FY31.

guidance_outlook: Leverage (net debt / combined EBITDA) at close expected at 1.9x-2.5x depending on acceptance, reducing to about 1x by FY2030.
Transaction expected to be cash EPS accretive and reported EPS accretive in Year 1 excluding one-time transaction expenses.
Goodwill vs other intangibles split about 70:30; intangibles amortised over 8 years.
Acquisition-related bridge interest at Euribor plus 175-250bps, roughly 4.1%-4.8% (4.1%-4.5% quoted in Q&A).
Revenue and cost synergies to be detailed only after regulatory approvals; management says margins will be maintained or improved.
New large deal is accretive to revenue and margin from Q2 onwards with no major ramp-up needed.

Public offer timeline: BaFin filing within 4 weeks, offer clearance in 10 working days to 2 weeks, 4-week acceptance period plus optional 2-week extension; Persistent AGM late July to seek shareholder approval. Squeeze-out possible over about 2 years; no domination agreement intended for 2 years.
capex_capacity: Transaction is fully debt-funded via a committed €1.4bn Barclays bridge facility, which also covers Nagarro refinancing if required, backed by a Persistent parent corporate guarantee.
Management said it does not intend a QIP or further dilution; private equity participation at asset level is being considered but no decision taken.
Management said it has moved from capex-heavy models to an opex model, funding working capital to support cash generation.
demand_pricing: Net new large deal from an existing US-headquartered technology customer: ~$125M annually and ~$650M+ over 6.5 years; customer name not disclosed under NDA.
Persistent has two $100M+ accounts, with a third approaching; the combined entity has 180 logos above $1M (Nagarro's largest customer under $50M) and over 350 $1M+ accounts.
Customer overlap between the two companies is in the single digits, with fewer than 10 significant overlapping customers.

Management said T&M model will decline over time but is not dead; Nagarro's T&M share was cited as 65-68% by analysts. Cannibalisation of T&M revenue acknowledged, with SASVA platform cited as a response.

qa_highlights.question: Has there been incremental due diligence on Nagarro's books given BaFin queries, and why is the multiple at a premium?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legal and tax diligence on BaFin queries (carve-out from Allgeier and accounting principles) found no impact on performance; the premium was described as reasonable for a control transaction.

qa_highlights.question: Will Nagarro run independently for two years post-closing, and why no cash-plus-share structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Persistent will work with management and aim for a squeeze-out over about 2 years, with no hurry. Management said a share swap was not feasible under German public-to-private dynamics; no QIP or dilution planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ramp and margin profile of the large deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is net new with little ramp needed, end-to-end product engineering and support, accretive from Q2, at a fairly healthy margin above company average.

qa_highlights.question: How will the combined entity sustain growth given Nagarro's slow growth and the long tail of accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to cross-selling of ERP/CX and mining of 180 $1M+ logos, with tail-account rationalisation possible to release SG&A. It said Nagarro's recent growth was affected by distraction from its take-private process.

qa_highlights.question: Decision tree on acceptance: what if below 50%, and what follows above 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Persistent holds 21% via SPA; management board commitment of about 13-14% takes it near 35%, with another 35-40% considered broadly committed. Management sees 50%+ as very likely; majority gives control of the supervisory board.

risks_watch: Regulatory approvals (including RBI and various EU jurisdictions) and BaFin clearance of the offer document; close targeted Q4 CY26 to early Q1 CY27.
Acceptance level versus the 50%+1 minimum; leverage moves between 1.9x and 2.5x depending on acceptance.
Nagarro's revenue flat for about two years, with several vertical declines (horizontal tech, energy/utilities, telecom, travel) flagged by analysts.
Integration of a two-year squeeze-out path with minority shareholders; synergy plan and value-creation plan not yet shared.
Cash conversion and debt servicing of roughly €1.4bn of acquisition debt, plus the T&M model and AI cannibalisation risk.
533179|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and assertive on strategic fit, growth and margin ambitions, but deliberately evasive on specifics pending regulatory approvals (no synergy numbers, value-creation plan, or customer names). Pushback was given to analysts on Nagarro's EBIT margins and the premium paid.

we believe we have paid a reasonable premium for a control transaction.
we do not believe that the combined entity will be at any significant lower margins than what Persistent has today.
We don't intend doing any QIP, just to be clear for everyone. We don't intend diluting our stake at this point in time.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.when: post close, Q4 CY26 to early Q1 CY27
rows.why: Management guides cash and reported EPS accretion in Year 1 excluding one-time transaction expenses, but gave no organic revenue guidance and no Q1 FY27 results were discussed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Leverage of 1.9x-2.5x at close on ~€1.4bn acquisition debt at Euribor+175-250bps (~4.1%-4.8%) raises interest cost and execution risk; Nagarro revenue flat for ~2 years and T&M share 65-68% faces cannibalisation.

rows.why: Signed ~$650M over 6.5 years (~$125M annually) with an existing US technology customer, accretive from Q2 with little ramp needed and a margin above company average.

rows.label: Nagarro take-private closing
rows.when: Q4 CY26 to early Q1 CY27
rows.why: Voluntary offer at €81/share (EV €1.27bn), 21% already secured via SPA plus ~13-14% board tender intent, with 50%+1 minimum acceptance; management sees 50%+ as very likely, subject to RBI and EU approvals.

rows.label: Leverage down to ~1x by FY2030
rows.why: Net debt/combined EBITDA of 1.9x-2.5x at close, expected to reduce to about 1x by FY2030 as cash generation repays the €1.4bn bridge debt.

tone.note: Management was confident on the $125M net-new deal, accretion and the 50%+ acceptance path, but evasive on synergies, value-creation plan and customer names pending approvals; analysts pushed on Nagarro's EBIT margins, the premium paid, and T&M cannibalisation.

533179|2026-09.headline: Persistent Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to USD 487.6M, but EBIT margin fell to 15% and reported PAT dropped 25.4% on Nagarro deal costs.
533179|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew 7.8% QoQ and 20% YoY in USD to USD 487.6M, the 26th sequential quarter of growth, with rupee revenue of Rs 46,639M (+30.3% YoY). EBIT margin was 15% (down 100 bps QoQ and 130 bps YoY) as wage hikes and a 90 bps amortisation hit from the large software deal offset ESOP and currency tailwinds. Reported PAT of Rs 3,515.1M (7.5% margin) was hit by about 3.1% from Nagarro transaction costs, while operating PAT rose 5% YoY to Rs 4,951.5M. Bookings slowed: TCV was USD 633.5M and ACV USD 481M, with management citing deal slippage and a decision-making slowdown linked to Middle East dynamics. The Nagarro acquisition is progressing, with about 94% of shares tendered and closing guided to Q4 CY26 or Q1 CY27.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 22.5% YoY in USD terms.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue declined 8.5% YoY, attributed to one acquired key client ramping down and one fixed-price engagement completing its planned ramp-down; management called these client-specific.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 19.4% YoY; rest of world grew 67% YoY on a smaller base.

segments.name: Software, High-Tech and Emerging
segments.commentary: Grew 28.5% YoY, driven by the large software deal from last quarter and the new Software Reinvention offering.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Grew 16.2% YoY, supported by a vendor consolidation win at a large financial services client.

segments.name: Healthcare and Life Sciences
segments.commentary: Grew 12% YoY; management said growth should resume, citing a slowdown from a couple of customer-specific dynamics.

guidance_outlook: EBIT margin aspiration of 16-17%; management said it is an aspiration, not guidance, with no year-end target committed.
Nagarro deal closing expected by Q4 CY26 or Q1 CY27; remaining RBI, Austria and Spain FDI approvals expected within 4-8 weeks.
Nagarro acquisition one-time expenses of about USD 50M in total over 3-4 quarters; about USD 19-20M incurred in Q2 and USD 25-30M more to come.
Post-closing, intent to squeeze out minority shareholders (about 94% acquired) and an estimated 5-6 months to integrate the two companies.
Acquisition debt cost assumed at 5-6% net; USD 1.25B debt and equity raise planned to replace the Euro 1.4B bridge loan, including USD 450M equity or equity-linked instruments.
Transaction-related one-time costs may be treated as an exception for ESOP vesting conditions (12% revenue growth and 12% EPS growth), subject to shareholder approval.
capex_capacity: Headcount rose by 958 QoQ to 29,598 at end of Q2 FY27.
Utilisation fell 70 bps QoQ to 85.8%, reflecting proactive hiring for large-deal ramp-up; utilisation drag was about 20 bps on EBIT margin.
Trailing 12-month attrition was 11.9%, down from 12.3% in Q1.

The large software deal (about USD 650M over 6.5 years) carries about USD 4M per quarter of added amortisation on third-party licences and cloud spend, a 90 bps EBIT margin hit that management expects to ease as spend is optimised and revenue scales.
Internal AI IP (SASVA, iAURA, Gen AI) development cost includes significant people cost plus tools; management said it can rise QoQ with new feature development.
demand_pricing: Q2 bookings were USD 633.5M TCV and USD 481M ACV, versus Q1 TCV of USD 1,146.2M and ACV of USD 536.8M which included the USD 650M large deal; management said some deals slipped and decision-making slowed in recent weeks, linked to Middle East dynamics.
Top 5 customers grew 38.9% YoY, top 10 grew 29.9%, top 20 grew 25%, top 50 grew 24%, top 100 grew 21.6%.
Customers above USD 20M annual revenue rose from 12 to 13, above USD 10M from 25 to 34, above USD 5M from 56 to 60, and above USD 1M from 191 to 280.
BFSI demand themes: vendor consolidation, data modernisation for AI and legacy (mainframe) modernisation; management did not give formal guidance but said all segments should grow well.

Software Reinvention Services targets AI-native product development and cost reduction of legacy products; in one case, a marquee software client's product run cost fell 45%. Management said outcome-based, revenue-share commercials with a backstop, and that the revenue upside is not in the deal financials.
Nagarro target: about 200 USD 1M+ customers with only 10 overlapping with Persistent's, per management's diligence view.

qa_highlights.question: Is high token cost pushing enterprise clients to IT services vendors, and is BFSI an early AI adopter?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Kalra said mid-market ISVs are the most AI-adopting segment, with BFSI and healthcare slower due to regulation. Clients are using small or open-weight models and token FinOps, with services firms brought in to optimise model choice and cost.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 90 bps large-deal amortisation hit persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinit Teredesai confirmed it will stay in the base for the next two to three quarters and gradually reduce as cost is optimised and revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: Is the USD 650M large deal included in last quarter's TCV, and why are Q2 bookings softer?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Kalra said the deal was included in Q1 TCV of USD 1,146.2M and ACV of USD 536.8M, which included USD 125M ACV from it. Q2 ACV of USD 481M and TCV of USD 633.5M were described as a reasonable clip, with some slippage and no productivity-driven decline.

qa_highlights.question: Will software licence costs stay at current levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Kalra said it is a mix of licences embedded in deal products and Persistent's own tool investment; levels should be assessed on overall profitability as the reinvention practice grows.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin recovery expected post wage hike, and what is the year-end target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 16-17% aspirational margin range, not guidance, with optimisation and deal growth as the levers.

qa_highlights.question: What are quick wins from Nagarro after closing?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Kalra said a synergy plan can only be built after closing; a cooperation agreement already allows cross-selling. Nagarro has about 200 USD 1M+ customers with only 10 overlapping with Persistent's.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of acquisition debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinit Teredesai said 5-6% on a net basis, depending on timing; the Nagarro revolver is about 5 banks at SOFR-linked pricing and is being refinanced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of the USD 50M one-time costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinit Teredesai said costs cover investment banking fees, bridge loan commitment fees, legal, regulatory filings, travel and funding costs; about USD 19-20M was incurred in Q2 and USD 25-30M is expected over the next 3-4 quarters.

risks_watch: Deal-win momentum: Q2 ACV and TCV were well below Q1 and management cited slippage and slower decisions linked to Middle East dynamics.
Europe revenue fell 8.5% YoY, and Healthcare and Lifesciences growth slowed to 12% YoY; management expects a recovery but did not commit to a timeline.
Margin pressure: 90 bps amortisation from the large deal and utilisation at 85.8% must reverse for the 16-17% aspiration to be reached.
Nagarro closing risk: Austria and Spain FDI and RBI approvals outstanding; USD 1.25B debt and equity raise and 5-6% debt cost are still to be executed.
Reported PAT and EPS will remain depressed by one-time costs over the next 3-4 quarters; ESOP vesting treatment still needs shareholder approval.

533206|2026-03.headline: SJVN FY26 PAT rose 4% to INR 1,008 crore on a one-time tariff true-up, while Q4 PAT jumped to INR 125 crore, helped by INR 679 crore of prior-year sales recognition.

533217|2026-03.headline: HMVL Q4 FY26: consolidated EBITDA up 5% to INR 131 crore on 23% margin despite revenue down 2% to INR 558 crore, driven by Print ad yields.

Print drove the improvement, with advertising growth led by yield (rate) increases rather than volume. Radio revenue fell on a high events-led base and remained loss-making at operating EBITDA level, and the company surrendered six loss-making radio frequencies. Management is discontinuing the OTTplay digital subscription business, with residual servicing costs expected mainly in FY27. Net cash stays above INR 1,000 crore, but other income fell about INR 50 crore on mark-to-market losses on treasury holdings.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other operating income rise almost 100% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: It is due to forfeiture of contractual AFE revenue that counterparties did not pay within the specified period.

qa_highlights.answer: OTTplay had advertised in the print newspaper; with OTTplay moved to discontinued operations, the intersegment revenue was eliminated, reducing Print revenue and PBIT by the same amount.

qa_highlights.answer: Other income fell on mark-to-market losses on the treasury as yield curves hit record highs (10Y near 7%); management plans to hold to maturity. Assetvault is an AFE investment with no cash outlay and is a marketing-property partnership.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said no further closure losses are expected; the only likely items are small servicing losses in FY27 and statutory impacts from new labour codes.

qa_highlights.answer: No such plan so far; the Board intends to invest the cash in core print and digital businesses of tomorrow.

533217|2026-06.headline: HMVL Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 15% to INR 497 crore and EBITDA nearly 3x to INR 90 crore, while a preferential equity issue at ~INR 24.7 drew shareholder pushback.
533217|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 15% YoY to INR 497 crore, with EBITDA up nearly 3x to INR 90 crore (margin up 12 points) and PAT of INR 47 crore (9% margin). Print drove growth, with advertising up 15% to INR 295 crore and operating revenue up 16% to INR 376 crore, while Digital revenue fell about 28% and Radio stayed flat with negative EBITDA. Management also announced a preferential issue at the SEBI-formula price (~INR 24.7 per share) in HT Media and Digicontent Ltd, not HMVL, to retire 30-50% of debt; this drew sharp objections from minority shareholders on dilution and pricing. Treasury gains and asset-sale profit lifted other income in HMVL.

Anna Abraham said a preferential issue is faster (2-3 months) and gives more certainty than a rights issue, which carries underwriting and under-subscription risk.

qa_highlights.answer: Gupta said the market values HMVL at about one-third of book, the promoter is subscribing on the same terms, and all options (including OTTplay decision) are being discussed at Board level. Pathak said he voted against the resolution.

qa_highlights.answer: Gupta said HT Media has carried debt for three to four years, built up post-COVID from English Print and Radio operations, and that the combined net cash figure hides this.

qa_highlights.question: Rohan Agarwal: what is the nature of the other income jump at HMVL?
qa_highlights.answer: Anna Abraham said it comprised treasury gains (mutual fund NAV-based, driven by yield curve movement at quarter end) and realised profit on sale of assets; no MTM on equity investments. Future levels cannot be predicted.

qa_highlights.question: Rohan Agarwal: outlook for newsprint costs, hedging, and whether the 13% Print margin is a baseline; would cover price hikes help?
qa_highlights.answer: Gupta said newsprint is 25-40% of costs, peaked near USD 650-700/MT, and there is no forward market; 13% margin can be used as a model baseline. Anna Abraham said Q2 newsprint is slightly higher and cover price hikes are difficult given existing hikes.

533267|2026-06.headline: Cantabil Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% to INR178.8 crores and EBITDA margin widened to 33.2%, but PAT margin slipped to 9.1%.

533269|2026-03.headline: VA Tech Wabag FY26: revenue up ~20%, PAT up 26%, order book INR 17,200 crore (over 4x revenue), net cash ~INR 950 crore.
533269|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue growth of about 20% year-over-year and PAT growth of 26%, with EBITDA margin at 13.3% and ROCE near 20%. Order intake was about INR 7,500 crore versus about INR 5,700 crore last year, taking the order book to INR 17,200 crore, up 26% YoY. Net cash (ex-HAM investment) was about INR 950 crore, up 35% from INR 700 crore, and the company has been net cash positive for 13 consecutive quarters. Management reiterated the 15-20% growth and 13-15% EBITDA guardrails, with a new five-year strategy to be published later in the year. Q&A focused on Middle East pipeline (Kuwait and Saudi orders expected), quarterly India-cluster profitability, lumpy EPC revenue, and the municipal platform and HAM plans.

segments.name: Municipal vs Industrial revenue mix
segments.commentary: Municipal about 80% and industrial about 20% of revenue. Management is adding industrial and mentioned BPCL, Reliance and Aramco-linked pursuits.

segments.name: India vs ROW
segments.commentary: Revenue split about 50:50 India and rest-of-world. Order backlog split about 58-60% India and 40-42% ROW.

segments.commentary: Key projects include Chennai 45 MLD TTRO (rehab plus O&M, INR 1,000+ crore), Chennai ADB-funded ring main, Kodungaiyur reuse O&M, Perur desalination (Southeast Asia's largest per management), Bangladesh and Nepal projects. Digha-Kankarbagh STP won GWI best wastewater project. Quarterly Indian profit fell from about INR 127 crore to INR 60 crore per the questioner; management said to judge on blended multi-year margins.

segments.name: Middle East and Africa cluster
segments.commentary: Management calls MEA the growth engine; Yanbu desalination mega order won. Al-Haer 200 MLD STP is 83% physically complete. Kuwait order expected to be signed soon (management guided to this quarter); Saudi order may slip to next quarter. Namibia and Senegal in execution; Zambia civil works started.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guardrail of 15-20% CAGR and EBITDA margin of 13-15% reiterated; new five-year strategy and guardrails to be published later this year, expected to be better than current guidance.
Order book to remain above 3x revenue (currently over 4x); ROCE expected to cross 20% within a couple of years; O&M target 20% in 3-5 years.

Management expects revenue to rise in coming periods as new India orders (Kodungaiyur, Chennai ring main, BPCL, Reliance, BWSSB, DJB) convert; CFO said next year could be about 35% higher but is lumpy.

Municipal platform (HAM-style) and industrial tenders expected to be finalised over the next quarter; no HAM bids confirmed yet.

Management says desalination water costs about 8 paise per litre and reuse about 5-6 paise per litre.

533269|2026-06.headline: VA Tech Wabag Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.8% YoY to INR 887 crore, PAT up ~37% to INR 90 crore, order backlog record INR 19,400 crore.
533269|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR 887 crore (+20.8% YoY), EBITDA INR 116 crore (+21.7%, margin just over 13%) and PAT INR 90 crore (+~37%, 10.2% margin). Order intake exceeded INR 3,400 crore, 77% from international markets, taking the order book to a record INR 19,400 crore (over 4x revenue). Management said the company stayed net cash positive for the 14th consecutive quarter, and new wins included a 60 MIGD Kuwait desal plant and the third phase of Ajman STP in the UAE. Management guided 15-20% revenue growth for the year and reiterated a 13-15% medium-term EBITDA margin band, with FY27 more likely at 13-14%.

segments.name: Revenue mix by business
segments.commentary: EPC 82% and O&M 18% of revenue. India 48%, overseas 52%.

segments.name: Order intake
segments.commentary: Q1 order intake over INR 3,400 crore: EPC ~INR 2,960 crore, O&M ~INR 470 crore. International 77%, India 23%.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: Record INR 19,400 crore: 66% EPC, 34% O&M; roughly balanced India vs international. Management put Middle East at about 35-40% of backlog. Two framework orders (~INR 600 crore) were removed as not yet effective.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: O&M revenue grew about 7% YoY in the quarter. Management said it will grow in line with project completions moving into O&M phase (Ghaziabad, Digha-Kankarbagh completed; Perur next year).

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guided at 15-20% for the year; management said it expects to meet it and to deliver above guidance.
EBITDA margin: medium-term blended band 13-15%; FY27 expected at 13-14%, with a stated aspiration of 15% by year end.
Working capital guided to stay in the 100-110 day range despite growth; long-term Wriddhi 2.0 strategy to be presented at the May FY27 investor meet.
Backlog expected to execute over about 36 months; international EPC cycles 24-30 months, India about 36 months.
capex_capacity: Asset-light model: management said no capex is needed to take orders and there are no capacity constraints.
Perur desal project (Chennai, JICA-funded): about 75% complete, 1 lakh cubic metres of concreting done, marine works finished; commissioning over the next few quarters.
Kodungaiyur: agreement signed, DPR submitted to the PE; refurbishment (1.5 years) to start any time, followed by 18.5 years of operation.
Kuwait 60 MIGD SWRO (with HEISCO) and Kutaisi (Georgia) project started; Ajman STP phase 3 is a design-build sewage biorefinery.
demand_pricing: Order intake was dominated by international wins: Kuwait desal (first project there), Ajman STP phase 3 in UAE, Vienna Water Works high-end drinking water, plus repeat Indian orders in Bengaluru and Delhi (Byramangala, Bellandur, Mitraon/DJB).
Bid pipeline: management cited about USD 2-3 billion across MEA and India (about INR 20,000-25,000 crore), with India about USD 1-1.5 billion. No order inflow target was given.
Management said the Middle East conflict has had no material impact on projects; it has written force majeure letters to customers covering price and time impacts.
Domestic traction is returning in industrial and municipal segments; management still sees larger deal sizes overseas.
Industrial share of backlog is about 12-13%, with an aim of 20-25% over time; traditional industrial is ~90% oil and gas.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall YoY, and were there one-off provisions in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed margin differences to project mix (more EPC vs EP). It said other expenses included standard provisions for delay or anticipated default under a tighter policy, which can be reversed on collection. No one-off was described.

qa_highlights.question: What is the share-of-profit from associates (~INR 5.5 crore) and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: It is mainly from HAM projects that moved from construction to O&M. Management said it includes construction-phase risk releases, so it may not recur at the same level.

qa_highlights.question: Is the forex gain operational and how does it affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said forex gains arise from transactions (invoices, collections, payments) and are treated as operational; translation gains go through reserves. It said it has a natural hedge and uses PCFC for residual exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Will the order backlog execute faster outside India?
qa_highlights.answer: International EPC cycles are 24-30 months versus about 36 months in India; the backlog is expected to execute over about 36 months overall.

qa_highlights.question: Is the TSGENCO receivable (~INR 140 crore) recoverable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the matter is sub-judice, the Supreme Court verdict is in its favour, and it would not give a timeline.

risks_watch: Forex gains formed a significant part of Q1 profit; management says they are operational, but the standalone operating margin excluding forex fell from 15.8% to 8.9% (as cited by an analyst).
Middle East geopolitical exposure: 35-40% of backlog is in the Middle East; execution risk around logistics, imports and prices, with force majeure notices issued.
Rising provisions for delays or defaults in other expenses under the new, more stringent policy.
O&M growth slowed to about 7% YoY; recurring revenue growth depends on project completions moving into O&M.
TSGENCO receivable (~INR 140 crore) still in arbitration with no timeline; Kodungaiyur refurbishment start awaits PE approval.
533269|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and defensive. Management pushed back repeatedly on margin, forex and geopolitical questions, calling forex operational and the Middle East impact minimal. It was evasive on the Perur revenue recognised and on the EPC/EP split for the quarter.
key_quotes: Importantly, we remained net cash positive for the 14 th consecutive quarter, reinforcing the strength of our balance sheet and our disciplined approach to the growth.
Our order book position reached a historic high of INR 194 billion, that is INR 19,400 crores, almost $1.8 billion, which is over four times of our revenue base
So we have a natural hedge when it comes to it. Whatever is the small component of difference between the revenues and the cost, that is anyway covered through a PCFC.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin at 13-14% (Q1 just over 13%) and aspires to 15% by year end, but analysts flagged standalone operating margin ex-forex falling from 15.8% to 8.9% and rising provisions, so expansion is conditional.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management says no capex is needed to take orders and there are no capacity constraints; Perur (about 75% complete) and Kodungaiyur refurbishment are existing projects, not new capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue growth guided at 15-20% for FY27 (midpoint 17.5%), Q1 revenue +20.8% to INR 887 crore, and record INR 19,400 crore order book (over 4x revenue) executing over ~36 months.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is asset-light with no capacity constraint; no new capex plan was announced and the Wriddhi 2.0 strategy is only due at the May FY27 investor meet.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said it expects to meet 15-20% growth and deliver above guidance, backed by Q1 growth of 20.8% and a 4x order book, but offered no explicit raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Middle East holds 35-40% of backlog with force majeure notices issued, $600 crore-equivalent framework orders (~INR 600 crore) removed as not effective, and provisions for delays/defaults rising under the new policy.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or model launches were discussed; the call covered new contract wins only.

rows.label: Record INR 19,400 crore order book with Kuwait and Ajman wins
rows.why: Order book is over 4x revenue and Q1 intake exceeded INR 3,400 crore (77% international), with backlog expected to execute over about 36 months.

rows.label: TSGENCO receivable (~INR 140 crore) recovery
rows.why: Matter is sub-judice in arbitration; management says the Supreme Court verdict is in its favour but gave no timeline.

rows.label: Working capital held at 100-110 days
rows.why: Management guided working capital to stay in the 100-110 day range despite growth; current NWC is 108 days.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 15-20% growth guide, the record order book and net cash, but defensive on margins, forex gains and the Middle East; analysts pressed on the ex-forex margin drop from 15.8% to 8.9%, forex quality and associate profit recurrence.

533271|2026-03.headline: Ashoka Buildcon Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA fell 7% to INR168 crores; FY27 guidance calls for 20% revenue growth and 9.5-10.5% margin.
533271|2026-03.overview: Standalone total income fell 10% YoY to INR1,819 crores in Q4 FY26, with EBITDA of INR168 crores (9.2% margin, up 20 bps) and PAT of INR49 crores versus INR60 crores a year earlier. For FY26, standalone total income declined 17% to INR5,952 crores and EBITDA declined 6% to INR636 crores. Consolidated Q4 EBITDA was INR302 crores at a 15.1% margin. Management attributed the weak year to slower industry awarding, project delays, input cost inflation and fixed-cost under-absorption, and it guided to recovery in FY27 led by monetisation cash flows and a 20% revenue growth target.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Saudi hotel and Mumbai ITMS orders in the standalone order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Saudi Arabia (INR900 crores share) and IGR (INR1,100 crores) are executed by SPVs and sit outside ABL standalone books, captured only in consolidation. Mithi River and traffic management are in the order book under Others, with ABL executing them back-to-back.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 EBITDA margin weak and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited price escalation pressure and year-end ECL provisions of INR28 crores (inventory and debtors). FY27 standalone margin guided at 9.5-10.5%, with ECL reversals expected over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital situation and what are receivable cycles?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables are milestone-linked. Power T&D cycle is 5-7 months with 30-40% advance; road EPC cycle is about 3-3.5 months. Management expects normalisation to 110-120 days post-September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why were HAM monetisations delayed and what are the cash inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Delays are tied to NHAI provisional COD receipts. Completed sales: HAM ~INR1,150 crores and BOT ~INR1,800 crores. Upcoming: ~INR750+ crores from 4 assets by June, ~INR400 crores from 2 by December.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax impact on HAM asset sale gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Capital gains at 12.5%; effective tax about nil at ACL (carry-forward losses) and about INR22 crores at ABL. Combined effective tax on remaining HAM sales estimated at 6-7%.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans to sell Chennai ORR and Jaora-Nayagaon?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, sale of both is being pursued over the next 12-18 months; a small monetisation process has been launched with good buyer interest.

ECL provisions (INR28 crores in Q4) and receivable build-up in Power T&D; receivable days must normalise to 110-120 by September 2026.
Monetisation timing depends on NHAI PCOD and appointed dates; INR550 crores deferred toll-extension consideration depends on NHAI decisions.

NHAI bidder disclosure rule on project casualties and debarment is still being defined by the Road Federation.
Bangladesh order book flat at INR374 crores; management says work continues at slow pace.

533271|2026-06.headline: Ashoka Buildcon Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 55% YoY to INR292 crores on HAM/BOT monetisation; FY27 revenue growth guidance cut to 10-15% from 20%.
533271|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income was flat YoY at INR1,320 crores, with EBITDA down 17% to INR126 crores (9.5% margin) and PAT up 3% to INR31.5 crores. Consolidated total income fell 21% to INR1,534 crores, mainly because of BOT and HAM asset monetisation in Q3 FY26, and consolidated EBITDA fell 55% to INR292 crores (19.0% margin). Management cut FY27 revenue growth guidance to 10-15% from 20% and EBITDA margin to roughly 9-9.5% from about 10%. Order book stood at INR15,251 crores as of 30 June, with about INR450 crores added after quarter-end, and the company is pivoting to international, railway and power T&D work as domestic highway awarding stays subdued.

Asset monetisation of about INR1,150 crores (quoted as INR1,100 crores later in the call): four assets targeted by September 2026 (about INR700 crores) and two assets by Q4 FY27. Chennai ORR expected by year-end; Jaora-Nayagaon by March 2027 or H1 FY28.
Post-monetisation third-party debt guided at INR500-600 crores; total debt including subsidiary debt about INR1,100-1,200 crores.

FY28 margins expected to improve to 10.5-11% on projects, per management; standalone interest cost guided to about INR200-210 crores for FY28, versus INR225-240 crores for FY26 (INR313 crores was cited for FY26 by an analyst; the management figure for FY25 was INR225-240 crores).
HAM equity requirement: INR179 crores for FY27 on existing HAM projects (including Bowaichandi), then INR72 crores each in FY28 and FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current bid pipeline, by sector, and how much is bid but not yet opened?
qa_highlights.answer: NHAI/MoRTH about INR1 lakh crore, states about INR25,000 crore, railways about INR50,000 crore, plus power T&D and renewables EPC bids. Bids submitted but not yet opened total about INR8,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue growth guidance changed and what is the order inflow and margin outlook?

Order inflow guided at INR6,000-8,000 crore: INR800 crore won in Q1, L1 in about INR1,800 crore expected to convert in Q2. FY27 margin about 0.5 pp below the roughly 10% start-of-year target, with H2 ramp-up expected to help.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and realisation for the asset monetisation, and are there holdbacks?

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and interest cost outlook after monetisation?

Standalone interest cost about INR60 crore in Q1, expected near INR50 crore by year-end; FY28 interest guided at INR200-210 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall in Q1 and will FY28 margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 costs were loaded by new administrative staff and overheads for new verticals, expected to rationalise over coming quarters. FY28 projects are expected to deliver margins of about 10.5-11%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Chennai ORR and Jaora-Nayagaon monetisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Chennai ORR expected by year-end, pending investor freeze; Jaora-Nayagaon by March-end 2027 or H1 FY28, dependent on authority compliance. Equity invested: Jaora total project equity INR278 crore, company's acquired-stake cost about INR418 crore; Chennai ORR effective cost about INR300 crore for 100%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the economics of the Gems and Jewellery Park and Guyana orders, and how is overseas revenue split?
qa_highlights.answer: Gems and Jewellery Park (51% JV, INR450 crore contract) could yield about INR100 crore a year over five years; overall project size about INR1,000 crore over five years. Guyana four-laning valued at about INR338 crore. Q1 overseas revenue about INR145 crore, about 80% from Guyana.

risks_watch: Domestic highway awarding remains subdued: only about 5 km awarded in June and construction down 32% YoY in June, so Q3-Q4 awarding recovery is a key test.

533293|2026-06.headline: KOEL Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 16% to INR1,461 crore, but EBITDA fell 4% and margin contracted to 11.2% on commodity costs and export weakness.

Standalone EBITDA declined 4% YoY to INR165 crore and margin compressed to 11.2% from 13.5%, which management attributed to lower export volumes, elevated commodity costs and a lag between cost inflation and price realisation. Standalone net profit fell 9% to INR99 crore. Consolidated revenue rose 13% to INR2,000 crore, with consolidated net profit down 17% to INR111 crore. Management said pricing actions have been taken across most businesses and expects profitability to improve as they flow through over coming quarters.
