534748|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 19.45% QoQ to INR 287.70 crore and EBITDA margin to 17.41%, with net profit at INR 12.37 crore.
534748|2026-03.overview: Total income for Q4 FY26 was INR 287.70 crore, up 19.45% QoQ from INR 240.86 crore. EBITDA rose 118.12% QoQ to INR 50.10 crore, with margin up 788 bps to 17.41%. Net profit was INR 12.37 crore versus INR 2.28 crore in Q3, with a 4.30% net margin. For FY26, total income was INR 1,066.42 crore, EBITDA INR 138.03 crore and net profit INR 26.99 crore. Management said it redeemed INR 43.19 crore of NCDs in one tranche and cut debt by nearly INR 68 crore over the last two quarters.

segments.name: TMT rebar / long products (Simhadri brand)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 rebar volume was 49,760 tonnes, up from about 39,000 t in Q3. Management said the average EBITDA per tonne was about INR 9,000-9,500 in the last quarter versus about INR 6,000 in earlier quarters, and about INR 6,800-7,000 on a yearly average.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Power segment revenue fell in FY26. Management attributed this to kiln refurbishments; it expects data-centre tie-ups and capacity expansion to improve consumption.

segments.name: Logistics (SEIL Logistics and Infra Company)
segments.commentary: A subsidiary formed to run a private freight terminal and logistics at Visakhapatnam, with railway sidings. MoUs with the Andhra Pradesh government cover about 150 acres adjacent to the existing land.

guidance_outlook: Management said Q4 FY26 is 'fine' but later years should be better; it expects steady margins while the market stays buoyant.
Management expects FY27 volumes to roughly double once the reheating furnace and capacity expansion come on stream from Q2 FY27, with capacity mostly doubled.
Sustainable EBITDA guidance given as about INR 7,000 per tonne on average volumes of 40,000-50,000 tonnes per quarter.

Finance cost is expected at about INR 12-13 crore per quarter, not below 10, after the new loan costs and trade finance charges fall away. Refinancing is targeted to bring the cost of debt to about 9%.

Existing capex (reheating furnace, furnace refurbishment, kiln work) is to be completed in FY27. New greenfield capex for the 1 million tonne green steel plant is about one year away, pending groundbreaking and the strategic investor's inputs.
Pledged shares are expected to be released once refinancing is complete and IMR funds are received.
capex_capacity: A reheating furnace is being installed, expected to start from Q2 FY27 and to add about 50,000 tonnes of new bar capacity. Management said it will raise rolling mill efficiency by 30-40%.
Billet and rebar capacities were raised by about 44-45% at the end of FY25. Utilisation is about 46-47% for rebar and 55-56% for billet, with a target of 70-75% in FY27.
Expansions already under way are expected to be operational by end-July 2026.
Land bank: about 400-450 acres existing; another 150 acres targeted for the logistics park and 150 acres for steel manufacturing. MoUs cover a 1 million tonne green steel plant.
Planned capex and debt paydown are to be funded from INR 300 crore of share warrant money from IMR Group and internal accruals.
demand_pricing: Management said the Indian steel outlook is strong, citing infrastructure, housing, railways, defence and import substitution. It also said Andhra Pradesh and Visakhapatnam projects (Google AI hub, ArcelorMittal, Amaravati) are sources of demand, and that the company is an approved vendor for them.
April 2026 sales were described as 'great' and May as slightly weaker due to heatwave and the war situation. Management expects a June recovery.
Management said the company is largely insulated from the ongoing war, except for some diesel cost in transport. Coal, iron ore and scrap are sourced locally.
The company was re-empanelled under MES for TMT bar supplies to the Ministry of Defence.

qa_highlights.question: What does the company plan to fund its capacity growth and reduce its debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has MoUs with state governments for expansion and a 1 million tonne green steel plant. Project reports are pending, and the plan is to announce them once formalised.

qa_highlights.question: When is the balance payment expected from IMR on the share warrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 300 crore warrant subscription is expected within about six months and will fund growth, including green steel.

qa_highlights.question: What is the finance cost trend, and why did it rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 finance cost was INR 7.50 crore, not INR 17 crore. The analyst then cited Q3 at INR 13 crore and Q4 at INR 17 crore; management attributed the difference to new loan processing costs and supplier trade finance. Term debt has fallen from about INR 350 crore to INR 250 crore, and current debt is about INR 270 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What were rebar volumes and what is the FY27 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY26 rebar sales were 49,760 tonnes. Management said FY27 capacity is expected to roughly double from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current capacity utilisation and when will it reach 85-90%?
qa_highlights.answer: Rebar utilisation is about 46-47% and billet about 55-56%. Management expects 70-75% in FY27 after the reheating furnace is commissioned.

qa_highlights.question: Why are the company's shares 100% pledged, and will this change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pledge is linked to past bank exposure. It expects the pledge to be released after refinancing, to a debt cost of about 9%, and once IMR funds are received.

risks_watch: Debt and funding: the IMR INR 300 crore warrant money has not yet been received and is expected in about six months. Refinancing to about 9% is planned but not yet closed.
Finance cost: management guided to INR 12-13 crore per quarter, which is well above the analyst's expected single-digit level.
Margin sustainability: the EBITDA margin of 17.41% is above the earlier 11-12% range, and management called the steel market 'buoyant' but cyclical.
Execution: FY27 volume doubling depends on the reheating furnace and expansions running from Q2 FY27.
Demand softness in May 2026 due to heatwave and war-related conditions.
Governance: management agreed to consider quarterly investor calls, which are not yet in place.

534816|2026-03.headline: Indus Towers Q4 FY26: reported EBITDA INR 44.6bn (+1.6% YoY, 55.1% margin) and FY26 final dividend of INR 14/share distributing full-year FCF of INR 37.6bn.
534816|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR 81bn (+4.8% YoY) and core rental revenue INR 53.1bn (+5.4% YoY), with co-locations up 5.6% YoY. Reported EBITDA was flat-to-up YoY but down 1% QoQ, held back by a Q4 one-time settlement hit to revenue, a Q3 positive one-off in other expenses, and higher seasonal maintenance spend. Full-year PAT fell 28.1% YoY to INR 71.4bn because FY25 carried a INR 51bn receivables write-back; normalised EBITDA and PAT grew 11.4% and 13%. The Board recommended a final dividend of INR 14/share, distributing the full FY26 free cash flow, with management guiding to a steady and progressive payout going forward.

financial_highlights.value: INR 11.1bn in Q4; INR 37.6bn in FY26

segments.name: Towers and co-locations (India)
segments.commentary: Q4 added 4,892 macro towers and 6,192 co-locations, taking the base to about 264,500 towers and 428,000 co-locations (+6.1% and +5.6% YoY). Tenancy ratio stable at 1.62; leaner-tower co-locations exceed 14,000, portfolio about 442,000 including leaner towers.

segments.name: Energy
segments.commentary: Energy revenue fell QoQ on cost optimisation and seasonal energy cost decline; energy margin -3.6% in Q4 vs -5.2% a year earlier. Solar access added at about 2,500 sites in Q4, taking the total to about 42,400; diesel consumption down about 7% YoY.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Operating licence secured in Zambia with on-ground execution starting; Uganda and Nigeria in final regulatory stages. Commercial frameworks and initial orders in place with the anchor customer; capex for Africa described as not significant initially.

segments.name: Non-tower / DAS / IBS
segments.commentary: Company says it reached leadership in IBS in Q4; DAS deployments picked up in metros, tunnels and highways. No figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Final dividend of INR 14/share recommended; management says the endeavour is steady and progressive distribution, with no minimum payout formula (dividend policy: FCF distributed at year-end, subject to working capital).
Management does not give forward numbers; says order book is healthy for the next few quarters with growth-oriented capex (about 70% of capex is growth, about 25% replacement/maintenance).
Full-year EBITDA margin said to be in line with the 55%-plus expectation.
Africa tower deployment expected to begin soon in Zambia, with ramp-up as approvals come through in Uganda and Nigeria.
capex_capacity: Q4 tower additions 4,892 and co-location additions 6,192; FY26 full-year additions about 15,200 towers and 22,500 co-locations.
Over 85% of sites digitally connected (fuel sensors, backhaul monitoring, smart meters, power equipment).
About 531,000 5G BTSs installed in the base; growth expected from loading on existing towers, with selective tower footprint expansion later.
Management flagged supply-side tightness in tower materials linked to LPG availability and West Asia conflict, affecting deployment timelines and costs.
demand_pricing: Core revenue growth muted by Q4 FY25 one-time reconciliation benefit (about 2.1pp of base) and a Q4 FY26 one-time settlement; management cited organic service revenue growth of about 5-5.5% YoY after adjusting for an Airtel tower acquisition.
Annual escalations of about 2.5% cited as a revenue driver.
Management said a major customer's contract expiries affect only a very small portion of the portfolio; some Jio tenancies have expired but are still operating, with minor churn.
Management expects tenancy ratio trend to change as second anchor customer ramps; cannot give a directional outlook.
Diesel-price pass-through is said to be billed on actuals with no lag; industrial (bulk) diesel price rise does not affect the company's retail diesel purchases.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about the FCF from last year's VI dues reversal, now that FY26 FCF is almost fully distributed, and what capex guidance applies?
qa_highlights.answer: Board evaluated FCF and desired debt levels and chose to distribute FY26 FCF; capex about 70% growth, 25% replacement, and no forward numbers given, with a healthy order book.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a formal dividend policy, and is there a minimum payout?
qa_highlights.answer: Policy is on the website: the Board considers distributing year-end FCF, subject to working capital and other conditions; no minimum payout amount is specified.

qa_highlights.question: Why has FY25 cash not been released, given earlier comments about distributing it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Board did not compartmentalise cash by year; it assessed full FCF and debt levels, with total distributions of about INR 37-38bn.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 maintenance spend a one-off or a structural reset as towers age?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to seasonality (clear-weather Q3/Q4 and pre-monsoon preparation) plus a deliberate tower-strengthening programme; said cost per tower has fallen over 3-4 years and the base is not reset.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the sequential EBITDA decline and per-tower drop?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 revenue hit by a one-time settlement; Q3 had a positive one-off in other expenses; network maintenance up 5.6% QoQ; full-year margin still on track at 55%-plus.

qa_highlights.question: Why are single-tenancy tower additions rising and what is the Vodafone rollout impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said co-location additions exceeded tower additions in Q3 and Q4; some towers move from other tower companies to Indus (net addition), so a direct split is not possible.

qa_highlights.question: When will Africa operations start, and will NOC be local or in India?
qa_highlights.answer: First tower in Zambia expected very soon, well within six months; NOC location not yet decided.

qa_highlights.question: Do the Jio tower contract expiries lead to churn, and were renewals at the same terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Some expired tenancies still operate; very minor percentage churned; renewals continue on the same terms, with no incremental concessions mentioned in response.

risks_watch: Customer financial health and non-renewal of expired tenancies (management says a small portion of the portfolio), and tenancy ratio trend as second anchor customer ramps.
Supply-chain tightness and cost inflation from the West Asia conflict and LPG availability, affecting tower deployments and costs.
Maintenance cost trend on the aging portfolio, and whether Q4 maintenance spending repeats.
Dividend sustainability versus capex and Africa investment, plus debt levels after the Airtel tower acquisition funding.
Energy margin (-3.6% in Q4) under diesel and grid price changes; smart meter mandate by CEA.

534816|2026-06.headline: Indus Towers Q1 FY27 gross revenue rose 4.6% YoY to INR 84.3 bn; EBITDA up 3.0% to INR 45.2 bn, margin 53.6%.
534816|2026-06.overview: Gross revenue grew 4.6% YoY to INR 84.3 bn, with core rental up 5.2% YoY to INR 53.7 bn on tower and colocation additions. Reported EBITDA rose 3.0% YoY to INR 45.2 bn, but margin fell 1.5 pp YoY to 53.6%; adjusting for a prior-year INR 0.9 bn write-back, EBITDA grew 5.2%. Energy margin was -4.6% (seasonal, plus past-period settlements), while diesel consumption fell 13% YoY. Management reiterated a firm order book for 3-4 quarters and began Africa rollouts guidance for next quarter, with economics still undisclosed. The CFO also announced his departure after five years.

segments.commentary: Energy revenue rose 9.5% QoQ on seasonal diesel use and higher diesel prices; diesel consumption down over 13% YoY; solar access on about 46,000 sites (about 3,700 added); solar installed base 259 MW.

534976|2026-03.headline: V-Mart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 24% with 12% LTL growth and EBITDA up 56% to INR106 crore at 10.9% margin.
534976|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was a strong quarter: 29 new stores opened (record quarterly additions), like-to-like growth of 12% (V-Mart 12%, Unlimited 9%), and total sales up 24%. 535693|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 50% to INR365 crore and PAT nearly doubled to INR59.61 crore, with an INR1,600 crore order book (4.46x FY26 revenue).
535693|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 (year ended March 31, 2026) revenue from operations of INR365 crore, up 50% from INR242 crore, with EBITDA of INR83.45 crore (margin 22.83%, up 280 bps) and PAT of INR59.61 crore (up roughly 100%). Management attributed the gain to Q2 and Q3 monsoon-quarter execution, where revenue reached INR180 crore versus INR70 crore a year earlier. Q4 standalone revenue was INR93.93 crore, PBT INR16.79 crore, PAT INR14.78 crore and EPS INR5.09. This was the company's first earnings call, and Q&A covered order book conversion, real estate plans, promoter pledge, and JV revenue sharing.

segments.name: EPC infrastructure
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR349.81 crore (roughly 90% of total) with segment profit INR51.88 crore. Management said EPC margins range 13-20%, averaging about 15%, with niche river and slope protection works at 18-19%.

segments.name: Real estate
segments.commentary: Revenue INR19.58 crore (about 5-7% of total per an analyst's figure; management said about 10%), with segment profit INR16.70 crore vs INR14.75 crore last year. Revenue fell because FY25 included industrial plot sales (about INR4 crore) that did not recur. Management cited about 85% margins, almost entirely rental.

segments.name: Order book by vertical
segments.commentary: Total INR1,600 crore: Roads and Bridges INR498 crore, Buildings INR405 crore, Railways and Tunnels INR400 crore, River Protection INR250 crore. About 60% expected to execute in FY27 and 40% to spill into FY28.

guidance_outlook: Management targets maintaining about 50% revenue growth and current profitability margins over the next two to three years, and said it expects this momentum for about five years.

Projects expected to be about 70% BIL and 30% JV partners by revenue, varying project to project.
capex_capacity: Funding for new projects planned through surety bonds (now accepted across all departments), bank guarantees, and joint ventures; no capex or capacity figures were given.
Near-continuous execution achieved in the monsoon quarters by shifting workflow to lower-rainfall areas; no capacity utilisation numbers disclosed.
Average execution period for new bids is two to three years.
demand_pricing: Order book of INR1,600 crore at FY26 end, 4.46x FY26 revenue; about 50% acquired in the last six months, and management said revenue recognition from new orders takes six to seven months due to design and land work.
Pipeline mix stated as about 40% buildings, 20% protection works and 40% roads.

Management cited Northeast drivers: PM Gati Shakti, Bharatmala, Act East, five to six railway lines in 10 years, Bhutan (Gelephu) rail bid, border roads and fencing, hydropower in Arunachal, and district-level universities and hospitals in Assam.
Management said Northeast competitors are fewer, and that NE projects (terrain, river and slope protection) carry higher margins than mainland contractors.

qa_highlights.answer: All road projects are EPC or item-rate; none are HAM. EPC margins range 13-20%, averaging about 15%, with niche works at 18-19% and general infrastructure at 11-13%.

qa_highlights.answer: Around 50% of the book was won in the last six months; EPC design, land and approvals take six to seven months before revenue recognition begins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bid pipeline and FY27 bidding outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Current pipeline is about INR3,000 crore with results in 30-45 days; FY27 bidding is expected at INR7,000-8,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did real estate revenue fall in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 included about INR4 crore of industrial plot sales that did not recur in FY26; real estate profit rose to INR16.70 crore from INR14.75 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will capital be deployed to fund growth, and is there a debt reduction plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to surety bonds plus bank guarantees, and JVs with partners, rather than a stated debt reduction target.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said approximately 70% of order book revenue comes to BIL and 30% to JV partners, varying by project.

535693|2026-06.headline: Brahmaputra Infra Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.24% YoY to Rs 110.79 crore, with PAT up 9.57% to Rs 16.48 crore.
535693|2026-06.overview: Consolidated top line crossed Rs 110 crore for the first time in a quarter, up 20.24% YoY and 17.95% QoQ, driven by EPC activity. Consolidated EBITDA rose 13.08% YoY to Rs 25.15 crore, while PAT grew 9.57% YoY to Rs 16.48 crore. Management said Rs 429 crore of orders were booked in the quarter and the order book stands at about Rs 1,600 crore, with roughly 50% yet to start. Management also addressed cash conversion, pointing to Rs 165 crore of OCCPS repayments from June 2027 and arbitration recoveries of Rs 200-225 crore expected over two years.

financial_highlights.change: vs 22.04% in Q4 FY26 (as stated on call)

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Consolidated EPC revenue Rs 104.47 crore (vs Rs 87.53 crore in the prior quarter as stated on call); consolidated PBT Rs 14.71 crore (vs Rs 11.43 crore QoQ).

segments.name: Real Estate & Other Income
segments.commentary: Consolidated real estate revenue Rs 6.33 crore, up about 65% YoY from Rs 3.82 crore; real estate PBT Rs 5.40 crore. Management cites 85-90% margins for this segment.

guidance_outlook: Management targets FY27 order book of about Rs 2,500 crore by year-end, against roughly Rs 1,600 crore currently.
Management expects a historic top line and bottom line in FY27 and said it will keep EPC growth at the rate of the last 2-3 years.
Management expects no margin compression for FY28-FY29 and says growth will come from higher order inflow.
Around 80% of the Rs 800 crore-plus order book to be executed over 18 months is expected to bill in the first year, per management.
New mixed-use shopping mall (Rs 500-700 crore valuation) to start construction by year-end; first phase rent yield from FY29-FY30, with three-phase rental target of Rs 50-60 crore annually.
Tax rate expected to rise to 20-22% after 2028 once Section 43B deductions on past interest run off; FY27 effective rate 12-15%.
capex_capacity: Current order book about Rs 1,600 crore plus, executable over 18-30 months.
Bid pipeline about Rs 2,500 crore; focus on railways, institutional buildings (universities, medical colleges), and flood and slope protection works.
Ramping up flood protection technical team by recruiting more engineers.
Balance sheet: bank guarantee limit Rs 100 crore and CC limit Rs 100 crore; soft surety bond limit about Rs 50 crore, enabling bids of up to Rs 1,000 crore more.

Land and assets: about 4 lakh sq ft of shopping mall area, industrial park on 100-200 acres, 30-35 bigha land parcel; land value Rs 100-200 crore and City Centre valuation Rs 600-700 crore (management estimate).
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 order inflow of Rs 429 crore across railways, roads and highway maintenance; over Rs 300 crore booked in the last 75 days.

Major orders: Rs 140 crore road-over-bridge for Northern Central Railway; Rs 81.98 crore staff quarters for NF Railway; Rs 70.18 crore five-year O&M from MoRTH on a Mizoram NHAI corridor; Rs 25.78 crore Assam road maintenance from NHIDCL.
Management says it is selective on bids and avoids hyper-competitive volume work; about 50% of the order book is outside Northeast India.
Wayside Amenities (NHAI land leases, 30-year) bids pending; results expected next month.
Management states that cash-flow issues are concentrated in pre-2020 legacy projects now in arbitration.

qa_highlights.question: What is the executable order book for FY27 and FY28, and what is the bid pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book of Rs 1,600 crore plus, executable over 18-30 months; bid pipeline about Rs 2,500 crore, focused on railways, institutional buildings and flood/slope protection.

qa_highlights.question: How will cash conversion improve given large receivables, WIP, retention and OCCPS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no stuck-up money or slow-moving WIP on post-2020 projects; debtors about Rs 15-20 crore with 45-90 day billing cycles. Pre-2020 legacy projects in arbitration: over Rs 100 crore monetised in five years, about Rs 150 crore still pending, with Rs 200-225 crore expected over two years including bank guarantee releases. OCCPS of Rs 165 crore repayment starts June 2027 and runs to 2034; management plans to swap OCCPS with arbitration awards.

qa_highlights.question: Is real estate a core hedge or to be divested?
qa_highlights.answer: No plans to divest; both segments to operate jointly. Mall development is planned to start by year-end with rental income of Rs 50-60 crore at full three-phase build-out.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Assam floods on ongoing projects?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of works are outside Northeast and unaffected; some Upper Assam projects were affected, but emergency variation works offset this with no negative impact on billing or turnover.

qa_highlights.question: How is pan-India expansion being pursued and does it include light real estate?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion is selective, project-by-project; West Bengal is a strategic target. Asset-light real estate via NHAI Wayside Amenities bids is being pursued, with a large Assam bid awaiting results.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Current 12-15% effective rate reflects Section 43B deductions on past interest; expected to move to 20-22% after 2028.

Real estate and mall project depends on compliances; construction start expected by end-FY27 and rental income only from FY29-FY30.
Tax rate expected to rise to 20-22% after 2028, which will lower PAT growth versus the current 12-15% rate.
Several figures on the call were inconsistent (e.g., order book quoted as Rs 1,000 crore, Rs 1,600 crore and Rs 800 crore; margin figures). Verify against filed results.
key_quotes: In fact, 50% of our current order book is yet to start.
There is no backlog and there is no slow-moving WIP as of date.

So, we are very much confident that in the subsequent quarters, the same momentum with the healthy bottom line will be continue and we keep, expect all the stakeholders support and we are very much sure that in 2026-2027, we will give a historic number from the top line and from the bottom-line point of view.
So, there is no stuck up of money, and currently, we are in a positive cash flow statement position.

535754|2026-03.headline: Ambuja Cements FY26: record 73.7 Mt volumes, but Q4 cost ~INR4,500/t; FY27 volume guided ~80 Mt and cost cut of INR250/t targeted.
535754|2026-03.overview: Ambuja's Q4 FY26 call (consolidating Orient Cement for 11 months and Penna from August 2025) showed record FY26 volumes of 73.7 Mt, up 16% YoY, with normalized FY26 EBITDA of INR6,539 crore (INR887/t, up 12%) and PAT of INR2,647 crore (up 17%). Management said Q4 cost per tonne was about INR4,500, above its earlier INR4,000 exit aspiration, due to acquired-asset underperformance, freight, packing, fuel, branding and repairs. Management called the reset partial: FY28 capacity targets slip toward FY30, capex is cut to INR6,000-6,500 crore for FY27, and the company says cost peaked in Q4. Demand is expected to be soft and industry price hikes are small (about INR10/bag).

financial_highlights.metric: Premium cement share of trade sales

financial_highlights.change: up ~INR1 vs Dec quarter; down vs ~INR255 last year

segments.name: Sanghi Industries (acquired)
segments.commentary: Cement capacity utilization about 57%; management targets 65-70% in FY27. Rail link at Naliya is an add-on, not in base case; seven marine vessels ordered for delivery from next year.

segments.name: Penna Cement (acquired)
segments.commentary: Utilization about 46%; management targets 55-60% in FY27. Breakdowns and deferred maintenance cited; Sanghi and Penna together hold 19 Mt capacity, with a 5-10% utilization uplift targeted.

segments.name: Orient Cement
segments.commentary: Management says Orient is running at full capacity; Orient was consolidated for 11 months in FY26.

segments.name: Ambuja and ACC existing assets

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated volume guided at ~80 Mt, about 8% growth, versus industry growth of 5-5.5%.
FY27 cost reduction of INR250/t on a full-year average; cost peak of ~INR4,500/t in Q4, Q1 FY27 seen flattish, with savings accelerating over the remaining three quarters.
Minimum cost reduction of INR250/t in FY27 and another INR250/t in FY28 (INR500 cumulative); management says the earlier INR3,650/t target is not abandoned.

Capacity to reach ~119 Mt by end FY27 after ~10 Mt of additions (commissioning Aug-Sep 2026 window); FY28 target capacity slips toward FY30; Maratha adds 4 Mt clinker; Mundra (2 Mt clinker) and Assam (2 Mt clinker) follow in about 24-28 months.
FY27 capex estimated at INR6,000-6,500 crore; project IRR hurdle of 18% stated.
Management did not give EBITDA/t guidance; said it is too early to estimate given volatility.
capex_capacity: Capacity 109 Mt at FY26 end after 10.7 Mt grinding and 7 Mt clinker added (Marwar, Farakka, Sankrail, Sindri, Krishnapatnam, Jodhpur, Bhatapara).
Clinker capacity 69 Mt now, rising to 73 Mt with Maratha (4 Mt).
About INR4,000 crore of capex already under execution (capacity, WHRS, fly ash transport); balance is debottlenecking and maintenance.

Recalibrating growth capex: shutting some grinding units in North UP, Bihar, South Gujarat and Maharashtra to move them closer to markets; a Bihar grinding unit planned; Dahej Line 2 as clinker-plus-cement example.
Management paused new projects until current ones are completed; engineering to be finalized over next 6 months.
demand_pricing: Industry price rise in March quarter was about INR10/bag, INR15-20 only in selected pockets; management says industry cannot pass on costs under relentless pricing pressure.
April-May demand described as subdued and soft; management would be happy if industry recovers half of a price hike.
Q4 FY26 volume growth was muted (Orient-adjusted flat YoY per an analyst); packing bag shortages linked to West Asia conflict cost volume in March.
Premium cement gap versus base product INR50-55/bag for super premium and INR20-25/bag for premium; price gap with the number-one player is INR5-10 in some districts.
Management expects FY27 demand to be soft due to inflation and weak monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q4 cost about INR4,500/t when management earlier pointed to an INR4,000 exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR4,000 was an aspiration for the March exit; March averaged ~INR4,100 normalized, with INR250 escalation from West Asia. Causes cited: branding, repairs at acquired plants, freight, packing, fuel and heat consumption, and lower government incentives.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost reduction is assumed for FY27 after Q4 inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR4,500 is the peak; a INR250/t reduction gives ~INR4,250/t for FY27 on a full-year average, with Q1 FY27 flat at ~INR4,500.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR3,650/t cost target be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani said the target is not abandoned; INR500/t cumulative over two years is the committed minimum, with further runway to the earlier target.

qa_highlights.question: Why the reset in capacity and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani said performance fell short of commitments, citing cost, wrong contractor choice, projects started without full engineering, and breakdowns at Penna and Sanghi; ~80% of the five KPIs relate to cost.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a target IRR for capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani stated a project IRR of 18%, all equity-funded.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cause of high working capital and negative ACC operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinod Bahety said ACC has MSA receivables from Ambuja that will be settled via an ICD after shareholder approval; Ambuja's core working capital fell to 20 days from 30 days.

535754|2026-06.headline: Ambuja Cements Q1 FY27: EBITDA up 331 bps to 16.7% and net cost down INR206/t to INR4,241/t, while total volumes fell (trade -2%, non-trade -21% YoY).
535754|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a value-over-volume quarter: trade share rose to 78% from 74%, and operating EBITDA reached INR1,589 crore on revenue of about INR9,500 crore. Net operating cost fell INR206/t sequentially to INR4,241/t, which management said absorbed about INR110/t of West Asia-related cost inflation. Volumes declined, with trade down 2% and non-trade down 21% YoY, and management attributed the quarter's weakness to diesel shortages, packing material issues and deliberate exits from low-margin South volumes. Management guided to 8% FY27 volume growth, citing July trade volumes up 8% YoY, and reiterated INR4,250/t full-year cost guidance.

Q2 FY27 net cost guided to be slightly better than June-quarter levels, after absorbing potential geopolitical cost rise of about INR100/t.

Installed capacity to reach 119 Mtpa by end-FY27 (adding about 10.2 Mt); 8-10 Mtpa of organic additions planned each year thereafter.
Long-term capacity utilisation target 70-75% on a value-focused basis; green power share to reach 60% by FY28 (48% on revenue-plus-consumption basis).
capex_capacity: Trial runs started at Dahej (1.2 Mt expansion); Salai Banwa (UP, 2.4 Mt) started; Bhatinda (Punjab, 1.2 Mt) and Jodhpur (Penna, 2 Mt cement / 3 Mt clinker) commissioned or stabilising, with Jodhpur clinker supplying grinding units from Q2.
Kalamboli (Mumbai, 1 Mt) and Warisaliganj (Bihar, 2.4 Mt) expected in Q2 FY27 (Warisaliganj most likely September).

RE capacity 973-975 MW (of 1,122 MW target; about 150 MW remaining); WHRS 228 MW rising to about 376 MW.
Three coal blocks in focus; first expected to be operational in about 30 months. AFR (alternative fuel) substitution at about 7%, targeted at 10-15% in FY27.
Sanghi: about INR600 crore jetty expansion for clinker. Penna: INR100-150 crore for AFR and WHRS. About 3.5 Mt of old ACC capacity temporarily closed for around six months.
demand_pricing: Management says cement demand was stable across infrastructure, housing and construction; July trade volumes reportedly up 8% YoY.
Q1 headwinds: diesel availability, packing material shortages and logistics disruption in West and East. Logistics lead distance fell from 269 km to 249 km YoY, yet freight per tonne was flat.
NSP rose sequentially but fell YoY; management attributed the gap to Incoterm and channel-cost netting. Analyst comparison put Q1 NSP about INR100/t below UltraTech's reported NSP.
Blended cement share 85%; clinker factor down about 3% to 64%.
Q2 FY27 cost pressure expected from geopolitical escalation (West Asia, fuel).

qa_highlights.question: Is it fair to expect muted FY27 volume growth if the value-over-volume strategy holds, given Q1 volume loss and earlier ~80 Mt chase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 8% FY27 volume growth, citing July trade volumes up 8% YoY; non-trade is a 'well calculated' reduction, with market share said to have held or improved only on trade.

qa_highlights.question: Will green power be consumed in-house, and what is the incremental benefit as captive use rises versus selling power?
qa_highlights.answer: About 45 crore units sold in Q1; roughly 50% (about 20 crore units) expected to be consumed in Q2. Green power share is 34% on consumption basis, 48% on revenue-plus-consumption basis, targeted at 60% by FY28. Grid power costs INR7-8/unit versus the cost of captive green power, and sales are capped at around 10% of output.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 FY27 net cost rise given inventory buffers, and what is the full-year cost path?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 net cost expected to be broadly in line with or slightly better than the June quarter, after absorbing a potential geopolitical rise of about INR100/t. FY27 target INR4,250/t reiterated; FY28 target INR4,000/t or below. Clinker inventory about one month, coal about three months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade volumes still decline YoY, and how did the regions perform?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 hit by diesel shortages, packing material issues and logistics disruption. North trade +2% YoY, West grew in trade and non-trade, East sustained, South cut about 1 Mt of low or negative EBITDA volume, Central degrew on blended-cement shift. Capacity utilisation 65%.

qa_highlights.question: Where did the INR206/t sequential cost reduction come from, and what was the gross saving after West Asia cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to fly ash sourcing, RE power price per unit, clinker factor down about 2-3%, marginal logistics gains (INR10/t), and fixed cost optimisation. Management said the INR206/t saving absorbed about INR110/t of West Asia cost, implying gross savings of about INR316/t.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NSP down about INR100/t versus UltraTech's reported NSP, and what are the Incoterm and netting effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NSP is netted for certain channel and Incoterm costs (ex-works terms), and that channel investment is being expensed against NSP. It did not quantify the gap and said NSP is market-driven.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company keeping plants temporarily closed and treating non-trade differently at acquired assets?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3.5 Mt of old ACC and one acquired-company facility temporarily closed for around six months; management said these are not permanent closures. Karan Adani said non-trade volumes at acquired assets were largely at negative or marginal EBITDA, so the company is prioritising value over volume.

risks_watch: Whether July's 8% trade volume growth holds and whether non-trade volume decline (-21% YoY in Q1) stabilises, given guidance needs roughly 12-13% growth in the remaining nine months.
Geopolitical and fuel cost pressure in Q2 (about INR100/t potential rise) versus the INR130-150/t cost-lever pipeline and the INR4,250/t full-year target.
Execution risk on capacity: Kalamboli and Warisaliganj (Q2 FY27), Maratha clinker slipped to Q1 FY28, Mundra around 2029, and 8-10 Mtpa annual additions thereafter.

Reconciliation gap: management did not provide a breakdown of cement vs RMC vs power vs fly ash cost, and deferred several analyst requests (fly ash/power cumulative P&L, RMC margin drop to about 7%, fixed cost bridge) to offline follow-up.

Accounting items to monitor: O&M cost equalisation across quarters still under discussion with auditors; INR24 crore termination-related exceptional item (VRS in South); depreciation true-up after Sanghi and Penna merger.
Green power transition: grid connectivity for some cement plants expected in two to three quarters, and green power share target of 60% by FY28 depends on consumption rising from about 50% of sales.
key_quotes: Our strategy remains clear and consistent, creating sustainable value ahead of volume.
Net operating cost reduced to INR4,241 per metric ton, a reduction of INR 206 PMT from the previous quarter.
So the operating company, Ambuja has no debt.

535755|2026-03.headline: ABFRL Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR1,990 crore; Pantaloons grew 19% and reported loss narrowed to INR164 crore.
535755|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 16% YoY to INR1,990 crore, with Pantaloons up 19% (17% core format) and TMRW up 45%. Excluding a INR97 crore one-time demerger gain in the base quarter and an INR83 crore non-cash derivative gain at WROGN (TMRW associate), management said EBITDA grew 29% YoY at an 11.5% margin. Reported loss was INR164 crore versus INR171 crore a year earlier, and PAT loss narrowed to INR235 crore on an adjusted basis from INR289 crore. Management flagged a weaker wedding calendar, a marginal March slowdown from geopolitical disruption, and 3-4% raw material inflation with 5-8% price increases under evaluation for H2.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 17% Pantaloons core format growth, and how much was EOSS timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the EOSS shift to January, merchandise resets in three categories (over 20% growth each in Q4), record sell-through, and new large-format stores. It said Nov-Mar like-to-like growth was about 7%, with total growth about 9%.

qa_highlights.question: Will FCF and cash use strain liquidity given the FCF-positive target of FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said standalone gross cash was INR2,100 crore at the start of FY26, with INR1,150 crore available for the next two years. qa_highlights.question: Is there a need for equity infusion, and what net debt level is comfortable?

qa_highlights.question: Why is the store addition guidance not accelerating despite strong LTL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the store pipeline takes 6-9 months to build and that prior rapid expansion lowered quality, so guidance is unchanged for now, though management is inclined to scale faster later.

qa_highlights.question: What is the OWND profitability and why are its store additions slower than Pantaloons?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Pantaloons margin is 18-18.5% and OWND losses explain the gap at segment level. OWND store additions are slower because it is a multi-year build focused on getting store economics, merchandise and team right.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material inflation and pricing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material inflation is 3-4% (later cited as 3-5%), and management is evaluating 5-8% price increases in H2, depending on category, without a firm decision.

535755|2026-06.headline: ABFRL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% to INR2,026 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 8.2% and reported loss widened to INR249 crores.
535755|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 11% Y-o-Y to INR2,026 crores, with established businesses growing high-single digits at stable margins and newer businesses growing about 30%. EBITDA was INR167 crores (8.2% margin), with the Y-o-Y decline attributed mainly to lower treasury income and investment in new businesses; excluding treasury income, management says EBITDA rose. Reported loss widened to INR249 crores from INR234 crores, driven by higher Ind AS depreciation and finance costs from new stores. Wedding-related demand was hit by Adhik Maas, and TCNS like-to-like growth slowed to about 2%, which management called disappointing.

qa_highlights.question: Why TMRW revenue growth slowed and expected trajectory
qa_highlights.answer: Management said primary sales grew 11% vs 35% base last year and secondary grew 16-17%. Expects TMRW to deliver 20%+ revenue growth for the year and lower annual losses; FY27 is significant, with profitability targeted in FY29 to FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Period-end cash and debt; whether FY27 is still an investment year
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone gross cash about INR1,000 crores vs roughly INR1,150-1,200 crores at start of year, with about INR500 crores expected by year-end. Losses to be lower on an annual basis in FY27 and lower again in FY28, with full profitability in FY29. TMRW has already raised INR500 crores for its own growth plan.

qa_highlights.question: Pantaloons LTL trajectory after Q4 and adjustment for Adhik Maas; demand read
qa_highlights.answer: April was weak, May significantly double-digit, June softer; quarter LTL about 4% vs 14% in Q4, which included an EOSS shift. Management targets at least high-single-digit LTL for the full year and described demand as steady, not strong.

qa_highlights.question: TCNS LTL slowdown to about 2% and outlook
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a disappointing quarter for organic performance, citing liquidation of old inventory over the past 12-15 months; margin was slightly better YoY. Store additions of 35-40 are expected, with LTL returning to high-single-digit to early double-digit in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Ethnic segment growth outlook for FY27 given weak H1 and TCNS drag
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the overall ethnic portfolio to grow 20%+ for FY27, with H2 significantly higher than H1. TCNS is expected to return to early double-digit growth.

qa_highlights.question: Galeries Lafayette revenue run rate, losses, and additional store plans; TMRW store and profitability plan; Tasva economics
qa_highlights.answer: Galeries Lafayette revenue not disclosed; still operationally loss-making. The Collective plus Galeries Lafayette expected to break even at combined level in H2 FY27. Next store planned in Delhi in 2-3 years. Tasva needs INR400-500 crores revenue to turn profitable; plans 25-30 new stores on ~90 base and sees mid-teens LTL.

qa_highlights.question: Inflation, pricing, and margin outlook for Pantaloons and OWND
qa_highlights.answer: Input inflation about 4%+ in both businesses; about half passed on in pricing. Cost pressure expected mainly in Q2 and Q3, with gross margin impact in H2. No higher discounting expected in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan for FY27
qa_highlights.answer: Capex plus working capital about INR450 crores for FY27, with capex about INR300+ crores for new stores and renovations.

535789|2026-03.headline: Sammaan Capital's IHC takeover closed 31 March 2026; all three domestic agencies upgraded within 50 days, lifting bonds ~100 bps and targeting FY27 PAT of INR1,400 crore.
535789|2026-03.overview: This was the first earnings call after IHC's strategic investment, with IHC's share allotment completed on 31 March 2026 and IHC holding 28.5% equity (43.5% after warrant conversion within 18 months). Management said INR5,652 crore (USD 592 million) has been received via equity and 25% warrant upfront, with about INR3,200 crore (USD 335 million) due on warrant conversion. CRISIL (9 April), CARE (12 May) and ICRA (23 May) upgraded the company to AA+ across all three, with CRISIL and ICRA up one notch and CARE up two. The call centred on a multi-year plan (FY27 to FY30) with a 4.4% steady-state ROA, cost-to-income falling to about 26%, and a shift to a co-lending and asset-light model, alongside a legacy-book write-off/credit cost discussion. The call also included a correction of the FY30 ROA figure from 8-odd percent to 4.4%.

segments.name: Residential mortgages (prime and affordable)
segments.commentary: Prime mass-market home loans (8.5% to 10% yield) to be sourced for sale to banks; affordable portion (10% to 13%) to be held on balance sheet. Management says mortgages drive growth in FY27 and FY28.

segments.name: Business loans and micro-LAP
segments.commentary: Prime mass-market loans yield 9.5% to 11% and are to be sold; semi-urban and micro-LAP loans yield 11% to 13.5% and are to be held.

segments.name: CRE project loans
segments.commentary: Done only on a co-origination basis with credit funds, pari-passu with no credit guarantee, with the company taking roughly 10% to 15% of disbursements.

segments.name: Gold loans and loans against securities
segments.commentary: Planned as the next secured products; gold needs a separate branch network, with wider product launches from FY28. About 240 branches are already sized for other products.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursements of about INR30,000 crore; Q1 FY27 disbursements to be at least 50% to 60% above Q4 FY26, then a 30% to 40% step-up on that base.

Marginal cost of funds to fall about 160 bps; cost of funds to decline 150 bps over three years; 270 bps total reduction tied to AA to AAA migration (120 to 150 bps on AA to AA+, and the rest on AA+ to AAA).
Portfolio mix target: 60% secured and 20% unsecured or semi-secured, with 80% retail; about 30% of incremental disbursements through co-lending or direct assignment.
Gearing capped at about 3.5x to 4x; liquidity held at the higher of 6 months of repayments or 10% to 15% of borrowings.
Target AUM of INR2 lakh crore and high-teen ROE (about 18%), with the timeline described as 'in no hurry'; FY27 and FY28 growth to be mainly mortgages.
capex_capacity: Branch network to grow fivefold to about 1,600 branches; workforce to rise to 20,000 people, with about 8,000 by end of FY26 per management.
A gold loan branch costs about INR20 lakh to set up and takes about 3 years to become fully productive and profitable; investment is not described as running into tens or hundreds of crore.
Technology spend (CRM upgrade and Salesforce deployment about 6 months ago) is expensed through the P&L, not capitalised; 37 AI use cases identified.
Targets: agent productivity up 30%, mortgage turnaround from 5 to 7 days to 2 to 3 days, loans per person per month from 0.6 to 2-plus.
demand_pricing: Management says productivity rose 2x between March and April 2026 following the shift to an asset-light model.
Disbursals of about INR72,000 crore planned for FY29 versus INR50,000 crore in CY17 and CY18 (as cited by management).
Competition: management says there are few AAA-rated NBFCs and that the market has room for new entrants; it cites AAA players (and 3 to 4 other AA+ players) disbursing around INR50,000 crore a year.
Management says insurance cross-sell reaches over 90% of borrowers.
Management says about 90% of borrowings are onshore; domestic bonds have appreciated about 100 bps since the IHC announcement, with international bonds about 250 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Varun Ahuja (BlackRock): Will offshore rating agencies follow the onshore upgrades, and is the slow cost-of-funds decline due to non-call fixed-maturity debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects international agencies to follow the domestic upgrades. Bonds cannot be renegotiated and have 3 to 4 year maturities, so the cost decline comes with a lag; incremental borrowing at lower cost and bank renegotiation are the levers.

qa_highlights.question: Renish (ICICI Bank): How will the company build non-mortgage portfolios, who will run them, and how will costs be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it has run secured and unsecured products at scale before, that tech and app-based lending help, and that people and tech investment will be made. Growth in FY27 and FY28 will be mainly mortgages, given no rush to hyper-grow.

qa_highlights.question: Bhanu Chauhan (Barclays): What share of growth comes from core versus new products?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 and FY28 disbursals are 80% existing products, falling over time; by FY30 the mix is targeted at 50% mortgage-backed and 50% other products.

qa_highlights.question: Avinash Singh (Emkay): How will competition from AAA NBFCs be handled, and is the FY30 ROA of about 8% correct?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the FY30 ROA figure was an error and corrected it to 4.4%, with FY27 at 1.8%, FY28 at 3.7% and FY29 at 4.4%. It says the market is large enough and that mortgage front-loading and co-lending support productivity.

qa_highlights.question: Naintara Ghosh (Deutsche Bank): How much investment is needed for the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment is mainly branches and people rather than large capex; technology costs already incurred (CRM, Salesforce) run through the P&L, and product-level ROA can be shared on request.

qa_highlights.question: Vineet Sharma (Param Capital): What drives the NIM rise from 3.5% to 5.8% when cost of funds is not falling as fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the NIM gain comes from the spread on sold-down loans (AUM less loan book rising from about INR30,000 crore to INR45,000 crore in FY28), and that equity adds liquidity without a P&L cost. Cost of funds shown is for on-balance-sheet borrowings only.

qa_highlights.question: Arun Antony (JM Financial): Is the 270 bps cost-of-funds reduction for FY27 still achievable given the West Asia conflict and rising yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 270 bps, with 120 to 150 bps coming from AA to AA+ and the rest from AA+ to AAA, and said the company is operationally, financially and promoter-ready for AAA.

qa_highlights.question: AS Raju (individual investor): What is the outstanding write-off as of 31 March, and will recoveries be included in projections?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said recoveries of about INR7,000 crore from amounts provided are built into the projections and described the provisions as credit costs, not write-offs. It said asset reconstruction company sales recover 70% to 80%.

risks_watch: Execution on FY27 disbursals (INR30,000 crore) and Q1 FY27 step-up; management's productivity claims rely on a 2x jump in one month.
Cost-of-funds path: 270 bps depends on AA to AAA migration; international agency ratings are still pending, and about 90% of borrowings are onshore.
Warrant balance of about INR3,200 crore (USD 335 million) due within 18 months, plus IHC's rise to 43.5%.
Credit-cost and recovery assumptions: the legacy book had provisions, with recoveries of about INR7,000 crore assumed; the call did not give a detailed write-off schedule.
Cost-to-income falling from ~50% to ~26% while hiring and building new products, with a risk of cost overrun during the transition.
A FY30 ROA projection error was corrected on the call; the revised presentation should be checked for other inconsistencies.

535789|2026-06.headline: Sammaan Capital posted Q1 FY27 PAT of INR243 crores, with cost of funds falling from 10.5% to 10% and AUM at INR56,239 crores.
535789|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 as the first quarter under IHC ownership, with PAT of INR243 crores after last quarter's balance-sheet markdowns. Disbursements were about INR3,875-3,900 crores across five products to roughly 12,000 new customers, and net NPA is 0.15%. Cost of funds declined through the quarter, helped by rating upgrades (domestic AA to AA+, international B+ to BB-) and repricing of existing borrowings. Management reiterated a shift from portfolio management to growth, a build-out of branches, tech and senior hiring, and multi-year targets for cost of funds, cost-to-income, ROE and ROA.

financial_highlights.change: Following balance-sheet markdowns and provisions taken in the prior quarter; no YoY comparison stated
Stated as in line with guidance; no QoQ figure given

Described as standard in normal course of business
Down about 50 bps during the quarter

segments.commentary: About INR2,000 crores disbursed in Q1, the largest product by disbursement; micro LAP planned as a mainstay.

segments.name: Loans against securities / unsecured / credit-fund deal
segments.commentary: Loans against securities INR262 crores and unsecured about INR100 crores in Q1; one INR840 crore co-lending deal with an Asia-based credit fund (20% Sammaan, 80% fund).

guidance_outlook: Disbursements: INR10,000 crores in H1 FY27 (Q1 on target) and INR20,000 crores in H2, total INR30,000 crores for FY27; INR40,000-50,000 crores in FY28.
Cost of funds: 9.6% by September, 9.3% by end-FY27, and 7-8% range over the next 2-3 years; management said below 8% over three years.
Cost-to-income: about 50% in FY27, declining from H2 FY28, targeted at 30-35% by FY29.
Branches: about 240 at end of H1 FY27, rising to 270, with 800 branches targeted by end of FY28.
Five-year targets cited on the call: ROE 6.8% to 18.7%, ROA 1.8% to 8.1%, NIM 3.5% to 8%, as put out on May 20.
Inorganic growth to be considered from FY28; the bias for now is to build.
capex_capacity: Branch network to rise from about 240 at end-H1 FY27 to 270; 23 master service centres across 20 states; management targets 800 branches by end of FY28.
Digital-first app to go live in H2 FY27, integrating a new Salesforce-based CRM and a new loan management system, plus a data lake.
Digital personal loans to launch on the app in H2 FY27; gold loans, two-wheeler loans and BNPL-type e-commerce tie-ups targeted by end-FY28.
53 AI use cases under implementation, with about 60% to be implemented in FY27; about 66% of identified use cases reportedly in motion.

demand_pricing: FY27 disbursement mix: about 75% mortgage-backed (two-thirds retail, one-third wholesale AUM with about 20% kept on balance sheet), 25% new products; about 90% secured and 10% unsecured in FY27, moving to 80:20 in FY28.

Securitisation and asset-light model: at least 30% of origination to be securitised or sold down, with 60-70% kept as a backup option; assets below 9.5% to be sold down via direct assignment, above 9.5% sliced between balance sheet and securitisation.
Asset yield universe cited from 8.5% (prime) to about 20% (unsecured); LAP 11-12% and affordable loans 12-13% also eligible for securitisation.
Fee income expected to rise, with direct assignment fee income kicking in around October 2026 with about a six-month lag.
97% of Q1 disbursements and 97% of AUM are secured.

qa_highlights.question: Raghav Garg (Ambit): Will lower cost of funds be passed on to customers for acquisition, or will spreads be retained?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy rides on lower cost of funds plus asset-light model; sub-9.5% assets to be sold down via direct assignment and higher-yield assets kept or securitised, balancing fee and spread income.

qa_highlights.question: Bhanu Chauhan (Barclays): How much upfront opex and what is the cost-to-income path?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex will rise in absolute terms, offset by fee income with a lag of a quarter or two; cost-to-income around 50% this year, declining from H2 FY28, reaching 30-35% by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Abhiram Iyer (Deutsche Bank): What is the asset-class breakup of the roughly INR3,000 crore per half target?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 mix about 75% mortgage-backed and 25% new products; disbursement breakdown to expand from 4-5 boxes to at least 8 by end-FY27 and 15 by end-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Vinit Agarwal (Bajaj Alternates): What tangible benefits has IHC delivered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 90 bps saving on about INR50,000 crore borrowings (about INR450 crore annualised), targeting a further 70 bps; software procurement at 30-50% of earlier costs; and senior talent additions.

qa_highlights.question: Sanket (DAM Capital): What is IHC's larger vision beyond lending in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Dalia Khorshid (IHC) said the group is open to opportunities in India across fintech, digital, AI and financial services, with Sammaan seen as a platform; management said FY27 is for stabilisation and other fee businesses will be evaluated later.

qa_highlights.question: Niharika (CapGrow): Are the five-year ROE, ROA and NIM targets achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident, citing rating upgrades, lower cost of funds, asset-light model and tech, with governance as the enabler.

qa_highlights.question: Nilesh Sharma (Monomer): What are disbursement targets for this and next financial year?

Recoveries and asset quality: management said recoveries will exceed internal projections and that no P&L pain is expected, but the Q1 PAT of INR243 crores relies on net recoveries of INR240 crores; watch recovery run-rate and ARC sale outcomes.
Five-year targets (ROE 6.8% to 18.7%, ROA 1.8% to 8.1%, NIM 3.5% to 8%): management stated confidence but gave no interim milestones beyond FY27 targets; track progress against these.
Governance and inorganic plans: statutory auditor change and internal audit co-sourcing partner selection were said to be closing this quarter; inorganic growth deferred to FY28.

536974|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR142 crore (up ~80% YoY), but EBITDA margin fell to 9.96% on March raw material spike.

Q4 EBITDA rose 66% to INR14.16 crore, but margin slipped 86 bps YoY to 9.96%, which management attributed to a sharp March raw material price increase. FY26 total income was INR419 crore (up 44%), with EBITDA of INR6.32 crore at an 11.03% margin as stated. The Ahmedabad plant is now operational and the company's credit rating was upgraded during FY26. Management is focused on shifting mix toward solar EPC and non-subsidy micro-irrigation to improve working capital.

segments.commentary: Maharashtra order of ~1,500 pumps in FY26 was the first year in that state; a new 500-pump order worth ~INR11 crore came in Q4. Management says pump EBITDA margin is similar to micro-irrigation.

qa_highlights.answer: Management sees continued central government support for PM-KUSUM and rooftop schemes and expects growth to persist for a considerable period.

536974|2026-06.headline: Captain Polyplast Q1 FY27 total income rose 16.3% YoY to Rs 81.66 crore, with EBITDA margin up 99 bps to 12.07%.
536974|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of Rs 81.66 crore (+16.3% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 9.86 crore (+26.7%) and net profit of Rs 4.66 crore with diluted EPS of Rs 0.78. Management said the quarter was hit by geopolitical-driven raw material inflation but revenue growth and margin both improved. Solar EPC order wins of 1,500 pumps in the first four months were highlighted, with 800 already executed and 700 pending. Ahmedabad plant (70,000 sq ft) commenced production, and the company was listed on NSE in July 2026.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Two verticals: solar water pumping (PM-KUSUM, currently only Maharashtra; empanelled in Maharashtra and Gujarat) and rooftop. Management did not quantify segment revenue or growth; said solar revenue was H2-weighted last year. Targets solar EPC contribution of 50% over next 3 years.

guidance_outlook: Blended EBITDA margin expected to improve about 10-15 bps every quarter as Ahmedabad ramps up; volume growth cited as main margin driver.
Micro-irrigation margin uplift of 1-1.5% expected once Ahmedabad is fully operational, over the next 2-3 years.
Raw material (LLDP/HDPE) prices up about 30-35% versus Jan/Feb levels after a ~50% spike at end-March; price revisions expected to be largely complete by end of Q2, with full benefit from Q3.
Central government price revision mechanism expected by end-September.

Dedicated solar execution team already set up; limited incremental manpower needed in states with existing micro-irrigation teams.
demand_pricing: Solar pump orders: 500 pumps from MSEDCL in Q1 and 1,000 more in July 2026; 800 of 1,500 executed, 700 pending, expected to be completed by end of August 2026.

Replacement demand in mature states (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu) currently about 10-20% of micro-irrigation demand.
Export growth said to be in line with domestic growth from a very low base; future growth to come from new customers. Africa and Latin America named as focus markets.
Other states' solar tenders expected to be floated around September; awaiting tender release.

qa_highlights.question: Solar pump growth outlook and share in business?

qa_highlights.question: Working capital cycle for micro-irrigation vs solar pumps?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-irrigation payment cycle 5-6 months (8-10 months in Andhra Pradesh); solar pump receivable cycle 3-4 months. Majority of working capital sits in receivables, not inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Ahmedabad facility margin benefit and ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-irrigation margin benefit of 1-1.5% when fully operational; blended margin uplift of 10-15 bps each quarter during ramp-up. Initial focus on cost efficiency, standalone sales later.

qa_highlights.question: Export growth drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Export growth similar to domestic, but from a very low base; meaningful growth requires new customers.

Execution bottleneck in solar pump installation as order book scales; export still a small base.

537259|2026-03.headline: Suyog Telematics Q4 FY26 revenue INR221 crore, EBITDA margin ~74%, PAT ~30%; Vodafone 5,000-tenancy order expected by June-end drives FY27 plan.

537259|2026-06.headline: Suyog Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR710 mn (+6.1% YoY on electricity-inclusive basis), net profit INR145 mn; Vodafone Idea rollout began mid-June with 150 tenancies converted.
537259|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR710 mn, up 6.1% YoY against INR668 mn restated for electricity, with EBITDA of INR420 mn (59.3% margin) and PBT of INR195 mn. From 1 April the company began including electricity reimbursement in revenue after a GST-related guidance change, which lowered the reported EBITDA margin from about 70% to 59.3%. Vodafone Idea orders started flowing around 15-16 June; 95 towers (150 tenancies) were converted in June. Management said most growth will show from Q2 onwards, with the full benefit in FY28. Net profit margin was about 20% against 25% a year ago, which management attributed to a vendor-provision reversal in the prior-year quarter.

segments.name: Tower / IP1 infrastructure (India)
segments.commentary: Exit Q1 FY27 with 6,103 towers and 7,468 tenancies; tenancy ratio about 1.2x. Q1 additions were mainly macro sites, with a few kilometres of fibre laid.

segments.name: Fibre
segments.commentary: Management expects fibre at 5-8% of total revenue in FY27, with no major jump this year.

guidance_outlook: Target of 3,000 Vodafone Idea tenancies in FY27 (described as conservative); about 35-40% expected in H1 and 60% in H2. Management also cited ~850 tenancies in hand (150 done plus 700+ open).
Revenue per tower to be about INR31,000 ex-electricity; about INR50,000 per site with electricity per management's arithmetic.
EBITDA margin (with electricity) guided at around 59%, to be maintained in coming quarters; PAT margin to stay around 20%.

Management aims for INR100 crore quarterly revenue (INR400 crore annualised) from Q4 and PAT growth from ~22% to 24%, per the MD. The CFO flagged that Ind AS rent accounting mutes EBITDA margin in early years.
Tenancy ratio target of 1.8x by end FY28 or early FY29.
Vodafone Idea FY28 target of about 5,000 further sites; Vodafone share of revenue targeted at 30-32% once the 3,000 sites are delivered.
capex_capacity: Zinc battery: sourced from GBB Batteries (Kerala plant) rather than manufactured in-house; first batch of 10-15 sites expected by mid-September, with a 100H unit at about INR33,000 vs INR48,000 for lithium (up ~50% in about 2.5 months).
Zinc battery expected to lower CapEx and some operating costs; management said it would be the first IP company in telecom to deploy it on sites.
Funding: management said internal accruals and bank funds cover the planned rollout. No fundraise decided; may come in Q2/Q3 if orders exceed plan.

BSNL: about 186 sites with pending billing from a prior ~1,000-site batch; expected to resume revenue in Q2 if Tejas equipment issues are resolved. No new BSNL projects booked until billing is confirmed.
demand_pricing: Vodafone Idea: about 45,000-site rollout plan over 18-24 months (3,000-3,500 per month); INR6,400 cr secured from SBI, with a further INR25,000-30,000 cr under discussion. Vodafone currently plans about 12,000 sites through September, and management expects roughly 30,000 in FY27.
Airtel and Jio not doing major rollouts per management. BSNL announced INR77,000 cr capex for 2 lakh sites over 5 years, but no new BSNL work is being taken until billing is confirmed.
Revenue share (per management): Airtel 48.1%, Vi 27%, Jio 22.6%, BSNL 2.3%.
MSAs with all operators are blanket frameworks with no fixed volume commitment; a 10-year lock-in with Vodafone was cited.
Sharing mix: 80% anchor and 20% shared on new Vodafone sites; macro sites carry tenancy ratios of 2-3x.

qa_highlights.question: What is the zinc battery project, its cost, and its margin and revenue impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Zinc battery is bought from GBB Batteries, not manufactured in-house. Management said it cuts CapEx (100H unit at INR33,000 vs INR48,000 lithium) with no quantified EBITDA impact given.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence and breakdown of the 3,000 Vodafone tenancies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident. It sees 850 tenancies in hand (150 done, 700+ open), expects 35-40% in H1 and 60% in H2, and says 80% will be on new towers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is BSNL no longer being pushed in guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not commit BSNL volumes until billing is confirmed. Tejas equipment issues have delayed BSNL rollouts by 1-1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT margin fall from 25% to 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Prior-year quarter included a vendor-provision reversal from Vi; management says the underlying margin is about 20-21% with electricity included.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Vodafone target fall from 12,000 to about 10,500 tenancies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 3,000 figure is conservative and tied to funds already secured; the target will rise as Vodafone confirms more funding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tenancy ratio path?
qa_highlights.answer: Current ratio is about 1.2x; target is 1.8x by end FY28 or early FY29, since macro sites carry 2-3 tenancies with recovery in 18-24 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are fibre's share and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Fibre is 5-8% of revenue and stays at that level in FY27; management says it is 100% recurring and carries a similar EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 189/186-site BSNL billing status?
qa_highlights.answer: 186 sites are still pending billing; management expects revenue from them to start in Q2.

risks_watch: Vodafone Idea funding: the 3,000-tenancy target depends on further SBI and consortium funds of INR25,000-30,000 cr; management says it will only raise its own targets once those are confirmed.

Monsoon season may slow Q2 conversions.
Lithium battery costs up ~50% in 2.5 months; zinc battery first batch due mid-September and not yet proven on sites.
Funding: management is not ruling out a fundraise; the earlier call suggested one could come, and the analyst flagged this as an open question.
Margin optics: electricity reimbursement now in revenue, so margins are not comparable with prior periods, and the CFO flagged Ind AS rent accounting as muting EBITDA in early years.

537291|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 19% to INR 4,316 million, but gross margin normalised to 56% from 63% and PAT fell about 8% to INR 384 million.
537291|2026-03.overview: Nath Bio-Genes reported FY26 revenue of INR 4,316 million (+19% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 525 million (12% margin) and PAT of INR 384 million (9% margin). Gross margin fell to 56% from 63% in FY25 on richer product and market mix, and the tax rate rose to 11% from 5%. Growth was led by maize (volume +54%, value +78%), paddy (volume +25%, value +37%) and cotton Bt, while plant nutrition fell 18% on China export restrictions. Management guided FY27 top-line growth of 15-20% (calling 15% the base case) with slightly higher EBITDA and net margins, though guidance was qualified as conservative.

financial_highlights.change: down about 8% YoY per analyst question; effective tax rate 11% vs 5%
scaled up ahead of FY27 season

segments.name: Cotton (incl. Bt)
segments.commentary: Flagship hybrids Sanket and Jumbo drove Bt cotton volume up 22% YoY, with average Bt realisation up from INR 275 to INR 293 per unit as stated on the call. Management said supply constraints of the prior two years were resolved this year.

segments.name: Paddy
segments.commentary: Paddy volume grew 25% YoY to 75,619 quintals and value rose 37%. Management said paddy growth exceeded its 20-25% expectation.

segments.name: Maize
segments.commentary: Volume rose 54% YoY to 9,639 quintals and value rose 78%; maize is now 10.72% of revenue and the fastest-growing non-cotton, non-paddy crop.

segments.name: Vegetable seeds
segments.commentary: Value fell about 11%, while average realisation rose 6% from INR 1,178 to INR 1,244 per kg, reflecting a shift to premium products.

segments.name: Plant nutrition
segments.commentary: Segment revenue fell 18% due to China export restrictions that disrupted supply; management expects normalisation in the coming year.

segments.name: Cotton-paddy combined and NCP
segments.commentary: Cotton-paddy share of revenue rose to 58% from 52%. Non-cotton, non-paddy (NCP) segment grew only about 4%; wheat and mustard value grew 10-15%.

segments.name: International (Uzbekistan JV)
segments.commentary: JV contributed about INR 15 crore (INR 150 million) to consolidated revenue for the first time in FY26, mainly cotton seed sales.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at 15-20%, with management saying 15% is the expected figure, described as conservative.
EBITDA margin to be maintained, with a slight upward trend in EBITDA and net profit margin in FY27.
Gross margin expected to settle around 53-54% per management's earlier view, versus 56% in FY26.
Finance and scheme-related costs expected to stay at about 1.5 percentage points above FY26 levels as a share of sales, per management.
International revenue target: not more than 10-15% of group revenue over 3-5 years; no financial target set for Uzbekistan yet.
Management said it hopes to cross INR 500 crore of top line soon, with no formal commitment.
capex_capacity: Capex policy is asset-light: only land bank and vehicles are capitalised; management is averse to investing in processing plants and storage, preferring rented capacity.
Cumulative cold storage, warehouse and conditioning godown capacity is 25,000 metric tons.
Maize processing need is about 15-20 days a year, which management cited as the reason not to own processing machinery.
Cotton production constraints of the prior two years were stated to be resolved this year, with production of about 70-80% of target versus 20% earlier.
demand_pricing: India's seed market is about USD 4-4.5 billion, growing at a 12-14% CAGR over five years, per management.
Management said cotton area is flat, so share gains come from competitors, and it expects further share gains next year.
Scheme spend fell to 28% of sales from 32% last year (in value terms, schemes rose); other marketing costs rise with inflation at 5-10%.
Central Asia: management cited a cotton market of about USD 100 million in Uzbekistan and about USD 450 million for all crops; the wider Central Asia market could reach USD 1 billion in 5-6 years.
Management said competition is now in-house, with new products such as product 2020 seen as better than Sanket.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Uzbekistan JV structure, crops sold, and revenue target over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Khurana said the JV has been operating for three years and this was the first year sales matched production; no financial targets are set yet. Dr. Kulkarni said the addressable market is about USD 500 million for Uzbekistan, and management will set targets after the next season.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue will international operations contribute over the next 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not more than 10-15% of revenue, which at a INR 1,000 crore top line would equal INR 100-150 crore. It described this as conservative.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and revenue guidance by crop, and how is El Nino factored in?
qa_highlights.answer: Top line expected to grow 15-20%, with cotton around 20%, paddy above 20-25% and maize a key driver. Management said El Nino affects crops differently, but it expects balanced growth through crop, geography and duration diversification.

qa_highlights.question: Are there FY27 capex plans for processing, cold storage or new geographies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex is minimal, limited to land bank and vehicles, because processing and storage can be rented and maize processing is needed for only 15-20 days a year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall and tax rate rise to 11% from 5%? What is the effective tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the PAT pressure to higher finance costs, scheme and marketing spend, and gross margin falling from 64% to about 56%. It said PAT margin dips about 1 percentage point, with costs stabilising.

qa_highlights.question: Is cash flow negative and why is inventory rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said free cash flow by formula is about negative INR 13 crore, but cash and bank balances of about INR 70-80 crore offset it. Stock build-up reflects cotton production recovering to 70-80% of target, and inventory is expected to be sold over the next two years given cotton's 5-7 year shelf life.

risks_watch: Gross margin normalisation to 53-56% could continue to compress PAT, which fell about 8% YoY despite 19% revenue growth.
Inventory of INR 4,446 million and trade payables of INR 1,305 million, with cash flow negative by about INR 13 crore on a formula basis; watch inventory turns and working capital.
Finance costs rose to INR 133 million from INR 96 million, linked to working-capital borrowing.
Monsoon and El Nino risk: management says exposure is mitigated by multi-geography and multi-duration products, but no quantified sensitivity was given.
Non-cotton, non-paddy segment grew only about 4%, so reliance on cotton and paddy (58% of revenue) remains high.
Uzbekistan JV has no revenue target yet; international contribution is about 3-4% of revenue (INR 15 crore of INR 4,316 million) and may take time to grow.

538268|2026-03.headline: Wonderla Q4 FY26 revenue rose 40% YoY to INR135 crore and EBITDA doubled to INR43.8 crore at 32% margin, helped by Chennai ramp-up and a Labour Code provision reversal.
538268|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever Q4 by income, with revenue from operations up 40% YoY to INR135 crore and footfalls up 30% to 8.79 lakh, driven mainly by the newly opened Chennai park. PAT rose 49% to INR16.4 crore, aided by reversal of certain tax and Labour Code-related provisions created in Q3 FY26. For full FY26, revenue grew 13% to INR518.8 crore and EBITDA rose 9% to INR160 crore, but PAT fell 25% to INR81.7 crore against a deferred-tax credit of INR24.1 crore in FY25. Hyderabad footfall declined 7% for the year, and management guided to no large capex in FY27 apart from sustaining capex of INR35-40 crore.

financial_highlights.change: -25% YoY (vs INR109.3 crore; FY25 included INR24.1 crore deferred tax credit)

segments.name: Chennai Park (commenced Dec 2025)
segments.commentary: December footfall about 75,000 at launch; Q4 footfall about 1.91 lakh per management's figure cited by analyst. Management says first full quarter performance is in line with mature Kochi and Hyderabad parks, with Q4 EBITDA margin about 30%.

segments.commentary: FY26 footfall down about 7% YoY, attributed to summer weather and early monsoon, a school-group ban after road incidents (est. 50,000-60,000 footfall impact), and softer Q3 school groups. Management says it is still strong on a two-year basis.

Management expects EBITDA margins to settle around 40% over the next year as launch costs fade, subject to all parks including Chennai delivering.
A&P spend to be maintained at 7-8% of top line; no launch expenses expected in Q1 FY27.

Management says non-ticket revenue share should move towards 50:50 within 4-5 years, with 40:60 near term.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex: no large projects; sustaining capex INR35-40 crore.
