Hyderabad softness linked to weather and school-group ban; Ramoji Film City cited as a non-competing film city.
Management guides against predicting footfall or EBITDA until a full year at Chennai is complete.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Chennai footfall moderate to about 64,000 per month after strong December start, and what is happening in Hyderabad (FY26 footfall down 7%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Chennai: December launch month had higher marketing spend and Christmas seasonality; Jan-Feb are lean months. Hyderabad: early monsoon, Operation Sindoor-linked demand softness in summer 2025, and school-group weakness in Q3; management says two-year growth is still strong.

qa_highlights.question: Why are FY26 EBITDA margins only about 30% when older parks run around 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: corporate cost centre, one-time Labour Code costs, ESOP expenses, Chennai launch expenses and corporate setup costs are absorbed into the parks' margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the QIP-funded expansion been slow, and what is the status of new deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the shift to Tier 1 cities (land scarcity, slower government approvals) is the only cause; it is in talks with at least 4 state governments and hopes to close 1-2 deals this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for depreciation and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Chennai adds about INR45-50 crore annual depreciation; new investments add 8-10% of cost to annual depreciation. Margins expected to normalise towards 40% as parks mature.

qa_highlights.question: Will Bangalore resort ADR move after refurbishment?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects a 7-12% ADR increase from the current about INR6,300 after the refurbishment.

qa_highlights.question: Why do new rides not drive repeat visits?
qa_highlights.answer: MD: day outings need planning and most guests visit once a year or less; repeat rates are structurally low, and the core target is the 10-25 age group.

risks_watch: Hyderabad footfall trend: second consecutive year of decline, with FY26 footfall down about 7%.
Chennai sustainability: management declines to forecast beyond one full year; Q4 Chennai footfall moderated from the December launch peak.
Discretionary spend and West Asia tensions could pressure FY27 demand and supply chains.
Pace of new park additions: depends on Tier 1 land and state approvals; no deal signed yet.
Depreciation step-up of about INR45-50 crore in FY27 from Chennai, plus launch-cost normalisation to test margin recovery.

538446|2026-03.headline: Moneyboxx Q4 FY26 total income rose to INR63.23 crore (from INR52 crore), but Q4 PAT was only INR0.47 crore amid high credit costs and AUM at INR893 crore.
538446|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of transition, correction and strengthening, after MFI guardrails and stress in small-ticket secured lending hit collections and asset quality. Secured loans rose to about 68% of AUM (from 45% a year earlier), and collection efficiency was around 93.5% for the quarter. Gross NPA was 3.59% and net NPA 1.75%, both lower year on year, but Q4 profit was thin and AUM was down versus last year due to an ARC transaction. Management guided to AUM growth of 43-44% for FY27 and a sharp pickup in disbursements from May 2026, while acknowledging moderate growth so far.

Secured disbursements were 67% versus 49% last year; target is nearly 80% secured AUM by March 2027. Average secured ticket size is INR6 lakh, with run-rate INR8-9 lakh.

segments.commentary: Launched in FY26; disbursements were about INR50 lakh in April, ramping roughly 10x in May to a possible INR5 crore. Management targets about 10% of AUM by March 2027. Average ticket about INR4 lakh, tenure about 4 years, yield about 22-24% including fees, with a second-loss fee guarantee after 3% first loss.

segments.commentary: Unsecured lending to be restricted to one state; below INR5 lakh secured ticket discontinued in most branches from April. A small digital unsecured lending initiative is planned to start in the current quarter, enabled by the in-house LOS Moneyboxx One.

Management sees collection stress concentrated in the INR3-4 lakh secured ticket segment; SARFAESI and Section 138 actions started from May 2026.
Management expects a seasonal April-June weakness to be offset by solar loans, which peak in those months.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the post-MFI-guardrail shift, a senior team overhaul, decentralised credit and removal of sub-INR5 lakh secured tickets. It said top leadership is now in place, and that disbursements and AUM should grow month-on-month from May-June 2026, with FY27 AUM growth of 43-44% projected.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost appears high relative to AUM; how will opex come down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged high cost, attributing it to low AUM and hiring experienced staff; said cost should fall as AUM grows and that 20-25% of monthly business will come through partnerships without a sales team.

qa_highlights.question: Will the shift to secured lending lower yields, and what are the ROA/ROE targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management accepted that yields will fall on secured and partnership business, but said lower opex and credit cost should offset this. It cited peers at 12-15% returns on assets as the benchmark, without giving specific ROA/ROE targets.

qa_highlights.question: Any new geographies or products planned?
qa_highlights.answer: No new states in FY27; the 12-state footprint is considered sufficient. Solar is the new product (about 10% of AUM targeted), with one or two more products and a cattle-loan FLDG partnership planned this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is demand slowing due to macro uncertainty and inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said appetite exists, but lenders have tightened norms and some demand has declined. Lending to restaurants was paused due to LPG shortage. It pointed to green shoots in the MFI segment and government guarantee support for working-capital loans.

Net interest and fee income fell to INR31.02 crore from INR38.52 crore, NIM dropped to 12.3% from 14.36%, and PAT was INR0.21 crore versus INR0.24 crore. Management pointed to partnership channels, solar lending and a digital product as the next growth drivers, with secured AUM targeted at about 80% by March 2027.

538562|2026-03.headline: Skipper Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR1,666 crore (+29.4% YoY) and PAT rose 70% to INR75.6 crore; FY27 guided to 15% revenue and ~30% PAT growth.
538562|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter to date: revenue INR1,666 crore (+29.4% YoY), EBITDA INR173.4 crore (+40.2%, margin 10.4% vs 9.6%) and PAT INR75.6 crore (+70%, margin 4.5%). FY26 revenue reached INR5,552.8 crore (+20%) with PAT of INR207.3 crore (+42%) and EBITDA margin of 10.3%. Order book closed at a record INR8,501.9 crore on record FY26 inflows of INR5,678 crore, but management flagged a temporary slowdown in domestic bidding and export disruption from the Middle East conflict, and guided FY27 conservatively at 15% revenue growth. Trade receivables rose sharply to INR1,485 crore, which management attributed mainly to a INR260 crore collection slipping into April and higher domestic billing.

segments.name: Engineering (T&D)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,248 crore, up over 33% YoY; FY26 revenue INR4,359 crore, up 24% YoY on transmission infrastructure demand.

segments.name: Polymer
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue crossed INR500 crore (about INR507 crore) as a record; volumes grew about 40% while value growth was lower due to lower commodity prices. Margin still low single digit.

segments.commentary: Management said non-T&D is about 14% of the order book, mainly O&M for a BSNL project; infra revenue is largely T&D-driven. Order book has fallen from about INR2,000 crore to about INR1,000 crore over 6-7 quarters, per analyst.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: about 15% revenue growth (conservative, on an elevated base) and about 30% bottom-line growth, which management said is backed by the existing order book rather than new orders.
No explicit FY27 EBITDA margin number; management expects some margin improvement over FY26 but called it a challenging year with higher costs. Long-term aspiration is 12% EBITDA margin.
Management expects a return to 20-25% growth from FY28 as exports reopen and domestic bidding recovers; order awarding expected to approach FY25 levels from FY27.
FY27 capex guided at about INR250 crore, similar to prior years.
Export order book targeted to rise to 25% and eventually 50% of the order book (currently about 10%).
capex_capacity: Capacity expansion of 75,000 tonnes is due for commissioning by June 2026 (spillover from March), taking capacity to 450,000 tpa; utilisation above 85%.
Further 75,000 tpa planned in each of FY27 and FY28, targeting 600,000 tpa by FY28.
Management expects significant use of the new 75,000 tpa from Q3 FY27; full utilisation takes a couple of quarters. Expansion is expected to add about INR1,000-1,200 crore revenue annually.
Test Bed 2 commissioned, giving dual test beds at one location; a 293-tonne tower test set a record and a 350-tonne test is planned next month.
Growing substation business: about 4 high-voltage substation projects currently being executed.
demand_pricing: Order book INR8,501.9 crore (90% domestic, 10% export); FY26 inflows INR5,678 crore; Q4 inflow INR1,029 crore.
Bidding pipeline over INR33,000 crore, about 60-65% domestic and balance export; historical order conversion of 20-25%.

FY26 domestic bidding was well below FY25 because of ROW, forest clearance and transformer/HVDC equipment constraints; several projects (e.g., Krishnagiri REZ Ph-1, Vizag-Kakinada-Tuticorin, 800 kV Barmer HVDC) slipped into FY27. Management said bidding rebounded in April.

Export pressure: Middle East disruption and higher sea freight are slowing decisions in export markets; management said freight is largely passed through via FOB/CIF renegotiation and export is about 10% of the order book.
Pricing: mix of variable- and firm-price contracts; management said firm-price contracts carry buffers for commodity inflation. Raw materials are 100% indigenous.

Market share: Power Grid holds about 50% of TBCB bids and is over 90% of the domestic order book; private developers under 10%. Skipper claims about 50% of transmission-line capex as addressable (about INR50,000 crore on a INR1 lakh crore annual base).

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables almost double to INR1,485 crore despite 20% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a INR260 crore receipt due in late March came in on 1-2 April, and domestic Q4 revenue rose about 45% YoY with longer domestic realisation cycles plus GST; INR600-700 crore was already realised in April. Management said none of the debtors are sticky.

qa_highlights.question: What conversion ratio applies to the INR33,000 crore pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Historically 20-25%; management hopes to maintain that but declined to give an inflow number.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 revenue guidance only 15% if order book is strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Export execution is uncertain given geopolitics and export orders are unlikely to execute this year; management called 15% conservative on an elevated base, with effort to beat it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for FY27 EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: No exact guidance; management expects to improve on FY26's about 50 bps gain, with long-term aim of 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company move more capacity to domestic and maintain 20% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said domestic bidding was weak in FY26 and it is pursuing domestic opportunities, but kept guidance conservative; 20-25% growth expected from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company positioned for private-developer HVDC projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Private players are under 10% of the order book; management is in active talks with Tata Power, Adani and Resonia and says it is fully qualified for HVDC, currently executing a couple of HVDC projects.

qa_highlights.question: Are polymer non-Eastern market gains on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes grew about 40%, and presence has expanded outside the East, but the company is still small versus national players and remains focused on the Eastern region.

qa_highlights.question: Is the substation business margin-dilutive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said substation projects carry margins similar to the Engineering business on a project basis, though infra EPC is lower margin in general.

538562|2026-06.headline: Skipper Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4.5% to a record INR1,310 crore, EBITDA up 10% to INR140 crore, margin 10.7%; FY27 guided at 15% growth.

538567|2026-03.headline: Gulf Oil Q4 FY26 posted record quarter: 45,000 KL lubricant volume (+14%), EBITDA INR 135 crore, FY26 revenue above INR 4,000 crore.
538567|2026-03.overview: Management reported record quarterly volume, revenue and EBITDA for Q4 FY26, with lubricant volume up about 14% and revenue up about 14%. FY26 lubricant volume grew 10.5% to 1,68,000 KL, and consolidated revenue crossed INR 4,000 crore for the first time. Margin pressure is building from the Middle East crisis and rupee depreciation, with crude moving from about USD 65-70 in February to USD 90-120 in March onward. Management is prioritising supply security and per-litre price pass-through, and is holding its 12-14% EBITDA margin band as the target. The Board recommended a record FY26 dividend of INR 51 per share, including a INR 30 final.

538635|2026-06.headline: Snowman guides 10-15% top-line growth for FY27 despite war-driven volume dip; Gateway ICD volumes stagnant, DFC-JNPT link now complete.
538635|2026-06.overview: Joint Gateway Distriparks and Snowman Logistics call covering Q1 FY27. Management attributed the volume softness to the West Asia conflict (since April), which cut imports sharply in April-May, and to July weather disruptions at ports; market share is described as intact while the underlying market has de-grown. Snowman pricing rose 5-7% on average across warehousing customers, and management guided 10-15% top-line growth across all segments. Rail EBITDA was pressured by lower double-stacking (39% vs 40-42% earlier), higher underframe and empty running, and wage and fuel inflation, with relief expected from Q2. Management reported no specific Q1 financial figures in the call.

financial_highlights.change: reached after special dividend paid earlier this year
about 95% are customs bonds to government authorities

segments.name: Gateway ICD / rail
segments.commentary: Market share intact but market de-grew in operating regions; JNPT exposure about 5% of rail volume. Rail EBITDA per TEU fell on lower double-stacking, higher empty running and underframe usage, and wage and fuel costs.

segments.name: Snowman warehousing
segments.commentary: Pricing up 5-7% on average; about 24,000 additional pallets expected by end of FY27 (Pune first, then Patna).

segments.name: Snowman 5PL
segments.commentary: Service margin typically 5-6%; no new 5PL customer added in Q1, with new names possibly by Q3-Q4.

segments.name: CFS (Gateway)
segments.commentary: Volumes improved and a pricing increase taken to offset fuel and wage hikes; margin uplift possible in Q2. Management is not actively pursuing a sale.

segments.commentary: Around 500 containers a month currently, with scope to scale as network expands.

Management said June and July trends were similar to Q1 and declined to give specific monthly figures, citing listed-company restrictions.
Shipping lines reportedly prefer single-dip over double-dip on the West Coast, which could shift some volume to JNPT; management described this as early, exploratory.
JNPT is about 6 rail slabs more expensive than Mundra for North-bound rail haulage; industry talk of special haulage relief is unconfirmed.
Warehousing market shifting from unorganised to organised; competitive intensity described as ongoing, with CONCOR the largest rail competitor.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said share is intact and the market itself has de-graded due to the war; double-digit growth for the year is still expected once the situation clears.

qa_highlights.question: How much MAT credit supports the low cash tax rate, and when does full tax apply?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Kartik Aiyer said the company will pay at 18.88% for at least 7-8 years, using accumulated MAT credit; management noted cash tax rose only INR 1-2 crore YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why has rail EBITDA per TEU weakened, and what is the fix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower import share, lower double-stacking, higher underframe and empty running, port imbalance at Mundra and Pipavav, and steep wage hikes (Haryana up 35%); recovery expected as volumes return, with fuel impact visible in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the JNPT exposure and the economics of shifting to it?
qa_highlights.answer: JNPT is about 5% of rail volume; on current pricing it is more expensive for North-bound customers but yields higher revenue and slightly higher EBITDA per TEU for Gateway due to distance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the CFS business and its land?
qa_highlights.answer: A sale was explored about 1.5 years ago without a satisfactory valuation; no active process now, though management is open to a good offer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value of the land bank?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a formal valuation; cited Garhi (85-90 acres) at INR 25-30 crore per acre on outright purchase, with total land of about 475 acres.

Jaipur ICD litigation outcome (final arguments in September 2026) and Indore/Ankleshwar commissioning timelines.

538666|2026-03.headline: Sharda Cropchem FY26 PAT rose 124% to INR 681 crores on record revenue of INR 5,268 crores; FY27 revenue guided at 10-15%.
538666|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 13% YoY to INR 2,065 crores, with EBITDA up 75% to INR 513 crores and PAT up 57% to INR 319 crores. Gross margin expanded 750 bps to 37.3%, aided by a sharp rise in FX contribution (+11.7% in Q4). For FY26, revenue rose 22% to INR 5,268 crores, EBITDA rose 69% to INR 1,040 crores (19.7% margin), and PAT rose 124% to INR 681 crores. The company remains debt-free with INR 702 crores of cash and liquid investments. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 10-15%, gross margin around 35% plus or minus a few points, and EBITDA margin of 18-20%.

538666|2026-06.headline: Sharda Cropchem Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to Rs.1,074 crore and EBITDA 25% to Rs.178 crore, but reported PAT of Rs.88 crore was cushioned by lower forex gains.
538666|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 9% YoY to Rs.1,074 crore, with volume down 1.6% and forex contributing 12.7 points. EBITDA margin expanded 220 bps to 16.6% and gross margin rose 120 bps to 36.7%, driven by mix in NAFTA, LATAM and rest of world. Europe revenue softened as distributors cut stock after an unusual heatwave, though Europe gross margin improved to 44.2%. Forex gain fell to Rs.7.5 crore from Rs.73.1 crore, so reported PBT and PAT looked weaker, while management said PBT before forex grew 16% to Rs.111 crore. Management maintained FY27 guidance of 10-15% revenue growth and about 35% gross margin.

segments.commentary: Largest market; revenue softened as distributors cut stock after heatwave. Gross margin 44.2% vs 42.9% in Q1 FY26. Management said restocking has largely normalised.

segments.name: NAFTA
segments.commentary: Gross margin 32.8% vs 25.9% a year ago; growth strong and margins improved this quarter.

segments.name: LATAM
segments.commentary: Among the strongest growth engines this quarter, but gross margin fell to 16.9% from 28.0% a year ago.

segments.name: Rest of world
segments.commentary: Gross margin 30.8% vs 26.8% in Q1 FY26; growth reported as good with better profitability.

Management said prices are improving sequentially after a severe decline about two years ago.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO pointed to the investor presentation, which gives PBT and EBIT excluding forex. He said more clarity will be provided in future presentations.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe mix and price increases drove margins, LATAM volumes grew but margins dipped, and it expects Europe and NAFTA margins to stay in the same range.

538668|2026-03.headline: Meghna Infracon FY26 revenue rose 15.84% to INR46.2 crore, but PAT fell 4.28% as carry-over securities profits lapsed.
538668|2026-03.overview: Management described the company as transitioning from Naysaa Securities to a Mumbai-focused redevelopment developer. FY26 revenue from operations was INR46.2 crore versus INR39.88 crore, and Q4 revenue was INR18.48 crore, up 52.47% YoY. FY26 PAT was INR5.59 crore, down about 4.28% YoY, which management attributed to the absence of carry-over profits from the earlier securities business. Management guided to a sharp increase in GDV and profitability over the coming years, with current GDV pipeline stated above INR2,100 crore.

+52.47% YoY vs INR12.12 crore in Q4 FY25
Increase of about INR6.92 crore YoY as stated

segments.commentary: Wagle Estate commercial project, GDV INR300 crore, launch date blocked for 22 June 2026 subject to RERA. Meghna One is a Grade A gold-certified green building.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a shift to more premium projects and maturing projects from prior-year launches, which lifted collections.

qa_highlights.question: Unsold inventory across ongoing projects and FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Riviera has one unit left; Rivaan six unsold units with bookings pending registration; Pranam 30-35% conversion this quarter; Manju Villa three units; Joshville about 15% left.

qa_highlights.question: Which of the upcoming projects launch in FY27 and approval timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Wagle Estate launch 22 June 2026 pending RERA by end-June; Khar RERA delayed by pending approvals, bookings in Q2 2027; Bandra West launch Q2 2027 with bookings from Q3 2026; Juhu/Vile Parle slipping 15-20 days into Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Kandivali approvals and funding plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Land registration done; awaiting height approval from MoD. Self-funded so far; open to project-level debt, with pre-sales and accruals as main funding.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT and EBITDA margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Securities carry-over profits ended after the 2024 transition; project lifecycle delayed profit booking; higher delivery costs and acquisition costs compressed margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative despite profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Company aims to stay nearly debt-free; cash went into acquisitions of future projects that management expects to lift GDV and profit.

qa_highlights.question: Pace of project addition and GDV growth?

538685|2026-06.headline: Shemaroo Q1 FY27 revenue fell 6% to about INR 132 crore, but EBITDA loss narrowed to about INR 2 crore from INR 56 crore.
538685|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was about INR 132 crore, down 6% YoY, with digital down about 17% to INR 56 crore and traditional up 5% to INR 76 crore. EBITDA loss narrowed sharply to about INR 2 crore versus INR 56 crore a year earlier, after about INR 20 crore of new-initiative spend; excluding that, existing operations EBITDA was about INR 18 crore. Net loss reduced to about INR 8 crore. Management said this is the first quarter after the inventory charge-off exercise, now in a normal charge-off cycle, and guided to double-digit blended growth, EBITDA-positive for the year, and bottom-line positive next year.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of approx. INR 56 crore (call analyst cited 55.5 crore) in Q1 FY26
materially reduced YoY; no prior figure stated

segments.name: Digital media
segments.commentary: Revenue approx. INR 56 crore, down 17% YoY, as select B2B syndication deals were deferred on geopolitical uncertainty; consumer business grew on fresh content and ad monetisation. Management targets double-digit digital growth.

segments.name: Traditional media
segments.commentary: Revenue approx. INR 76 crore, up 5% YoY, helped by closure of B2B licensing deals that offset subdued ad environment. Management expects roughly flat traditional revenue for FY27, with near-term ad outlook subdued due to BARC ratings blackout.

segments.name: ShemarooMe (OTT, Gujarati)
segments.commentary: Acquired OHO Gujarati catalogue in April 2026 (over 22 Gujarati originals); released 10 new titles in the quarter. Company does not disclose subscriber, ARPU or revenue figures; management said it is about two years from OTT profitability.

segments.name: YouTube
segments.commentary: Approx. 9 billion views across channels in the quarter; Shemaroo Filmi Gaane passed 74.7 million subscribers and Shemaroo Entertainment 61.9 million. Management said views are seasonal but viewership share remains strong.

guidance_outlook: Blended revenue growth aim of healthy double digits over the next 2-3 years; digital targeted at double-digit growth, outpacing recent low-double-digit industry digital growth by a couple of percentage points.
Traditional media revenue expected flattish for FY27, not declining.
Aim for EBITDA-positive for full FY27 (conservative view); management expects bottom-line positive next year (FY28).
Debt reduction plan for FY27, but no quantified target given; quarterly fluctuations possible given geopolitical and BARC blackout impacts.
Aspiration of around 20% EBITDA margin in 2-3 years, not a committed target; management said it is not sure it will be achieved.
New-initiative spend to be cut by more than 50% in FY27 versus FY26; management said the company is on track.
capex_capacity: Content strategy shifted: new content creation scaled down in traditional, while new content acquisition is being scaled up in digital.
Traditional channel rationalisation possible; company now runs two FAST channels after earlier shrinking the number.
OTT (ShemarooMe) needs ongoing content and customer-acquisition spend (ATL, BTL and performance marketing); management said little upfront capex is needed.
Inventory of INR 348 crore at Q1 end; management said no remaining write-down risk and the company is now in a normal charge-off cycle.
demand_pricing: Digital decline attributed to deferred B2B syndication deals (geopolitical uncertainty) and lumpy B2B revenue; consumer digital grew on fresh content and better ad monetisation.
Traditional ad market subdued for a long period; BARC ratings blackout in recent month has hit traditional and syndication revenue.
Acquired content is priced competitively against other bidders, so new-content margins are lower than on legacy content already amortised or charged off.
YouTube Shorts monetisation has not moved meaningfully; company is focusing on connected-TV long-form content, and is only experimenting with micro-dramas.
FAST channel ecosystem globally has been shrinking for roughly 12-18 months; company is tracking it and scaling only if monetisation improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised EBITDA excluding the new-initiative investment, and what revenue is needed for positive EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding about INR 20 crore of new-initiative spend, EBITDA would have been about INR 18 crore. Management said margin depends on both revenue growth and cost cuts, and on revenue mix, so it would not give a revenue threshold.

qa_highlights.question: Is the content library under-monetised, and what growth is expected over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no under-utilisation, citing 9 billion views in the quarter. Traditional monetisation is declining while digital is growing. The aim is healthy double-digit blended growth, outdoing digital industry growth by a couple of points.

qa_highlights.question: Debt reduction plan and FY27 profitability and revenue mix?
qa_highlights.answer: A debt reduction plan exists for FY27 but no figure was given. EBITDA-positive for the year is the conservative aim, with bottom-line positive next year. Digital is seen at double-digit growth and traditional roughly flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why not grow digital faster, around 20%, given 9-10% CAGR over FY24-FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said industry underlying growth was low, and it would not burn cash to grow faster, since that would strain cash flow and the balance sheet. It cited its leadership in Gujarati entertainment.

qa_highlights.question: Which digital segments carry the highest margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin depends on content age, not platform. Legacy content can yield 80-90% margins, newly acquired content can be near zero or negative, and production work can earn 10-20%. YouTube is not inherently high-margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state margin, and is 20% EBITDA the aim on a reported basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management was not satisfied with current margins and aspires to upwards of 20% EBITDA in 2-3 years. It declined to say whether this is on a reported basis net of all investments, and said the structural shift in the media industry is a factor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and inventory at quarter end, and is further write-down likely?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt was INR 311 crore and inventory INR 348 crore at quarter end. Management said the company is in a normal charge-off cycle with no further rationalisation planned.

qa_highlights.question: How long until ShemarooMe reaches break-even, and will it disclose subscriber or revenue data?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is about two years from OTT break-even. It does not disclose DAU, MAU, subscriber, ARPU or platform revenue, and said it has no current plan to start.

risks_watch: Digital revenue fell 17% YoY on deferred B2B syndication deals; lumpy B2B timing could keep quarterly digital revenue volatile.
Traditional ad market remains weak and BARC ratings blackout is hurting traditional and syndication revenue.
Debt of INR 311 crore against an EBITDA-positive-for-year aim; quarterly debt movements may vary.
Limited disclosure: no OTT subscriber, ARPU or platform revenue data, and no quantified debt target; analysts asked for more granularity.
YouTube Shorts and micro-drama monetisation still unproven; a possible YouTube monetisation policy update was not confirmed.
538685|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the operating trajectory and cost discipline, but evasive on specifics: it declined to give debt targets, OTT data, profitability timing, or a revenue threshold for breakeven. It acknowledged margins are below its own aspiration.
key_quotes: Every quarter, I think we should be seeing an improvement on a quarter-on-quarter basis.
Are we satisfied with it? Definitely not.
I think if I see a 2 -3 year perspective, I think definitely upwards of 20% EBITDA is something that we should aim for.

538715|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12.5% to INR264.48 crores, EBITDA up 45.6% to INR54.59 crores at a 20.6% margin, with the order book at a record INR174 crores.
538715|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 12.5% to INR264.48 crores, below management's earlier 20-25% target, because supplies on some large UPVC window and door projects in Maharashtra and Delhi NCR were deferred by buyers. Profitability improved sharply: EBITDA margin expanded 460 bps to 20.6%, PAT rose 67.2% to INR30.14 crores, and Q4 EBITDA margin crossed 21%. The company deployed about INR27 crores of capex in FY26 under a Board-approved INR100 crores programme spanning FY26-FY28, and entered aluminium windows and facade with INR56 crores of orders. Working capital rose as management paid suppliers early and stocked PVC resin and polymers ahead of West Asia-related price increases.

financial_highlights.change: Management says it will not reach 0.75
Record high; vs INR120-140 crores last year

segments.name: PVC/UPVC polymer products
segments.commentary: Management said about 84% of FY26 revenue (about INR220 crores) came from PVC and UPVC, of which about INR60 crores was UPVC windows and the rest PVC profiles. EBITDA margin in this segment was higher than modular; PBT margin was about 16.6%.

segments.name: Modular furniture (Dynasty)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR43 crores (about 16% of sales), with PBT margin around 9%, which management said was up about 80% YoY. Four new builder brands were added, including Godrej, M3M and Smart Homes, and exports to Europe are growing.

segments.name: Plastic profile core segment
segments.commentary: Revenue grew over 13% and segment profitability rose 63%, per management. PVC profile capacity rose by 3,600 MT to 27,600 MT per annum, with utilisation around 66% in FY26.

segments.name: Aluminium windows and facade (Bangalore/Jaipur)
segments.commentary: New vertical under Mr. Varghese with INR56 crores of orders and revenue starting in Q4 FY26. Management guides INR40-50 crores of FY27 revenue; it targets EBITDA margins of about 20%.

segments.name: WPC doors and WPC wall/ceiling panels
segments.commentary: WPC door line (about INR10 crores capex) has finished trials and is due for commercial launch in Q2 FY27. Management expects about INR15 crores of FY27 revenue; WPC wall and ceiling profile lines are planned for Q3-Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Long-term target of about 30% revenue CAGR while sustaining EBITDA and PAT margins; management says 20%+ EBITDA margin is sustainable.
FY27 PVC profile extrusion volume growth of at least 20%; modular furniture growth of 20-25% expected.
FY27 new-capex revenue addition of INR55-60 crores, with aluminium facade INR40-50 crores and WPC doors about INR15 crores.
INR100 crores capex over FY26-FY28: about INR27 crores in FY26, INR35-40 crores in FY27 and INR20-30 crores in FY28.
Existing extrusion capacity can deliver more than INR450 crores of profile revenue at 85% utilisation; management did not give a year for reaching it.
Working capital expected to improve materially in FY27 as inventory is consumed and supplier payment cycles normalise.
capex_capacity: PVC profile extrusion capacity raised by 3,600 MT from 24,000 MT to 27,600 MT per annum in FY26; utilisation about 66%, with 80% cited as the practical benchmark.
WPC door line: machines commissioned and trials underway; commercial launch expected from Q2 FY27. WPC door capacity not yet finalised.
WPC wall and ceiling profile extrusion planned for Q3-Q4 FY27.
Aluminium windows and facade: Bangalore unit implemented; a new Jaipur factory site is under construction with capex planned in FY27. Custom fabrication, so no defined capacity.
Management expects ROE and ROCE of about 25-26% to be sustained on the new capex; it also said the new capex would earn similar returns across segments.
demand_pricing: Order book INR174 crores: UPVC windows and doors about INR84 crores, modular furniture about INR34 crores, aluminium windows and facade about INR56 crores; 100% expected to execute in 18-24 months.
Price hikes: three price revisions since the West Asia conflict began, up to 30 April. Management estimated 15-18% raw material cost inflation across its product lines.
Roughly 30% of revenue is fixed-price; B2B PVC profile distribution (over 60% of revenue) carries price revision clauses. Aluminium projects carry NALCO-linked base-price pass-through clauses.
Management said PVC resin fell from about INR115 in March to INR80-85 now; prices can move both ways.
Mobilisation advances of 10-20% of project value; net advances exceed INR7 crores versus about INR5 crores last year.
Management says WPC doors have no direct competition in India today; aluminium facade faces large international system brands and local fabricators.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the shortfall versus the 20-25% growth target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said buyers deferred supply on some large UPVC window and door projects in Maharashtra and one or two in Delhi NCR. Order book was healthy and the shortfall was described as timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is a 20%+ EBITDA margin sustainable amid raw-material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing product mix, upgraded offerings for upper-middle and high-end customers, and pre-buying of raw materials in February-March. It expects price revisions to offset the 15-18% input cost rise.

qa_highlights.question: Why did payables fall to almost zero and inventory and receivables rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it paid suppliers in full in the last two months of FY26 to secure supply during the Middle East disruption and bought PVC resin and polymers heavily in March. Receivables rose only in line with revenue, and it expects the cycle to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 volume growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to at least 20% volume growth in PVC profile extrusion, with new verticals adding on top. Price growth was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR100 crores capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly internal accruals (about INR50 crores of operating cash generation in FY26), with some borrowing. Debt-to-equity is currently 0.56 and is not expected to reach 0.75.

risks_watch: Revenue timing risk: deferred project deliveries by buyers caused the FY26 shortfall against the 20-25% target.
Raw material and aluminium price volatility tied to crude oil and LME aluminium; the aluminium contracts carry base-price clauses, but UPVC and modular contracts are largely fixed-price.
Working capital: inventory build, receivables growth and near-zero payables; management guided to normalisation in FY27.
Execution of the new WPC door launch in Q2 FY27 and the aluminium facade ramp-up, including the Jaipur factory build.
The 30% CAGR target rests on new verticals with no revenue history; management has not disclosed WPC capacity figures.
Margin sustainability: management says 20%+ EBITDA margin is durable, but competitive pricing and price-cut pressure are noted in the call.
538715|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on margins, capex and the 30% CAGR target, but defensive on the FY26 revenue miss and the working capital build. Several answers were vague on volumes, pricing and WPC capacity, and some figures were corrected during the call.
key_quotes: Q4 was our strongest quarter ever, with EBITDA margin crossing 21% and PAT growth of nearly 55% year-on-year.
Importantly, this is a matter of timing, not a loss of business, as our underlying demand remains robust.
Based on our current visibility, we are targeting approximately 30% CAGR revenue growth over the long term while maintaining sustainable EBITDA and PAT margins.
It's a cost-plus pricing, definitely it's a cost-plus pricing.

rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 460 bps to 20.6% in FY26 with Q4 above 21%, management calls 20%+ sustainable, and price revisions are expected to offset a 15-18% input cost rise; competitive price-cut pressure is a counterweight.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: PVC profile capacity rose 3,600 MT to 27,600 MT in FY26 (about 15%), WPC door line starts commercial launch in Q2 FY27, WPC wall/ceiling lines are planned for Q3-Q4 FY27, and the Jaipur aluminium factory is under construction with FY27 capex.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides a minimum 20% growth in PVC profile extrusion volume, with PVC utilisation at only 66%, a record INR174 crore order book, and modular growth guided at 20-25%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: A Board-approved INR100 crore programme already covers FY26-FY28 (INR27 crore spent, INR35-40 crore in FY27), so new announcements depend on the WPC and Jaipur ramp; utilisation is only 66%, well below the 80% benchmark, which argues against an immediate new plant.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Order book is a record INR174 crore versus INR120-140 crore last year, and FY27 new-capex revenue is guided at INR55-60 crore, but FY26 revenue grew only 12.5% against a 20-25% target.

rows.why: FY26 revenue missed the 20-25% target at 12.5% because buyers deferred UPVC projects in Maharashtra and Delhi NCR; the 30% CAGR is long-term with no year, and the WPC and aluminium ramps have no revenue history.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: WPC door line has finished trials and is due for commercial launch in Q2 FY27, with about INR15 crore of FY27 revenue expected; WPC wall and ceiling profiles follow in Q3-Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Record INR174 crore order book
rows.why: Order book is INR174 crore versus INR120-140 crore last year, with UPVC about INR84 crore, modular about INR34 crore and aluminium about INR56 crore, all expected to execute in 18-24 months.

rows.label: Working capital normalisation in FY27
rows.why: Payables fell to near zero after full supplier payments in the last two months of FY26, and inventory was built ahead of West Asia price rises; management expects the cycle to normalise in FY27, while net mobilisation advances rose to over INR7 crore from about INR5 crore.

rows.label: Raw material price revisions
rows.why: Three price revisions since the West Asia conflict, with 15-18% input inflation estimated; B2B PVC distribution (over 60% of revenue) has price revision clauses, but about 30% of revenue is fixed-price and PVC resin has fallen from about INR115 to INR80-85.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins above 20%, the INR100 crore capex and the 30% CAGR, but defensive on the FY26 revenue miss, the working capital build and vague WPC capacity figures; analysts pushed on volumes, pricing and the revenue shortfall.

538730|2026-03.headline: PDS FY26 revenue rose 4% to ₹13,110 crores, Q4 PAT nearly doubled QoQ to ₹72 crores, and the order book is up ~11% to ₹5,074 crores.

Q4 PAT rose about 95% QoQ to ₹72 crores on better operating leverage, cost control and lower finance costs. Net debt fell to about ₹105 crores from ₹374 crores despite the Knit Gallery acquisition. Management guided to mid-single-digit revenue growth and ~10% profit growth for FY27, with gross margin up 40-50 bps a year and opex growth below top-line growth; analysts pressed on the gap between order-book growth and the guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~16-17 day working capital sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not go back to 17 days and aims to hold current levels for the year, with quarterly fluctuations possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Poeticgem and Simple Approach margins erode?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to one-time redundancy costs from the BCG-led efficiency programme in H2; both verticals are expected to return to profit growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the order book growth (11%) not translate into higher revenue growth (5-6%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited customer caution on inventory and shipment pushbacks; UK and Europe order book is only ~3-4%, Asia ~8-9%, Americas ~30%.

qa_highlights.question: How does PDS keep winning share with retailers like Walmart?
qa_highlights.answer: Pallak Seth said 70-80% of retailer sourcing goes through third-party vendors and that PDS offers four services: manufacturing, strategic vendor (design-led sourcing), sourcing-as-a-service, and brands.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the Ted Baker (New Lobster) business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is negotiating with ABG for ~$2-2.5 million a year in financial support for 12 months, with a request to extend it for 24 more months; a conclusion is expected in 4-6 weeks.

Concentration in top-10 clients (two faced challenges in FY26); top-10 growth guided at ~7-8%.

538730|2026-06.headline: PDS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% to ₹3,444 crore, EBITDA up 90% to ₹96 crore, and net debt fell 73% to ₹29 crore.
538730|2026-06.overview: PDS reported Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹3,444 crore (+15% YoY), with gross margin up 63 bps to 20% and EBITDA of ₹96 crore (margin 2.8%, +111 bps). PAT rose 43% YoY to ₹29 crore, though other income fell to ₹9 crore from ₹40 crore that included a ₹22 crore FX gain last year. Order book grew 23% YoY to ₹6,095 crore, and management announced new mandates with annual potential of about US$330 million. Net working capital fell to 1 day and net debt to ₹29 crore, with management stating a commitment to low single-digit working capital days.

vs ₹40 crore in Q1 FY26 (which included ~₹22 crore FX gain)
+11% YoY in INR; flat in USD
down 73% from ₹105 crore at Mar-26; net debt/equity 0.02x, net debt/EBITDA 0.07x

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹227 crore (+4% YoY), EBIT ₹15 crore, EBIT margin 6.5%; management aims to upgrade customer mix toward fashion customers via the Busana partnership.

capex_capacity: Asset-light sourcing model used to add capacity; management said it could onboard 4-5 third-party factories within ~6 months for a large account, versus a US$50-60 million manufacturing investment otherwise.
Depreciation increase reflects Knit Gallery acquisition and capitalisation of UK office property.
Ongoing SAP upgrade to S/4HANA and AI/digital investment across sourcing, pricing, supply management and operations.

US accounts reopened or added: Coles, Walmart, Fashion Nova, T.J. Maxx, PBS, American Eagle; management says 70-80% of key US accounts are now opened.
Europe: growth from Mango (Spain), CCC (Poland); Gerry Weber's bankruptcy replaced by new German accounts.

New Lobster (brand management) revenue ~₹100 crore in Q1; other licensed brands ~₹350 crore annually (~₹90 crore per quarter) and profitable.

qa_highlights.question: Order book up 23% and Q4 up 11% versus earlier mid-single-digit guidance; should growth be much higher this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Jain said the order book has shaped up well and management is positive, but asked analysts to focus on Q2 repeating the Q1 trend and to revisit guidance after mid-year.

qa_highlights.question: Are new-vertical investments on track for the ~₹80 crore annual scale-down, given Q1 at ₹37 crore, and how will US investment and PBT be factored in?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects more profitability over coming quarters and said the full-year P&L impact of new initiatives would broadly be in line with prior expectations; no explicit ₹80 crore reconfirmation was given.

qa_highlights.question: Finance cost stayed flat despite lower net debt; will it keep rising with factoring as revenue grows?
qa_highlights.answer: Sadik Sunasara said interest cost is not going up, with quarterly ups and downs possible. Sanjay Jain said USD interest cost is stagnant and directionally flat or lower, with early payment discounts (EPD) offsetting interest, and more EPD-vs-gross-margin disclosure from Q2. Average USD borrowing cost is about 7-8%.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI a cost-saving lever only or also a revenue driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Pallak Seth said AI currently drives productivity, citing a China subsidiary with 60 staff whose turnover doubled to $120 million, with local software under $25,000 a year. Customer-facing AI design helped win the French retailer contract.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1-day working capital a cyclical mix effect or structural, and could it return to negative as in FY23?
qa_highlights.answer: Sadik Sunasara said the 1 day reflects a higher share of factorable receivables; structurally management guides to low single-digit days, with 0 to 1 days possible in some quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Americas (+48%) and Europe (+21%) growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Pallak Seth said 70-80% of key US accounts are now open and volumes are scaling, with Coles, Walmart, Fashion Nova, T.J. Maxx, PBS and American Eagle cited. In Europe, growth came from Mango (Spain) and CCC (Poland), with new German accounts replacing Gerry Weber.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the 555 target today given macro and currency factors?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Jain said 555 remains a long-term goal; the Gerry Weber and Matalan (about US$140 million to US$70 million) setbacks cost 12-18 months of stabilisation. Management now focuses on sequential EBITDA margin and PAT improvement each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the outsourced opportunity and how does PDS grow wallet share once inside a retailer? Is there a risk retailers bypass PDS to deal with factories directly?
qa_highlights.answer: Pallak Seth cited Marks & Spencer exploring a 50/50 in-house vs third-party split, with a US$100 million opportunity that PDS could serve asset-light with 4-5 third-party factories in about 6 months versus US$50-60 million of capex. He said standalone factories have little value and PDS's factories are the next tier, not the top 5-10.

qa_highlights.question: How much Ted Baker loss is in Q1 and for FY27, and what is the resolution path?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Jain said Q1 Ted Baker PBT loss was about US$2 million and FY27 losses should not exceed US$2-3 million. Discussions with Authentic Brands Group are ongoing after franchisee administration in the UK and US.

qa_highlights.question: What profit can sourcing-as-a-service and brand management generate over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Jain said the ~₹1,700 crore GMV under execution produced ~₹42 crore revenue (~2.5% of GMV) and ~₹10 crore PBT (~25% of revenue), excluding newly signed contracts. Brand management is separate; ~₹350 crore a year of licensed brands earns about ₹90 crore a quarter profitably, while New Lobster is about ₹100 crore a quarter and being fixed.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 delivery: management asked that Q2 repeat Q1 trend; guidance to be revisited after mid-year.
Finance cost trajectory: flat-to-down in USD terms depends on EPD offsetting interest; watch the promised EPD vs gross margin disclosure from Q2.
Ted Baker and New Lobster: FY27 losses guided at up to US$2-3 million; resolution with Authentic Brands Group still pending.

Account concentration and client risk: Matalan halved from ~US$140 million to ~US$70 million, Gerry Weber bankruptcy; US$330 million annual mandates and the French retailer GMV (US$300-400 million option) still ramping over 12-24 months.
Sourcing concentration: more than 50% of sourcing from Bangladesh; diversification into India (Knit Gallery) and Egypt is at early stage.
Working capital at 1 day relies on factoring of receivables; sustainability of low single-digit days and of the factoring-led interest mix.
key_quotes: So my request and specific response to your question is that let's stay focused on one more healthy quarter and maybe post the mid of the year, we can revisit any of the guidance or anything.

But rather than talking of 555 and the time horizon. We believe in it, what is important is that every quarter now, there should be improvement in the EBITDA margin, which we have achieved in quarter 1 and the corresponding improvement in PAT.
So, to summarize, dollar terms, interest cost stagnant, had we not allowed EPD to come up, the interest costs should have been gone south, but we will keep supplementing it as the quarters pass by.
A factory in the middle of Asia has zero value in my view, zero value.

538734|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR171 crore with EBITDA margin at 23.6%, but order inflow lagged and management pushed new order wins into Q2 FY27.

Full-year FY26 operating revenue was INR661 crore (up 58%), EBITDA INR145 crore (21.9% margin) and PAT INR133 crore (up 111%). Q4 order booking was only INR62 crore, and management said several Q4 closures slipped into Q1 and Q2 FY27. Analysts pressed on order inflow, unbilled revenue (around INR330-350 crore), receivables aging, and the loss-making US subsidiary (VTS), where management guided to breakeven in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is happening on the acquisition front and what is the funds plan?

qa_highlights.question: Receivables and recovery from government clients?

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade payables and unbilled revenue rise?

qa_highlights.question: Status and outlook of VTS (US subsidiary)?

qa_highlights.question: Order book execution period and pipeline?

538962|2026-06.headline: Minda Corporation Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR 1,846 crore (+33.2% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 212 crore at an 11.5% margin.
538962|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 33.2% YoY to INR 1,846 crore, up 8% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR 212 crore (11.5% margin, +19 bps YoY). PAT of INR 206 crore included a one-time exceptional gain of INR 106 crore from consolidating Minda VAST. Associate Flash Electronics grew revenue 42% YoY to INR 533 crore but its EBITDA margin dipped to 15.4% on commodity and labour costs. Management said the quarter was margin-pressured by raw material, freight and wage inflation, with pass-through mechanisms expected to recover it over one to two quarters.

financial_highlights.change: +216% YoY from INR 65 crore; includes INR 106 crore exceptional gain from Minda VAST consolidation

financial_highlights.change: Share of group revenue rose from 15% to 19%
vs 6.5% in Q1 FY26; Q4 FY26 about 6.5-7%

segments.name: Mobility mix (revenue)

segments.name: Minda VAST (JV, now consolidated)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 22% YoY in the quarter; margin 8.4% vs 6.5% a year earlier. Kit value about INR 8,000-13,000 per vehicle.

Switches order (lifetime order book above INR 1,000 crore): SOP expected in Q1 FY28; about INR 150 crore revenue in FY28 and peak in FY29.
Turntide motor controller SOPs expected in October-November 2026.

Flash margin dip expected to reverse in one to two quarters as indexation with customers aligns.
Furukawa share of profit (17.5% holding) expected to be temporary dip.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guidance about INR 400 crore, spread across verticals and divisions, not specific to EV.

Order wins spread across vehicle access, castings, wiring harness, clusters and new energy and electronics, across ICE and EV, two-wheeler, PV and CV, domestic and export.
Export order book about 8-10% of total order book.
Flash domestic/international split: about 90% India, 10% international.

qa_highlights.question: Raghunandhan NL (Nuvama): How will order ramp-ups in clusters and wiring harness support FY27 and FY28 sales, and what categories were the Q1 order wins in?
qa_highlights.answer: Wiring harness grew more than 30% YoY and instrument cluster more than 35% YoY in Q1, with momentum expected to continue into FY28. Q1 order wins spanned vehicle access, castings, wiring harness, clusters and new energy/electronics, across ICE and EV, two-wheeler, PV, CV, domestic and export, described as evenly split.

qa_highlights.question: What were Minda VAST's revenue and EBITDA in Q1, and what are its growth and margin prospects?
qa_highlights.answer: VAST revenue grew 22% YoY, lifting group passenger vehicle share from 15% to 19% with consolidation. Margin was 8.4% vs 6.5% in Q1 FY26. Kit value is about INR 8,000-13,000 per vehicle, with products under development that could lift it, spread across PV OEMs in India and exports to Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Can Flash grow 30% for the full year given EV demand, and what margin is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 20-24% YoY growth for Flash, citing the need to build capacity first. Long-term Flash EBITDA margin is expected at 16-17%, with the Q1 dip attributed to labour and commodity inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex guidance and its EV vs core split? What are the Turntide SOP timing and utilisation? How does group margin compare with peers, and can contract labour help?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR 400 crore, not allocated specifically to EV or ICE. Turntide SOPs are expected in October-November 2026, with lines being tested. Group capacity utilisation is about 77-80%. Management said the group is in the first quartile of the industry and guided group EBITDA of 11.5-12% for the rest of FY27, with 12.5% targeted by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Vipul Kumar (Narnolia): Is there a revenue shortfall of INR 3,000-3,500 crore against the FY30 target, and what levers close it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the estimate and reiterated INR 17,500 crore by FY30 from existing business growth, premiumisation, exports, new products (about INR 4,600 crore) and inorganic opportunities. It said organic growth is tracking about 30%.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue did Minda VAST merger add, and what was the Q4 FY26 VAST margin? Can cost inflation be passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidation added about INR 125 crore of revenue. Q4 FY26 VAST margin was about 6.5-7%. Most index-linked commodities have back-to-back pass-through with a lag of a quarter or two, and customers are expected to support pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did share of profit from associates and JVs fall from about INR 31 crore to about INR 18 crore, and is the Furukawa contribution recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Flash PAT contribution fell to about INR 18-19 crore from about INR 25 crore in Q4 FY26, due to excess depreciation at Flash. Furukawa contributed INR 80 lakh vs INR 5 crore in Q4. Management called the dip temporary, expecting Flash back on track in one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the sunroof SOP for Q2 on track, and what is the status of the passenger vehicle EV motor work at Flash?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunroof (Spark Minda HCMF) product trials were approved first time and the SOP is on track for Q2. Flash has magnet-less motors across segments, some under customer testing, with one PV customer engagement and two or three partnerships pending.

qa_highlights.question: What are the switches order ramp and Flash cross-selling expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Switches lifetime order book exceeds INR 1,000 crore, with SOP in Q1 FY28, about INR 150 crore revenue in FY28 and peak in FY29. Die casting cross-sell for Flash started in August 2026, with wiring harness under testing; no specific INR 50-70 crore figure was confirmed.

Pass-through lag on raw material, freight and wage costs; a one-to-two quarter lag could keep group margin near 11.5% against the 11.5-12% guide.
Flash growth of 20-24% against EV demand and capacity build-out; management said capacity must be added first.

Quality of Q1 profit: PAT of INR 206 crore includes a INR 106 crore one-time exceptional gain from VAST consolidation; underlying PAT is much lower.
Vision 2030 target of INR 17,500 crore, disputed by an analyst on the FY30 gap; watch the organic growth rate versus the about 30% cited.
key_quotes: So, this is the same momentum which is expected to continue over the upcoming quarters, going into FY28 as well.
And we are very confident that on a longer -term basis, the company should maintain a margin anywhere between 16% to 17%.
There will be pressure, but given that these are all exceptional times, we have to support customers, customers will also support us.
We believe that Flash will be back on track in the next one or two quarters.

538979|2026-03.headline: Greenlam Q4 FY26 consol revenue rose 26% YoY to INR858 crore, with EBITDA pre-forex up 57% to INR107 crore; FY26 PAT fell 18% to INR56 crore.
538979|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR3,000 crore, up 18.6% to INR3,046 crore, with EBITDA before forex up 21% to INR334 crore. Q4 was the strongest quarter, with revenue of INR858 crore and EBITDA margin before forex of 12.5%. Full-year PAT fell 18% to INR56 crore, which management attributed to chipboard operating losses plus higher interest and depreciation in the first full year of the chipboard plant. Management guided to about 18% top-line growth in FY27 and no new capacity beyond two laminate lines in Andhra Pradesh, with the focus on utilising existing assets.

financial_highlights.change: Company expects to reduce by about INR50 crore in FY27

financial_highlights.value: 51 days in Q4; 57 days for FY26
financial_highlights.change: Q4 improved 4 days from 55 days; FY26 level broadly flat

segments.name: Laminates & Allied
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR658 crore (+14% YoY), EBITDA margin before forex 17.2% (+350 bps); FY26 revenue INR2,433 crore (+9.3%), margin 15.9%. Q4 sales volume 5.15 million sheets (+4.5%) at INR1,243/sheet; FY26 utilisation 86%.

segments.name: Plywood & Allied
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR119 crore (+18% YoY), EBITDA loss before forex INR3.8 crore; FY26 revenue INR400 crore (+18.4%), EBITDA loss INR29.5 crore. FY26 realisation INR257/sq m; Q4 INR246/sq m. Utilisation about 45-50% in Q4.

segments.name: Panel & Allied (Chipboard)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR80 crore (+47% QoQ), EBITDA loss before forex INR2.2 crore, utilisation 49% and sales volume 38,800 cubic metres (+34% QoQ) at INR20,562/cubic metre. FY26 revenue INR213 crore, EBITDA loss INR23 crore, utilisation 39%, realisation INR19,370/cubic metre.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth of about 18%, maintained despite raw material cost pressure and possible demand disruption.
Laminates revenue growth of about 10-12% in FY27.
Plywood and chipboard expected to reach EBITDA breakeven in FY27; chipboard breakeven stated as achievable around 50% utilisation.
Two new laminate lines at Andhra Pradesh expected to start production by end of FY27, adding about 2 million sheets of capacity; management sees no need for a fifth plant.
No new capacity additions beyond the two laminate lines in FY27; plywood pan-India expansion not expected until FY28.
Plywood realisation expected to stay flat or move only a few percentage points; no significant upside seen.
capex_capacity: Two laminate lines being added at Andhra Pradesh plant, about 2 million sheets, expected by end of FY27; brownfield, so faster than greenfield.
Laminate capacity: management says about 20% headroom at 86% FY26 utilisation; laminate utilisation has reached 108-110% annualised in the past.
Chipboard plant (first year of operation) is stabilised; utilisation 39% for FY26 and 49% in Q4, targeted to rise further.
Plywood utilisation about 45-50% in Q4; management aims for near-full utilisation of existing plant by FY28.
Pre-laminated chipboard share is rising; management ambition is up to nearly 100% of chipboard output laminated; share not disclosed on call.
demand_pricing: Price increases were implemented from April 2026 after raw material costs rose from March due to the West Asia conflict; most RM cost increases passed on domestically, and 4-5% in export markets plus rupee depreciation.
Some softening in chemical raw material costs since; minor market price corrections.
No demand destruction seen so far, but secondary sales are weak and cash flows tight in the market; some customers postponing projects and some stocking up earlier.
Middle East exports impacted in March and April; May normalised. Management says impact is limited.

Competition: larger organised players gaining share from midsized and unorganised players under cost and cash-flow pressure; closest domestic competitor is of similar size. Internationally competes with Wilsonart, Formica and regional players.
Plywood Q3 weakness was due to certification issues, resolved in Q4, with good March sales.

qa_highlights.question: What laminate growth is expected in FY27 and is the company outpacing the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects laminate top-line growth of about 10-12% in FY27 and believes it may be outpacing the industry, though it cannot verify industry data. Distribution, product range and presence in domestic and international markets are cited as drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Plywood realisation outlook as the business matures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said realisation may stay broadly flat, with changes of only a few percentage points, because it is already near the top of the category price range. Growth will come from volume, including the lower end of premium categories. Tier 2 is not being targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Peak laminate utilisation and need for further expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation has reached 108-110% annualised in the past and could get there again depending on mix. With two million sheets of capacity due by year-end and about 20% headroom at 86%, no further expansion is needed for now, and the position is reviewed quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook and breakeven timing for plywood and chipboard?
qa_highlights.answer: Laminate margin is expected at about 16-17%. Plywood and chipboard are both expected to break even in FY27; chipboard Q4 loss narrowed to about INR2 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Reports of particle board plants converting to MDF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not aware of any such conversions. It believes the processes differ and that particle board demand will grow with the QCO for furniture.

qa_highlights.question: Demand impact of the war-driven price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand has held for the last two months, but secondary sales are weak and some projects are delayed. Supply disruption from smaller players helped the company. It sees mixed signals and a possible slowdown if prices stay high.

risks_watch: Raw material costs (chemicals) and their pass-through; Q4 gross margin fell 410 bps QoQ on input costs.
West Asia conflict: Middle East export disruption in March-April, freight and transit delays.

Laminate Andhra Pradesh lines due by end FY27; execution risk.

538979|2026-06.headline: Greenlam Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 18% YoY to INR797 crore, with EBITDA before forex up 48% to INR81 crore and net profit of INR21 crore versus a loss a year earlier.
538979|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 18% YoY to about INR797 crore, while gross margin held near 53% (52.9%) despite sharp input and freight cost increases. EBITDA before forex rose 48% to INR81 crore, with margin up 210 bps to 10.2%, and net profit turned positive at INR21 crore against a INR15.5 crore loss last year. Laminates grew 7% but volumes fell 6% because about INR27 crore of export shipments slipped into Q2 due to container and vessel constraints from the West Asia conflict. The chipboard business turned EBITDA positive for the first time, and plywood losses narrowed. Management reiterated FY27 laminate revenue growth of 10-12% and total revenue growth target of 18%, but gave no visibility on freight or raw material normalisation.

539083|2026-03.headline: Inox Wind Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue flat YoY at INR1,306 crore; FY27 guidance of ~75% revenue growth and 20%+ EBITDA margin.
539083|2026-03.overview: Inox Wind reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of INR1,306 crore (flat YoY), EBITDA of INR333 crore, PBT of INR216 crore, PAT of INR106 crore and cash profit of INR268 crore, with FY26 revenue of about INR4,500 crore against an earlier INR5,000 crore target. Management attributed the shortfall to geopolitical disruption: delayed imported ECS components, shipping and commodity cost pressures, and a PSU contract with payment delays. The company is pivoting from turnkey EPC to equipment supply, with equipment supply now about 50% of the order book and a target of 75% to 80%. Inox Green (O&M) reported Q4 total income of INR120 crore (up 40% YoY) and EBITDA of INR57 crore, and it is guided to above INR600 crore EBITDA in FY27 after consolidating two pending acquisitions and a demerger.

financial_highlights.value: INR4,600 crore against INR5,000 crore guideline
financial_highlights.change: INR400 crore shortfall expected to be recovered in Q1-Q2 FY27
about INR40 crore from acquisition-linked debt, about INR10 crore value-added services, about INR10 crore treasury

segments.name: Inox Wind (WTG/EPC)
segments.commentary: Consolidated Q4 revenue INR1,306 crore flat YoY with EBITDA INR333 crore; order book 3.1 GW, with about 600 MW added in FY26, and visibility of more than 24 months. Only about 500 MW of the order book is from group company Inox Clean.

segments.name: Inox Green (O&M / evacuation)

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 75% over FY26 (approx. INR7,500 crore on a INR4,500 crore base), with EBITDA margin of about 20% (stated as '20% to 20%').

Group Inox Clean targets about 14 GW capacity by FY29, adding about 3 GW+ annually, of which 20-30% is expected to be wind, to drive recurring orders for Inox Wind.
New 4.4 MW turbine on track for approvals and commercial launch within calendar 2026, expected to aid penetration and margins.
Most EPC projects expected to be completed by H1 FY27, except one leading job, after which projects await statutory compliances for commissioning.
capex_capacity: Inox Green's two acquisitions cover about 6.5 GW of operational wind O&M assets; entity one order expected within a couple of weeks, entity two expected within 60-90 days.

Evacuation infrastructure demerger from Inox Green into Inox Renewable Solutions approved by NCLT Ahmedabad; about INR1,000 crore gross block and INR50-55 crore annual depreciation removed. Completion expected in 1-2 months.
Cranes moving in-house (half in-house, a couple more due this year); power transformer manufacturing started last year and ramping up.
Management plans to expand into power electronics (transformers, inverters, power electronics, ECS) with details to follow in coming months.
Group Inox Clean has about 2 GW installed, 6 GW solar module and 3 GW cell capacity; targets 10 GW each of IPP, cell and module over about 15 months.
demand_pricing: Order book 3.1 GW, diversified; recent wins include Aditya Birla, Gentari/Amplus, Jakson Green, First Energy and Leap Green. Multiple customer negotiations near closure.
Order mix is about 50:50 turnkey to equipment supply, targeted to move to 75% equipment supply (management also cited 75-80%).

Management says margins are guided at about 20% or higher on equipment supply; equipment supply is on LC terms, passing steel price changes through, reducing exposure to land/ROW cost and payment delays.
Revenue mix: about 10% O&M and 90% Inox Wind currently; O&M expected to rise to about 18-20% of consolidated revenue.
Management said it does not have FY27 order inflow targets and is 'sold out' for about 2.5 years on its stated ambitions.

qa_highlights.question: How will the two Inox Green acquisitions contribute to EBITDA and when will they be consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said both acquisitions carry roughly 50% EBITDA margins, as they are former OEMs with substations and evacuation systems. Entity one's order is expected within a couple of weeks; entity two is 60-90 days away, and all revenues from 1 April 2026 are to be reflected in consolidated results.

qa_highlights.question: What was the FY26 working capital position against the INR5,000 crore guideline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it achieved INR4,600 crore against the INR5,000 crore guideline, with the INR400 crore balance expected in Q1-Q2 FY27 after supply-chain issues from delayed imported ECS components.

qa_highlights.question: What was actual MW execution in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give megawatt execution, saying the company guides on revenue only, and reiterated this stated policy.

qa_highlights.question: Will equipment supply shift raise margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins stay at about 20% or higher, with equipment supply carrying less risk and more upfront cash; O&M at about 50% margin would add a higher-margin bias.

qa_highlights.question: Other income of INR61 crore at Inox Green: how much is recurring and how much is treasury?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR40 crore relates to the two acquisitions (debt-linked, net of deferred tax, roughly INR25-26 crore at PAT level), INR10 crore is value-added services and INR10 crore is treasury income.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Inox Green revenue fall QoQ from about INR78 crore to INR69 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the quarterly variation to value-added services timing (about INR8-9 crore) and said the annualised run-rate is the right measure.

risks_watch: Working capital: about INR400 crore of FY26 working capital target still outstanding, expected in Q1-Q2 FY27; PSU customer payment delays noted.
Execution: reliance on imported ECS components, shipping delays and commodity cost increases; geopolitical risk cited as cause of revenue miss.
Credibility: FY26 revenue of INR4,500 crore was below the INR5,000 crore target and Q4 revenue was flat YoY; management declined to disclose MW execution.

Capital allocation and dividend policy for Inox Green not yet defined; management said a policy would follow consolidation.

539083|2026-06.headline: Inox Wind Q1 FY27 consol revenue INR872 crores, adjusted EBITDA INR237 crores (~27% margin), PAT INR64 crores; FY27 guidance of 75% revenue growth reaffirmed.

The order book is about 4.4 GW after a 200 MW NLC India LOA, and an MOU for 1.5 GW with INOX Clean (500 MW firm). Analysts pressed hard on the H2-weighted guidance, flat year-on-year Wind revenue and the pending INR400 crore deferred revenue, and management largely refused to quantify quarterly numbers.
