539118|2026-03.headline: VRL Logistics Q4 FY26 total income rose 6% YoY to INR859 crore, with tonnage back to 3% YoY growth and EBITDA margin at 21.4%.
539118|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR859 crore, up about 6% YoY and 3% QoQ, helped by better realisation, new clients and return of previously lost accounts. Realisation per ton was about INR8,147, up roughly 3% YoY, and daily tonnage crossed 11,500 tons. EBITDA margin was about 21.4%, down about 190 bps YoY from an exceptional Q4 FY25 (23%+) but up about 48 bps QoQ. FY26 total income was about INR3,245 crore, profit INR237 crore (up about 29%), and EBITDA margin 20.8%. Management guided to FY27 tonnage growth of 6-7% and kept an EBITDA margin of around 20%+ despite fuel cost pressure, which it plans to pass on via selective rate hikes and fuel surcharges.

financial_highlights.change: down ~190 bps YoY; up ~48 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: Return on capital employed / return on equity (FY26)

financial_highlights.change: INR101 crore vehicles; INR165 crore land and buildings

segments.name: Tonnage / volume
segments.commentary: Tonnage decline was 13% in Q1 FY26 and about 7% for full FY26; Q4 returned to about 3% YoY growth. April 2026 YoY volume growth was about 8% per management.

segments.name: Customer mix (Q4 YoY)
segments.commentary: New customers contributed about 17% of quantity, lost customers reduced volume by about 14%, and existing customers grew about 1%.

segments.name: Commodity mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: Textiles and cloth about 17-18%, agri (equipment, fertiliser, pesticides) about 10-11%, others (industrial, pharma, books, auto) about 5-6% each. Management says petrochemical-linked goods such as plastics are seeing lower demand.

segments.name: Booking mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: TO PAY and PAID spot bookings about 80%, ACCOUNT customers about 15-16%, FTL about 6-7%.

segments.name: Door-to-door
segments.commentary: Share rose to about 38-40% of commodities from about 33-34% earlier; realisation is about INR1-1.5 per kg higher for door delivery.

guidance_outlook: FY27 tonnage growth guided at 6-7% for the full year, with at least about 2% sequential growth each quarter.
New branches expected to add about 2-3% to FY27 tonnage; about 100 net new branches planned in FY27 (100+ gross openings, fewer closures).
EBITDA margin to be maintained around 20%+ (near 21% in Q1 FY27 per management), with some basis-point impact from the withdrawal of bulk fuel purchase.
FY27 capex guided at INR300-350 crore: about INR100-150 crore for vehicles and INR200+ crore for land and buildings.
Depreciation not expected to rise materially because most new investment is in land (non-depreciable).
Fuel price pass-through via selective route rate hikes, chargeable-weight change (1 cubic feet from 8 kg to 9 kg on certain routes) and fuel surcharge in contracts.
capex_capacity: Fleet: about 6,000 owned vehicles per management; vehicle count fell from about 6,100+ to about 5,900 YoY, with about 500 additions planned in FY26 (100+ done, about 400 more by December 2026) and no scrappage planned.
Network: about 1,293 branches and 50 trans-shipment hubs across 24 states and 4 UTs as of March 2026; about 110 branches opened in FY26 with about 55-60 closed, net about 40-50.
Vehicle life: normal replacement at up to 15 years; earlier only for outdated or accident-damaged vehicles.
About 77% of fleet debt-free and 14% fully depreciated.
Hubs in pipeline: 2-3 locations including Nagpur and Raipur.
demand_pricing: Q4 volume growth came from new customers and return of lost accounts after contract restructuring; management says lost customers are returning due to service levels.

Fuel: diesel prices rose about INR3 recently; management said it has passed through on selected routes but not across the network, and that a 2x increase in rates within a week means pricing will be reviewed over 1-2 months.
Fuel procurement cost per litre rose from INR84.52 to INR85.54 as direct refinery purchase fell from 41% to 36% of volume (bulk purchase withdrawn).
Competition: most of the industry is unorganised; VRL says it is at a premium to unorganised operators but comparable to organised players and express cargo on corporate accounts.
Demand headwind: petrochemical and crude-linked goods such as plastics are seeing weaker demand, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume growth outlook and what efforts drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects at least 6-7% full-year tonnage growth and about 2% sequential growth per quarter, driven by completed rate rationalisation, marketing, new branches and new customers.

qa_highlights.question: Will fuel-driven price hikes hurt volumes, and how is fuel cost passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume pressure is from weak petrochemical-linked demand, not fuel prices. Hikes were applied on selected routes, with fuel surcharges in contracts; April 2026 YoY volume grew about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin impact of lower bulk fuel purchase?
qa_highlights.answer: Some basis points of margin impact; management said it is flexible to hold EBITDA around 20% and the bulk purchase facility has already been lost.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lorry hire charges rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Fleet fell from about 6,100 to 5,900 vehicles while tonnage grew, so outside hired vehicles were used to carry the extra volume, plus higher lorry hire rates.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new branch contribution and depreciation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: New branches contributed about 1-1.5% of Q4 growth; FY27 branches expected to add 2-3%. Depreciation is not expected to rise much, as land is a large share of new investment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the business mix and competitive positioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix is about 80% spot (TO PAY/PAID), 15-16% account, 6-7% FTL; door-to-door about 38-40%. Rates are at a premium to unorganised players and comparable to organised players.

risks_watch: Fuel price volatility and geopolitical risk; the pass-through lag could compress margins in the near term, per management's own caveat.
Weak demand in petrochemical-linked commodities (plastics etc.) could offset recovery.
Reliance on hired vehicles (lorry hire cost rose) while owned fleet shrinks.
Achievement of 6-7% FY27 volume growth depends on net new branches (about 100) ramping up.
Management did not disclose kilometre-based metrics; lead distance is about 270-280 km and capacity 15-18 tons.
539118|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on volume recovery and pricing pass-through, but cautious on near-term margins, with management stating some temporary disconnect is possible. Answers on fuel pricing and competition were direct, while the company declined to disclose the bus-business question (not in business) and kilometre data.
key_quotes: And ultimately, the cost, whatever additional costs will come, that needs to be pass it on to the customers.
So, on a full year basis, we are expecting around INR300 crores to INR350 crores capital expenditure.
But definitely, on a full quarter basis, we are planning to maintain similar EBITDA numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin was 21.4% in Q4 FY26 (down about 190 bps YoY) and guided at around 20%+ with Q1 FY27 near 21%, while bulk fuel purchase withdrawal costs some basis points and fuel pass-through lags.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 100 net new branches planned in FY27 (100+ gross openings) adding 2-3% to tonnage, plus 2-3 hubs in pipeline including Nagpur and Raipur, while the owned fleet shrank from about 6,100 to 5,900 and about 400 more vehicles are due by December 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: FY27 (at least 2% sequential growth each quarter)
rows.why: Management guides 6-7% FY27 tonnage growth, with April 2026 up about 8% YoY, Q4 at about 3%, and new customers contributing about 17% of quantity against about 14% lost volume.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex guided at INR300-350 crore (INR200+ crore for land and buildings) and utilisation read is not disclosed, so a land and branch capex plan is guided but not new.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Tonnage returned to about 3% YoY growth in Q4 and April 2026 grew about 8%, so the 6-7% FY27 guide could be exceeded if new customers and returning accounts keep coming, but petrochemical demand is weak.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged a near-term margin risk from fuel: diesel up about INR3, procurement cost per litre rose from INR84.52 to INR85.54 as refinery share fell from 41% to 36%, and pass-through is only on selected routes, with pricing reviewed over 1-2 months.

rows.label: Return of lost customer accounts
rows.why: Lost customers cut Q4 volume by about 14%, and management says they are returning on service levels, which supports the 6-7% FY27 tonnage guide.

rows.label: Fuel pass-through via rate hikes and surcharges
rows.why: Diesel rose about INR3; hikes applied on selected routes, pricing review over 1-2 months, and contracts carry a fuel surcharge, though the network-wide pass-through is not yet complete.

rows.label: Weak petrochemical-linked demand (plastics)
rows.why: Management says plastics and crude-linked goods are seeing lower demand, a headwind that could offset the recovery in volume.

tone.note: Management was confident on the volume recovery (April 2026 up about 8%) and fuel pass-through, but cautious on near-term margins given bulk fuel purchase withdrawal; analysts pushed on fuel pricing, competition and kilometre data, which management did not disclose.

539118|2026-06.headline: VRL Logistics Q1 FY27 PAT rose to Rs 81 crore (9% margin) on freight realisation up 9% to Rs 8,546/tonne and volumes up 9%.
539118|2026-06.overview: Revenue rose about 18% YoY to Rs 885 crore and EBITDA rose 22% to Rs 193 crore, with margin up 71 bps to 21.8%, despite a sharp fuel cost spike (procurement cost Rs 83 to Rs 94/litre). Management passed through the cost increase via rate hikes of roughly 5% in the quarter, and volumes grew about 9% YoY to 10.19 lakh tonnes. Net debt fell to Rs 391 crore from Rs 440 crore, and the board approved a Rs 280 crore buyback at Rs 320/share, subject to shareholder approval. Full-year guidance is raised to about 8% volume growth.

up ~22% YoY from Rs 158 crore (21.1%); margin up 36 bps QoQ from 21.4%
up from Rs 50 crore (6.7%) YoY; described as highest-ever quarterly profit

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 volume growth now expected around 8% (earlier guidance 6-7%); July volumes grew about 10%, and Q2 about 9% is expected.
Freight rates expected to improve further from 8,546/tonne if fuel prices do not fall; if fuel falls, rates may be cut by about 2-3% (a Rs 4 fuel cut implies about 2% price impact).
EBITDA margin of about 20-21% considered maintainable for the next 3-4 years.
Volume growth of 7-8% a year expected over the next 3-4 years.
Free cash flow of Rs 120-130 crore per quarter; Rs 480-500 crore for the full year.
Capex of Rs 200-240 crore a year (vehicles Rs 120-140 crore; property balance); debt expected to stay at current levels after buyback.
capex_capacity: Fleet of about 6,000 owned vehicles; about 79% debt-free and 13% fully depreciated; old vehicles being scrapped.
Network of about 1,300 branches, up about 108 YoY and 16 added in Q1; about 40-50 branches are owned premises, with the rest leased (Ind AS 116 lease liability).
Existing truck capacity is fully utilised; growth beyond it needs new vehicles or outside hired vehicles (lorry hire rose).
Full-year property capex planned at Rs 150-160 crore for sorting centres (about 12-13 of 50 transshipment hubs already owned; 3-4 more identified).
Vehicle capex of about Rs 100 crore for the rest of FY27.
demand_pricing: Blended freight realisation up 9% YoY; management says about 5% was a price increase taken in Q1 (April-May fuel-driven rate hikes plus later increase after government fuel price revision), described as sustainable.
Volume growth of about 9% = about 6% from existing customers and about 3% net from new customers; about 16-17% of tonnage lost from low-margin customers, partly recovered.
About 85% of LTL business is on PAID and TO PAY terms; receivable days about 10-12.
Bulk fuel purchase stopped as bulk price was about Rs 15/litre above retail when crude spiked.
About 70% of the industry is unorganised; VRL estimates it is about 30% organised.
Agriculture is about 10-11% of volumes; lower monsoon may slightly weigh on coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How much price hike was taken and will it sustain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 5% was taken in Q1 across fuel-driven hikes, and it is sustainable; if fuel falls, rates would be cut 2-3%. Freight realisation of Rs 8,546/tonne would hold absent fuel changes and may improve further, as mid-quarter hikes are not fully in the Q1 average.

qa_highlights.question: Is 9% volume growth the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year volume growth now expected at about 8%, up from 6-7% guidance, supported by branch expansion and recovery of lost customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and how does it fund the buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual FCF of Rs 480-500 crore funds capex of Rs 220-240 crore and the buyback; debt will stay at about the current level (about 0.3x debt-to-equity).

qa_highlights.question: Why buyback rather than debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: Buyback replaces dividend, as about Rs 175 crore was paid as dividend last year; debt is already nominal at about 0.3x debt-equity.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of DFC and rail on the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Company is in talks with the Ministry of Railways on hub-to-hub rail use; collaboration is minimal today and management says it would not hurt the customer-facing business.

qa_highlights.question: Karnataka minimum wage impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Rule not yet in force (challenged in court); impact expected to be small as salaries are already above minimum wage, with only statutory contribution changes.

risks_watch: Fuel price path (Gulf/crude volatility): fuel cost pass-through works both ways, with rate cuts of 2-3% if fuel falls.
Sustainability of ~9% volume growth after the recovery of lost low-margin customers; full-year guidance raised to 8%.
Buyback of Rs 280 crore at Rs 320/share is subject to shareholder approval; promoters are not participating.
Lower monsoon could weigh on agriculture (10-11% of volumes) in coming quarters.
Karnataka minimum wage rule is pending in court; statutory cost impact is possible.
Shift in lead distances from East/Northeast expansion: management says the NTKM impact is only 2-3%.
539118|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Q1 earnings, volume visibility and pricing durability, while repeatedly tying the rate increase to fuel prices. Answers were sometimes vague on specifics (for example, the buyback funding mechanics and the timing of the rail arrangements).
key_quotes: The effective decision making and its implementation process of the company proven that the increase in cost has been passed on to the customers without any impact on the growth in volumes.
And this is a sustainable increase in prior trade.
So, all put together, we will definitely have a good revenue growth in the coming quarters with the maintenance of existing profitability margins.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 volume growth guided ~8% with July ~10% and Q2 ~9% expected, backed by about 6% growth from existing customers and about 3% net from new customers; longer term guide is 7-8% a year for 3-4 years.

rows.why: Management has already committed Rs 200-240 crore annual capex (vehicles Rs 120-140 crore, property Rs 150-160 crore for sorting centres), and with the fleet at full utilisation, further vehicle and hub capex announcements are the likely follow-through.

rows.why: Volume guide already raised to ~8% from 6-7%, with July at ~10%; freight rates of Rs 8,546/tonne may improve further as mid-quarter hikes are not fully in the Q1 average, but this is conditional on fuel not falling.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Fuel is the main swing factor: if fuel falls, rates may be cut 2-3% (a Rs 4/litre fuel cut implies about 2% price impact), and agriculture (10-11% of volumes) may weigh on volumes with a lower monsoon.

rows.why: Board approved Rs 280 crore buyback (about 0.9% of... not disclosed as share count) funded from FCF of Rs 480-500 crore a year, replacing dividend of about Rs 175 crore last year; promoters not participating and approval pending.

rows.label: East and Northeast expansion
rows.why: East and Northeast is about 10% of tonnage and grew 22-25% YoY off a small base via new branches, with NTKM impact only 2-3%.

rows.label: Karnataka minimum wage rule
rows.why: Rule not yet in force and challenged in court; management expects a small impact as salaries are already above minimum wage, with only statutory contribution changes.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume visibility (8% FY27 guide, July ~10%), price durability and the 20-21% margin; it was vaguer on buyback funding mechanics and the timing of rail arrangements, and analysts pushed on fuel pass-through and volume sustainability after recovering low-margin customers.

539141|2026-03.headline: UFO Moviez Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 43% YoY to ₹1,342 mn and FY26 net profit rose 161% to ₹249 mn, though Q4 EBITDA fell 13% QoQ.
539141|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 43% YoY to ₹1,342 mn and 2% QoQ, with EBITDA up 55% YoY to ₹182 mn but down 13% QoQ from ₹210 mn. Net profit was ₹45 mn, down 30% QoQ from ₹64 mn. For FY26, revenue grew 15% to ₹4,864 mn, EBITDA 36% to ₹803 mn and net profit 161% to ₹249 mn. Management attributed the strong March to Dhurandhar: The Revenge, while receivables and DSO rose sharply because much of that film's revenue was booked at year-end.

segments.name: Digital cinema advertising network
segments.commentary: Advertising footprint at 4,049 screens: 2,597 multiplex and 1,452 single. Management says it remains the largest multiplex screen advertising network in India.

segments.commentary: Discontinued in FY26 due to inconsistent pipeline; old vans (over 10 years) were sold for about ₹2-3 cr. Company remains empanelled and may serve opportunities through third-party tie-ups.

guidance_outlook: Management is 'optimistic about sustaining growth momentum' with a healthy content pipeline and focus on advertising network and premium cinema initiatives.
Q1 FY27 started mixed with Bhooth Bangla, Raja Shivaji and Pati Patni Aur Woh Do; upcoming releases include Peddi, Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai, Welcome to the Jungle, Sarpanch and Cocktail 2.
Management expects ad-sharing ratio to gradually decline as revenues scale, since about 80% of revenue-sharing expense sits under minimum guarantee structures.
Management will provide DSO information for periods above 120 days in future quarters where a major film boosts year-end receivables.
Management says it intends to pursue both invested and non-invested (aggregated) advertising inventory models; activation and off-screen advertising initiatives are at an early, phased stage.
capex_capacity: Advertising footprint at 4,049 screens (2,597 multiplex, 1,452 single) as of the call.

Debt is raised mainly to fund expensive theatre equipment, typically via LC converted into loan, so debt movements are lumpy quarter to quarter.
Multiplex screens about 2,500 now vs about 1,000 when ad-sharing was 30-35%.
demand_pricing: Q4 box office: January strong (Ikkis, The Raja Saab, Border 2, Mardaani 3); February soft (O Romeo, Do Deewane Seher Mein); March strongest on Dhurandhar: The Revenge.
Q4 CDC and VPF revenues per screen declined YoY and QoQ because February was nearly blank and wide releases of Dhurandhar and Border crowded out other films; full-year CDC and VPF revenues grew.
Ad-sharing with theatres rose from the legacy 30-35% to about 59.5% because of multiplex mix and aggregated inventory where UFO did not invest; management says it is not losing pricing power.
UFO network delivered about 38% of footfalls for Dhurandhar and received about 30% of its ad revenue share, per management, using its ProCAT measurement tool.
Receivable cycle for ad sales is 110-150 days, up to 160 days depending on corporate or government clients.

qa_highlights.question: Why are employee and operating costs rising faster than revenue, and why keep the caravan business loss-making?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the employee cost rise is mainly variable pay (about ₹9 cr) paid this year after no payout last year. Caravan operations were shut down in FY26 and the vans sold for about ₹2-3 cr.

qa_highlights.question: Why have trade receivables risen so fast (₹162 cr vs ₹115 cr), and is DSO a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed the rise to higher ad revenue and a large Dhurandhar booking at March end. DSO was 147 days vs 121 in FY25 and about 134 in FY19; provisioning is adequate. Management agreed to show DSO for periods above 120 days in future.

qa_highlights.question: Is UFO losing pricing power as ad-sharing with theatres rose to about 59.5% from 33%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied losing pricing power. It cited multiplex mix, rental-linked minimum guarantees and aggregated inventory where UFO did not invest. It expects the ratio to decline as revenues scale.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue per screen fall in CDC and VPF in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said February was almost blank and blockbusters like Dhurandhar and Border drew wide releases, so other films avoided the window. Full-year CDC and VPF revenue still rose, and management says the business has stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of software, footfall monitoring and off-screen or activation initiatives?
qa_highlights.answer: Footfall and ProCAT are used to market the network to advertisers. Activation and off-screen advertising work has started but is at an early, phased stage.

qa_highlights.question: What was free cash flow, and why does debt rise while cash improves?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO did not give an FCF figure. Net cash rose from ₹48.3 cr to ₹59 cr despite about ₹15 cr tied in working capital including TDS. Debt is raised for theatre equipment via LC-to-loan conversions, and the company keeps both cash and debt by policy.

risks_watch: Receivables and DSO (147 days) could stay elevated if Dhurandhar-type year-end releases recur; watch for the new >120-day DSO disclosure.
Q4 EBITDA fell 13% QoQ and net profit fell 30% QoQ, so momentum is uneven quarter to quarter.
Ad-sharing ratio near 59.5% compresses margins; the company expects it to moderate as minimum guarantees are exceeded.
Employee costs rose to ₹94.7 cr; management says cost optimisation is ongoing.

Q1 FY27 started mixed; success depends on the named Peddi, Welcome to the Jungle and Cocktail 2 releases.

539141|2026-06.headline: UFO Moviez Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose to ₹1,118 mn (vs ₹1,090 mn YoY) and advertisement revenue grew 33% YoY, helped by Dhurandhar spillover.
539141|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose about 3% YoY to ₹1,118 mn, while EBITDA was flat at ₹189 mn versus ₹193 mn a year earlier and PAT fell to ₹56 mn from ₹65 mn. Management credited a 33% YoY jump in advertisement revenue to the spillover from "Dhurandhar" and to annual advertisers onboarded around it. Product sales declined YoY, driven by roughly ₹7 crore lower international sales because Dubai imports were delayed by the regional war; management says these orders remain in hand. Releases fell to 399 titles in the quarter from 456 in Q1 FY26.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Advertisement revenue grew 33% YoY, with spillover from Dhurandhar and new annual advertisers. Advertising footprint is 3,891 screens (2,565 multiplex, 1,326 single).

segments.name: Product sales
segments.commentary: Declined YoY mainly due to international product sales falling about ₹7 crore on Dubai import delays. Indian product sales rose marginally. International sales were over 80% of product sales until last year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects delayed international product orders to be executed in Q2 FY27, or at the latest Q3 FY27.

539150|2026-03.headline: PNC Infratech FY26 standalone revenue fell to INR 4,633 crore; management guides ~30% growth to INR 6,000 crore in FY27 with ~12% EBITDA margin.
539150|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue was INR 1,458 crore with 12.02% EBITDA margin and PAT of INR 100 crore, while FY26 standalone revenue of INR 4,633 crore was below earlier expectations due to delayed appointed dates on four projects worth over INR 4,400 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR 6,000 crore (~30% growth), FY28 about 25% higher, and EBITDA near 12% in FY27, citing bitumen and crude-driven cost pressure partly offset by new escalation mechanisms. The company has an unexecuted order book above INR 22,000 crore, and it is diversifying into solar, BESS, coal mining and water. Net surplus on a standalone basis was INR 327 crore, while consolidated net debt to equity was 0.76 times.

segments.name: Highways (HAM/EPC/BOT)
segments.commentary: Four delayed projects (three NHAI, one MPRDC) worth over INR 4,400 crore drove lower FY26 turnover; 14 HAM projects with aggregate bid cost above INR 17,200 crore, 5 at PCOD/COD and 6 under construction.

segments.name: Water (Jal Jeevan Mission, irrigation)
segments.commentary: About INR 300 crore received in FY26 from state payments; FY27 revenue target INR 750 crore. Andhra irrigation: INR 380 crore work done to 31 March, ~INR 700 crore remaining, FY27 target ~INR 200 crore.

segments.name: Coal mining (MDO/item-rate EPC)
segments.commentary: Order of ~INR 2,956 crore over five years; FY26 turnover ~INR 68 crore; FY27 target ~INR 400 crore and FY28 ~INR 600 crore. Capex of ~INR 350 crore, of which ~INR 250 crore spent in FY26.

segments.name: Solar and BESS
segments.commentary: Order of ~INR 2,000 crore in development; physical execution to start Q3 FY27 after PPA with NHPC. Revenue target INR 600 crore in FY27 and INR 1,400 crore in FY28; equity requirement ~INR 400 crore, ~INR 120 crore in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue guided at ~30% growth to ~INR 6,000 crore; FY28 ~25% growth to ~INR 7,500 crore.
FY27 standalone EBITDA margin guided at ~12%; FY28 margin to be shared later, expected ~12% if commodity prices normalise.
FY27 new order inflow target ~INR 15,000 crore (INR 3,957 crore highways secured so far, plus ~INR 2,000 crore solar); 60-70% targeted from highways.
FY27 capex target INR 150 crore; interest cost expected to fall INR 3-4 crore from current quarter.
Equity infusion for HAM projects: INR 542 crore remaining over two years, ~INR 350 crore in FY27; internal accruals expected to cover it.
Revenue targets: Varanasi-Kolkata packages INR 1,600-1,800 crore; Jalna-Nanded and Pune Ring Road INR 1,500-1,600 crore; Haryana Orbital Rail balance ~INR 360 crore to FY27/FY28.
capex_capacity: Coal mining capex ~INR 350 crore, ~INR 250 crore spent in FY26; FY27 company capex target INR 150 crore.
Solar: land identified, connectivity in-principle approval received, final approval expected in 1.5-2 months; physical execution from Q3 FY27 after PPA with NHPC.
HAM equity: INR 1,623 crore total requirement (excluding two new HAMs awaiting LOA); INR 1,081 crore infused to March 2026.
Western Bhopal HAM: appointed date expected by end-September 2026 after alignment change; ~INR 100 crore FY27 revenue assumed.
Two new NHAI HAM projects in UP (bid cost INR 3,483 crore combined): appointed date expected in Q4 FY27.
demand_pricing: NHAI awarded 3,124 km in FY26, over 30% below the 4,500 km target; management expects awarding to improve but timing uncertain.
EPC competition described as cutthroat; management sees less competition in larger HAM and BOT-Toll projects, citing reduced bidder numbers on two recent HAM wins of about INR 1,700 crore each.
Company submitted 15 EPC bids and one HAM bid worth ~INR 14,000 crore; price bids expected to open before end-May and in June.

MoRTH cost escalation mechanism from 1 April 2026 for EPC/HAM/PBMC projects with monthly price adjustment (earlier three months); management expects revised authority cost or extended compensation for new tenders.
Back-to-back pass-through: SPV inflation indices (WPI/CPI) and bitumen price compensation flow to EPC contractor per management.
Vertis Infrastructure Trust: entire payment for the 12-asset divestment received, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How can FY27 and FY28 revenue and margins be viewed given the FY26 shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided ~30% growth to ~INR 6,000 crore in FY27 and ~25% in FY28 (~INR 7,500 crore), with ~12% EBITDA in FY27; some margin pressure expected in Q1-Q2 from bitumen and crude costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of the INR 6,000 crore guidance between approved and pending projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance excludes new orders; based on awarded projects with appointed dates, except Western Bhopal (~INR 100 crore assumed) and only 30% of the INR 2,000 crore solar order (INR 600 crore) is included.

qa_highlights.question: Will diversification into new segments hurt margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no cross-subsidy effect is expected; earlier target was 13-13.5% EBITDA, now guided ~12% across the mix, with water and irrigation earlier delivering similar margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on the Varanasi-Kolkata packages and Haryana Orbital Rail?
qa_highlights.answer: Varanasi-Kolkata: INR 336 crore revenue in FY26, INR 1,600-1,800 crore targeted in FY27, no obstructions. Haryana Orbital Rail: over INR 400 crore done (53%), balance ~INR 360 crore to be executed in FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest cost outlook and what drove the Q4 jump to INR 30 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 rise was from working capital utilisation and term loan interest on machine financing; management expects a reduction of INR 3-4 crore from the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company bid for BOT-Toll projects and how will asset monetisation proceed?
qa_highlights.answer: No BOT-Toll bid submitted yet; evaluating NHAI BOT-Toll opportunities and direct bidding is planned. Monetisation of the five PCOD assets is under evaluation; no framework announced.

Consolidated net debt to equity of 0.76x and rising working-capital-linked interest cost.

539199|2026-03.headline: SG Finserve FY26 PAT rose 58% to INR 128 crore on a INR 3,936 crore loan book (up 75%), with management guiding AUM growth of 25-30% medium term and 35-40% for FY27.
539199|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 operating income of INR 334 crore (up 96% YoY), closing loan book of INR 3,936 crore (up 75%, stated as an all-time high) and PAT of INR 128 crore (up 58%). Q4 PAT was INR 42 crore, up 30% QoQ, and Q4 fee income was about INR 6.2 crore against about INR 1.5-1.9 crore in earlier periods. Management reiterated nil NPA as its guidance and said it is comfortable with leverage of about 1.9x, aiming for 3x over two to three years without fresh equity. Q&A covered NPA philosophy, TReDS entry, related-party exposure and the sharp rise in fee income, and several answers were framed as conservative guidance.

segments.name: Supply chain finance (dealer / anchor financing)
segments.commentary: More than three-fourths of the business per management. Construction is the largest sector at about 35% of AUM, followed by automotive; average ticket about INR 5 crore per borrower.

segments.name: Factoring
segments.commentary: Bilateral factoring commercialised in March 2026 with INR 175 crore outstanding at 31 March. TReDS participation expected to go live in Q1 FY27 through RXIL and M1xchange.

segments.name: Cross-sell (LAP, working capital, business loans)
segments.commentary: Opportunistic cross-sell within the anchor/dealer ecosystem at near-zero acquisition cost; management said it is not a core focus. Mobile is about 2% of AUM.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance of 25-30% CAGR medium to long term; FY27 aspiration of 35-40% AUM growth.
Profit guidance of 30-35% CAGR, measured on full-year PAT of the previous financial year, not Q4 exit run rate.
Profitability range: ROA 4.5-5%, ROE 14-16%, cost to income 13-17%.
Leverage to rise from about 2x to 3x over two to three years, in phases; comfortable range 2x-3x.
Internal AUM target of INR 10,000 crore in three to four years without fresh equity, with bank lines of INR 3,000-3,500 crore.
NPA guidance remains nil; management said the aim is no losses, while acknowledging that lending involves losses.
capex_capacity: Operates from 30 hub locations pan-India, each covering about a 100 km radius; business is 100% domestic with no import-export financing.
Bank lines of more than INR 3,000 crore, with INR 3,000-3,500 crore estimated, not fully utilised.
Gross disbursements for FY26 crossed INR 25,000 crore; Q4 disbursements about INR 7,700 crore against a book of about INR 3,900 crore (average churn about 45 days).
New businesses (unspecified) are under groundwork, subject to regulatory approvals; timing of FY27 or FY28 uncertain.
demand_pricing: Management said fewer than 100 of the top 500 corporates are active in supply chain finance, and only 25-30% of anchors' sales are covered by organised programmes, so headroom is large.

Management estimated the wider supply chain market, including PSU banks, at upward of INR 1 lakh crore; five to six private banks and a few NBFCs each run AUM of INR 10,000-15,000 crore in dealer finance.
Fee income is being pursued as a strategy; fees on disbursements range from 10 paise to 50 paise, with some cases at 1%.
Management said no stress is visible in top sectors but is monitoring geopolitical and fuel/gas supply risks; steel import effects are yet to be assessed.

qa_highlights.question: How does the business model support nil NPAs, and is there a buffer in NPA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exposure is short-term (about 45-day churn), invoice-backed and end-use monitored, with anchors paid directly and early-warning tracking of dealer cycles. It said Ind AS ECL and RBI rules limit conservative provisioning, with about INR 18 crore provision already held; the guidance is nil NPA by design.

qa_highlights.question: What is the leverage target and how will growth be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Leverage is about 1.9x; management sees 3x as acceptable and aims to reach it in two to three years in phases. Bank lines of INR 3,000-3,500 crore are available, so growth to INR 10,000 crore AUM is possible in three to four years without fresh equity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fee income jump in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fee income is now a strategic focus and that Q3 fees were under-captured; it expects Q4-level fees (about INR 6 crore) to become the norm.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% growth guidance conservative, and is FY27 guidance different?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is deliberately conservative and aims for 35-40% AUM growth in FY27, with 25-30% as the medium-term average. Earlier conservatism was attributed to a management change.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the loan book goes to group companies?
qa_highlights.answer: Related-party exposure is less than INR 100 crore; channel financing to group companies is around 30% of the overall book.

qa_highlights.question: Did steel prices drive the AUM increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the steel price rise did not drive the 31 March AUM; growth came from volume and FY26 average AUM doubled to INR 2,640 crore.

risks_watch: Fee income reliance: Q4 fee income of about INR 6.2 crore is far above prior quarters; sustainability is unproven.
Geopolitical and fuel/gas supply disruption could stress steel, auto and construction borrowers (top sectors), though no stress was reported.
Earlier guidance inconsistency across quarters, which an investor raised; conservative framing may need to be tracked against actuals.
Leverage increase from 1.9x to 3x and the timing of TReDS go-live in Q1 FY27 and of new business approvals.
Concentration in the construction sector (about 35% of AUM).

539199|2026-06.headline: SG Finserve posts record Q1 FY27 PBT of INR72 crore (+27% QoQ) and loan book of INR4,552 crore (+82% YoY) with nil NPAs.

Net worth reached INR1,539 crore, leverage moved to 2.2x from 1.9x at March 2026, and CRAR stood at 32%. Annualised ROA was 5.1% and ROE 14%, with nil NPAs reported. Management reiterated FY27 PBT visibility of about INR300 crore (about 75% YoY), with AUM guidance of INR5,500 crore for FY27 and a 25-30% AUM CAGR over three to four years.

segments.name: Supply chain finance and working capital
segments.commentary: Management said about two-thirds of business financing sits in working capital, supply chain and factoring; about one-third of AUM is from the APL Apollo ecosystem, down from a higher share, and 52 anchor mandates are running (5 added in Q1).

segments.name: Factoring (TReDS and bilateral)
segments.commentary: Factoring outstanding was INR225 crore in June versus INR175 crore in March; commercialised in March-April 2026, with yields at par with channel finance for TReDS and at or slightly above for bilateral deals.

segments.name: Beyond supply chain (cross-sell LAP, opportunistic)
segments.commentary: Roughly one-third of business financing; management named digital lending and loan against property as products under consideration, with no retail or consumer lending.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PBT visibility of about INR300 crore (about 75% YoY); PAT about INR225 crore; FY27 closing equity about INR1,700 crore; FY27 AUM about INR5,500 crore (management called INR6,000 crore aspirational).
Targeted AUM CAGR of 25-30% over three to four years, with profitability CAGR of 30-35%; INR10,000 crore AUM now targeted for FY30 (earlier guidance was INR7,500 crore for FY30) and possibly FY29.
Quarter-on-quarter growth normalised to about 8-10% for PAT, with AUM growth of about 15-16% QoQ, after adjusting for INR337 crore equity received at end-March and early April.
Cost-to-income to be kept below 15%; opex maintained at about 1% of average book.
Leverage to move from 2x towards 3x over about two years, taking ROE from 14% towards 16% with ROA held at around 4.5-5%. No equity raise planned through the growth phase up to INR10,000 crore AUM.
Insurance broking subsidiary (SG Insurance Brokers) incorporated; IRDAI licence pending, commercialisation at least two to three quarters away, and not expected before Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: No capex or physical capacity discussed; the business is asset-light, with about 30 locations for sales coverage.
ESOP pool of 20 lakh approved by shareholders; about 10.32 lakh granted in April and about 50,000 granted in July to new joiners, leaving about 9 lakh unallocated with no timing decided.
GIFT City entity approval received from the board, subject to dual RBI and IFSCA approvals; long-term plan.
Board has approved AIF and ARC business; no timeline given.
demand_pricing: Average portfolio yield held at about 12.5% in Q3, Q4 and Q1, with factoring added without diluting or enhancing the overall yield.
Management said geopolitical uncertainty is hitting the MSME and trader business through lower incremental working capital needs, but has not yet translated into credit pressure.

Management said it does not compete with large banks and NBFCs, and fills the gap left when a dealer's bank working capital limit falls short of its requirement; for example, INR2 crore gap on a INR10 crore need.
Management estimated the addressable market as receivables of about INR25 lakh crore on the balance sheets of the top 1,000 corporates.
Management said the MoU-based anchor pipeline (52 anchors, INR7,700 crore MoU value) is a dummy limit and should not be read as book visibility.

qa_highlights.question: Will equity be raised this year, given net worth near INR1,510 crore and projected FY27 book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no equity raise is needed; net worth is INR1,539 crore at 30 June, and FY27 closing equity should be about INR1,700 crore, with leverage rising from 2x towards 3x over about two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 AUM guidance only 25-30% CAGR when growth is far higher currently?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called itself a conservative lender, citing the aim of nil NPAs, low credit cost and a balance sheet able to absorb shocks; 25-30% AUM CAGR is described as healthy and sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Is NPA-free status sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nil NPA is the stated aim, but acknowledged that losses can occur in lending; a larger net worth and profitability would be the buffer.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q1 run rate persist, given that H2 is usually stronger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR4,000 crore average book sustains the base, with incremental growth on top; QoQ PAT growth of 8-10% is targeted after normalising the equity infusion.

qa_highlights.question: Why is cost-to-income only 7% against a 14% guide?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified the right metric is opex at about 1% of average book, and the company guides to cost-to-income below 15%.

qa_highlights.question: What is SG Insurance Brokers and when will it start?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a wholly owned subsidiary for B2B fee-based cross-sell to the existing anchor and borrower ecosystem, not underwriting; subject to IRDAI approval and at least two to three quarters away.

risks_watch: Credit risk without NPAs: management concedes losses can occur, and nil NPA is a stated aim, not a guarantee.
Geopolitical stress on MSME and trader working-capital demand could slow new business growth, though credit costs are so far unaffected.
Q1 PBT was boosted by equity received in late March and April (INR337 crore), so QoQ growth should normalise to about 8-10%.

Insurance broking and factoring scale-up depend on regulatory approvals and team build-out; factoring is still small (about 5% of AUM).

539199|2026-09.headline: SG Finserve posted an all-time high quarterly PAT of INR59 crore in Q2 FY27, with loan book at ~INR5,700 crore and H1 PBT of INR150 crore.
539199|2026-09.overview: Management reported record Q2 FY27 PAT of INR59 crore and a loan book of about INR5,700 crore, up roughly 25% QoQ on period-end basis (average AUM up 17% QoQ). Asset-to-equity rose from 2.8x to 3.7x over the last year, and quarterly ROE reached about 15%. Management revised its mid-term debt-to-equity ceiling from 3x to 4x, which it said would take AUM to about INR11,000 crore, and it expects no equity raise this year. New initiatives during the quarter included factoring/TReDS, digital lending, loan against property (LAP), and a stake in an AI/digital subsidiary, plus a GIFT City subsidiary and an AIF pending SEBI approval.

segments.name: Supply chain finance (dealer / deep-tier)
segments.commentary: Supply chain is ~70% of AUM. Group ecosystem share of book has fallen to 25%; the company powers ~60 brands. Steel and building products ~35% of AUM and auto ~20%.

segments.name: Factoring / TReDS
segments.commentary: Factoring licence received in March 2026; now ~15% of book after starting in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Digital lending (BharatPe merchant LSP model)
segments.commentary: ~10,000 loans disbursed; book only INR121 crore at 30 Sep 2026. Management expects ~10% of AUM in 2-3 years.

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP) / business loans
segments.commentary: Just started in Delhi NCR with four disbursals and INR17 crore outstanding; tickets above INR25 lakh.

segments.name: Project finance
segments.commentary: 12 accounts disbursed recently, none commercially operational; management expects starts in 6-9 months.

guidance_outlook: Debt-to-equity mid-term ceiling revised from 3x to 4x; board approved incremental borrowing in the call's board meeting.
AUM growth guidance of 30-35% CAGR on a one-year-forward basis; profitability CAGR guidance of 35-40%.
Management targets INR10,000-11,000 crore AUM in 2-3 years, implying ~100% growth from current book; equity dilution or higher leverage mandate expected only after that.
Full-year PAT guidance of INR225 crore reiterated; management said it may do slightly better.
Expects around 7,000 crore AUM by year end on current run rate (per management comment); Q2/Q4 seasonality of 2-3% on the higher side.
Target of adding 2 anchor corporates per month for the next 12-18 months.
GIFT City finance subsidiary (~INR48 crore investment approved) expected operational in about a year, subject to RBI and IFSCA approvals.
Planning to keep ROA above 4.5% and cost-to-income below 15%; yield maintained at ~13% on AUM.
capex_capacity: Headcount ~100 (roughly doubled in one year); per-employee annualised PAT above INR2 crore; presence in 34 locations.
Digital lending built on LSP framework; in-house AI/digital stack being built via a 15% stake in a subsidiary rather than external SaaS.
New subsidiaries: AIF (Cat III equity AIF, SEBI approval awaited), AMC subsidiary, GIFT City finance company (~INR48 crore), shared services company (cost amount undecided), AI/technology subsidiary.

Lending rates are benchmarked to the SGFL benchmark rate; management said any repo-linked cost increase would be passed on, though benchmark not yet raised.
Management positions the company as filling the INR10-20 'untied' portion of borrowers' funding need after banks/NBFCs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise equity this financial year, given borrowings near 3x net worth?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Debt-to-equity mandate raised to 4x, with incremental borrowing approved by the board; equity dilution or higher leverage considered 2-3 years out.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue grow ~18% QoQ while AUM grew 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Income accrues on daily outstanding; average AUM grew 17% QoQ, so period-end growth overstates income growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost as a percentage of income rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher leverage (asset-to-equity 2.8x to 3.7x); management said this lifts ROE.

qa_highlights.question: What is the collection efficiency and DPD profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Monthly collection efficiency 99.5%; 60+ DPD is zero overall and 30+ DPD is zero in non-supply-chain book; 0.5% slips to 1+ DPD and is mostly collected within 30 DPD.

qa_highlights.question: How does the RBI draft on revolving credit affect the model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the product is term-based with no rollover or extension, so it is aligned; only documentation and reporting systems need tweaks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of funds and funding mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Single source is banks and NBFCs (19 lenders), plus opportunistic commercial paper; cost of borrowing about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q2 credit cost increase a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Provisioning is an ECL/IRAC regulatory requirement, not cash credit cost; ~INR25 crore accumulated on ~INR5,700 crore book, and nil NPA is the target.

qa_highlights.question: Why would borrowers choose SG over banks?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowers often get INR80-90 of a INR100 requirement from banks; SG funds the remaining untied portion, under a coexistence model across PSU banks, private banks, large NBFCs and mid-layer NBFCs.

risks_watch: Leverage rising toward the 4x D/E ceiling; equity dilution likely around INR10,000-11,000 crore AUM given the ~3x price-to-book; watch the CCD/OCD option.
Finance cost ratio rising (44.5% of interest income); repo hike and benchmark pass-through timing unclear.
Draft RBI norms on revolving credit could require documentation and system changes for supply-chain products (about two-thirds of AUM).
BharatPe digital-lending book: management acknowledged gross NPAs are possible, relying on FLDG and LSP cushions.
New businesses (AIF, GIFT City, LAP, project finance) carry execution and gestation risk; project finance accounts not yet operational.
Management said the Q2 front-loading of growth may normalise; the 30-35% growth guide must be tested in H2.
Opex discipline as headcount and locations expand; the cost-to-income target is below 15%.

539221|2026-03.headline: Sportking expects top line up 7-10% and margins to expand 15-20% QoQ over next three quarters on higher yarn prices and a long sales book.
539221|2026-03.overview: Management described a resilient Q4 FY26 with revenue broadly stable and profitability improved, driven by better yarn realisation and stronger cotton yarn demand. Demand was attributed to China's resurgence as a cotton yarn importer, Bangladesh recovery, and a stronger rupee-driven competitiveness shift for Indian spinning. Management said spreads are at roughly three-year highs and expects margins to expand over the next two to three quarters, with the 150,000-spindle greenfield project slated for commercial operations in Q3 FY27. Acquisitions of a majority stake in Marvel Dyers and Processors and the Sobhagia Sales manufacturing facilities were approved, with closure targeted within the calendar year.

financial_highlights.value: Broadly stable (no figure stated on call)

financial_highlights.change: Expected to reverse in Q1 if rupee does not depreciate further
Management estimate for current/coming financial year

segments.name: Cotton yarn (core)
segments.commentary: Demand robust across segments for last 2-3 months; yarn prices moved from about USD2.70-2.80/kg average last quarter to near USD3.30 now. Export book covers about 90 days, with the current quarter largely sold.

segments.name: Acquired entities (Marvel Dyers and Processors; Sobhagia Sales facilities)
segments.commentary: Combined revenue about INR200 crores (7-8% of turnover). Group companies expected to be flattish in FY26 and grow 15-20% in FY27 after reengineering, versus management's earlier 20-25% framing.

guidance_outlook: Top line expected to rise 7-10% over the next three quarters on higher yarn prices; no volume growth as plant runs at 95-96% optimum utilisation.

Quarter-on-quarter margin expansion targeted at least 15-20% over the next two to three quarters, supported by spreads and the long sales book; management said it would be disappointed not to deliver 15%+ margins in H1 but declined to give formal guidance.

Greenfield 150,000-spindle expansion (approx. INR1,000 crores) expected to start commercial operations in Q3 FY27, with a little contribution in Q3 and a more substantial contribution from Q4 and fully from FY28.
40 MW solar to commence by end-May 2026, saving INR14-15 crores annually.
Acquisitions expected to close within the current calendar year at the latest; bigger downstream plans to be shared after 6-9 months of integration.
EU and UK FTAs expected to be effective by end of FY27 (UK in 2-3 months, EU in about 6 months per management's read of government sources).
capex_capacity: Greenfield expansion of approximately INR1,000 crores adds about 150,000 spindles; land acquired, machinery advances released, construction on schedule, commercial operations targeted Q3 FY27 in Odisha.
Ramp-up: first output about 2 months after commissioning, then about 15-16% of capacity added each month; 97-98% utilisation expected about 6 months after commissioning.

40 MW solar plant to commence by end-May 2026 under Punjab policy, supplying about 7 crore units per year at about INR3.70/unit, saving about INR2/unit (INR14-15 crores annually). Management said no further ground-mounted solar planned in Odisha, only possible small rooftop solar.

Acquisition of majority stake in Marvel Dyers and Processors Pvt Ltd approved by Board; acquisition of manufacturing facilities of Sobhagia Sales Pvt Ltd on slump-sale basis and land and building on lease basis, subject to definitive agreements and approvals.
Current plant running at about 95-96% of optimum capacity.
demand_pricing: China's share of Indian cotton yarn exports rose from about 7-8% to roughly 25-30% per management; Sportking's China exports rose from about 2-3% to about 10-12% of its exports in the last quarter.
Bangladesh remains Sportking's largest export market; domestic demand has picked up since March after the US tariff removal.
Cotton yarn spread about USD1.00/kg (skein cost vs. yarn price) versus USD0.65-0.70 over the last couple of years; cotton spreads at about 3-year highs.
Cotton covered for 3-6 months; management did not disclose coverage levels, saying all good mills cover most of the season's cotton by end-March.

CCI bought 106 lakh bales of a projected 310 lakh bale crop (about 33-34%), which management says lifts market prices toward MSP at harvest; government import-duty relief on cotton awaited within a couple of months.
Export mix roughly 50% international, plus or minus 5%, which management expects to stay in this range with FTAs.

qa_highlights.question: How will new capacity ramp, and why are spreads rising and sustainable for 2-3 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads supported by a 90-day export book already largely sold for the current quarter and cotton covered for 3-6 months. New greenfield capacity is on timeline, with 97-98% utilisation about 6 months after commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: Is China a durable demand source given historical volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged volatility but said Chinese domestic demand has turned after 4-5 years of weakness and that China now needs to import cotton given peaking domestic production and high cotton duties.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to margins once new-crop cotton prices fall or rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current spreads are among the best of the last 3 years even at today's cotton prices; April-September is seasonally weak and October-March is seasonally stronger. No crystal ball on pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for H1 FY27 and quarter-on-quarter trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects QoQ margin expansion of at least 15-20% over the next 2-3 quarters, citing higher yarn prices (USD3.30 vs USD2.70-2.80) and the long sales book. It declined to give formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the acquisitions and synergies on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquired entities are about 7-8% of turnover (about INR200 crores). Immediate margin impact is small; they serve as labs for downstream expansion. Closure expected this calendar year at the latest.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 margin and the forex hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Better spreads and robust demand drove margin; some small provisions held it back. The forex loss was a notional mark-to-market on unshipped and unreceived items at the all-time-high dollar on 31 March, expected to reverse if the rupee does not weaken further. Management said it books sales the same day and holds no open risk.

risks_watch: Chinese demand volatility; management acknowledged China has been a volatile market.
New-crop cotton prices and procurement cost in October onward could compress spreads; no guidance given on post-H1 margins.
Greenfield project timeline (Q3 FY27 start) and ramp-up pace; construction risk.
Pending duty decision on cotton imports; CCI procurement share (about 33-34%) influences domestic prices.
Forex mark-to-market swings on open export and import items; Q4 contained a notional charge.
Integration and value addition of acquired downstream businesses; long-term plans to be disclosed after 6-9 months.
Macro risk from multiple wars and higher inflation forecasts, per management.
Group company revenue fell over FY23-FY25; FY26 expected flat, growth of 15-20% in FY27 needs delivery.

539221|2026-06.headline: Sportking Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin reached about 18.8% on yarn spreads of INR133/kg versus INR107 last quarter, with management guiding 18-20% margins to be hard to sustain.
539221|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong start, with healthy revenue growth and a significant profitability improvement driven by better cotton yarn realisations, strong export demand and disciplined raw material buying. The overall spread rose to INR133/kg from INR107 in the prior quarter, and the EBITDA margin was cited at about 18.8%. Management said the margin is elevated, expects the next two quarters to stay around these levels, and expects longer-term margins near 15% after the Odisha plant. The solar project started commercial operations late in the prior quarter (about 10 days of contribution) and is guided to save about INR15 crore a year, with the full 90 days flowing from the current month.

segments.name: Cotton yarn
segments.commentary: Better realisations cited as main driver of margin expansion; spread rose to INR133/kg from INR107/kg. Management said the Odisha plant will add to revenue from Q4.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Management targets a 55:45 export-to-domestic split. China and Bangladesh together account for about 60-70% of Sportking's exports; China's incremental yarn demand was the main driver of the recent uptick.

segments.name: Fabric and garments (proposed acquisitions)
segments.commentary: Proposed acquisitions of Marvel Dyers and Sobhagia Sales are expected to add 8-10% to top line and similar EBITDA share from next year, with about INR250 crore impact from next financial year once the deal completes.

capex_capacity: Greenfield 150,000-spindle expansion in Odisha: first-phase production expected in Q3 FY27, full project targeted within FY27; announced cost about INR975-1,000 crore.
Management expects 30-40% of potential revenue from the new plant in Q4 FY27 and targets 90% plant utilisation by March 2027 and 96-97% by the start of FY28; ramp-up expected to take 5-6 months.
Odisha margins expected at least 300-400 bps above existing plants, per management.
Odisha incentives: INR2.50/unit power subsidy, 30% capital subsidy with no cap, land subsidy tied to employment, and about INR7,000 per employee employment subsidy.
Land is available to triple Odisha capacity; further capex depends on balance sheet and leverage comfort.
Solar project commissioned and operating; expected to cut annual power cost by 12-15%.
demand_pricing: Management said demand from all markets remains healthy and expects festive-season support domestically.

Global cotton yarn demand improved as China became a large buyer, pushing Indian yarn prices higher; management said China imports about 20,000 tonnes against India's roughly 400,000 tonnes monthly output.
Order book kept at 70-90 days, similar to end of last quarter.
Cotton prices rose about 10-11% over the last quarter; management says most purchases were made about 3 months earlier and that Q2 should be similar to or better than Q1.
India-UK FTA signed last month, but no orders yet; management expects 6-9 months for orders to reflect in the order book.

Management expects China to remain a buyer because Chinese cotton prices are above international levels. Bangladesh's spinning sector is under strain from gas and capital costs, which helps Indian yarn demand.
Exports to the US are indirect via downstream vendors whose offtake has roughly doubled in the last 6 months.
guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected around 18-19% for the next two quarters; longer-term margin guided around 15% after Odisha, with 12-14% described as the comfortable range.
FY27 revenue target about INR3,000 crore (around 20% growth); FY28 target above INR4,000 crore with Odisha.
Solar savings about INR15 crore annually; full 90-day contribution expected from the current month.
Absolute EBITDA expected to keep rising in FY28 even if percentage margins moderate.
Cotton import duty waiver runs to 31 October; management is lobbying the government to extend it and says FY27 inventory is already covered for two quarters.
Acquisition completion expected in about one more quarter, with full impact from next financial year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin sustainability and what drove the 18.8% margin, including the import duty effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cotton import duty made no contribution to Q1 because raw material was already bought; margins should stay around current levels for two quarters, with absolute EBITDA expected to keep trending higher.

qa_highlights.question: Is the spread of INR133/kg sustainable for a year or two?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to predict precisely, expects cotton prices to ease after the new crop, and said the inventory effect will be larger in the next two quarters because Q1 realisations lagged cotton prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Odisha plant reach high utilisation and what is the revenue run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 96-97% utilisation by start of FY28; no Q3 revenue assumed, with 30-40% of potential revenue from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the merger financing and debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly preferential shares, with cash outflow of about INR25-30 crore and no meaningful incremental debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add capacity beyond Odisha Phase 1?
qa_highlights.answer: Land exists to triple Odisha capacity; further capex depends on the balance sheet and leverage comfort.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term product mix shift toward value-added products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said value-added fabric and garment share would be about 10% in the next year; longer-term plans to be announced once there is more visibility.

risks_watch: Cyclicality: management itself flagged 18-20% margins as likely not sustainable long term and cited FY22 peaks as an aberration.
Cotton input cost: prices up 10-11% in the last quarter; management expects a moderation after October, but the import duty waiver ends on 31 October unless extended.
Capacity additions: spread strength may attract new spindle capacity; management says it has not seen announced projects.
Odisha ramp-up: 5-6 month ramp, targeted 90% utilisation by March 2027, and margin accretion (300-400 bps) depend on execution.
Acquisitions of Marvel Dyers and Sobhagia Sales: completion timing has slipped and the contribution is still under progress.
Export concentration: China and Bangladesh make up 60-70% of exports; the China-driven demand could reverse.
539221|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, margins and the Odisha plant, but guarded on forward cotton and spread outlook, with repeated statements that it is difficult to predict. Evasive on pricing details, declining to share cotton cost or realisation numbers.

And the 18%, 19%, 20% might not be sustainable in the long-term, but we expect them to be healthier than where they were in last 2, 3 years going forward next year.
So I won't take it as a benchmark for the volatility of margins. Otherwise, they stay between 12% to 14%, which is where we are comfortable actually.

539254|2026-03.headline: AESL FY26 capitalisation of about INR15,300 crores; FY27 capex guided at INR21,000-22,000 crores and capitalisation at INR21,000-22,000 crores.
539254|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 as a year of heavy commissioning, led by the Mumbai HVDC project (INR7,000 crores, commissioned 15 March 2026) and 82.29 lakh smart meters installed in the year against a 70 lakh target. Management guided FY27 capex to about INR21,000-22,000 crores (transmission about INR15,500 crores) and FY28 to about INR22,000-25,000 crores, with capitalisation of INR21,000-22,000 crores in FY27 and about INR13,000 crores in FY28. Credit ratings were described as improved to AAA+/AAA for most assets, with interest costs falling, and net leverage is to be held at 4.5x-4.7x. Management declined to give formal EBITDA guidance but said transmission EBITDA could reach about 3x current levels over 36-40 months and that FY27 consolidated EBITDA could be about INR11,500 crores versus INR8,726 crores in FY26 (as stated by the CEO).

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 smart meter operating EBITDA (non-Ind AS, full year)
financial_highlights.value: INR593 crores (Ind AS-basis figure as stated by CFO, Q4 INR214 crores)

financial_highlights.metric: Transmission EBITDA run-rate add from FY26 commissioned projects

segments.commentary: FY26 capitalisation INR10,260 crores; market share of bids improved to about 29-30% vs 20-25% earlier; FY27 capex guided at about INR15,500 crores, FY28 about INR20,000 crores. Mumbai HVDC (INR7,000 crores) commissioned 15 March 2026 with full-year tariff of about INR1,300 crores to accrue from FY27.

RAB has grown from about INR5,400 crores to about INR10,500 crores.

segments.commentary: About 5,000 MW renewable capacity contracted, of which about 1,400 MW tied up with third-party consumers; margins on tied-up capacity stated above INR0.50 per unit. Detailed C&I presentation deferred to May next year.

FY28 capex about INR22,000-25,000 crores (transmission about INR20,000 crores, distribution about INR2,000 crores, smart metering about INR1,500 crores plus new orders).

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 and FY28 capex expectations by business?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR21,000-22,000 crores (transmission 15,500, distribution 2,350, smart metering 3,900); FY28 about INR22,000-25,000 crores (transmission 20,000, distribution 2,000, smart metering 1,500 plus new orders).

qa_highlights.question: How will the FY26 HVDC and capitalisation translate into FY27-28, and how much CWIP reconciles with the transmission capitalisation guide?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capitalisation about INR21,000-22,000 crores and FY28 about INR13,000 crores. Management said heavy equipment procured late in the year is capitalised immediately, so CWIP alone does not explain the INR14,500-15,000 crores transmission capitalisation target.

qa_highlights.question: How should the leverage be viewed given negative free cash flow in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said assets are funded 70:30 debt to equity, with only the equity portion from internal accruals, and the company is comfortable funding existing capex; net leverage to stay at 4.5x-4.7x.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA contribution from FY26 commissioned transmission projects and the win rate in tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,600 crores of incremental transmission revenue on full run-rate; win rate improved to close to 30% from 20-25%, with a target band of 25-30%.

qa_highlights.question: How will Mumbai HVDC revenue be booked in FY27, and what is the status of Pole 2?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year tariff about INR1,300 crores to accrue from FY27 once approved by regulator; Pole 2 is still under MERC and STU evaluation with no commitment.

qa_highlights.question: Why did smart meter operating EBITDA figures differ between the nine-month and full-year presentations?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said operating EBITDA is a function of meters installed and there was no restatement; he said the figures would be checked offline as the analyst cited a nine-month figure of INR466 crores that did not reconcile.

qa_highlights.question: Can operating profit double or triple, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said FY27 consolidated EBITDA could be about INR11,500 crores; CFO said transmission EBITDA could reach about 3x current levels in 36-40 months, with distribution EBITDA about INR2,500 crores rising to INR3,000-3,200 crores and smart metering EBITDA INR2,400-3,000 crores once fully built.

539254|2026-06.headline: AESL Q1 FY27: Energy Solutions platform delivered about INR 570 crore EBIT on 3,325 MU long-term sales; management frames AESL as a full-scale utility.
539254|2026-06.overview: Management said AESL has moved to a full-scale utility with four operating businesses (transmission, distribution, smart metering, Energy Solutions) and expects consistent quarter-on-quarter reporting. Quarterly capex was close to INR 3,500 crore. Energy Solutions is the new focus: about 5 GW of take-or-pay supply and 3,500 MWh of storage tied up, with long-term offtake being built out. Management said the IntelliSmart acquisition is pending CCI approval. Analysts pressed on the sustainability of Energy Solutions margins, which management tied to whether purchase positions are back-to-back with sales.

539254|2026-09.headline: AESL Q2 FY27: total income up over 50%, EBITDA up ~67%, PAT up 145% as Energy Solutions earned strong merchant margins; smart meter deployment lagged.
539254|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a strong quarter, with total income up over 50%, EBITDA up close to 67% and PAT up 145% year on year. Capex deployed in H1 reached about INR7,850 crore, described as an all-time high, with transmission capex guided to about INR14,000 crore for FY27. Energy Solutions revenue was over INR2,000 crore and EBITDA over INR800 crore in the quarter, helped by merchant market conditions that management said will not be repeated at that level. Smart meter installations were slower than expected in H1, which management attributed to consumer resistance and utility-specified installation scopes. Transmission commissioning in H1 was minimal, with ROW issues in Gujarat delaying Halvad and Navinal, and management still targets some FY27 commissioning.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited consumer resistance and utility-specified scopes (Maharashtra HT consumers first, Bihar tagging); with these resolved, pace is expected to rise significantly.

539300|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's strongest quarter, with consolidated revenue up 92.32% YoY to INR197.59 crore and EBITDA up 76.67% to INR20.14 crore. Sequentially, revenue grew about 20%, and EBITDA margin rose to 10.19% from 9.31% in Q3, helped by the Guwahati ramp-up from January 2026. For FY26, revenue rose 237.34% to INR607.75 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 9.66% from 14.24% and PAT margin to 5.76% from 6.11%, which management attributed to product mix. Management reiterated an INR1,000 crore revenue aspiration by FY28 and an internal 7% PAT margin target.

segments.commentary: FMCG revenues crossed INR500 crore in FY26 and now form the majority of revenue. Intermediates are about 15% captively consumed and 85% sold to FMCG players such as ITC and Jyothy Labs; management expects 15-20% growth.

segments.commentary: Started contributing meaningfully in FY26 from Bhilwara. Management expects about 20% growth in coming years and says FMCG will remain the largest contributor.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the INR800 crore annualised run-rate from Q4 plus 10-15% organic growth and new soap customers, and said existing capacity is sufficient.

qa_highlights.question: What sustainable EBITDA and PAT margins should be expected, and is 7% PAT reachable in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the YoY margin decline to product mix, targets about 7% PAT, and said it will be nearly reached in FY27 with about 1-1.25% of operating leverage from higher utilisation.

qa_highlights.answer: Textile is expected to fall from about 20% of revenue to 10-12% at most; no demerger is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10-15% organic growth conservative given the run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified that the 10-15% organic growth is over and above the INR800 crore base; acquisitions in FMCG will be considered if ROI is attractive.

539300|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 120.64% YoY to INR276.33 crores, but EBITDA margin compressed to 8.18% on raw-material and crude-linked cost pressure.
539300|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR276.33 crores, up 120.64% YoY and 39.85% QoQ, with PAT of INR15.04 crores (up 130.67% YoY). EBITDA rose 94.41% YoY to INR22.59 crores, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 8.18% from 9.28% a year earlier and 10.19% in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the margin squeeze to dyes, chemicals, boiler fuel, LABSA and PP packaging costs linked to geopolitical crude volatility, which hit the textile business hardest. Installed FMCG and FMCG-intermediate capacity rose to 20,840 tons per month after a 1,700 MT soap line was commissioned at Roorkee. Management guides FY27 revenue of INR900-1,000 crores and a ~6% profitability level, with a further 0.75-1% improvement in FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: Dyes, chemicals, consumables, boiler fuel and LABSA rose; PP packaging spiked. Textile prices could not be raised in Q1; management expects normalisation by Q3 or Q4.

qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue INR900-1,000 crores, FY28 growth 15-20%; FY27 profitability about 6%, rising 0.75-1% in FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation at 50-55%; another 25-30% expected by FY28; little new capex needed for one to one-and-a-half years.

qa_highlights.answer: Roorkee capacity was funded from the subsidiary's retained earnings. INR98.65 crores raised was used for Bhilwara food and Guwahati soap/noodle/cosmetics facilities, not for Sunrakshakk Agro acquisition, which predated the raise. No further fundraising is planned.

539301|2026-03.headline: FY26 bookings hit record INR1,550 crore (+22% YoY) while FY26 revenue fell to INR564 crore from INR713 crore on revenue-recognition timing.
539301|2026-03.overview: Arvind SmartSpaces reported record FY26 bookings of INR1,550 crore, up 22% YoY, with Q4 bookings crossing INR600 crore for the first time. Full-year revenue declined to INR564 crore from INR713 crore, which management attributed to timing of revenue recognition and occupation certificates slipping into FY27, while adjusted EBITDA fell to INR156 crore and PAT to INR103 crore. Q4 PAT rose 103% YoY to INR44 crore on revenue of INR155 crore. Business development added projects worth INR3,140 crore in FY26, and a further INR2,400 crore Mumbai high-rise was signed after year-end.

qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of 22-25% margins on new sales; a short commodity spike of a quarter or so can be absorbed within budgeted contingency.

539301|2026-06.headline: Arvind SmartSpaces Q1 FY27 presales rose 147% YoY to INR432 crores; PAT jumped to INR97 crores on Orchards Phase 1 BU receipt.

demand_pricing: Management says underlying demand is strong; Aqua City plus broader core-market strength drove bookings.

Price increases expected to moderate after 3-4 years of strong appreciation; company does not underwrite large price hikes.
Bengaluru price uplift giving better margins on some older projects.
Management sees Mumbai, Bengaluru and Ahmedabad each delivering 22-25% EBITDA; no Tier 2 plans for now.
Management sees annual residential absorption of INR3-4 lakh crores across the three focus markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is Aqua City-driven booking strength project-specific or indicative of underlying demand in Gujarat and Bengaluru?

qa_highlights.question: What is the unrecognised revenue conversion and normalised margin outlook?

qa_highlights.question: How is OCF flattening and what is FY27 OCF guidance?

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt and leverage comfort level?

qa_highlights.question: How will BD of INR600-1,000 crores be funded?

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for an annuity or commercial portfolio?

risks_watch: Revenue and margin are lumpy and dependent on OC timing, with some OCs lined up in Q4; the Q1 margin of about 48-49% is well above the 25% portfolio average.
Net debt to equity rising from prior level to 0.29x as BD accelerates; management's comfort threshold is 1:1.
Launch execution: 6 launches worth INR3,000-3,500 crores this year depend on approvals, including Pen Khopoli.
Labour and construction cost inflation is gradual per management but may pressure margins.
Guidance inconsistency: BD cash deployment quoted as INR600-900 crores in one answer and INR600-1,000 crores in another.
