rows.label: IRDAI commission rules and April 2027 op-risk RWA
rows.why: IRDAI commission consultation could cut fee income, with management expecting offset from repo hikes and FCNR benefit (about INR30 crore fee income and about INR60 crore opex from FCNR in Q2), but no quantum given; op-risk RWA rules from April 1, 2027 expected to offset ECL capital impact.

rows.label: Cost-to-income at 55% for FY27
rows.why: Management firmly expects 55% incremental cost-to-income for FY27 on a 500 bps jaws gap (H1 jaws 553 bps, Q2 592 bps), though it depends on sustaining that gap for three quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on NIM recovery to about 5.8% by Q4, the 55% cost-to-income and FCNR economics, and pre-empted NIM and ROA questions; analysts pressed on the liquidity drag, the mortgage and card asset-quality trends, the insurance commission quantum (not given) and the credit cost outlook.

539448|2026-03.headline: IndiGo posted a Q4 FY26 net loss of 25.4 billion rupees, driven by 48.2 billion rupees of FX losses; FY26 underlying profit ex-FX and exceptionals was 75 billion rupees.
539448|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was hit by the December operational disruption tail, a March demand break from Middle East escalation, and a sharp rupee depreciation of about 5% in the quarter. Total income for the quarter was about 238 billion rupees (up about 3%), and EBITDAR ex-FX was 64.4 billion rupees at a 28.7% margin versus 31.0% a year earlier. Q4 capacity growth slowed to 3% (about 10% in Jan-Feb) and PRASK fell 4% to 4.46 rupees. Management guided to a mid-teens PRASK increase for Q1 FY27 on fuel charges and a low base, but flagged higher costs and a seasonally softer period from mid-June, with capacity recalibration planned.

financial_highlights.change: vs net profit of 30.7 billion rupees in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 underlying net profit (ex-FX and exceptionals)
financial_highlights.change: vs around 89 billion rupees in FY25
vs 68.6 billion rupees, margin 31.0% in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 net profit ex-FX and exceptionals
financial_highlights.change: vs 29.8 billion rupees in Q4 FY25
vs 228.6 billion rupees, margin 28.3% in FY25

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Expected to absorb most redeployed capacity in Q1 FY27 (metro, new airports Navi Mumbai and Jewar, and leisure markets); management says domestic fuel pass-through is largely matched by yield due to government and OMC support (fuel up only 25-30% vs over 100% internationally).

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Middle East and Europe were about 18% of capacity (around 160 daily flights); flights cancelled after the 28 Feb crisis, ramped to about 20s per day in March, and now about two-thirds of the 160 are operating, with full capacity targeted by end-June. International fuel charges pass through only partially.

segments.name: Fleet and network
segments.commentary: Fleet of 441 aircraft at FY26 end after 72 gross additions (51 owned-order, 21 damp-leased) and 65 redeliveries; 97 domestic and 45 international destinations; first A321 XLR inducted, deployed on Athens and Istanbul.

segments.name: Loyalty (BluChip)
segments.commentary: More than 11 million registered members; co-brand partners include SBI Cards, Kotak, Axis and IDFC First Bank; asset-light programme.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 capacity expected up around 3-4% YoY, with domestic-heavy mix as Middle East capacity ramps back.
Q1 FY27 PRASK (all-in, including fuel charge) guided to a mid-teens % increase YoY on April-May booking and pricing trends, off a low base.
CASK ex-fuel ex-FX guided to mid- to high-single-digit increase (previously mid-single-digit), dependent on utilisation and rupee.
Measured capacity optimisation from mid-June: returning damp-leased narrowbodies, reducing older CEO-generation fleet use and route recalibration; discussions with widebody ACMI partner.
No dividend recommended for FY26; no full-year ASK guidance given.
Pratt & Whitney AOG groundings in the 40s, expected to trend to the 30s by year-end; no OEM guidance beyond that.
capex_capacity: FY26 fleet: 51 aircraft inducted from original orderbook plus 21 damp-leased; 37 original-orderbook and 28 damp-lease redeliveries; fleet 441 at FY26 end.
No change to delivery schedule from the order book; flexibility is via damp-lease returns and older-technology aircraft.
Prepaid aircraft loans for 17 aircraft; 36 aircraft now unencumbered (book value above 95 billion rupees); 53 aircraft on finance leases with underlying ownership.

Capital investment of USD 820 million in GIFT City entity for aviation asset acquisition; further USD 450 million (43.4 billion rupees) prepayment of finance-lease obligations towards GIFT City entity.
Integrated Corporate Campus announced as a long-term investment.
demand_pricing: FY26 passengers above 123 million (highest ever); seat growth about 5%, passengers up about 4%, ASK growth 9.5%, RPK growth 7.5%.
Q4 demand: January residual December impact, February stabilised, March hit by Middle East escalation; April soft, May stronger per management.
Fares sticking; management says market currently inelastic to fare hikes, pricing managed daily.
Fuel: Singapore jet fuel up more than 100 points; domestic ATF increase about 25-30% after government and OMC support; Q4 fuel CASK down around 5% YoY with a one-month lag.
Q4 CASK ex-fuel ex-FX 3.15 rupees, up around 7% YoY (rupee-driven dollar costs, low utilisation, annual contractual increases).
Corporate travel: no softness seen per management; April soft, May stronger.

qa_highlights.question: Are fares fully passing through cost pressures, domestic versus international, and what is the international utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said domestic fuel pass-through is largely recovered; international fuel is at market prices and only partly passed through via a fuel charge. International load factors were low in March and April, improving in May; no firm standalone international load-factor figure given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the mid-teens PRASK growth is base effect versus demand strength?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY26 May was extremely weak due to Pahalgam-related disruption, so the base is low; May demand is positive, and PRASK reflects both yield and load factor.

qa_highlights.question: Will fleet deliveries change?
qa_highlights.answer: No change to deliveries; near-term flexing via returning damp leases (narrowbodies) and reducing older CEO-generation aircraft given fuel burn.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CASK ex-fuel ex-FX outlook and rupee sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance moved to mid- to high-single digit increase. FX sensitivity is still about 900 million rupees per 1 rupee move; net dollar exposure about 10 billion rupees, with about 1.3 billion rupees hedged.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging policy change given rupee volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedge ceiling raised from $1 billion to $3 billion: $1 billion for 12-month cash flows and $2 billion over 2 to 5 years; hedged position currently $1.3 billion. Fuel hedging is at an early internal-deliberation stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall quarter on quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Reversal of accruals for leadership payouts; year-on-year cost growth in line with normalised inflation and salary increases.

risks_watch: Fuel prices and the ATF pass-through: government and OMC relief is partial, and management is still negotiating with the Ministry of Petroleum on lower VAT pass-through.
Rupee: each 1 rupee move against the dollar is about 900 million rupees of mark-to-market impact; CASK ex-fuel ex-FX headwind will build as FX costs flow through.
Middle East route recovery: about two-thirds of 160 daily flights back; full capacity targeted by end-June, subject to risk assessment.
Seasonally softer demand from mid-June plus elevated fuel could pressure Q2 yields and load factors.
Pratt & Whitney groundings in the 40s; no OEM guidance beyond the 30s by year-end.
Leadership transition: Willie Walsh joins as CEO from early August 2026.
539448|2026-03.management_tone: Candid and cautious on the near term, with repeated caveats that guidance is directional and volatile. Management was confident on May demand, pricing power and balance-sheet strength, and deflected on international-specific load factors and Air India comparisons.
key_quotes: Not only did the December disruption cause a significant impact on our results, what transpired fell short of the standards we set for ourselves when we began this journey in 2006.
So the demand is good for the month of May.
So, one is balancing out both in terms of what the fuel charge and the base price needs to be, along with the load factors that the revenue management teams are focused on.
For the moment, what we are seeing is as we take the fares up, the market is inelastic to these hikes in fares.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: CASK ex-fuel ex-FX guided up to mid- to high-single-digit growth (raised from mid-single-digit) and Q4 EBITDAR ex-FX margin fell to 28.7% from 31.0%, though a mid-teens PRASK rise in Q1 FY27 could offset part of it.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Q1 FY27 capacity guided up 3-4% YoY, with Middle East capacity (about two-thirds of ~160 daily flights now operating, full by end-June) ramping back; but no new aircraft beyond the existing order book and mid-June capacity trimming is planned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 FY27 capacity guided at 3-4% and May demand described as stronger, but mid-June seasonal softness and capacity recalibration (returning damp leases, reducing CEO-fleet use) cap volume growth; FY26 passengers grew about 4% on about 5% seat growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Delivery schedule unchanged and flexibility comes via damp-lease returns and older-technology aircraft rather than new orders; prior commitments already cover fleet, though a USD 820 million GIFT City aviation asset investment and a Corporate Campus were announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q1 FY27 PRASK guided to mid-teens % increase off a low base (May FY26 hit by Pahalgam disruption), but management flagged higher costs and softer demand from mid-June, with CASK ex-fuel guidance worsened.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Mid-June seasonal softness, elevated fuel, CASK ex-fuel ex-FX guide raised to mid- to high-single digits, and rupee sensitivity of about 900 million rupees per 1 rupee move (net dollar exposure about 10 billion rupees, only 1.3 billion hedged) all point to downside risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First A321 XLR inducted and deployed on Athens and Istanbul; further XLR deployments are implied but not specifically dated.

rows.label: Fare stickiness and daily pricing
rows.why: Management says market is inelastic to fare hikes and fares are sticking, with domestic fuel pass-through largely matched by yield, supporting the mid-teens PRASK guide.

rows.label: Pratt & Whitney groundings easing
rows.why: AOG groundings in the 40s expected to trend to the 30s by year-end, with no OEM guidance beyond that, so capacity relief is gradual and unquantified past that.

rows.label: Hedging ceiling raised to $3 billion
rows.why: Hedge ceiling lifted from $1 billion to $3 billion ($1 billion for 12-month flows, $2 billion over 2-5 years) against only $1.3 billion hedged today, which reduces rupee earnings volatility over time.

tone.note: Management was confident on May demand, fare pricing power and balance sheet, but cautious on near-term costs, mid-June softness and international load factors, and deflected on Air India comparisons; analysts pushed on international utilisation and the cost and rupee outlook.

539448|2026-06.headline: IndiGo swung to a net loss of INR 2.4 billion in Q1 FY27 as fuel CASK rose ~80% YoY, despite yield growth of 21.3%.
539448|2026-06.overview: IndiGo reported total income of INR 256 billion (up ~19% YoY), with EBITDAR of INR 38.3 billion at a 15.6% margin versus 28% a year earlier. Net loss was INR 2.4 billion against a profit of INR 21.8 billion in Q1 FY26; ex-currency the loss was about INR 56 million. Yield rose 21.3% and load factor fell 1.3 points to about 83%, but fuel cost rose sharply on Middle East-linked jet fuel prices and the rupee's depreciation of more than 11%. For Q2 FY27 management guided flattish capacity and PRASK growth above 25%, while holding the single-digit FY27 ASK guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 57.4 billion, 28% margin in Q1 FY26
vs profit of INR 21.8 billion in Q1 FY26; ex-currency loss ~INR 56 million

financial_highlights.value: INR 529 billion (free INR 390 billion, restricted INR 139 billion)

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic fuel charged on a government/OMC-capped formula (25% cap on March reference price) from 1 April to 8 June; market-linked from 9 June. May was the best month ever for IndiGo domestic, with over 10 million domestic passengers.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Fuel always billed at market rates, so international fuel cost rose faster than domestic. International capacity largely recovered in June; the Middle East was at around 90-95% of pre-war departures at end-June (about 150 daily before the war, 20-30 at the trough).

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 capacity expected flattish YoY, driven by route rationalisation and temporary international suspensions (e.g., Langkawi, Ho Chi Minh City, Hong Kong, Shanghai; expected to restart in October).
Q2 FY27 PRASK expected to grow more than 25% YoY; loads expected flattish to slightly down, similar to Q1.
FY27 ASK growth guidance held in single digits; FY28-FY30 capacity growth guided at early double digits to mid-teens; 300 billion-rupee capacity figure cited for FY30 at the analyst meet.
FY27 CASK ex-fuel ex-forex expected at the higher end of single digits, possibly lower end of early double digits.
International share of ASK targeted at around 40% by 2030 (about 33% currently).
No guidance given on RASK-CASK spread; damp-lease decision deferred to Q3 FY27 depending on Middle East and fuel trends.
capex_capacity: Fleet at quarter end: 432 aircraft; inducted 13 aircraft from original orderbook (via GIFT City entity) and redelivered 9 orderbook aircraft and 13 damp-leased aircraft.
Q1 capacity growth ~3% YoY, broadly in line with guidance; Q1 was Middle East-driven, Q2 reduction is off-season related.
Older CEO-technology aircraft parked where commercially appropriate; prioritising fuel-efficient aircraft.
Signed MoU with CFM International for over 1,000 LEAP-1A engines for future deliveries, including engine MRO and long-term material services.
Bought 4 engines via GIFT City entity; partial payment for land for unified campus.
Started flights to Jamnagar; first airline to operate from Jewar airport (Noida).
demand_pricing: Pricing actions drove yield up ~21%; management says price discipline is holding in Q2 and yields are tapering upward.
April demand hit by disruption and recalibration; May was the strongest month for the domestic industry; June yields held up while international was managed selectively.

Fuel: Singapore jet fuel up nearly 120% (Brent up ~50% YoY on average). ATF in June reportedly fell to about INR 110-115/litre at the blended level before rebounding; management estimated the quarter's blended effective rate around INR 140-150/litre.
Rupee depreciated more than 11%, inflating dollar costs (leases, maintenance, supplementary rentals).
Lite Fare (no check-in bag, add-on purchasing) launched; Accor ALL loyalty platform went live; SITA OptiClimb fuel-optimisation tested.

qa_highlights.question: Impact on load factors from higher yields, and is capacity rationalisation driven by this?
qa_highlights.answer: Load factor fell only 1.3 points in Q1; Q2 loads expected flattish to slightly down as capacity is cut, with pricing discipline holding.

qa_highlights.question: Has fuel consumption per ASK changed, and what was the effective fuel rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumption per ASK unchanged; only the rate moved. Management described the April-8 June domestic cap (25% on a March reference), VAT/excise, and market-priced international and private supply, with an average around INR 140-150/litre.

qa_highlights.question: Will the fuel CASK increase of ~63% QoQ reconcile with the OMC price-cap releases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to March being an elevated base, the capped domestic formula plus taxes, market-priced international fuel, and private suppliers pricing at market.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 capacity guidance changing?
qa_highlights.answer: No change: FY27 ASK growth still single digits. Mid-teens growth is still held for FY28-FY30 (described as early double digits to mid-teens).

qa_highlights.question: Any risk of having to compensate OMCs for April-May fuel support?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the April-8 June bills were settled on the agreed formula, and it expects no extra burden because fares were passed through.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FX loss and supplementary rental trends?
qa_highlights.answer: FX mark-to-market loss was about INR 80 million; the rupee moved only about 10 paise over the quarter, on a USD exposure of about USD 8-9 billion. Supplementary rentals rose on currency and escalation, with a Q4 release base effect.

qa_highlights.question: Will yields hold after fuel normalises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is price-led for now; after fuel moderates, it expects to return to volume-led growth and hold prices, with mid-teens growth post FY27.

risks_watch: Fuel volatility: forward curves moved up again in July with Brent back above USD 90; a Hormuz disruption could bring Q1-like fuel levels.
Middle East airspace: capacity at around 90% of pre-war levels, but the crisis has flared again; management is assessing further restoration.
Ability to sustain yields beyond Q2 as capacity returns for the Q3 peak season, and the damp-lease decision in Q3.
Cost pressure: CASK ex-fuel up ~11% YoY; deferred senior management increments to be reassessed in six months; gratuity-related exceptional costs expected in Q3 and Q4.
Reported news on airport operators entering airlines: management said it is watching developments and gave no decision.
539448|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and pricing near term, but cautious and evasive on margin: management declined to give a spread or fuel-pass-through target and repeatedly described the environment as too volatile to guide on profitability.
key_quotes: As we enter a seasonally softer demand period and continue to manage fuel and airspace volatility, we are adopting a prudent and measured approach to capacity.
So, there's no kind of a target, but we just want it to be a healthy kind of a spread.
We are holding to the guidance that we gave at the analyst meet.
The headwinds are too significant.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDAR margin fell to 15.6% from 28% YoY and the company posted a net loss of INR 2.4 billion; CASK ex-fuel is up ~11% and management declined to guide spread or pass-through, though a fuel normalisation would help.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Fleet at 432 aircraft; FY28-FY30 capacity growth guided at early double digits to mid-teens per year, backed by a 1,000+ LEAP-1A engine MoU for future deliveries, while Q2 FY27 capacity is flattish YoY and FY27 ASK growth is single digit (Q1 capacity ~3% YoY).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 capacity guided flattish YoY with loads flattish to slightly down (Q1 load factor ~83%), and international flights to Langkawi, Ho Chi Minh City, Hong Kong and Shanghai suspended until October; volume growth returns only with FY28 capacity.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only ~83% load factor (down 1.3 pts), but the fleet is growing toward mid-teens capacity for FY28-FY30, with 4 engines bought via GIFT City, partial land payment for a unified campus, and a 300 billion-rupee capacity figure cited for FY30.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 PRASK guided to grow more than 25% YoY with yields still tapering upward after 21.3% yield growth in Q1, but loads are flattish to slightly down and fuel could reverse the gain.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Fuel is volatile (Brent back above USD 90 in July, Q1 blended ATF ~INR 140-150/litre vs ~INR 110-115 in June), CASK ex-fuel up ~11% YoY, and the Q1 net loss of INR 2.4 billion shows margins are exposed; management gave no spread or profitability target.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Lite Fare (no check-in bag, add-on purchasing) has just launched, Accor ALL loyalty went live, and SITA OptiClimb fuel optimisation is in test, but no specific new-product timeline beyond these was given.

rows.label: International ASK share to ~40% by 2030
rows.why: International share is about 33% currently and management reiterated the 40% target by 2030, with Middle East at ~90-95% of pre-war departures at end-June.

rows.label: Damp-lease decision and fuel-pass-through regime
rows.why: Damp-lease decision deferred to Q3 FY27 (13 damp-leased aircraft redelivered in Q1), depending on Middle East and fuel trends; domestic fuel moved to market-linked pricing from 9 June after the 25% capped formula.

rows.label: Older CEO-technology aircraft parked
rows.why: Older aircraft are already being parked where commercially appropriate and fuel-efficient aircraft are prioritised, with 9 orderbook and 13 damp-leased aircraft redelivered in Q1.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, pricing discipline and FY28-FY30 mid-teens capacity growth, but cautious and evasive on margins, declining to guide spread or fuel pass-through; analysts pushed on fuel cost reconciliation, the 63% QoQ fuel CASK jump, and the FX and supplementary rental trends.

539450|2026-03.headline: S H Kelkar Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA Rs 83 crore at 13.5% margin, steady sequentially; management guides ~13.5% for H1 FY27 despite raw-material inflation.
539450|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA was Rs 83 crore at a 13.5% margin, flat sequentially, after a one-off sale of about Rs 35 crore of low-margin products. FY26 reported EBITDA margin was 10.2%, with PAT hit by a higher consolidated tax rate from loss-making subsidiaries. Management said raw-material inflation (inventory prices up 12-13%+) had not yet hit Q4 but will show in coming quarters, and it is pricing through to clients on a 2-3 month inventory cycle. FY27 capex is guided at about Rs 140 crore and borrowings at about Rs 800 crore, with a full-year guidance withheld due to uncertainty.

financial_highlights.metric: Gross margin (Q4 FY26, net of one-off)
FX contribution to revenue growth (Q4 and FY26)

financial_highlights.change: From Rs 93 crore in Q3; includes about Rs 6 crore one-off MTM impact in trust; normal run-rate Rs 94-95 crore per quarter
Equivalent to about Rs 50 crore annual business

segments.name: India Fragrance and Flavours (mature)
segments.commentary: Management put the mature India fragrance and flavours base at about Rs 1,300-1,400 crore, with flavours volumes growing rapidly and margins improving on operating leverage. India volumes dipped slightly in March due to Middle East shipment delays, since restored.

segments.name: Aroma Global Ingredients / Middle East / Southeast Asia
segments.commentary: Management called Middle East and Southeast Asia phase 2 growth markets. Q4 rest-of-world sales grew about 34% YoY per analyst question; Southeast Asia factory built last year with break-even reported.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Growth was muted over recent quarters because of capacity constraints. The Almere, Netherlands plant is now fully operational, with about Rs 10 crore of annual sales transferred on day one; management targets a return to double-digit growth.

segments.name: US and UK development centres
segments.commentary: US centre started last year and Manchester UK centre started this year. Management said US business of about 1 million (about 200,000 already in hand) is contracted; these are seen as 3-4 year ramps, with Rs 80-85 crore annual opex across three new centres.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to maintain adjusted EBITDA at about 13% to 13.5% through H1 FY27, with Q1 more visible and Q2 subject to monitoring; it wants to keep EBITDA above 12-13%.
Gross margin expected at about 42% and thereabouts in H1 FY27, with absolute profitability to be protected via pricing pass-through.
Management said it is confident of achieving Rs 300 crore-plus EBITDA in FY27 and at least FY25 levels, with more visibility on H1.
FY27 capex is expected at about Rs 140 crore, mostly front-loaded in the first two quarters.
Borrowings expected around Rs 800 crore in FY27; gross debt may rise in the next 3-6 months before falling, with a target to reduce debt by 10% every year over the long term.
Management declined to give full-year FY27 guidance, citing raw-material and inflation uncertainty beyond H1.
capex_capacity: Almere greenfield factory in Netherlands is fully operational, debottlenecking European growth that was near full utilisation.
Vanavate facility in Maharashtra expected to go on stream in coming months, likely around end of current quarter, with a six-month transition from the Mulund factory; Mulund to close next year.
Vashivali facility rebuild restarted after a fire; it may be available around Q3 FY27 but may not be needed immediately, with full operation next year.
Creative development centres in Germany (labs functional for a couple of months), Manchester UK, and US are the new opex-heavy initiatives, with break-even in about 3 years.
demand_pricing: Raw-material inventory prices are up about 12-13%+; power and fuel costs are also rising. About 40% of raw materials are directly crude-linked and about 30% indirectly linked.
Management said price increases have been secured from many clients, including large global accounts, and Q1 FY27 is described as secured on price, supply contracts and inventory.
Management expects overall industry demand to be muted in the next year or so, with share gains expected for the company during inflationary periods.
Management said it gained market share in India in the first few weeks of Q4-end, as smaller players hold less inventory buffer.
Flavours margins improved sequentially on rapid volume growth and operating leverage, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Return on the Rs 350 crore capex and Rs 80-85 crore opex in new centres: when will returns come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said returns will take longer than 1-2 years; new centres break even after about 3 years and markets are 20-25x India in size. Management said it is on track in US and Europe and has no large India capex planned apart from fire-related rebuild.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins normalise to low teens this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, it expects to reach that level quickly, while noting the adjusted EBITDA target is about 13-13.5% for H1.

qa_highlights.question: How much raw material cost is passed on, and how will inventory cycles affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can pass on RM increases under contracts, holds 2-3 months of raw material and sets client prices against stock on hand, reviewing every 2-3 months; it expects no repeat of the past inventory-driven margin lag.

qa_highlights.question: FX impact on revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: FX added about 3% to 3.5% to revenue growth in Q4 and FY26; management said revenue transactions are broadly neutral but the dollar loan creates translation pressure on margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the detailed margin roadmap (13% to 17%) not been published, and what is the CCC outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reported EBITDA target of about 14% by FY29 stands, but priorities have shifted to quarterly delivery after the March 2026 environment change. Cash conversion cycle is about 140 days and expected to persist until inflation stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Rs 35 crore low-margin exit hurt FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no, citing strong demand and early indications in the first 45 days of Q1; European growth is expected to accelerate with the Almere plant.

risks_watch: Raw-material and crude-linked cost inflation has not yet fully flowed through; management expects pressure in coming quarters despite pricing actions.
Gross debt is expected to rise in the next 3-6 months due to inventory build, and insurance receipts after the fire may lag capex.
Start-up losses of about Rs 80-85 crore a year from US, UK and Germany development centres continue until revenue ramps (about 3 years).
Supplier contract honouring in flavours and raw material availability over the next 2-3 months.
Management did not give full-year FY27 guidance and deferred the detailed margin roadmap.
539450|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on H1 FY27 margin and pricing visibility, but cautious and non-committal beyond H1 due to raw-material and inflation uncertainty. Management was candid about the Rs 35 crore one-off and the reported margin gap, and it deferred the detailed three-year margin plan.
key_quotes: So, as we have given our guidance and even if you look at the fourth quarter this year, we are at 13% and something adjusted EBITDA from the sustainable operating business.
We believe that we have taken adequate steps to keep close to this number at least for the first half of this year and we will wait and watch and see and take corrective steps as necessary.
Our key objective remains clear, protecting margins while ensuring supply security for our customers.
I am actually confident that we will hit the Rs. 300 crore plus EBITDA for this year.

rows.why: Management cites rapid flavours volume growth, share gains during inflation as smaller players hold less inventory, Q1 FY27 secured on price and supply, and rest-of-world sales up about 34% YoY in Q4, though full-year revenue guidance was withheld.

539524|2026-03.headline: Dr. Lal PathLabs Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16.6% to Rs 703 crore; FY27 guided to early-to-mid-teens growth and 27-28% margins.
539524|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 16.6% YoY to Rs 703 crore, driven by sample volume growth of 12.9%, while Q4 EBITDA rose 10.5% to Rs 187 crore at a 26.6% margin. Q4 PAT fell to Rs 132 crore from Rs 156 crore, as last year included a Rs 41 crore one-time benefit and this year had a Rs 30 crore Labour Code charge in Q3. FY26 revenue grew 12.2% to Rs 2,763 crore with a 27.2% EBITDA margin, and the Board approved a final dividend of Rs 4 per share. Management guided FY27 revenue growth to early-to-mid-teens and margins to 27-28%, while stepping up spending on labs, infrastructure and A&P.

vs Rs 156 crore in Q4 FY25

segments.commentary: Sustained double-digit growth through the year, with added testing locations to improve turnaround time.

Reagent supply: about 3-4 months of inventory and long-term contracts; a prolonged Middle East conflict could affect imported reagent supply and cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other expense up sharply in Q4, and is the margin sustainable into FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited infra upgrades including Delhi NCR and higher A&P spend as geographies expand; FY27 margin guided at 27-28% with investment in labs continuing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise about 19% YoY in Q4, and was there a regrouping?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 129 crore vs Rs 108 crore: courier and transport costs were regrouped from employee benefit to other expenses; the rise reflects 14 new labs and Sovaaka operations, not the Labour Code.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 tax rate near 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: A reversal of deferred tax after an income tax assessment and refund; the underlying tax rate is still about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the basis for early-to-mid-teens FY27 growth when the post-COVID run rate was 10-12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Lab and collection network additions are maturing, Delhi NCR is expected to keep growing at double digits, and Suburban is recovering; the range is 13-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Is GLP-1 adding to patient volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth reflects the collection and lab network and that no differential impact from GLP-1 is being ascribed.

qa_highlights.question: Is Suburban's revenue or margin separately reported, and where does its margin stand?
qa_highlights.answer: Suburban is no longer reported separately and is part of West; management said West margins still have room to improve, and the company-wide margin is 27-28%.

Reagent and consumable supply and cost risk from the Middle East conflict after about 3-4 months of inventory.

539524|2026-06.headline: Dr. Lal PathLabs Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.1% to Rs 798 crore, with EBITDA margin of 31.0%, and guidance may move toward mid-teens growth.
539524|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 798 crore grew 19.1% YoY, described as the highest quarterly growth in four years, led by patient volume growth of 8.2% and sample volume growth of 10.7%. EBITDA rose 28.7% to Rs 247 crore (31.0% margin) and PAT rose 27.2% to Rs 170 crore. Management said the CGHS/ECHS price revision adds 2-3% to realisations, and it may be more towards mid-teens revenue growth than early teens. Management will not revise the 27-28% margin guidance until after Q2, and leans towards reinvesting any upside.

segments.name: Swasthfit (bundled wellness packages)
segments.commentary: Growing about 20% YoY, but its share of revenue is flat at about 27% because total revenue grew at a similar pace. Management expects this growth to be sustained.

segments.name: B2C vs B2B
segments.commentary: B2C is about 75% of the mix and B2B about 25%, which management considers a good balance and intends to keep.

segments.name: Genomics
segments.commentary: Contributes less than 5% of the portfolio and is not yet moving significantly; management does not disclose it separately.

segments.name: West India (Suburban)
segments.commentary: Growth is close to double digits after LIMS integration. Suburban profitability is no longer tracked separately after its voluntary liquidation and back-end merger.

segments.name: Delhi NCR
segments.commentary: Management aims to grow it at double digits, in line with or close to overall revenue, and says it is achieving this.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth now seen towards mid-teens rather than early teens for FY27, versus the earlier guidance; the Q1 beat was slightly ahead of expectations.
EBITDA margin guidance of 27-28% is unchanged for now; management will reassess after Q2 and leans towards reinvesting any upside into growth.
Patient volume growth guidance of 6-7% for FY27 is unchanged; management said Q1 came in slightly ahead and that it is too early to call the full year.
CGHS/ECHS price uplift of about 2-3% at company level is expected to flow through for at least another 2-3 quarters and to support margins for one or two more quarters.
General price increase is not planned for H1; it will be reassessed towards the end of the year based on competitor pricing and cost pressures.
Capex of about Rs 140-150 crore per year; 12-15 lab additions planned for FY27 and 3-4 radiology centres (Delhi NCR plus 1-2 pilots in Tier 2 towns).
International business is a 3-5 year project; management has not set a contribution target and says it will remain below 5% for at least the next five years.
capex_capacity: Capex guidance of about Rs 140-150 crore for the year, covering maintenance capex plus high-end radiology centres in Delhi NCR and Tier 2 North India.
Plans to add 12-15 labs in FY27, similar to last year; network addition numbers are disclosed once a year.
Plans to add 3-4 radiology centres this year, mainly Delhi NCR plus 1-2 pilots in Tier 2 towns outside Delhi NCR.
Capacity utilisation is not disclosed; management says capacity is never a constraint in pathology.
Sovaaka premium wellness centre: only the first centre is launched and is in the learning and stabilisation phase; no scale-up yet.
demand_pricing: Patient volume growth of 8.2% was spread across geographies; management said it is too early to call a sustained shift from the 5.5-6% levels of two quarters ago, because the fever season has not yet started.
CGHS/ECHS price revision is worth about 2-3% of realisations; the rest of the 10% rise in revenue per patient came from test and geography mix, per management.
Industry growth acceleration is described as structural and broad-based across geographies, with no single trigger identified yet.
Competitive intensity is seen as staying high; management sees no structural price change in recent quarters.
Gross margin is near 81%. Management says higher-realisation tests carry higher COGS, so margin is unlikely to improve significantly.
Weather in Q1 was unusual (more heat, some showers), and its effect on diagnostics volume is not yet known.
Tier 3 and below is about 39% of FY26 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the realisation growth comes from CGHS/ECHS, and will it continue for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: CGHS/ECHS price increase adds about 2-3% at company level and should continue for at least another 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the guidance be upgraded from 27-28% margin and mid-teens growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is more likely to be mid-teens than early teens; margin guidance will be reviewed after Q2, with a lean towards reinvestment.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Swasthfit growth sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Swasthfit grew about 20% in Q1 and management expects this rate to be sustained, with traction in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Neuome and international plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Neuome (30% stake, up to Rs 3.5 crore) is a diagnostic supply-chain innovation play with operational benefit, not a new business. International is a long-term project: Ghana (80% of Sunshine Healthcare, up to GHS 45.6 million) and a Dubai subsidiary, with focus on Africa, Middle East, CIS and Southeast Asia; no target set.

qa_highlights.question: How should the cash of about Rs 1,700 crore be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Primarily M&A to build presence in the West and South, plus high-end radiology centres as capex on top of maintenance capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost as a percentage of revenue fall to 16.6%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is a reclassification of logistics and courier costs out of manpower cost into other costs, applied like-to-like in the previous quarter too, not a structural change.

risks_watch: Margin guidance of 27-28% is not revised until after Q2; the CGHS/ECHS price pass-through is expected to support margins for only one or two more quarters, so the margin trajectory in H2 depends on reinvestment choices.

Patient volume growth (8.2% in Q1) is unproven as a sustained shift; management wants Q2 and Q3 through the fever season before drawing conclusions, and Q1 weather was unusual with effects not yet known.
General price increase is not planned for H1 and will be reassessed toward year-end based on competitor pricing and cost pressures; competitive intensity is expected to stay high.
Gross margin near 81% is not expected to improve materially; management flagged possible currency and inflation pressure on imported testing material if geopolitical cost pressures continue.
Employee cost ratio of 16.6% partly reflects a reclassification of logistics and courier costs, which limits like-to-like comparison with historical 18-19% levels.

Capital deployment of about Rs 1,700 crore cash is mainly directed to M&A in West and South India, with no deal size or timeline disclosed; international contribution is expected to stay below 5% for at least five years.

So the idea always is to reinvest for future growth. That is the dominant idea.
I think we need the cycle to run through quarters for us to say that it has really caught on because we have not yet entered fever season this time round.
I do not think any of us are banking on competitive intensity reducing in this industry.

539551|2026-03.headline: Narayana Q4 FY26: India margin rose to 25.1% (from 21.5%), but consolidated EBITDA dipped to ~20% on UK acquisition costs; management gives no formal guidance.
539551|2026-03.overview: Management highlighted high-end case mix and robotic cardiac volumes (about 100 robotic cardiac cases a month in Bangalore) driving India ARPP and margin gains. The UK business (PPG, acquired with five months in FY26) diluted consolidated margins and PAT; management says ~200 bps of the ~500 bps margin drop was one-time deal costs, normalising to ~22%. Cayman insurance losses (USD 5 million in the quarter) remain high, with a loss ratio of about 110–112% and price increases from June. India clinics continue to lose cash because of corporate overheads, and FY26 greenfield capex was only INR 109 crore against INR 424 crore planned.

segments.commentary: Margin 25.1% vs 21.5% a year ago, attributed to transformation initiatives, robotic cardiac and high-end transplant work, and higher-configuration beds; volumes stagnated while ARPP grew. Mumbai (SRCC) broke even in Q4.

segments.commentary: Clinic and insurance losses flat at ~INR 66 crore in FY26; management expects similar cash burn into FY27 as 11 Bangalore clinics expand and Kolkata is added, and clinics will be merged into hospital reporting from FY27.

segments.commentary: Five months consolidated in FY26; acquisition costs and transition/IT separation costs weighed on margin, and PAT is negative mainly from amortisation. Management says cash PAT covers the GBP 150 million 7-year loan, which is serviced in the UK.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Cayman hospital growth outlook?

539682|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 56.9% YoY to Rs 728 million and PAT rose 95% YoY to Rs 117 million, with EBITDA margin at 21.2%.
539682|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached Rs 728 million, up 56.9% YoY and 16.3% QoQ, with growth attributed to direct advertiser demand in Quick Commerce, BFSI, FinTech and Retail and to international expansion through agency and reseller models. EBITDA was Rs 154 million (21.2% margin, up 240 bps YoY) and PAT was Rs 117 million (16.1% margin, up 320 bps YoY). Management highlighted the launch of the Mobavenue Neural Engine, the PiiX Apple-ecosystem product, US entry and Singapore/Philippines operations. Direct clients' share of revenue fell to 65.2% from 73.9% in FY26, which management attributed to the agency/reseller route used for international expansion.

segments.commentary: Make up the remaining ~34.8% of revenue. Management cited agency and reseller models as an accelerator for international growth.

segments.commentary: Newly launched in Q1 for Apple Search Ads, custom product pages and ASO; management said revenue contribution is negligible today and it will start in India.

qa_highlights.question: Why did direct client share fall from 73.9% to 65.2%, and what is the optimal mix with agency/reseller partners?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift is from the agency/reseller entry route for international markets. It described this as a small-to-medium-term approach and expects the direct advertiser base to return to a normal position over the long term.

qa_highlights.question: What moat protects the Neural Engine from global platforms replicating it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it owns the full stack across all three P3 layers and that proprietary consented signals feed a closed feedback loop, with pricing linked to outcomes. It pointed to rising revenue per outcome as evidence.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is 56.9% growth, and what would normalise it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it optimises for full-year performance and targets 30% growth and 20% EBITDA margin over the long term. It said quarter-to-quarter variation is expected as international markets scale.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 56.9% growth: market or share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said general market growth cannot explain 56.9%. It attributed growth to international markets (UK first, then LatAm, Philippines, US, Singapore) and premium inventory such as streaming, CTV, Apple ecosystem and DOOH.

qa_highlights.question: What is PiiX's revenue contribution and size of opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PiiX revenue is negligible today. It cited Apple's Indian reach at about 6% growing to 8-10%, and said the product will start in India before going international.

qa_highlights.question: How will the preferential raise proceeds be allocated, and what are the key risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said proceeds are mainly for strategic acquisitions with disciplined selection, plus technology investment. Named risks were regulation, currency (revenue balanced between INR and USD), AI disruption and inflation; no near-term inflation impact was seen.

539686|2026-03.headline: K.P. Energy FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,500 crore (up 57% YoY) and Q4 PAT hit a record INR 78.69 crore.
539686|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 consolidated total revenue of INR 1,505.54 crore (up 57% YoY), EBITDA of INR 328.44 crore (up 68%) and PAT of INR 181.4 crore (up 57%). Q4 net sales reached an all-time quarterly high of INR 631.81 crore, up 83% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at 21% (up 194 bps YoY) and PAT of INR 78.69 crore. The order book is about 2 GW (INR 3,000 plus crore), with about 230 MW added in Q4, while operating cash flow weakened due to higher inventory (WTG turbines) and advances. Management guided to 40-50% growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did IPP unit generation and revenue decline in Q4 YoY?

539730|2026-03.headline: Fredun Pharma Q4 FY26 total income rose 27.27% YoY to INR213 crore, EBITDA margin expanded 326 bps to 13.67%, and management guides 25-30% FY27 top-line growth.
539730|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR213 crore (up 27.27% YoY), EBITDA INR29.13 crore (up 67.05%, margin 13.67%, +326 bps) and net profit INR11.07 crore (up 56.47%). For FY26, total income was INR639.12 crore (up 40.08%), EBITDA INR94.79 crore (margin 14.83%, +276 bps) and net profit INR33.21 crore (up 59.59%). Management said new-age businesses (pet care, mobility, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, hormones, anti-aging) carry higher gross margins and are growing 40-50% CAGR, while vintage business grows 10-20%. Management guided to 25-30% top-line growth for FY27 and said margins will keep rising for about 8 quarters before a spike. Working capital and finance cost were the main investor concerns.

financial_highlights.change: +27.27% YoY vs INR167.41 crore in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Vintage business (pharma, exports, institutional, tolling, third-party branding, Fredun DC)
segments.commentary: Growing 15-20% YoY per management (later said 10-15% on cruise control); exports about INR110-120 crore, tolling about INR24 crore, indirect exports/institution sales about INR120-130 crore, third-party branding INR45-50 crore, Fredun DC INR25-30 crore. Over 1,000 registrations pending.

segments.name: Pet care
segments.commentary: About INR42-43 crore of FY26 sales; 42 functional food biscuit variants being launched; Wagr.in e-commerce/pet portal soft launch expected late June to early July 2026.

segments.name: Mobility (BraceOn, DigiOn, NebOn, Mobilitics)
segments.commentary: About INR29-30 crore of FY26 sales; management targets INR100 crore run-rate in 2-2.5 years and INR250-300 crore in 5-7 years. Mobilitics (physiotherapy) targeted at INR30-40 crore in two years; growing 55-60% CAGR per management.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: About INR26 crore of FY26 sales per management.

segments.name: Cosmetics (mass market)
segments.commentary: About INR20-22 crore of FY26 sales; dermaceutics gross margins cited at 80-90%.

segments.name: Hormones and anti-aging (launch)
segments.commentary: Two new lines being launched via doctor channel, starting in MMRDA region and metros; NAD+ manufacturing and exclusive API import rights cited. Hormone gross margin cited at around 50%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth of 25-30% over FY26 targeted; management says run-rate is in line and it could do better.
EBITDA/PAT margin expected to keep rising for about 8 quarters, then a sudden profit spike once new-age demographic reach saturates (about 7-8 quarters, or 2.5-3 years per another answer).
Long-term PAT target of 10-12% in the next few years on a 2-3x top line.
Mix goal: new-age business to reach about 50% of revenue within the next few years, and about 70:30 within 2-3 years after that; transition to consumer company over 7-8 years.
Management expects finance-cost percentage to fall within 3-4 years as ratios improve.
Pet care goal: products across a pet's life by 2032-33; a first-in-India formulation in Stage 4 trials expected within 12 months.
capex_capacity: About 43 manufacturing locations; around 80% or more of products made in-house, with contract manufacturing used for wheelchairs, braces and sterile products (liquid injections, PFS, dry powder injections, beta-lactams).
12-13 additional packing lines to be added by end-September 2026.
A new wing to be constructed within the existing plant; no capex amount or timeline given beyond the packing lines.
Management targets top-3 or top-4 manufacturing capacity at one location within 2.5 years; cluster of 4 plants at one location.
Facilities being set up for functional foods, with plans for wet pet food manufacturing.
demand_pricing: Order book of about INR320-330 crore in hand, equal to 6-7 months of orders, per management.

Raw material costs rose due to Middle East/geopolitical tensions and petroleum-linked inputs; management said 3-4 months of buffer stock shielded margins, with a 1-2% cost absorbed by buyers on some products.
Some products repriced upward; management said price increases were passed through and that the impact on bottom line is nil.
Vintage business growth 15-20% per one answer and 10-15% per another; new-age growth 40-50% CAGR from a smaller base.
Mobility competitors named as Visco and Timo; management claims no online-brand exposure and an offline-only distribution model.

qa_highlights.question: Growth plan for the hormone and anti-aging launches (Keshav Toshniwal).
qa_highlights.answer: Two lines launching via doctor channel, starting MMRDA and metros, with online sales of medicated hormone products planned; NAD+ manufacturing and exclusive API import rights cited; CDSCO rule limiting prescribing to certified doctors seen as favourable.

qa_highlights.question: Mobility scale-up strategy (Vinod Shah).
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 mobility sales about INR30 crore; INR100 crore run-rate targeted in 2-2.5 years; distribution to match Maharashtra in 17-18 states within 2.5 years; Mobilitics physiotherapy pre-bookings full.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material inflation and demand slowdown from geopolitics (Ankit).
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price rises were absorbed by buffer stock and passed through; 1-2% absorbed on some products; no impact to bottom line; orders ahead of six to seven months.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split between vintage and new-age businesses (Nikhil Agarwal).
qa_highlights.answer: Vintage contributes most FY26 revenue (exports INR110-120 crore, institutional INR120-130 crore, third-party branding INR45-50 crore); new-age includes pet care INR42-43 crore, mobility INR29-30 crore, nutraceuticals INR26 crore, cosmetics INR20-22 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify FY27 growth (Nishita Shanklesha).
qa_highlights.answer: Management intends 25-30% top-line growth over FY26, says run-rate supports it, and notes a history of under-promising and over-delivering.

qa_highlights.question: Finance cost and debt (Keshav Toshniwal).
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged rates are higher, said absolute debt will rise with scale, and expects the cost percentage to decline over the next 3-4 years; debt serviced comfortably.

qa_highlights.question: Free cash flow and working capital (Devang Shah).
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is INR270 crore against about INR700 crore revenue (vs INR220 crore on INR450 crore earlier); operating cash flow now positive; debt-to-equity 0.8; more working capital and debt may be needed for growth.

risks_watch: Working capital intensity: inventory of about INR270 crore; management concedes working capital and debt needs will rise with growth.
Finance cost: management acknowledged higher interest rates; absolute debt expected to rise before ratios improve.
Geopolitical raw-material inflation: petroleum-linked inputs rising; pass-through of 1-2% cost absorbed by buyers on some products.
Pet care Wagr.in launch slipping repeatedly (earlier mid-June, now late June to early July); management acknowledged a 3-4 month delay.
Margin path depends on new-age mix, with management's 10-12% PAT projection still lacking a timeline beyond a few years.
Unquantified figures: the stated 1,000+ pending registrations and the ambiguity between 8-quarter and 2.5-3 year margin timelines.
539730|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and promotional, with broad claims on margins, growth and new categories (hormones, anti-aging, pet care, mobility) and limited hard data. Cautious only on finance cost and working capital, which management addressed by pointing to positive operating cash flow and a planned strategy.
key_quotes: We can consider a growth and overall growth of around 25% to 30% on our top line from the last year.
Last 19 years, our growth is a 32% CAGR. There's not a single year of degrowth in the last 19 years.
Working capital is not a worry for us right now.
We are not a inorganic growth Pet Care company where we are spending money to sell our products.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 326 bps YoY to 13.67% in Q4 FY26 and FY26 margin is 14.83% (+276 bps); management says margins keep rising for about 8 quarters, helped by higher-margin new-age mix (hormone gross margin ~50%, dermaceutics 80-90%) and buffer stock shielding raw-material costs for 3-4 months.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 12-13 additional packing lines are committed for completion by end-September 2026 and a new wing is planned within the existing plant, though no capex amount or timeline is given for the wing.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 25-30% top-line growth for FY27 (midpoint 27.5%) backed by a INR320-330 crore order book equal to 6-7 months of orders, and new-age lines growing 40-50% CAGR while vintage grows 10-20%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not disclosed, but the 12-13 packing-line addition and new wing, plus a stated goal of top-3/top-4 capacity at one location within 2.5 years, point to further capex, though no amount or board approval is given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says the run-rate supports 25-30% growth and that it has a history of under-promising and over-delivering, but gives no hard upgrade figure.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Pet care Wagr.in launch has already slipped from mid-June to late June/early July (a 3-4 month delay acknowledged), and raw-material inflation from petroleum-linked inputs is rising with 1-2% cost absorbed by buyers on some products.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Two hormone/anti-aging lines are launching via the doctor channel starting MMRDA and metros, 42 functional food biscuit variants are being launched, and Wagr.in soft launch is expected late June to early July 2026.

rows.label: Working capital and debt needs rise with growth
rows.why: Inventory is INR270 crore against about INR700 crore revenue (vs INR220 crore on INR450 crore earlier), debt-to-equity is 0.8, and management concedes more working capital and debt will be needed, though operating cash flow is now positive.

rows.label: Mobility scale-up to 17-18 states
rows.why: Mobility sales are about INR30 crore in FY26 with a INR100 crore run-rate target in 2-2.5 years, and distribution is to match Maharashtra across 17-18 states within 2.5 years.

rows.label: Finance cost percentage to fall
rows.why: Management acknowledges higher interest rates and says absolute debt will rise with scale before the finance-cost percentage declines over 3-4 years, so near-term finance cost pressure persists.

tone.note: Management was confident on margin expansion, 25-30% FY27 growth, new categories and the 12-13 packing lines, and cautious only on finance cost and working capital; analysts pushed on working capital, finance cost and the Wagr.in delay.

539730|2026-06.headline: Fredun Pharma Q1 FY27 standalone total income rose 90.44% YoY to INR228.25 crores; EBITDA INR32.78 crores, margin 14.36%.
539730|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income for Q1 FY27 was INR228.25 crores, up 90.44% YoY, with EBITDA of INR32.78 crores (up 92.90%) and EBITDA margin of 14.36% (up 18 bps). Net profit was INR13.17 crores (up 94.63%), with net margin at 5.77% (up 12 bps). Management attributed the strong Q1 partly to orders booked at old prices in the prior quarter and higher stock carried into Q4 FY26. Management reiterated FY27 revenue target of around INR800 crores and said it is on track to overachieve, declining to commit to INR1,000 crores.

segments.commentary: Growing ~35-45% YoY per management, with some growing faster off lower bases; vintage business growing ~15-20% YoY.

segments.name: Fredun GX (generics)
segments.commentary: Present in ~19 states (vs 17 cited in question), revenue base ~INR100-110 crores; management guides 25-35% growth, and 30-35% for the next four years.

segments.name: Pet care (incl. functional foods)
segments.commentary: Current pet care business ~INR40-45 crores; functional foods FY27 target INR18-24 crores; guided 40-50% growth over next 3-4 years. Cat food launch planned around Q4 FY27, with a target of INR100 crores within 3-3.5 years of launch.

segments.name: Wagr.in (pet e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Soft launch around 15 June 2026 in beta; ~1,500-2,000 products listed; management expects brand onboarding complete within 20-25 days and beta testing done in 60-65 days. Described as a separate company within the Fredun ecosystem.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target around INR800 crores; management says it is in line to achieve and hopes to cross it, but declined to commit to INR1,000 crores.

Management expects margin improvement and a profitability step-up in roughly 7-11 quarters as demographic reach completes; it expects EBIT margin to be near 12-13% within about 12 quarters, with timing uncertainty of a quarter either way.
Working capital absolute value will rise with revenue (e.g., at INR2,000-3,000 crores revenue), but management sees it in line with manufacturing peers.
capex_capacity: CapEx plan of INR30-40 crores in FY27, with a similar INR30-40 crores next year; INR35-45 crores per year for the next two years per management.
Maintenance capex estimated at about 2% of revenue at ~INR1,000 crores revenue level.
Goal by end-December 2028 / early 2029 to be among the largest manufacturing units at a single location in India.
Five plants in Palghar; management cites ~43 locations where products are manufactured.
Functional food capacity build-out underway; OEM supply planned for other companies.
demand_pricing: Management attributed part of Q1 strength to orders booked at old prices in Q4 FY26 ahead of price increases, and to higher stock held in the prior quarter.
Q1 is seasonally weaker as sales targets drive purchases in Q4; orders typically start rolling in around end-April.
Pharmacies and distributors are said to be willing to hold more inventory of Fredun products; GX repeatability described as high.
Functional foods: Jain variant picked up well in certain pockets; 42 functional food variants being added; cat biscuit treats planned.
Gross margin ranges cited: pet care 45-55%, mobility 40-50%, nutrition 35-50%, dermaceutics 70-75%. Management said it may sacrifice some margin to drive penetration.

qa_highlights.question: Where can Fredun be in 3-5 years, given FY27 Q1 revenue nearly matches FY23 full-year revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended growth of ~30-35% for next 3 years from new-age brands (35-45%), vintage (15-20%), new capacity, and 43 manufacturing locations.

qa_highlights.question: How large can domestic GX become over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: GX is in ~19 states with a base of ~INR100-110 crores; guided 25-35% growth, and 30-35% over the next four years.

qa_highlights.question: Can you guide CapEx for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: INR30-40 crores in FY27 and similar next year; INR35-45 crores per year for two years; maintenance about 2% of revenue at ~INR1,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 so strong and will future quarters keep this growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly due to old-price bookings and higher stock in Q4 FY26; future quarters expected to grow at roughly Q1's rate.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital outlook and interest cost trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital at ~INR170-175 crores on ~INR850 crores run rate, rising with scale; interest cost falling as limit usage declines; rating upgraded from BBB to BBB+.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory days target?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently ~135-140 days, targeted at ~120 days within four quarters, with a 110-125 day range expected long term.

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue hit INR1,000 crores and EBIT INR100 crores this year, and will EBIT margin reach 12-13%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit; FY27 target ~INR800 crores, on track to overachieve. EBIT margin near 12-13% expected in roughly 12 quarters, with timing uncertain.

539787|2026-03.headline: HCG FY26 revenue rose 15% to INR2,545 crore and adjusted EBITDA margin widened 70 bps to 18.5%, while Q4 revenue growth slowed to 11.3%.
539787|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR652 crore (+11.3% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA was INR125 crore (+17% YoY, margin 19.2%, +90 bps). Management attributed the Q4 slowdown to deliberate exit of low-margin business and softer medical value travel, linked to the Middle East conflict. The company completed a INR425 crore rights issue, reduced net debt to EBITDA to 1.4x, and agreed to sell the Milann fertility business at an EV of INR63 crore. Management reiterated about 15% medium-term growth and a target of about 1,000 added beds by FY30.

financial_highlights.change: 87% when adjusted for ESOP settlement one-off
interest cost about INR40 crore per quarter; expected to decline

segments.name: South cluster
segments.commentary: About 39% of FY26 revenue, grew about 13% for the year; Q4 growth moderated by softer medical value travel and paring of low-margin business. South margins already above 25%.

segments.name: West cluster
segments.commentary: Largest contributor at about 45% of FY26 revenue, grew about 14%, led by Gujarat and Maharashtra inflows and Ahmedabad capacity expansion; Ahmedabad center utilization about 50%.

segments.name: East cluster
segments.commentary: About 11% of FY26 revenue, grew about 11%; Cuttack and Ranchi performing well, Kolkata expected to benefit from clinician onboarding.

segments.name: International (Kenya)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 39% YoY in Q4 and 71% for FY26, driven by radiation oncology and PET services ramp-up; Q4 growth was below earlier estimates per management.

segments.name: Milann (fertility)
segments.commentary: Being sold to Inviga Healthcare Fund at EV of INR63 crore; equity consideration INR37.6 crore, 75% upfront at closing expected in Q1 FY27, balance over 18 months. Center count reduced from 9 to 6.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term revenue growth estimate remains close to 15%; management expects Q4 low-margin exit and Middle East-related MVT softness to normalise over the next couple of quarters.
Margin expansion of about 100 bps targeted; management said it is confident of delivering the earlier estimate, with West and East clusters the main sources of expansion.
Existing hospitals with in-hospital expansion expected to deliver at least 75-80% of growth over the next couple of years; remainder from new centers.
Internal net debt to EBITDA ceiling of 2.5x for medium to long term.
About 1,000 beds to be added by FY30: about 400 greenfield and about 600 brownfield. Near-term brownfield additions of 200+ beds over 24 months (Cuttack 75, Vizag 50, Ranchi 30, Bhavnagar 20+).
Bangalore KR flagship at 30%+ ROCE; company expects 20% ROCE over the next four to five years.
capex_capacity: North Bangalore comprehensive oncology center commenced in Q4 FY26, with medical, surgical and radiation oncology, nuclear medicine, PET-CT, BMT and MR-Linac (pay-per-use model).
Brownfield expansion of 200+ beds over next 24 months at about INR45 lakh per bed, implying INR90-100 crore growth capex.
Whitefield: existing site considered too small; management seeking an alternate asset offering 120-130 beds.
Greenfield pipeline: 10-12 cities under evaluation, including Pune, Surat, Coimbatore, Nellore, Lucknow and Jalandhar.
Day-care centers to be expanded from five to about 13-15 over 24 months (8-10 additional).
demand_pricing: Growth drivers cited: North Bangalore, Whitefield, brownfield expansion, addition of about 23 oncologists in Q4 FY26, day-care expansion, ORC outreach and sales acceleration.
Payor mix improved by about 100 bps over the last couple of quarters; company is deliberately exiting low-margin business, which weighed on ARPP growth.
Management expects ARPP to improve over the medium to long term as low-margin business is replaced by higher-margin, higher-realisation business.
Center utilization of 58% (blended across chemo beds, OT, radiation machines), not occupancy; Ahmedabad at about 50%.
Management stated growth has been broad-based across regions, with 18 cities and 25 hospitals in the network.

qa_highlights.question: How should Q4 11% revenue growth be read given Q4 seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited deliberate exit of low-margin business and Middle East conflict impact on medical value travel to West and South; expects normalisation over the next couple of quarters and medium-term growth near 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Debt targets and margin expansion by cluster?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt to EBITDA at 1.4x, internal ceiling 2.5x. Margin upside mainly from West and East, as South is mature with margins above 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost outlook after rights issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects some reduction after the rights issue and long-term debt repayment; average interest cost is 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation growth despite low-margin exits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is not the only objective; margin and returns take priority, with short-term revenue impact and long-term ARPP benefit. Could not quantify revenue forgone.

qa_highlights.question: Reasons for Milann divestment and buyer selection?
qa_highlights.answer: Milann footprint fell from 9 to 6 centers, margins low and only marginally above break-even post-rent; non-core. Inviga chosen through a competitive sale process.

qa_highlights.question: MR-Linac ownership and Bangalore ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: MR-Linac is pay-per-use for an asset-light model. Bangalore KR runs at 30%+ ROCE; company targets 20% ROCE over four to five years.

539807|2026-03.headline: AvenuesAI FY26 consolidated revenue from operations rose 103% to INR8,116 crores and PAT 58% to INR332 crores, while net revenue grew 15% to INR603 crores.

Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR2,490 crores (+115% YoY, +5% QoQ), net revenue INR149 crores (+11% YoY), and adjusted PAT INR95 crores (+90% YoY). 539807|2026-06.headline: Gross revenue rose 109% YoY to INR 2,680 crore and PAT rose 45% to INR 85 crore, while net revenue fell 3% to INR 147 crore.

539872|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11.3% YoY to INR165.6 crore with gross margin up 210 bps to 48.3%; management guides 10-15% revenue growth for FY27.
539872|2026-06.overview: Bajaj Healthcare reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR165.6 crore, up 11.3% YoY and 8.2% QoQ, with EBITDA of about INR29.6 crore (17.8% margin) and PAT from continuing operations of INR13.9 crore (8.4% margin). Domestic API was the main growth driver at INR92.3 crore (up 27% YoY), while exports (INR50.1 crore) and formulations (INR23.3 crore) contributed the rest. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 10-15% and EBITDA margins of 18-20% for FY27 and FY28, and reiterated pipeline timelines for peptide, oncology API, and CDMO/novel-drug launches. Receivable days fell to 131 from 145 at FY26 end, and the call was the company's first earnings call.

segments.name: Domestic API
segments.commentary: Revenue INR92.3 crore, up 27% YoY; management said API prices were broadly stable QoQ and the growth was not price-led. Ascorbic acid and salts contribute about 8-10% of revenue.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Revenue INR50.1 crore in Q1. Magnesium L-Threonate (nutraceutical ingredient supplied to a US innovator) is the largest export product at about 10% of FY26 revenue, with FY27 growth guided at 15-20%. Management expects export share to rise to 30-35% over time.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR23.3 crore in Q1. Cenobamate CDMO launch expected to add INR10-12 crore in FY27; Oncocare brand business covers 15+ brands across 23 states and 3 UTs.

EBITDA margin of 18-20% for FY27 and FY28.

Receivable days expected to settle at 110-120 days going forward.

Oncology API dedicated facility: commercial target Q4 2028.
Gen Rx Pharmaceutical facility in Nashik (solid dosage forms): acquisition pending NCLT approval; commercial production expected in H2 2027.
Savli DSIR-approved R&D centre expansion of over 10,000 sq ft, expected to be operational by August 2026, housing 100+ researchers. R&D spend rose from 0.4% of sales in 2024 to 2.2% in 2026.
Three loss-making Tarapur plants: one sold, two remain with no buyer yet; sale proceeds not quantified.
demand_pricing: API prices stable QoQ in Q1; management said future pricing depends on geopolitical developments and oil prices.
Semaglutide (first peptide planned) market price cited at USD120-150 per gram. Plant is designed for global markets, with initial work for India.
CDMO: DMFs filed in UK and EU and six CEP approvals received in the last 6-8 months. Management said first customer revenue could come at end-FY28, with quantum not yet estimated.
Cenobamate: SEC recommendation received; DCGI NOC and state licence still pending; tie-ups with eight Indian marketing companies, with the company acting as CDMO partner.
Suvorexant: BE studies completed; commercialisation expected Q4 FY28 because the patent is still in force.

Vitamin C is about 8-9% of revenue; backward integration via ICT MoU expected to complete in 2029. Eight to ten API molecules being backward-integrated, expected to be 20-25% of revenue, with a 1-2% margin uplift.

539889|2026-03.headline: Parag Milk Foods Q4 FY26: gross margin rose to 28% from 25.9% in Q3, but EBITDA margin slipped to about 8.1% and core-category volumes fell 3%.

539889|2026-06.headline: Parag Milk Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR945 crores (record Q1), but EBITDA margin slipped to 7.4% from 7.7% and PAT fell 20%.
539889|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue reached a record INR945 crores, up 11% YoY in value and 3% in volume. EBITDA grew 6% to INR70 crores, with margin down 30 bps to 7.4%; PBT was broadly flat and PAT fell 20% on higher current tax. Gross profit rose 11% to INR258 crores with gross margin stable at about 27.3%, which management attributed to calibrated pricing and mix. Flagship categories (ghee, cheese, paneer, dahi; 61% of revenue) saw volume fall 2% YoY, with B2C growing and B2B declining modestly; new-age business (Pride of Cows and Avvatar) grew 59% and reached about 13% of revenue.

financial_highlights.change: +11% YoY; gross margin stable (27.3% vs 28% in Q4 FY26 per call)

segments.name: Flagship categories (ghee, cheese, paneer, dahi)
segments.commentary: 61% of Q1 revenue; volume down 2% YoY on transient slowdown in certain channels, value up 10%. B2C grew strongly while B2B declined modestly; B2C flagship growth was 'high single digit to close to double digit'. Dahi now included in flagship (previously in Others).

segments.name: New-age business (Pride of Cows, Avvatar)
segments.commentary: Grew 59% YoY, about 13% of revenue vs 9% a year earlier. Portfolio expanded into protein bars, ready-to-drink (RTD) coffee with 15 g protein per serving (launched Q1), creatine. Management said new-age margins are roughly double the company average, without giving a figure.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: Down 46% YoY per analyst question; management said this reflects PSI and state incentive income falling after GST cut on ghee and cheese from 12% to 5% in September 2025, plus dahi moving into flagship. UHT and beverages performed reasonably well.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 revenue growth above 10%, with Q2 and Q3 supported by festive demand.
Calibrated price increases will continue in response to commodity costs; ghee prices were raised late in Q1 and new-age prices were revisited recently.
Milk prices described as stable; slight increase possible in coming months due to monsoon-linked seasonality and festive demand.
Distribution target of more than 1.5 million outlets within three years.
Management aspires to return flagship B2C growth to double digits; B2B will be pursued where margins allow.
capex_capacity: Cheese capacity to double from 60 to 120 metric tons per day over about 1.5 years, targeted by March 2028.
Doubling cheese capacity to be paired with a parallel expansion in whey protein generation; milk procurement to be scaled up to match.
Renewable energy: a solar JV with Tata Power Solar; biogas power from farm (about 5,000 cattle); the investment value was INR4.6 crores per the annual report, not INR50 crores.
demand_pricing: Whey protein prices reportedly moved from about INR2,500/kg to about INR3,400/kg recently; management said global whey demand is structural, not temporary.
Management said Avvatar retail prices rose only in stages, not 100% as an analyst suggested; consumers switch between protein formats as prices change.
Q1 B2B volumes were deliberately forgone where customers negotiated hard on pricing, to protect margins.
Avvatar sales are 75% via quick commerce, e-commerce and website, and 25% via traditional retail and specialised protein outlets.
Management said Google searches and website traffic rose about 200% over the last two months, after the India's Got Latent association.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth break the roughly 10% sales growth band?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will exceed 10%, with Q2 and Q3 festive quarters expected to drive it; Q1 is seasonally weak.

qa_highlights.question: How is Avvatar up 59% when retail prices reportedly doubled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume also grew strongly and that prices rose in stages, not 100%; new products and lower-cost protein entry formats contributed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin flat despite mix improvement and price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said milk cost pass-through was complete in Q1 at INR42/litre, and the mix gain was offset by milk inflation; gross profit growth matched revenue growth at 11%.

qa_highlights.question: Why are core-category volumes falling despite wider distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is in B2B, where volumes were given up to protect profitability; B2C is not declining.

qa_highlights.question: Can B2B channel losses be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to name customers or channels or give numbers, citing commercial sensitivity; B2B deals are short-term and come and go.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Samay Raina / India's Got Latent deal's cost and ROI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose cost, timeline or ROI, calling it a special commercial deal aimed at awareness.

qa_highlights.question: Is Avvatar's whey price rise a margin hit given backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose cost of production per kg or margin impact by product, saying margins are reported on a blended basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income spike in alternate quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income is usually higher in March due to annual fair-value gains on biological assets (cattle); Q1 FY26 also had a one-off gain on sale of the idle Sonipat plant.

539957|2026-03.headline: MGL Q4 FY26 net profit fell to INR132 crore from INR202 crore QoQ as West Asia LNG disruption curtailed industrial supply to about 80%.
539957|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 average sales volume rose 6.15% YoY to 4.672 mmscmd, with CNG at 3.349 mmscmd and DPNG at 0.605 mmscmd. Industrial and commercial supply was curtailed to about 80% from mid-March after the West Asia LNG disruption, and gas cost rose as the pooled gas mechanism replaced part of Henry Hub supply. FY26 EBITDA fell to INR1,451 crore from INR1,570 crore and PAT to INR847 crore from INR1,041 crore. Management declined to give firm FY27 margin guidance, saying it would prioritise volume growth and pass through costs only where alternate-fuel pricing allows.

540005|2026-09.headline: LTM Q2 FY27 revenue rose 5.1% YoY in constant currency to USD 1.24bn, with order inflow of USD 1.3bn and EBIT margin at 15.6%.
540005|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was USD 1.235bn, up 1.1% QoQ and 5.1% YoY in constant currency, with INR revenue of Rs 11,808 crores (+13.6% YoY). EBIT margin expanded 10bps QoQ to 15.6%, while PAT margin fell to 11.7% from 12.7% because Q1 included a one-time gain on Voicing.AI. Cash conversion weakened sharply (OCF/PAT 39%, FCF/PAT 24%) due to gratuity funding under the labour codes, an ad hoc TDS timing effect, and advance tax. Order inflow of USD 1.3bn was AI-centric, short-tenure deals, and management is deliberately shifting KPIs away from TCV. Management reiterated that H2 will be better than H1, with the Saudi business (routed via a JV and classified under Tech) a drag this quarter.
