qa_highlights.question: Is the seasonal Tech decline recurring every year, and what is the Saudi effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Tech decline reflects the annual renewal cycle of the top tech account (fiscal starting July) plus Saudi business routed through a JV with a tech company. Management expects Tech to return to normal growth from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will TCV become less relevant, and will LTM disclose ACV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI deals are shorter and faster to revenue, so TCV understates them. ACV disclosure is planned but deferred by about one more quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth reach high-single or double digits by FY28, and is FY27 close to FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 lost about 0.6-0.7% of growth to Saudi, expects H2 better than H1, and aims for FY28 as the stronger year; FY27 growth near FY26 is an endeavour, not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the top BFSI client's vendor spend cut a medium-term risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the consolidation from 50+ vendors to five is a multi-year benefit to LTM, with productivity headwinds already passed through in Q3-Q4 of last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is payout low versus peers, and what are capital allocation plans?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said payout rose to about 45% from about 40%; reinvestment via M&A and organic investment (BlueVerse, GCC, talent) is prioritised. M&A is open but must be white-space and fairly priced.

qa_highlights.question: Has the macro or pricing environment changed?

rows.why: Kolkata Global Delivery and AI Competency Center already opened and BlueVerse expanded to Hyderabad, with a GCC business unit planned, but no capacity numbers given and utilisation is flat at 86.4%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides H2 better than H1 (H1 YoY growth 5.4%) and Q3/Q4 better than Q1, backed by USD 1.3bn order inflow, though Q2 lost about 0.6-0.7% of growth to Saudi.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 86.4% excluding trainees (above 80%), but the company is already adding centres and a GCC unit, with no capex quantum disclosed; cash of about Rs 15,300 crores gives room.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only holds guidance: FY27 growth near FY26 is an endeavour, not committed, and Q2 growth was 5.1% constant currency.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Saudi/Middle East disruption cost about 0.6-0.7% of growth in Q2 and Rest of World fell 1.4% QoQ, and FY27 growth parity with FY26 is not committed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management committed to build new domain-specific SLMs every quarter (three created this quarter, six AI patents granted), and a GCC business unit details are promised in coming days.

rows.label: AI-led order inflow of USD 1.3bn with short-tenure deals
rows.why: Order inflow of USD 1.3bn in Q2 was majority AI-led and faster-to-revenue (AI projects run 6 months to 1 year), supporting H2 revenue, though TCV is no longer comparable and ACV disclosure is deferred.

rows.label: Randstad Digital acquisition closure
rows.when: Q3 FY27 close, integration 3-4 months after
rows.why: Approvals are expected in Q3 with closure by end of Q3, then 3-4 months to realign acquired Australia and Europe markets; Q4 amortisation headwind said to be not significant.

rows.label: Cash conversion normalisation
rows.why: OCF/PAT fell to 39% from 79% and FCF/PAT to 24% from 63%; gratuity funding completes by October and OCF/PAT is expected to normalise in Q3 but not return to prior levels.

tone.note: Management was confident on AI momentum, H2 recovery and FY28 as the stronger year, but cautious on near-term growth given the Saudi/Middle East hit and Tech seasonality; analysts pressed on ACV disclosure and FY27 growth parity, which management called an endeavour, not a commitment.

540025|2026-03.headline: Advanced Enzyme Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 2,034 million, a record quarter, with EBITDA margin steady at 31%.
540025|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue reached INR 2,034 million (+22% YoY, +18% QoQ) and FY26 revenue reached INR 7,458 million (+17%), both record levels per management. EBITDA rose 39% YoY to INR 632 million at a 31% margin, and PAT rose 69% YoY to INR 453 million (22% margin). Human Healthcare, Animal Healthcare, Bioprocessing and Specialized Manufacturing all grew on a YoY basis, with Serratiopeptidase volumes a key driver. Management flagged input cost inflation (fuel, salt, solvents, packaging, logistics) and a challenging US market, and guided to steady margins and a double-digit growth aspiration for FY27 without quantified guidance.

segments.name: Human Healthcare
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 1,281 million (+24% YoY, +33% QoQ); FY26 +15%. Contributes 63% of revenue; growth from pharma API, biocatalysis and nutrition volumes.

segments.name: Animal Healthcare
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 250 million (+19% YoY, +2% QoQ); FY26 +25%. Contributes 13% of revenue, driven by Asia.

segments.name: Bioprocessing
segments.commentary: Q4 +17% YoY but -10% QoQ; FY26 +16%. Food business +20% YoY in Q4 and +19% FY26; non-food -1% YoY and -7% QoQ, flat FY26.

segments.name: Specialized Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Q4 +17% YoY and +16% QoQ; FY26 +23%. Represents 9% of revenue.

segments.name: JC Biotech (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 172 million, EBITDA INR 15 million, PAT INR 3 million; FY26 revenue INR 728 million (vs INR 600 million), EBITDA INR 92 million, PBT INR 29 million.

segments.name: Evoxx (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 88 million, EBITDA INR 19 million, PAT INR 14 million; FY26 revenue INR 319 million (+50%), EBITDA INR 72 million, PAT INR 50 million.

segments.name: Scitech (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 179 million, EBITDA INR 38 million, PAT INR 29 million; FY26 revenue INR 668 million (+23%), EBITDA INR 104 million (+37%), PAT INR 45 million (+22%).

guidance_outlook: Management expects steady margins in FY27 and says the momentum will continue; no numeric revenue or margin guidance was given.
Aspiration of double-digit growth in FY27, with expected 'little growth' from US (not negative) and healthy growth from India across human nutraceutical, food and animal feed.
Margin impact from US cost pressures could be 1-2%, per management, but the base assumption is unchanged margins.
Price increases to offset cost inflation are planned to start from the new year (FY27), per management.
R&D spend expected to rise by about INR 50 million in absolute terms; R&D capex about INR 50 crore this year (total about INR 130 crore, per call).
Biocatalysis expected to show some growth in FY27, described as moderate; Nashik R&D centre expected operational in H2 FY27, targeting threefold capacity in first phase.
Anti-inflammatory enzyme EU novel food approval expected this year; management says it could give exclusivity for 5-10 years but no numbers given.
capex_capacity: Fermentation capacity of about 500 cubic metres; infrastructure in place to add 50% capacity immediately, with a decision on expansion at a subsidiary after September 2026.
Main-company capacity expansion decision to be taken after September; capacity increment at a subsidiary possible this year.
Nashik R&D centre to become fully operational in the latter half of FY27; management said this is among the largest research centres it knows of.
R&D capex planned at about INR 50 crore in FY27 within a total of about INR 130 crore cited on the call.
demand_pricing: Pricing for the Indian Serratiopeptidase business described as broadly constant; growth was volume-driven, with price increases planned to pass on costs from the new year.
Gross margin moderated QoQ; management attributed this to product mix (higher domestic share) and cost inflation, offset by productivity gains and operating leverage.

US business: market shifting toward registration and studies; revenue down about 11% YoY in INR in Q4 per analyst's calculation. Management says growth will be modest, with US demand under pressure from discretionary spending.
Tariffs: company absorbing about 10% of tariff cost for now and passing on gradually; no full pass-through.
Serratiopeptidase: YTD growth about 45% and QoQ about 54%, shared for the last time, per management.
Top product (anti-inflammatory enzyme) 23% of FY26 revenue; top 10 customers 23% of revenue vs 22% in FY25.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin moderate QoQ despite EBITDA margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited variable vs fixed cost mix and productivity gains on some products, with inflation partly offsetting; no quantified gross margin figure was given on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Is there price increase in Indian Serratiopeptidase or only volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is more or less constant and growth is volume-driven; cost pass-through is planned from the new year.

qa_highlights.question: What is happening with US revenue, and should strategy change?
qa_highlights.answer: Market is shifting to registration and studies; strategy is changing accordingly. Management expects US growth in FY27, though 'very challenging'.

qa_highlights.question: Biocatalysis revenue for Q4 and FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave FY26 biocatalysis revenue of INR 247 million vs INR 174 million in FY25; no Q4 figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation and buyback given INR 700 crore cash and no interim dividend?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said the board will evaluate options, including buyback, and decide at the right time; no decision announced.

qa_highlights.question: Why has operating leverage not lifted gross margin from the 75% level seen post-COVID?
qa_highlights.answer: Management chose customer traction over margin for now, and expects margins to stay around current levels.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (fuel, salt, solvents, packaging, logistics) with limited ability to pass through quickly; management says near-term margin pressure is likely.
US business softness: discretionary spending pressure, tariffs, and a shift in market structure; Q4 US revenue down about 11% YoY in INR per analyst.
Senior management change: Deepak Roda left; his Indian and US responsibilities split between two heads.
Competition in Serratiopeptidase and the decision to stop disclosing product-level growth may limit visibility.
Biocatalysis trials face regulatory and competitive challenges; timing of revenue uncertain.
Patent count reduced from 17 to 15 in investor presentation as non-revenue patents were dropped.
Probiotics revenue reported lower YoY because sales are now bundled into formulations; the company does not separate them.
540025|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the FY26 numbers and long-term positioning, but cautious and somewhat evasive on US outlook, cost pass-through and product-level detail. Management repeatedly described FY27 as 'very challenging' while guiding to steady margins.
key_quotes: This is going to be a very challenging year no matter what, okay.
Quality of revenue is extremely well and very stable.
So, we expect little growth coming from the U.S., and not like the negative growth.
In terms of pricing, the pricing is more or less constant. It's more driven by the volume.

financial_highlights.change: +69% YoY; QoQ figures stated inconsistently (INR 432m or 532m in call)

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides steady margins (~31% EBITDA in Q4 FY26) with 1-2% US cost-pressure risk, and price increases to offset inflation only start in FY27, so expansion is conditional rather than guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 (subsidiary fermentation increment); Nashik R&D cent
rows.why: Subsidiary fermentation can add a 50% capacity increment with infrastructure already in place, with the decision after September 2026; Nashik R&D centre (threefold research capacity in phase 1) expected operational in H2 FY27, but the main-company capacity call is deferred past September.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Growth is volume-driven: Serratiopeptidase YTD about +45%, Q4 Human Healthcare +24% YoY, FY26 revenue +17%, and management aspires to double-digit FY27 growth, though US is only expected to grow 'little'.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not quantified and main-company expansion decision is explicitly deferred to after September; R&D capex of about INR 50 crore in FY27 (INR 130 crore total) is already planned, so a main-company capex announcement is conditional.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric guidance was given; management frames FY27 as 'very challenging' with steady margins and only a double-digit aspiration, and US revenue fell about 11% YoY in INR in Q4 per analyst calculation.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Input cost inflation (fuel, salt, solvents, packaging, logistics) is absorbed at about 10% of tariff cost with pass-through only from FY27, and US margin impact could be 1-2%, so margin pressure is possible before price increases land.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Anti-inflammatory enzyme EU novel food approval is expected this year (top product was 23% of FY26 revenue), which could give 5-10 years of exclusivity, but no numbers were given and approval timing is uncertain.

rows.label: Price increases to pass on cost inflation from FY27
rows.why: Management plans price increases from the new year to offset inflation, but Indian Serratiopeptidase pricing is broadly constant today and tariffs are only about 10% absorbed-and-passed gradually.

rows.label: Biocatalysis moderate growth in FY27
rows.why: FY26 biocatalysis revenue was INR 247 million vs INR 174 million in FY25 (+42%), with management guiding only 'moderate' FY27 growth and facing regulatory and competitive challenges.

rows.label: Buyback or capital return from INR 700 crore cash
rows.why: Chairman said the board will evaluate options including buyback against INR 700 crore cash and no interim dividend, but no decision has been announced.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY26 record and long-term positioning but cautious on the US outlook, cost pass-through and product-level detail, and called FY27 'very challenging'; analysts pushed on gross margin moderation, US strategy, pricing vs volume and capital allocation.

540025|2026-06.headline: Advanced Enzyme Q1 FY27 revenue rose 2% YoY to INR 1,898 million, but EBITDA fell 10% to INR 510 million as margin dropped to 27%.
540025|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR 1,898 million grew 2% YoY but fell 7% QoQ, held back by an extra INR 100 million sales reversal for export shipments still in transit. EBITDA declined 10% YoY and 19% QoQ to INR 510 million, with margin at 27% versus 30% a year ago, attributed to lower realisation, higher power and fuel costs, and a sales-mix shift. PAT was INR 386 million, down 5% YoY. Management guided to a return to about 30-32% EBITDA margin, double-digit growth for the rest of the year, and announced a INR 697 million buyback and full acquisition of JC Biotech.

segments.name: Human Healthcare
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,139 million, down 7% YoY and 11% QoQ on lower Pharma API sales; 60% of revenue. India sales INR 580 million (vs INR 659 million YoY, INR 699 million QoQ); international INR 559 million (vs INR 552 million YoY, INR 582 million QoQ). B2C USD 1.14 million vs USD 1.12 million a year ago.

segments.name: Animal Healthcare
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 252 million, down 3% YoY and up 1% QoQ; 13% of revenue.

segments.name: Bioprocessing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 306 million, up 30% YoY and down 5% QoQ, driven by Food business; 16% of revenue.

segments.name: Specialized Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 200 million, up 41% YoY and 11% QoQ; 11% of revenue.

segments.name: Biocatalysis (within reporting)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 45 million vs INR 44 million in Q4 FY26; management expects stronger growth in H2 FY27.

segments.name: JC Biotech (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 195 million (vs INR 211 million YoY), EBITDA INR 26 million (vs INR 33 million), PAT INR 10 million (vs INR 14 million).

segments.name: evoxx (subsidiary, Europe)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 74 million (vs INR 70 million YoY), EBITDA negative INR 13 million, PAT negative INR 18 million (vs EBITDA INR 14 million and PAT INR 7 million a year ago).

segments.name: SciTech (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 201 million (vs INR 145 million YoY), EBITDA INR 31 million, PAT INR 13 million (vs negative PAT INR 8 million a year ago).

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 86 million in Q1 FY26 (4.62% of revenue)

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 120-130 crore capex to be spent in FY27 and what is the growth component?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed INR 123 crore for FY27, about INR 20 crore may slip to Q2; about INR 20 crore maintenance, INR 50 crore R&D facility, balance growth. Fermentation utilisation is around 70-75%, with a capacity decision next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is US growth lagging the market, and what is the reason for the about 14% decline in international Human Nutrition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a weak US environment, the shift to branding most ingredients (which takes time), geopolitical issues, tariffs and hiring challenges; expects US growth of 8-10% at most at this juncture.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 growth reach 12%+ given the sales reversal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, it expects double-digit growth in the balance three quarters; the INR 10 crore incremental reversal (about 8% drag) is expected to come back in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Will the sales reversal normalise, and what caused it?
qa_highlights.answer: Export shipments were booked but still in transit at quarter end, so revenue was not recognised; the incremental reversal was INR 100 million over normal quarterly reversals and has already been recorded as of the call date.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30% EBITDA margin achievable, and will energy costs ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to return to about 30% and cited 30-32% as the target, with energy costs easing from Q2 through operational efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of novel food approval and the EFSA process?
qa_highlights.answer: Still under EFSA consideration; management said it could take three to six months, depending on authorities, and the process is on and off.

qa_highlights.question: Which new products and markets are driving future growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not track product-level sales; 15-20 molecules are in the pipeline, with expansion into biocatalysis, animal feed, ruminant, food, baking and detergent; bioenergy has no revenue yet and is deferred to after the new R&D facility next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital position at June 30, 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory about INR 190 crore, receivables about INR 131 crore, payables about INR 41 crore, net working capital about INR 280 crore; working capital cycle about 125-138 days.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA margin to return to about 30% for the full year, with 30-32% EBITDA margin cited as the target range for the rest of FY27.
Double-digit revenue growth expected for the balance three quarters of FY27; management says the Q1 INR 100 million incremental sales reversal (about 8% growth drag) should reverse in Q2.
Margin recovery expected from lower power and fuel costs and operational efficiency from Q2 onward.
US business guided to about 8-10% growth at current juncture; management said about 8% by year-end, and US is not expected to exceed 8-10% near term.
Biocatalysis expected to deliver good growth in H2 FY27.
Management said it expects progressive momentum as the year advances and asked shareholders to assess the business on an annual horizon.
capex_capacity: Management confirmed INR 123 crore capex plan (as discussed at AGM) to be spent in FY27; about INR 20 crore may slip into Q2 FY27, mainly at a subsidiary.

Of the INR 123 crore: about INR 20 crore normal/maintenance capex, about INR 50 crore for R&D facility already under work in progress (expected functional in the next quarter or so), balance growth capex; not segment-specific.
Fermentation capacity utilisation is about 70-75% (vs the 55-60% the company historically cited); management will decide in the next quarter on starting capacity-expansion capex.
New R&D facility expected next year; JC Biotech facility is capacity-constrained for solvent handling and capacity is being increased.
demand_pricing: Revenue INR 1,898 million; Human Healthcare down 7% YoY on lower Pharma API sales; India sales INR 580 million (vs INR 699 million in Q4, INR 659 million a year ago); international INR 559 million (vs INR 582 million in Q4, INR 552 million a year ago).
International Human Nutrition declined about 14% in the quarter; management attributed this to US business shift toward branding of ingredients, geopolitical issues, tariffs and hiring challenges.
Pricing: management said realisation is better than Q4 and Q1 FY26 because some prices were increased; declined to quantify competitive pricing pressure on the largest product.
Top 10 customers about 23% of revenue (27% a year ago); top 10 products about 45% (49% in Q4 FY26). Management said 70-80% of customers are constant and 20-30% of business changes each period.
Specialized Manufacturing up 41% YoY; Bioprocessing up 30% YoY on Food business; Animal Healthcare down 3% YoY.
Europe (evoxx) revenue INR 74 million, growth mainly from food area per management. SciTech revenue INR 201 million vs INR 145 million a year ago.
Serratiopeptidase: management declined to disclose quarterly number; said a reported ban would have no meaningful impact (about 1%) given the FDC combination.
Protein hydrolysis products began generating sales in the quarter; sugar-management patent (Alternansucrase) granted in the US.
risks_watch: US business: growth stalled, branding transition and geopolitical/tariff headwinds; management gave no quantified new-product plan for US.
Margin: power and fuel costs elevated; FY27 30% EBITDA target depends on cost normalisation from Q2.
Revenue timing: INR 100 million extra export reversal shows dependence on shipment timing; Q2 must show reversal and double-digit growth.
Product concentration: serratiopeptidase dependence is high; regulatory/ban news flagged, though management says impact is about 1%.
Pricing and competition on the largest product: management declined to quantify realisation changes.
Capacity: utilisation at 70-75% triggers a capex decision next quarter; watch for capex commitments beyond INR 123 crore.
Governance/disclosure: management declined to disclose serratiopeptidase numbers, Starya Labs is not yet operational, and inventory and several questions were deferred.
key_quotes: Our fundamentals remain strong, execution continues to be solid, and we are well positioned to capitalize on growth opportunities.
We remain confident in delivering sustainable revenue growth consistent with our annual guidance.
As of now, we think we should be able to grow in double digits.
Yes. We expect that it shall come back to the normal level of about 30% of EBITDA.
540025|2026-06.management_tone: Cautious and defensive: management described Q1 as soft and muted, blamed geopolitics, energy costs and US business changes, and repeatedly deflected QoQ and product-level questions while keeping FY27 guidance of double-digit growth and about 30% margin.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: from Q2 FY27 (H2 FY27 for full-year ~30%)
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to 27% from 30% a year ago and 31% in Q4 FY26; management guides 30-32% from Q2 on lower power and fuel costs and efficiency, but the FY27 target relies on energy cost normalisation.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: R&D facility functional next quarter or so; new R&D facility
rows.why: Fermentation utilisation is 70-75% (vs 55-60% historically cited) and management will decide on starting capacity capex next quarter, while INR 50 crore R&D facility is already under work in progress; no new plant dated.

rows.when: Q2 FY27 onward; double-digit growth for the balance three qu
rows.why: Q1 revenue was INR 1,898 million, up 2% YoY, held back by a INR 100 million export reversal (about 8% growth drag) that management expects to come back in Q2; US guided only 8-10%, so the double-digit call leans on the reversal.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Fermentation utilisation of 70-75% is approaching the 80% threshold, and management says it will decide on capacity-expansion capex next quarter; the INR 123 crore FY27 plan is already set, so a new announcement depends on that decision.

rows.why: Management held FY27 guidance of double-digit growth and 30-32% margin, but Q1 EBITDA fell 10% YoY and US growth is capped at 8-10%, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.why: Management said EFSA review could take three to six months and the process is on and off, with no date committed.

rows.label: Biocatalysis growth in H2 FY27
rows.why: Biocatalysis revenue was INR 45 million in Q1 (vs INR 44 million in Q4 FY26), and management expects good growth in H2 FY27, though the number is small.

540047|2026-03.headline: Dilip Buildcon FY26 consolidated PAT rose to INR1,398 crores on revenue down 20.6% to INR8,984 crores; FY26 order inflow INR18,548 crores.
540047|2026-03.overview: FY26 standalone revenue fell about 22% to INR7,005 crores, while standalone EBITDA dropped about 19% to INR734 crores and standalone PAT rose to INR841 crores from INR311 crores. Consolidated EBITDA was INR1,766 crores at a 19.6% margin. Management reframed the company into three verticals (EPC, MDO coal mining, and Assets/InvIT) and targets 75% of profit from long-term assets by FY29. Management guided FY27 standalone revenue growth of 30-40%, EBITDA margin of 11-12%, and INR10,000-12,000 crores of new orders, with net debt-free status targeted by FY28.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Builds assets for the group; FY26 order inflow INR18,548 crores and completions INR2,812 crores. Management targets INR10,000-12,000 crores of new orders in FY27 and 30-40% revenue growth.

segments.name: MDO (coal mining)
segments.commentary: FY26 coal production 28.72 million tonnes (Siarmal 22.35 Mt, Pachhwara 6.37 Mt). Revenue from mining about INR1,600 crores currently, guided to about INR2,500 crores in FY27, about INR3,100 crores in FY28 and about INR4,000 crores in FY29. Target 57 Mt by FY29.

segments.name: Assets / InvIT
segments.commentary: Holds about INR1,600 crores of InvIT units. Next tranche of 11 HAM assets expected to yield about INR1,800 crores of InvIT units for incremental investment of INR169 crores, with transfers through Q1 FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue growth of 30-40% over FY26, supported by an order book of almost INR28,000 crores.
FY27 standalone EBITDA margin target of 11-12%.
Targeting INR10,000-12,000 crores of new order inflow in FY27.
Standalone debt reduction of INR600-800 crores in FY27; interest outgo expected at INR375-400 crores; net debt-free by FY28.
Coal production target of about 57 Mt by FY29; Siarmal about 33-35 Mt in FY27 and 50 Mt by FY29.
Management expects about 75% of profit from long-term assets and 25% from EPC by FY29.

Transmission and solar projects: equity requirement about INR1,600 crores (solar about INR1,200 crores, transmission about INR400 crores); DBL targets 15% of equity with 85% from outside investors; transmission EBITDA margin above 24% and IRR in high teens; commissioning about 2 years from start.
capex_capacity: Siarmal coal handling plant capex pending; a revenue-share kicker applies once it reaches COD.
Pottangi mine to be set up over the next 3 years.
Next InvIT tranche: 11 HAM assets, transfers 4 assets in Q1 FY27 and the balance in Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.
Under-construction projects of about INR1,000 crores plus invested, to be transferred to InvIT.
Gross block about INR3,600 crores and net block about INR800 crores, stated to be debt free.
demand_pricing: Average monthly infrastructure tendering in FY26 was about INR1.4 trillion, below the government's FY26 target, due to state elections, regulatory scrutiny and administrative delays.

Bitumen and HSD (diesel) cost inflation from elevated crude prices; government contracts only partly pass this through via WPI/CPI-linked formulas, so some margin impact is expected, mainly in coal where HSD is a major cost.
Coal MDO pricing is contracted per tonne: about INR500 per tonne at Siarmal and about INR1,100 per tonne at Pachhwara.
Q4 mining margin fell temporarily because about 6 Mt of coal is stuck at Siarmal due to delayed government evacuation and rake unavailability.
Management stated 90% of the last 20 years' revenue came from national government and other states, and only 10% from the Madhya Pradesh state government.

qa_highlights.question: Will MDO revenue and profitability be shared quarterly, and what is the profitability outlook after the coal handling plant capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, MDO revenue and profitability will be shared quarterly. Revenue is projected at about INR2,500 crores in FY27 and INR4,000 crores by FY29, with similar margins to be assumed; no monetisation plan for the subsidiaries is announced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected InvIT distribution after the transfers, given lower distributions from Alpha?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said transfer timing changed in FY26 and distributions are envisaged in slide 24; FY26 Shrem and Alpha dividend and interest income was INR64.5 crores, with total distributions close to INR100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What are the equity structure, IRR and commissioning timeline for the transmission and solar projects?

540047|2026-06.headline: DBL Q1 FY27 standalone revenue Rs 1,930 crore and EBITDA margin 10.32%; consolidated PAT fell to Rs 128 crore from Rs 271 crore.

Consolidated revenue dipped to Rs 2,378 crore from Rs 2,620 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of Rs 429 crore (18.05% margin). Management reiterated FY27 guidance (revenue growth 30-40%, EBITDA margin 10-12%, debt reduction Rs 600-800 crore) and announced a stake sale in under-construction transmission and solar projects (about Rs 8,400 crore project cost) to Alpha Alternatives.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 11-12% remain unchanged, and will revenue growth be back-ended?

qa_highlights.question: How much bid value is pending opening, and what is the working capital outlook?

Siarmal coal fee is 78% until the CHP is ready, rising to 100%, with a major revenue jump expected in FY29. Full-year math given as about Rs 600/t for Siarmal and Rs 1,200/t for Pachhwara.

Siarmal equity will be funded from internal accruals, and the bank has permitted use of accruals within the project.

The focus is on standalone net-debt-positive by FY28, while consolidated debt will cycle as assets are built and transferred to InvIT. Rs 7,801 crore consol net debt is referenced; the company cites Rs 45,000 crore of road HAM projects done.

540048|2026-03.headline: S.P. Apparels Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell to INR 364 crore (from INR 399 crore) and EBITDA margin to 12.2%; management guides INR 2,000 crore FY27 revenue.
540048|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was soft on volumes: consolidated revenue declined year-on-year to INR 364 crore and EBITDA to INR 44 crore, with PAT down to INR 18.59 crore, as US tariff after-effects and shipping disruption delayed orders. Full-year consolidated revenue grew 13.2% to INR 1,578 crore and EBITDA rose 16% to INR 217 crore. Management says US orders are returning, guides to INR 2,000 crore consolidated revenue in FY27, and points to Sri Lanka ramp-up and EU/UK FTA benefits. Current utilisation is cited at 64%, and the timing of recovery in H2 FY27 is the key uncertainty.

segments.name: Young Brand Apparel
segments.commentary: FY26 adjusted revenue INR 321.26 crore and adjusted EBITDA INR 49.23 crore; Q4 adjusted revenue INR 66.88 crore (vs INR 81.37 crore) and adjusted EBITDA INR 8.47 crore (vs INR 12.85 crore). Business is 100% US-customer based and was hit by tariffs.

segments.name: SPUK (UK)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue GBP 7.5 million (INR 87.04 crore) with positive EBITDA of INR 1.10 crore. Q4 revenue was INR 35.04 crore vs INR 18.34 crore a year earlier. Order book is GBP 6.1 million.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 71.54 crore (vs INR 79.41 crore); EBITDA loss narrowed to INR 6.1 crore from INR 6.84 crore. Management says Retail was EBITDA-positive from Q2 to Q4 FY26, and that finance cost, not depreciation, keeps it PAT-negative.

FY27 revenue split given as INR 1,800 crore Garmenting (incl. Young Brand and Sri Lanka), INR 150 crore SPUK, INR 80-90 crore Retail.

Adding 300 machines costs about INR 200-250 crore; management said capacity is not the constraint, people are.

qa_highlights.question: Is rupee depreciation driving incremental volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said duty-paid status versus duty-free Bangladesh and Sri Lanka helps competitiveness and is bringing more business. The CFO added that 80% of orders are covered when booked, so there is no direct benefit from depreciation.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR 2,000 crore FY27 target be reached, given Sri Lanka and Sivakasi ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Sri Lanka FOB is about INR 45 crore in FY26, targeting INR 200-250 crore in FY27. Sivakasi adds about INR 40-50 crore, and H2 FY27 is expected to see the recovery as utilisation rises from 64%. Analyst arithmetic came to about INR 1,850 crore, and the gap was not fully bridged.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15% margin guidance on consolidated or Garmenting basis?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the 14-15% margin applies to consolidated figures in one answer, and later said the 15% applies to the Garmenting division only, with INR 2,000 crore on a consolidated basis. The basis is therefore ambiguous.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SPUK revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: SPUK has an order book of GBP 6 million and is targeting a further GBP 6-8 million for FY27, for GBP 12-14 million in total. Two anchor customers are each expected to give about GBP 8 million, and 2-3 more customers are being added.

qa_highlights.question: Will Retail become PAT positive?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said Retail is at EBITDA breakeven, and that finance cost on Retail Ventures is the drag. He said equity raising is needed and the company is ready to raise it now.

qa_highlights.question: Has labour returned after the capacity cut?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said workers left after the US capacity reduction, and that 30-40% have returned. Recruitment and training are ongoing, and management said this is not a labour disruption.

540078|2026-06.headline: Mitsu Chem Plast Q1 FY27 net profit rose 566% YoY to INR 873.83 lakhs on a 16.29% EBITDA margin, with total income up 11.62%.
540078|2026-06.overview: Total income reached INR 9,532.78 lakhs (+11.62% YoY) and EBITDA INR 1,549.48 lakhs (+209.50% YoY), with margin expanding to 16.29% from 5.87%. Net profit of INR 873.83 lakhs was up sequentially from INR 771.73 lakhs in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the gain to operating efficiency and product mix, and announced a proposed 3,550 MTPA capacity addition on top of 32,450 MTPA. Management said it now prioritises bottom line over top line, and that the INR 1,000 crore revenue target by FY28 remains in place.

segments.commentary: Accounts for about 19.8% of the business per management, including furniture parts and other parts. Management expects faster growth here than in containers, but gave no target mix.

Management expects utilisation to stay around 64-65%, or about 70% as a healthier level.

Proposed addition of 3,550 MTPA, to be used across all three verticals (containers, furniture parts and others).

Lead time from machinery order to commercial operation is about 6-9 months, per management.
Utilisation was 60-64% through FY26; seasonal peaks reach about 85%.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is strong across all verticals, with containers in particular high demand.

Raw material prices rising on geopolitical and crude-linked pressures; management says suppliers have raised prices and customers have accepted pass-through, with local sourcing used since imports were stopped years ago.
Raw material pass-through to customers is generally on a one-month lag; specialised cases are negotiated individually.
Pricing is a cost-plus markup on raw material; management said other value-add and efficiency gains drive the margin, not the pass-through alone.

Company is rationalising SKUs (around 500) by dropping low-margin products; added more than 30 customers in Q1 and more than 150 in the last year (the two figures were stated inconsistently on the call; the 150 figure is probably cumulative for the year).

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion to about 16%, and is it sustainable given raw material pressure?

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex for the 3,500 MTPA expansion and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said approximately INR 2 crore, funded by a mix of internal accruals and debt, and that the capacity is already online.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects roughly the same sequential growth each quarter, while focusing more on profit than revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Does a 16% EBITDA margin represent a new normal, and how does the pass-through work?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10-12% is the normal range and double-digit margins will remain, with pass-through about one month in arrears.

qa_highlights.question: Why add capacity when utilisation is only 64%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said machinery lead time plus 6-9 months of set-up requires planning ahead; utilisation is seasonal, reaching about 85% at peak.

qa_highlights.question: Which businesses will drive the INR 1,000 crore target, and what is the IBC project?

540115|2026-03.headline: LTTS Q4 FY26 revenue rose 0.3% YoY to $305.9 Mn and EBIT margin reached 15.2%, with mid-16% margin targeted by Q4 FY27 or earlier.
540115|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 continuing-operations revenue was $305.9 Mn, up 0.3% YoY and down 1.7% QoQ, as the company exited low-margin work and divested SWC (Smart World). EBIT margin rose 40 bps QoQ to 15.2%, the second straight quarter of expansion, with gross margin up 150 bps QoQ. Management said the restructuring is complete, with about $19 Mn annualised revenue exited in Q4 and no further restructuring costs expected. It advanced the margin aspiration to mid-16% by Q4 FY27 or earlier and set a 5-year Lakshya 31 plan of 13%-15% USD CAGR and 16%-17% EBIT margin, with no annual guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 16%-17% margin a five-year target or achievable sooner?

qa_highlights.question: When will the 13%-15% CAGR show up, and when do $100 Mn+ and several-hundred-million accounts emerge?
qa_highlights.answer: No annual guidance. A $50 Mn+ trailing-12-month account was delivered in Q4, the first in a long time. Build-out to $100 Mn accounts is mostly organic and will take time; Alind Saxena now focuses on large deals and growth markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 13%-15% CAGR in USD and does the 12.4% historical figure include SWC?
qa_highlights.answer: The 13%-15% is USD-based, and the 12.4% five-year CAGR includes SWC. Reported-currency targets may be added over time.

qa_highlights.question: How big are the six bets and what investment is planned?

qa_highlights.question: Will there be more restructuring, and what is the reason for the $19 Mn exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Gupta said the Q4 exceptional charge covers the $19 Mn annualised exit in Europe, Israel and the UK, with no further restructuring costs expected.

540115|2026-06.headline: LTTS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 1.5% QoQ in constant currency to $309.9 Mn, with EBIT margin up 50 bps QoQ to 15.7%.
540115|2026-06.overview: LTTS grew revenue 1.5% QoQ and 1.9% YoY in constant currency, to $309.9 Mn (Rs 2,940 crore, +2.9% QoQ, +11.5% YoY in rupee terms). EBIT margin expanded to 15.7%, up 50 bps QoQ and 200 bps YoY, and free cash flow was 153% of net income. Sustainability grew 4.3% QoQ and 11.3% YoY, while Tech declined on a medical program stop and large deals slipping into early Q2. Management reiterated sequential growth in revenue and margins for each quarter and a mid-16% EBIT margin on or before Q4 FY27, but declined to give annual guidance.

540115|2026-09.headline: LTTS Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.7% QoQ in constant currency to $317.1M, with EBIT margin at 16.3%, ahead of its mid-16% aspiration.
540115|2026-09.overview: Revenue reached $317.1M (up 2.7% QoQ and 4.8% YoY in constant currency, continuing operations), and INR 3,040 crore (up 3.4% QoQ, 12.1% YoY). EBIT margin widened 60 bps QoQ to 16.3%, and management said the mid-16% aspiration was reached a couple of quarters early. Large deal TCV was $203M with over 50% AI-led, and management said the USD100M shortfall from last quarter's target would be recovered over Q3 and Q4. Reported net income of INR 548 crore included a one-time INR 165 crore gain from the SWC divestment, which is now complete.

financial_highlights.change: +53.7% QoQ; +66.8% YoY; includes INR 165 crore one-time SWC gain
vs 77 days in Q1; guided range 80 to 85 days
vs INR 3,394 crore at end Q1

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Revenue up 2.3% QoQ, with growth from Auto North America, Aero and Rail, and Trucks and Off-highway. Auto Europe remained muted; management expects it to recover next year. Auto is about 50% of Mobility revenue. Margin 16.9%.

segments.name: Sustainability
segments.commentary: Up 13.4% YoY and 4.9% QoQ; now about 30% of revenue per the CFO (38% per the later AI-revenue answer, which conflicts). Nearly half of Q2 large deal wins were here. Margin 29.5%. Management says it is on track for another double-digit growth year.

segments.name: Tech
segments.commentary: Described as stable. Tech Infra and Semcon were strong, Media steady. A global telecom equipment AI program began ramping this quarter. Margin 12%, up 50 bps QoQ. Management expects Tech to be muted in Q3, with Medtech recovery in Q4.

segments.name: Engineering Intelligence (EI)
segments.commentary: Annualized EI-led revenue of $120M in Q2, which management said is about 9.5% of revenue. Headcount was 24,035 and more than 16,000 engineers were upskilled in AI. Over 50% of Q2 large deal wins were AI-led.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 revenue expected to be better than H1, both QoQ and YoY, per management.
Near-term EBIT margin expected around mid-16% levels; aspiration to maintain it.
Long-term aspiration: 13% to 15% revenue CAGR with 16% to 17% EBIT margin over 3 to 5 years.
Wage hike effective Q3, expected impact of 50 to 80 bps on margin; margin guidance stated as inclusive of this.
Effective tax rate guided at 26% to 26.5%.
Management expects to recover the roughly USD100M shortfall from the prior quarter in Q3 and Q4 to keep a USD200M-per-quarter deal pace.
Tech expected muted in Q3; Medtech growth expected from Q3 or Q4; Systems and Platforms growth to accelerate from Q4.
capex_capacity: Set up a dedicated Data Center Engineering business line covering AI infrastructure, servers, storage, ODMs and OEMs.
Launched a new EI lab with NVIDIA for physical AI applications across manufacturing, robotics and supply chain.
Investment in Munich and an EI center to target European auto work.
Headcount rose marginally from 23,845 in Q1 to 24,035 in Q2.
demand_pricing: Large deal TCV of $203M across segments in Q2, with over 50% AI-led. Order backlog and pipeline both up YoY; pipeline up more than 25% YoY.
Offshore mix 55.9%; fixed-price mix 35.6%, rising toward higher-value and outcome-based engagements.
Average deal tenures have lengthened slightly. Management cited roughly 5 to 7 years for a $100M deal, 4 to 5 years for $50M, about 3 years for $25M.
Management says it charges a premium for AI-led work but declined to quantify AI-led margins by service line.
Rupee realized at 95.9 per dollar in Q2, depreciating 1.09% QoQ.
Attrition range-bound at 14.7%.
Europe auto remains weak; management said there is little Middle East exposure in oil and gas.

qa_highlights.question: How has Sustainability volatility come down, and how much revenue is long-term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management split Sustainability into four areas (Oil and Gas/Chemicals, FMCG, Energy Automation, Industrial Machinery and Building Tech), built digital twin and AI solutions, and said large deals from last year are now converting to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Middle East situation affecting oil and gas or overall business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East business is very small and it is not seeing significant impact; work is focused on the US and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Will European auto recover next year, and is it an industry-wide turnaround?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Europe auto to stabilize in the next 6 to 9 months and grow again in 9 to 12 months, as European OEMs rebase and India-based providers replace local vendors. Auto Europe is about 50% of the auto portion of Mobility, and the company does not quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DSO of 78 days comfortable, or is there room to improve it?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company is comfortable at 78 days, well below the 80 to 85 day guided range, and expects to operate around this level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the SWC divestment affect the reported numbers, and what is the run rate from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the INR 165 crore was a one-time gain. From Q3 only continuing operations will be reported, with the SWC operating line of about $36M excluded.

qa_highlights.question: Why are clients converting deals to revenue now, and what changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to AI capex across chips, software, industrials, telecom and infrastructure, clients focusing on growth rather than cost cuts, and LTTS being 9 to 12 months ahead of peers on AI, which it says is gaining share.

qa_highlights.question: What are sustainable margins, and what is the Q4 exit margin?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said near-term margins should be taken at around mid-16% EBIT, with levers from mix, AI and productivity, net of the wage hike. Management did not give a Q4 exit margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wage hike impact, and what does H2 growth mean?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the wage hike in Q3 would have a 50 to 80 bps margin impact. Management said H2 will be better than H1 both QoQ and YoY, without a quarterly number.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the $120M annualized EI revenue was recognized in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the $120M is annualized, so about $30M per quarter. Most AI deal wins have not yet gone into operation, and the company will report AI-led revenue quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI-led revenue defined, and what is its profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: AI revenue counts deliverables where a significant part is created using the AI stack. Management declined to quantify AI-led profitability, but said AI is a margin lever.

risks_watch: Auto Europe remains muted and may need write-offs before recovery; management's recovery timing is 6 to 12 months.
Tech is expected to be muted in Q3 and Medtech recovery is pushed to Q3 or Q4 after a major program ramp-down.
Wage hike of 50 to 80 bps in Q3 may pressure margins if growth lags.
H2 growth acceleration depends on converting the USD100M-plus deal backlog; most AI deal wins are not yet operational.
Middle East escalation could affect oil and gas demand if it persists, per management's own caveat.
540115|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on margins and deal momentum, with specific H2 commitments, but cautious on Auto Europe and Tech. Management declined to quantify AI-led margins and quarterly guidance, and hedged the Medtech recovery timing.
key_quotes: EBIT margins improved 60 bps quarter -on-quarter to 16.3%, delivering ahead of timeline on our aspiration for mid-16% EBIT levels.
I'm confirming to you that H2 will be better year-on-year and quarter-to-quarter than H1, sequentially as well as year-on-year, right?
Near term, you should take it to be at these levels, around mid-16% EBIT levels.
We will make sure that we get you the extra USD100 million in Q3 and Q4 because we want to keep to that 200 million pace.

rows.why: Utilisation is not disclosed and no capex quantum was given; the Munich EI center and Data Center Engineering line are planned, but no spend was quantified.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.why: Q2 large-deal TCV was $203M and management plans to recover the roughly $100M shortfall in Q3 and Q4 to keep a $200M-per-quarter pace, though most AI deal wins are not yet operational.

540133|2026-03.headline: ICICI Pru Life FY26 VNB rose 10.9% to ₹26.29bn with margin up 190bp to 24.7%, but APE grew only 2.2% and RoEV fell to 11.9%.
540133|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed absolute VNB growth of 10.9% to ₹26.29bn and VNB margin expansion to 24.7% (from 22.8%), while APE grew just 2.2% to ₹106.41bn. Retail protection was the standout, up 32.3% for the year and 60.5% in Q4, offsetting weak agency, direct, linked and annuity lines. Profit after tax rose 34.6% to ₹16bn, helped by a ₹1.14bn gain on sale of ICICI Pension Fund Management Company; excluding it, PAT grew 25%. EV operating assumption changes (GST input-tax-credit loss, persistency) and a ₹2.64bn persistency variance (mainly the 100% premium back annuity) pulled RoEV down to 11.9%. Management said West Asia disruption hurt March new business across all lines except protection, and it deferred Ind-AS adoption by a year via forbearance.

segments.name: Retail protection
segments.commentary: Grew 32.3% YoY in FY26 and 60.5% in Q4; 13% of addressable population covered. Protection mix rose 2.2pp to 17.9% of VNB mix.

segments.name: Group protection
segments.commentary: Up 7.1% YoY; group term +14.6%, credit life +1.8%. Group business overall +14.5%, 18.3% of APE.

segments.name: Linked (ULIP)
segments.commentary: APE up 1.6% YoY; two-year CAGR 14.2%. Focus on high sum assured ULIP to cushion market volatility.

segments.name: Non-linked savings
segments.commentary: APE grew 15.4% YoY for nine months but declined YoY in Q4 as a prior-year Q4 launch normalised; full year roughly flat. Par:non-par roughly 2:1.

segments.name: Annuity
segments.commentary: Four-year CAGR about 20%; stabilised at about 7% of retail mix. Heavy single-pay skew and 100% premium back product drove persistency issues.

segments.name: Group Funds
segments.commentary: Grew 26% YoY.

segments.name: Agency channel
segments.commentary: APE ₹26.86bn; with direct, 47.4% of retail APE. Growth weak on high annuity base, but improving sequentially through the year.

segments.name: Direct channel
segments.commentary: APE ₹14.30bn; growth lagged on base effects. Focus on NRI via GIFT City and online channel.

segments.name: Bancassurance
segments.commentary: Grew 3.6% YoY; 29.8% of APE. 53 bank partnerships with access to 26,400+ branches.

segments.name: Partnership distribution
segments.commentary: Grew 23.4% YoY; 13.2% of APE. Over 1,500 non-bank partnerships.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 growth number given; management called the environment volatile and said it is too early to commit.
Long-term RoEV expected at 13-14%, depending on yield curve and VNB growth; RoEV to become less significant once Ind-AS is adopted.
Management said VNB margin of 24.7% (with persistency and mortality/expense assumptions now set) is the baseline going forward.
Ind-AS go-live deferred by a year via forbearance; current-year results remain on existing I-GAAP with Ind-AS as alternate financials.
Would reprice non-par products if the yield curve moves down; no en masse repricing so far, only cohort-level changes (1-3% at some peers).
capex_capacity: Distribution: 2.42 lakh+ advisers, 53 bank partnerships, 1,500+ non-bank partnerships.
Agency strategy centres on micro-market-led branch expansion and technology/analytics productivity tools.
No capex or capacity figures were disclosed in the call.
demand_pricing: West Asia conflict hurt new business in March 2026 across all products except protection, per management.
Industry retail sum assured grew 2.5x in the post-GST-reform period versus pre-reform; GST removed 18% on retail protection.
Non-par sales are constrained because bank FD rates are steep relative to G-Sec-linked pricing, so customers switch products.
Management said it has not cut prices en masse; the yield curve benefit was retained rather than passed to customers.

Persistency: 61st month decline attributed to a regulatory definition change; 25th month decline seen as spillover from 13th month, largely annuity-driven. Non-linked 13th-month persistency fell from 86.8% to 73.2%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 growth strategy and non-par outlook, and what is the par/non-par mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth outlook not committed given volatility. Par:non-par mix roughly 2:1 for the year, with some quarters higher or lower.

qa_highlights.question: Is the persistency experience built into VNB margin assumptions, and what about surrender value regulation?
qa_highlights.answer: Persistency is reviewed at year-end; permanent changes go into assumptions and temporary ones run through variances. Early surrender-value product experience is not yet showing a material difference after 5-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is agency growing slowly, and how will it be revived?
qa_highlights.answer: Agency was held back by a high annuity base in the prior year. The 3-year CAGR is about 12-13%; micro-market-led agency strategy is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Did the West Asia war affect new business, and how does demand differ across products?
qa_highlights.answer: March new business was hit across the board except protection. Management declined to quantify the impact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Ind-AS transition plan and its capital impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Forbearance sought for one year, citing awaited joint expert group clarity on CSM inputs. Solvency stays on the existing basis (227%) until RBC is implemented.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 2.5pp economic variance uplift in VNB margin, and was pricing changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Yield curve gains were held in economic assumptions, while product repricing sits in new business profile. Pricing was not materially changed; cost efficiencies were used to hold prices.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the EV split between VIF and net worth reclassified?
qa_highlights.answer: Shareholder share of MTM on policyholder-fund assets and derivatives moved from net worth to VIF to align with market practice. Total EV is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2.64bn persistency variance related to FY26 VNB?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost none of it relates to FY26 business; it is entirely back-book.

qa_highlights.question: Any update on commission regulation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not aware of discussions beyond data requests from the regulator; distributor remuneration talks are continuous.

risks_watch: APE growth of 2.2% against market growth of 10-11% (two-year CAGR ~7-8% vs market 10-11%); share loss risk.
Persistency weakness in annuity, 13th/25th/61st month cohorts; surrender-value regulation effects are still unknown.
GST input-tax-credit loss and pricing lag; operating assumption change of -0.5% of opening EV.
Geopolitical volatility weighing on March and April sales; FY27 growth guidance withheld.
Possible regulatory commission cuts; management gave no sensitivity.
Ind-AS transition and RBC solvency regime changes; the next-year forbearance outcome is open.

Management was evasive on non-par pricing, commission regulation and the drivers of the persistency decline. It acknowledged the agency and direct channel shortfall and the below-market APE growth.

I think one of the biggest tailwinds that we have got as an industry has been the GST reform, and that is felt most in protection.

540133|2026-06.headline: ICICI Pru Life Q1 FY27: VNB up 24.9% YoY to ₹5.71 bn at 26.7% margin, driven by retail protection growth of 60.4%.
540133|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 VNB grew 24.9% YoY to ₹5.71 bn, with VNB margin at 26.7%, up 200 bps from FY26's 24.7%. PAT rose 27.8% YoY to ₹3.86 bn. Growth was led by protection: sum assured up 31.8% to ₹4.90 trn and protection APE up 45.7%, while savings APE rose only 5.8% and non-linked APE fell about 9.5% as fixed deposits attracted customers. Management repeatedly stated there is no margin target and no formal guidance, and that absolute VNB growth is the focus.

segments.name: Retail protection
segments.commentary: Grew 60.4% YoY, third straight quarter above 40% after GST exemption; share of APE 10.5% vs 7.5% a year ago. Retail sum assured up 45.9% to ₹1.13 trn.

segments.name: Group protection (credit life + group term)
segments.commentary: Grew 37.8% YoY; MFI credit life recovered after a long slowdown, non-MFI momentum continued.

segments.name: Savings
segments.commentary: Savings APE ₹15.40 bn, up 5.8% YoY; savings share of mix fell to 72.1% from 78.1%. Linked APE up 6.4%; non-linked including annuity broadly flat at ₹4.94 bn; group funds up 42.2%.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: APE up 2% YoY to ₹4.63 bn, improved from negative growth in prior quarters; channel shifting to higher sum assured and protection.

segments.name: Direct
segments.commentary: APE up 8.3% YoY to ₹2.86 bn; agency plus direct contributed 45.5% of retail APE.

segments.name: Bancassurance
segments.commentary: Grew 5.6% YoY, 27.4% of APE; management attributes this to partner-bank recalibration.

segments.name: Partnership distribution
segments.commentary: Grew 29.5% YoY, 14.6% of APE; management cites a near 20% five-year CAGR and no single partner above 5%.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Grew 38.8% YoY, 22.9% of APE.

guidance_outlook: Management gave no VNB growth or margin guidance; it said margin is not a fixation and absolute VNB growth is the goal.
Second-half retail protection growth is expected to taper from the 60%+ level, as the base steepens; management said it would be 'very unlikely' to stay above 60% in H2.
The input tax credit drag continues for one more quarter (Q2) and then enters the base from Q3.
MFI credit life is expected to add to growth in H2 on a favourable base.
Non-par is expected to pick up only when fixed-deposit alternatives become less attractive; no timeline given.
No en-masse protection repricing is planned; repricing will be targeted by cohort as business as usual.
capex_capacity: Distribution: 2.44 lakh+ advisors, 52 bank partnerships covering 26,800+ bank branches, and 1,500+ non-bank partnerships.
Agency roadmap centres on micro-market-led branches and technology/analytics; management said FY27 agent additions would be similar to FY26's roughly 70,000.
Direct channel focus on online scaling and the NRI segment via GIFT City.
AI/ML is embedded across the customer journey, covering demand generation, automated underwriting, renewals, service and claims investigation (slide 32 of the investor presentation).
demand_pricing: Retail protection is growing on the GST exemption, which took effect after the GST reforms, plus pre-approved sum assured offers and digital income validation for onboarding.
Non-par savings is subdued because fixed deposits offer high sticker rates; management said the company is not staying away and keeps repricing.
Non-linked APE fell about 9.5% YoY, per a question from BNP Paribas; management attributed this to non-par weakness.
Annuity growth of about 33% YoY was led by regular-premium deferred annuity, not single premium; the par to non-par ratio in non-linked is about 2:1.
Persistency: 13th month 84.0% vs 84.5% at March; 25th month fell from 81% to 77% due to carry-through from last year's surrenders. Collections grew about 9%.
Management denied any en-masse protection price changes; the target protection buyer is around age 35.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the VNB margin, and is the GST input tax credit drag still affecting it?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Dhiren Salian said the margin was largely product mix; the non-availability of input tax credit continues for one more quarter (Q2) before entering the base from Q3. He did not quantify the drag.

qa_highlights.question: Why is non-par not selling, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed-income alternatives, mainly fixed deposits with high sticker rates, are more attractive to customers. Non-par is not being avoided and is repriced as conditions allow, but the pickup depends on those alternatives easing.

qa_highlights.question: Will Standard Chartered remain an open-architecture partner after Prudential's change in promoter status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Standard Chartered has been a 10-year partner, that both sides value it, and that ICICI Bank is the largest single channel at about 15% of business with no other distributor above 5%.

qa_highlights.question: How does expense management look, and what is the ITC drag in rupees?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost-to-premium is up on the input tax credit loss, partly offset by productivity and AI/ML gains. It did not quantify the ITC impact and said the schedules would show the GST component. It said EOM is well within the cap, without disclosing the figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any VNB growth guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management declined to give VNB growth guidance, including the 20-25% range an analyst proposed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Prudential promoter-to-investor reclassification?
qa_highlights.answer: Prudential holds just under 22%. The board approved its request to reclassify as investor, and the company has submitted it to IRDAI, awaiting its response. Management said no sell-down is required under its reading of the rules.

risks_watch: Sharp H2 deceleration in retail protection, which management said will taper from 60%+ as the base steepens, could slow VNB growth.
Non-par savings and non-linked APE stay weak while fixed-deposit sticker rates remain high; the pickup timing is open.
Bank partner relationships, including Standard Chartered after Prudential's change in promoter status, and recalibration at partner banks (bancassurance +5.6%).
AUM outflows from surrenders and maturities (AUM ₹3.34 trn); 25th-month persistency fell to 77% from 81%.
Pending IRDAI decision on Prudential's promoter-to-investor reclassification, and the planned rename to ICICI Life Insurance Limited.
Possible NBFC insurance distribution rules from January, flagged by an analyst; management had no view.

540136|2026-03.headline: HPL Electric FY26 revenue crossed Rs 1,800 crore; C&I grew 26% to Rs 784 crore and Q4 C&I hit a record Rs 214 crore.

Consumer and Industrial (C&I) grew 26% to Rs 784 crore and rose to 43% of revenue from 37%, led by wires and cables (up 50% to Rs 340 crore). Smart metering recovered from an industry-wide execution disruption earlier in the year, with Q4 its strongest quarter, and the order book stood at over Rs 3,200 crore (over 97% metering) as of 22 May 2026. Management flagged C&I margin pressure in FY26 from mix shift and a lag in passing on commodity-linked price increases, which it expects to ease from late April and May.

540136|2026-06.headline: HPL Electric Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35% YoY to ₹515 cr, but EBITDA margin fell to 12.26% on raw-material inflation, with metering margins roughly halved.

Consumer & Industrial (C&I) hit a record ₹278 cr (+55% YoY, ~54% of revenue) and Metering & Systems grew ~17% to ₹234 cr. EBITDA margin moderated to 12.26% as metals, industrial plastics and semiconductors inflated after February 2026 due to West Asia geopolitical disruption, and depreciation from recent capacity investments weighed on PAT. Management guided that pricing and mix actions are under way, with margin recovery expected over one to three quarters if input costs ease.

rows.why: Mercedes component goes to 100% Endurance volume after a competitor with 40% share went bankrupt, and Europe Q1 order intake was €13.9 million; however Europe order momentum softer overall and management did not commit on it.

540173|2026-03.headline: PNB Housing Q4 FY26 disbursements rose 36% YoY to INR 9,355 crores; FY27 guidance is loan book above INR 1 lakh crore and ROA 2.4-2.5%.
540173|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 disbursements grew 36% YoY and 50% QoQ to INR 9,355 crores, with retail disbursements up 32% YoY to INR 9,020 crores. PAT rose 19% YoY to INR 656 crores in Q4 and 18% to INR 2,291 crores for FY26, helped by negative credit cost of 45 bps from write-off pool recoveries. Spread compressed 10 bps QoQ to 2.12% on lower incremental yields and balance transfer pressure in Prime, while reported NIM rose 6 bps to 3.69%. Management guided that yields have bottomed out, with FY27 retail loan growth of 18-20%, NIM of 3.55-3.65% and ROA of 2.4-2.5%.

financial_highlights.change: -15 bps QoQ; FY26 7.57% vs 7.86% in FY25
+13% YoY; opex to ATA 1.05% FY26, 1.08% Q4
Recoveries INR 167 crores in Q4, INR 330-332 crores in FY26

segments.name: Affordable
segments.commentary: Q4 disbursement INR 1,249 crores, up 59% QoQ but flat YoY; FY26 disbursement about INR 3,800 crores, targeted to grow about 50%. Management says GNPA in affordable is below 0.6%.

segments.name: Emerging Market
segments.commentary: Disbursement grew 34% YoY in Q4. Segment share of retail loan book rose with affordable plus emerging at 40% of retail book (37% a year earlier).

segments.name: Prime
segments.commentary: Disbursement grew 43% YoY in Q4 despite yield pressure from rate cuts. Management says Prime disbursement largely replenishes runoff; Prime loan growth is about 9%.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Restarted with INR 335 crores disbursed in Q4 FY26; corporate loan book INR 401 crores at 31 March 2026. Target yield 11.5-12%, capped at about 3% of book in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Loan book to cross INR 1 lakh crore in FY27.
Retail loan book growth of 18-20% in FY27; overall book growth stated as 18-20%.
NIM guided at 3.55-3.65% for FY27; management expects spread-NIM gap to normalise from Q1 FY27.
ROA guided at 2.4-2.5% for FY27.
Credit cost expected to stay negative at about 15-20 bps in FY27, with recoveries of INR 200-250 crores.
Opex to ATA expected to stay in a 1-1.1% range; cost of borrowing stable or 5-10 bps better.
Affordable and emerging to reach about 50% of the book in two to three years; corporate to reach 5-6% in year two and 8-9% in year three.
capex_capacity: Opened 35 branches in Q4 FY26, taking the network to 393 branches (229 affordable, 87 emerging market).

Industry housing finance growth cited at 12-13%; the company describes itself as third-largest in the industry.

Non-housing share of the book at 32.4% vs 30.6% in Q3; PBC retail home loans at 65%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the spread fall while NIM rose, and will the ROA gap normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinay Gupta said the divergence is a methodology difference (daily spread convention vs monthly NIM averaging) and should normalise from next quarter, with NIM in a 5-10 bps range of current trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: What credit cost is built into the 2.4-2.5% ROA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinay Gupta said credit cost is expected to remain negative at about 15-20 bps in FY27, with write-off pool recoveries continuing; mix shift to emerging, affordable and corporate should support NIM over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did affordable disbursements weaken and is it linked to asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajai Kumar Shukla said affordable disbursements rebounded in Q4, mid-year challenges were temporary and fixed, and quality is not the reason; Prime disbursement reflects replenishment of runoff.

qa_highlights.question: What early bounce and stress indicators are visible for April?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said April bounce rates are similar to March, with no significant jump; a one-off government-employee EMI bounce was cleared the next day.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management confident yields have bottomed out?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajai Kumar Shukla said no repo change in recent months, so balance transfer outflows should restrict, supporting yield; BT out improved from Q3 to Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What was the nature of the INR 335 crore corporate disbursement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one case in FY26 was about INR 360-370 crores, primarily in Mumbai; focus is on reputed builders in about seven or eight top cities, with corporate at about 3% of book in FY27.

risks_watch: Yield recovery depends on balance transfer outflows staying restricted and on no further rate cuts; management also flagged possible upside in market rates.
Credit cost is negative because of write-off pool recoveries (about INR 500 crores corporate and INR 325 crores retail remaining); normalisation could weigh on ROA.
Opex grew 13% and the full cost of 35 Q4 branches will flow into FY27; opex to ATA target 1-1.1%.
Cost of borrowing: management expects only stable to 5-10 bps improvement; a rating upgrade is being pursued as a lever.
Geopolitical and crude-oil risk could affect inflation, rates and asset quality, though management sees no early stress as of mid-April.
Prime 30+ DPD on a like-for-like basis is 2.72% (investor presentation figure of 3.31% includes Stage-2 SICR accounts).

540173|2026-06.headline: PNB Housing Q1 FY27 PAT rose 4% YoY to INR 557 crore, with ROA 2.37% and ROE 11.44%, while NIM fell 19 bps QoQ to 3.50%.
540173|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 PAT grew 4% YoY to INR 557 crore, with ROA of 2.37% and ROE of 11.44%. Disbursements moved to a cheque-realisation basis this quarter, so reported disbursement grew 18% YoY to INR 5,882 crore against 56% on the old cheque-handover basis. Loan book grew 15% YoY to INR 89,670 crore, NIM moderated to 3.50% and gross NPA was 0.95%. Management says margin and yield have bottomed and expects Q2 to be much better than Q1, especially in Affordable.

Prime yield mix benefit about 10 to 15 bps; Affordable yield up about 50 bps QoQ per management.

qa_highlights.question: How should yield and cost of funds trend, and does the medium-term NIM expansion thesis from mix shift toward Affordable/Emerging/CF still hold over two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin, yield and cost of funds have all bottomed; gradual margin improvement expected from H2 FY27. Construction finance capped at 3% of book in FY27; Affordable and Emerging share at 41% now, targeting 45% by FY27-end and nearly 50% in two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the gross disbursement momentum (55%+ on cheque-handover basis) carry into Q2 and make the 18-20% loan growth guidance conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to beat both gross and net Q2 numbers, said Q2 gross will be much better than Q1 and July showed strong gross and net momentum. It said it expects to do much better than the 18-20% loan growth guidance but did not raise it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did leverage and NII move sharply when debt-to-equity barely changed?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said average leverage rose from 3.6x to 3.75x; Q4 disbursement realisations flowed into Q1 borrowings, and lower investment yields also weighed on total yield.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gap between reported and gross disbursement across all segments, and what is Affordable growth on a like-for-like basis?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap spans Prime, Emerging and Affordable since retail and wholesale moved to debit-from-account recognition. Like-for-like Affordable YoY growth is about 11%.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO said credit cost should stay negative through FY27 given line of sight on recoveries. FY27 ROA guided around 2.4%; FY28 around 2.3% as credit cost normalises; long-term 2.3% to 2.35%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did recoveries of about INR 77 crore not fully flow through ECL writeback, and where did the difference go?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said regular OTS settlements cost about INR 10-12 crore, booked as write-offs in Prime and Emerging legacy pool, explaining the gap versus the INR 67 crore recovery figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is Q2 net disbursement growth versus Q1 net, and what does July look like?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall Q2 net disbursement expected about 60-70% above Q1 net; Affordable 2.5x-2.6x Q1 net. Management said July was promising, with Prime and Emerging contributing 15-18% of Affordable business in July.

qa_highlights.question: How much benefit from rating upgrades and when will it show in cost of borrowing?

qa_highlights.question: Prime yield rose 8 bps: how much is mix versus like-for-like, and does self-employed mix raise risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 10-15 bps benefit to mix shift toward self-employed and non-home loans; without mix, Prime yield would have been roughly stable at 8.92-8.95%. Delinquency in Prime and Emerging said to have improved QoQ.

Going forward, we feel NIM has largely bottomed out and should start improving from second half of this financial year.
So it was an artificial lift in NIM in Q4, whereas that start getting normalized from Q1 onwards.

540175|2026-03.headline: Regency Fincorp FY26 PAT rose 170% to INR13.4 crore on AUM of INR261.2 crore (up 45%), with secured MSME now about 61% of AUM.
540175|2026-03.overview: Maiden earnings call for FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) covering AUM, disbursements, profitability and asset quality. Management said the book is shifting from unsecured and JLG microfinance toward secured MSME lending and a planned salaried digital lending product (Cash My Salary app). Net NPA rose to 0.74% from 0.31%, which management attributed to legacy JLG and short-tenor unsecured loans. Management outlined a target of INR500-550 crore AUM this year and INR3,000 crore by FY30, funded by INR400-450 crore of expected lender borrowings. Cost of funds is currently 13-14%, with a target of 11-12% and a longer-term aim of 10-10.5%.

segments.name: Secured MSME lending
segments.commentary: Secured share of disbursement rose to about 57% in FY26 from 23% in FY25; secured book is about 61% of AUM versus 18% a year earlier. Average tenure 48-60 months, LTV 50-60%, ROI reducing from 20% to 24%.

segments.name: Unsecured MSME lending
segments.commentary: Book run down from about INR104 crore to about INR60 crore. Tenure around 12 months, kept for cash flow and collection continuity.

segments.name: JLG (group microfinance)
segments.commentary: About 10.5% of AUM. No disbursements since November 2025. Expected about 70% run-down by end FY27 and zero by end of calendar 2027.

segments.name: Digital personal loans (Cash My Salary)
segments.commentary: Salaried borrowers earning above INR45,000; pilot live with approval in 30-45 minutes; priced at about 24% flat for a six-month tenor. Targeted at 15-20% of AUM.

guidance_outlook: AUM target of about INR500-550 crore this year, roughly doubling from INR261 crore, with about 80% secured MSME, about INR75-100 crore digital, and INR400 crore secured.
Branch network to roughly double to about 50 branches by end FY27 and mid-calendar 2027, from 23 currently.
Cost of funds target of 11-12% this year (from 13-14%), with a further goal of 10-10.5% within 12 months; 10.25% cited for a net cost of funds.
Opex expected at about 2-2.75% of AUM; lending rates expected at 15-16% after cost reductions.
AUM target of INR3,000 crore by FY30.
NIM expected to be maintained at current levels rather than increased; PPI licence approval expected in the coming quarter or financial year.
capex_capacity: 23 branches; average branch AUM about INR10-12 crore (range from INR3 crore to INR10 crore).
Branches capable of disbursing about INR2-2.5 crore per month on average.
Plan to raise INR400-450 crore from banks and NBFCs this year, including ICICI, Axis, Yes Bank, LC Venture Debt, Lighthouse Canton and others.
RBI NOC received for PPI licence; digital wallet RedPay to launch within 12 months.
INR25 crore raised via compulsorily convertible debentures in April 2026, to fund secured MSME growth and digital lending.
demand_pricing: Average MSME ticket size INR35-45 lakh; collateral is residential or commercial constructed property (no land, industrial land or agri land), with an LTV of 50-60%.
Lending is restricted to non-trading MSMEs (hardware, small restaurants, hotels, small manufacturers); no real estate or trading lending.
Collection efficiency about 95-96% on zero-month basis and 97-98% on zero-plus basis.
Zero-plus DPD about INR2.2 crore (under 1% of AUM); 90-day PAR about INR65-70 lakh per the Q&A answer, and about INR40-60 lakh in another answer.
Expansion focus remains North India (Punjab, Haryana, Uttarakhand, UP, NCR); West India is next and South is not planned for 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What collateral secures the MSME loans and what is the SARFAESI and recovery process?
qa_highlights.answer: Collateral is mainly residential or commercial property at 50-60% LTV, with an average collateral value of INR65-75 lakh. Only one 90-DPD secured account is in legal recovery, expected to be liquidated within the quarter; in-house lawyers handle notices and third parties handle recovery.

qa_highlights.question: How will AUM reach INR500-550 crore and then INR3,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans to run down the unsecured book, raise INR400-450 crore from lenders, double branches to about 50, and keep opex at 2.5-2.75%. It targets INR3,000 crore AUM by FY30.

qa_highlights.question: How are NIMs protected as the mix shifts to secured lending, and what is the cost of funds target?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM is about 10.75-11% and is expected to hold at current levels as the digital product at about 24% offsets lower MSME yields. Cost of funds is 13-14% today, targeted at 11-12%, with a further decline possible once public sector banks lend.

qa_highlights.question: What drives asset quality deterioration and is the NPA rise structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the NPA rise to legacy JLG and Karja Mukti Abhiyan stress in Punjab and Haryana, plus short-tenor loans. It said the secured salaried book is less risky and cited industry NPA of about 1.5-1.6% versus its 0.76%.

qa_highlights.question: What differentiates the company and how does the PPI licence help?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sources 100% of leads in-house with no DSA, and the PPI wallet will give bank-statement visibility for early risk signals and cheaper lead generation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the cost of funds fall to 8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit to 8%, saying it expects a significant reduction in cost of funds and would pass part of the 2% arbitrage to customers within 12 months.

risks_watch: Net NPA rose to 0.74% from 0.31%, and the secured book is still seasoning; watch 90-DPD and collections in the secured book.
