540497|2026-03.headline: S Chand FY26 EBITDA hit Rs1,449m (18.1% margin) with net cash Rs1,048m; FY27 revenue growth guided at 10-15%, margin at 17-19%.
540497|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue came in at the guided Rs8,000m, with gross margin held near 68% despite a 6% GST hike on paper. EBITDA rose to Rs1,449m (18.1% margin, within the 18-20% guidance) and PAT grew 21% to Rs731m. Operating cash flow was Rs747m, below the ~Rs1,000m five-year average, because receivables (160 days) and inventory (232 days) rose. Management guided FY27 operating revenue growth of 10-15%, EBITDA margin of 17-19% (1pp below FY26), and OCF above Rs1,000m.

financial_highlights.change: sustained despite 6% GST hike on paper
vs Rs2,753m and 140 days in Q4FY25
vs Rs1,401m and 223 days in Q4FY25

segments.name: Publishing (curriculum/school books)
segments.commentary: Growth was mainly volume-led with muted pricing; publishing margins improved as the mix shifted toward sourced content in digital, per management. Old and new syllabus books were adopted in FY26, and new series (Mylestone, My Zen, SmartK, Solid Steps) are in over 1,500 schools.

segments.name: Digital / AI dataset content licensing
segments.commentary: Revenue grew over 60% YoY in FY26, with management citing roughly Rs32 crore in FY25 and Rs40 crore targeted for FY27. Digital margins were lower than last year despite Rs10-11 crore of incremental revenue, which shows the margin dilution from sourced content (sourced share rose from about 20% to 70%).

segments.name: International (CPD Singapore)
segments.commentary: Acquired January 2026; supplementary books for Singapore/IGCSE/IB curricula. Last-year revenue was about USD0.5m (Rs5-6 crore), with sales only in Singapore and Malaysia. Management expects roughly Rs5-7 crore of capex over 2-3 years and a 1-2 year build-up in India.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating revenue growth of 10-15%, mainly volume-driven.
FY27 EBITDA margin band of 17-19%, below FY26 because of paper, logistics, packaging and fuel cost inflation; management expects a 6-8% price increase.
Operating cash flow above Rs1,000m in FY27; receivables and inventory expected to normalise in 1H FY27.
Content licensing revenue target above Rs400m in FY27; management says this is a pipeline view and may change.
FY27 year-end net cash of about Rs130-135m after roughly Rs20 crore capex; buyback under consideration once the war-related uncertainty settles.
Full NCF (new syllabus) adoption expected across K-12 over FY27-28.
capex_capacity: Rs20 crore capex this year is mainly for a new state-of-the-art printing plant near Delhi with more space and digital printing (POD) machines.
About 80-85% of printing is in-house and 15-20% outsourced; the new plant is aimed at in-sourcing and improving working capital.
Management did not give a margin contribution from the new plant in the first one or two years.
International business capex of Rs5-7 crore expected over 2-3 years; team of 10-15 people.
Raw material (paper) inventory was about Rs29 crore at year-end, equal to under a month in peak season and about 3 months off-peak.
demand_pricing: Paper prices expected up 10-15% for FY27; supplier negotiations were not finalised at the time of the call.
Price increases are capped at about 6-8% because of customer pushback.
Around 40-60% of paper is imported, depending on the year; a stronger dollar and higher logistics costs are a factor.
Higher education has shrunk from about 20% of the business pre-COVID to about 8%, citing piracy and lower book purchases by students; school segment is up 20-25%.
Management estimates a 10-15% market share in private school publishing and a school retention rate above 70%.
AI licensing: about 30-40% of the content repository is licensed to date; about 100% of term-license renewals so far have been retained; pricing is varied and has seen a slight correction.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 10-15% growth guidance inclusive of any NCF upside, and how big can AI licensing become?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10-15% is a sound guidance on a large base, with growth volume-driven. AI licensing targets Rs100 crore over time; it is a mix of one-time (about 30%) and term licences (about 70%). Management said it would not give margins due to client confidentiality, though in-house content is near 90% margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there no buyback despite a strong net cash position and low valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a buyback is under consideration and the Board will decide later. It is waiting for the war-related uncertainty to ease and for paper and consumables prices to settle. FY27 year-end net cash is expected at about Rs130-135m.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins return to 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company now prioritises cash conversion over margin. Operating cash flow was Rs800m-era levels of Rs38m in the past versus Rs75m this year, and the company wants working capital efficiency and not revenue growth that does not convert into cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs400m+ licensing revenue be from in-house or sourced content?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects roughly 60% in-house and 40% sourced, based on the current pipeline. The target is per SKU or title licensed, not per user.

qa_highlights.question: Why are the entities kept separate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said each acquired brand has its own sales team and school relationships, which lets the group capture more of each child's book bag. Consolidation would risk losing market share.

risks_watch: Working capital: receivables at 160 days and inventory at 232 days; management expects normalisation in 1H FY27, which needs to be checked in the Q1 numbers.
Margin pressure from paper, fuel and logistics inflation; the 17-19% band is below FY26's 18.1%, and FY27 price hikes are capped at 6-8%.
Dependence on AI licensing: revenue is lumpy, pricing is varied, and client budgets are the stated constraint; margin on sourced content is lower.
Middle East conflict is delaying collections from schools in the region.
Higher education decline (about 8% of the mix from about 20% pre-COVID).
Integration and returns from CPD Singapore; management said more clarity will come next year.
Buyback and dividend decisions remain open; the company is currently paying Rs4/share interim dividend.

540497|2026-06.headline: S Chand Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 12% YoY to Rs1,145m, but EBITDA loss of Rs97m and PAT loss of Rs187m widened the reported loss.
540497|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was Rs1,145m, up 12% YoY, with gross margin improved. EBITDA turned to a loss of Rs97m and PAT to a loss of Rs187m, hit by marketing costs pulled into Q1 from Q2 and a one-time tax rate adjustment. Management pre-bought paper ahead of expected price rises, lifting inventory and slightly raising net working capital days. Net cash reached a record Rs1,182m after Rs141m dividend, and FY27 guidance of 10-15% operating revenue growth and 17-19% EBITDA margin was reiterated.

financial_highlights.change: Wider loss YoY due to one-time tax rate adjustment
vs Rs1,160m in Q4FY26, after Rs141m dividend

segments.name: School Education (K-12)
segments.commentary: Refreshed curriculum brands Mylestone, My Zen, SmartK and Solid Steps received repeat adoptions; Mylestone (650+ schools) and My Zen (about 500 schools) together generated about Rs55-60 crore in FY26. New partnerships with Allied, Jump Maths, Penguin and Speedlabs added to the offering.

segments.name: Content Licensing
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 revenue of about Rs9 crore (Rs91m); about Rs14 crore booked to date. Target is above Rs40 crore for FY27 and growing active clients from 5 to 10.

segments.name: International (CPD Singapore, acquired)
segments.commentary: Q1 contribution about Rs1 crore; target of SGD 1m (about Rs7.5 crore) by year end. Management says it was profitable earlier, currently investing in content and marketing with limited burn; India and Middle East K-12 expansion will take 1-2 academic cycles.

qa_highlights.answer: Management pre-bought to hedge against higher USD-linked import costs, logistics and Middle East tensions; paper prices may firm up next quarter. About 25% of annual consumption bought, versus the usual August-October purchase window.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 17-19% margin guidance inclusive of paper price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Guidance assumes a 10-12% paper price increase; management said a 40% rise would be a different case.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of buyback and acquisitions?

540530|2026-06.headline: HUDCO guides FY27 disbursement of about INR65,000 crore and a INR3 lakh crore loan book by 2029-30, with spreads held near 2%.
540530|2026-06.overview: Management skipped the headline numbers and focused on policy tailwinds (urban challenge fund, bankable projects) and the pipeline. FY27 disbursement target is about INR65,000 crore against about INR5,000 crore achieved last year, with borrowing plan of about INR70,000 crore approved. Two June MoUs (Gujarat and Bihar, each above INR1 lakh crore) were presented as pipeline, with sanctions expected to start this quarter. Management reiterated a spread of around 2% and NIM of around 3%, though an analyst cited Q1 spread near 1.8%, and said compression is due to fast growth and should reverse by Q3.

financial_highlights.change: Lower due to Board decision not to create DTL on special reserve

financial_highlights.value: about INR20,000 crore; INR4,000 crore+ received in Q1

segments.name: Urban infrastructure / sustainable finance
segments.commentary: Q1 sanctions included ring roads, expressways, irrigation, water grid, industrial corridors, power generation/distribution, Telangana urban infra and water supply/sewage. Management said water and sanitation are the core sustainable-finance focus, aligned with AMRUT and MoHUA priorities.

segments.name: Housing
segments.commentary: Housing portfolio is shrinking because states are not bringing counterpart funding under PMAY; housing lending is priced around MCLR of about 8.6%.

segments.name: Private sector / PPP project finance
segments.commentary: New PPP project finance division; 2 projects sanctioned in Q1 worth about INR6,000-7,000 crore. Disbursement expected to start in the latter part of FY27. No internal target set.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement target about INR65,000 crore; borrowing plan about INR70,000 crore approved by Board.
Loan book target of INR3 lakh crore by 2030 (FY30); FY28 not planned, with mid-FY28 review and market disclosure if course correction needed.
Spread to be maintained around 2% and NIM around 3%; spread expected to reflect in Q3 as Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 disbursements capitalise.

Gujarat and Bihar MoUs (each above INR1 lakh crore; combined about INR2 lakh crore): sanctions to start in Q2 FY27 for Gujarat, with works in Q4 FY27 or earlier; MoUs valid 5 years, disbursement over around 5 years.

FX borrowing: RBI forex window tie-up of about USD2 billion (about USD700 million drawn), all-in cost about 5.5-6.5% including hedging, with ECB share possibly rising from about 10% to 20% of borrowings.
capex_capacity: Gujarat MoU: metro, RRTS, Olympic/Commonwealth Games infrastructure (Commonwealth Games Ahmedabad 2030), highways; sanctions expected this quarter.
Bihar MoU: 12 satellite towns; Bihar road projects of about INR21,000 crore identified; tourism, metro and digital parks under discussion.
Repayments of INR15,000-16,000 crore expected over remaining quarters of FY27.
demand_pricing: Analyst cited Q1 spread near 1.8%; management attributed compression to accelerated growth and expects 2% spread to return by Q3.
Competition for state financing from NABARD, NaBFID and commercial banks has pushed rates down, per management.
Borrowing mix: about 70% domestic (bank loans and bonds), about 10% ECB currently; ECB could rise to 20% over next five years.
Management said yield is not split between urban infra and housing; rates are sector-specific.

qa_highlights.question: What is the short-term foreign exposure and what are the lending rates/portfolio yield?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said short-term foreign currency loans have been retired and over 99% is 5-year borrowing. Spread guided around 2%, NIM around 3%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FX accounting loss issue behind us, and how will the Gujarat and Bihar MoUs translate into sanctions?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance director said no FCNRs maturing in FY27 or FY28 except USD200 million maturing in 2028, which is secured; no forex losses foreseen this year. Gujarat sanctions expected this quarter; Bihar has 12 satellite towns and road projects.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR3 lakh crore loan book guidance conservative given MoU visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed partly, citing land acquisition, social and political issues and state compliance before contract award; said projects typically complete within 5 years, so 5-year horizon is preferred.

qa_highlights.question: What is the internal target for private sector / PPP book?
qa_highlights.answer: No target set for private sanctions; approach is case-by-case with good entities and strong concessions. UCF PPP projects in water, desalination, drainage and sewage are expected; UCF gives 50% VGF.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 disbursement and repayment outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 disbursement about INR65,000 crore; total repayments about INR20,000 crore, with INR4,000 crore+ received in Q1 and INR15,000-16,000 crore expected in the remaining quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the forex window borrowing size and cost?
qa_highlights.answer: USD2 billion tie-up is the minimum; all-in cost including hedging about 5.5-6.5%, as RBI covers most hedging and HUDCO pays about 1.5%.

risks_watch: Spread: Q1 spread near 1.8% per analyst vs 2% guidance; watch Q2 and Q3 for recovery as higher-yield disbursements capitalise.
Execution risk on the INR3 lakh crore 2030 loan book and the MoU-linked sanctions, given land, political and state-compliance delays.
Gross NPA of about INR1,600 crore, of which about INR1,100 crore sits in NCLT (mostly pre-2013 projects); management targets resolution in FY27.
Rising ECB share (up to 20%) increases FX exposure, dependent on forex window availability and cost.

540575|2026-06.headline: Star Cement Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR203 crore (INR1,497/t) from INR230 crore, with PAT at INR74 crore versus INR98 crore on subsidy cuts and fuel costs.

540595|2026-03.headline: Tejas Networks Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8% QoQ to INR333 crores, but Q4 PAT loss widened to INR211 crores; FY26 PAT loss INR909 crores.
540595|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR333 crores, up 8% QoQ from INR307 crores, with EBIT loss narrowing to INR219 crores from INR239 crores. PAT loss widened to INR211 crores from INR197 crores in Q3, and FY26 revenue was INR1,103 crores against a PAT loss of INR909 crores. Management described FY26 as a transition year after the BSNL 4G project, with delayed wireline and wireless projects causing a revenue shortfall, while R&D and capex were maintained. Order book closed at INR1,514 crores versus INR1,019 crores a year earlier, with India at about 88% of revenue and around 83% of order book, excluding the BSNL 4G add-on PO. Senior management and CFO changes were announced during the call.

Net working capital fell to INR4,235 crores on lower receivables, while net debt rose to INR4,384 crores from INR4,277 crores as capex and operating costs were funded.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR2,300 crore order book include the INR1,500 crore BSNL order?

qa_highlights.question: Why no wins outside BSNL in India for wireless?

540602|2026-03.headline: GTPL Hathway swung to a Q4 FY26 net loss as consolidated reported EBITDA margin fell to 9.7% and operating margin to 18%.
540602|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 4% YoY to INR9,344 million, but the quarter posted negative PAT driven by two fewer operating days (~INR12 crore revenue impact), year-end impairment/provisions (~INR7.5-8 crore) and a forex revaluation loss (~INR9 crore). FY26 consolidated revenue grew 7% to INR37,466 million, with net profit attributable to parent of INR156 million. Subscriber base was flat in the quarter as capex shifted to the Headend-In-The-Sky (HITS) platform, and management guided to renewed consolidation and capex of about INR350 crore per year.

Transponder contracts for HITS are USD-denominated, creating forex revaluation exposure; accounted under depreciation and ROU assets.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no subscriber growth in cable and broadband this quarter, and are the exceptional items recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Cable focus shifted to converting the base and HITS cost savings, with expansion from Q1 FY27; broadband net adds were muted but are expected to resume next quarter. The impairment was described as a one-time item on old analogue-era investments.

qa_highlights.question: How long can industry consolidation last, and what has held back other HITS adopters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 40-45 million subscribers sit with small MSOs and that consolidation will accelerate post-HITS launch, with about 800 MSOs in India. Competition is defined broadly to include OTT, telcos and social platforms.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 40-45 million small-MSO base can be acquired in FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, saying talks are underway with large players and that deal announcements should come by next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the quarter's operating margin drop from 22% to 18% due to one-offs above the line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 18% is affected by the two-day shortfall (Q4 has 90 days versus 92 in Q3, when margin was 24%); the one-time items sit below EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27-FY29 and the maintenance versus growth split?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR350 crore per year, with about INR150 crore for broadband and about INR200 crore for cable and HITS; about 50% maintenance and 50% growth, totalling about INR700 crore over two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROCE target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says normalised ROCE is about 15%, and expects to return to that level in 2-3 years as growth capex is deployed; FY26 ROCE was in single digits.

540602|2026-06.headline: GTPL Hathway Q1 FY27 consolidated income rose 12% YoY to INR 1,020 crore, but net profit fell to INR 2.3 crore on higher depreciation and finance cost.
540602|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income grew 12% YoY and 9% QoQ to INR 1,020 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of INR 109 crore (10.7% margin) and net profit of INR 2.3 crore. Management attributed the PAT decline of about INR 8 crore YoY mainly to a roughly INR 6 crore rise in depreciation and finance cost from capitalising right-of-use assets for HITS infrastructure. Standalone total revenue rose 16% YoY to INR 693 crore, with standalone EBITDA of INR 64.4 crore (9.3%) and net profit of INR 1.9 crore. The company signed a business transfer agreement to acquire the digital TV business of 7 ACT Group companies for INR 36.23 crore cash, with about 6 lakh subscribers, targeted to close by 15 September 2026.

segments.name: Digital TV
segments.commentary: Subscriber base of 9.60 million at 30 June 2026, of which 8.9 million paying; business partners above 51,000. Management said Digital TV revenue declined YoY as new, lower-ARPU markets dilute the mix; the Digital TV capex is about 50% of the INR 400 crore FY27 plan.

segments.name: Broadband
segments.commentary: Active subscribers of 1.06 million, up 10,000 YoY; ARPU INR 470; average data consumption 436 GB per user per month, up 6% YoY. Home pass base 5.95 million with about 75% FTTX-ready; extraction rate about 16-17%.

guidance_outlook: ACT acquisition (INR 36.23 crore, about 6 lakh digital TV subscribers across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Odisha, Karnataka) to close by 15 September 2026; contribution expected from Q2 mid-quarter and fuller effect in Q3; no revenue or EBITDA contribution figures given yet.
Operating margin (22% currently) expected to rise to about 25% as HITS benefits materialise.
HITS savings expected to reach about 40-50% of benefit in FY27 and 100% from FY28; management expects full benefits from end-Q3 to start-Q4 FY27.
FY27 capex planned at about INR 400 crore, split roughly 50% broadband and 50% digital TV.

540611|2026-03.headline: AU SFB Q4 FY26 profit rose 65% YoY to ₹832 crore with ROA 1.8%, but management guided FY27 credit cost near 0.90% and flagged margin pressure.
540611|2026-03.overview: AU Small Finance Bank reported a strong Q4 FY26, with PAT up 25% QoQ and 65% YoY to ₹832 crore and quarterly ROA of 1.8%, helped by seasonal factors. Deposits grew 10% QoQ and 23% YoY, and loans grew 8% QoQ and 21% YoY, both ahead of the stated private sector benchmark of 13%. Slippages fell 17% QoQ to ₹659 crore and GNPA improved to 2.03%. Management said Q4 was flattered by seasonality, a day-count benefit and lower reversals, and that cost of funds may have bottomed after recent rate hikes.

segments.name: Commercial banking
segments.commentary: Commercial banking is 22% of lending, at about ₹31,000 crore (+29% YoY, +12% QoQ), plus about ₹11,000 crore of non-fund book. It currently funds about 56% of its requirement internally, with a goal of full self-funding alongside transaction banking and CMS.

segments.commentary: Inclusive banking grew 8% QoQ. Non-overdue collection efficiency in MFI was 99.7% (vs 99.3% in Q3), and 92% of the MFI book is covered under CGFMU.

segments.commentary: Digital unsecured grew 4% QoQ. Personal loans rose 19% QoQ from a low base, and credit cards broadly stabilised after about five quarters of decline. Total unsecured fell 1% YoY.

segments.commentary: Total deposits reached ₹1.52 lakh crore (+10% QoQ, +23% YoY). CASA grew 9% QoQ and 20% YoY, with CASA ratio about 28%. Branch banking is about 60% of deposits, and stable deposits are 79%.

Asset mix shift toward secured assets may pressure yields, as unsecured grows slower than the rest of the book.

Outbound AI-led calling campaigns aim to reach 25% of total calls over the next two quarters.
Organisational consolidation: agri merged into business banking, and home loans and MBL share back-end teams.
demand_pricing: Management said the home loan/affordable housing market is too competitive, with new NBFCs and HFCs entering, so it is not growing there irrationally.

Long-term cost-of-funds aspiration is to trade near the prevailing repo rate (5.25% currently), against about 6.75% now.
Wheels growth was driven by improving affordability across segments.

qa_highlights.question: What are the details of the ₹21 crore contingency provision created in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Tripathi said these were ordinary business banking working-capital standard accounts, not high-value specific cases. The provision was added on an internal risk assessment of security cover, with no specific segment or aggregate exposure disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why were savings and term deposit rates raised well ahead of the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal said it is a combination of how much to raise, cost of money, CASA and retail/wholesale mix and CD ratio. He noted cost of money fell 32 bps in FY26 against an expected 15-20 bps, and that liabilities are managed daily and monthly through ALCO.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable ROA and what levers drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Jain said Q4 is seasonally strong and the aim is to hold ROA around 1.8% on a full-year basis next year. Levers are opex-to-assets improvement and lower credit costs from MFI and credit cards. No numeric target was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 margin was from IT refund and other one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Jain said the IT refund helped only slightly and was not material. He said cost of funds may have bottomed, and the seasonal benefits from lower day count and lower slippages will not recur next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How should cost-to-assets evolve as the bank moves to a universal banking licence?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal said FY27 cost to assets should go below 4%, with a first benchmark of about 3.5% in three to five years. He declined to give a number for AI-driven cost savings, calling the technology too early-stage to quantify.

qa_highlights.question: What credit cost should be assumed going forward, and how will the new RBI ECL norms affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal suggested building credit cost around 0.90%, and said Q4 should not be annualised. On ECL, management said it was too early to comment. Vivek Tripathi said 90% of the book is secured and CGFMU covers MFI, and the guideline applies from April 2027.

540611|2026-09.headline: AU SFB Q2 FY27 PAT up 53% YoY to INR858 Cr; deposits up 29% YoY, GNPA down to 1.99%.

Asset quality improved on a YoY basis, with GNPA at 1.99% and credit cost including guarantee premium at 0.8%, driven by unsecured normalisation. NIM fell 9 bps QoQ to 5.8% on higher investment book and seasonality, and management flagged cost-of-funds and yield pressure from the 25 bps repo hike. 540678|2026-06.headline: Cochin Shipyard Q1 FY27 PAT fell to INR 151.45 crore from INR 187.82 crore on turnover of INR 1,094.21 crore; ISRF JV with DP World's Drydocks World valued at INR 1,800 crore.

UK-India FTA effective 15 July 2026, but non-tariff barriers such as 50% testing of Indian shipments remain; EU FTA expected around December 2026 or January 2027.
Ocean freight costs have more than doubled since Q4 FY26 due to war-led disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume below the 12,500-14,000 MT run-rate, and what growth is expected for the rest of the year?

qa_highlights.question: What is the RTE contribution and its margin premium over RTC?

qa_highlights.question: Will US tariff refunds be received?
qa_highlights.answer: No refunds have been received yet. Timing and outcome are unclear because of ongoing US legal proceedings.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 realisation a new high versus history, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Similar levels were seen in FY22 during COVID phase 2, but those were driven by panic buying and hurt volumes. The company aims for a sustainable level through a richer value-added mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US CVD and ADD outlook?

qa_highlights.question: What new adjacent products are being commercialised?

540701|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell 4% to INR 6,776 mn and EBITDA to INR 600 mn, mainly from an INR 10 mn order deferred to H2.
540701|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 6,776 mn versus INR 7,080 mn a year earlier, a 4% decline, which management attributed mainly to an order pushed from Q1 into the latter half of FY27. EBITDA fell to INR 600 mn from INR 1,406 mn, and the company posted a loss before tax of about INR 512 mn after finance costs of about INR 370 mn and an FX loss of about INR 117.3 mn. The CDMO segment revenue fell to INR 5,343 mn while Marketable Molecules rose to INR 1,432 mn. Management guided to single-digit group revenue growth for FY27 with EBITDA margin similar to or slightly above FY26, and said a promoter-level ECB of up to CHF 200 mn is expected to close in 60-90 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why does cash stay overseas rather than repay India debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiary-to-parent loans are not permitted, and repatriation via dividends triggers tax leakage, so Swiss cash is kept as deposits to fund overseas needs.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the company swung between profit and loss quarter to quarter?

qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated goodwill is above INR 4,000 crores, restated at closing rates and not amortised; standalone goodwill is about INR 550 crores and is amortised; original INR 1,350 crores.

540704|2026-03.headline: Matrimony.com Q4 FY26 consolidated billing rose 9.9% YoY to INR 126.1 crore; management guides Q1 FY27 PAT to more than double.
540704|2026-03.overview: Matchmaking billing grew 10.5% YoY to INR 125.4 crore in Q4 FY26, ahead of revenue growth of 8.4%, and Matchmaking EBITDA margin improved to 22% from 17.7% a year ago. Consolidated PAT rose 18.9% YoY to INR 9.7 crore, but full-year PAT fell to INR 34.2 crore from INR 45.3 crore as FY26 revenue grew only 0.9% and the Marriage Service and other segment loss persisted. Management said the one-year "Till You Marry" package is now flowing into revenue, narrowing the gap between billing and revenue. Management expects Q1 FY27 PAT to more than double year on year and billing growth in double digits or high single digits.

540710|2026-03.headline: Capacite Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 6% to INR712 crores, with EBITDA up 27% to INR109 crores at a 15.3% margin.
540710|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 6% YoY to INR712 crores and EBITDA rose 27% to INR109 crores, with margin expanding to 15.3% from 12.8%. PAT fell to INR45 crores from INR53 crores as other income dropped to INR1.5 crores from INR33.5 crores. FY26 order inflow was INR4,446 crores, above the INR3,500 crore guidance, and working capital days fell 43 days. Management attributed the weak revenue growth to labour shortfall after West Bengal and assembly elections, and flagged commodity-driven escalation lag, with an INR10 crore provision and a margin guidance cut to 15.5-16.5% for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How are war and commodity prices affecting execution and profitability, and are contracts fixed cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Private projects have 100% commodity pass-through, and government contracts have escalation, but indices lag actual prices for electrical and aluminium items. A INR10 crore provision was taken and will be reversed if escalation catches up over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue growth only 6% in Q4 and how much revenue was lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the shortfall to labour migration around the West Bengal and BMC elections. It estimated about INR40-45 crores lost in Q4 and about INR125 crores for FY26, and said a tree-cutting permission delay on one IIT project also hurt revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 CIDCO, MHADA, NBCC and Signature Global revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CIDCO is seen at INR500-600 crores and MHADA at INR350-400 crores. Management did not give project-level figures for NBCC or Signature Global, and offered IR follow-up for top 5-6 projects. It also expects INR25-30 crores from Raymond.

qa_highlights.question: How will finance costs trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest cost fell from 12.65% to 9.65% over 15 months after the rating upgrade to BBB+. FY27 finance cost is expected to fall by INR6-8 crores in absolute terms, and bank guarantee commissions have nearly halved.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin downside if the war persists?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15.5% is the worst case on current inputs, but further rises in USD, fuel or commodities could hit EBITDA and PAT. It will update in Q1 or at the latest Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PSU/private split of the order book and the Q1 order pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects PSU to stay around 50-60% of the order book and gave a quarterly inflow pipeline of about INR1,000 crores in Q1 and Q2, and INR2,500-3,000 crores in H2.

540710|2026-06.headline: Capacite Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 7% to INR629 crore, but EBITDA fell 3% to INR99 crore after a INR10 crore commodity provision.

PAT fell to INR40 crore (6.2% margin) from INR47 crore, impacted by an additional INR10 crore provision for non-ferrous commodity price escalation not yet covered by government indices. Management attributed the weak execution to labour shortages (workforce fell to about 7,000 in June, roughly 30% short) and a delayed IIT Bombay start, and said labour is now fully in place. Order book stood at INR13,535 crore, with FY27 inflow guidance of INR4,500-5,000 crore and INR1,071 crore booked so far.

540716|2026-06.headline: ICICI Lombard Q1 FY27 PAT fell 46.0% to ₹4.03 bn, driven by a ₹1.65 bn Motor TP judgement provision and two large Fire losses.

Combined ratio rose to 107.2% from 102.9%, including a 2.8 pp hit from the Supreme Court Motor TP judgement provision and a 1.0 pp hit from two Fire large losses. Excluding these items, the combined ratio was 102.3% versus 102.2% a year ago, and PAT would have been ₹5.75 bn (down 23.0%). Investment income fell to ₹11.74 bn from ₹12.88 bn as capital gains halved, partly offset by higher portfolio yield and duration.

segments.commentary: De-grew 13.8% in Q1 FY27 amid pricing pressure; SME share rose to 33.6% from 28.4%. Fire line declined 27.8% for the industry and the company de-grew about 32%; June Fire de-growth improved to about 18% for the company.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Grew 14.0% in line with industry (13.9%), market share 10.5%; new vehicle sales up 33.6% vs industry 14.9%. Mix: private car 49.8%, two-wheeler 28.7%, commercial vehicle 21.5%. Motor combined ratio 106.6% in FY26 vs industry 128.0%.

Motor claims and servicing scale were cited as operating metrics, not capacity: Preferred Partner Network served 75.6% of non-OEM motor claims in Q1 FY27 vs 74.6% in Q1 FY26; 168,521 health and travel claims were serviced through the IL TakeCare app vs 141,116 a year earlier.

qa_highlights.answer: Closed cases typically do not reopen after court finality, so impact is largely on open exposures. Excluding the two large losses, Fire loss ratios should be within the historical 65-70% average range; the company has never exceeded 100% in Fire.

qa_highlights.answer: The award relates to a policy about seven to eight years old and is on a gross basis; the company will pursue legal remedies and believes the net P&L impact is not material given reinsurance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the reserve prudence buffer still generate releases given the ₹165 crore charge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its reserving philosophy is unchanged, prudence will continue, and reserving triangles should continue to show favourable development over cycles.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term APE growth target of around 14%, in line with the 3-5 year CAGR; FY26 individual APE growth was 13% versus 13% guidance.
VoNB margin guided to 26-28% range for FY27-28, with the company aiming to report above 27%; management declined to extend the range to FY27-29.
GST impact on first-year commission for business written before 22 September 2025 is about 1.8-1.9% of margin on an annual basis; management says it is largely absorbed in the 27.5% margin.
Opex ratio expected to carry a full year of GST in FY27, but management expects it not to rise materially; IT and branch spend to continue.
Deferred annuity (regular-pay) product targeted for launch by June 2026, otherwise the next quarter.
Ind AS transition: forbearance sought, with adoption from 1 April 2027.
capex_capacity: Opened 120 new branches in FY26 and added over 1.2 lakh agents on a gross basis; management says newer branches are on track but not yet at breakeven.
Continued investment planned in branches, IT infrastructure and agency training; management says no other major expense is planned beyond IT strengthening.
Solvency of 1.90 funded by internal accruals with no fresh capital raised; the company is assessing Ind AS and RBC impacts.
demand_pricing: Customers are investing where they see value despite geopolitical volatility; February and March growth was described as decent, and management expects continued sales growth.
Q4 bancassurance sales declined year on year; management said the whole insurance sector was sluggish in Q4 and that banca met its internal budget for the year.
Non-par pricing is being adjusted with interest rates; a new non-par product replaced the existing one to reflect current yields, passing some benefit to customers.
Management is not planning higher sum assured ULIPs for now, but will decide on launching them in due course.
Online business grew 47% on APE; 99.7% of individual proposals were submitted digitally and 57% of individual policies went through automated underwriting.

qa_highlights.question: Is the persistency assumption change a negative in the VNB walk, and is there a reset in persistency assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is about 50 bps and not significant; changes were minor refinements across mortality, persistency and expenses, with a persistency improvement from long-term protection.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 14% growth at risk given banca grew only 9-11% for three years, and is banca realistically 10-11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not guide channel-level growth; growth would come from agency and other channels, with 14% as an optimal mix. Protection growth is ticket-size-light and supports policy count.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 27-28% margin guidance conservative given FY26 ex-GST margin of 29%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a matter of perception; the range gives flexibility to balance 14% growth with margin, and the product mix is being improved.

qa_highlights.question: What is the GST impact on margins going forward and the opex ratio trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: GST for the second half is already in the 27.5% margin, and the full-year effect is about 1.8-1.9%. Opex ratio would be about 5.5% without GST and the Labour Code versus 5.3% in FY25; the 6.1% reflects GST and Labour Code costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EV operating variance strongly positive while VNB assumptions were strengthened?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said positive variance comes mainly from mortality and persistency, with lower expenses contributing. Assumption changes are minor refinements, and new and in-force business differ in product mix. Economic variance of 3.66% is split as 2.15% from equity, with the balance from bonds.

qa_highlights.question: Does open architecture in banca pose a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is unaware of any such decision, that RBI guidelines are draft and due from 1 July and do not mention open architecture, and that the company will respond to regulatory changes if they arise.

risks_watch: GST treatment on commissions: the full-year impact in FY27 and whether it is offset by product mix.
Persistency: the 61st-month drop linked to COVID-era ULIP sales, and the effect of assumption refinements on VNB.
Banca growth at around 9-11%: the agency and other channels must carry the 14% target.
Equity market volatility affecting ULIP demand and the 65% ULIP share of individual APE.
Regulatory: draft RBI guidelines effective 1 July, Ind AS transition from FY28 and RBC framework, plus any open architecture mandate for banks.
Deferred annuity launch timing (June 2026 target) and non-par repricing with yield volatility.

540719|2026-06.headline: SBI Life Q1 FY27 VNB rose 29% to INR14.1bn, but VNB margin fell to 26.2% as GST and a one-off GTI group deal diluted mix.
540719|2026-06.overview: Individual rated premium grew 14% to INR39.7bn with private market share of 22.2%, and all product segments and channels grew. Profit after tax rose 22% to INR7.2bn, helped by supportive market conditions, while the GST impact was INR2.3bn for the quarter. VNB margin of 26.2% was down year on year, which management attributed mainly to a higher share of lumpy group business (GTI) in APE. Management said the margin was within its 26–28% guidance, at the lower end, and expects it to move to the upper end as individual mix normalises.

financial_highlights.change: Margin down YoY; GST impact INR2.3bn

segments.name: Individual rated premium / APE
segments.commentary: Individual APE INR39.9bn, +14% YoY; ULIP INR24.5bn (61% share vs 65% in Q1 FY26); guaranteed non-par savings INR9.7bn, +27%. Non-ULIP share of IRP reached 38%.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group NBP INR32.9bn (37% of NBP), +41% YoY; group APE INR53.8bn, +36%; group protection APE INR12.3bn, +313%, driven by a large one-off GTI contract.

segments.name: Protection
segments.commentary: Individual protection APE INR1.9bn, +18%; pure protection +41% on individual APE; ROP share of individual protection 68% vs 73% a year ago.

segments.name: Bancassurance (SBI and RRBs)
segments.commentary: 47% of total APE; individual APE INR24.5bn, +10%; SBI branch productivity INR4.1mn, +7%. Other banks grew 19% on individual NBP and 31% on APE; their mix is about 80% non-ULIP.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Individual APE INR13.1bn, +20%; agent productivity INR2 lakh; non-ULIP share rose from 43% to 46%; 34,000+ agents added gross and 11 new branches opened.

segments.name: Other channels (direct, corporate agents, brokers, online)
segments.commentary: Grew 160% and contributed 28% of total APE; management did not split this into organic and group components.

guidance_outlook: IRP growth guidance of 14–15% for FY27 reaffirmed.
VNB margin guidance of 26–28% for FY27 maintained; management expects the margin to move toward the upper end as individual mix normalises.
GST drag expected for one more quarter (Q2 FY27), with the impact ending thereafter; GST was waived from 22 September, so about 2.5 months of impact remain in Q1.
Pure protection growth expected to keep outpacing ROP; the company is shifting focus from ROP to non-ROP and pure protection.
Regular-pay deferred annuity plan expected to launch within the next quarter.
Non-ULIP share of IRP targeted to be sustained at around this level for the year.
Other-expense ratio expected to normalise over the next three quarters, but higher stamp duty tied to sum assured growth will persist.
capex_capacity: Agency network: more than 100 branches opened over the last two to three years, and 11 new branches in Q1 FY27.
Agent additions: over 34,000 agents added on a gross basis in Q1 FY27.
New corporate agency tie-up with J&K Bank; business expected to start in the current quarter.
Automation: 99.9% of individual proposals submitted digitally; 67% processed through automated underwriting.
demand_pricing: Individual sum assured grew 46% YoY and group new business sum assured grew 265%; rider sum assured is 39% of individual sum assured.
Rider attachment on ULIP is about 45–50%, up from roughly 35% when introduced about 1–1.5 years ago; management expects it to hold or improve.
Non-par pricing is reviewed against yield movements; IRR for customers was raised in June after the yield curve moved.
The 61st-month persistency dip is attributed to the COVID cohort moving through policy years; management expects it to normalise by end-Q3 FY27.
Credit protect business was flat YoY; management expects an uptick in coming quarters.
Misselling ratio 0.02%; death claim settlement ratio 98.8%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 60 bps product-mix drag on VNB margin is due to the GTI group deal, and what is the normalised margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 60 bps mix drag relates only to GTI and that the company does not disclose product-wise margins. It said margin should return to normal as IRP share normalises. The 40 bps assumption-related item reflects the March 2026 annual review, and there was no assumption change in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GST drag going to persist, and how do expenses look?
qa_highlights.answer: GST drag of about 1.1 percentage points in Q1 is expected to continue into Q2 and then fade. Management said the rise in other expenses reflects one-off stamp duty tied to higher sum assured and labour code impacts, and it expects these to normalise over the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will agency growth be sustainable and will the channel mix shift affect costs or margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Agency APE grew 20% in Q1, with the current quarter at 19%-plus. Management expects a stronger contribution from agency in the remaining three quarters and a balanced mix of banca and agency going forward. It did not discuss cost impact in detail.

qa_highlights.question: What proportion of ULIPs carry rider attachment, and how is protection classified?
qa_highlights.answer: Rider attachment on ULIPs is about 45–50%, up from roughly 35% when riders were introduced 1–1.5 years earlier. Riders are counted within individual protection, and rider APE was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is individual protection growth lower than peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift from ROP to pure protection lowers ticket size, which makes headline growth look subdued. Individual protection grew 22% by its own measure against pure protection growth of 41%, with ROP share at 68%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the regular-pay deferred annuity plan launch slip, and what are the non-par and regulatory views?
qa_highlights.answer: The deferred annuity plan is expected in the next quarter and is being developed for an opportune time. On non-par, management said pricing is reviewed against yield movements. On regulation, management said it sees the company as well placed and expects future rules to be positive for the industry.

risks_watch: Group/GTI lumpiness: a large one-off group contract diluted Q1 VNB margin; sustainability of group APE mix and margin recovery to 26–28% range is the key test.
GST drag of about 110 bps on margin in Q1 FY27 with another quarter expected; watch whether Q2 drag falls as indicated.
Other-expense ratio rising (opex ratio 7.7% vs 6.3%) due to stamp duty and labour codes; watch cost discipline.
61st-month persistency dip due to COVID cohort; management expects normalisation by end-Q3 FY27.
Credit protect flat YoY; watch for the promised uptick.
Rider APE not disclosed; pure protection ticket size is smaller, so protection growth optics may stay weaker than peers.
Regulatory changes flagged as an open question by management; details not yet clear.
540719|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on top-line growth and the full-year IRP and VNB margin guidance, but defensive on the margin decline, which it attributed to one-off group business and GST. Management was evasive on quantifying the GTI margin drag and product-level margins, and declined to comment on individual contracts.

And going forward, with higher focus on individual policies, the margin is going to be towards the upper range of our guidance.
So the GST was waived from 22nd of September. So there will be some impact for 2.5 months in the current quarter also.
Hopefully within next quarter, you will be able to see that.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 11 new agency branches in Q1 FY27 on top of 100+ over 2-3 years and 34,000+ gross agent adds, but no quantified capacity plan or capex was given, so the expansion is incremental distribution rather than a defined capacity build.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Individual rated premium grew 14% with private market share at 22.2%, and agency APE grew 20% with the current quarter at 19%-plus; management reaffirmed 14-15% IRP growth for FY27.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only reaffirmed IRP growth of 14-15% and VNB margin of 26-28%; no raise was signalled, and Q1 IRP growth of 14% sits at the bottom of the range.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Individual APE grew 14% and ULIP share fell to 61% from 65%, and the 61st-month persistency dip plus opex ratio rising to 7.7% from 6.3% could pressure growth or margin if they persist.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management guided the regular-pay deferred annuity plan to launch within the next quarter, and the J&K Bank corporate agency tie-up starts in the current quarter.

rows.label: Group/GTI lumpiness drives APE mix
rows.why: Group APE rose 36% to INR53.8bn with group protection APE +313% from one large GTI contract, so the individual mix and margin recovery depend on whether group lumpiness fades.

rows.label: ULIP rider attachment rising
rows.why: Rider attachment on ULIPs is about 45-50%, up from roughly 35% 1-1.5 years ago, and management expects it to hold or improve, supporting protection mix.

rows.label: Opex ratio normalisation
rows.why: Opex ratio rose to 7.7% from 6.3% on one-off stamp duty and labour code effects; management expects normalisation over three quarters, though stamp duty tied to sum assured growth persists.

tone.note: Management was confident on IRP growth of 14-15% and the 26-28% VNB margin guide (toward upper end) but defensive on the margin decline, and evasive on quantifying the GTI drag; analysts pressed on margin normalisation and the drivers behind the lower protection growth.

540725|2026-03.headline: Share India standalone Q4 FY26 PAT rose 368% YoY to INR 75 crore on revenue of INR 383 crore (+103%).
540725|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue nearly doubled to INR 383 crore and PAT rose to INR 75 crore from INR 16 crore, with EPS of INR 17.6 versus INR 11.7. For FY26, standalone PAT rose 20% to INR 298 crore on revenue of INR 395 crore. Consolidated FY26 PAT was flat-to-down at INR 324 crore versus INR 328 crore, held back by fair value adjustments on investments held by group companies. Management pushed diversification into MTF, PMS, wealth distribution, debt (Share India Cred), AIF and commodities, while flagging RBI curbs on intraday bank limits for prop trading.

segments.name: Broking and trading (prop vs client)
segments.commentary: Prop contributed ~70% of revenue but ~49% of consolidated FY26 profit (~52% standalone). Client turnover reportedly exceeded prop turnover (53% vs 47%) for the first time; target 60% client share of turnover by year-end.

segments.name: MTF (margin trading finance)
segments.commentary: MTF book grew from INR 239 crore (FY25) to INR 424 crore (FY26); Dec-25 level was INR 457 crore. FY27 target INR 650 crore; FY28 vision also cited as INR 650 crore.

segments.name: NBFC
segments.commentary: Reported NIM of 17.64% for FY26, roughly flat with FY25; management said NIM will decline as the book shifts to secured lending.

segments.name: uTrade (algo platform)
segments.commentary: Active clients crossed 5,000 in FY26 (5,231 currently); still small in revenue, with focus on adoption. Multi-broker plan slowed by a SEBI circular requiring vendors to set up separately for each broker.

segments.name: Wealth management and PMS
segments.commentary: PMS launched in Q4 FY26 with AUM above INR 100 crore; FY27 target INR 200 crore. Third-party distribution team under Charu Sehgal to start operations in Q3. AIF CAT-3 application filed with SEBI, approval expected by end-Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Share India Cred (debt)
segments.commentary: Started operations in Q1 FY27 with six issues closed; FY27 target at least INR 500 crore of issues.

segments.name: Institutional business
segments.commentary: Institutional empanelments rose 35% from 137 to 186.

segments.name: Other subsidiaries
segments.commentary: NBFC, merchant banking, insurance and technology together contributed about 7% of FY26 bottom line. MSCI (Metropolitan Stock Exchange) cash segment doing INR 300-400 crore daily volume; Sizable stake held.

guidance_outlook: Annual EBITDA ~38% (+/-2%) and PAT margin ~22% (+/-2%) reaffirmed; management says no structural Q4 pressure.
MTF book target INR 650 crore by FY27, with mgmt saying INR 200 crore incremental is achievable if markets stay normal; deviation possible in low single digits on sentiment.
Target 30 new Tier-3 company-owned branches in next 2-3 years; 6 more targeted by FY27 year-end on top of 7 existing.
Prop share of profit targeted to fall to ~30% in three years; client share of turnover to reach 60% by FY27 year-end.
Share India Cred target INR 500 crore of issues in FY27; PMS AUM target INR 200 crore by FY27-end.
Silverleaf merger pending at NCLT; expected to conclude within about a quarter.
capex_capacity: Seven company-owned Tier-3 branches operating (Hyderabad, Indore, Bhopal, Varanasi, Agra, Raipur, Nagpur), with six more targeted by end FY27.
Target of at least INR 10-15 crore MTF per Tier-3 branch per year; 30 branches implied INR 300-500 crore.
AIF CAT-3 approval awaited from SEBI; wealth-management operations to start Q3 FY27.
Silverleaf merger pending at NCLT; post-merger plans include HFT trading.
MSCI exchange planning IPO segment, SME segment, and derivatives launch in FY27 (subject to approvals).
demand_pricing: Management said Q4 was volatile, with commodities (gold, silver, crude, natgas) driving turnover; cash ADTO rose to ~INR 2,000 crore in Q4 FY26 from ~INR 1,500 crore, and total ADTO rose to ~INR 4,500-5,000 crore from ~INR 1,400 crore in Q4 FY25 (figures as stated in call). Options were ~18% of Q4 ADTO.
MTF demand said to have risen in the last 1.5 months; Tier-3 pricing reportedly better because of less competition from sub-brokers.

RBI curbs: intraday bank limits for prop trading withdrawn; bank guarantees allowed for client business. Management estimates ~20% impact on overall deposits/limits used but minimal bottom-line effect; bank guarantees valid to 30 June can continue to expiry (up to March 2027).
SEBI market-making framework expected in 3-4 months; company is lobbying RBI for liquidity-provider relief.
Mgmt estimates INR 40,000-50,000 crore of capital to exit the market due to RBI curbs, which it expects to widen per-trade margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why do margins dip every March quarter and is that sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said Q4 was weak in FY25 and FY26 due to volatile markets; management prefers annual view with EBITDA ~38% and PAT ~22% (+/-2%). Sachin Gupta said Q4 pressure is not structural.

qa_highlights.question: Status of uTrade multi-broker plans and monetisation model?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Gupta said talks with Motilal Oswal and Dhan stalled after a SEBI circular requiring third-party vendors to set up infrastructure separately per broker, which is costly. No monetisation details were given.

qa_highlights.question: At what MTF AUM does the interest spread become meaningful, given borrowing costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said full-year borrowing costs will flow into FY27 and new NCD and third-party borrowing lines could cut costs by a few hundred basis points. Tier-3 direct branches are meant to remove mediators and lift NIM.

qa_highlights.question: Break up of brokerage vs prop income?
qa_highlights.answer: Prop contributes ~70% of revenue but ~49% of FY26 consolidated profit (52% standalone). Client turnover exceeded prop turnover for the first time (53% vs 47%).

qa_highlights.question: Impact of RBI regulation on prop business and Market Maker regime?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated ~20% impact on limits used and minimal impact on bottom line. Company sought liquidity-provider status; the company is hybrid-classified and can continue bank guarantees until expiry (up to March 2027).

qa_highlights.question: Ballpark revenue diversification in the next three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for 70% client and 30% prop share of profit over three years. Non-broking segments were ~7% of FY26 bottom line; detailed split not disclosed.

risks_watch: RBI curbs on prop intraday limits effective around 1 July 2026; watch for actual impact on prop turnover and margins versus the ~20% management estimate.
Consolidated PAT flat YoY due to fair value losses on group investments; recurrence risk.
NIM compression expected in NBFC as lending shifts to secured products; MTF book is cyclical with market sentiment.
Regulatory changes: SEBI vendor-per-broker circular hurts uTrade multi-broker plans; market-making framework still pending.
Silverleaf NCLT approval and AIF CAT-3 approval timing are uncertain.
540725|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and diversification, but defensive and hedged on the RBI prop curbs and market-dependent targets. Management repeatedly stressed that targets depend on normal markets and geopolitical stability.
key_quotes: So, the Company should be able to continue with the current margins. There is nothing like Q4 type of pressure on us.

So, hardly 20% impact in the overall limits will be there from the prop side, but on the bottom-line side, I don't think there will be much impact or there will be any impact, because per trade margin will improve.
So, MTF definitely depends on the market performance, and whatever the external reasons are, if market is performing good, demand for MTF goes up.

540725|2026-06.headline: Share India Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 48% YoY to Rs 124.41 crore on revenue of Rs 448 crore; management targets ~20% growth this year.

IRIS CARBON ARR grew 33% on disclosure-management wins and iDEAL ARR grew 17%, while SupTech added 3 new logos including the Government of Qatar. Post the TaxTech divestment, cash was about INR155 crore and net worth rose to INR200 crore from INR76 crore. Management reiterated the INR500 crore revenue aspiration and said the Middle East crisis is a watch item rather than a current drag.

540743|2026-03.headline: Godrej Agrovet Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR2,333 crore; FY27 guidance is early double-digit revenue and mid-teens PBT growth.
540743|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 9% YoY to INR2,333 crore and PBT before exceptional items rose 16.8% to INR87 crore, driven by volume growth and better mix. For FY26, revenue crossed INR10,000 crore at INR10,233 crore (+9%) and PBT before exceptionals rose 17.2% to INR569 crore. Animal Nutrition volumes grew 15% in Q4, Astec reached EBITDA break-even for the year, and Crop Care was hit by co-marketing channel inventory carry-forward. Management guided to early double-digit consolidated revenue growth and mid-teens PBT growth for FY27, with the Iran war and a weak monsoon forecast flagged as variables.

segments.name: Animal Nutrition
segments.commentary: Q4 volumes +15% YoY, well ahead of industry; cattle feed +24%. Margins expanded, helped by new Type 1 products, East and Central share gains, raw material cost reconfiguration, and a ~INR9.5 crore pet food manufacturing income booked in other income.

segments.name: Oil palm
segments.commentary: FY26 marked by record area expansion, strong volume growth and an all-time high oil extraction ratio. Q4 is seasonally weak (~60,000 t of FFB out of 6.37 lakh t annually) but margins held. Specialty fat refinery to start rolling out in May 2026.

segments.name: Crop Care
segments.commentary: Q4 hit by carry-forward of co-marketing channel inventory, lowering in-house volumes; partly offset by specialty products. FY27 is guided as a recovery year, with recovery from Q2 and very high double-digit growth in top and bottom line.

segments.name: Astec LifeSciences
segments.commentary: Achieved EBITDA break-even in FY26; Q4 revenue and EBITDA grew strongly on CDMO volumes, realisations and utilisation. FY26 mix was ~48% enterprise and ~52% CDMO; exports ~53% of revenue. Board reconstituted with Arijit Mukherjee as Executive Director.

segments.name: Creamline Dairy (CDPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~5% YoY ex bulk sales in Q4; profitability pressured by elevated milk procurement costs. Management expects milk prices to ease gradually from Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Godrej Foods
segments.commentary: EBITDA margins improved significantly in Q4 on Live Bird and Yummiez; branded revenue salience above 80% in FY26. Live Bird trading is being phased out; momos and frozen chicken entries planned.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 volume-led Animal Nutrition growth, oil palm and Astec CDMO, but cautious and evasive on the monsoon, palm oil prices and the Astec structure decision; analysts pushed on the Iran war overhang, monsoon effects and guidance sustainability.

540743|2026-06.headline: Godrej Agrovet Q1 FY27 consolidated sales rose 10% to INR2,852 crore; Crop Care fell 16.2% on delayed monsoon, while management still targets double-digit FY27 PBT growth.
540743|2026-06.overview: Consolidated sales grew 10% YoY to INR2,852 crore despite a delayed monsoon and geopolitical-driven inflation. Animal Nutrition (revenue +12.6%, reported segment result +29%) and Oil Palm (revenue +28.9%, segment result +14.4%) carried the quarter. Crop Care revenue fell 16.2% on a dry June and slower kharif sowing, and Dairy margins were squeezed by milk procurement costs and packaging inflation. Astec reached EBITDA breakeven versus an INR11 crore loss a year ago. Management reiterated FY27 double-digit consolidated PBT growth (versus earlier mid-teens guidance) but deferred a firmer view on Crop Care until end-September.

financial_highlights.change: Cattle feed volume +15%; total segment volume +7%
Segment result +14.4%; EBIT margin ~17% vs 19% a year ago (per analyst)
vs EBITDA loss of INR11 crore in Q1 FY26
Value-added share of sales 49% vs 42% a year ago

segments.name: Animal Nutrition
segments.commentary: Revenue +12.6% on robust demand and better realisations; cattle feed volume +15% and overall segment volume +7%. Poultry volumes deliberately reduced in unprofitable geographies. Cattle feed is about 55-56% of the segment; fish feed about 7%.

segments.name: Oil Palm
segments.commentary: Revenue +28.9% on higher CPO and PKO realisations and volume; FFB volumes broadly flat versus a strong early-monsoon base. Segment result +14.4%, with margin down on a pricing-formula effect that management calls one-off.

segments.name: Crop Care
segments.commentary: Revenue -16.2% as a dry June and slow kharif sowing hit cotton herbicide volumes, with margin contraction. Ashitaka and Takai together contribute about 18-20% of Q1 sales; Ghassnash soybean herbicide launched.

segments.name: Astec LifeSciences
segments.commentary: EBITDA breakeven versus an INR11 crore loss a year ago; revenue moderately lower on product mix. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of more than 20%, with an 8-9% Q1 dip to be recovered; CDMO dissilience around 50-52%.

segments.name: Dairy (CDPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue +11.4% and volume +8%, but profitability hit by elevated milk procurement prices and packaging inflation. Route-to-market reconstitution (about 18-20 months) under new CEO Gaurav is starting.

segments.name: Godrej Foods
segments.commentary: Revenue broadly stable as live bird trading is planned to fall 15-20% a year and go near zero over 3-4 years. Branded B2C (Yummiez, Real Good) volume +28% and about 32% of the Foods business; profitability hit by input costs.

segments.name: Bangladesh JV (ACI Godrej Agrovet)
segments.commentary: Returned to growth, with double-digit growth in volume, revenue and PBT.

qa_highlights.question: What FFB volume growth and EBITDA trajectory can Oil Palm deliver over 3-5 years, and what capex and returns are involved in value addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Kataria guided FFB volume growth of high single digit to early double digit over 4-5 years, targeting double digit; specialty fats refinery to start in September, with a 16-18% IRR hurdle and about 200 bps EBITDA uplift at scale. He did not give an explicit EBITDA number.

qa_highlights.question: Can Crop Care recover in H2, and is the consolidated mid-teens PBT growth still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was hit by a 40% June deficit; July is better than last year's base, and it will decide on the recovery by end-September. Consolidated growth now targeted at double digit, with the exact level to be given by end-Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Astec: revenue outlook and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Arijit Mukherjee said FY27 revenue growth is now expected at more than 20%, with the 8-9% Q1 dip to be recovered; CDMO margins intact and enterprise margin normalising as prices fall.

qa_highlights.question: Will the palm oil shift need extra capex, and what is the Foods/Dairy pricing picture?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex stays within the INR300-350 crore envelope already guided. Dairy volume grew 8% but packaging and milk costs hit margin; Foods B2C is in a 3-4 year investment phase, with live bird trading being wound down.

qa_highlights.question: How much maize inflation has Animal Nutrition passed through, and what is EBIT per tonne?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60-70% of commodity cost increases passed on; EBIT per tonne guidance held at roughly INR2,050-2,150, with Q1 EBITDA per tonne in that range or slightly higher.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Oil Palm segment margin fall from 19% to 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to a one-off pricing-formula change in the quarter and flat FFB, offset by better OER; expects margins to even out over the year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Crop Care lagging peers, and what are margins on the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is segment-mix and macro driven (cotton herbicide concentration), not share loss; new products carry lower margin than Hitweed but healthy, with total Crop Care EBIT margin seen at about 26-27%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated PBT growth: management still targets double-digit growth, narrowed from the earlier mid-teens guidance; exact position in the range to be given by end-September (end Q2).

Astec LifeSciences: FY27 revenue growth guided at more than 20% (up from the ~20% earlier guidance); Q1 revenue dip of 8-9% to be recovered in later quarters; CDMO dissilience around 50-52% for the year, with some CDMO shift from H1 to H2.
Astec enterprise margin: Q1 benefited from low-priced raw material and war-driven finished goods price increases; prices now easing, margin normalising. CDMO margins intact.

Oil Palm: FFB volume growth of high single digit to early double digit over the next 4-5 years (LRP); management says it targets double digit; full-year FFB growth guided at high single digit to double digit; margin drop expected to even out over the year.
Animal Nutrition: EBIT per tonne guidance held at roughly INR2,050-2,150 per tonne.
Crop Care: no firm FY27 numbers; recovery quantum to be assessed by end-September after cotton herbicide season. Crop Care EBIT margin expected to hold around 26-27% despite tough year.

Dairy: milk procurement prices expected to stay at current elevated levels for 2-3 quarters; packaging inflation expected to ease by August; some impact may persist in Q2; cost initiatives to be doubled down on in H2.
Godrej Foods: live bird trading to decline 15-20% a year and go near zero over 3-4 years; branded B2C to be in investment phase for 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Overall business-level capex guidance of roughly INR300-350 crore, phased over 3-4 quarters; includes the integrated palm oil complex (phase 1 started, nursery and CPO mill; seed garden in 18-24 months; refinery later) and specialty fats refinery (rollout late August/early September 2026); management says no new investment beyond this envelope.

Oil Palm area expansion: added about 17,000 hectares last year and on track to repeat this year; LRP target to take area from about 80,000 ha to about 150,000 ha, with Telangana and Northeast expansion; about 50% of plantations are juvenile (0-4 years).
New capex hurdle: IRR of around 16-18% required for new assets; management says the specialty fats downstream business, when scaled, adds roughly 200 bps to overall EBITDA profile.

Godrej Foods: investments in automation of plants and advertising behind branded B2C; NPD pipeline including chicken momos (launched about 4 months ago) and wet momos (planned in 3-4 months), and frozen chicken category push.
demand_pricing: Animal Nutrition: revenue +12.6% on demand and realisations; cattle feed volume +15%, fish feed volume up ~20%+ (about 7% of segment), cattle feed about 55-56% of segment; total segment volume +7% as poultry was deliberately cut in unprofitable geographies. Management says it passed on about 60-70% of commodity (maize) inflation.

Oil Palm: revenue +28.9% on higher CPO and PKO realisations; oil extraction ratio 18.8% vs 18.4%; FFB volume broadly flat against a strong early-monsoon base last year. Segment margin dipped on a pricing-formula change that management calls one-off.

Crop Care: revenue -16.2% on a 40% June rainfall deficit delaying sowing; cotton herbicide volume hit. Ashitaka (maize) and Takai (paddy insecticide) together 18-20% of Q1 sales; July said to be better than last year's base. risks_watch: Crop Care recovery depends on the cotton herbicide season and erratic rainfall; management will give a firm view only by end-September.
Dairy margin pressure from elevated milk procurement prices (expected to persist 2-3 quarters) and packaging costs, with some impact likely in Q2.
Oil Palm Q1 margin decline (19% to 17% EBIT) attributed to a pricing formula; watch whether H2 margin recovers as management expects.
Astec: CDMO revenue shifting from H1 into H2, and the 8-9% Q1 dip must be recovered to hit the more-than-20% FY27 target.

Godrej Foods reported top line stays near flat (1-2%) while B2C invests; profitability is pressured by input costs and the investment phase.
key_quotes: So I would say, yes, there has been a hit in the quarter 1, which has very clearly come because of this weather pattern.
Nothing crosses our bridge broadly beyond -- until we are doing an IRR of around 16% to 18%, and this meets that bridge for us.
But I think one thing we're still pretty confident of is that we'll be able to target a double -digit growth still.
We have a tight filter on this very clearly. This is a high ROCE business for us.
