540749|2026-03.headline: MAS Financial Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 25% YoY to INR104 crore, with AUM at INR15,304 crore, up 19%.
540749|2026-03.overview: Consolidated PAT for Q4 FY26 was INR104 crore versus INR83 crore a year earlier, and full-year PAT was INR379 crore, up 21%. Standalone AUM grew 18.71% and standalone PAT grew 23.39% YoY in the quarter to around INR100 crore. Standalone net Stage 3 was 1.70%, slightly better than 1.72% in December 2025, while gross Stage 3 edged up to 2.57% from 2.56%. Cost of borrowing fell 42 bps YoY to 9.39%, and management guided to 9.20-9.25% over the next two to three quarters. Credit cost was elevated because of deliberate aggressive write-offs of 90+ DPD assets, which management said were funded from profit.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Micro-enterprise loans (MEL)
segments.commentary: AUM rose about 20% to INR5,737 crore from INR4,793 crore.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - SME loans
segments.commentary: AUM grew 15.78% to INR5,213 crore from INR4,502 crore.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Two-wheeler
segments.commentary: AUM grew 35.43% to INR1,063 crore from INR785 crore; yields cited at 19-23%.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: AUM grew 11% to INR1,085 crore from INR979 crore; growth being deliberately slowed for 1-2 quarters.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Salaried personal loan
segments.commentary: AUM grew around 22% to INR1,264 crore from INR1,040 crore.

segments.name: Housing finance subsidiary
segments.commentary: AUM rose 22.41% to INR940 crore from INR768 crore; Q4 PAT INR3.70 crore vs INR2.64 crore, net Stage 3 0.68%. Management aims for INR1,000 crore, now about a quarter later than planned.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 20-25% on a sustained basis; long-term target of INR1 lakh crore AUM by 2036.
Credit cost guided at 1-1.25% of closing AUM statistically, with management indicating about 1.25-1.3% on closing AUM, and up to about 1.5% in quarters with aggressive write-offs.
Cost-to-NII guided at 35-37%; ROA after opex and credit cost targeted at 2.75-3%.
Yield range-bound at 16-17%, expected to be sustained into FY27.
Cost of borrowing guided to fall from 9.39% to around 9.20-9.25% over the next 2-3 quarters.
Branch additions of 30-35 planned in FY27 after a year of consolidating existing branches.
Dividend: final dividend INR0.75 per share, total INR2 per share for FY26, about 10% payout.
Capital adequacy to be maintained at around 20%; debt tie-up for about half of FY27 done, full-year tie-up expected soon.
capex_capacity: More than 200 branches and about 16,500 centres; branch network to grow by 30-35 in FY27.
Average cash and cash equivalent balance of about INR1,000 crore plus unutilised cash credit of over INR200 crore.
Cash credit facility of about INR1,500 crore across 14 banks, utilised at 70-75%.
Sanctioned facilities over INR2,000 crore as of 31 March (term loans, NCDs, direct assignment, co-lending).
Term loan sanctioned pipeline of about INR1,300 crore; INR750 crore term loan raised in Q4 at 3-5 year tenor; INR100 crore NCDs raised in Q4.
Direct assignment of INR940 crore executed in Q4; a further INR500 crore+ of direct assignment and co-lending sanctions to be used in the current quarter.
demand_pricing: Direct sourcing is about 64% of the book; fintech partnerships are about 10% of business.
Yield rose about 40 bps sequentially, attributed to fintech mix and 2-wheeler growth; SME yields were also higher.
Management said assignment income is amortised, not upfront, and the NII rise was mainly from lower borrowing cost and the MCLR reset.
Standalone 90+ write-offs were aggressive in FY26 (more than 0.10% of assets), mostly unsecured per management.
Caution list added petrol pumps, gas agencies, transporters and some chemical industries in Feb-March 2026, alongside textile and agro, due to West Asia supply concerns.
Management reported no slowdown in disbursement growth as of the call.

qa_highlights.question: How is MAS using data and AI for risk-adjusted growth, and what early warning systems exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it back-tests risk models on its own repayment experience, not generic bureau scores; it moved from LOS to business rule engines and plans AI-based risk management after 6-9 months. Field checks included more than 2,000-3,000 commercial vehicle borrowers after the Middle East crisis, plus bounce data from 100% bank or e-NACH collections.

qa_highlights.question: Will the West Asia crisis and inflation affect lending and asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said asset quality should hold but is being watched closely; it is growing CV more slowly as an energy- and logistics-linked precaution. Disbursement growth has not slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for cost of borrowing and the Q4 cost of borrowing trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of borrowing is 9.39% and is expected to fall to 9.20-9.25% over 2-3 quarters. Q4 interest expense was about INR222 crore vs INR219 crore in Q3, with the MCLR reset adding to NII.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the origination and fee cost high, and what is driving opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the fees and commission depend on product structure. Fintech partners get the spread as commission, and yields rose about 0.5%. Opex is judged against ROA, not in isolation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise and what is the normalised level?
qa_highlights.answer: The rise was from deliberate write-offs of 90+ DPD assets, not stress. Normal credit cost is 1-1.25% of closing AUM; 1.5% is possible in quarters with aggressive write-offs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is CV growth slow, and what is the write-off and recovery policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is slowing CV growth for 1-2 quarters due to logistics and transport risk. Write-offs occur after 360 days across all products; recoveries are credited to P&L net.

risks_watch: Rising inflation and energy costs from the West Asia crisis could hit logistics, transport and fuel-linked MSMEs.
Credit cost is a function of aggressive write-off policy; quarterly credit costs could run towards 1.5%.
Pricing may need to be passed on to borrowers if borrowing costs fall, which could compress the yield gain.
Housing finance subsidiary's INR1,000 crore AUM target now slips about a quarter.
Debt tie-up for FY27 is only about half complete; rate reduction depends on market conditions.
Gross Stage 3 is at 2.57%, up slightly QoQ.
540749|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth and profitability, with a clear 20-25% AUM growth target. Cautious on the macro, with CV growth slowed and sector caution lists expanded. Management was less direct on the split of NII growth and on the detail of the write-off strategy.
key_quotes: And on the asset side, we continue to have the confidence to grow anywhere between 20% to 25%, given the positive macro situation because we always prioritize risk management and profitability over just the growth.
So, we are at a striking distance away from INR1,000 crores.
We have cash credit facility of approximately INR1500 crore spread over 14 banks, of which we maintain utilization level of around 70 %-75%, keeping the remaining portion as liquidity buffer.
So, we do not upfront income in order to improve the profitability or the NII growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Cost of borrowing falling 14-19 bps (9.39% to 9.20-9.25%) with yields held at 16-17% should widen spread, though pass-through to borrowers and higher credit cost offset part of the gain.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management plans 30-35 branch additions in FY27 on a base of more than 200 branches and about 16,500 centres, after a year of consolidation; no utilisation figure was given, so this is a planned branch rollout rather than capacity stress.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM growth is guided at 20-25% sustained, consolidated AUM is up about 19% to INR15,304 crore, and disbursement growth showed no slowdown as of the call, with INR500 crore+ of assignment and co-lending sanctions queued for the current quarter.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed as a balance-sheet event; the branch rollout is opex-led and utilisation is not disclosed, so no new capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Cost of borrowing is guided down from 9.39% to 9.20-9.25% over 2-3 quarters, which supports NII, but pricing may be passed on to borrowers and the yield is held at 16-17%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Credit cost is guided at 1-1.25% of closing AUM but could run to about 1.5% in quarters with aggressive write-offs, and gross Stage 3 edged up to 2.57% from 2.56%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or model launch was discussed; the two-wheeler and SME lines are existing growth segments.

rows.label: Debt tie-up for FY27 about half complete
rows.why: Debt tie-up for about half of FY27 is done with full-year tie-up expected soon; the INR750 crore Q4 term loan and INR1,300 crore term-loan pipeline support the 20-25% AUM target, but rate relief depends on market conditions.

rows.label: Caution list expansion and CV growth slowdown
rows.why: CV AUM grew only 11% to INR1,085 crore and growth is being deliberately slowed for 1-2 quarters, with petrol pumps, transporters and other sectors added to the caution list due to West Asia supply concerns.

rows.label: Housing finance subsidiary to reach INR1,000 crore AUM
rows.when: about one quarter later than planned
rows.why: Housing AUM grew 22.41% to INR940 crore with Q4 PAT of INR3.70 crore vs INR2.64 crore, so the INR1,000 crore target is close and now slips about a quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident on 20-25% AUM growth, cost of borrowing falling to 9.20-9.25% and ROA of 2.75-3%, and cautious on the West Asia macro, CV slowdown and credit cost at up to 1.5% from aggressive write-offs; analysts pressed on opex, origination fees and the write-off and recovery policy.

540749|2026-06.headline: MAS Financial Q1 FY27: consolidated AUM up 21% to INR16,100 crores and PAT up 27% to INR110 crores; credit cost guided 1.25%-1.75%.
540749|2026-06.overview: Consolidated AUM grew about 21% YoY to INR16,100 crores and PAT rose about 27% to INR110 crores, with standalone PAT up 25% to INR105 crores. Asset quality was stable, with standalone GNPA at 2.58% and NNPA at 1.70%, flat QoQ, and a management overlay of INR17.60 crores held. Borrowing cost fell 55 bps YoY to 9.25%, while credit cost rose to about 1.6% of AUM, which management attributed to higher on-book mix, a 5 bps rise in Stage 1/2 provisioning and prudent write-offs. Management reiterated 20-25% AUM growth guidance, with the call leaning toward the upper end for FY27.

segments.name: MEL (Micro/MSME loans)
segments.commentary: Book grew 23% from INR5,009 crores to INR6,153 crores; MEL is about 77% of loan book combined with SME.

segments.name: SME loans
segments.commentary: Grew 21% from INR4,526 crores to INR5,485 crores.

segments.name: Two-wheeler loans
segments.commentary: Grew 19% from INR872 crores to INR1,039 crores; management said Q1 is seasonally muted, with festive Q3/Q4 stronger.

segments.name: Commercial vehicle (used CV)
segments.commentary: Grew 13% from INR967 crores to INR1,096 crores; eligible demand softer on fuel-cost-driven credit tightening, with growth push deferred 1-2 quarters.

segments.name: Salaried personal loans
segments.commentary: Grew 21% from INR1,131 crores to INR1,374 crores; about 9% of the loan book.

segments.name: Housing finance subsidiary
segments.commentary: AUM INR976 crores, GS3 0.98% and NS3 0.68%; PBT up 62% to INR5.70 crores; average yield about 14%, credit cost about 0.5%. Expansion into Tamil Nadu and Karnataka starts this quarter.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance maintained at 20-25%, with management saying the full year is very likely to be at the higher end of the range.
Credit cost to stay in a 1.25%-1.75% range, depending on product mix; management pointed to commercial vehicles as high-yield, high-loss.
ROA target of 2.75%-3.25%, with an aspiration of 3%+.
Net interest margin target of 8%-8.5% on a 7%-7.5% spread; incremental borrowing cost 9.2%-9.25%, expected to stay stable (9.2%-9.3% per Q&A).
Direct distribution share (currently 66%-67%) expected to reach 70%-72% in 1-1.5 years; off-book target kept at 20-25% of AUM.
Used CV growth expected to pick up only after 1-2 quarters; housing finance AUM expected to inch up in the next few quarters.
Credit rating upgrade being pursued, timing not given; sub-9% borrowing cost called far-fetched in the next 1-2 quarters.
capex_capacity: Distribution of 16,500 centres through 209 branches, with more than 200 NBFC partners providing about 33% of originations; direct share 67%.
Employee count reduced by 380 in Q1 due to technology adoption; no quantified headcount target given.
In-house tech team of close to 100 people; LOS live for all products, with BRE added and straight-through processing improving.
Branches opened after March 2024 expected to mature (sweat) by 2027-28 or earlier.
demand_pricing: Standalone MSME/SME demand stable across manufacturing and trading; eligible demand fell in Q1 due to tighter credit screens on energy-dependent sectors (restaurants, gas-dependent manufacturing, export businesses).
Used CV demand robust, but eligible demand lower because of fuel-cost tightening.
Two-wheeler Q1 degrowth QoQ attributed to seasonality; monsoon and Gujarat floods flagged as temporary and not expected to cause major stress.
Working capital demand rising for some businesses on higher input costs; underwriting parameters also tightened.
Write-offs were INR29 crores in March and INR19 crores in June, offset by higher ECL provisioning, keeping impairment cost flat QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise from about 1.2-1.3% to about 1.6% of AUM despite the microfinance impact and Q4 write-offs last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher on-book assets (on-book up 8.25% QoQ vs AUM up 5.5%), which added INR6-7 crores of Stage 1/2 provisioning from a 5 bps rise to 0.7%. Prudent write-offs and mix shift toward higher-yield commercial vehicles also contributed; ROA not affected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20-25% growth guidance at risk given the West Asia conflict and energy-linked stress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said energy-dependent segments were tightened early and stress was limited; eligible demand fell in Q1 and Q2 but normalised, and guidance is expected to hold with the upper end targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Will borrowing cost fall further from 9.25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to predict and depends on RBI and liquidity; the target is to stabilise at 9.2%-9.3%, with a credit rating upgrade being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the Stage 1/2 provisioning increase and whether there are macro-related buffers?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage 1/2 provisioning rose to 0.7% from 0.65%, adding INR6-7 crores; management described it as a buffer.

qa_highlights.question: What was the nature of the INR10 crore OCPS redemption in the subsidiary MRHMFL?
qa_highlights.answer: The OCPS was refunded to the parent because the housing subsidiary's CRAR exceeded 37% and it did not need the capital.

qa_highlights.question: Why did off-book share fall and what is the housing finance growth plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Off-book is dynamic and chosen by price; target stays at 20-25%. Housing finance plans to expand into Tamil Nadu and Karnataka from Q1, with results expected in Q3-Q4.

risks_watch: Used CV: eligible demand softer on fuel-cost-driven credit tightening; management says growth push is 1-2 quarters away, and CV is high-yield, high-loss, so credit cost direction depends on mix.

Credit cost: rose to about 1.6% of AUM from about 1.2-1.3% a year earlier; management guides a 1.25%-1.75% range and Stage 1/2 provisioning went to 0.7% from 0.65% (INR6-7 crores), which management calls a buffer.
Energy-linked and West Asia stress: eligible demand fell in Q1 and Q2 and management says it has normalised; the next quarter will show whether this holds.
Borrowing cost: 9.25% average with incremental cost at 9.2%-9.3%; a sub-9% level is called far-fetched in the next 1-2 quarters, and the credit rating upgrade has no timing.

Off-book share fell below the 20%-25% target this quarter; management says it is opportunistic and the target is unchanged. Gujarat floods and monsoon effects on two-wheeler and collections are still unquantified.
key_quotes: So, very high possibility, yes. We are working on that quite optimistic. Can't predict, but you are thinking on the right lines.
So, that is the impact which translates to roughly around between INR5 crores to INR7 crores in provisioning.
Difficult to comment right now because the cost of borrowing is dependent on the macro situation.

540750|2026-03.headline: IEX Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 10.8% YoY to INR 129.8 crore on record 39.4 billion units traded volume.
540750|2026-03.overview: IEX delivered record quarterly electricity volume of 39.4 billion units (up 24.3% YoY) and consolidated revenue of INR 196.4 crore (up 12.5%), with PAT up 10.8% to INR 129.8 crore. Full-year PAT rose 14.9% to INR 492.9 crore and a final dividend of INR 2 per share was declared. Exchange prices fell sharply on higher sell-side liquidity (DAM down 12.2% YoY in Q4), and other income dropped about 29% sequentially-adjusted per analyst, attributed to treasury mark-to-market losses in March. Market coupling (CERC draft of April 17, 2026 naming Grid India as MCO, comments till May 16) is the dominant overhang, with management disputing its benefit. Gas exchange (IGX) volumes fell 8% in Q4 on Middle East supply disruption and management expects no growth in Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: INR 2 per share (200% of face value)

segments.name: Electricity - DAM/RTM
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 DAM price averaged INR 3.89/unit (down 12.2% YoY) and RTM INR 3.68/unit (down 15%) as DAM sell-bids rose about 49%. RTM was 39% of electricity volumes in FY26 (55 billion units, up about 41%).

segments.name: Green market (G-DAM)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 green volume rose 26.5% to 2.4 billion units; FY26 volume 10.8 billion units (+23%).

segments.name: Renewable energy certificates (REC)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 RECs traded 71.7 lakh (+6% YoY); FY26 187 lakh (+5%).

segments.name: IGX (gas exchange)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume down 8% on Middle East supply disruption; FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu (+28%); Q4 PAT INR 9.4 crore (+5.4%). Exchange holds about 3% of India's gas consumption and 20% of spot market.

segments.name: ICX (I-REC)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 issued 46 lakh I-RECs (+29% YoY); FY26 179 lakh (over +200%). Q4 revenue INR 2.2 crore; FY26 INR 7.7 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management expects electricity volume growth of 15-20% annually to continue in FY27, dependent on demand-supply conditions.
IGX gas volumes expected flat YoY in Q1 FY27 and to grow from Q2 FY27 if Middle East supply normalises.
Coal exchange: draft Coal Regulations 2025 out; final regulations expected later in calendar 2026; board gave in-principle approval to explore setting up a coal exchange.
Management says market coupling would add no value and cost Grid India extra; IEX says it would absorb software changes at no extra cost.
Buyback under consideration; SEBI has not finalised the mechanism, and the company is awaiting SEBI's open-market route draft.
capex_capacity: IGX IPO process has been initiated; management says it is progressing well but did not give status detail.
PNGRB has given IGX until December 31, 2026 to complete the stake reduction.
Pending CERC approvals: TAM extension to 11 months, green RTM petition (reserved), and peak DAM/peak RTM segments for merchant storage (reserved).
BESS: 13 GW under first VGF tranche underway; about three-quarters of the 30 GW second tranche awarded.
SECI 500 MW / 3-hour RE CfD pilot (1,500 MWh/day), backed by a INR 76 crore stabilisation fund; applies to battery capacity per management.
demand_pricing: DAM sell liquidity rose about 44% for FY26; FY26 DAM average INR 3.86/unit (down about 14%) and RTM INR 3.59/unit (down 16%).
More than 70% of cleared volume is now through the API system; management says over 5,000 industrial consumers use the platform.
Management says exchange customer count is rising and no customers have been lost to rival exchanges since the July 2025 coupling order.
Management sees the TAM segment (uniform liquidity across three exchanges) as evidence that transaction fees (about INR 0.036-0.037/unit) would hold up under coupling.
VPPA interest is currently limited, per management; data centres and multinationals could add demand later.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall about 29% versus the recent quarterly run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vineet Harlalka said the December quarter included a one-time treasury gain, and March saw mark-to-market losses from the Iran conflict and rupee weakness. He expects the numbers to recover as markets recover.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the final PMR and market coupling procedure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot estimate; PMR 2021 was notified in February 2021 after a 2019 draft, and the regulator will consider comments and market redesign.

qa_highlights.question: Would IEX lose volumes and margins if market coupling goes through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customer loyalty and value-added services would retain share; cited TAM margins holding at about INR 0.036-0.037/unit despite shared liquidity. No additional software cost is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is RTM coupling feasible, given 48 auctions a day?
qa_highlights.answer: Management doubts RTM coupling is feasible: it would move from 48 to 288 five-minute blocks with no slack time, and an aggregation failure at one exchange could cause price jerks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the buyback stance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said a buyback is a good option after the revised tax structure; the company is considering it and awaiting SEBI's open-market route decision.

qa_highlights.question: Will electricity volume growth continue in FY27 and why did REC volumes fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 15-20% volume growth. On RECs, management said there was no fall: REC volume rose 5% in FY26.

risks_watch: Market coupling: CERC draft (April 17, 2026) names Grid India as MCO; comments close May 16, 2026, and the timeline for final rules is unknown.
Gas exchange volumes weak in Q1 FY27 on Middle East supply disruption and high gas prices.
Treasury and other income volatility from mark-to-market swings (other income fell in Q4).
Continued DAM/RTM price decline (down 12-15% YoY in Q4) could pressure fee income if volumes do not offset.
Pending CERC approvals (TAM 11-month extension, green RTM, peak DAM/RTM) and the legal challenge to market coupling.

540750|2026-06.headline: IEX Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose about 12% to Rs 134.8 crore on Rs 202.8 crore revenue, with electricity volume up 16% to 37.5 billion units.
540750|2026-06.overview: IEX reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of Rs 202.8 crore and PAT of Rs 134.8 crore, up about 12% YoY, on electricity volume of 37.5 billion units (+16%). Real-Time Market growth was the main driver, with RTM up about 25% in Q1 and its share of mix reaching about 34% last year. Management used the analyst meet to push a set of new products (Green RTM, peak contracts, 11-month TAM, carbon trading, coal exchange) while pushing back on CERC's proposed market coupling and the Day-Ahead Market pilot, which it has challenged at APTEL and the Supreme Court. The call was mostly a policy and product narrative; no formal FY27 guidance was given.

segments.name: Electricity (DAM / RTM / TAM)
segments.commentary: RTM is now roughly the size of DAM; DAM share of mix fell from 95% in FY16 to about 39%, RTM rose to about 34% in FY26, and RTM is up about 25% in Q1 FY27. Term-Ahead Market and Green Market are about 7-8% of the mix.

segments.name: IGX (gas exchange, associate)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu and PAT Rs 42 crore; Q1 FY27 volume 27.5 million MMBtu and PAT Rs 16 crore. DRHP filed for IPO of a 22.3% stake to bring IEX's 47.3% holding down to 25% under PNGRB rules, after a one-year extension.

segments.name: ICX (I-REC / environmental)
segments.commentary: Sole I-REC issuer in India; management cited about 200% growth in I-REC volumes last year. Q1 REC volumes were down sharply YoY, which management attributed to the first quarter and possible RPO buy-out confusion.

segments.name: Indian Coal Exchange (new)
segments.commentary: Incorporated as a separate company in June 2026; coal rules notified 4 June 2026 require e-auction and marketplace trades to move to exchanges within six months of launch. Market size cited at about 120 million tonnes today, with a target of at least 100 million tonnes in year one.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 volume or revenue guidance given; management expects RTM volumes to grow about 25-30% a year.
Management expects carbon credit trading to begin in FY27, with BEE targeting 1 October 2026.

Management expects the Green RTM, peak-power contracts (DAM and RTM) and 11-month TAM products to be approved by CERC; timing was not committed, and the 11-month TAM application has been pending for over two years.
Management sees the exchange-routed share of electricity rising to about 25% over five to six years, against about 14-15% short-term market today.
Management said it would consider a buyback in future, citing SEBI's revised market-buyback rules.
Management said the coal exchange's fee should exceed those of MSTC and M-Junction, since exchanges perform price discovery, clearing and settlement.
capex_capacity: Management cited about 80 GW of thermal capacity in the pipeline, 41 GW under construction with PPAs signed, 20 GW awarded, and 16 GW in planning; most is expected in FY31-FY33.
Management said it has built a hot standby for RTM and a DC-to-DR switch; both were positioned as ready for the proposed 5-minute bidding window.

BESS merchant capacity cited: ACME about 3,200 MWh, Juniper about 500 MWh, Adani about 3,400 MWh, with more than Rs 9,000 crore of BESS VGF support. Management said the arbitrage window may last 3-5 years.
The SECI 500 MW CfD pilot for peak power was cited as launched; it is a peak-power product, not solar.
demand_pricing: Management expects demand growth of about 5-5.5% a year, versus 11% in Q1 FY27 on heat and delayed monsoon. Peak demand touched about 271 GW in May and July.
Management said exchanges as a group grew 18% in FY26 against 1% demand growth.

On market coupling, CERC proposed Grid India as Market Coupling Operator, with DAM first. Management said it has challenged the July 2025 order at APTEL (order dated 13 February 2026) and is now before the Supreme Court; a second hearing was held on 27 July 2026.
Management said that even after coupling, DAM share could fall 20-40%, but said business impact would not be significant. The market-share loss figure is management's own estimate.
Management said top-10 sellers account for about 40% of the sell side and the top-buyer concentration is 50-60%, with 800-900 participants daily.

Management cited an RTM realisation issue in a Q&A: an analyst's per-unit realisation calculation (about 0.4 paisa vs 3.7 paisa a year earlier) was not reconciled; management pointed to incentives in REC and TAM.

financial_highlights.change: about 11% QoQ per management; YoY not stated

qa_highlights.question: What RTM share of the mix to expect over the next 3-5 years, and what could be the next star product after RTM (peak contracts, Green RTM, BESS)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RTM has grown about 30-35% CAGR since 2020 and expects RTM volumes to keep growing 25-30% a year, possibly exceeding DAM volumes over time; it named BESS as a potential next growth product. No numeric RTM share target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will IEX pursue a buyback given low valuations, and can IEX shareholders get a reservation in the IGX IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an IGX IPO reservation for IEX shareholders is not really possible as it is an independent IPO. It said a buyback will be considered in future, since SEBI has revised the rules for market buybacks.

qa_highlights.question: Why has RTM grown to near DAM size in India, unlike in Europe where DAM dominates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to 25-year PPAs covering about 85% of DISCOM demand, with DAM used for seasonal and daily shortfalls and RTM used to handle renewable variability; it said PPAs will persist because banks lend only against them.

qa_highlights.question: How far can exchange share of electricity grow given long-term PPAs dominate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exchange-routed share could reach about 25% of generation in five to six years, versus about 14-15% in the short-term market today, as bilateral and trader transactions shrink.

qa_highlights.question: Who bears the cost of Grid India as Market Coupling Operator, and will MCO fees force IEX to cut fees?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all costs are ultimately passed to consumers, directly or indirectly, and that cost allocation and fee questions are among the open issues Grid India has raised with CERC; no timeline or answer was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the likely timeline for final market coupling regulations, and what is the expected DAM market-share loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a timeline, citing the need to examine software, settlement and reliability, and compared it to availability-based tariff taking years. On share loss, management said it sees no material loss given customer integration, though it earlier estimated DAM share could fall 20-40%.

qa_highlights.question: Does the market coupling challenge affect CERC approval of the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Goel said the legal challenge is against the order, not CERC, and that regulators and government are aligned on peak power products. He said delays are due to procedural hurdles and the products will be released over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did REC volumes fall about 80% YoY and QoQ, and why is standalone realisation per unit down sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is early in the year and that a draft allowing RPO buy-out has created market confusion, which will lift REC volumes once clarified. On realisation, management pointed to incentives in REC and Term-Ahead Market and did not reconcile the 0.4 paisa vs 3.7 paisa comparison.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-duration 11-month Term-Ahead contract timeline, given the application is over two years old?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is difficult to say when approval will come, as CERC is reviewing performance of the existing 3-month contracts and standardising longer contracts, and that contracts beyond 3 months are currently not significant in volume.

qa_highlights.question: How does the 0.3% social welfare gain claim and DAM coupling risk relate to customer concentration, and what is the buyer/seller concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said top-10 sellers account for about 40% of the sell side, buyer concentration is about 50-60% of volume, and 800-900 participants trade daily; it said concentration on the buy side has been falling.

qa_highlights.question: Why are sell bids in daytime far above cleared volumes, and is solar being curtailed in the exchange?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit said about 10,000-12,000 MW clears in daytime, of which solar is only about 2,000-3,000 MW, and curtailment is mainly thermal, not solar; solar has not reached the stage of curtailment on the exchange.

qa_highlights.question: How long will BESS arbitrage last and are two cycles per year feasible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two cycles are possible on 100-150 days, mainly in winter, and that arbitrage may last 3-5 years, with no definitive model; it cited FY26 arbitrage of Rs 4.81 per cycle versus Rs 5.03 in FY25 and Rs 3.80 in FY24.

risks_watch: Timing of CERC approval for Green RTM, peak power contracts and 11-month TAM; orders reserved, and the 11-month TAM application has been pending over two years.
Market coupling: Supreme Court hearing (second hearing 27 July 2026), Grid India's objections to MCO design, and management's own 20-40% DAM share-loss estimate.
Proposed RTM window cut from 15 to 5 minutes and gate closure from 75 to 50 minutes, which could reduce liquidity or affect bidding systems.
Q1 FY27 REC volume decline and a draft RPO buy-out rule that could change REC demand; realisation per unit fell sharply in the analyst's calculation and was not reconciled.
Coal exchange: registration and licensing under way, six-month transition away from e-auction, and competition from MSTC and M-Junction; fee levels not yet set.
IGX IPO (22.3% stake sale) and PNGRB stake dilution from 47.3% to 25%; IGX Q1 PAT of Rs 16 crore needs to hold.
key_quotes: And I am sure with the kind of trust which we have built over the years in these last 18 years, we should be able to retain significant market share even in the Day-Ahead Market.
So, as far as business is concerned, I do not think it is going to be significant.
So, it will be difficult for me to give any timeline on this , I can only tell you one thing that sometime in 1994-95 when availability--based tariff was first discussed in the country.
The IGX IPO is an independent IPO, but buyback, yes definitely, we will consider it in future because now SEBI also has revised its rules for doing the buyback through the market.
540750|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth drivers, RTM and BESS arbitrage, and the view that market coupling will have limited business impact. Noticeably cautious and non-committal on timelines for CERC approvals, market coupling regulations, the 11-month TAM contract, and the buyback, and openly declined several numeric questions.

540755|2026-03.headline: GIC Re FY26 profit after tax rose 25.23% to INR8,392.18 crores, with combined ratio down 2.79 points to 106.02%.
540755|2026-03.overview: GIC Re reported FY26 gross premium of INR44,006.74 crores, up from INR41,153.95 crores, and PAT of INR8,392.18 crores. Q4 PAT rose to INR2,254.24 crores from INR2,182.88 crores, while Q4 investment income fell to INR3,059.46 crores from INR3,903.02 crores. Management said the global market is moving from hardening to a competitive phase, with April 1 domestic renewals and January 1 international renewals showing price pressure. Management guided to a 1-2 point combined ratio improvement in FY27 and expects low single-digit growth.

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Accounts for 75% of FY26 gross premium (INR32,979.23 crores). Domestic combined ratio was cited at around 101-102%, an improvement of roughly 250 bps versus FY25 per an analyst's reading; property is about 30% of the domestic book.

segments.name: International business
segments.commentary: FY26 gross premium of INR11,027.51 crores. Motor international is shrinking due to pruning (US contract ended; Israel and Turkey proportional treaties reduced), with claims running off more slowly than premium. Property results improving since it has no long tail.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: About 83% of motor portfolio is domestic and about 60% of that domestic portion is obligatory. Domestic motor growth came from additional domestic treaties; international motor premium has degrown over three years.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: More than 99% domestic. Proportional treaties; some reserve strengthening under way, results described as fairly stable. Management is cautious on government schemes.

segments.name: Fire
segments.commentary: Q4 fire premium decline of around 20% was attributed to international portfolio; management said the quarter alone may not reflect the full year. Domestic fire will not grow at April 1 renewals.

guidance_outlook: FY27 combined ratio targeted to improve by 1-2 percentage points year-on-year; management said it would prefer to hold or improve on the FY26 106% level.
FY27 growth expected to be low single-digit; management said it would not chase premium in a soft market.
Obligatory share of 4% declared for GIC Re for FY26-27; management flagged possible glide-path pressure on obligatory share over time.
Solvency will be used for impending RBC and IFRS transitions; dividend payout raised to 13.25%, about 32.5% higher than earlier.
capex_capacity: Solvency ratio improved to 4.21 at year-end from 3.70, which management said supports capital deployment and the RBC and IFRS transitions.
Net worth excluding fair value change grew to INR51,301.27 crores from INR43,106.52 crores.
demand_pricing: April 1 domestic renewals were pressured by competition and softening fire pricing; GIC Re used reinsurance levers (proportional structures) so the first impact is borne by insurers. Contracts above a threshold were declined.

Cell prices expected to stay firm through at least Q3 FY27 due to BESS demand; mitigation via pre-booking long lead-time orders.
Nepal: about 100+ three-wheeler units shipped or in process; African markets (Tanzania, Ethiopia) at exploratory stage.
HCV deployments: about 22 trucks at Welspun's Anjar port, plus single-digit deployments at Vizag and Chennai ports, and Wonder Cement at Tuna and Dahej ports.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further price hikes from customers to offset steel-driven margin compression in Engineering and MFP, or is Q1 profitability the underlying run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said steel increases from Q4 and Q1 are recovered with a 2-3 quarter lag and expects margin neutralisation in coming quarters; it declined to quantify the Q1 under-recovery but reiterated double-digit EBIT margin growth guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the steel under-recovery be recovered cumulatively, not just passed through with lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed: steel price increases including Q1 will be fully recovered.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in MFP to drive 11.5% revenue growth, given railways was a drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was volume-led with no price recovery yet; railways remained a drag and the Hyundai-dependent unit was weak, while a western region greenfield plant is delayed by six months.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly Rs 40-50 Cr reduction in e-mobility negative EBIT, and is this one-off?

qa_highlights.question: Are e-mobility losses past peak and what are breakeven timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Directionally yes, losses are past peak if volumes keep rising QoQ; one business expected to break even this year and two more in the next financial year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is three-wheeler billing (1,924 in Q1) above Vahan registrations?
qa_highlights.answer: Billing-to-registration lag of 30-45 days; FY26 billing was about 6,700 vs Vahan about 6,500, and Q4 billing was only about 1,200 due to a supply-link issue. Numbers tend to tally within 3-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: How much standalone capital will be infused into new ventures in FY27?

qa_highlights.question: How will non-steel inflation (fuel, freight) from the West Asia crisis be recovered, and when will margins normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Discussions with OEMs on non-steel recovery have started; an update is expected in about a quarter, and management is hopeful most of it will be recovered.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the cycles margin expansion and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Strong Q1 seasonality (schools and colleges reopening) and higher market share; management targets about 2 more basis points (likely percentage points) of improvement, with about 5% margin as the current target.

qa_highlights.question: What is Orange Koi, and what is the plan?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jayem outlook, and are its batteries for captive use?

qa_highlights.question: What are group capex plans excluding CG Power?

qa_highlights.question: What is the structure and timing of external investors in TI Clean Mobility?
qa_highlights.answer: Three external investors hold CCPS that convert only at IPO, with no fixed timeline; stake will be set by valuation at that time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demand outlook and export share for Engineering?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand expected to stay bullish for one or two quarters barring geopolitical disruption; exports grew at double-digit rates and are about 14% of TI revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cell supply and price outlook for Clean Mobility?
qa_highlights.answer: Cell prices expected to stay firm at least through Q3 FY27 due to BESS demand; mitigation via pre-booking long lead-time orders and locking prices.

540768|2026-03.headline: Mahindra Logistics returned to profit in Q4 FY26, with reported PAT of INR20.2 crores versus a INR6.7 crores loss a year earlier.
540768|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14% YoY to INR1,791 crores and gross margin expanded to 10.5% from 9.5%. Adjusted EBITDA (after deducting long-term lease rent) rose to INR57 crores, a 3.2% margin versus 2.4% a year earlier. Full-year reported PAT was INR2.3 crores against a INR35.8 crores loss in FY25, after a Q3 exceptional gratuity charge under the new Labour Codes. Express (MESPL) remained EBITDA-negative for FY26 but gross-margin positive for the full year and close to EBITDA breakeven per management. Freight forwarding faces West Asia-related headwinds going into FY27.

segments.name: Contract Logistics
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR1,381 crores (+12% YoY); FY26 revenue INR5,490 crores (+16%) and reported EBITDA INR389 crores (+24% vs INR314 crores). Management cites gross margin growth of 19% in Q4 from exiting non-profitable customers.

segments.name: Express (MESPL)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 49% YoY; FY26 revenue INR449 crores (+25%), gross margin 1.3% for the full year. Quarterly GM rose from INR20 lakh in Q2 to INR2.7 crores in Q3 and INR6.6 crores in Q4. FY26 EBITDA loss INR31 crores vs INR51 crores loss in FY25.

segments.name: Freight Forwarding
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR89 crores (+17% YoY); gross margin +50% YoY. FY26 revenue grew 14%, EBITDA INR10.1 crores vs INR6.8 crores in FY25. Q4 growth is now facing West Asia-related headwinds.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR386 crores (+22% vs INR316 crores). Q4 revenue grew 42% YoY and gross margin 17% YoY; growth driven by large B2B accounts, with utilisation improvement a focus on the asset-heavy Alyte Prive premium offering in Delhi.

segments.name: Last-mile delivery
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR72 crores (-18% YoY, from INR89 crores) after deliberate site exits. Gross margin rose to INR6.5 crores in Q4 from INR2.7 crores in Q3; EBITDA moved from a INR1 crore loss in Q3 to a INR2.2 crore profit in Q4.

Express: management said it will invest in technology in FY27 after two years of limited tech investment.

capex_capacity: White space reduced by 3 lakh sq ft in Q4 and 9 lakh sq ft in FY26; contract logistics warehousing footprint fell from about 20.4 million sq ft in Q3 to about 19 million sq ft in Q4 per analyst data.

Management said a diesel price rise of 10-15% would be passed through to customers 100% with no lag, but flagged possible macro inflation impact.
Consolidated e-commerce and quick-commerce revenue exceeds INR1,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is Express volume growth, and can it sustain mid-teens revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Express volume growth is mid-to-high teens YoY, and that a mid-teens revenue growth target is achievable. Volume is no longer disclosed alone as it is not a sufficient metric without yield.

qa_highlights.question: Is adjusted EBITDA margin likely to surpass the pre-Ind AS FY18-19 levels of about 3.6-3.9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it agreed directionally but gave no forward guidance and said the turnaround has only just started.

qa_highlights.question: When will Express reach EBITDA breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA breakeven is the immediate goal and it is 'very close', but gave no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further last-mile pruning or declines to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all last-mile pruning was done in FY26 and the business is now expected to grow with profitable clients.

qa_highlights.question: Are there similar receivable provisions expected? What drove the INR28 crore credit provision?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the provision reflects prudence on aged receivables under management judgment. She said nothing similar warrants provisioning at present.

qa_highlights.question: Is the West Asia conflict affecting other segments, and how would a fuel price spike affect the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only Freight Forwarding is affected so far; other segments are on plan. A 10-15% diesel rise would be passed through immediately, but management flagged broader economic inflation risk.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Express industry yield, and what share of Express revenue is e-commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share industry-level yield comparisons or the e-commerce share of Express revenue, citing competitive sensitivity.

540768|2026-06.headline: Mahindra Logistics swung to Q1 FY27 PAT of INR 25.4 crore from a INR 10.8 crore loss, with consolidated revenue up 23% to INR 2,003 crore.

Adjusted (Ind AS 116) EBITDA was INR 57 crore, up 76% YoY, at 2.8% margin. PAT of INR 25.4 crore includes INR 4 crore of interest on income tax refund, so operating PAT was about INR 21.4 crore. Contract Logistics gross margin was diluted YoY by start-up costs, manpower shortages and minimum wage revisions, while the Express business reached a positive gross margin and narrower EBITDA loss.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Contract Logistics gross margin contract, and is 7% the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Three factors: start-up costs from opening a site almost every week, ad hoc manpower hiring, and lagged fuel pass-through. About half of the YoY dilution is start-up cost, which should normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Express EBITDA loss narrow only INR 1 crore sequentially when gross margin rose about 120 bps?

540768|2026-09.headline: Mahindra Logistics Q2 FY27 PAT rose to INR26 crore (from a INR10 crore loss) and MESPL (Rivigo) turned EBITDA-positive at INR2.3 crore.
540768|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 24% YoY to INR2,095 crore and EBITDA rose to INR124 crore (5.9% margin, up 90 bps YoY). Contract logistics (about 80% of revenue) grew 28% with EBITDA of INR115 crore, while gross margin stayed at 10.1% consolidated (up 40 bps QoQ). MESPL (Rivigo) posted its first EBITDA-positive quarter, and management pivoted the last-mile business from a no-loss to a growth strategy. Freight forwarding revenue fell 44% YoY on leadership transition, and a tech transformation project was approved for start around Q4 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR85 crore in Q2 FY26; margin +90 bps YoY
vs loss of INR10 crore in Q2 FY26; vs INR25 crore in Q1 FY27
vs minus INR210 crore in H1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR308 crore (cash INR363 crore, debt INR55 crore)

segments.name: Contract logistics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,688 crore (+28% YoY vs INR1,317 crore); EBITDA INR115 crore vs INR89 crore. Gross margin grew 20% YoY; vacant space cut to 5% of June 2025 levels.

segments.name: MESPL (Rivigo, B2B express)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR169 crore (+69% YoY); EBITDA INR2.3 crore vs minus INR9 crore in Q2 FY26, first EBITDA-positive quarter. QoQ improvement was more yield-led than volume-led.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Revenue INR119 crore (+33% YoY vs INR90 crore); EBITDA INR3.4 crore vs INR2.1 crore. Management says gross margin grew 19% YoY; B2B is the majority of the mix.

segments.name: Last-mile delivery (LMD)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR68 crore, down 23% YoY from INR88 crore by choice; EBITDA INR1.6 crore vs INR0.4 crore; gross margin up 18.6% YoY. Strategy shifted from no-loss to growth; YoY growth expected from Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Freight forwarding
segments.commentary: Revenue INR50.6 crore (+12% QoQ, down 44% YoY); EBITDA INR1.7 crore, down only INR0.5 crore YoY. H2 FY27 described as a build phase, with real delivery expected in FY28.

guidance_outlook: Contract logistics gross margin: target of about 100 bps improvement from exit of FY26 (about 11% FY26 level per analyst framing); management clarified this is a medium-term target, not two to four quarters.
Capex for FY27 about INR110 crore (INR100 crore plus or minus INR10 crore); roughly half spent in H1, mostly in contract logistics and the 2x2 car-carrier JV.
MESPL: next milestone is PAT positivity; no formal timeline given, described as a multi-year growth story with continued investment in network and hubs.
Growth now targeted from the LMD business and from new business wins, with an internal target to grow new business wins 3.5x versus last year; H1 is running ahead of that.
Festive-season flex-capacity costs in Q3 expected to recur, as in prior years.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex about INR110 crore (INR100 crore plus or minus INR10 crore); H1 spend about half, per management.
Capex mainly in contract logistics and in the 2x2 car-carrier JV serving Mahindra auto and tractor business.
Board approved a business transformation project (new tech platform for MESPL and MLL) on 23 Oct 2026; execution to start around Q4 FY27; investment amount not disclosed.
MESPL is adding real estate and hubs to handle higher capacity and is expanding its pin-code coverage.
Standalone balance sheet debt-free since September 2025; consolidated debt INR55 crore, mainly vehicle loans under the asset-right model.
demand_pricing: Contract logistics growth driven by new client additions and higher wallet share with existing customers; e-commerce, manufacturing, telecom and last-mile cited as strong verticals.

Fuel cost increase of INR8.10 per litre-equivalent (as stated) was fully passed through; manpower cost pressure (including PF wage-ceiling change from INR15,000 to INR25,000) is only partly passed through because many contracts lack pass-through clauses.
MESPL: yield-led QoQ improvement from selective calibration actions; management expects volume-led growth going forward through network expansion.
M&M share of consolidated revenue about 60% (58% in FY26); management says there is no internal target to reduce M&M share.
Monsoon was 14% below LPA nationally, unevenly distributed across states; management says overall FY27 plan is intact.

qa_highlights.question: How should the steady-state EBITDA margin of MESPL be thought of, versus a peer at 10-12%, given possible network investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no explicit guidance. Next milestone is PAT positivity, with full visibility on the path; MESPL is a multi-year, decade-long story with continued investment after PAT positivity.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the sequential contract logistics gross margin improvement only 30 bps given fuel pass-through and onboarding?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel pass-through was fully completed and reflected in the 30 bps gain. Manpower costs are not fully passed through, and new costs (e.g., PF slab change) add pressure; the 100 bps gross margin improvement target is reaffirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Was there capacity build-up for the festive/e-commerce peak, and what is the tech platform investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Flex sites were added for peak, with 3-4 days' notice from customers; these costs recur each Q3. Tech project approved by Board today; amount not disclosed; details to be shared once execution starts around Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Clarify whether the 100 bps margin improvement is gross or EBITDA, and from what base.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 100 bps target is at the gross margin level, measured from the exit rate of FY26 rather than the full-year FY26 average.

qa_highlights.question: Key growth drivers for the next 2-3 years, and any remaining cost levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth from new clients, wallet share, e-commerce and LMD; cost control largely played out, so growth is the main lever now. New business wins are running ahead of the 3.5x internal target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for LMD, freight forwarding and mobility, and their capital employed?
qa_highlights.answer: LMD is moving to growth; freight forwarding is in a build phase in H2 FY27 with results expected in FY28 and zero capex; mobility B2B has long-term contracts and B2C is limited to Delhi. Capital employed is low and returns exceed the ROCE threshold, per the CFO.

qa_highlights.question: Is the M&M share of revenue set to fall?
qa_highlights.answer: No internal target to reduce M&M share; M&M share is about 60%, and the aim is to win 100% of M&M business.

risks_watch: Contract logistics gross margin (10.1% consolidated) must improve by about 100 bps over the medium term; manpower cost pass-through remains incomplete.
Festive-season flex staffing costs in Q3 FY27 and possible volume spillover for MESPL.
Freight forwarding revenue down 44% YoY; geopolitical disruption and high spot container rates are delaying new contracts.
MESPL needs to convert EBITDA positivity into PAT positivity while funding network expansion and the new tech platform.
Concentration on M&M (about 60% of revenue) and on automotive and manufacturing verticals, which management acknowledges can be cyclical.
Monsoon shortfall (14% below LPA) and uneven regional impact.
540768|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the turnaround, especially MESPL EBITDA positivity and the balance sheet, but cautious and somewhat evasive on margin timelines and tech investment amounts. Management repeatedly stressed that margin targets are medium-term and declined to quantify MESPL margins or the tech spend.
key_quotes: Whitespace reduction, you would recall, has been an issue in the past few quarters, and we had committed in quarter one of last year that we would reduce our whitespace that time of 1.6 million by 95%.

Isha Dalal: ...that margin improvement target that we have, I'm again repeating, is over the medium term. Medium term, and I have specifically clarified in the past, does not mean two quarters, four quarters.
In H1, we are doing better than that. And this is what is giving us confidence that if we are winning businesses like that, then the growth momentum will continue to shape our trajectory forward.

This is a kind of a I would say a decade story.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Contract logistics revenue grew 28% YoY to INR1,688 crore on new client additions and wallet share; MESPL volume growth expected via network expansion, while LMD revenue fell 23% YoY by choice and returns to YoY growth only from Q3 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is guided at about INR110 crore for FY27 and a Board-approved tech platform (amount undisclosed) starts around Q4 FY27, but utilisation was not disclosed so there is no hard trigger for a new capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Contract logistics new business wins are running ahead of the 3.5x internal target and Q2 revenue grew 24% YoY, but management gave no revenue growth number to raise.

rows.label: MESPL (Rivigo) PAT positivity
rows.why: MESPL turned EBITDA-positive at INR2.3 crore (vs minus INR9 crore a year ago) on INR169 crore revenue, and management says it should achieve PAT positivity, but gave no formal timeline and continued network investment is ongoing.

rows.label: Freight forwarding build phase
rows.why: Freight forwarding revenue fell 44% YoY to INR50.6 crore and the business is in a build phase in H2 FY27, with real delivery expected only in FY28; geopolitical disruption is delaying new contracts.

rows.why: The PF wage-ceiling change (INR15,000 to INR25,000) adds cost and many contracts lack pass-through clauses, so pass-through is only partial, while fuel (INR8.10 per litre-equivalent) was fully passed through.

540769|2026-03.headline: New India Assurance FY26 profit after tax rose 40% to INR 1,384 crore, but combined ratio worsened to 122.57% on wage-revision charges.
540769|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 GWP grew only 1.63% to INR 11,619 crore, reflecting competitive property pricing, while Indian domestic GDP grew 10.9% versus the industry's 9.3%. The full-year combined ratio rose to 122.57% (116.67% excluding the wage revision impact) as the company absorbed INR 3,525 crore of wage and family pension revision costs. Incurred claim ratio rose to 98.65% on Motor TP court awards, the Air India aviation loss, marine claims and NATCAT flood claims not fully recovered under reinsurance. Management guided to a Motor single-digit growth and double-digit overall growth in FY27, led by Health Retail.

financial_highlights.change: +1.63% vs INR 11,433 crore in Q4 FY25
+61% vs INR 347 crore in Q4 FY25
vs 116.78% in FY25; 116.67% excluding wage revision (vs 115.34%)
vs INR 6,124 crore loss in FY25
vs 1.91 times in FY25; regulatory minimum 1.5 times

segments.name: Health and PA
segments.commentary: 47.57% of book; premium up 12.62% in FY26 but only 2.58% in Q4. ICR improved to 99.05% from 100.98%, helped by TPA audits raised from 30% to 50%.

segments.name: Fire
segments.commentary: Premium up 10.76% in FY26 but down 4.33% in Q4 on property rate cuts. ICR rose to 76.54% from 71.20% on small NATCAT claims not fully reinsured.

segments.name: Marine
segments.commentary: Premium up 11.43% in FY26 and 20.26% in Q4; ICR jumped to 86.74% from 53.74% on cargo claims and a general average claim.

segments.commentary: Premium declined as inward crop reinsurance was not accepted; ICR rose to 96.15% from 81.02% on legacy claims.

segments.name: Other lines
segments.commentary: Premium up 12.48% in FY26 and 2.03% in Q4; ICR rose to 63.40% from 58.77%. Miscellaneous ex-crop grew about 26% per analyst question, driven by engineering, liability and surety bonds.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 industry growth in double digits; New India to grow double digits overall.
Motor growth to be single digit in FY27, with focus on profitability over volume.
Overall ratios expected to show a reducing trend in FY27 as Motor portfolio recalibration takes hold.
Motor mix target: private cars and two-wheelers to dominate; CVs above 7,500 cc to be reduced; two-wheelers to move toward double-digit share selectively.
Motor OD premium increases planned on selected segments; commissions and payouts to be adjusted dynamically in commercial lines.
Health Retail to be the primary growth driver under the 'GO RETAIL' mandate.
capex_capacity: Motor portfolio churn started from Q2 FY26; management says about another year is needed to reach the target mix.
IT infrastructure revamp nearing completion; all retail products online; mobile super apps for customers, intermediaries and surveyors launched.
Automated survey appointment and digital survey reports implemented.
Digital marketing and sales piloted for a few Health products, to be extended to other lines.
Bharat Maritime Pool operationalised with sovereign guarantee; company acting as lead insurer for P&I and hull risk.
demand_pricing: Industry GDP reached about INR 3.36 lakh crore in FY26, up 9.3%; New India's domestic share rose from 12.56% to 12.74%.
Segment market shares: Fire 17.56%, Marine 17.77%, Motor 9.91%, Health and PA 14.93%, other lines 15.13%.
Property rates fell sharply in H2 FY26 on competition, driving Fire Q4 degrowth.
Motor competition described as extremely competitive; discounts rising every quarter over the past year.
Motor sales recovered after GST rationalisation: private cars grew 17.8% and two-wheelers 21.5% in H2 FY26; Q4 growth was 16.3% and 24.7%.
Distribution mix (domestic): broker 35.79%, direct 30.13%, agency 25.91%, dealer 7.56%, bancassurance 0.61%.
Commissions cut across many lines including Health; reinsurance commissions increased. Q4 commission ratio fell to 9.53% from 11.17%.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the Motor portfolio course correction take, when will loss ratios fall, and will OD premiums be repriced?
qa_highlights.answer: Correction began in Q2 FY26 and needs about another year; overall ratios expected to fall in FY27. OD premium increases planned on selected segments. Competition remains extremely competitive with discounts rising each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the target Motor mix?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 mix: private cars 47.56%, commercial vehicles 45.60%, two-wheelers 6.79%. Plan to exit CVs above 7,500 cc and grow private cars and two-wheelers, with two-wheelers toward double digits selectively.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the commission ratio decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissions reduced across many lines including Health, and reinsurance commissions increased, so net commission moved in the company's favour.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 growth outlook and capital gains for FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Double-digit growth expected for the company, with Motor at single digit. FY26 capital gains were about INR 5,477 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Where will Health and PA profitability go?
qa_highlights.answer: Health ICR reduced by about 2% and commission ratio cut, which management says significantly raised segment profitability; individual Health demand supported by 18% GST waiver.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is market share gain and how will underwriting discipline hold with faster growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth described as strategic, mainly retail; underwriting guidelines set by head office with strict periodic monitoring.

risks_watch: Combined ratio of 122.57% and ICR of 98.65%; watch whether ratios fall in FY27 as management guided.

Q4 GWP growth of 1.63% and Fire degrowth of 4.33% amid property rate cuts.

rows.why: Management plans OD premium increases on selected segments, with Motor OD ICR at 108.85% versus 104.22% a year earlier, though competition is extremely intense and discounts are rising each quarter.

540774|2026-03.headline: IFGL Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 2% YoY to INR 276 crore and FY26 consolidated income grew 14% to INR 1,904 crore; consolidated Q4 EBITDA margin 8.6%.
540774|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 total income was INR 278 crore (+2% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 11.8%, while FY26 standalone EBITDA margin was 11.3%. Domestic revenue grew 7% YoY in Q4 and 20% for FY26 to INR 864 crore, but exports fell 11% in FY26 on geopolitical and market headwinds. Margins were hit by product mix shifts, lower exports and higher raw material and freight costs. Management also announced a senior leadership reshuffle, with Mukesh Rawal moving to India operations and Manoj Rakhecha to international operations.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 2.15 per share (21.5% of face value)

segments.name: Domestic (India)
segments.commentary: Domestic revenue reached INR 864 crore, up 7% YoY in Q4 and 20% for FY26. Management says growth comes from share gains in large integrated steel plants and new small foundry accounts; it does not split the growth by source.

segments.name: Exports (India-made)
segments.commentary: Export revenue fell 11% in FY26 on geopolitical and external market headwinds. Management says volumes have started to improve, and it has added manpower to rebuild export accounts.

segments.name: USA (Americas)
segments.commentary: US revenue grew 26% YoY in Q4 and 25% in FY26, with subsidiary EBITDA margins back in the high-teens (described later as double-digit). Management calls the margins sustainable.

segments.name: Sheffield Refractories (UK)
segments.commentary: Management reports strong performance with healthy growth, operating leverage and sustained customer demand. Phase 1 of the India technology transfer is complete.

segments.name: Hofmann Ceramics (Germany)
segments.commentary: Losses fell significantly in FY26 after turnaround steps and cost cuts. Management expects the business to move close to breakeven during FY27.

segments.name: Monocon (UK)
segments.commentary: Revenue recovered despite losing a key high-margin UK customer after a plant closure. Management targets breakeven by Q4 FY27 and is entering foundry and new geographies.

guidance_outlook: Management is targeting double-digit domestic volume growth in FY27, and says it expects to grow well above underlying market growth over the medium term.
Management expects US results to show major growth in FY27 and expects the Americas to remain an important contributor.
Hofmann is expected to move close to breakeven during FY27; Monocon is targeted to reach breakeven by Q4 FY27.
Management is in talks with customers on price revisions and expects a reasonable pass-through of cost increases.
The Sheffield plastic ramming technology is expected to be ready for full-fledged market entry by end of CY2026, after trials.
Consolidated amortisation of about INR 26.7 crore a year ends from FY27 because the legacy goodwill from the 2017 amalgamation is fully amortised.
capex_capacity: Greenfield project in Khurda, Odisha: work has picked up, but the Board is still evaluating pace and structure, with no timeline given.
Gujarat (Bhachau) greenfield plant: awaiting statutory approvals from the Government of India under Press Note 3; no timeline given.
Vizag plant: first energy optimizing furnace (EOF) campaign completed with a lining and tuyere blocks made in-house, exceeding 1,000 heats.
Management says recent capex in Vizag, Rourkela and R&D will mature and generate returns; capex is described as under control.
Alumina and basic brick capacity for cement is planned at Bhachau and a joint venture basic brick line is coming up.
demand_pricing: Indian steel capacity expansion announcements are expected to drive refractory demand; management says customers increasingly prefer full-range refractory solution providers.
Raw material costs remain elevated due to energy, freight and currency; imported minerals and shipping rates are the key cost swing factors.
Competitive pricing has been accepted in bricks and casting flux to win new accounts, with margins initially lean.
Early FY27 saw LPG availability issues linked to West Asia developments.
Europe: order books are improving, with policy support for domestic manufacturing, defence and infrastructure. German foundries serving specialised alloys are on an uptrend.
Monocon has raised prices where input and logistics costs require, and says customers are accepting this.

qa_highlights.question: What operational triggers will reverse the five-year decline in return metrics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said market conditions have changed and pointed to the US turnaround and Hofmann/Monocon fixes, with results expected within a year. It also said recent capex will mature and generate returns.

qa_highlights.question: Why has working capital expanded, and what is the plan for inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said working capital cycle has reduced versus last year and cash was generated from it, and that inventory is on a declining trend. No quantified inventory days were given.

qa_highlights.question: How will capital deployment be balanced against rising net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said debt is negligible, that investment in Vizag, Rourkela and R&D is for future returns, and that capex is under control. Consolidated debt is INR 195.6 crore against cash of INR 122 crore.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Sheffield technology transfer add to top line, and what is the delta?
qa_highlights.answer: Mukesh Rawal said the customer base is identified, equipment is online and trial orders are in hand, with full market entry expected by end of CY2026. He said the revenue delta would be provided later by the CFO. No figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US demand outlook for Q1 FY27 and for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects major US growth in FY27, with new customer trials succeeding. Mexico is growing and foundry business is being added in the US and Mexico.

qa_highlights.question: Is the domestic volume growth target 15-20% for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company is at least targeting double-digit domestic growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Monocon's turnaround and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Monocon is entering new geographies and products, including foundries, with trials underway. Management aims to restore profitability by Q4 FY27 and is seeking price hikes where needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why are exports underwhelming, and is it a deliberate pullback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift to India was a deliberate decision because global steel is shrinking, and it will retarget exports as opportunities arise. Geopolitical factors and European plant closures were cited.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving senior management exits?
qa_highlights.answer: Mihir Bajoria said the exits are normal churn after the former CEO, Mr. Arasu, left with his team. Mukesh Rawal said the top team is restructured and in place, and he returns full-time from August.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from product mix, lower exports, and raw material and shipping cost swings; price pass-through is still under negotiation.

Export volumes fell 11% in FY26 and export accounts may need rebuilding.
Hofmann and Monocon are still loss-making, with breakeven targets for FY27 and Q4 FY27.
Working capital and inventory levels are high, and consolidated net debt has emerged versus earlier cash-rich position.
Ongoing ambiguity over Khurda and Gujarat greenfield timing, pending government approvals.

I'm pleased to share that Phase 1 has been successfully completed, including product recipe transfer, knowledge sharing and joint product development activities.

540774|2026-06.headline: IFGL Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA fell 17% YoY to INR31 crore on raw material and LPG cost spikes, while consolidated PAT rose 58% to INR17 crore.
540774|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue rose 8% YoY to INR297 crore, with domestic up 7% and exports up 9%, but gross margin fell to 43% from 47% on higher raw material prices. Standalone EBITDA dropped 17% YoY to INR31 crore as input costs and LPG availability constraints outpaced price increases, which management says will pass through with a lag. Consolidated total income rose 13% YoY to INR515 crore and consolidated EBITDA rose 2% to INR40 crore, with PAT up 58% to INR17 crore. The Europe segment was weak because British Steel's low output cut offtake at Sheffield Refractories, while US operations grew double digits with improving margins.

financial_highlights.change: Management says base has grown; target double-digit for year-end

segments.name: Standalone India
segments.commentary: Revenue INR297 crore (+8% YoY); EBITDA INR31 crore (-17% YoY) hit by raw material costs and LPG/fuel price surge. Price increases were implemented but are only partly offsetting costs.

segments.name: Europe (Monocon UK + Sheffield Refractories)
segments.commentary: Management attributed the weak quarter mainly to Sheffield Refractories' low sales due to British Steel's blast furnace problems, with losses rising to about INR7 crore from INR3 crore QoQ (per analyst). Monocon UK losses reportedly fell QoQ and it is approaching breakeven.

segments.name: US subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Revenue grew double digits YoY with improved margins from cost optimization; management described margins as more than double-digit and robust.

segments.name: Monocon and Sheffield Refractories (overall)
segments.commentary: Combined revenue grew double digits YoY despite headwinds; Monocon has opened offices in Australia and Saudi Arabia and is entering iron and steel and foundry refractories.

segments.name: Hofmann Ceramic
segments.commentary: Order book held at similar levels YoY; management targets reducing losses and breakeven by end FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects price increases to flow through progressively over coming quarters, but says they are temporary and offset only input cost rises, with no additional margin expected from them.
Consolidated EBITDA margin target is double digit, dependent on geopolitics and overseas demand; earlier 12% margin reference was not reaffirmed explicitly.
British Steel expected to restart blast furnace and normalize offtake in Q2 FY27; Sheffield Refractories expected back to normal.
Speciality Steel (ex-Liberty Rotherham) melt shops are expected to restart around November-December 2026 per market sources.
Management says staff cost is at about 10% of revenue and is not expected to go beyond this level.
Management believes the worst is behind on profitability, but cautioned that conditions can change quickly.
capex_capacity: Sheffield Refractories Phase 1 plastic ramming mass production has started at IFGL Vizag facility; marketing trials underway, with full customer trials and accreditation still needed.
Adding mag carbon brick and casting flux new lines could add INR150-200 crore of revenue at peak capacity for these two products.

Chinese JV: government appropriate authority approval sought; authorities advised changing location and reapplying, so the project is on hold. Investment so far is only in land (Gujarat), with some spend.

R&D facility in Odisha: management said spend is around INR20 crore, disputing an analyst's INR100-150 crore figure. R&D is developing foundry materials, thin slab caster tundish SEN for the US, and recycled material use.
demand_pricing: India steel demand forecast to grow 7.4% in 2026 and 9.2% in 2027 (management citation).
US steel production up 6% YoY; US business revenue up double digits, with new product introductions (thin slab caster tundish SEN) made in the US.
UK: British Steel now in public ownership; British Steel produced at very low levels in Q1 due to blast furnace problems.
Ocean freight spikes due to geopolitical situation hit UK and China operations.
Price increases were negotiated per contract and are temporary, tied to input costs from geopolitical tension.
Management said there was no market share loss in domestic business; the base has grown, which lowered the percentage growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove overseas subsidiary growth and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Manoj Rakhecha said the Americas drove top-line growth with robust margins. Management expects momentum to continue across subsidiaries and aims to turn loss-making units (UK, Europe, America, Germany) back to profit. Company-wise margins were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall 17% if there was no competitive pricing pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said raw material and LPG/fuel costs rose sharply due to geopolitics, and price increases from customers were not enough to offset them.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Europe EBITDA turn negative (-8%) after nearing breakeven in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe comprises Monocon UK and Sheffield Refractories. Sheffield's sales were low because British Steel's output was minimal; Monocon UK is near breakeven. Q2 expected to normalize; no orders lost, just timing.

qa_highlights.question: Will staff costs stay near 10% of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Agarwal said standalone staff cost of INR28.7 crore is up from INR24 crore in Q4 but level with Q1 FY26; management aims to contain it. Consolidated employee cost rose partly due to a provision reversal last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is 12% consolidated EBITDA margin still the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is aiming for double-digit consolidated EBITDA margin, dependent on geopolitics and overseas demand, and expects to return to that level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Chinese JV and R&D investment?
qa_highlights.answer: The Chinese JV is on hold pending government approval; the company must change location and reapply. Only land in Gujarat has been bought so far. R&D spend is about INR20 crore per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is the worst behind for profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Manoj Rakhecha agreed with that view for today but cautioned that conditions can change quickly; he cited early green shoots in European steel.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak revenue capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: No overall peak revenue figure given; the two new lines (mag carbon brick and casting flux) could add INR150-200 crore at peak.

British Steel blast furnace restart and Sheffield Refractories offtake: management expects normalisation in Q2 FY27; a delay would keep Europe segment loss-making.
Monocon UK and Europe losses: Europe EBITDA went to -8% with Sheffield losses rising to about INR7 crore from about INR3 crore QoQ (per analyst); track whether Monocon UK reaches breakeven.
Speciality Steel (ex-Liberty Rotherham) melt shop restart, reported by market sources for November-December 2026; no firm confirmation given.
Chinese JV on hold pending government approval, with a location change and reapplication required; only land in Gujarat acquired so far.

Consolidated employee cost: management says standalone staff cost is around 10% of revenue and will not go beyond this; consolidated employee cost rose partly due to a prior-quarter provision reversal. Watch for containment.
key_quotes: The contraction was primarily driven by higher raw material costs arising from geopolitical unc ertainties and supply chain disruptions, along with elevated LPG costs due to availability constraints during the quarter.
And these are all temporary price increase based on the input cost, which has increased on this geopolitical front.
So far it's only been done in land and some money has been spent because we've been marketing other products
So definitely, the worst is behind us.

540775|2026-03.headline: Khadim India Q4 FY26 revenue fell to INR83.6 crores (vs INR93.8 crores) with PAT of just INR0.77 crores; FY27 target is ~INR400 crores at 14% EBITDA.
540775|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations declined to INR83.6 crores from INR93.8 crores a year earlier, with gross margin of 51.5%, EBITDA of INR11.9 crores (14.3% margin) and PAT of INR0.77 crores (0.9% margin). For FY26, revenue fell 12% to INR367.1 crores, EBITDA was INR49.1 crores (13.4%) and PAT INR3.1 crores. Management attributed the decline to store closures, lower primary sales to franchisees and deliberate inventory and creditor reduction, which cost an estimated INR10-15 crores of sales over the last two quarters. The company also completed the demerger of its distribution and manufacturing business into KSR Footwear Limited during the year.

segments.name: Retail (COCO and franchise network)

segments.commentary: Grew 6% YoY in FY26, driven by men's formal and semi-formal footwear; new launches planned.

segments.commentary: Grew 46% YoY in FY26, with traction in premium and semi-premium categories.

FY27 EBITDA margin target of around 14%.
