Every 5-10% revenue growth could add about 100-200 bps to EBITDA margin; PAT margin of 2-2.5% cited as achievable if sales grow.
Inventory to be rebuilt in Q1 FY27 and to a level sufficient for about INR400 crores of sales by end of first half FY27; no store closures expected beyond those already done.
Net debt target of INR110-115 crores post restructuring.
capex_capacity: Store rationalisation largely complete (about 60 closed over two years); new openings to be mainly franchise EBO and TFM formats, where the company invests only in stock, with COCO used at strategic high-revenue locations.
Target steady state of around 200 COCO stores.
Working capital limits largely unutilised; management expects EBO collections to fund cash flow.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 volume about 14 lakh pairs vs about 12 lakh pairs in Q3 FY26; revenue flat QoQ due to discounting.
Demand soft through FY26, with pressure in mass and value segments; April 2026 sales hit by state elections in Bengal and Assam.

Premium products carry 2-3% higher gross margin than mass products and less discounting.
Raw material prices up about 20-25% since February 2026; company raised MRP by INR25-50 in retail, with more pressure in distribution than retail.
GST rate cut passed through on price, but management said demand did not rise and ASP fell somewhat YoY.

qa_highlights.question: How can the company sustain a 14% EBITDA margin with revenue falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline came from store closures and lower franchise primary sales; revenue should hold around INR400 crores and EBITDA around 14% next year after cost cuts.

qa_highlights.question: Why has blended gross margin declined?
qa_highlights.answer: Price cuts on products under INR500 over the last 1-2 years; Q4 margin improved and FY27 ASP increases should keep gross margin at 48-50%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was inventory reduced sharply (about 40% YoY)?
qa_highlights.answer: A deliberate call to cut inventory days; some Q4 sales were lost, and the company cleared discounted stock and reduced creditors.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue not recover in Q4 after inventory correction?
qa_highlights.answer: Stock replenishment ordered in Q4 arrives in Q1, so the benefit flows in one to two quarters; INR10-15 crores of sales lost over the last two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company moving from mass value to premium?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said Khadim remains a middle-class mass value brand and will add premium products such as British Walkers and Sharon as a blend.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade payables fall from about INR196 crores to INR111 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly the demerger, since last year's figure included both entities; the rest came from deliberately reduced purchases and creditor payments in Q3 and Q4.

risks_watch: Revenue still well below FY25 levels; FY27 INR400 crore target depends on inventory rebuild and recovery in demand.
Raw material cost volatility (up 20-25% since February 2026), with pressure on gross margin.
Working capital and cash: cash fell sharply in FY26 (partly demerger transfer), and receivables from franchisees are to be corrected.
Athleisure is structurally limited by small store formats, so growth there is capped.
Skechers scale-up and e-commerce share (about 5%) remain unproven.

540776|2026-03.headline: 5paisa Q4 FY26 total revenue rose 8% QoQ to INR 85.5 crore, with PAT of INR 44.3 crore and a INR 468 crore rights issue completed.
540776|2026-03.overview: Management described a volatile quarter driven by the Iran war, Brent above USD 100/bbl, rupee weakness and AI-related valuation pressure, with indices down about 11%. Customer acquisition rose 33% QoQ to over one lakh in Q4, taking the total base to 51.8 lakh. Broking revenue grew 13% QoQ to INR 41.8 crore and aligned income rose 5% to INR 20.7 crore. Profit fell slightly YoY (per the CFO) due to tech and HR investment, and the rights issue lifted net worth above INR 1,100 crore.

segments.commentary: Average client funding book INR 410 crore, up 8% QoQ. Eligible MTF stock universe expanded from 700 to 1,500+ stocks; investor limit raised to INR 3 crore.

segments.commentary: MF AUM INR 1,761 crore, down 6% QoQ, partly due to mark-to-market on falling markets. Stock SIPs reintroduced and ETF dashboard launched.

The average client funding book (MTF plus T+5) was INR 422 crore, up 3% QoQ, and mutual fund AUM reached INR 2,073 crore, up 18% QoQ. segments.name: Cash equities
segments.commentary: Cash ADTO grew in Q1 per management, with no quantified figure given.

540777|2026-03.headline: HDFC Life FY26 VNB rose only 2% to INR 4,034 crores; NBM fell to 24.2% after GST and surrender-value impacts, with Q4 growth slowing at HDFC Bank.
540777|2026-03.overview: FY26 individual APE grew 7% YoY, but top-line growth fell below the company's original expectation, with the slowdown concentrated in Q4 from unabsorbed GST, softer bancassurance and deferred demand in March. Proprietary channels grew 15-16% in Q4 and FY26, and protection grew 43% for the year. VNB rose 2% to INR 4,034 crores and NBM fell 140 bps to 24.2%, with 130 bps from GST/SSV, 90 bps from fixed-cost absorption, and 40 bps from persistency assumption strengthening, partly offset by 120 bps of product mix. Management said the GST drag is tapering (about 110 bps in Q4) and should be neutralised by H1 FY27.

segments.commentary: Mix rose about 300 bps YoY to around 8% of individual APE in Q4; AGNI, a variable annuity linked to Nifty 50, launched in Q4 at a ticket size of INR 25 lakh and above.

segments.commentary: Grew about 500 bps ahead of the company; over 250 branches added in 30 months contribute about 13% of agency top line. FC base grew 43% gross.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand to deeper markets, and what are the returns?

Profit after tax was INR 611 crores (up 12%, or 17% excluding GST), embedded value INR 65,860 crores and solvency 185%. 13-month persistency moderated about 200 bps to 84%, and HDFC Bank channel business stayed soft as the company ceded share during competitive pricing in FY26 and says it has now recovered.

540777|2026-09.headline: HDFC Life H1 FY27 VNB rose 12% to ₹2,037 crore at a 24.7% margin, while solvency fell to 180% on capital consumption.
540777|2026-09.overview: Q2 individual APE growth of 13% (overall) and 11% in H1 kept HDFC Life ahead of the private industry, with individual weighted received premium up 11% in Q2 and market share up 10bps to 16.2%. VNB reached ₹2,037 crore (up 12%, Q2 up 15%) and margin expanded to 24.7% from 24.5%. Persistency softened on unit-linked renewals and a non-par cohort, and the EV walk showed negative operating and investment variances from equity underperformance, yield rises and wider credit spreads. Solvency fell to 180%, prompting a ₹500 crore subordinated debt raise. Management spent much of the call on the IRDAI distribution-economics consultation paper, where it was non-committal on specifics.
